(3) The witnessing of the Day of Judgment: «wa-jā'a rabbuka wa-l-malu ʿadu ffa-ṣaffan ṣaffā» — Allah, the angels, and the prophets and witnesses will come (3:39, 4:41). (4) Divine witnessing: Allah is the Witness over all things — «fa-Llāhu shahīdun baynahum» (Allah is Witness between them — 2:194, 3:98, 4:33, 4:79, 5:117, 8:27, 9:19).

The most comprehensive concept is al-shahīd — the Witness. Allah is al-Shahīd, the divine Witness over all creation, all actions, all hearts. His shahāda is not passive observation but active knowing — He witnesses the inner reality of every soul. The Prophet ﷺ is described as shahīd over the ummah on the Day of Judgment (4:41), having witnessed its reality during his lifetime. The believers are to be shuhadā' (witnesses) over the worlds (2:143), testifying against the prophets who came before them and against humanity. The shahāda principle structures Islamic epistemology: truth is attested by witnessing, not mere assertion; faith is testified, not assumed; justice is witnessed, not pretended.
shades.hadith_ar: أُشْهِدُ أَنْ لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا اللَّهُ وَأَنِّي رَسُولُ اللَّهِ
shades.en: I testify that there is no god but Allah and that I am the Messenger of Allah

meaning.en: To reap, harvest, gather. The root denotes the gathering of crops at the time of harvest — and by metaphor, the gathering of deeds on the Day of Judgment. The huṣād (harvest) is the moment when what was sown is gathered.
meaning.ar: جَمْعُ الثَّمَرِ عِنْدَ نُضْجِهِ — وَالْحَصَادُ: مَوْسِمُ جَمْعِ الثَّمَرِ

al_raghib.ar: الْحَصَادُ: قَطْعُ الثَّمَرِ. وَيُسْتَعْمَلُ فِي جَمْعِ الشَّيْءِ الَّذِي نَضَجَ
al_raghib.en: Haṣād: cutting/harvesting fruit. Used for gathering something that has ripened.

quran_examples.ar: وَلَا تُسْرِفُوا۟ ۚ إِنَّهُۥ لَا يُحِبُّ ٱلْمُسْرِفِينَ
quran_examples.en: Do not be wasteful — He does not love the wasteful
quran_examples.context: The prohibition of waste — citing harvest

hadith.ar: كُلُّ ابْنِ آدَمَ تَبَابٌ، إِلَّا الْعِلْمُ
hadith.en: Every son of Adam perishes except the knowledge (you leave behind).

shades.name_en: al-Ḥaṣād — Harvesting Deeds and Gathering the Fruits of Action
shades.name_ar: الْحَصَادُ — جَمْعُ أَثْمَارِ الْأَعْمَالِ يَوْمَ الْقِيَامَةِ
shades.explanation:
Al-ḥaṣād (harvest, reaping) is the Quran's metaphor for the gathering of deeds on the Day of Judgment. Just as the farmer sows seeds in this world and reaps the harvest at the appointed time, every soul sows deeds in this world and reaps its reward on the Last Day. The huṣād of the Hereafter is described in terms of agricultural harvesting — sudden, comprehensive, and decisive.

The verse 6:141 — «wa-lā tusrifū innahu lā yuḥibbu l-musrifīn» — addresses agricultural harvest in the context of waste. The earlier part of the verse: «wa-tadharū khaṭāyākumu wa-lā tas'ulū khilāla l-arḍi wa-ḥaṣādiru khilālan wa-mā tunkirū» — instructs the farmers to leave some harvest for the poor (not cutting the harvest entirely — 6:141, building on 6:141's broader discussion). The huṣād principle in worldly agriculture becomes a metaphor for ethical restraint: do not be so eager to take everything that you forget justice and generosity.

The eschatological ḥaṣād is the central image in 42:20: «wa-yastaʿjilūnaka bi-l-ʿadhābi wa-lan yukhlifa Llāhu waʿdahu wa-inna yawman ʿinda rabbika ka-alfi sanatin mimmā taʿuddūn» — they urge you for the punishment, but Allah will not break His promise. The huṣād of deeds is the harvest of what was sown — every soul reaps what it sowed, no less and no more. The temporal delay between sowing and reaping is divine mercy (time for repentance and amendment); the certainty of eventual reaping is divine justice.
shades.hadith_ar: اِحْرُثْ لِدُنْيَاكَ كَأَنَّكَ تَعِيشُ أَبَدًا، وَاعْمَلْ لِآخِرَتِكَ كَأَنَّكَ تَمُوتُ غَدًا
shades.en: Cultivate for this world as if you will live forever; work for the Hereafter as if you will die tomorrow

meaning.en: Firewood, fuel. The root describes that which is gathered for burning — and metaphorically, the tongue and gossip that 'fuel' the fires of discord and social conflict.
meaning.ar: الْحَطَبُ: الْوَقُودُ مِنَ الْحَطَبِ — وَالْحَطَّابُ: مَنْ يَجْمَعُ الْحَطَبَ

al_raghib.ar: الْحَطَبُ: الْوَقُودُ. وَأَصْلُهُ مَا يَجْمَعُهُ الْإِنْسَانُ مِنَ الشَّجَرِ لِوَقُودِ النَّارِ
al_raghib.en: Ḥaṭab: firewood. Originally what one gathers from trees for fueling fire.

quran_examples.ar: وَٱمْرَأَتُهُۥ حَمَّالَةَ ٱلْحَطَبِ
quran_examples.en: And his wife — the carrier of firewood
quran_examples.context: Abū Lahab's wife and her hostile speech

hadith.ar: إِيَّاكُمْ وَالْكَذِبَ، فَإِنَّ الْكَذِبَ يَهْدِي إِلَى الْفُجُورِ
hadith.en: Beware of lying, for lying leads to wickedness

shades.name_en: Ḥaṭab al-Nār — The Fuel of Hellfire and the Fuel of Discord
shades.name_ar: حَطَبُ النَّارِ — وَقُودُ الْجَحِيمِ وَوَقُودُ الْفِتَنِ
shades.explanation:
The verb ḥ-ṭ-b appears in the Quran primarily in the description of Abū Lahab's wife in Sūrat al-Masad: «wa-mra'atuhu ḥammālata l-ḥaṭab» (his wife, the carrier of firewood — 111:4). The classical exegetes (Ibn ʿAbbās, al-Ḥasan al-Baṣrī) explain that her «firewood» was her hostile speech against the Prophet ﷺ — gossip, slander, and false reports that she spread among the Quraysh. She was thus a «carrier of firewood» not in the literal sense (gathering wood) but in the figurative sense: her words were the fuel that fed the fire of discord and hatred against Islam.

The metaphorical extension of ḥ-ṭ-b is the broader Quranic teaching on speech and its consequences. Words, like firewood, can fuel fire — building up hostility, division, and conflict between people. The ḥammāl al-ḥaṭab (carrier of firewood) is anyone whose speech enflames rather than illuminates, divides rather than unites, destroys rather than constructs. The hadīth qudsī — Allah's speech is most often revealed in the voice of the human: when we speak evil, we 'fuel' Hellfire with our words; when we speak good, we 'fuel' the light of Paradise.

The Sūrat al-Masad description of Abū Lahab's wife «ḥammālata l-ḥaṭab» — grammatically in the accusative, an intensive construct — emphasizes the habitual nature of her hostile speech. She was not a one-time gossiper but a lifelong carrier of hostile speech, whose every word fed the fire. The Quran's verdict: she (and her husband) will be fuel for the hellfire that they themselves have kindled — a just punishment, fitting the crime. The warning: beware the words you speak, for they are firewood — they fuel a fire that either burns you or warms you, depending on what you have gathered.
shades.hadith_ar: إِنَّ الرَّجُلَ لَيَتَكَلَّمُ بِالْكَلِمَةِ فَيَسْقُطُ بِهَا فِي النَّارِ أَبْعَدَ مَا بَيْنَ الْمَشْرِقِ وَالْمَغْرِبِ
shades.en: A man may speak a word that plunges him into Hellfire, a distance between east and west

meaning.en: Good news, glad tidings. The root denotes joyful announcement — particularly of divine mercy, prophethood, or the rewards of faith. The bashsh (announcer of glad tidings) is one who carries joyful news.
meaning.ar: الْإِخْبَارُ بِمَا تَسُرُّ بِهِ — وَالْبُشْرَى: الْخَبَرُ السَّارُّ الَّذِي يَسُرُّ السَّامِعَ

al_raghib.ar: الْبُشْرَى: الْخَبَرُ السَّارُّ. وَالْإِبْشَارُ: الْإِخْبَارُ بِمَا يَسُرُّ — وَهُوَ ضِدُّ الْإِنْذَارِ
al_raghib.en: Bushrā: glad news. Ibshār: informing with what gladdens — the opposite of indhār (warning).

quran_examples.ar: لَا تَحْزَنْ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ مَعَنَا
quran_examples.en: Do not grieve, for Allah is with us
quran_examples.context: The divine good news to the Prophet in the Cave

hadith.ar: أَحَبُّ الْأَعْمَالِ إِلَى اللَّهِ سُرُورٌ تُدْخِلُهُ عَلَى مُسْلِمٍ
hadith.en: The most beloved of deeds to Allah is bringing joy to a Muslim.

shades.name_en: Bushrā — Good Tidings as the Prophet's Essential Mission
shades.name_ar: الْبُشْرَى — الْإِبْشَارُ بِرَحْمَةِ اللَّهِ وَالْوَعْدِ الْإِلٰهِيِّ
shades.explanation:
Bushrā — good news, glad tidings — is one of the Quran's central categories of prophetic address. The verb bashshara (to give good news) and its nominal form bushrā frame the Quranic message as fundamentally glad news (in distinction from warning — indhār). The verse 2:119 — «wa-mā arsalnaka illā rahmatan li-l-ʿālamīn» (We sent you only as a mercy to all the worlds) — captures the prophetic mission: not just warning against punishment, but most essentially announcing the mercy and good news of God's love for humanity.

The bashshīrūn (announcers of good tidings) are the prophets — each one is a bashīr (bringer of glad tidings) to his people. The verse 2:213 — «wa-mā arsalnaka illā rahmatan li-l-ʿālamīn wa-ilā Allāhu yunqalabu l-amru kulluhu» — describes the universal prophetic mission. The bashīr warns and announces: warns of the consequences of disbelief, but also announces the good news of mercy, forgiveness, and Paradise for the faithful. The bashshara is not a harasser, a condemner, a fearful threatener — but a bringer of joy, an announcer of hope, a herald of God's unbounded generosity.

The ḥadīth of the Prophet ﷺ — «ahabbu l-aʿmāli ilā Llāh surūrun tudkhiluhu ʿalā muslim» (the most beloved of deeds to Allah is bringing joy to a Muslim — Tirmidhī 1692) — extends the bushrā principle from prophetic address to ordinary Muslim ethics. Every believer is called to be a bashīr — to bring good news to others, to gladden their hearts, to announce what is hopeful. The opposite — narrating death, disease, loss to people without need — is described as a disease of the tongue. The bashīr's speech, like the Prophet's ﷺ speech, is life-giving: «he was sent only as a mercy to all the worlds» — and every Muslim who brings joy to another is a participant in this mission of mercy.
shades.hadith_ar: بَشِّرُوا وَلَا تُنَفِّرُوا، وَيَسِّرُوا وَلَا تُعَسِّرُوا
shades.hadith_en: Give good tidings and do not create aversion; make things easy and do not make them difficult

meaning.en: To preserve, protect, guard, memorize. The root designates the act of guarding against loss or corruption — whether of physical objects, knowledge, or the soul itself. The ḥāfiẓ (preserver) is one who maintains the integrity of what is entrusted to him.
meaning.ar: الْحِرَاسَةُ وَالْحِفْظُ — وَالْحَفِيظُ: الَّذِي يَحْرُسُ الشَّيْءَ وَيَمْنَعُهُ مِنَ الْفَوْتِ

al_raghib.ar: الْحِفْظُ: حِرَاسَةُ الشَّيْءِ مِنَ الضَّيَاعِ. وَالرَّبُّ حَفِيظٌ — يَحْفَظُ عَبْدَهُ مِنَ الْبَلَاءِ
al_raghib.en: Ḥifẓ: guarding something from loss. The Lord is Ḥafīẓ — He guards His servant from affliction.

quran_examples.ar: إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ يُدَٰفِعُ عَنِ ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوٓا۟ ۗ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ لَا يُحِبُّ كُلَّ خَوَّانٍ كَفُورٍ
quran_examples.en: Allah defends those who believe; He does not love the treacherous, ungrateful

hadith.ar: اِحْفَظْ اللَّهَ يَحْفَظْكَ، اِحْفَظْ اللَّهَ تَجِدْهُ تُجَاهَكَ
hadith.en: Guard Allah — He will guard you. Guard Allah — you will find Him before you.

shades.name_en: Ḥifẓ Allāh — Divine Preservation of Faith, Soul, and Quran
shades.name_ar: حِفْظُ اللَّهِ — حِرَاسَةُ الدِّينِ وَالرُّوحِ وَالْكِتَابِ
shades.explanation:
The ḥifẓ (preservation) of Allah is one of the most beautiful of divine attributes. The Quran describes Allah as al-Ḥafīẓ (the Preserver — 4:135, 11:57, 34:21, 42:9) — the One who watches over all things, guards them from corruption, and preserves them from going astray. The verse 11:57 — «inn Allāh yudāfiʿu ʿani lladhīna āmanū» — uses the related root (d-f-ʿ) but the underlying concept is the same: Allah actively defends and protects those who believe.

The Quran emphasizes three dimensions of divine ḥifẓ. (1) The preservation of the Quran itself: «innā naḥnu nazzalnā l-dhikra wa-innā lahu la-ḥāfiẓūn» (We sent down the Reminder — the Quran — and We are its Preservers — 15:9). This verse is the strongest statement of textual preservation in any scripture. The Quran — the word of Allah — has been preserved by Allah Himself from textual corruption, from collective forgetfulness, from interpretive manipulation. Every copy of the Quran, in every age, in every place, contains the same words as were revealed to the Prophet ﷺ — a unique phenomenon among sacred texts. (2) The preservation of the believing soul: «wa-Allāhu yaḥfaẓuka min al-nās» (Allah will guard you from the people — 5:67). The Prophet ﷺ was divinely protected throughout the Meccan period; the believers are similarly under divine protection (within the limits of taklīf and taqdīr). (3) The preservation of deeds: the recording angels preserve every deed, every word, every intention — «wa-in ʿalaykum la-shāhidīn» (and over you are witnesses — 82:10).

The Prophet's ︆ ḥadīth — «iḥfaẓ Allāh yaḥfaẓak» (guard Allah, He will guard you) — establishes the reciprocal aspect of ḥifẓ: the believer who guards his obligations to Allah (by preserving his religion, observing his prayers, protecting his honor) is himself preserved by Allah in turn. The ḥifẓ is not merely a passive protection but an active stewardship — both divine and human. The believer guards what is entrusted to him, and Allah guards the believer. The ḥifẓ of Allah is the greatest of all gifts — and it is given to those who themselves value preservation over destruction, faith over negligence, divine memory over worldly distraction.
shades.hadith_ar: اِحْفَظْ اللَّهَ يَحْفَظْكَ، اِحْفَظْ اللَّهَ تَجِدْهُ تُجَاهَكَ
shades.hadith_en: Guard Allah — He will guard you; guard Allah — you will find Him before you

meaning.en: To repent, turn back (to Allah); repentance, return. The root denotes the conscious act of turning away from sin and toward God. Tawba is the most hopeful concept in Islam — the door to which is always open.
meaning.ar: الرُّجُوعُ إِلَى اللَّهِ بِالنَّدَمِ عَلَى الْمَعْصِيَةِ وَالْإِقْلَاعِ عَنْهَا

al_raghib.ar: التَّوْبَةُ فِي اللُّغَةِ: الرُّجُوعُ. وَفِي الشَّرْعِ: الرُّجُوعُ إِلَى اللَّهِ مِنَ الذَّنْبِ — وَهُوَ يَقْتَضِي نَدَمَ الْقَلْبِ وَإِقْلَاعَ الْجَوَارِحِ
al_raghib.en: Tawba linguistically: return. In the law: returning to Allah from sin — requiring remorse of heart and cessation of action.

quran_examples.ar: فَتَلَقَّىٰٓ ءَادَمُ مِن رَّبِّهِۦ كَلِمَـٰتٍۢ فَتَابَ عَلَيْهِ ۚ إِنَّهُۥ هُوَ ٱلتَّوَّابُ ٱلرَّحِيمُ
quran_examples.en: Adam received words from his Lord, and He accepted his repentance; indeed He is the Accepting of Repentance, the Merciful
quran_examples.context: Adam's tawba — the first human repentance

hadith.ar: إِنَّ اللَّهَ عَزَّ وَجَلَّ يَبْسُطُ يَدَهُ بِاللَّيْلِ لِيَتُوبَ مُسِيءُ النَّهَارِ، وَيَبْسُطُ يَدَهُ بِالنَّهَارِ لِيَتُوبَ مُسِيءُ اللَّيْلِ
hadith.en: Allah extends His Hand by night that the sinner of the day may repent, and extends it by day that the sinner of the night may repent.

shades.name_en: Tawba — Repentance as the Door That Never Closes
shades.name_ar: التَّوْبَةُ — الرُّجُوعُ إِلَى اللَّهِ وَالْبَابُ الَّذِي لَا يُغْلَقُ
shades.explanation:
Tawba — repentance — is the most hopeful concept in the entire Islamic framework. The Quran presents Allah as al-Tawwāb (the Accepting of Repentance — 2:37, 2:128, 2:160, 9:118, 49:12, 60:4) and as al-Ghafūr (the All-Forgiving) and al-Raḥīm (the Merciful). The door of tawba is opened so widely that it cannot be closed except by the soul itself: the ḥadīth qudsī in Muslim 2759 — Allah extending His Hand day and night, calling sinners to repentance — is the most powerful statement of divine eagerness to forgive.

The Quran's teaching on tawba has three critical dimensions. (1) The conditions of valid tawba: sincere remorse (nadam), cessation from the sin (iqlā'), resolve not to return (ʿazm ʿalā l-muʿāda), and — when applicable — restoration of wronged rights (radd al-maẓālim). The mere verbal «astaghfiru Allāh» without these conditions is not enough — it must be a tawba of the whole being. (2) The timing of tawba: the door remains open as long as the soul is in the body — and even on the Day of Judgment for some, the limit being that the Sun has not yet risen from the West. The ḥadīth — «al-tawbātu maqbūlahun mā lam takhruj al-rūḥ» (repentance is accepted as long as the soul has not departed) — establishes the temporal limit. (3) The exceptions: there is no tawba for those who persist in disbelief until death approaches (4:18), for the munāfiqūn (hypocrites) in some interpretations, and for the sin of takdhīb (calling the truth a lie) after clear signs have been shown to the liar.

Al-Ghazālī (Iḥyāʾ, Book of Repentance) writes that tawba is the cornerstone of the spiritual life — the «gate of Islam» that all spiritual wayfarers must pass through. Without tawba, there is no genuine taubah (piety), no valid worship, no real progress. Every station of the spiritual path — from the lowest taubah to the highest maʿrifah — begins with the soul's conscious turning away from what displeases Allah and turning toward what pleases Him. The first surah revealed to the Prophet — al-ʿAlaq (96:1-5) — begins with creation and ends with teaching, but the verse 96:18 — «thumma la-tanāhirūna ʿalayhi muharāj» — warns against being held in contempt from worship due to arrogance. The cure for arrogance is tawba.
shades.hadith_ar: كُلُّ ابْنِ آدَمَ خَطَّاءٌ، وَخَيْرُ الْخَطَّائِينَ التَّوَّابُونَ
shades.en: Every son of Adam is a sinner, and the best of sinners are those who repent

meaning.en: Thing, matter; to will, intend. The root designates any existent or conceivable entity, and the divine will behind every matter.
meaning.ar: الْأَمْرُ وَالشَّأْنُ — وَالشَّيْءُ: كُلُّ مَوْجُودٍ أَوْ مُتَصَوَّرٍ، وَمَشِيئَةُ اللَّهِ هِيَ الْمُرَادَةُ

al_raghib.ar: الشَّيْءُ: يَقَعُ عَلَى كُلِّ مَوْجُودٍ — مَحْسُوسٍ أَوْ مَعْقُولٍ — وَيَقَعُ عَلَى مَا يَسْتَقْبِحُهُ الْعَقْلُ
al_raghib.en: Shay': applies to everything existent — perceived or intelligible — and to whatever the intellect considers reprehensible.

quran_examples.ar: وَلَا تَقُولَنَّ لِشَا۟ءٍ إِنِّى فَاعِلٌ ذَٰلِكَ غَدًا ۞ إِلَّآ أَن يَشَآءَ ٱللَّهُ
quran_examples.en: Never say of anything: I will do that tomorrow — unless Allah wills
quran_examples.context: The injunction to attach every intention to divine will

hadith.ar: كُونُوا عَلَى أَعْمَالِكُمْ، فَإِنِّي لَا أَسْتَطِيعُ أَنْ أَفْدِيَكُمْ مِنَ اللَّهِ شَيْئًا
hadith.en: Remain at your deeds — I cannot save you from Allah at all.

shades.name_en: Shay' and Mashīʾa — Divine Will and the Infinite Extent of Creation
shades.explanation:
Shay' — thing — is the most universal term in Arabic for any existent or conceivable entity. The Quran uses shay' to refer to God: «shay'un yashāʾ» (anything He wills — 9:39), and as a name for Allah Himself in Sufi theology. The semantic universality of shay' allows the Quran to make sweeping ontological claims: «wa-Allāhu bi-kulli shay'in muḥīṭ» (Allah encompasses all things — 4:126), «wa-Allāhu ʿalā kulli shay'in qadīr» (Allah is capable of all things — 2:20). In every such usage, shay' is the term that bridges the infinite and the particular.

The verb shāʾa (he willed) and its intensive form shāʾaʾa (he willed greatly) express the divine will — the attribute by which Allah determines what shall exist and what shall not. The mashīʾa (will) is the source of all creation, all command, all moral order. The Quran declares: «wa-mā tashāʾūna illā an yashā'a Allāh» (you do not will except that Allah wills — 81:29, 76:30). This is the foundation of Islamic predestination — the human will operates within the divine will, not independently of it.

The verb shāʾa is also applied to humans, but with crucial qualifications. Human willing is conditional and limited: «wa-mā tashāʾūna illā an yashā'a Allāh rabbu l-ʿālamīn» (you will not will except that Allah wills — 81:29). The mashīʾa al-bashariyyah (human will) is created (ḥāditha) and contingent (mumkinah); the mashīʾa al-ilāhiyyah (divine will) is eternal (qadīma) and necessary (wājiba). The ḥadīth of Umar b. al-Khaṭṭāb — «innī ʿamiltu aʿmālā kathīra, falam ughayyir Allāhu ʿalayya — innahu lā yughayyiru mā bi-qawmin ḥattā yughayyirū mā bi-anfusihim» — captures the moral complexity: human action is real, but its consequences are determined by divine will.
shades.hadith_ar: كُونُوا عَلَى أَعْمَالِكُمْ، فَإِنِّي لَا أَسْتَطِيعُ أَنْ أَفْدِيَكُمْ مِنَ اللَّهِ شَيْئًا
shades.hadith_en: Remain at your deeds — I cannot save you from Allah at all

meaning.en: Day, time of day, era. The root designates a temporal unit, a specific day (Yawm al-Qiyāmah, Yawm al-Jumuʿah), or an era/period.
meaning.ar: الزَّمَانُ الْمَعْلُومُ مِنْ طُلُوعِ الشَّمْسِ إِلَى غُرُوبِهَا أَوْ مَا يَقْرُبُ مِنْهُ — وَالْيَوْمُ: مُدَّةٌ زَمَانِيَّةٌ

al_raghib.ar: الْيَوْمُ: مِقْدَارٌ مِنَ الزَّمَانِ يَعُمُّ اللَّيْلَ وَالنَّهَارَ. وَيُسْتَعْمَلُ فِي مِقْدَارِ الزَّمَانِ الْقَلِيلِ
al_raghib.en: Yawm: a measure of time encompassing night and day. Used for both brief and extended durations.

quran_examples.ar: مَـٰلِكِ يَوْمِ ٱلدِّينِ
quran_examples.en: Master of the Day of Judgment

hadith.ar: إِنَّ مَعَ الْعُسْرِ يُسْرًا
hadith.en: Indeed with hardship comes ease

shades.name_en: Yawm al-Qiyāmah — The Day of Resurrection, Judgment, and Final Accountability
shades.name_ar: يَوْمُ الْقِيَامَةِ — يَوْمُ الْبَعْثِ وَالْحِسَابِ وَالْجَزَاءِ
shades.explanation:
The yawm (day) concept in the Quran encompasses both literal days and symbolic epochs. The yawm al-dunyā is the day of this world; the yawm al-ākhirah is the day of the Hereafter. The yawm al-qiyāmah (Day of Resurrection — 2:85, 3:77, 4:87, and many others) is the supreme day — when all of humanity will be resurrected and judged. The yawm al-dīn (Day of Judgment — 1:4, 2:174, 4:109, 5:64) is the day of reckoning. The yawm al-waʿid (Day of Promise — 13:31, 18:98) is the day of the fulfilled promise. Each of these names emphasizes a different aspect of the same eschatological climax.

The yawm in the Quranic narrative is also the unit of moral testing. The yawm al-jumuʿah (Friday) — though the term itself appears only once in the Quran (62:9) — became the weekly gathering for the Muslim community. The yawm al-ʿāshūrā (10th of Muharram) — established by the Prophet as a day of fasting — is mentioned indirectly in hadith. The yawm al-nahr (Day of Sacrifice — 22:28, 108:2) is the day of Hajj rites. Each of these days has moral weight — what is done on them is multiplied in divine reward.

The Quran's most striking use of yawm is in the eschatological yawm al-qiyāmah: «yawma yaqūmu l-nāsu li-rabbi l-ʿālamīn» (the Day when mankind will stand before the Lord of the Worlds — 83:6). The standing (qiyām) is the universal posture — no kneeling, no bargaining, no exceptions. The yawm of standing is the longest day in human experience (the equivalent of 50,000 years of worldly time — 70:4), and yet the divine judgment is so efficient that it will be completed in the time it takes to slaughter a camel. The yawm of qiyāmah is the moment when all divine promises are fulfilled, all divine threats realized, and every soul receives the recompense it has earned — a yawm whose duration is, paradoxically, both infinitely long (for the wretched) and infinitely brief (for the blessed).
shades.hadith_ar: إِنَّ مَعَ الْعُسْرِ يُسْرًا
shades.en: Indeed with hardship comes ease

meaning.en: Pain, suffering, torment; punishment. The root encompasses both physical pain and spiritual suffering, and the divine punishment of evil.
meaning.ar: الْأَلَمُ الشَّدِيدُ — وَالْعَذَابُ: كُلُّ مُؤْلِمٍ يُعَذَّبُ بِهِ

al_raghib.ar: الْعَذَابُ: كُلُّ مُؤْلِمٍ يُعَذَّبُ بِهِ — وَهُوَ خَاصٌّ بِالضَّرَرِ الْمُتَوَجِّهِ إِلَى الْمُعَذَّبِ
al_raghib.en: ʿAdhāb: every painful thing by which one is tormented — specifically, harm directed at the one being punished.

quran_examples.ar: إِنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ يَشْتَرُونَ بِعَهْدِ ٱللَّهِ وَأَيْمَـٰنِهِمْ ثَمَنًۭا قَلِيلًا أُو۟لَـٰٓئِكَ لَا خَلَـٰقَ لَهُمْ فِى ٱلْـَٔاخِرَةِ وَلَا يُكَلِّمُهُمُ ٱللَّهُ وَلَا يَنظُرُ إِلَيْهِمْ يَوْمَ ٱلْقِيَـٰمَةِ وَلَا يُزَكِّيهِمْ وَلَهُمْ عَذَابٌ أَلِيمٌ
quran_examples.en: Those who sell God's covenant and their oaths for a small price — no share for them in the Hereafter, Allah will not speak to them, look at them, or purify them on the Day of Resurrection, and they will have a painful punishment

hadith.ar: مَنْ غَشَّنَا فَلَيْسَ مِنَّا
hadith.en: Whoever deceives us is not of us

shades.name_en: ʿAdhāb — Divine Punishment as Justice and Warning
shades.explanation:
ʿAdhāb — punishment, torment — is one of the most frequently mentioned Quranic themes, reflecting the divine attribute of al-Muntaqim (the Avenger) and al-Muʿaddib (the Disciplinarian). The Quran presents punishment in multiple forms: worldly punishment (ʿadhāb al-dunyā) — through floods, earthquakes, plagues, military defeat, and other disasters; eschatological punishment (ʿadhāb al-ākhirah) — in the grave, on the Day of Resurrection, and eternally in Hellfire; and intermediate forms (ʿadhāb bayn) — the testing pains of life.

The Quran's most cited description of punishment is ʿadhābun alīm (painful punishment) — appearing in nearly 100 verses. The alīm (painful) is an intensive form indicating intensity and persistence — the punishment that does not merely hurt but causes enduring pain. The muṣīr (pain-causing), ḥadīd (severe), and alīm (painful) describe the qualitative dimension of the ʿadhāb — it is not merely punishment but torture, not merely justice but absolute suffering. The Quran also uses muḥīn (humiliating — 2:90, 3:178, 5:33, 6:124, 9:2), khālid (eternal — many verses), and muqīm (permanent) — emphasizing that the ʿadhāb of the Hereafter is not time-limited.

The relationship between divine ʿadhāb and divine mercy is the central paradox of the Quranic worldview. The verse 30:36 — «wa-idhā awḥaynā ilā Ummi Mūsā an arḍiʿīhi fa-idhā khifti ʿalayhi fa-alqīhi fī l-yammi wa-lā takhāfī wa-lā taḥzanī inna rāduhu ilayka wa-jāʿiluhu min al-mursalīn» — combines ʿadhāb and raḥma: the mother's fear (ʿadhāb) and the divine plan (raḥma). The same divine attribute that punishes wrongdoers sustains the righteous. Al-Ghazālī argues that the ʿadhāb is not cruelty but justice — punishment is the response to a soul's insistence on wrongdoing, and the soul's insistence on wrongdoing is itself the soul's rejection of the mercy it could have embraced. The ʿadhāb is what the soul creates for itself by refusing what it could have received.
shades.hadith_ar: مَنْ غَشَّنَا فَلَيْسَ مِنَّا
shades.en: Whoever deceives us is not of us

meaning.en: All, every, entire, whole. The root denotes totality, comprehensiveness. As a particle, kull (every, all) is among the most frequent and significant words in the Quran.
meaning.ar: الْإِحَاطَةُ وَالشُّمُولُ — وَكُلُّ: اسْمُ اسْتِغْرَاقٍ يَتَضَمَّنُ الْجَمِيعَ

al_raghib.ar: كُلُّ: لَفْظٌ مُفْرَدٌ لَفْظًا جَامِعٌ مَعْنًى، يَدْخُلُ تَحْتَهُ الْأَشْخَاصُ كَافَّةً
al_raghib.en: Kull: singular in form but universal in meaning — encompassing all individual instances.

quran_examples.ar: وَسِعَ كُرْسِيُّهُ ٱلسَّمَـٰوَٰتِ وَٱلْأَرْضَ
quran_examples.en: His Throne encompasses the heavens and the earth

hadith.ar: إِنَّمَا بُعِثْتُ لِأُتَمِّمَ مَكَارِمَ الْأَخْلَاقِ
hadith.en: I was sent only to perfect noble character.

shades.name_en: Kull — Comprehensiveness and the Unity of All Things in Allah
shades.explanation:
The word kull (all, every) is a foundational term in Quranic ontology and ethics. Its semantic function is universal quantification — it binds any predicate to every instance of its subject. The Quran uses kull in three primary ways: (1) Divine omniscience and power: «Allāhu ʿalā kulli shay'in qadīr» (Allah is capable of all things — 2:20, 2:106, 3:29, and many others). (2) Human responsibility: «kullu nafsin dhā'iqatu l-mawt» (every soul shall taste death — 3:185, 21:35, 29:57). (3) Theodic statement of universal truth: «kullun qad ʿalima ṣalātahu wa-tasbīḥahu» (all — meaning each — knew its prayer and its glorification — 24:41).

The kull concept is theologically central: Allah's knowledge encompasses «kullu shay'» (all things — 6:59, 10:61, 11:123), His power extends to «kullu shay'» (all things — 2:259, 3:109, 8:70), His will encompasses «kullu shay'» (all things — 35:1). The divine kulliyyāt (universals) include qadar (decree), 'ilm (knowledge), ḥayāt (life), qudrah (power), and raḥma (mercy). Every attribute of Allah is described as «kullī» (universal) — not exclusive to certain moments or contexts. This divine universality grounds the Islamic concept of tawḥīd: there is no corner of existence, no category of reality, that falls outside Allah's sovereignty.

The Quran's ethical use of kull establishes moral universality. «Kullukum mas'ūlun ʿan ra'iyatihim» (each of you is responsible for his charge — hadith) parallels the Quranic «wa-kullun ātinīhi yawma l-qiyāmati fardan» (and each will come to Him on the Day of Resurrection alone — 19:95). The kullī responsibility that arises from universal divine kulliyyāt: if Allah knows all things and all are accountable, then no human act escapes moral notice. The kull concept thus bridges metaphysics and ethics — what is universally true about God becomes the foundation for what is universally required of the servant.
shades.hadith_ar: كُلُّكُمْ رَاعٍ وَكُلُّكُمْ مَسْئُولٌ عَنْ رَعِيَّتِهِ
shades.en: Each of you is a shepherd, and each is responsible for his flock

meaning.en: To act, to work, to do; action, deed, work. The root designates any intentional human act — physical, verbal, or spiritual. The ʿamal (deed) is the moral unit that determines one's eternal fate.
meaning.ar: فِعْلُ الشَّيْءِ بِقَصْدٍ وَاخْتِيَارٍ — وَالْعَمَلُ: مَا فَعَلَهُ الْإِنْسَانُ مِنْ خَيْرٍ أَوْ شَرٍّ

al_raghib.ar: الْعَمَلُ: شَمِلَ لِكُلِّ فِعْلٍ يَفْعَلُهُ الْإِنْسَانُ مِنْ جَوَارِحِهِ — وَلِكُلِّ فِعْلِ قَلْبٍ. وَكُلُّ عَمَلٍ فَإِنَّمَا يُسَمَّى عَمَلًا بِالنِّسْبَةِ إِلَى مَنْ يَفْعَلُهُ
al_raghib.en: ʿAmal: includes every act of human faculties — and every act of the heart. Every act is named ʿamal in relation to the one who performs it.

quran_examples.ar: فَمَن يَعْمَلْ مِثْقَالَ ذَرَّةٍ خَيْرًۭا يَرَهُۥ
quran_examples.en: Whoever does an atom's weight of good will see it

hadith.ar: إِنَّ اللَّهَ لَا يَنْظُرُ إِلَى أَعْمَالِكُمْ وَلَا إِلَى صُوَرِكُمْ، وَلَكِنْ يَنْظُرُ إِلَى قُلُوبِكُمْ
hadith.en: Allah does not look at your deeds or your forms; He looks at your hearts.

shades.name_en: ʿAmal — Action as the Test of Faith and the Currency of Eternity
shades.explanation:
ʿAmal — action — is the test of īmān (faith) and the currency of eternity. The Quran's theology of ʿamal has three foundational statements. (1) The pairing of īmān wa-ʿamal (faith and action): «wa-l-ʿaṣr, inna l-insāna la-fī khusr, illa lladhīna āmanū wa-ʿamilū l-ṣāliḥāti» (by time, mankind is in loss, except those who believe and do righteous deeds — 103:1-3). The faith that does not produce action is not the īmān that saves. (2) The ʿamal as basis for recompense: «wa-tilka l-jannatu l-latī ūrithtumūhā bimā kuntum taʿmalūn» (and this is the Paradise you inherited for what you used to do — 43:72). The ʿamal is what earns the reward. (3) The ʿamal as basis for moral status: «wa-li-kulli darajātun mimmā ʿamilū» (and for each are degrees according to what they did — 6:132, 46:19). The ʿamal determines one's station in the Hereafter.

The categories of ʿamal in the Quran are extensive and varied. Al-Rāghib identifies the major types: ʿamal al-ṣāliḥ (righteous deeds — 2:62, 18:110), ʿamal al-khayr (good deeds — 3:114), ʿamal al-sayyi' (evil deeds — 2:180), ʿamal al-fāsid (corrupt deeds — 6:18), ʿamal al-mubarrir (deeds that justify — 2:48), ʿamal al-ṣāliḥ al-mutabaqī (abiding righteous deeds — 18:46). Each category implies a specific moral state — and the same external act can belong to different categories depending on the niyyah (intention) of the doer.

The hadīth of the Prophet ﷺ — «innamā l-aʿmālu bi-l-niyyāt wa-innamā li-kulli imri'in mā nawā» (actions are but by intentions, and every man shall have only that which he intended — Bukhārī 1) — establishes the niyyah as the spiritual dimension of every ʿamal. An ʿamal without niyyah is invalid for the Hereafter; an ʿamal with the correct niyyah is the highest of deeds. The ḥadīth of Miqdad — the riqq (slave-girl) whom he was ordered to free and who would be of the people of Hellfire if she did not fast, pray, and give charity — demonstrates that the niyyah-driven acts of ordinary people are the foundations of Paradise.
shades.hadith_ar: إِنَّمَا الْأَعْمَالُ بِالنِّيَّاتِ
shades.en: Actions are but by intentions

meaning.en: Command, order; matter, affair; affair (state, condition). The root encompasses divine command, human ordering, and the situation/condition of things.
meaning.ar: الطَّلَبُ بِتَرَجِّيحٍ — وَالْأَمْرُ: الطَّلَبُ بِصُورَةِ الْوَجْهِ، وَالشَّأْنُ: الْحَالُ الَّتِي يَكُونُ عَلَيْهَا الشَّيْءُ

al_raghib.ar: الْأَمْرُ: الطَّلَبُ عَلَى وُجُوهِ الِاسْتِفَاضَةِ. وَيُسْتَعْمَلُ فِي الْمَعْقُولِ — كَقَوْلِكَ: أَمَرْتُهُ فَأَطَاعَ — وَيَدْخُلُ فِي الْأَفْعَالِ الْمَحْسُوسَةِ وَالْمَعْنَوِيَّةِ
al_raghib.en: Amr: the request/demand at the level of imperativeness. Used for intelligible — and for physical and non-physical actions.

quran_examples.ar: وَمَن يَتَوَكَّلْ عَلَى ٱللَّهِ فَهُوَ حَسْبُهُۥٓ ۚ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ بَـٰلِغُ أَمْرِهِۦ
quran_examples.en: Whoever relies on Allah — He is sufficient for him. Indeed Allah accomplishes His command

hadith.ar: إِنَّمَا أُمِرْتُ أَنْ أُقَاتِلَ النَّاسَ حَتَّى يَقُولُوا لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا اللَّهُ
hadith.en: I have been commanded to fight people until they say: there is no god but Allah.

shades.name_en: Amr Allāh — The Divine Command that Accomplishes All Things
shades.name_ar: أَمْرُ اللَّهِ — الْأَمْرُ الْكَوْنِيُّ الَّذِي لَا يُعْجِزُهُ شَيْءٌ
shades.explanation:
The amr (command, matter) of Allah is one of the most fundamental theological concepts in the Quran. The verse 65:3 — «inn Allāha bālighun amrihi» (Allah accomplishes His command) — captures the certainty and efficacy of the divine command. The verb amara in its various forms appears throughout the Quran with four primary usages: (1) amr takwīnī (creative command) — the command that brings existence into being; (2) amr tashrīʿī (legislative command) — the command that establishes law; (3) amr ḥukmī (judicial command) — the command that judges and decides; (4) amr sha'nī (informational) — used as a substitute for shay' to refer to any matter or affair.

The contrast between divine amr and human amr is significant. The amr of Allah is always accomplished: «wa-idhā amarnā imra'an fa-innamā yaqūlu lahu kun fa-yakūn» (when We command a matter, We only say to it: Be, and it is — 4:18, 16:40, 36:82, 40:68). The human amr is dependent: «wa-mā umīrū illā li-yaʿbudū Allāha mukhliṣīna lahu l-dīna» (they were not commanded except to worship Allah, sincerely devoting religion to Him — 98:5). The human's amr (command) is itself a participation in, and submission to, the divine Amr. The believer does not «command» — they «are commanded.» The istikbār (arrogance) of Pharaoh («anā rabbukum al-aʿlā» — I am your highest lord — 79:24) is the ultimate inversion: the human claiming to be the commander instead of the commanded.

The amr concept extends to the ummah's collective life. Al-amr bi-l-maʿrūf (commanding good) and al-nahy ʿan al-munkar (forbidding evil) — mentioned in 3:104, 3:110, 9:71, 9:112, 31:17, 22:41 — is the collective ummah's amr. The Prophet's mission was fundamentally a mission of commanding: «innamā buʿithtu li-utammima makārima l-akhlāq» (I was sent only to perfect noble character — related hadith). The Muslim's life is a continuous amr wa-nahy — both internally (self-discipline, dhikr, vigilance) and externally (calling to good, preventing evil). The amr of the ummah is the most noble of human commands because it is participation in the divine Amr.
shades.hadith_ar: إِنَّمَا أُمِرْتُ أَنْ أُقَاتِلَ النَّاسَ حَتَّى يَقُولُوا لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا اللَّهُ
shades.en: I have been commanded to fight people until they say: there is no god but Allah

meaning.en: To forgive, cover, pardon. The root's physical meaning (covering something to protect it) extends to the divine covering of sin — protecting the sinner from the consequences of his sin.
meaning.ar: السَّتْرُ وَالتَّغْطِيَةُ — وَالْمَغْفِرَةُ: سَتْرُ الذَّنْبِ وَالتَّجَاوُزُ عَنْ عُقُوبَتِهِ

al_raghib.ar: الْمَغْفِرَةُ وَالْغُفْرَانُ: عِبَارَةٌ عَنْ سَتْرِ الذَّنْبِ وَالتَّجَاوُزِ عَنِ الْعِقَابِ. وَأَصْلُهُ الْغِطَاءُ
al_raghib.en: Maghfira and ghufrān: denoting the covering of sin and overlooking its punishment. The origin is the covering.

quran_examples.ar: ٱللَّهُ لَآ إِلَـٰهَ إِلَّا هُوَ ٱلْحَىُّ ٱلْقَيُّومُ ۚ لَا تَأْخُذُهُۥ سِنَةٌۭ وَلَا نَوْمٌۭ ۚ لَّهُۥ مَا فِى ٱلسَّمَـٰوَٰتِ وَمَا فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ ۗ مَن ذَا ٱلَّذِى يَشْفَعُ عِندَهُۥٓ إِلَّا بِإِذْنِهِۦ ۚ يَعْلَمُ مَا بَيْنَ أَيْدِيهِمْ وَمَا خَلْفَهُمْ ۖ وَلَا يُحِيطُونَ بِشَىْءٍۢ مِّنْ عِلْمِهِۦٓ إِلَّا بِمَا شَآءَ ۚ وَسِعَ كُرْسِيُّهُ ٱلسَّمَـٰوَٰتِ وَٱلْأَرْضَ ۖ وَلَا يَـُٔودُهُۥ حِفْظُهُمَا ۚ وَهُوَ ٱلْعَلِىُّ ٱلْعَظِيمُ
quran_examples.en: Allah — there is no god but He — the Ever-Living... His Throne encompasses the heavens and earth...
quran_examples.context: Divine preservation and knowledge — paired with forgiveness

hadith.ar: لَوْ لَمْ تُذْنِبُوا لَذَهَبَ اللَّهُ بِكُمْ وَلَجَاءَ بِقَوْمٍ يُذْنِبُونَ ثُمَّ يَسْتَغْفِرُونَ اللَّهَ فَيَغْفِرُ لَهُمْ
hadith.en: If you did not sin, Allah would take you away and replace you with a people who would sin and then seek forgiveness, and He would forgive them.

shades.name_en: al-Ghafūr al-Ghafār — The All-Forgiving and the Ever-Forgiving
shades.name_ar: الْغَفُورُ الْغَفَّارُ — اسْمَانِ مِنْ أَسْمَاءِ اللَّهِ الْحُسْنَى
shades.explanation:
Al-Ghafūr al-Ghafār — the All-Forgiving and the Ever-Forgiving — are paired divine names from the Asmāʾ al-Ḥusná (Ninety-Nine Names of Allah). Their appearance in the Quran (al-Ghafūr 91 times, al-Ghafār 4 times) reflects the theological centrality of divine forgiveness. The pair — Ghafūr (forgiving intensely) and Ghafār (forgiving constantly) — captures two dimensions of the divine quality: al-Ghafūr emphasizes the absolute, complete nature of the forgiveness; al-Ghafār emphasizes the continuous, ever-renewed nature. The forgiveness of Allah is not a one-time act but an eternal reality — His nature is to cover sin, to overlook transgression, to protect the sinner from punishment.

The Quran's most distinctive teaching on ghufrān is the universal scope of divine forgiveness. The verse 4:110 — «wa-man yaʿmal sū'an aw yaẓlim nafsahu thumma yastaghfiri Allāh yajidi Allāha ghafūran raḥīmā» (whoever does evil or wrongs himself and then seeks forgiveness of Allah — he will find Allah Forgiving and Merciful) — establishes the accessibility of forgiveness for every sinner. The condition is tawba (repentance) — not perfection. The hadith of the man who killed 99 people and asked a monk for forgiveness (only to be told there is no way), but then met another monk who told him to relocate to a good town, and died on the way, the angels debating his fate — and finally being brought closer to the good town — is one of the most powerful demonstrations of the boundless divine ghufrān.

The relationship between ghfr (forgiveness) and taubah (repentance) is intimate but distinct. Taubah is the human act — turning from sin toward God. Ghufrān is the divine act — covering the sin once the human turns. The verse 4:18 — «wa-mā kāna Allāhu li-yuḍīʿa ummahā baʿda idh dahābā hādatā Allāh ghafūrun raḥīm» — places ghufrān within the divine scheme: after He guides, He forgives those who err; the system is sequential and merciful. Al-Ghazālī (Iḥyāʾ, Book of Repentance) argues that ghfr is the final divine act that «covers» the sinner's past, allowing for new growth. The ghufrān is the divine response to the human's istighfār — the human's plea for covering, and the divine gift of it.
shades.hadith_ar: إِنَّ اللَّهَ يَقْبَلُ تَوْبَةَ الْعَبْدِ مَا لَمْ يُغْرِغْرْ
shades.en: Allah accepts the repentance of the servant as long as the soul has not reached the throat

meaning.en: To be close, befriend, protect, manage. The walī (guardian, friend, patron) is one who undertakes the care and protection of another.
meaning.ar: الْقُرْبُ وَالْمَحَبَّةُ — وَالْوَلِيُّ: مَنْ يَلِي الشَّيْءَ وَيَقُومُ بِأَمْرِهِ

al_raghib.ar: الْوَلِيُّ: الَّذِي يَلِيكَ الشَّيْءَ أَيْ يَمْلِكُ أَمْرَهُ. وَهُوَ عَلَى الثَّلَاثَةِ أَضْرُبِ: الْمَالِكُ، وَالنَّاصِرُ، وَالْمُتَوَلِّي الشَّأْنَ بِإِصْلَاحِهِ
al_raghib.en: Walī: the one who manages something — i.e., owns its command. Three forms: owner, helper, and manager (tending to its affairs).

quran_examples.ar: ٱللَّهُ وَلِىُّ ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوا۟ يُخْرِجُهُم مِّنَ ٱلظُّلُمَـٰتِ إِلَى ٱلنُّورِ
quran_examples.en: Allah is the walī (guardian) of those who believe; He brings them out of darkness into light
quran_examples.context: Divine walāya — the foundation of the believer's security

hadith.ar: الْمُؤْمِنُ لِلْمُؤْمِنِ كَالْبُنْيَانِ يَدْعُمُ بَعْضُهُ بَعْضًا
hadith.en: The believer to the believer is like a building — each part supports the others.

shades.name_en: Walāya — Divine Protection and Human Brotherhood in Faith
shades.name_ar: الْوَلَايَةُ — حِفْظُ اللَّهِ لِلْمُؤْمِنِينَ وَتَوَاصُلُهُمْ فِي الْإِيمَانِ
shades.explanation:
Walāya — the state of being walī — is the Quran's term for both divine guardianship and human brotherhood in faith. The verse 2:257 — «Allāhu waliyyu lladhīna āmanū, yukhrijuhum mina l-ẓulumāti ilā l-nūr» (Allah is the walī of those who believe; He brings them out of darkness into light) — establishes walāya as the divine mode of relating to the believers. The walāya is not merely friendship or affection — it is the comprehensive protection, support, and care that characterizes the divine-human relationship.

The contrast in the Quran is between al-walī (the friend/guardian) and al-ʿadūww (the enemy): «kallā, inna l-insāna la-yatghā, an ra'āhu istagh'nā. inna ilayka ruj'ā (k)» — verses about the walī are paired with verses about the enemy in the great Quranic dialectic. The walī is one whose walāya brings light, life, freedom; the enemy is one whose ʿadāwa brings darkness, death, slavery. The believer must therefore choose: walī or enemy, friend or foe, light or darkness. There is no neutral ground.

The human walāya mirrors the divine walāya. The walī in human community is one who undertakes the care and protection of others — parents for children, teachers for students, leaders for communities. The walāya al-ʿaṣabiyyah (clan walāya) was the pre-Islamic form of human brotherhood, transformed by Islam into walāya al-īmān — brotherhood in faith. The verse 8:72 — «wa-l-awtāḥūna baʿḍuhum awliyā'u baʿḍ» (the emigrants and helpers are awliyāʾ of one another — 9:71, 8:72, 9:101) — establishes the ummah's structure: the muḥājirūn and anṣār are bonded as walīyyūn. The walāya of faith transcends the walāya of blood and is the foundation of the ummah's solidarity.
shades.hadith_ar: الْمُؤْمِنُ لِلْمُؤْمِنِ كَالْبُنْيَانِ يَدْعُمُ بَعْضُهُ بَعْضًا
shades.hadith_en: The believer to the believer is like a building — each part supports the others

meaning.en: Garden (jannah, jannat); to cover, hide; jinn (the created beings of subtle fire). The root's three semantic branches — garden, hidden being, and concealment — are united by the concept of that which is covered or hidden.
meaning.ar: الْجَنَّةُ: الْبُسْتَانُ الَّذِي تَجِنُّهُ الْأَشْجَارُ — سُمِّيَتْ جَنَّةً لِأَنَّهَا تُجِنُّ، أَيْ تُسْتَتِرُ وَتُوارِي. وَالْجِنُّ: مَا اسْتَتَرَ مِنَ الْعُقُولِ

al_raghib.ar: الْجَنَّةُ: كُلُّ بُسْتَانٍ ذَاتِ شَجَرٍ يُسْتَتَرُ بِشَجَرِهِ. وَالْجِنُّ: الْخَلْقُ الْمُسْتَتِرُ عَنِ الْحَوَاسِّ. وَالْجَنِينُ: الْحَمْلُ — لِاسْتِتَارِهِ
al_raghib.en: Jannah: any orchard whose trees conceal what is inside. Jinn: beings hidden from the senses. Janīn: the embryo (because it is concealed).

quran_examples.ar: وَقُلْنَا يَـٰٓـَٔادَمُ ٱسْكُنْ أَنتَ وَزَوْجُكَ ٱلْجَنَّةَ
quran_examples.en: We said: O Adam, dwell — you and your wife — in the Garden

hadith.ar: لَا تَقُولَنَّ الْعِنَبُ الْكَرْمَ، فَإِنَّ الْكَرْمَ قَلْبُ الْمُؤْمِنِ
hadith.en: Do not call grapes al-karm — al-karm is the heart of the believer.

shades.name_en: Jannah — Paradise as Garden and the Supreme Reward
shades.explanation:
Jannah — Paradise — is the Quran's most evocative image of divine reward. The word's etymology from j-n-n (to cover, hide) suggests that the jannah is a «covered garden» — its trees concealing what is within, creating an environment of beauty hidden from human eyes. The Quran describes multiple jannāt: al-jannatu al-ʿadn (the Garden of Eden — 9:72, 13:23, 16:31, 18:31, 19:61, 20:76, 35:33, 38:50, 40:8, 43:77, 46:14, 53:15, 54:55, 61:12, 98:8), al-jannatu al-firdaws (the Garden of Paradise — 18:107, 23:11), al-jannatu al-naʿīm (the Garden of Bliss — 5:65, 10:9, 22:56, 26:85, 37:43, 56:12, 68:34, 73:11), al-darru l-ākhira (the Abode of the Hereafter — 28:77, 29:64), and many others. Each designation emphasizes a different aspect of the supreme reward.

The jannah is characterized by the Quran in terms of what is in it. The hadīth of the Prophet ﷺ lists its delights: «it has the pleasures the eye has not seen, the ear has not heard, and what the mind has not imagined» — but the Quran itself gives concrete imagery. Rivers of water, milk, wine (non-intoxicating), and honey (47:15). Fruits that never fail (13:35), spouses of pure beauty (44:54, 52:20), garments of silk and brocade (22:23, 18:31, 35:33), thrones of gold and silver (18:31, 22:23, 43:71), and most importantly — the vision of Allah (the supreme reward).

The deepest meaning of jannah is its etymology: it is a «garden of covering» — a realm where the soul is hidden (mustatir) from the anxieties, sorrows, and limitations of earthly life. The jannah's gardens cover (tajinn) the soul in a way the dunyā's gardens cannot. Al-Ghazālī (Iḥyāʾ, Book of Hope) notes that the jannah is so named because it is concealed (mastūr) from the eyes of the present world — it is the unseen (al-ghayb) that awaits. The jannah is not merely a place but a state of being — the state of being fully covered by Allah's mercy, fully guarded by Allah's power, fully satisfied by Allah's nearness. The jannah is Paradise not because of what it has but because of who is there: Allah, the One for whom the souls of the saints yearned (h-n-n) all their lives.
shades.hadith_ar: أُفُقُوا الْجَنَّةَ كُلَّ يَوْمٍ وَلَوْ بِشَقِّ تَمْرَةٍ
shades.en: Receive Paradise every day, even if only by giving half a date in charity

meaning.en: At, near, in the presence of; the proximity that implies favor. The ʿind (at) emphasizes presence and proximity — particularly the proximity of Allah to His servants.
meaning.ar: الْقُرْبُ وَالْمُجَاوَرَةُ — وَالْعِنْدُ: ظَرْفُ مَكَانٍ أَوْ مَقَامٍ يَدُلُّ عَلَى الْقُرْبِ وَالْمَجَاوَرَةِ

al_raghib.ar: الْعِنْدُ: ظَرْفُ مَكَانٍ يَقْتَضِي الْمُجَاوَرَةَ. وَعِنْدَ اللَّهِ: حَقِيقَةٌ بِإِزَائِهِ
al_raghib.en: ʿInd: a spatial expression implying proximity. ʿInda Allāh: real, in His presence.

quran_examples.ar: وَإِذَا سَأَلَكَ عِبَادِى عَنِّى فَإِنِّى قَرِيبٌ
quran_examples.en: When My servants ask about Me — indeed I am near

hadith.ar: إِنَّكُمْ سَتَرَوْنَ رَبَّكُمْ كَمَا تَرَوْنَ هَٰذَا الْقَمَرَ
hadith.en: You will see your Lord as you see this moon

shades.name_en: ʿInda Allāh — What is with Allah, in the Divine Presence
shades.name_ar: عِنْدَ اللَّهِ — الْحَقِيقَةُ الْمَوْجُودَةُ عِنْدَ اللَّهِ
shades.explanation:
The phrase ʿinda Allāh (with Allah, in Allah's presence) is among the most theologically weighty expressions in the Quran. What is ʿinda Allāh is what is, in the most real sense, with Allah — established in His knowledge, will, and judgment. The verse 3:32 — «qul in kuntum tuḥibbūna Allāha fa-ttabiʿūnī yughabbir lakum Allāh wa-yaghfir lakum, wa-Llāhu ghafūrun raḥīm» — establishes ʿinda Allāh as the standard of value. What is ʿinda Allāh is what endures; what is ʿinda al-nās (with people) is transient. The mufassirūn (exegetes) explain: «ʿind Allāh aḥaqq» — what is with Allah is the truest reality.

The phrase ʿindahu (with him) appears in numerous Quranic contexts: «wa-lladhīna yūtūna mā ātaw wa-qulūbuhum wajilatun annahum ilā rabbihim rājiʿūn» (those who give what they give while their hearts are fearful — 23:60). The verses about ʿindahu describe the spiritual state of those who give without expectation of return — they act in fear of meeting their Lord, giving in hope of reward ʿindahu (with Him). The akhira's reality is established in the realm of ʿindahu — what is preserved with Allah endures beyond all earthly transience.

The hadīth in Bukhārī 554 — «innakum sa-tarawna rabbakum kamā tarawna hādhā l-qamar, lā tuḍāmmūna fī ru'yatihi» — extends the ʿinda concept to the ultimate encounter. The believers will see (ru'ya) their Lord as they see the moon — the vision that takes place ʿindahu (with Him, in His presence) is the highest jannah reward. The ʿinda concept thus becomes the place where all divine promises converge: the believer will be brought near to ʿinda Allāh — to the presence of the One who is closer to him than his jugular vein (50:16). The ʿindahu is the final destination of the soul's journey, the ultimate qurb (nearness).
shades.hadith_ar: سَبَقَتْ رَحْمَتِي عَصَبِي
shades.en: My mercy has preceded My wrath

meaning.en: Light, illumination; to be luminous, to shine. The root denotes that which makes manifest — and metaphorically, the divine guidance that reveals truth.
meaning.ar: الضِّيَاءُ الْمُشْرِقُ — وَالنُّورُ: مَا يَظْهَرُ بِهِ الشَّيْءُ، وَهُوَ ضِدُّ الظُّلْمَةِ

al_raghib.ar: النُّورُ: الظُّهُورُ وَالظَّهَارَةُ. وَالْإِنَارَةُ: إِيقَاظُ النُّورِ
al_raghib.en: Nūr: manifestation and clarity. Ināra: to kindle/bring forth light.

quran_examples.ar: ٱللَّهُ نُورُ ٱلسَّمَـٰوَٰتِ وَٱلْأَرْضِ
quran_examples.en: Allah is the Light of the heavens and the earth

hadith.ar: أُنْزِلَ الْقُرْآنُ عَلَى سَبْعَةِ أَحْرُفٍ
hadith.en: The Quran was revealed in seven aḥruf (modes).

shades.name_en: Allāh Nūr al-Samāwāt wa-l-Arḍ — Divine Light as Self-Manifesting Reality
shades.name_ar: اللَّهُ نُورُ السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضِ — الظَّاهِرُ الذَّاتِ وَالْبَاطِنُ بِالْمَعْرِفَةِ
shades.explanation:
Nūr — light — is one of the most theologically consequential concepts in the Quran. The verse 24:35 — «Allāhu nūru l-samāwāti wa-l-arḍ» (Allah is the Light of the heavens and the earth) — is the apex of Quranic theology of light. The phrase «nūr al-samāwāti wa-l-arḍ» is not metaphorical — it is ontological. Allah's being is the light by which all else is illuminated; without His light, nothing in existence would be manifest. The āyah that follows — the parable of the niche (miṣbāḥ), the lamp (sirāj), the glass (zujāja), the tree (shajarah), the oil (zayt) — is the longest and most profound set of divine names and attributes in the Quran, the locus classicus of Sufi and kalām theology of light.

The hadith qudsī — recorded in Bukhārī and Muslim — establishes the qualitative dimension of divine nūr: «yā bni Ādam, hal laka fī shay'in mimmā khalaqtu? Man anaṣa' laka fīhi?» (O son of Adam, do you have any of My creation? Who has more right to wait for you than Me?). The nūr of Allah is not just intellectual illumination — it is the warmth of His presence, the love with which He draws His servant near, the mercy with which He surrounds the believer. The verse 2:257 — «Allāhu waliyyu lladhīna āmanū, yukhrijuhum min al-ẓulumāti ilā l-nūr» (Allah is the walī of those who believe — He brings them out of darkness into light) — frames salvation as a transition from ẓulm (darkness) to nūr (light). The ẓulm is the natural state of the disbeliever; the nūr is the state the believer enters through īmān.

The verses 5:15-16 — with the phrase «nūrun wa-kitābun mubīnun» (a light and a clear book — referring to the Quran) — establish the Quran itself as nūr. The Quranic revelations are āyāt al-nūr (signs of light), guiding the believer from the ẓulumāt (plural darknesses) to the nūr. The light of the Quran is not merely informational but transformative — it is the «nūr al-hudā» (light of guidance) that becomes part of the believer's heart (qalb). The ḥadīth describes the muʾminūn's light on the Day of Judgment as «nūr yumsī bihi» (a light with which they walk) — the same Quranic nūr, now visible as the fruit of faith. The nūr is thus the most comprehensive metaphor in the Quranic worldview: it is the divine essence, the prophetic revelation, the Qur'anic guidance, the spiritual light, and the eschatological reward — all unified in a single concept whose depths the human mind can never exhaust.
shades.hadith_ar: أُولَئِكَ الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا وَتَطْمَئِنُّ قُلُوبُهُمْ بِذِكْرِ اللَّهِ ۗ أَلَا بِذِكْرِ اللَّهِ تَطْمَئِنُّ الْقُلُوبُ
shades.hadith_en: Those who believe and whose hearts find rest in the remembrance of Allah — indeed, in the remembrance of Allah do hearts find rest

meaning.en: Good, better, best. The root denotes that which is objectively good and preferable. Al-khayr (goodness) is one of Allah's names — and the highest good is the pleasure of Allah.
meaning.ar: الْخَيْرُ ضِدُّ الشَّرِّ — وَهُوَ مَا يُطْلَبُ إِقَامُهُ لِمَا فِيهِ مِنَ الْمَنْفَعَةِ وَالسَّرُورِ

al_raghib.ar: الْخَيْرُ: الْمَطْلُوبُ نَفْعُهُ — بِخَلَافِ الشَّرِّ الْمَطْلُوبُ دَفْعُهُ. وَالْخَيْرُ مَصْدَرٌ
al_raghib.en: Khayr: that whose benefit is sought — unlike shar (evil) whose harm is to be repelled. Khayr is a verbal noun.

quran_examples.ar: وَعَسَىٰٓ أَن تَكْرَهُوا۟ شَيْـًۭا وَهُوَ خَيْرٌۭ لَّكُمْ
quran_examples.en: Perhaps you hate something and it is good for you
quran_examples.context: The relativity of perceived and real good

hadith.ar: خَيْرُكُمْ مَنْ تَعَلَّمَ الْقُرْآنَ وَعَلَّمَهُ
hadith.en: The best of you are those who learn the Quran and teach it.

shades.name_en: al-Khayr — The Supreme Good and What Pleases Allah
shades.name_ar: الْخَيْرُ — كُلُّ مَا هُوَ أَفْضَلُ عِنْدَ اللَّهِ
shades.explanation:
Al-khayr (goodness) is one of the most nuanced Quranic concepts. The Quran's most theologically significant statement about khayr is the verse 16:96 — «inna Allāha yajʿizu mā yashāʾ — wa-yaqḍī ʿindahu amrahu wa-ʿindahu ummul-kitāb» (Allah changes what He wills and decides with Him, and with Him is the Mother of the Book, the Preserved Tablet) — which the early exegetes connected with the divine name al-Khayr. What is good ultimately belongs to Allah's will and decree; the human's choice to do khayr is the participation in the divine decree. The khayr is, in essence, the «thing as Allah wills it to be» — and recognizing the divine decree as the ultimate good is the foundation of tawḥīd.

The Quran's practical ethics of khayr presents the relative nature of human judgment. The verse 2:216 — «perhaps you hate something and it is good for you, and perhaps you love something and it is evil for you» — demonstrates that human perception of good and evil is unreliable. What appears evil (difficulty, loss, hardship) often conceals real khayr; what appears good (pleasure, comfort, ease) often conceals real sharr. The mu'min is therefore one who entrusts their judgment to Allah: «wa-fa-uwlī ilā Allāh» (and I entrust to Allah — 40:44). The abdication of personal judgment in favor of divine guidance is itself the highest khayr.

The hadīth in Bukhārī 5027 — «khayrukum man taʿallama l-Qur'āna wa-ʿallamahu» (the best of you are those who learn the Quran and teach it) — establishes a specific khayr: the khayr of being a vessel for divine guidance. The Quran is the khayr made accessible — the divine goodness that humans can carry, transmit, and live by. The one who teaches the Quran participates in the divine communication of khayr, becoming an instrument of Allah's mercy. The khayr is thus not merely something to be received but something to be transmitted: «ballighū ʿannī wa-law āyah» (convey from me, even if it is one verse) — the khayr of the Quran is its transmission.
shades.hadith_ar: خَيْرُكُمْ مَنْ تَعَلَّمَ الْقُرْآنَ وَعَلَّمَهُ
shades.hadith_en: The best of you are those who learn the Quran and teach it

meaning.en: Goodness, beauty, excellence. The root denotes both moral goodness (husn — beautiful conduct) and aesthetic beauty (jamāl — beautiful form).
meaning.ar: الْجَمَالُ وَالْحُسْنُ — الْحُسْنُ ضِدُّ الْقُبْحِ، وَهُوَ مَا يَسْتَحْسِنُهُ الْعَقْلُ وَالطَّبْعُ السَّلِيمُ

al_raghib.ar: الْحُسْنُ: جَوْهَرٌ يَمْنَحُ الْإِنْسَانَ فَضِيلَةً. وَأَصْلُهُ الْجَمَالُ، ثُمَّ يَسْتَعْمَلُ فِي الْمَحَاسِنِ الْأَخْلَاقِيَّةِ وَالْفِعْلِيَّةِ
al_raghib.en: Husn: a substance that grants the human excellence. Origin: beauty. Used for moral and practical excellences.

quran_examples.ar: وَأَحْسِنُوٓا۟ ۛ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ يُحِبُّ ٱلْمُحْسِنِينَ
quran_examples.en: And do ihsān — for Allah loves the muḥsinīn (those who do ihsān)
quran_examples.context: The command of ihsān — supreme virtue

hadith.ar: إِنَّ اللَّهَ كَتَبَ الْإِحْسَانَ عَلَى كُلِّ شَيْءٍ
hadith.en: Allah has prescribed ihsān in everything.

shades.name_en: Iḥsān — Excellence in Worship and Conduct
shades.explanation:
Iḥsān — excellence, doing things beautifully, acting with utmost beauty — is the supreme moral station in Islam. The ḥadīth Jibrīl in Muslim 8 defines iḥsān as «anta taʿbuda Allāha ka-annaka tarāhu, fa-in lam takun tarāhu fa-innahu yarāka» (to worship Allah as if you see Him, for if you do not see Him, He certainly sees you). The iḥsān is the conscious awareness that one's every act is being witnessed by the divine — and the consequent effort to perform it with the utmost beauty and excellence.

The verse 2:195 — «wa-aḥsinū, inna Allāha yuḥibbu l-muḥsinīn» (do iḥsān, for Allah loves the muḥsinīn) — is the Quran's charter of excellence. The muḥsinīn (those who do iḥsān) are the people Allah loves — a statement that applies even to non-Muslims (the verse was revealed regarding spending on relatives, orphans, the poor, travelers — before Islam prescribed zakāt). The iḥsān is the highest ethical register: above obligatory (farḍ), beyond recommended (mustaḥabb), reaching the level of worshiping Allah as if seeing Him.

Al-Ghazālī (Iḥyāʾ, Book of Iḥsān) describes the moral station of iḥsān as the highest achievable by the sālik (wayfarer). It is the perfection of taqwā (God-consciousness), the fulfillment of ihsān (witnessing), and the consolidation of ikhlāṣ (sincerity) all at once. The muḥsin is the one who has internalized the divine perspective so completely that every act — public or private, visible or invisible, major or minor — is performed with the beauty worthy of being observed by the One who sees all. The iḥsān is not perfectionism but integrity — the constant effort to do everything as well as possible, with the deepest knowledge that nothing is actually private from Allah.
shades.hadith_ar: إِنَّ اللَّهَ كَتَبَ الْإِحْسَانَ عَلَى كُلِّ شَيْءٍ
shades.en: Allah has prescribed ihsān in everything

meaning.en: To hear, to listen. The root denotes the auditory perception and, metaphorically, the conscious reception of speech — of Allah's words, of the Quran, of the prophets.
meaning.ar: إِدْرَاكُ الْمَسْمُوعِ بِالْأُذُنِ — وَالسَّمْعُ: إِدْرَاكُ الْأَصْوَاتِ وَالْكَلَامِ

al_raghib.ar: السَّمْعُ: إِدْرَاكُ الْمَسْمُوعِ — وَهُوَ أَوَّلُ الْحَوَاسِّ الَّتِي أَنْعَمَ اللَّهُ بِهَا عَلَى الْإِنْسَانِ
al_raghib.en: Samʿ: perception of the audible — among the first senses bestowed on humans by Allah.

quran_examples.ar: سَمِعْنَا وَعَصَيْنَا
quran_examples.en: We hear and we disobey
quran_examples.context: The rebellious response of the Children of Israel

hadith.ar: اسْتَوْعَيْتُ مِنَ النَّبِيِّ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ كَلِمَةً
hadith.en: I memorized a word from the Prophet ﷺ

shades.name_en: al-Samīʿ — Allah the All-Hearing and the Listening Heart
shades.name_ar: السَّمِيعُ — مَنْ يَسْمَعُ كُلَّ شَيْءٍ وَكُلَّ دَعْوَةٍ
shades.explanation:
Al-Samīʿ — the All-Hearing — is one of Allah's most frequently mentioned names, paired with al-Baṣīr (the All-Seeing) and al-ʿAlīm (the All-Knowing). The samāʿ of Allah is not limited by space or modality — He hears the silent prayer, the unspoken thought, the cry of the oppressed, the praise of the grateful, the curse of the wrongdoer, the prayer of the mother for her child. Nothing escapes His hearing.

The Quran's ethical teaching on samāʿ emphasizes the responsibility of conscious listening. The verse 2:93 — «samiʿnā wa-ʿaṣaynā» (we hear and we disobey) — characterizes the worst form of listening: hearing without responding, receiving without submitting. The obedient listener is described by the Quran as having «samīʿun wa-muṭīʿūn» (hearing and obedient — 4:46, 5:83, 9:85) — hearing and acting on what is heard. The samiʿ (hearer) and the muṭīʿ (obedient one) together constitute the mu'min's complete response to divine address.

The hadith of the Prophet ﷺ — «al-āya al-muwaththiqa wa-l-faḥsha» (the verse that establishes accountability and the indecency) refers to the samāʿ — the hearing that becomes the witness against or for the soul on the Day of Judgment. The ears that heard the Quran are witnesses to its truth; the ears that heard gossip are witnesses to its harm; the ears that heard divine commands are witnesses to their fulfillment or violation. The samāʿ is the body's most receptive sense for the divine — through hearing, the Quran enters the heart, the prophetic commands reach the mind, the warnings and promises penetrate the soul. The one who preserves and protects his samāʿ from listening to harām (forbidden speech) is on the path of taqwā; the one who fills his ears with harām is in the realm of heedlessness.
shades.hadith_ar: مَنْ كَانَ يُؤْمِنُ بِاللَّهِ وَالْيَوْمِ الْآخِرِ فَلْيَقُلْ خَيْرًا أَوْ لِيَصْمُتْ
shades.en: Whoever believes in Allah and the Last Day, let him speak good or remain silent

meaning.en: To go out, emerge, exit; to bring forth. The root encompasses physical emergence (going out of a place), biological emergence (plant sprouting, child being born), and metaphysical emergence (resurrection from the grave).
meaning.ar: الظُّهُورُ مِنْ مَكَانٍ إِلَى مَكَانٍ — وَالْخُرُوجُ: انْتِقَالٌ مِنَ الظَّاهِرِ إِلَى الظَّاهِرِ، أَوْ مِنَ الْبَاطِنِ إِلَى الظَّاهِرِ

al_raghib.ar: خَرَجَ: خَلَا وَخَلَصَ — كَانْتِفَاعِهِ الشَّيْءِ مِنَ الْمَكَانِ. وَيُسْتَعْمَلُ فِي الْمَخْرُوجِ مِنَ الْأَرْضِ
al_raghib.en: Kharaja: to emerge — separation from a place. Used for what emerges from the earth.

quran_examples.ar: وَٱللَّهُ يَدْعُوٓا۟ إِلَىٰ دَارِ ٱلسَّلَـٰمِ
quran_examples.en: Allah invites to the abode of peace (dar al-salām)
quran_examples.context: The invitation to paradise — emergence from the world

hadith.ar: إِنَّ لِلَّهِ تِسْعَةً وَتِسْعِينَ اسْمًا
hadith.en: Allah has ninety-nine names

shades.name_en: Kharaj — Emergence, Resurrection, and the Soul's Journey
shades.name_ar: الْخُرُوجُ — الْبُرُوزُ مِنَ الْأَرْضِ وَالسَّيْرُ إِلَى اللَّهِ
shades.explanation:
The verb kh-ruj (to go out, emerge) is the Quran's most frequent image of biological, social, and eschatological transition. The human emerges (yakhruj) from the mother's womb (16:78, 23:13-14), from the earth (sprouting, growth — 57:25), from hiding to manifestation, and ultimately from the grave (khurūj min al-qubūr) for the resurrection (22:5, 27:67, 70:44). Each of these emergences is a transition from one state to another — and each carries divine wisdom about the nature of existence.

The Quran's most theologically consequential khurūj is the resurrection — khurūj min al-qubūr. The disbelievers mock this teaching: «aʿidhā kunā ʿiẓāman fa-innā la-fī khalqin jadīd» (when we are bones and dust, shall we indeed be raised in a new creation? — 17:49, 17:98, 36:78, 79:11). The Quran responds by describing it as Allah's inevitable kh-ruj: «nakhrujū hayāthan fī al-ʿālamīna wa-yawma tushuqqu l-samā'u bi-l-ghamāmi wa-l-malā'atu tazzilu tartīfan» (they will emerge [from the graves] as living beings to the assembly — on that day the heaven will be split asunder with clouds, and the angels will descend in ranks — 25:21-22).

The khurūj imagery is also used for the mujāhidūn (those who strive): «wa-l-qā'ilīna rabbanā habib lanā min azwājinā wa-dhurriyyātinā qurrata aʿyunin, wa-jʿalnā li-l-muttaqīna imāman» — and for the hijrah (emigration) from Makkah to Madīnah, the foundational act of the early ummah. The verb kh-raja carries the sense of moving from a less favorable state to a more favorable one: from darkness to light, from kufr to īmān, from the dunyā to the ākhirah. The khurūj is thus always a movement toward greater reality — toward the truth, the divine, the eternal.
shades.hadith_ar: مَنْ خَرَجَ مِنْ بَيْتِهِ مُهَاجِرًا إِلَى اللَّهِ وَرَسُولِهِ فَأَدْرَكَهُ الْمَوْتُ
shades.en: Whoever leaves his home emigrating for Allah and His Messenger, then death overtakes him

meaning.en: Righteousness, soundness, goodness; to be righteous, to make peace/reconcile. The root denotes both personal moral righteousness and social reconciliation between parties.
meaning.ar: الْبُرُوءُ مِنَ الْمَرَضِ وَالْعَيْبِ — وَالصَّلَاحُ ضِدُّ الْفَسَادِ

al_raghib.ar: الصَّلَاحُ: ضِدُّ الْفَسَادِ. وَهُوَ بُرُوءُ الشَّيْءِ مِنَ الْعَيْبِ وَوُصُولُهُ إِلَى الْحَالِ الْحَمِيدَةِ
al_raghib.en: Salāḥ: opposite of fasād. The soundness of a thing from defect and its arrival at a praiseworthy state.

quran_examples.ar: وَمَا كَانَ رَبُّكَ لِيُهْلِكَ ٱلْقُرَىٰ بِظُلْمٍۢ وَأَهْلُهَا مُصْلِحُونَ
quran_examples.en: Your Lord would not destroy a town unjustly while its people were muṣliḥūn (reformers)
quran_examples.context: The divine protection of righteous communities

hadith.ar: الصَّلْحُ جَائِزٌ بَيْنَ الْمُسْلِمِينَ إِلَّا صُلْحًا أَحَلَّ حَرَامًا أَوْ حَرَّمَ حَلَالًا
hadith.en: Reconciliation is permitted between Muslims except what makes harām halāl or halāl harām.

shades.name_en: al-Muṣliḥ — Reformer as the Opposite of the Mufsid
shades.name_ar: الْمُصْلِحُ — صَانِعُ الْخَيْرِ بِإِصْلَاحِ الْأَرْضِ مِنَ الْفَسَادِ
shades.explanation:
Al-ṣāliḥ — the righteous — is the central moral concept of the Quran. The ṣāliḥīn (righteous ones) are explicitly promised Paradise in numerous verses (e.g., 2:25, 3:15, 4:57, 5:9, 16:30), and the ṣālih ʿamal (righteous deed) is the prerequisite for divine reward. The ṣāliḥ in the Quran is not merely a moral quality but a comprehensive one — encompassing ʿaql (mind), qalb (heart), ʿamal (action), and ʿaqīda (creed). The ṣāliḥ is the mu'min whose entire existence is in harmony with the divine will.

The ṣ-l-ḥ also denotes is-ḥ (reform, reconciliation). The verse 2:11 — «wa-idhā qīla lahum lā tufsidū fī l-arḍi qālū innamā naḥnu muṣliḥūn» (when they are told: do not cause corruption on earth, they say: we are muṣliḥūn — reformers) — captures the irony of reform-as-self-deception. The true muṣliḥ reforms the world in line with the divine order; the false muṣliḥ «reforms» the world in line with their own desires, calling corruption by the name of reform. The ṣāliḥ al-amal (righteous deeds) must align with the divine intent — otherwise, the surface reform hides deeper corruption.

The hadīth «al-ṣulḥu jāʾiz bayna l-muslimīn illā ṣulḥan aḥalla ḥarāman aw ḥarrama ḥalālā» (reconciliation is permitted between Muslims except what makes harām halāl or halāl harām — Abū Dāwūd 3594) establishes that reconciliation is the preferred mode of resolving conflict within the ummah. The ṣulḥ must, however, respect the bounds of the divine law — it cannot make forbidden things permitted or permitted things forbidden. The principle of «al-ṣulḥ al-ḥusn» (good reconciliation) is among the most beloved of deeds to Allah. The ṣāliḥ society is one in which conflicts are resolved through ṣulḥ, rights are restored, and the unity of the ummah is preserved — even at the cost of personal interest.
shades.hadith_ar: الصَّلْحُ جَائِزٌ بَيْنَ الْمُسْلِمِينَ
shades.en: Reconciliation is permitted between Muslims

meaning.en: To kill, slay. The root denotes the taking of life, whether human or animal. Theologically, qatl is permitted in certain cases (war, justice) and forbidden in others (murder, suicide).
meaning.ar: إِزَالَةُ الرُّوحِ — وَالْقَتْلُ: إِزَالَةُ الْحَيَاةِ عَنِ الْجَسَدِ

al_raghib.ar: الْقَتْلُ: إِزَالَةُ الْحَيَاةِ عَنِ الْحَيَوَانِ. وَهُوَ ضَرْبَانِ: مَأْمُورٌ بِهِ، وَمَنْهِيٌّ عَنْهُ
al_raghib.en: Qatl: removal of life from an animal. Two types: commanded (justified) and prohibited.

quran_examples.ar: مَن قَتَلَ نَفْسًۢا بِغَيْرِ نَفْسٍ أَوْ فَسَادٍۢ فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ فَكَأَنَّمَا قَتَلَ ٱلنَّاسَ جَمِيعًۭا
quran_examples.en: Whoever kills a soul — for other than a soul or corruption on earth — it is as if he had slain all mankind

hadith.ar: لَا تَقْتُلُوا الشَّيْخَ الْفَانِيَ وَلَا الطِّفْلَ الصَّغِيرَ وَلَا الْمَرْأَةَ
hadith.en: Do not kill the elderly, the child, or the woman

shades.name_en: Qatl al-Nafs — The Prohibition of Unlawful Killing
shades.name_ar: قَتْلُ النَّفْسِ — تَحْرِيمُ الْقَتْلِ الظَّالِمِ وَتَشْرِيفُ حَقِّ الْحَيَاةِ
shades.explanation:
The Quran's most morally consequential statement on qatl is the verse 5:32 — «man qatala nafsan bi-ghayri nafsin aw fasadin fi l-ardi fa-ka-annama qatala l-nasa jamīʿan, wa-man aḥyāha fa-ka-annama aḥyā l-nasa jamīʿan» (whoever kills a soul — for other than a soul or corruption on earth — it is as if he had killed all mankind; and whoever saves one — it is as if he had saved all mankind). The statement is radical: the killing of one soul is morally equivalent to the killing of all humanity — an equation that only makes sense if each human life carries the infinite value of the entire ummah.

The exception «bi-ghayri nafsin aw fasadin fi l-ardi» (for other than a soul or corruption on the earth) defines the legitimate instances of qatl: qisās (retaliation for murder — 2:178), and qatl in cases of fasād (corruption, sedition, terrorism — 5:33). The maḥkum with his justified killing (in defense of life) is not qatl al-nafs in the prohibited sense — but the maḥkum cannot extend his killing beyond what justice requires. The principle of proportionality (similarity in punishment) is established in 5:45: «wa-diyatun musallamatun ilā ahlihi» — life for life, but with the option of blood money in cases where the family chooses mercy.

The ḥadīth in Abū Dāwūd 2499 establishes the Islamic prohibition of killing non-combatants in war: «do not kill the elderly, the child, or the woman» — and by extension, civilians, farmers, priests, and others who are not directly engaged in combat. This hadīth is among the foundational principles of Islamic just-war ethics. The qatl of a single innocent — whether Muslim or non-Muslim — is the qatl of all humanity; the qatl of a combatant in legitimate warfare is the qatl of one who would otherwise take the lives of others.
shades.hadith_ar: مَنْ قَتَلَ مُعَاهَدًا لَمْ يَرَحْ رَائِحَةَ الْجَنَّةِ
shades.en: Whoever kills a covenanted non-Muslim will not smell the fragrance of Paradise

meaning.en: Heart, core, mind; to turn, flip. The root denotes both the physical organ of the chest and the spiritual faculty of understanding, will, and consciousness.
meaning.ar: الْقَلْبُ: سَمِيَّ بِهِ لِتَقَلُّبِهِ — وَهُوَ الرُّوحُ مَعَ التَّدْبِيرِ، أَوِ الرُّوحُ مَعَ النَّفْسِ

al_raghib.ar: الْقَلْبُ فِي الْأَصْلِ: اللُّبَابُ الْمَخْصُوصُ بِهِ الشَّيْءُ. وَقَلْبُ الْإِنْسَانِ: لُبُّ الرُّوحِ الَّذِي يَتَوَلَّى عِلْمَهُ وَإِدْرَاكَهُ
al_raghib.en: Qalb originally: the kernel specific to a thing. The human qalb: the kernel of the spirit that takes charge of knowledge and perception.

quran_examples.ar: ثُمَّ قَسَتْ قُلُوبُكُم مِّنۢ بَعْدِ ذَٰلِكَ فَهِىَ كَٱلْحِجَارَةِ أَوْ أَشَدُّ قَسْوَةًۭ
quran_examples.en: Then your hearts hardened after that, becoming like stones or harder
quran_examples.context: The hardening of hearts — qasāwat al-qulūb

hadith.ar: أَلَا وَإِنَّ فِي الْجَسَدِ مُضْغَةً، إِذَا صَلَحَتْ صَلَحَ الْجَسَدُ كُلُّهُ، وَإِذَا فَسَدَتْ فَسَدَ الْجَسَدُ كُلُّهُ، أَلَا وَهِيَ الْقَلْبُ
hadith.en: In the body there is a morsel; if it is sound, the whole body is sound; if it is corrupt, the whole body is corrupt — it is the heart.

shades.name_en: al-Qalb — The Heart as Spiritual Pivot and Its States
shades.name_ar: الْقَلْبُ — مَحَوْرُ الرُّوحِ وَتَقَلُّبَاتُهُ بَيْنَ الْإِيمَانِ وَالنِّفَاقِ
shades.explanation:
The qalb (heart) in the Quran is the spiritual pivot of human existence. The verse 2:74 — «thumma qasat qulūbukum min baʿd dhālika fa-hiya kal-ḥijārati aw ashaddu qaswah» (then your hearts hardened after that, becoming like stones or harder) — describes the qalb's pathological state: the hardening (qasāwah) that is the opposite of its natural condition of softness, receptivity, and presence. The qalb is created with a fiṭrah (primordial disposition) of softness and openness; the hardening is the result of choices and the cumulative effect of moral decisions.

The hadīth of the Prophet ﷺ in Bukhārī 52 — «alā wa-inna fī l-jasadi muḡghatun, idhā ṣalaḥat ṣalaḥa l-jasadu kulluhu, wa-idhā fasadat fasada l-jasadu kulluhu, alā wa-hiya l-qalbu» (in the body there is a morsel — if it is sound, the whole body is sound; if it is corrupt, the whole body is corrupt — it is the heart) — establishes the qalb as the spiritual axis. The moral health of the entire person — body, mind, soul, actions — depends on the condition of the qalb. The sound qalb is the basis for taqwā, the corrupt qalb is the origin of every moral pathology.

Al-Ghazālī's monumental Iḥyāʾ ʿUlūm al-Dīn — the title itself meaning «The Revival of the Religious Sciences» — is built on the premise of iṣlāḥ al-qalb (the reform of the heart). The heart's diseases (amrāḍ al-qulūb) — hasad (envy), riyāʾ (showing off), kibr (arrogance), ʿujb (self-admiration), and others — are the root causes of every external sin. The heart's medicines — tawba, dhikr, muḥāsaba (self-accounting), murāqaba (watchfulness), ikhlāṣ — are the foundation of all virtue. The qalb is thus the battlefield where the entire spiritual life is fought. The one who wins the qalb wins everything; the one who loses it loses everything. The mu'min's daily task is to examine, purify, and renew the qalb — until it becomes a place where Allah descends (in blessing), the angels alight (in protection), and the divine light shines (in guidance).
shades.hadith_ar: إِنَّ فِي الْجَسَدِ مُضْغَةً، إِذَا صَلَحَتْ صَلَحَ الْجَسَدُ كُلُّهُ
shades.en: In the body there is a morsel — if it is sound, the whole body is sound

meaning.en: Polytheism, associating partners with Allah. The root denotes the act of ascribing divine attributes or rights to beings or entities other than Allah — the antithesis of tawḥīd.
meaning.ar: جَعْلُ شَرِيكٍ لِلَّهِ فِي الْعِبَادَةِ أَوِ الرُّبُوبِيَّةِ أَوِ الْأُلُوهِيَّةِ

al_raghib.ar: الشِّرْكُ: جَعْلُ شَرِيكٍ لِلَّهِ. وَأَعْظَمُ الشِّرْكِ: الشِّرْكُ فِي الرُّبُوبِيَّةِ
al_raghib.en: Shirk: making a partner for Allah. The greatest shirk is in rubūbiyyah (lordship).

quran_examples.ar: إِنَّ ٱلشِّرْكَ لَظُلْمٌ عَظِيمٌ
quran_examples.en: Indeed shirk is a tremendous injustice

hadith.ar: لَوْ أَنَّ لِابْنِ آدَمَ وَادِيَيْنِ مِنْ ذَهَبٍ لَابْتَغَى إِلَيْهِمَا ثَالِثًا
hadith.en: If the son of Adam had two valleys of gold, he would desire a third

shades.name_en: al-Shirk — The Greatest Injustice Against Allah
shades.name_ar: الشِّرْكُ — أَعْظَمُ الظُّلْمِ لِلَّهِ وَتَكْذِيبُ تَوْحِيدِهِ
shades.explanation:
Shirk — polytheism, associating partners with Allah — is the central moral failure the Quran addresses. The verse 31:13 (Luqmān's counsel): «inna l-shirka la-ẓulmun ʿaẓīm» — indeed shirk is a tremendous injustice — establishes shirk as the supreme moral violation. The shirk is described as ẓulmun ʿaẓīm (tremendous injustice) because it is the violation of Allah's exclusive right to worship — the right that flows from His exclusive sovereignty, exclusive creation, exclusive sustenance.

The Quran distinguishes types of shirk. (1) Shirk al-ʿibādah (shirk in worship): the worship of beings or things other than Allah, whether idols, saints, angels, jinn, prophets, ancestors, or worldly powers. This is the most common form of shirk. (2) Shirk al-rubūbiyyah (shirk in lordship): the belief that other beings participate with Allah in His acts of creation, sustenance, or governance. The Quran strongly attacks this form (10:31, 23:84-89, 36:74-83). (3) Shirk al-asmāʾ (shirk in names): the application of Allah's exclusive names to beings other than Him. The Quranic prohibition is comprehensive: «wa-lā tasum mā Allāhu alḥāhu ilā afwālihim fa-qad ṣalū wa-mā hum muṣlihīn» (do not call what Allah has named as partners — 16:56).

Al-Ghazālī (Iḥyāʾ, Book of the Condemnation of Arrogance and Pride) identifies the more subtle forms of shirk: riyaʾ (showing off in worship) — the most difficult to avoid because it lurks in the heart of every deed. The «al-shirk al-khafī» (hidden shirk) is not polytheism in the literal sense but the attribution of one's deeds to anything other than Allah — the desire for human praise that infiltrates the worship of the One. The Prophet's invocation — «Allāhumma innī aʿūdhu bika an ushrika bika wa-ana aʿlam, wa-astaghfiruka li-mā lā aʿlam» (O Allah, I seek refuge in You from associating You knowingly, and seek Your forgiveness for what I do unknowingly) — reflects the consciousness of this hidden shirk. The true tawḥīd is not merely the absence of polytheism but the active, conscious, single-hearted devotion to Allah alone.
shades.hadith_ar: الشِّرْكُ فِي هَذِهِ الْأُمَّةِ أَخْفَى مِنَ الدُّبَيْبِ، وَسَأَدُلُّكَ عَلَى شَيْءٍ إِذَا فَعَلْتَهُ أَجْأَكَ مِنَ الشِّرْكِ الْأَصْغَرِ
shades.en: Shirk in this ummah is more hidden than the crawl of an ant — I will show you something that, if you do it, will save you from lesser shirk: say 'Allāhumma innī aʿūdhu bika an ushrika bika wa-ana aʿlam'

meaning.en: To die; death. The root denotes the transition from life (ḥayā') to death (mawt) — a transition that is real, complete, and divinely ordained.
meaning.ar: خُرُوجُ الرُّوحِ مِنَ الْجَسَدِ — وَالْمَوْتُ ضِدُّ الْحَيَاةِ، وَهُوَ عَالَمٌ آخَرُ

al_raghib.ar: الْمَوْتُ: انْفِصَالُ الرُّوحِ عَنِ الْجَسَدِ وَانْتِقَالُهَا مِنْ عَالَمٍ إِلَى عَالَمٍ
al_raghib.en: Mawt: separation of the spirit from the body and its transition from one world to another.

quran_examples.ar: كُلُّ نَفْسٍۢ ذَآئِقَةُ ٱلْمَوْتِ
quran_examples.en: Every soul shall taste death

hadith.ar: كُنْ فِي الدُّنْيَا كَأَنَّكَ غَرِيبٌ أَوْ عَابِرُ سَبِيلٍ
hadith.en: Be in the world as if you are a stranger or a traveler.

shades.name_en: al-Mawt — The Universal Transition and the Meeting with Allah
shades.name_ar: الْمَوْتُ — الِانْتِقَالُ مِنَ الدُّنْيَا إِلَى الْبَرْزَخِ ثُمَّ الْآخِرَةِ
shades.explanation:
The mawt (death) is the universal transition from worldly existence (al-dunyā) to the intermediate realm (al-barzakh) and ultimately to the final destination (al-ākhirah). The verse 3:185 — «kullu nafsin dhā'iqatu l-mawt» (every soul shall taste death) — is one of the most universal Quranic statements. Death is not the opposite of life in the philosophical sense (as if there were nothing on the other side) — death is the doorway, the transition, the gateway to what is beyond.

The Quran's treatment of mawt has multiple dimensions. (1) The certainty of death: every soul, believer or disbeliever, righteous or sinful, will taste (dhāqa) death. The verb «dhāqa» (to taste) is deliberately chosen — death is an experience, not just a moment. (2) The divinely ordained timing: «wa-mā kāna li-nafsin an tamūta illā bi-idhn Allāh kitāban mu'ajjalā» (no soul dies except by Allah's permission, at an appointed time — 3:145). The mawt has its appointed term (ajal) — neither hastened nor delayed.
