(3) The state of the deceased: «Allāhu yatawaffā l-anfusa ḥīna mawtihā wa-llatī lam tamut fī manāmihā, fa-yumsiku llātī qaḍā ʿalayhā l-mawta wa-yursilu l-ukhrā ilā ajalin musammā» (Allah takes the souls at the time of their death, and the ones that have not died, He takes during their sleep — He keeps the one He has decreed death for, and sends the others back until an appointed term — 39:42).

The hadith of the Prophet ﷺ — «kun fī l-dunyā ka-annaka gharībun aw ʿābir sabīl» (be in the world as if you are a stranger or a traveler — Bukhārī 6053) — establishes the proper relationship to mawt: the believer does not cling to the dunyā as if it were permanent, nor does he flee from it in despair — he lives in it as a traveler who will inevitably return. The mawt is the homecoming to the ākhirah, the meeting (liqāʾ) with Allah for which every soul was created. The mawt is not the end — it is the beginning of eternity.
shades.hadith_ar: كُنْ فِي الدُّنْيَا كَأَنَّكَ غَرِيبٌ أَوْ عَابِرُ سَبِيلٍ
shades.en: Be in the world as if you are a stranger or a traveler

meaning.en: Greatness, grandeur; old age, advanced in years; to be great. The root encompasses both the superlative quality of greatness and the temporal passage into old age.
meaning.ar: الْعَظَمَةُ وَالتَّفَوُّقُ — وَالْكِبَرُ: السِّنُّ الْمُتَقَدِّمَةُ، وَالْكِبْرِيَاءُ: التَّعَظُّمُ

al_raghib.ar: الْكِبْرُ: الْعَظَمَةُ وَالتَّعَالِي. وَالْكِبَرُ: سِنُّ الشَّيْخُوخَةِ. وَالْكِبْرِيَاءُ: التَّعَظُّمُ الْبَالِغُ
al_raghib.en: Kibr: grandeur and exaltedness. Kibar: advanced age. Kibriyā': utter grandiosity.

quran_examples.ar: وَلَا يُحِيطُونَ بِشَىْءٍۢ مِّنْ عِلْمِهِۦٓ إِلَّا بِمَا شَآءَ ۚ وَسِعَ كُرْسِيُّهُ ٱلسَّمَـٰوَٰتِ وَٱلْأَرْضَ ۖ وَلَا يَـُٔودُهُۥ حِفْظُهُمَا ۚ وَهُوَ ٱلْعَلِىُّ ٱلْعَظِيمُ
quran_examples.en: And His Throne encompasses the heavens and the earth — and He is the Most High, the Most Great

hadith.ar: يَقُولُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى: الْكِبْرِيَاءُ رِدَائِي، وَالْعَظَمَةُ إِزَارِي
hadith.en: Allah says: Pride (kibriyā') is My garment, and greatness (ʿaẓama) is My waist-wrapper.

shades.name_en: al-Kibriyāʾ — The Exclusive Divine Attribute and Its Prohibition to Humans
shades.name_ar: الْكِبْرِيَاءُ — صِفَةُ اللَّهِ الْخَالِصَةُ وَتَحْرِيمُ التَّكَبُّرِ عَلَى عِبَادِهِ
shades.explanation:
The kibriyāʾ (grandeur, pride in the divine sense) is among the most exclusive attributes of Allah. The ḥadīth qudsī in Muslim 2620 — «al-kibriyāʾu ridāʾī wa-l-ʿaẓamatu izārī» (Pride is My garment, Greatness is My waist-wrapper — and whoever disputes with Me in these, I shall punish him) — establishes that kibriyāʾ is not merely an attribute of Allah but a defining feature of His majesty. The image of garment and waist-wrapper evokes a noble robe and a wide sash — the visible markers of royalty and dignity. The human has no claim to kibriyāʾ — any human who claims it is a usurper.

The Quran's most powerful attack on human takabbur (arrogance, the claim to greatness) is the verse 40:35 — «wa-man yuẓallil Allāhu fa-mā lahu min mukrim» (whom Allah leads astray — no one can honor him). The ḥ-t-m of karāma (honor) is opposed to ḍ-l-l of ẓill (misguidance): Allah's guidance grants honor, and Allah's misguidance brings dishonor. The one who has ʿaẓama (greatness) in Allah's sight is honored; the one who has takabbur against Allah's command is disgraced.

The moral psychology of kibr is foundational to the Islamic tradition. The hadīth — «la-yadkhulu l-jannata man kāna fī qalbihi mithqālu dharratin min kibr» (no one with an atom's weight of kibr in his heart will enter Paradise — Muslim 91) — establishes the absolute prohibition of kibr in the believer. The kibr is not merely wrong behavior but a fundamental state of the heart that requires cure. Al-Ghazālī (Iḥyāʾ, Book of the Condemnation of Pride) analyzes the disease of kibr and prescribes its treatment: dhikr al-mawt (remembrance of death), muḥāsabat al-nafs (self-accounting), taʿāwun (helping others), and the cultivation of a humble vision of one's own reality before Allah. The cure for kibr is knowledge of one's own smallness before the greatness of Allah — for the one who truly knows Allah, pride in self becomes impossible.
shades.hadith_ar: الْكِبْرِيَاءُ رِدَائِي، وَالْعَظَمَةُ إِزَارِي
shades.en: Pride is My garment, Greatness is My waist-wrapper

meaning.en: Other than, different from, except. The root designates what is not the same as or not belonging to — used to exclude, compare, or distinguish.
meaning.ar: الْمُخَالِفُ — وَغَيْرُ: كُلُّ مَا عَدَا الشَّيْءَ وَمَلَاهُ

al_raghib.ar: غَيْرُ: اسْمٌ يُسْتَعْمَلُ لِوَصْفِ الشَّيْءِ بِمُخَالَفَتِهِ لِغَيْرِهِ — وَتَارَةً يَكُونُ بِمَعْنَى إِلَّا فِي الِاسْتِثْنَاءِ
al_raghib.en: Ghayr: used to describe something by its difference from others — sometimes meaning 'except' in exception.

quran_examples.ar: لَا إِكْرَاهَ فِى ٱلدِّينِ ۖ قَد تَّبَيَّنَ ٱلرُّشْدُ مِنَ ٱلْغَىۦ
quran_examples.en: There is no compulsion in religion — the right way has become clearly distinct from the wrong
quran_examples.context: The distinction of truth from falsehood

hadith.ar: لَا يُؤْمِنُ أَحَدُكُمْ حَتَّى يُحِبَّ لِأَخِيهِ مَا يُحِبُّ لِنَفْسِهِ
hadith.en: None of you truly believes until he loves for his brother what he loves for himself.

shades.name_en: al-Ghayr — Other than Allah, the Opposition to Tawḥīd
shades.name_ar: غَيْرُ اللَّهِ — كُلُّ مَا سِوَى اللَّهِ فَهُوَ مَخْلُوقٌ
shades.explanation:
The word ghayr (other than, except) is a foundational negative concept in the Quran. It is most consequential in the phrase ghayr Allāh (other than Allah), which identifies everything that is not Allah — and by implication, everything that is dependent upon Allah for its existence. The verse 2:256 — «lā ikrāha fī l-dīni, qad tabayyana l-rushdu mina l-ghayy» (there is no compulsion in religion; the right way has become clearly distinct from the wrong) — uses the related noun al-ghayy (error, misguidance) as the opposite of al-rushd (right guidance). The ghayr (other) in this verse is the way of misguidance, the false alternatives that compete with the divine way.

The Quran's emphasis on ghayr Allāh (other than Allah) is the negative side of tawḥīd. The positive side is la ilāha illā Allāh (no god but Allah). The negative excludes everything that is not Allah from worship; the positive affirms Allah alone as the proper object of worship. The mu'min is one who has fully excluded everything ghayr Allāh from his worship, his trust, his fear, his hope, his love. The mushrik, by contrast, has failed to make this exclusion complete — he worships Allah alongside other deities, trusts in other beings, fears other powers, hopes in other sources, loves other objects more than Allah.

The verse 2:107 — «wa-llāhu lā yaḥfazu mā yashā'u, wa-hum fī l-amri wa-l-mawālī wa-l-ākhirati hum khāsirūn» (Allah does not abrogate what He has sent down — and the mushrikūn are the losers) — establishes that even the «sealing of hearts» is in Allah's hand. Nothing ghayr Allāh can seal or unseal hearts; nothing ghayr Allāh can change what Allah has established. The ghayr (other than) is real but ultimately powerless — it exists within Allah's creation and is sustained by His will, but it has no autonomous force.
shades.hadith_ar: إِنَّ لِلَّهِ مَلَائِكَةً سَيَّاحِينَ يَكْتِبُونَ مَا تَعُدُّونَ
shades.en: Allah has angels who roam the earth, recording what you say

meaning.en: Sight, vision, insight. The root denotes the visual perception and, metaphorically, the inner sight of insight and discernment.
meaning.ar: الْإِبْصَارُ بِالْعَيْنِ — وَالْبَصَرُ: حَاسَّةُ الْإِبْصَارِ أَوِ الْإِدْرَاكُ الْبَاطِنُ

al_raghib.ar: الْبَصَرُ: حَاسَّةُ الْعَيْنِ الَّتِي يُدْرَكُ بِهَا الْمَرْئِيُّ. وَبَصِيرٌ: كَثِيرُ الْبَصَرِ، أَوْ مَنْ لَهُ بَصِيرَةٌ
al_raghib.en: Baṣar: the sense of the eye through which the visible is perceived. Baṣīr: one with much sight, or with insight.

quran_examples.ar: ٱقْرَأْ بِٱسْمِ رَبِّكَ ٱلَّذِى خَلَقَ
quran_examples.en: Read in the name of your Lord who created

hadith.ar: إِنَّ لِلَّهِ تِسْعَةً وَتِسْعِينَ اسْمًا
hadith.en: Allah has ninety-nine names

shades.name_en: al-Baṣīr — Allah the All-Seeing and the Inner Eye
shades.name_ar: الْبَصِيرُ — الَّذِي يَرَى كُلَّ شَيْءٍ وَلَا يَخْفَى عَلَيْهِ شَيْءٌ
shades.explanation:
Al-Baṣīr — the All-Seeing — is among the most frequently mentioned divine attributes, paired with al-Samīʿ (the All-Hearing). Allah's baṣar (sight) is not limited by space, modality, or quality — He sees the outer deeds and the inner intentions, the visible acts and the secret thoughts, the past and the future. The verse 96:1 — «iqra' bi-smi rabbika lladhī khalaqa» (read in the name of your Lord who created) — establishes that the source of all human knowledge (including the divine revelation) is the One who created the baṣar — who created the very capacity to see.

The Quran pairs al-Samīʿ and al-Baṣīr to emphasize that Allah's perception is comprehensive — He hears everything and He sees everything. The verse 6:103 — «wa-llāhu aʿlamu min al-mursalīn» — and many others establish that Allah's knowledge exceeds that of His messengers and all other beings. The «basāʾir» (insights, visions) of the heart are a special gift — the Quran itself is described as «hudan wa-shifā' wa-ḥudā» (guidance, healing, and light) that brings «basā'ir» (insights) to those who reflect (10:57).

The hadith of the Prophet ﷺ — «Allāhu al-Baṣīr yuhibbu al-baṣar» (Allah is the All-Seeer and loves those with baṣar — in this context meaning good appearance) — establishes a connection between divine baṣar (sight) and human baṣar (vision). The Muslim is one whose outward appearance is clean and whose inward vision is sound. The basīra (insight) is the inner sight that allows the heart to perceive truth and discern error — the spiritual faculty without which the external senses cannot serve the soul.
shades.hadith_ar: إِنَّ اللَّهَ خَبِيرٌ بِالْأَنْصَارِ
shades.en: Allah is well-aware of the eye-strategies (of enemies)

meaning.en: Family, kin, kinsfolk; to be related. The root denotes those joined by blood — the immediate family or the broader clan/tribe.

lexical_analysis.ibn_faris: أَصْلٌ وَاحِدٌ: الْمُؤَاخَاةُ بَيْنَ الْقَرَابَةِ. وَالْأَيُّ: الْقَرَابَةُ
lexical_analysis.al_raghib: الْأَيُّ: الْقَرَابَةُ الَّتِي تُؤَلِّفُ بَيْنَهُمُ الْمَحَبَّةُ

quran_examples.ar: وَٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا۟ بَعْضُهُمْ أَوْلِيَآءُ بَعْضٍ
quran_examples.en: Those who disbelieve are allies of one another
quran_examples.context: Kinship in faith versus kinship in kufr

hadith.ar: الرَّاحِمُونَ يَرْحَمُهُمُ الرَّحْمَٰنُ
hadith.en: The merciful are shown mercy by the Most Merciful

shades.name_en: al-Ayy — Kinship Bonds as Foundation of Mutual Responsibility
shades.explanation: The āy are those bound by blood relation through both lines of descent. The verse 8:72 establishes that the āy form a divinely-protected network of mutual protection, the alternative to the tribal clan-wars of the Jāhiliyyah. Ibn Taymiyyah argues that the āy has a right to the ʿirq (blood-wealth) only after the farā'iḍ are distributed.
shades.hadith_ar: مَثَلُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ فِي تَوَادِّهِمْ وَتَرَاحُمِهِمْ مَثَلُ الْجَسَدِ إِذَا اشْتَكَى مِنْهُ عُضْوٌ تَدَاعَى لَهُ سَائِرُ الْجَسَدِ بِالسَّهَرِ وَالْحُمَّى
shades.hadith_en: The example of the believers in their mutual love is like a body: if one part complains, the whole body responds.

meaning.en: Earth, land, ground; land, region. The root denotes the terrestrial world — the dwelling of humans and the foundation of physical existence.
meaning.ar: الْأَرْضُ: الْكُرَةُ الَّتِي نَحْيَا عَلَيْهَا، الْمَكَانُ الْوَاسِعُ

lexical_analysis.ibn_faris: الْأَرْضُ: الْمَكَانُ الَّذِي يَقَعُ عَلَيْهِ مَنْ عَلَيْهِ
lexical_analysis.al_raghib: الْأَرْضُ: الْكُرَةُ مَعْلُومَةٌ

quran_examples.ar: ٱلَّذِى جَعَلَ لَكُمُ ٱلْأَرْضَ فِرَٰشًۭا وَٱلسَّمَآءَ بِنَآءًۭ
quran_examples.en: Who made the earth a cradle and the sky a canopy
quran_examples.context: The earth as a divinely prepared dwelling

hadith.ar: إِنَّ اللَّهَ قَالَ: مَنْ عَادَى لِي وَلِيًّا فَقَدْ آذَنْتُهُ بِالْحَرْبِ
hadith.en: Allah said: Whoever is hostile to a friend (walī) of Mine, I have declared war against him.

shades.name_en: al-Arḍ — The Earth as Sustenance, Subjugation, and khalīfa's Domain
shades.explanation: The arḍ in the Quran appears in over 460 verses. It serves multiple functions: (1) The place of human dwelling — made firāsh (a spread, 2:22); (2) The locus of ʿibāda — where prostration occurs; (3) The field of khalīfa (2:30); (4) The witness on the Day of Judgment (99:1-3); (5) The recipient of divine kashf (35:39). On the Day of Resurrection, the earth says: this is the Day of Decision (77:38).
shades.hadith_ar: الْأَرْضُ جَمِيعًا قَبْضَتُهُ يَوْمَ الْقِيَامَةِ
shades.hadith_en: The earth will be entirely in His Grip on the Day of Resurrection

meaning.en: Sky, heaven; high, elevated. The root denotes the celestial realm — both the visible sky and the spiritual heavens.
meaning.ar: الْأَفْلَاكُ وَمَا فَوْقُهَا مِنَ الْعَوَالِمِ الْعُلْوِيَّةِ

lexical_analysis.ibn_faris: السَّمَاءُ: كُلُّ مَا عَلَا فَقَدْ سَمَاءَةٌ. وَالسَّمَاءُ: الْأَفْلَكُ
lexical_analysis.al_raghib: السَّمَاءُ: اسْمٌ لِمَا يَعْلُوكَ وَيَفُوقُكَ. وَأَصْلُهُ الِارْتِفَاعُ

quran_examples.ar: أَوَلَمْ يَرَ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُوٓا۟ أَنَّ ٱلسَّمَـٰوَٰتِ وَٱلْأَرْضَ كَانَتَا رَتْقًۭا فَفَتَقْنَـٰهُمَا
quran_examples.en: Do not the disbelievers know that the heavens and the earth were a single unit, then We split them apart?
quran_examples.context: The cosmogonic separation of heavens and earth

hadith.ar: سَبْعَةٌ يُظِلُّهُمُ اللَّهُ فِي ظِلِّهِ يَوْمَ لَا ظِلَّ إِلَّا ظِلُّهُ
hadith.en: Seven (categories) Allah will shade with His shade

shades.name_en: as-Samāwāt — The Seven Heavens and Their Theological Significance
shades.explanation: The samāwāt in the Quran are presented as a layered structure (sabʿ samāwāt — seven heavens, 17:44, 23:17, 41:12, 65:12, 67:3, 78:12). The cosmogonic verse 21:30 connects the cosmogonic act with the creation of all life from water. The heavens are characterized by divine attributes — al-Lawḥ al-Mahfūẓ is on the highest, the Kursī encompasses all, the ʿArsh is above all.
shades.hadith_ar: عُرِجَ بِي إِلَى السَّمَاءِ الدُّنْيَا فَرَأَيْتُ عَلِيَّ بْنَ أَبِي طَالِبٍ
shades.hadith_en: I was taken up to the lowest heaven, and there I saw Ali ibn Abi Talib

meaning.en: To protect, shield from fire or harm. The root denotes prevention of harm — particularly the divine protection of the righteous from punishment.
meaning.ar: الْحِفْظُ مِنَ الضَّرَرِ، وَقَايَةُ النَّفْسِ مِمَّا يُؤْذِيهَا

lexical_analysis.al_raghib: الْوِقَايَةُ: الْحِفْظُ عَنِ الْمَكْرُوهِ بِالِاحْتِرَازِ

quran_examples.ar: وَتَزَوَّدُوا۟ فَإِنَّ خَيْرَ ٱلزَّادِ ٱلتَّقْوَىٰ
quran_examples.en: And take provisions — but the best provision is taqwā
quran_examples.context: Provisions for the journey to the Hereafter

hadith.ar: سَبْعَةٌ يُظِلُّهُمُ اللَّهُ فِي ظِلِّهِ
hadith.en: Seven (categories) Allah will shade in His shade

shades.name_en: taqwā — Piety as Comprehensive Divine Protection
shades.name_ar: التَّقْوَى — الِاحْتِرَازُ مِنْ عَذَابِ اللَّهِ بِطَاعَتِهِ
shades.explanation: The taqwā is the central ethical concept in the Quran. The root w-q-y denotes protection, and taqwā is the human's protective armor against divine punishment. The verse 65:2-3 establishes the divine law: whoever fears Allah — He will make for him a way out and provide for him from where he does not expect. The taqwā is thus both the cause of protection and the comprehensive virtue: it requires abstaining from harām, performing the farā'iḍ, and maintaining an internal state of vigilance before Allah.
shades.hadith_ar: اتَّقِ اللَّهَ حَيْثُمَا كُنْتَ، وَأَتْبِعِ السَّيِّئَةَ الْحَسَنَةَ تَمْحُهَا
shades.hadith_en: Fear Allah wherever you are. Follow a bad deed with a good deed — it will erase it.

meaning.en: Last, end, ultimate. The root designates what comes at the end or after all else — the opposite of al-awwal (the first).
meaning.ar: الْأَخِيرُ، الَّذِي يَأْتِي بَعْدَ جَمِيعِ مَا سِوَاهُ

lexical_analysis.al_raghib: الْآخِرُ: هُوَ الَّذِي يَلِي الْأَوَّلَ. وَالدَّارُ الْآخِرَةُ: مَنْقَطَعُ الْمَسَافَةِ

quran_examples.ar: هُوَ ٱلْأَوَّلُ وَٱلْـَٔاخِرُ وَٱلظَّـٰهِرُ وَٱلْبَاطِنُ
quran_examples.en: He is the First and the Last, the Manifest and the Hidden

hadith.ar: كُنْتُمْ خَيْرَ أُمَّةٍ أُخْرِجَتْ لِلنَّاسِ
hadith.en: You are the best community raised for mankind

shades.name_en: al-Ākhirah — The Hereafter as Final Abode and Eternal Outcome
shades.name_ar: الدَّارُ الْآخِرَةُ — الْوَجْهُ الْأَخِيرُ مِنَ الْوُجُودِ الَّذِي لَا يَعْقُبُهُ فَنَاءٌ
shades.explanation: The ākhirah is the final dimension of existence — the abode that has no end, the dwelling that follows the dunyā. The verse 57:3 establishes ākhir as a divine name: Allah is the Last (al-Ākhir) in the sense that nothing comes after Him. The created ākhirah is the temporal mirror of this divine attribute. The pairing al-dunyā wa-l-ākhirah structures Islamic ethics: every deed must be evaluated for its consequence in both dimensions.
shades.hadith_ar: إِنَّ لَكَ فِي الْيَوْمِ خَيْرًا مِمَّا يَطْلُعُ عَلَيْهِ الشَّمْسُ أَوْ تَغْرُبُ
shades.hadith_en: You have in this day (or in the Hereafter) better than anything upon which the sun rises or sets.

meaning.en: Distance, remoteness; after. The root denotes spatial, temporal, and moral separation — being far from something in space, time, or spiritual state.
meaning.ar: الْمُسَافَةُ وَالْفَصْلُ بَيْنَ الشَّيْئَيْنِ زَمَانًا أَوْ مَكَانًا

lexical_analysis.ibn_faris: الْبُعْدُ: مَقَابِلُ الْقُرْبِ. وَهُوَ ضَرْبَانِ: بُعْدٌ مَكَانِيٌّ وَبُعْدٌ زَمَانِيٌّ
lexical_analysis.al_raghib: الْبُعْدُ: الْفَصْلُ بِطُولِ الْمَسَافَةِ أَوْ بِزِيَادَةِ الْمُدَّةِ

quran_examples.ar: وَتَزَوَّدُوا۟ فَإِنَّ خَيْرَ ٱلزَّادِ ٱلتَّقْوَىٰ
quran_examples.en: And take provisions — but the best provision is taqwā
quran_examples.context: Provisions for the journey to the Hereafter

hadith.ar: اقْتَرَبَتِ السَّاعَةُ وَلَا يَزِيدُ النَّاسُ عَلَى الدُّنْيَا حَرِيصًا
hadith.en: The Hour has drawn near, and people have only increased in greed for the world.

shades.name_en: al-Baʿd al-Manawī — Spiritual Distance from Allah
shades.name_ar: الْبُعْدُ الْمَعْنَوِيُّ — التَّنَحِّي عَنِ اللَّهِ وَعَنْ طَاعَتِهِ
shades.explanation: The baʿd in the Quran operates in multiple dimensions. The opposite is qurb (nearness, 2:186). The Islamic spiritual life is the journey from baʿd to qurb — from distance to nearness, from heedlessness to presence. Al-Ghazālī's Ihya' structures the entire path around this journey.
shades.hadith_ar: اقْتَرَبَتِ السَّاعَةُ وَلَا يَزِيدُ النَّاسُ عَلَى الدُّنْيَا حَرِيصًا
shades.hadith_en: The Hour has drawn near, and people have only increased in greed for the world

meaning.en: Way, path, road. The root denotes a way of going — physical path, means of access, or the way of life that one follows.

lexical_analysis.ibn_faris: السُّبُلُ: الطُّرُقَاتُ. وَالسَّبِيلُ: الطَّرِيقُ. وَأَصْلُ الْبَابِ: اسْتِطَاعَةُ الطَّرِيقِ
lexical_analysis.al_raghib: السَّبِيلُ: الطَّرِيقُ. وَقَدْ يُسْتَعْمَلُ فِي الطَّرِيقِ الْمَحْسُوسِ وَالْمَعْنَوِيِّ

quran_examples.ar: ٱهْدِنَا ٱلصِّرَٰطَ ٱلْمُسْتَقِيمَ
quran_examples.en: Guide us to the straight path

hadith.ar: الْجَنَّةُ مَحْفُوفَةٌ بِالْمَكَارِهِ
hadith.en: Paradise is surrounded by hardships

shades.name_en: as-Sabīl al-Mustaqīm — The Straight Path of Right Guidance
shades.name_ar: السَّبِيلُ الْمُسْتَقِيمُ — الطَّرِيقُ الَّذِي لَا يَعْدِلُ عَنِ الْحَقِّ
shades.explanation: The sabīl (path) is the central metaphor for the way of life in Islam. The sabīл al-mustaqīm (the straight path) is the one that does not bend or deviate — the path of divine guidance that leads to the destination. The Quran presents two main sabīls: the sabīl Allāh (the path of Allah) and the sabīl al-mujrimīn (the path of the criminals), the sabīl al-mu'minīn and the sabīl al-kāfirīn. The ʿaqīdah (creed) is essentially a choice between these two paths. The Quranic injunction wa-an ʿtabila sabīla man anāb ilayka (turn to those who turn to you — 31:15) calls for active engagement in the sabīл of those who turn to Allah.
shades.hadith_ar: الْجَنَّةُ مَحْفُوفَةٌ بِالْمَكَارِهِ
shades.hadith_en: Paradise is surrounded by hardships

meaning.en: Evil, ill, foulness. The root denotes what is morally repugnant, harmful, or shameful — the opposite of ḥasan (good).

lexical_analysis.ibn_faris: السُّوءُ: الشَّرُّ. وَالْمَسَاءَةُ: الشَّدِيدُ مِنَ الشَّرِّ
lexical_analysis.al_raghib: السُّوءُ: اسْمٌ لِمَا يَسُوءُ مِنَ الشَّرِّ. وَقَدْ يَسْتَعْمَلُ فِي الْأَفْعَالِ الْقَبِيحَةِ

quran_examples.ar: رَبَّنَآ ءَاتِنَا فِى ٱلدُّنْيَا حَسَنَةًۭ وَفِى ٱلْـَٔاخِرَةِ حَسَنَةًۭ وَقِنَا عَذَابَ ٱلنَّارِ
quran_examples.en: Our Lord, give us good in this world and good in the Hereafter, and protect us from the punishment of the Fire
quran_examples.context: The paired petition for hasan and protection from sawʾ

hadith.ar: اللَّهُمَّ إِنِّي أَعُوذُ بِكَ مِنَ الشَّرِّ كُلِّهِ
hadith.en: O Allah, I seek refuge in You from all evil.

shades.name_en: as-Sawʾ — Evil and Its Connection to Divine Wisdom
shades.name_ar: السُّوءُ — الشَّرُّ الَّذِي يَسْقُطُ عَلَى صَاحِبِهِ مِنْ ذَنْبِهِ
shades.explanation: The sawʾ (evil, ill) in the Quran is the comprehensive term for what is morally bad, harmful, or shameful. The verse 2:201 contrasts al-ḥasanah (good) with al-sayyiʾah (evil) — the dual petition of al-Fatihah expressed in the standing position of prayer: «rabbanā ātinā fī l-dunyā ḥasanatan wa-fī l-ākhirati ḥasanatan wa-qinā ʿadhāba l-nār». The Quranic theology of evil establishes that all evil comes from a source (either the soul's inclination toward evil, or external corruption), but the ultimate source of evil is the soul's own choices — the nafs ammārah bi-l-sūʾ (the soul commanding evil). The verse 39:49 establishes the moral calculus: «if good reaches the person, it grieves him; if evil touches him, he despairs» — illustrating the believer's proper response to both.
shades.hadith_ar: اللَّهُمَّ إِنِّي أَعُوذُ بِكَ مِنَ الشَّرِّ كُلِّهِ
shades.hadith_en: O Allah, I seek refuge in You from all evil

meaning.en: First, original, beginning; close family, kin. The root denotes what comes first (temporal, ontological, logical) and the close relatives of a person.
meaning.ar: الْأَوَّلُ ضِدُّ الْآخِرِ، وَالْأَوْلَى: الْأَحَقُّ وَالْأَقْرَبُ

lexical_analysis.ibn_faris: الْأَوَّلُ: ضِدُّ الْآخِرِ. وَالْأُولَى: الْأَقْرَبُ فِي الْحَقِّ
lexical_analysis.al_raghib: الْأَوَّلُ: الَّذِي يَسْبِقُ غَيْرَهُ. وَالْأُولَى: الْأَحَقُّ بِالشَّيْءِ

quran_examples.ar: هُوَ ٱلْأَوَّلُ وَٱلْـَٔاخِرُ وَٱلظَّـٰهِرُ وَٱلْبَاطِنُ
quran_examples.en: He is the First and the Last, the Manifest and the Hidden

hadith.ar: أَحَبُّ الْأَعْمَالِ إِلَى اللَّهِ أَدْوَمُهَا وَإِنْ قَلَّ
hadith.en: The most beloved deeds to Allah are those most consistent, even if few.

shades.name_en: al-Awwal — Divine Primacy and Cosmic Origins
shades.name_ar: الْأَوَّلُ — الَّذِي يَسْبِقُ كُلَّ شَيْءٍ وَلَيْسَ قَبْلَهُ شَيْءٌ
shades.explanation: The awwal (first) in the Quran is most consequentially applied to Allah as a divine name: «huwa l-Awwalu wa-l-Ākhiru» (He is the First and the Last — 57:3). The awwal in this divine sense is absolute primacy — no thing preceded Allah, no thing exists outside His eternal now, no beginning preceded His existence. The awwal is paired with al-Ākhir (the Last) to emphasize the totality of divine temporality: Allah encompasses all time within His being. The theological implications of al-Awwal are profound: Allah is the source of all beginning, the origin of all existence, the reference for all causality.
shades.hadith_ar: أَحَبُّ الْأَعْمَالِ إِلَى اللَّهِ أَدْوَمُهَا وَإِنْ قَلَّ
shades.hadith_en: The most beloved deeds to Allah are those most consistent

meaning.en: Many, much, abundance. The root denotes what is numerous or in large quantity — the opposite of qalīl (few).
meaning.ar: الْكَثْرَةُ ضِدُّ الْقِلَّةِ، وَالْكَثِيرُ مَا كَثُرَ عَدَدُهُ أَوْ مِقْدَارُهُ

lexical_analysis.ibn_faris: الْكَثْرُ: ضِدُّ الْقِلَّةِ. وَالْكَثِيرُ مِنَ الشَّيْءِ مَا كَثُرَ
lexical_analysis.al_raghib: الْكَثْرَةُ: ضِدُّ الْقِلَّةِ. وَيُسْتَعْمَلُ فِي الْعَدَدِ وَالْمِقْدَارِ

quran_examples.ar: وَإِذَا رَأَيْتَهُمْ تُعْجِبُكَ أَجْسَامُهُمْ ۖ وَإِن يَقُولُوا۟ تَسْمَعْ لِقَوْلِهِمْ ۖ كَأَنَّهُمْ خُشُبٌۭ مُّسَنَّدَةٌۭ
quran_examples.en: When you see them, their forms please you; and if they speak, you listen to their speech
quran_examples.context: The hypocrites — abundant in speech but empty of meaning

hadith.ar: أَقَلُّ الْكَلاَمِ وَأَكْثَرُ الذِّكْرِ
hadith.en: Less speech, more remembrance

shades.name_en: Kathrat al-ʿIbāda — Abundance of Worship and the Quality of Devotion
shades.name_ar: كَثْرَةُ الْعِبَادَةِ — الِاجْتِهَادُ فِي الطَّاعَاتِ وَمُوَالَاةُ الذِّكْرِ
shades.explanation: The k-th-r (abundance, multiplicity) in the Quran appears in theological, moral, and quantitative senses. The verse 62:10 — about the munāfiqūn — uses k-th-r in a negative sense: their abundance of speech, abundance of form, is deceptive, while they are «like propped-up logs of wood» (empty inside). The hadith of the Prophet ﷺ distinguishes between quantitative and qualitative abundance: «aḥabbu l-aʿmāli ilā Allāh adwamuḥā wa-in qall» — the most beloved deeds to Allah are the most consistent, even if few. The believer is not to seek katrah (many, abundant) deeds, but to seek taqwā in each deed, regardless of quantity.
shades.hadith_ar: أَحَبُّ الْأَعْمَالِ إِلَى اللَّهِ أَدْوَمُهَا وَإِنْ قَلَّ
shades.hadith_en: The most beloved deeds to Allah are those most consistent, even if few

meaning.en: Like, similar, example, parable. The root denotes resemblance and the comparative expression used to illuminate abstract concepts.
meaning.ar: الشَّبَهُ وَالنَّظِيرُ، وَالْمَثَلُ: مَا يُضْرَبُ لِتَوْضِيحِ الْمَعْنَى

lexical_analysis.ibn_faris: الْمَثَلُ: الشَّبَهُ. وَقَوْلُهُمْ: مَثَلٌ أَيْ شَبَهٌ
lexical_analysis.al_raghib: الْمَثَلُ: قَوْلٌ فِيهِ تَشْبِيهٌ وَتَقْرِيبُ مَعْنَى غَامِضٍ إِلَى مَعْنَى مَعْلُومٍ

quran_examples.ar: ٱللَّهُ لَا يَسْتَحْىِۦٓ أَن يَضْرِبَ مَثَلًۭا مَّا بَعُوضَةًۭ فَمَا فَوْقَهَا
quran_examples.en: Allah is not shy to strike a parable — even of a mosquito or anything above it
quran_examples.context: The divine use of mithāl (parable) — even the smallest

hadith.ar: مَثَلُ الَّذِي يَذْكُرُ رَبَّهُ وَالَّذِي لَا يَذْكُرُ رَبَّهُ مَثَلُ الْحَيِّ وَالْمَيِّتِ
hadith.en: The example of the one who remembers his Lord and the one who does not is like the living and the dead

shades.name_en: al-Mithāl — The Parable as Divine Pedagogy
shades.explanation: The mithāl (parable, example) is the Quran's primary pedagogical method — used to illuminate abstract concepts through concrete images. The verse 2:26 — «Allāhu lā yastahī an yaḍriba mathalan mā ba'ūḍatan» (Allah is not shy to strike a parable of a mosquito) — emphasizes the divine willingness to use even the simplest imagery. Al-Ghazālī argues that the mithāl is the most effective method of teaching because it builds on what the listener already knows, making the unfamiliar familiar. The Quran's mithāl-s include the parable of the spider's web (29:41), the rain-bringing cloud (30:48), the lamp in the niche (24:35), the good word (14:24-26), and many others — each designed to clarify a specific theological point.
shades.hadith_ar: مَثَلُ الَّذِي يَذْكُرُ رَبَّهُ وَالَّذِي لَا يَذْكُرُ رَبَّهُ مَثَلُ الْحَيِّ وَالْمَيِّتِ
shades.hadith_en: The example of the one who remembers his Lord and the one who does not is like the living and the dead

meaning.en: Some, part, portion. The root denotes a part of a whole — the relation of component to totality.
meaning.ar: الْجُزْءُ مِنَ الشَّيْءِ، وَمَا لَيْسَ بِالْكُلِّ

lexical_analysis.al_raghib: الْبَعْضُ: الْجُزْءُ مِنَ الشَّيْءِ. وَأَصْلُهُ مَا تَعَضَّى مِنَ الشَّيْءِ

quran_examples.ar: يَـٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوا۟ كُتِبَ عَلَيْكُمُ ٱلْقِصَاصُ فِى ٱلْقَتْلَى
quran_examples.en: O believers, qisās has been prescribed for you in cases of murder

hadith.ar: يَسِّرُوا وَلَا تُعَسِّرُوا، وَبَشِّرُوا وَلَا تُنَفِّرُوا
hadith.en: Make things easy, do not make them difficult; give glad tidings, do not create aversion

shades.name_en: al-Ba'ḍ and al-Ba'ḍ — Mutual Responsibility among the Believers
shades.name_ar: بَعْضُكُمْ بَعْضًا — التَّكَافُلُ وَالتَّضَامُنُ بَيْنَ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ
shades.explanation: The ba'ḍ (some, part) in the Quran operates in two main dimensions. (1) The ba'ḍ of reality: not everything is equal; the believer is not the same as the disbeliever; the good is not the same as the bad; the night is not the same as the day (91:4-9). The ba'ḍ emphasizes the differentiation that makes judgment meaningful. (2) The ba'ḍ al-takāful (mutual responsibility): the believers are a'wliyāʾ (allies) of one another (9:71), obligated to support one another, share burdens, and act in solidarity. The famous hadith — «al-mu'minu lil-mu'mini ka-l-bunyāni yad'umu ba'ḍuhu ba'ḍā» (the believer to the believer is like a building, each part supporting the others) — operationalizes the ba'ḍ in concrete social terms.
shades.hadith_ar: الْمُسْلِمُ أَخُو الْمُسْلِمِ، لَا يَظْلِمُهُ وَلَا يَخْذُلُهُ
shades.hadith_en: The Muslim is the brother of the Muslim; he does not wrong him nor abandon him

meaning.en: Below, nearer than, in front of. The root denotes spatial or relational inferiority — being lower or nearer (closer than something else).
meaning.ar: أَدْنَى، أَقْرَبُ، وَيُسْتَعْمَلُ فِي التَّحْقِيرِ وَالتَّقْصِيرِ

lexical_analysis.al_raghib: الدُّونُ: التَّقْصِيرُ عَنِ الْغَايَةِ. وَيُسْتَعْمَلُ فِي التَّقْصِيرِ الْمَادِّيِّ وَالْمَعْنَوِيِّ

quran_examples.ar: وَمَا جَعَلَهُ ٱللَّهُ إِلَّا بُشْرَىٰ لَكُمْ وَلِتَطْمَئِنَّ قُلُوبُكُم بِهِۦ ۖ وَمَا ٱلنَّصْرُ إِلَّا مِنْ عِندِ ٱللَّهِ
quran_examples.en: Allah gave it as glad tidings and for your hearts to be at peace — but victory comes only from Allah

hadith.ar: الْجَنَّةُ تَحْتَ أَقْدَامِ الْأُمَّهَاتِ
hadith.en: Paradise lies beneath the feet of mothers

shades.name_en: ad-Dūna — Inferiority and the Devaluation of Worldly Pursuits
shades.explanation: The dūna (nearer than, below) in the Quran expresses the relative inferiority of worldly pursuit compared to divine truth. The verse 4:32 — «wa-lā tashtawī l-ḥasanatu wa-lā l-sayyi'atu» (good and evil are not equal) — uses this concept to critique the assumption that all paths are equal. The verses 4:85 and 4:100 establish the moral priority: jihād fī sabīl Allāh (struggling in Allah's way) is superior to staying at home — the one who gives his life, wealth, and effort for the divine cause is at a higher station than the one who keeps it safe.
shades.hadith_ar: الْجَنَّةُ تَحْتَ أَقْدَامِ الْأُمَّهَاتِ
shades.hadith_en: Paradise lies beneath the feet of mothers

meaning.en: To meet, encounter, receive. The root denotes face-to-face meeting or encounter — particularly the meeting with Allah in the Hereafter.

lexical_analysis.ibn_faris: الْلِّقَاءُ: الْمُلَاقَاةُ. تَقُولُ: لَقِيتُ فُلَانًا أَيْ صَادَفْتُهُ
lexical_analysis.al_raghib: اللِّقَاءُ: الْوُصُولُ إِلَى الشَّيْءِ. وَيُسْتَعْمَلُ فِي الْإِصَابَةِ بِالْعَيْنِ، وَفِي الْمُقَابَلَةِ، وَفِي الِاجْتِمَاعِ

quran_examples.ar: وَلَقَدْ كَتَبْنَا فِى ٱلزَّبُورِ مِنۢ بَعْدِ ٱلذِّكْرِ أَنَّ ٱلْأَرْضَ يَرِثُهَا عِبَادِىَ ٱلصَّـٰلِحُونَ
quran_examples.en: We wrote in the Psalms after the Reminder: My righteous servants shall inherit the earth
quran_examples.context: The promised inheritance of the earth

hadith.ar: مَنْ أَحَبَّ لِقَاءَ اللَّهِ أَحَبَّ اللَّهُ لِقَاءَهُ
hadith.en: Whoever loves to meet Allah, Allah loves to meet him

shades.name_en: al-Liqāʾ — Meeting Allah as the Goal of Human Existence
shades.name_ar: لِقَاءُ اللَّهِ — الِاجْتِمَاعُ بِهِ يَوْمَ الْقِيَامَةِ
shades.explanation: The liqāʾ (meeting, encounter) is the Quranic concept of the meeting with Allah on the Day of Resurrection. The verse 32:23 — and the famous hadith — establish the spiritual state of those who long for this meeting: «man aḥabba liqāʾ Allāh aḥabba Allāhu liqāʾahu» (whoever loves to meet Allah, Allah loves to meet him). The liqāʾ with Allah is the consummation of the entire spiritual journey — the moment when the soul, freed from the body, returns to its origin and meets the One from whom it came. The Quran's distinction between al-manāra (the abode of peace — 6:127) and the sharru makān (the worst place — 22:60) corresponds to two different modes of liqāʾ: meeting with divine mercy or meeting with divine wrath.
shades.hadith_ar: مَنْ أَحَبَّ لِقَاءَ اللَّهِ أَحَبَّ اللَّهُ لِقَاءَهُ
shades.hadith_en: Whoever loves to meet Allah, Allah loves to meet him

meaning.en: God, deity; to worship; worthy of worship. The root produces the word Allāh (God) and al-ilāh (the deity).
meaning.ar: الْأُلُوهِيَّةُ: الِاسْتِحْقَاقُ لِلْعِبَادَةِ، وَالْإِلَهُ: الْمَعْبُودُ حَقًّا

lexical_analysis.ibn_faris: الْأَلِهَةُ: الْأُلُوهِيَّةُ. وَالْإِلَهُ: كُلُّ مَا اتُّخِذَ مَعْبُودًا. وَالْأُلُوهِيَّةُ: التَّأَلُّهُ
lexical_analysis.al_raghib: الْإِلَهُ: اسْمٌ لِكُلِّ مَعْبُودٍ. وَالْأُلُوهِيَّةُ: جَوْهَرُ الصِّدْقِ فِي الْمَعْبُودِيَّةِ. وَاللَّهُ: اسْمٌ لِلْمَعْبُودِ الْحَقِّ

quran_examples.ar: بِسْمِ ٱللَّهِ ٱلرَّحْمَـٰنِ ٱلرَّحِيمِ
quran_examples.en: In the name of Allah, the Most Merciful, the Especially Merciful

hadith.ar: أَفْضَلُ الْأَعْمَالِ أَنْ تَدْخُلَ عَلَى أَبَوَيْكَ أَوْ أَحَدِهِمَا
hadith.en: The best deeds include entering upon your parents (or one of them)

shades.name_en: Allāh and al-Ilāh — The Divine Name and the Concept of Divine Worthiness of Worship
shades.name_ar: اللَّهُ وَالْإِلَهُ — اسْمُ الْمَأْمُولِ الْوَحِيدِ لِلْعِبَادَةِ
shades.explanation: Allāh is the supreme divine name in the Quran — the personal name of the One God of Islam. Al-ilāh (the deity) is the conceptual name that applies to whatever is worshipped. The relationship between Allāh (God) and al-ilāh (deity) is the relationship between the reality and the concept. The basmalah «bismi Llāhi l-Raḥmāni l-Raḥīm» opens every surah and every important action in Islam. The Quran's central confession — «lā ilāha illā Allāh, Muḥammadun rasūlu Allāh» (no god but Allah, Muhammad is the messenger of Allah) — combines both: the denial of all false deities and the affirmation of the one true God. The verse 59:22-24 establishes Allāh as the name of the one who is al-wadūd (loving), al-majīd (glorious), and al-jabbār (compelling) — Allāh is not a metaphysical abstraction but a personal, loving, glorious Being.
shades.hadith_ar: اللَّهُمَّ أَنْتَ رَبِّي لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا أَنْتَ
shades.hadith_en: O Allah, You are my Lord, there is no god but You

meaning.en: Blessing, favor, comfort. The root denotes divine gifts and the comfort they bring to the recipient.
meaning.ar: الْإِنْعَامُ، وَالنِّعْمَةُ: مَا يَتَنَعَّمُ بِهِ، وَهِيَ الْعَطِيَّةُ الَّتِي تَسُرُّ

lexical_analysis.ibn_faris: النِّعْمُ: الْبُلُوغُ إِلَى الْمَنْفَعَةِ. وَالنِّعْمَةُ: الْحَالُ الْحَسَنَةُ
lexical_analysis.al_raghib: النِّعْمَةُ: الْإِنْعَامُ، أَوِ الْحَالُ الْمُسْتَفَادَةُ مِنَ الْإِنْعَامِ

quran_examples.ar: وَإِن تَعُدُّوا۟ نِعْمَتَ ٱللَّهِ لَا تُحْصُوهَآ ۗ إِنَّ ٱلْإِنسَـٰنَ لَظَلُومٌۭ كَفَّارٌ
quran_examples.en: If you tried to count Allah's blessings, you could not enumerate them — indeed man is unjust and ungrateful

hadith.ar: مَنْ لَمْ يَشْكُرِ الْقَلِيلَ لَمْ يَشْكُرِ الْكَثِيرَ
hadith.en: Whoever does not thank for the few will not thank for the much

shades.name_en: an-Niʿmah — Divine Favor as Both Gift and Test
shades.name_ar: النِّعْمَةُ — عَطِيَّةُ اللَّهِ الَّتِي تَسْتَلْزِمُ الشُّكْرَ
shades.explanation: The niʿmah (favor, blessing) in the Quran denotes every divine gift — visible (sustenance, health, children, wealth, knowledge) and invisible (faith, guidance, mercy, forgiveness, paradise). The verse 16:18 establishes the principle of countlessness: «if you tried to count Allah's blessings, you could not enumerate them — indeed man is unjust and ungrateful». The niʿmah is thus both divine generosity (in the giving) and divine test (in the receiving) — the recipient's response determines whether the niʿmah becomes a means of further reward (through gratitude) or a source of punishment (through ingratitude).
shades.hadith_ar: مَنْ لَمْ يَشْكُرِ الْقَلِيلَ لَمْ يَشْكُرِ الْكَثِيرَ
shades.hadith_en: Whoever does not thank for the few will not thank for the much

meaning.en: To ask, question, request. The root denotes seeking information or assistance.

lexical_analysis.ibn_faris: السُّؤَالُ: طَلَبُ الشَّيْءِ بِقَوْلٍ أَوْ إِشَارَةٍ
lexical_analysis.al_raghib: السُّؤَالُ: طَلَبُ الشَّيْءِ مَعَ التَّلَطُّفِ

quran_examples.ar: أَمْ تُرِيدُونَ أَن تَسْـَٔلُوا۟ رَسُولَكُمْ كَمَا سُئِلَ مُوسَىٰ مِن قَبْلُ
quran_examples.en: Or do you want to ask your Messenger as Moses was asked before?

hadith.ar: سَلْ اللَّهَ الْعَفْوَ وَالْعَافِيَةَ وَالْمُعَافَاةَ فِي الدُّنْيَا وَالْآخِرَةِ
hadith.en: Ask Allah for pardon, well-being, and protection in this world and the Hereafter

shades.name_en: as-Suʾāl and ad-Duʿāʾ — Asking as Both Request and Inquiry
shades.name_ar: السُّؤَالُ وَالدُّعَاءُ — طَلَبُ الْإِنْسَانِ مِنْ رَبِّهِ
shades.explanation: The s-ʾ-l (asking, requesting) in the Quran operates in two distinct dimensions. (1) The negative dimension: excessive questioning as a sign of doubt — the verse 2:108 warns against demanding from the Messenger as the Children of Israel demanded from Moses; the questioner may not be ready for the answer. (2) The positive dimension: asking Allah through duʿāʾ — the verse 2:186 promises that every invocation is answered. The distinction: the negative sāl is questioning the divine; the positive sāl is requesting from the divine. The hadith of the Prophet ﷺ — «sal Allāh al-ʿafwa wa-l-ʿāfiyah wa-l-muʿāfāh» — establishes the proper way of asking: asking Allah for the greatest of gifts — forgiveness, well-being, and protection.
shades.hadith_ar: سَلْ اللَّهَ الْعَفْوَ وَالْعَافِيَةَ وَالْمُعَافَاةَ فِي الدُّنْيَا وَالْآخِرَةِ
shades.hadith_en: Ask Allah for pardon, well-being, and protection

meaning.en: Nearness, approaching; near. The root denotes physical or temporal proximity, especially drawing close to Allah.

lexical_analysis.al_raghib: الدُّنُوُّ: الْقُرْبُ مَكَانِيًّا أَوْ مَعْنَوِيًّا

quran_examples.ar: وَٱسْجُدْ وَٱقْتَرِب
quran_examples.en: Prostrate and draw near
quran_examples.context: The divine command to draw near through prostration

hadith.ar: إِذَا أَحَبَّ اللَّهُ عَبْدًا نَادَى جِبْرِيلَ إِنِّي أُحِبُّ فُلَانًا فَأَحِبَّهُ
hadith.en: When Allah loves a servant, He calls Gabriel: Indeed I love so-and-so, so love him

shades.name_en: al-Dunuw — The Approach to Allah Through Worship
shades.name_ar: الدُّنُوُّ مِنَ اللَّهِ — الِاقْتِرَابُ بِالْعِبَادَةِ وَالطَّاعَاتِ
shades.explanation: The dunuw (approach, nearness) is closely linked to qurb. The verse 96:19 establishes that sujud (prostration) is the physical state of maximum nearness - the body in the lowest position while the soul is closest to its Lord.
shades.hadith_ar: إِذَا أَحَبَّ اللَّهُ عَبْدًا نَادَى جِبْرِيلَ إِنِّي أُحِبُّ فُلَانًا فَأَحِبَّهُ
shades.hadith_en: When Allah loves a servant, He calls Gabriel: Indeed I love so-and-so, so love him

meaning.en: Obedience, willingness, voluntary submission.

lexical_analysis.al_raghib: الطَّوْعُ: الِانْقِيَادُ بِرَضًا وَاخْتِيَارٍ

quran_examples.ar: فَلَا وَرَبِّكَ لَا يُؤْمِنُونَ حَتَّىٰ يُحَكِّمُوكَ فِيمَا شَجَرَ بَيْنَهُمْ
quran_examples.en: By your Lord, they will not believe until they make you judge in what has arisen between them
quran_examples.context: The full submission that is the mark of iman

hadith.ar: سَمِعْتُ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ يَقُولُ: مَنْ أَحَبَّ أَنْ يَجِدَ حَلَاوَةَ الْإِيمَانِ فَلْيَحْبَبْ الْمَرْءَ لَا يُحِبُّهُ إِلَّا لِلَّهِ
hadith.en: I heard the Messenger say: Whoever wants to taste the sweetness of iman should love the man whom he loves only for the sake of Allah

shades.name_en: at-Tawʿ — Obedience as Willing Surrender to Divine Command
shades.explanation: The tawʿ (obedience) in the Quran denotes active submission to divine command. The verse 4:65 establishes the quality of true iman: yuslimuna taslima - they submit in complete, unqualified submission.
shades.hadith_ar: سَمِعْتُ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ يَقُولُ: مَنْ أَحَبَّ أَنْ يَجِدَ حَلَاوَةَ الْإِيمَانِ فَلْيَحْبَبْ الْمَرْءَ لَا يُحِبُّهُ إِلَّا لِلَّهِ
shades.hadith_en: Whoever wants to taste the sweetness of iman should love the man whom he loves only for the sake of Allah

meaning.en: Warning, alerting. The root denotes the act of alerting to danger.

lexical_analysis.ibn_faris: النَّذِيرُ: الَّذِي يُنْذِرُ بِالْعَذَابِ
lexical_analysis.al_raghib: الْإِنْذَارُ: التَّخْوِيفُ مَعَ التَّعْظِيمِ

quran_examples.ar: وَتَقُولُوا۟ سَمِعْنَا وَأَطَعْنَا ۖ وَأُو۟لَـٰٓئِكَ هُمُ ٱلْمُفْلِحُونَ
quran_examples.en: And say: We hear and we obey - those are the successful
quran_examples.context: The combination of hearing and obeying

hadith.ar: لَقَدْ جَاءَكُمْ رَسُولٌ مِنْ أَنْفُسِكُمْ عَزِيزٌ عَلَيْهِ مَا عَنِتُّمْ
hadith.en: There has come to you a Messenger from among yourselves - heavy upon him is your hardship

shades.name_en: an-Nadhir — The Prophet as Warner to the Worlds
shades.name_ar: النَّذِيرُ — الْمُنْذِرُ بِالْعَذَابِ إِنْ لَمْ يُؤْمَنْ
shades.explanation: The nadhir (warner) is a foundational prophetic title. The Quran describes every prophet as a nadhir - sent to warn their ummahs of divine punishment. The verse 4:65 emphasizes the link between hearing and obeying - the one who truly believes both hears the warning and accepts it with submission.
shades.hadith_ar: لَقَدْ جَاءَكُمْ رَسُولٌ مِنْ أَنْفُسِكُمْ عَزِيزٌ عَلَيْهِ مَا عَنِتُّمْ
shades.hadith_en: There has come to you a Messenger from among yourselves - heavy upon him is your hardship

meaning.en: Gathering, collecting. The root denotes bringing things together.

lexical_analysis.ibn_faris: الْجَمْعُ: ضِدُّ التَّفْرِيقِ
lexical_analysis.al_raghib: الْجَمْعُ: ضَمُّ الشَّيْءِ بَعْضِهِ إِلَى بَعْضٍ

quran_examples.ar: إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ لَا يُضِيعُ أَجْرَ ٱلْمُحْسِنِينَ
quran_examples.en: Indeed Allah does not waste the reward of those who do good

hadith.ar: لَا تَقُصُّ رُؤْيَاكَ عَلَى أَخِيكَ فَيُؤْذِيَهُ
hadith.en: Do not narrate your dream to your brother lest it harm him

shades.name_en: al-Jamʿ — Gathering of Hearts and of All Things to Allah
shades.explanation: The jamʿ (gathering) operates in multiple dimensions: Friday gathering, Day of Resurrection gathering, jamʿ al-khayr (gathering of good things), jamʿ al-qulūb (unity of hearts). The jamʿ as a divine attribute: wa-huwa l-jāmiʿu bayna l-qulūb - only Allah can unite what humans have divided.
shades.hadith_ar: إِنَّ هَٰذِهِ الْأُمَّةَ سَتَمْرَجُ مَرَجَ اللَّهِ
shades.hadith_en: Indeed this ummah will be gathered in Allahs gathering

meaning.en: To look, see, consider, wait.
meaning.ar: إِقَاءُ الْبَصَرِ عَلَى الشَّيْءِ، وَالتَّرَيُّثُ فِي الْأَمْرِ

lexical_analysis.ibn_faris: النَّظَرُ: تَأَمُّلُ الشَّيْءِ بِالْبَصَرِ
lexical_analysis.al_raghib: النَّظَرُ: إِقَاءُ الْبَصَرِ لِتَأَمُّلِ الشَّيْءِ

quran_examples.ar: أَوْ كَٱلَّذِى مَرَّ عَلَىٰ قَرْيَةٍۢ وَهِىَ خَاوِيَةٌ عَلَىٰ عُرُوشِهَا
quran_examples.en: Or like the one who passed by a town - and it had fallen down upon its roofs
quran_examples.context: The parable of the man who passed by the ruined town

hadith.ar: مِنْ حُسْنِ إِسْلَامِ الْمَرْءِ تَرْكُهُ مَا لَا يَعْنِيهِ
hadith.en: Part of the beauty of a persons Islam is leaving that which does not concern him

shades.name_en: an-Nazar — Looking, Reflection, and the Deferral of Punishment
shades.explanation: The naẓar is both physical and intellectual. The verse 2:259 uses naẓar in the sense of careful intellectual consideration. The Quran most frequently invites intellectual naẓar - to look, to reflect, to consider the signs.
shades.hadith_ar: مِنْ حُسْنِ إِسْلَامِ الْمَرْءِ تَرْكُهُ مَا لَا يَعْنِيهِ
shades.hadith_en: Part of the beauty of a persons Islam is leaving that which does not concern him

meaning.en: To pierce, penetrate, bore through.

lexical_analysis.al_raghib: النَّفْجُ: الشَّقُّ الْوَاسِعُ

quran_examples.ar: أَوَلَمْ يَرَ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُوٓا۟ أَنَّ ٱلسَّمَـٰوَٰتِ وَٱلْأَرْضَ كَانَتَا رَتْقًۭا فَفَتَقْنَـٰهُمَا
quran_examples.en: Do not the disbelievers know that the heavens and the earth were a single unit, then We split them apart?
quran_examples.context: The piercing of the heavens and the earth apart from one another

hadith.ar: الرَّاحِمُونَ يَرْحَمُهُمُ الرَّحْمَٰنُ
hadith.en: The merciful are shown mercy by the Most Merciful

shades.name_en: an-Nafj — Cosmic Piercing as Origin of Distinction and Existence
shades.name_ar: النَّفْجُ — الشَّقُّ الْعَمِيقُ الَّذِي يُخْرِجُ مَا فِيهِ
shades.explanation: The nafj (piercing) appears in three Quranic contexts. The most famous is 67:30-31 - the divine nafj of the original unity into the multiplicity of creation.
shades.hadith_ar: الرَّاحِمُونَ يَرْحَمُهُمُ الرَّحْمَٰنُ
shades.hadith_en: The merciful are shown mercy by the Most Merciful

meaning.en: Sword, blade. The root denotes the cutting instrument — primarily the sword of war and justice.

lexical_analysis.al_raghib: السَّيْفُ: الشَّفْرَةُ مِنَ الْحَدِيدِ. وَسُمِّيَ بِهِ لِجَرْيِهِ فِي الْهَوَاءِ كَالسَّيْلِ

quran_examples.ar: وَإِذْ يَعِدُكُمُ ٱللَّهُ إِحْدَى ٱلطَّآئِفَتَيْنِ أَنَّهَا لَكُمْ وَتَوَدُّونَ أَنَّ غَيْرَ ذَاتِ ٱلشَّوْكَةِ تَكُونُ لَكُمْ
quran_examples.en: When Allah promised you one of the two parties would be yours — you wished for the unarmed one
quran_examples.context: The battle of Badr and the armed party

hadith.ar: الْجَنَّةُ تَحْتَ ظِلِّ السُّيُوفِ
hadith.en: Paradise lies beneath the shade of swords

shades.name_en: as-Sayf — The Sword as Instrument of Divine Justice and Jihād
shades.name_ar: السَّيْفُ — سِلَاحُ الْعَدْلِ وَالْجِهَادِ فِي سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ
shades.explanation: The sayf (sword) in the Quran is mentioned primarily in contexts of qitāl (fighting in Allah's cause). The hadith — «al-jannatu taḥta ẓilli l-suyūf» (paradise lies beneath the shade of swords) — establishes jihād's supreme value in Islam. The sword is the instrument by which the oppressed are freed, the faith is defended, and divine justice is enforced. But its use is governed by strict limits: only against those who wage war, only with proper declaration, only within the bounds of proportionality, never against civilians, never with mutilation, never with excess.
shades.hadith_ar: الْجَنَّةُ تَحْتَ ظِلِّ السُّيُوفِ
shades.hadith_en: Paradise lies beneath the shade of swords

meaning.en: To seek, search, ask politely. The root denotes gentle seeking or soft request — particularly in matters of courtship or earnest asking.

lexical_analysis.al_raghib: الرَّوْدُ: طَلَبُ الشَّيْءِ بِالتَّلَطُّفِ. وَرَوْدُ الشَّيْءِ: طَلَبُهُ بِالِاسْتِرْفَاقِ

quran_examples.ar: وَجَآءُوا۟ عَلَىٰ قَمِيصِهِۦ بِدَمٍۢ كَذِبٍۢ ۚ قَالَ بَلْ سَوَّلَتْ لَكُمْ أَنفُسُكُمْ أَمْرًۭا ۖ فَصَبْرٌۭ جَمِيلٌ
quran_examples.en: They brought his shirt with false blood. He said: Your souls have enticed you to something; patience is fitting

hadith.ar: مَلَعُونٌ مَلَعُونٌ مَنْ ضَرَبَ الْمُؤْمِنَ أَوْ غَشَّهُ
hadith.en: Cursed, cursed is he who strikes a believer or cheats him

shades.name_en: ar-Raʿd — Gentle Seeking and the Ethical Approach
shades.name_ar: الرَّوْدُ — الطَّلَبُ بِلِينٍ، الِاسْتِرْفَاقُ، وَسُؤَالُ الْحَاجَةِ بِأَدَبٍ
shades.explanation: The rawd (gentle seeking, soft request) is the polite mode of requesting something — courteous, gradual, and without coercion. The verse 80:6 — about the soul's ra'wd (gradual) search for its Lord — captures this gentle quality: the soul seeks not by force but by longing, not by violence but by love. In ethical discourse, the ra'wd characterizes the believer's approach to knowledge, forgiveness, and worship — not hasty or aggressive but deliberate and respectful. The verb tarawwada (to seek gently) is the paradigm of the patient, dignified seeking.
shades.hadith_ar: لَا تَلَقَّبُوا الْمُسْلِمِينَ بِالْأَلْقَابِ
shades.hadith_en: Do not address Muslims by offensive nicknames

meaning.en: Longing, yearning, intense desire. The root denotes the soul's passionate yearning, particularly for the beloved or the divine.

lexical_analysis.al_raghib: الْخَوْجُ: شِدَّةُ الشَّوْقِ. وَهُوَ مِنَ الصِّفَاتِ الْغَالِبَةِ عَلَى الْقَلْبِ

quran_examples.ar: وَلَقَدْ هَمَّتْ بِهِۦ ۖ وَهَمَّ بِهَا لَوْلَآ أَن رَّءَا بُرْهَٰنَ رَبِّهِۦ
quran_examples.en: She had desired him, and he would have desired her if he had not seen the proof of his Lord

hadith.ar: إِنَّ لِلَّهِ مَلَائِكَةً يَسْبِحُونَ فِي الْجَوِّ فَيَبْعَثُونَ الرُّوحَ عَلَى قَلْبِ عَبْدٍ يَسْأَلُ عَنِ اللَّهِ
hadith.en: Allah has angels who glide in the air and send the ruh (spirit) to the heart of the servant who asks about Allah

shades.name_en: al-Khawj — Yearning as the Soul's Movement Toward the Beloved
shades.name_ar: الْخَوْجُ — الشَّوْقُ الشَّدِيدُ، حَرَكَةُ النَّفْسِ نَحْوَ الْمَحْبُوبِ
shades.explanation: The khawj (intense yearning) in the Quran appears primarily in the story of Yusuf and Zulaykha — her passionate desire for Yusuf, expressed by the verb hamma (she desired intensely) and the related «khawj» concept. The story is famous for showing how the body can be overpowered by desire but the soul is preserved by the burhān (proof) of Allah. Sufi poetry later adopted khawj as the language of divine yearning: the soul's longing for union with the Beloved. Al-Ghazālī (Jawāhir al-Qur'ān) notes that khawj is the antecedent of tawakkul: the soul that yearns for Allah will find its way to Him.
shades.hadith_ar: مَا يَزَالُ الْعَبْدُ يَقْرَبُ مِنَ اللَّهِ بِالنَّوَافِلِ
shades.hadith_en: The servant continues to draw near to Allah through the supererogatory prayers

meaning.en: Heart (as organ); to flip, transform. The kalb is the physical heart — also a metaphor for the seat of emotion and intention.
meaning.ar: الْقَلْبُ: عُضْوُ الدَّمِ فِي الصَّدْرِ، وَأَيْضًا: مَوْطِنُ الْإِرَادَةِ وَالْعَاطِفَةِ

lexical_analysis.al_raghib: الْقَلْبُ: عُضْوٌ صَنَوْبَرِيٌّ فِي جَوْفِ الصَّدْرِ. وَيُسْتَعْمَلُ أَيْضًا لِمَوْطِنِ الْإِدْرَاكِ وَالْإِرَادَةِ

quran_examples.ar: فَإِنْ أَمِنَ بَعْضُكُم بَعْضًۭا فَلْيُؤَدِّ ٱلَّذِى ٱؤْتُمِنَ أَمَـٰنَتَهُۥ
quran_examples.en: If you trust one another, let the one who is entrusted deliver his trust

hadith.ar: أَلَا وَإِنَّ فِي الْجَسَدِ مُضْغَةً، إِذَا صَلَحَتْ صَلَحَ الْجَسَدُ كُلُّهُ، وَإِذَا فَسَدَتْ فَسَدَ الْجَسَدُ كُلُّهُ، أَلَا وَهِيَ الْقَلْبُ
hadith.en: In the body there is a morsel; if it is sound, the whole body is sound; if it is corrupt, the whole body is corrupt — it is the heart

shades.name_en: al-Qalb al-Bashari — The Human Heart as Physical and Spiritual Organ
shades.name_ar: الْقَلْبُ الْبَشَرِيُّ — عُضْوٌ فِي الصَّدْرِ وَأَيْضًا مَحَلُّ الْإِيمَانِ
shades.explanation: The qalb in its anatomical sense appears in several verses, often paired with the spiritual function. The verse 22:32 — «wa-man yuʿaẓẓim sha'ā'ira Llāh fa-innahā min taqwā l-qulūb» (whoever honors Allah's rites — it is from taqwā of the hearts) — connects the heart's spiritual state to outward religious observance. The physical heart (the organ that pumps blood) and the spiritual heart (the seat of intellect, will, faith) are both qalb in the Quran — the early Muslim physicians like Ibn al-Nafīs understood this connection and developed their anatomical studies in light of Quranic categories.
shades.hadith_ar: أَلَا وَإِنَّ فِي الْجَسَدِ مُضْغَةً، إِذَا صَلَحَتْ صَلَحَ الْجَسَدُ كُلُّهُ، وَإِذَا فَسَدَتْ فَسَدَ الْجَسَدُ كُلُّهُ، أَلَا وَهِيَ الْقَلْبُ
shades.hadith_en: In the body there is a morsel — if it is sound, the whole body is sound; if it is corrupt, the whole body is corrupt — it is the heart

meaning.en: Fifth; the fifth (part). The root denotes the ordinal and fractional fifth — including the obligation of one-fifth of certain revenues (khums) for specific causes.

lexical_analysis.al_raghib: الْخُمُسُ: اسْمٌ لِوَاحِدٍ مِنْ خَمْسَةِ أَجْزَاءٍ. وَقَدْ شُرِعَ فِي الْفَيْءِ وَالْغَنَائِمِ وَالرِّكَازِ

quran_examples.ar: وَٱعْلَمُوٓا۟ أَنَّمَا غَنِمْتُم مِّن شَىْءٍۢ فَأَنَّ لِلَّهِ خُمُسَهُۥ
quran_examples.en: Know that whatever you gain, one-fifth is for Allah

hadith.ar: وَمَا كَانَ لِرَسُولِ اللَّهِ أَنْ يَغُلَّ فَمَنْ يَغْلُلْ يَأْتِ بِمَا غَلَّ يَوْمَ الْقِيَامَةِ
hadith.en: It is not for the Messenger to be treacherous; whoever is treacherous will come with his treachery on the Day of Resurrection

shades.name_en: al-Khums — One-Fifth Allocation and the Categories of Islamic Finance
shades.name_ar: الْخُمُسُ — الْحَصَّةُ الْوَاحِدَةُ مِنَ الْخَمْسَةِ فِي الْفَيْءِ وَالْغَنَائِمِ
shades.explanation: The khums (one-fifth) is the divine allocation specified in 8:41 — one-fifth of all war booty, minerals, and treasures goes to Allah, His Messenger, the relatives, the orphans, the poor, and the traveler. The remaining four-fifths go to the warriors. The khums system reflects Islamic fiscal equity — the divine's share, the prophet's share (and his heirs), the social welfare beneficiaries — all funded by one-fifth of wealth that came through Allah's grace. This system preceded modern progressive taxation by more than a millennium.
shades.hadith_ar: وَمَا كَانَ لِرَسُولِ اللَّهِ أَنْ يَغُلَّ
shades.hadith_en: It is not for the Messenger to be treacherous

meaning.en: Striving, exerting, striving against. The root denotes effort, struggle, and the exertion of one's powers for a purpose.

lexical_analysis.al_raghib: الْجَهْدُ: الْمَشَقَّةُ. وَجَهَدَ الشَّيْءَ: بَالَغَ فِيهِ حَتَّى اسْتَقْصَى مَا فِيهِ

quran_examples.ar: جَـٰهَدَ فِيهِ وَٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوا۟ ۖ وَمَا یَزِدُ ٱللَّهُ ٱلْكَـٰفِرِینَ إِلَّا تَبَابًۭا
quran_examples.en: He strove for it, and those who believed — but Allah does not increase the disbelievers except in loss
quran_examples.context: The jihād of the believing ummah

hadith.ar: الْمُجَاهِدُ مَنْ جَاهَدَ نَفْسَهُ فِي اللَّهِ
hadith.en: The mujahid is the one who strives against his own self for the sake of Allah

shades.name_en: al-Jihad — Striving for the Cause of Allah
shades.name_ar: الْجِهَادُ — بَذْلُ الطَّاقَةِ فِي سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ، قَوْلًا وَفِعْلًا
shades.explanation: The jihad (striving) in the Quran is the comprehensive concept of struggle for the sake of Allah. The famous hadith — «al-mujāhidu man jāhada nafsahu fī Llāh» (the mujāhid is the one who strives against his self for the sake of Allah) — captures the inner dimension: the greater jihād is against the ego's base desires. The outer jihād (defensive war) is also sanctioned — the verse 22:78 calls on the believers to strive in Allah's cause with their wealth and their lives. Ibn al-Qayyim (Zād al-Maʿād) lists more than thirty stations of inner jihād — against despair, against forgetfulness, against hypocrisy, against excessive love of the world, against the influence of Satan.
shades.hadith_ar: الْمُجَاهِدُ مَنْ جَاهَدَ نَفْسَهُ فِي اللَّهِ
shades.hadith_en: The mujahid is the one who strives against his own self for the sake of Allah

meaning.en: To steal. The root denotes the act of taking what belongs to another secretly and without permission.
meaning.ar: أَخْذُ الشَّيْءِ مِنْ غَيْرِ إِذْنِ صَاحِبِهِ، سِرًّا

lexical_analysis.ibn_faris: السَّرِقَةُ: أَخْذُ الشَّيْءِ بِاخْتِلَاسٍ مِنْ حِرْزٍ مِثْلِهِ
lexical_analysis.al_raghib: السَّرِقَةُ: أَخْذُ الْمَالِ مِنَ الْمَالِ الْمَحْرُوزِ بِطَرِيقِ الْخَتْلِ

quran_examples.ar: وَٱلسَّارِقُ وَٱلسَّارِقَةُ فَٱقْطَعُوا۟ أَيْدِيَهُمَا جَزَآءًۢ بِمَا كَسَبَا نَكَـٰلًۭا مِّنَ ٱللَّهِ
quran_examples.en: Cut off the hands of the thief and the thiefess as recompense for what they have earned

hadith.ar: لَعَنَ اللَّهُ السَّارِقَ يَسْرِقُ الْبَيْضَةَ فَتُقْطَعُ يَدُهُ
hadith.en: Allah curses the thief who steals an egg and his hand is cut off

shades.name_en: as-Sariqah — Theft and its Punishment in Islamic Law
shades.name_ar: السَّرِقَةُ — أَخْذُ الْمَالِ بِسِرٍّ، وَحُكْمُهَا فِي الشَّرِيعَةِ
shades.explanation: The sariqah (theft) is one of the most clearly defined crimes in Islamic law. The Quran prescribes the cutting of the hand (qatʿ al-yad) as the hadd punishment — a severe but proportional response designed to deter theft and protect property rights. The hadith — «Allah curses the thief who steals an egg and his hand is cut off» — emphasizes that no theft is too small to be punished, while the Quranic context (5:38) emphasizes the severity: taqwā should restrain the hand from taking what belongs to others.
shades.hadith_ar: لَعَنَ اللَّهُ السَّارِقَ يَسْرِقُ الْبَيْضَةَ فَتُقْطَعُ يَدُهُ
shades.hadith_en: Allah curses the thief who steals an egg and his hand is cut off

meaning.en: To succeed, follow after; successor; the munafiq (hypocrite) — those who claim to follow but actually oppose.
meaning.ar: خَلَفَ: جَاءَ بَعْدَ غَيْرِهِ، أَوْ تَقَدَّمَ عَلَيْهِ. وَالْخُلْفُ: مَنْ يَأْتِي بَعْدَ الْمَاضِينَ

lexical_analysis.ibn_faris: الْخَلْفُ: أَنْ يَأْتِيَ بَعْدَ إِنْسَانٍ. وَالْخُلْفُ أَيْضًا: ضِدُّ الْوَفَاءِ
lexical_analysis.al_raghib: الْخَلْفُ: مَا يَأْتِي بَعْدَ شَيْءٍ. وَيُسْتَعْمَلُ فِي الْخَيْرِ وَالشَّرِّ. وَالْمُنَافِقُونَ: لِأَنَّهُمْ يُظْهِرُونَ الْإِسْلَامَ وَيُبْطِنُونَ غَيْرَهُ، فَهُمْ خُلْفٌ لِلْمُؤْمِنِينَ

quran_examples.ar: وَمِمَّنْ حَوْلَكُم مِّنَ ٱلْأَعْرَابِ مُنَافِقُونَ ۖ وَمِنْ أَهْلِ ٱلْمَدِينَةِ ۖ عَادُوا۟ عَلَى ٱلنِّفَاقِ
quran_examples.en: Among the Bedouins around you and among the people of Medina are hypocrites (munāfiqūn) — they are persistent in hypocrisy
quran_examples.context: The munāfiqūn — those who appear Muslim but harbor disbelief

hadith.ar: أَرْبَعٌ مَنْ كُنَّ فِيهِ كَانَ مُنَافِقًا خَالِصًا
hadith.en: Whoever has these four traits is a pure hypocrite

shades.name_en: al-Munāfiqūn — The Hypocrites and the Diseases of Their Hearts
shades.name_ar: الْمُنَافِقُونَ — الَّذِينَ يُظْهِرُونَ الْإِيمَانَ وَيُسِرُّونَ الْكُفْرَ
shades.explanation: The khalaf and the munafiq (related roots) describe a specific moral pathology: the religious pretender who outwardly professes faith but inwardly harbors disbelief. The hadith of the Prophet identifies four traits of the pure munafiq: when he speaks he lies, when he promises he breaks it, when entrusted he betrays, when he disputes he is obscene. Sūrat al-Munāfiqūn (63) is entirely dedicated to the munāfiqūn in the Prophet's time, exposing their strategies, their dangers, and their eventual divine punishment.
shades.hadith_ar: أَرْبَعٌ مَنْ كُنَّ فِيهِ كَانَ مُنَافِقًا خَالِصًا
shades.hadith_en: Whoever has these four traits is a pure hypocrite

meaning.en: To refuse, decline, reject. The root denotes volitional refusal — the active turning away from something that is offered or demanded.
meaning.ar: الْإِنَاءُ: الْإِمْسَاكُ عَنِ الشَّيْءِ عَلَى سَبِيلِ التَّعَدِّي وَالْكِبْرِ

lexical_analysis.ibn_faris: أَبَيْتُ الشَّيْءَ: أَمْسَكْتُ عَنْهُ عَلَى طَرِيقِ التَّعَدِّي. وَالْإِبَاءُ: ضِدُّ الْقَبُولِ
lexical_analysis.al_raghib: الْإِبَاءُ: الْإِمْسَاكُ عَمَّا يُمْكِنُ فِعْلُهُ. وَهُوَ ضِدُّ الْقَبُولِ. وَيَكُونُ مَحْمُودًا إِذَا كَانَ الْمُتْرُوكُ قَبِيحًا

quran_examples.ar: وَإِذْ قُلْنَا لِلْمَلَـٰٓئِكَةِ ٱسْجُدُوا۟ لِـَٔادَمَ فَسَجَدُوٓا۟ إِلَّآ إِبْلِيسَ أَبَىٰ وَٱسْتَكْبَرَ
quran_examples.en: When We said to the angels: Prostrate to Adam — they prostrated except Iblīs, who refused (abā) and was arrogant
quran_examples.context: Iblīs's refusal to prostrate — the original arrogance

hadith.ar: إِنَّ اللَّهَ قَالَ: مَنْ عَادَى لِي وَلِيًّا فَقَدْ آذَنْتُهُ بِالْحَرْبِ
hadith.en: Allah said: Whoever is hostile to a friend of Mine, I have declared war against him

shades.name_en: al-Ibāʾ — Refusal as Moral Choice, Pride, or Integrity
shades.name_ar: الْإِبَاءُ — الْإِمْسَاكُ عَنِ الشَّيْءِ أَمَامَ التَّعَدِّي، أَوِ الِاسْتِكْبَارِ
shades.explanation: The ibāʾ (refusal) in the Quran is the moral quality of volitional refusal. It is the most severe in Iblīs's abā to prostrate (2:34) — the original act of pride and disobedience. It is also the legitimate ethical stance when truth demands refusal: the man in Sūrat al-ʿAlaq (96:9-10) who refuses to disobey Allah, the believers who refuse to commit shirk even under persecution, the Prophet who refuses to compromise the message. The ibāʾ is therefore both the most dangerous and the most necessary of moral acts — its value depends entirely on what is being refused.
shades.hadith_ar: إِنَّ اللَّهَ قَالَ: مَنْ عَادَى لِي وَلِيًّا فَقَدْ آذَنْتُهُ بِالْحَرْبِ
shades.hadith_en: Allah said: Whoever is hostile to a friend of Mine, I have declared war against him

meaning.en: Confusion, perplexity, being at a loss. The root denotes the mental state of not knowing what to do — particularly in the face of unexpected or overwhelming events.
meaning.ar: التَّحَيُّرُ: عَدَمُ الْمَعْرِفَةِ بِمَا يُفْعَلُ مِنْ أَمْرٍ

lexical_analysis.al_raghib: التَّحَيُّرُ: دَهَشٌ يَعْرِضُ لِلْإِنْسَانِ مِنْ فَزْعٍ أَوْ سُرُورٍ أَوْ تَحَيُّرٍ فِي أَمْرٍ

quran_examples.ar: الٓمٓ ۚ غُلِبَتِ ٱلرُّومُ
quran_examples.en: Alif Lām Meem. The Romans have been defeated
quran_examples.context: The opening of Sūrat al-Rūm — about the defeat of the Byzantines

hadith.ar: إِنَّ اللَّهَ جَعَلَ لِكُلِّ أَمْرٍ سَعَةً وَلِكُلِّ سَعَةٍ أَجَلًا
hadith.en: Allah has appointed a duration and a deadline for every matter

shades.name_en: at-Tahayyur — Confusion in the Face of the Divine Order
shades.name_ar: التَّحَيُّرُ — الْحَيْرَةُ أَمَامَ عَظَمَةِ الْأَمْرِ الْإِلٰهِيِّ
shades.explanation: The tahayyur (confusion, perplexity) is the mental state described by the verb hayira — to be at a loss. The verse 6:71 — about the Prophet fearing that his people would flee from his message — uses the form nahāra nushūrā, implying the state of inner disturbance. The phenomenon of hayrah is the soul's response to encountering something beyond its comprehension — particularly the divine revelation. The Quran presents hayrah as a state the believer may experience but should not settle in: hayrah is the beginning of wisdom (recognizing one's limits) but not its end (seeking knowledge dispels it).
shades.hadith_ar: إِنَّ اللَّهَ جَعَلَ لِكُلِّ أَمْرٍ سَعَةً
shades.hadith_en: Allah has appointed a duration for every matter

meaning.en: Sin, crime, transgression. The root denotes the act that incurs guilt or blame — particularly the violation of divine command.

lexical_analysis.ibn_faris: الْإِثْمُ: مَا يَعْصَى اللَّهُ بِهِ. وَالْآثَامُ: الذُّنُوبُ. وَهُوَ ضِدُّ الْبِرِّ
lexical_analysis.al_raghib: الْإِثْمُ: جُزْءٌ مِنَ الْعَقَابِ. وَاسْتِعْمَالُ الْإِثْمِ فِي الذَّنْبِ لِأَنَّ الذَّنْبَ سَبَبُ الْإِثْمِ

quran_examples.ar: لَيْسَ عَلَيْكُمْ جُنَاحٌ أَن تَبْتَغُوا۟ فَضْلًۭا مِّن رَّبِّكُمْ ۚ فَإِذَآ أَفِضْتُم مِّنَ عَرَفَـٰتٍۢ فَٱذْكُرُوا۟ ٱللَّهَ عِندَ ٱلْمَشْعَرِ ٱلْحَرَامِ
quran_examples.en: There is no sin upon you for seeking bounty from your Lord
quran_examples.context: Commercial activity in the Hajj is not an ism

hadith.ar: لَا يَزْنِي الزَّانِي حِينَ يَزْنِي وَهُوَ مُؤْمِنٌ
hadith.en: The adulterer does not commit adultery while he is a believer

shades.name_en: al-Ithm — Sin as Violation of Divine Command
shades.explanation: The ithm (sin, crime) in the Quran denotes the act that violates divine law and incurs moral liability. The Quran distinguishes between al-ithm al-mu'tad (habitual sin — 25:68) and al-ithm al-mu'aththan (major sin — 4:31), as well as between sins that are forgiven (with taubah) and those that are not (without taubah). The ithm is not just an act but a state of the soul: the person who commits the ithm has been distanced from Allah by their own choice, and the only path back is taubah.
shades.hadith_ar: لَا يَزْنِي الزَّانِي حِينَ يَزْنِي وَهُوَ مُؤْمِنٌ
shades.hadith_en: The adulterer does not commit adultery while he is a believer

meaning.en: Pushing, driving away, repelling with force. The root denotes the act of forcefully pushing away — particularly someone or something repugnant.

lexical_analysis.al_raghib: الدَّفْرُ: الدَّفْعُ بِالطَّرْفِ. وَيُسْتَعْمَلُ فِي الطَّرْدِ بِالطَّرِيقِ الْمَكْرُوهِ

quran_examples.ar: مَّن يُرِدِ ٱللَّهُ بِهِۦ خَيْرًۭا يُصِفْهُ مِنَ ٱلْمُتْقِينَ
quran_examples.en: Whomever Allah wishes good for, He makes him among the muttaqūn

hadith.ar: لَا تَقُصُّصْ رُؤْيَاكَ عَلَى إِخْوَتِكَ فَيَكِيدُوا لَكَ كَيْدًا
hadith.en: Do not narrate your dream to your brothers lest they plot against you

shades.name_en: ad-Dafr — Driving Away the Impure and Repelling Evil
shades.name_ar: الدَّفْرُ — الطَّرْدُ بِالطَّرِيقِ الْمَكْرُوهِ، أَوِ الدَّفْعُ بِقُوَّةٍ
shades.explanation: The dafr (driving away) in the Quran appears in limited contexts but is a vivid image of forceful repulsion. The verse 83:13 describes the wicked «in adfāri nār» — in the driving blasts of fire. The dafr is the mode of expelling the demonic: the Prophet ﷺ taught seeking refuge from the evil whisperer, the dfr is the divine rejection of the kāfir on the Last Day, the rejection of evil whispers and wrongful actions. The dafr is the divine act of purification by exclusion: the holy and the pure is preserved by driving out the impure and the corrupt.
shades.hadith_ar: لَا تَقُصُّصْ رُؤْيَاكَ عَلَى إِخْوَتِكَ
shades.hadith_en: Do not narrate your dream to your brothers lest they plot against you

meaning.en: Letter, edge, extremity. The root denotes the outer edge of a thing — in grammar, a single letter of the alphabet.
meaning.ar: الْحَرْفُ: الطَّرَفُ وَالْحَدُّ، وَالْحَرْفُ مِنَ الْحُرُوفِ: أَصْلُ الْكَلِمَةِ

lexical_analysis.ibn_faris: الْحَرْفُ: الطَّرَفُ. وَكُلُّ شَيْءٍ لَهُ طَرَفٌ فَقَدْ حَرُفَ
lexical_analysis.al_raghib: الْحَرْفُ: الطَّرَفُ الْمُنْقَطِعُ عَنِ الشَّيْءِ. وَيُسْتَعْمَلُ فِي الْحُرُوفِ الَّتِي هِيَ أَصْلُ الْكَلَامِ

quran_examples.ar: مَّا يَسۡتَوِى ٱلْأَعْمَىٰ وَٱلْبَصِيرُ
quran_examples.en: Not equal are the blind and the seeing
quran_examples.context: The contrasting pair of sight and blindness

hadith.ar: أُفٍّ لِلرَّجُلِ يَقُصُّ عَلَيَّ الرُّؤْيَا يَعْجَزُ عَنْ تَفْسِيرِهَا
hadith.en: How awful for the man who narrates his dream to me and cannot interpret it

shades.name_en: al-Ḥarf — Letter, Sound, and the Building Blocks of Speech
shades.explanation: The ḥarf (letter, edge) in the Quran has two distinct uses. First, as a linguistic unit — the letters that make up speech. Sūrat al-Ḥijr opens with «alif lām rā» (1:1), the discrete letters of the Arabic alphabet, marking the divine authorship of language itself. Second, as an extremity or edge — the most subtle part of a thing. The hadith «innna llāha lā yaqbidhi ʿilman bi-naz'ihi min al-ʿibād» (Allah does not seize knowledge by removing it — Bukhārī 60) uses related terms to describe divine knowledge. The ḥarf in the Quran represents the most subtle and indivisible level of divine speech.
shades.hadith_ar: أُفٍّ لِلرَّجُلِ يَقُصُّ عَلَيَّ الرُّؤْيَا يَعْجَزُ عَنْ تَفْسِيرِهَا
shades.hadith_en: How awful for the man who narrates his dream to me and cannot interpret it

meaning.en: Chest, breast; the inner self. The root denotes the chest — both the physical location of the heart and lungs, and the seat of consciousness, intention, and faith.
meaning.ar: الصَّدْرُ: مُسْتَوْدَعُ النَّفْسِ وَالْقَلْبِ، وَمَكَانُ الْإِرَادَةِ وَالِاعْتِقَادِ

lexical_analysis.ibn_faris: الصَّدْرُ: أَعْلَى الْبَطْنِ. وَصَدْرُ الْإِنْسَانِ: مُسْتَوْدَعُ قَلْبِهِ
lexical_analysis.al_raghib: الصَّدْرُ: أَعْلَى الْبَطْنِ. وَيُسْتَعْمَلُ فِي مَوْطِنِ الْإِدْرَاكِ مِنَ الْإِنْسَانِ، وَهُوَ مَوْضِعُ الْقَلْبِ

quran_examples.ar: قُلْ إِن تُخْفُوا۟ مَا فِى صُدُورِكُمْ أَوْ تُبْدُوهُ يَعْلَمْهُ ٱللَّهُ
quran_examples.en: Say: Whether you conceal what is in your chests or reveal it, Allah knows it
quran_examples.context: Divine knowledge of the chest's contents

hadith.ar: أَلَا وَإِنَّ فِي الْجَسَدِ مُضْغَةً، إِذَا صَلَحَتْ صَلَحَ الْجَسَدُ كُلُّهُ
hadith.en: In the body there is a morsel — if it is sound, the whole body is sound; if it is corrupt, the whole body is corrupt — it is the heart

shades.name_en: aṣ-Ṣadr — The Chest as Seat of Consciousness and Faith
shades.name_ar: الصَّدْرُ — مَوْطِنُ الْإِيمَانِ وَمَكَانُ الِاعْتِقَادِ وَالْإِرَادَةِ
shades.explanation: The ṣadr (chest) in the Quran is the physical chest and, metaphorically, the inner self — the place where faith, intention, and consciousness reside. The verse 3:29 establishes that Allah knows what is in the ṣudūr (chests, plural) of His servants. The Islamic tradition developed an extensive spirituality of the ṣadr: its expansion (inshirāḥ) through faith and remembrance, its constriction (ʿiqāb) through sin and heedlessness. The Prophet ﷺ used to seek refuge from anxiety in the ṣadr (al-ḥamm wa-l-ḥuzn) and the deficient capacity to deal with it — a fundamental spiritual concern.
shades.hadith_ar: أَلَا وَإِنَّ فِي الْجَسَدِ مُضْغَةً، إِذَا صَلَحَتْ صَلَحَ الْجَسَدُ كُلُّهُ، وَإِذَا فَسَدَتْ فَسَدَ الْجَسَدُ كُلُّهُ، أَلَا وَهِيَ الْقَلْبُ
shades.hadith_en: In the body there is a morsel — if it is sound, the whole body is sound; if it is corrupt, the whole body is corrupt — it is the heart

meaning.en: Term, appointed time, deadline. The root denotes a fixed, determined time — particularly the term of life or the appointed time of an event.

lexical_analysis.ibn_faris: الْأَجَلُ: الْمُدَّةُ الَّتِي لَهَا نِهَايَةٌ مَحْدُودَةٌ. وَأَجَلُ الْمَوْتِ: الْمُدَّةُ الْمَحْدُودَةُ لِلْوَفَاةِ
lexical_analysis.al_raghib: الْأَجَلُ: الْمُدَّةُ الْمَحْدُودَةُ الَّتِي لَا يَعْلَمُ انْتِهَاءَهَا إِلَّا اللَّهُ. وَأَجَلُ الْوَفَاةِ: الْمُدَّةُ الْمَحْدُودَةُ لِانْتِهَاءِ الْعُمْرِ

quran_examples.ar: وَمَا كَانَ لِنَفْسٍ أَن تَمُوتَ إِلَّا بِإِذْنِ ٱللَّهِ كِتَـٰبًۭا مُّؤَجَّلًۭا ۗ وَمَن يُرِدۡ ثَوَابَ ٱلدُّنْيَا نُؤْتِهِۦ مِنْهَا وَمَن يُرِدۡ ثَوَابَ ٱلْـَٔاخِرَةِ نُؤْتِهِۥ مِنْهَا
quran_examples.en: No soul dies except by Allah's permission, at an appointed term (kitāb mu'ajjal)
quran_examples.context: The divine term of life is fixed and cannot be altered

hadith.ar: كُلُّ ابْنِ آدَمَ خَطَّاءٌ، وَخَيْرُ الْخَطَّائِينَ التَّوَّابُونَ
hadith.en: Every son of Adam is a sinner, and the best of sinners are those who repent

shades.name_en: al-Ajal — The Divine Term and the Appointed Time of All Things
shades.name_ar: الْأَجَلُ — الْمُدَّةُ الْمَحْدُودَةُ الَّتِي قَدَّرَهَا اللَّهُ لِكُلِّ شَيْءٍ
shades.explanation: The ajal (appointed term) in the Quran is the divinely ordained duration for each created thing — the lifespan of every soul, the duration of every nation, the time of every event. The verse 3:145 emphasizes that no soul dies except by Allah's permission, at a term written (kitāb mu'ajjal). The ajal is the cornerstone of the Islamic theology of qadar — the divine predestination that gives every life its specific duration. Al-Ghazālī (Iḥyāʾ, Book of Death) argues that awareness of the ajal is the foundation of spiritual preparation: knowing that the term is fixed, the believer works constantly as if tomorrow is the day of meeting.
shades.hadith_ar: كُلُّ ابْنِ آدَمَ خَطَّاءٌ، وَخَيْرُ الْخَطَّائِينَ التَّوَّابُونَ
shades.hadith_en: Every son of Adam is a sinner, and the best of sinners are those who repent

meaning.en: To forget, overlook. The root denotes the failure to remember or the act of leaving something out.
meaning.ar: تَرْكُ الِانْتِبَاهِ وَغَيْبَةُ الشَّيْءِ عَنِ الذِّكْرِ

lexical_analysis.ibn_faris: النِّسْيَانُ: غَيْبَةُ الشَّيْءِ عَنِ الذِّكْرِ مَعَ كَوْنِهِ مَحْفُوظًا
lexical_analysis.al_raghib: النِّسْيَانُ: غَيْبَةُ الشَّيْءِ عَنِ الْخَاطِرِ، وَهُوَ ضِدُّ الذِّكْرِ

quran_examples.ar: مَا نَنسَخۡ مِنْ ءَايَةٍ أَوۡ نُنسِهَا نَأۡتِ بِخَيۡرٍۢ مِّنۡهَآ أَوۡ مِثۡلِهَآ
quran_examples.en: Whatever verse We abrogate or cause to be forgotten, We bring a better one or the like
quran_examples.context: Divine naskh and divine nisyān — the verses that may be abrogated

hadith.ar: نِسْيَانُ الْقُرْآنِ نَسْيَانُ الْحَظِّ مِنَ الْإِسْلَامِ
hadith.en: Forgetting the Quran is heedlessness of Islam

shades.name_en: an-Nisyān — Human Forgetting and Divine Remembrance
shades.name_ar: النِّسْيَانُ — غَيْبَةُ الشَّيْءِ عَنِ الذِّكْرِ، ضِدُّ الْحِفْظِ وَالذِّكْرِ
shades.explanation: The nisyān (forgetting) in the Quran has two dimensions. (1) Human nisyān — the natural tendency to forget, to be distracted from remembrance, to err from forgetfulness (not from deliberate intent). (2) Divine nisyān (rare) — the verse 2:106 establishes that Allah may cause a verse to be forgotten in the abrogation process — a deliberate act of divine wisdom. The human cure for human nisyān is dhikr (remembrance) — the constant calling back to Allah. The hadith «nisyānu l-qurʾāni nisyānu l-ḥizz» (forgetting the Quran is the heedlessness of Islam) emphasizes that nisyān is a moral failure, not merely a cognitive one.
shades.hadith_ar: نِسْيَانُ الْقُرْآنِ نَسْيَانُ الْحَظِّ مِنَ الْإِسْلَامِ
shades.hadith_en: Forgetting the Quran is heedlessness of Islam

meaning.en: To hope, expect. The root denotes the expectation of good — the heart's anticipation of what is desired.

lexical_analysis.ibn_faris: الرَّجَاءُ: الْأَمَلُ. وَرَجَوْتُ الشَّيْءَ: أَمَّلْتُهُ
lexical_analysis.al_raghib: الرَّجَاءُ: تَوَقُّعُ الشَّيْءِ الْمَحْبُوبِ مَعَ طَلَبِهِ. وَهُوَ ضِدُّ الْيَأْسِ

quran_examples.ar: أُو۟لَـٰٓئِكَ ٱلَّذِينَ يَدْعُونَ يَبْتَغُونَ إِلَىٰ رَبِّهِمُ ٱلْوَسِيلَةَ أَيُّهُمْ أَقْرَبُ وَيَرْجُونَ رَحْمَتَهُۥ
quran_examples.en: Those they call upon themselves seek a way to their Lord — which of them would be nearest — and they hope for His mercy
quran_examples.context: The hope of those who worship besides Allah

hadith.ar: لَا يَقُولَنَّ أَحَدُكُمُ اللَّهُمَّ اغْفِرْ لِي إِنْ شِئْتَ، وَلْيَعْزِمِ الْمَسْأَلَةَ
hadith.en: None of you should say: O Allah, forgive me if You will. Let him be definite in asking

shades.name_en: ar-Rajāʾ — Hope as the Engine of Spiritual Action
shades.name_ar: الرَّجَاءُ — تَوَقُّعُ الْخَيْرِ مَعَ طَلَبِهِ، وَهُوَ ضِدُّ الْيَأْسِ
shades.explanation: The rajāʾ (hope) is the divine counterpart of khawf (fear) — together they form the bipolar emotional structure of the Islamic spiritual life. Al-Ghazālī (Iḥyāʾ, Book of Hope and Fear) analyzes rajāʾ as the motivation of those who seek to draw closer to Allah. Unlike al-ʿamal (hope — the stronger, more assertive form), al-rajāʾ is the gentler, more passive expectation — but both are essential. Rajāʾ without fear produces carelessness; fear without rajāʾ produces despair. The Prophet's supplication — «Allāhumma innī aṣ'aluka l-hudā wa-l-ʿaqābata wa-l-ʿāfiyata fī l-dunyā wa-l-ākhirah» (O Allah, I ask You for guidance, righteousness, and well-being in this world and the Hereafter) — expresses the rajāʾ that combines realistic hope with realistic fear.
shades.hadith_ar: لَا يَقُولَنَّ أَحَدُكُمُ اللَّهُمَّ اغْفِرْ لِي إِنْ شِئْتَ، وَلْيَعْزِمِ الْمَسْأَلَةَ
shades.hadith_en: None of you should say: O Allah, forgive me if You will. Let him be definite in asking

meaning.en: To fear, be afraid. The root denotes fear of a real or anticipated harm — particularly the fear of Allah which is the beginning of wisdom.
meaning.ar: الْفَزَعُ مِنَ الشَّيْءِ، خَاصَّةً خَوْفُ اللَّهِ

lexical_analysis.ibn_faris: الْخَوْفُ: فَزَعُ النَّفْسِ مِنْ شَيْءٍ تُحِبُّ الْحِرْزَ مِنْهُ
lexical_analysis.al_raghib: الْخَوْفُ: تَوَقُّعُ الشَّيْءِ الْمَكْرُوهِ مَعَ التَّهَيُّبِ. وَهُوَ ضِدُّ الْأَمْنِ

quran_examples.ar: فَلَا تَخْشَوْهُمْ وَٱخْشَوْنِى وَلِأُتِمَّ نِعْمَتِى عَلَيْكُمْ وَلَعَلَّكُمْ تَهْتَدُونَ
quran_examples.en: Do not fear them — fear Me, and so that I may complete My favor upon you, that you may be guided
quran_examples.context: The divine command to fear Allah over all other objects of fear

hadith.ar: لَا يُؤْمِنُ أَحَدُكُمْ حَتَّى يُحِبَّ لِأَخِيهِ مَا يُحِبُّ لِنَفْسِهِ
hadith.en: None of you truly believes until he loves for his brother what he loves for himself

shades.name_en: al-Khawf — The Fear of Allah as Foundation of Wisdom
shades.name_ar: الْخَوْفُ — فَزَعُ النَّفْسِ مِنْ عَذَابِ اللَّهِ، وَتَهَيُّبُ مَلَكُوتِهِ
shades.explanation: The khawf (fear) in the Quran is the third of the three spiritual states mentioned together with rajāʾ (hope) and ḥubb (love). Khawf is the awe-filled fear of divine majesty — not the panic of helplessness but the responsive humility of the creature before the Creator. The verse 2:150 establishes the hierarchy: «do not fear them, fear Me» — the divine khawf is to be prioritized over all worldly fears. Al-Ghazālī (Iḥyāʾ, Book of Hope and Fear) treats khawf as one of the highest spiritual stations — the more one knows Allah, the more one fears Allah, but the fear is seasoned by hope so that it does not become despair.
shades.hadith_ar: إِنَّمَا الْمُؤْمِنُونَ الَّذِينَ إِذَا ذُكِرَ اللَّهُ وَجِلَتْ قُلُوبُهُمْ
shades.hadith_en: The believers are those whose hearts tremble when Allah is mentioned

meaning.en: Lost, squandered, wasted. The root denotes the state of being wasted or destroyed — opposite of preservation.
meaning.ar: الذَّهَابُ ضَيَاعًا، إِتْلَافُ الشَّيْءِ بِلَا فَائِدَةٍ

lexical_analysis.al_raghib: الضَّيْعُ: إِتْلَافُ الشَّيْءِ حَتَّى يَذْهَبَ. وَيُسْتَعْمَلُ فِي كُلِّ مَا لَا انْتِفَاعَ فِيهِ

quran_examples.ar: إِذْ قَالَ لِقَوْمِهِۦ يَـٰقَوْمِ أَيُّهُم يُنصُرُنِىٓ إِلَى ٱللَّهِ ۖ قَدۡ خَسِرَ ٱلَّذِينَ كَذَبُوا۟ وَفَجَرُوا۟
quran_examples.en: When he said to his people: Who would help me toward Allah? Those who denied and were defiant have indeed lost
quran_examples.context: Noah warns his people about their loss

hadith.ar: لَا تَزُولُ قَدَمَا الْعَبْدِ يَوْمَ الْقِيَامَةِ حَتَّى يُسْأَلَ عَنْ عُمُرِهِ فِيمَ أَفْنَاهُ
hadith.en: The servants feet will not move on the Day of Resurrection until he is asked about his age — how he spent it

shades.name_en: aḍ-Ḍayʿ — The Wasted Life and the State of Loss
shades.name_ar: الضَّيْعُ — إِتْلَافُ النَّفْسِ وَالْعُمْرِ بِلَا طَاعَةٍ
shades.explanation: The ḍayʿ (loss, being wasted) in the Quran describes the state of those who have wasted their lives, their opportunities, and their faculties — the opposite of ihṣān (excellence in use). The verse 11:42 establishes khusr (loss) as the consequence of denying Allah and persisting in corruption. The verse 2:143 emphasizes that the Muslim ummah must not be ḍayʿ (wasted, deviant, lost) but must remain on the middle path. The ḍayʿ is the state of those who have not used their resources — time, talents, wealth, opportunities — for what they were created for.
shades.hadith_ar: لَا تَزُولُ قَدَمَا الْعَبْدِ يَوْمَ الْقِيَامَةِ حَتَّى يُسْأَلَ عَنْ عُمُرِهِ فِيمَ أَفْنَاهُ
shades.hadith_en: The servants feet will not move on the Day of Resurrection until he is asked about his age — how he spent it

meaning.en: To fulfill completely, pay in full. The root denotes the completion of a debt, promise, or obligation in its entirety.

lexical_analysis.ibn_faris: الْوَفَاءُ: إِتْمَامُ الشَّيْءِ عَلَى وُجُوهِهِ. وَأَوْفَى الشَّيْءَ: أَتَمَّهُ
lexical_analysis.al_raghib: الْوَفَاءُ: أَدَاءُ الْحَقِّ الْوَاجِبِ، أَوِ الْوَعْدِ، أَوِ الْعَهْدِ كَامِلًا

quran_examples.ar: وَإِنَّ ٱللَّهَ لَا يُضِيعُ أَجْرَ ٱلْمُحْسِنِينَ
quran_examples.en: Indeed Allah does not waste the reward of those who do good
quran_examples.context: Allah's wafāʾ (fulfillment) of His promise to the muḥsinīn

hadith.ar: آيَةُ الْمُنَافِقِ ثَلَاثٌ: إِذَا حَدَّثَ كَذَبَ، وَإِذَا وَعَدَ أَخْلَفَ
hadith.en: The sign of the hypocrite is three: when he speaks he lies, when he promises he breaks it

shades.name_en: al-Wafāʾ — The Fulfillment of Promises, Covenants, and Debts
shades.name_ar: الْوَفَاءُ — إِتْمَامُ الْوَعْدِ وَالْعَهْدِ وَالدَّيْنِ كَامِلًا
shades.explanation: The wafāʾ (fulfillment) is one of the most emphasized moral qualities in Islam. The verse 5:1 commands: «awfū bi-l-ʿuhūd» (fulfill the covenants) — the divine obligation that applies to all covenants, contracts, and promises. The wafāʾ is a divine attribute as well: Allah is al-Wafī (the Fulfiller — described in the hadith qudsī) who keeps His promises and fulfills His covenants.
