The opposite is khudhlān (breach) — the moral corruption of the munāfiq who promises and breaks, who covenants and betrays. The wafāʾ is the foundation of trust (amāna) and social cohesion.
shades.hadith_ar: آيَةُ الْمُنَافِقِ ثَلَاثٌ: إِذَا حَدَّثَ كَذَبَ، وَإِذَا وَعَدَ أَخْلَفَ
shades.hadith_en: The sign of the hypocrite is three: when he speaks he lies, when he promises he breaks it

meaning.en: Profit, gain. The root denotes the increase or benefit from a transaction — the opposite of loss (khusrān).
meaning.ar: الرِّبْحُ: الزِّيَادَةُ فِي الْعَقْدِ عَلَى الْأَصْلِ، وَهُوَ ضِدُّ الْخُسْرَانِ

lexical_analysis.ibn_faris: الرِّبْحُ: نَقِيضُ الْخُسْرَانِ. وَرَبَحَ الشَّيْءَ: زَادَ عَلَيْهِ
lexical_analysis.al_raghib: الرِّبْحُ: الزِّيَادَةُ عَلَى رَأْسِ الْمَالِ. وَالرَّابِحُ: الَّذِي يَزِيدُ عَلَى رَأْسِ مَالِهِ

quran_examples.ar: أُو۟لَـٰٓئِكَ ٱلَّذِينَ ٱشْتَرَوُا۟ ٱلضَّلَـٰلَةَ بِٱلْهُدَىٰ فَمَا رَبِحَت تِّجَـٰرَتُهُمْ
quran_examples.en: Those who purchased misguidance in exchange for guidance — their trade has brought no profit
quran_examples.context: The spiritual metaphor of trading and loss

hadith.ar: لَوْ أَنَّ لِابْنِ آدَمَ وَادِيَيْنِ مِنْ ذَهَبٍ لَابْتَغَى إِلَيْهِمَا ثَالِثًا
hadith.en: If the son of Adam had two valleys of gold, he would desire a third

shades.name_en: ar-Ribḥ — Profit in This World and the Hereafter
shades.name_ar: الرِّبْحُ — الزِّيَادَةُ عَلَى رَأْسِ الْمَالِ، وَالْفَوْزُ بِالْأَجْرِ
shades.explanation: The ribḥ (profit) in the Quran is used both in the literal commercial sense (2:279) and metaphorically for spiritual gain. The verse 2:16 compares the exchange of misguidance for guidance (or vice versa) to commercial transactions — and the result is either ribḥ or khusrān. The verse 2:279 prohibits ribā (usury) while permitting bayʿ (sale) — emphasizing that legitimate profit is permitted but exploitative gain is not. The true ribḥ is the spiritual: the gain from īmān, taqwā, and good deeds is the ultimate ribḥ.
shades.hadith_ar: لَوْ أَنَّ لِابْنِ آدَمَ وَادِيَيْنِ مِنْ ذَهَبٍ لَابْتَغَى إِلَيْهِمَا ثَالِثًا
shades.hadith_en: If the son of Adam had two valleys of gold, he would desire a third

meaning.en: Religion, way of life; debt, obligation; judgment, recompense. The root denotes both the system of belief and practice (the dīn) and the system of obligation and recompense (the din).
meaning.ar: الدِّينُ: الْجَزَاءُ وَالْحِسَابُ، وَأَيْضًا: الْمِلَّةُ وَالشَّرِيعَةُ

lexical_analysis.ibn_faris: الدِّينُ: الْجَزَاءُ. وَقَوْلُهُمْ: دِينُ الرَّجُلِ: مَا لَهُ عَلَيْهِ مِنَ الْحَقِّ. وَأَيْضًا: الطَّاعَةُ وَالْمِلَّةُ
lexical_analysis.al_raghib: الدِّينُ فِي الْأَصْلِ: الْجَزَاءُ. ثُمَّ أُطْلِقَ عَلَى الْحُكْمِ، ثُمَّ عَلَى الطَّاعَةِ، ثُمَّ عَلَى الْمِلَّةِ

quran_examples.ar: مَـٰلِكِ يَوْمِ ٱلدِّينِ
quran_examples.en: Master of the Day of Recompense
quran_examples.context: The opening of al-Fātiḥah — the foundation of tawḥīd

hadith.ar: مَالُ الْيَتِيمِ ظُلْمٌ إِذَا ضَيَّعَهُ مَنْ كَانَ وَلِيَّهُ
hadith.en: The wealth of the orphan is a violation (zulm) if the one responsible for him squanders it

shades.name_en: al-Dīn — Religion as the Comprehensive System of Way and Accountability
shades.name_ar: الدِّينُ — الشَّرِيعَةُ الْإِلٰهِيَّةُ، أَوِ الْحِسَابُ وَالْجَزَاءُ
shades.explanation: The dīn (religion) is the comprehensive term for the system of belief, practice, and accountability established by Allah. The verse 1:4 — Māliki yawm al-dīn (Master of the Day of Recompense) — frames dīn as the divine accounting on the Day of Resurrection. The verse 5:3 — «innī khtartuka wa-staḍḍa'tuka li-l-islāma l-dīna» (today I have perfected your religion for you) — establishes dīn as Islam in its complete form. Al-Ghazālī distinguishes: dīn as the structure of divine commands and prohibitions; dīn as the inner state of ʿibāda and dīn as the system of accountability — all unified under the same term.
shades.hadith_ar: مَالُ الْيَتِيمِ ظُلْمٌ إِذَا ضَيَّعَهُ مَنْ كَانَ وَلِيَّهُ
shades.hadith_en: The wealth of the orphan is a violation (zulm) if the one responsible for him squanders it

meaning.en: To earn, acquire, gain. The root denotes the action of acquiring something through effort — particularly moral deeds or worldly sustenance.

lexical_analysis.ibn_faris: الْكَسْبُ: اكْتِسَابُ الشَّيْءِ. وَالْكَسْبُ أَخَصُّ مِنَ الطَّلَبِ
lexical_analysis.al_raghib: الْكَسْبُ: طَلَبُ الشَّيْءِ بِحِيلَةٍ. وَيُسْتَعْمَلُ فِي الْخَيْرِ وَالشَّرِّ. وَفِي الشَّرِيعَةِ: تَكَلُّفُ تَحْصِيلِ الْمَالِ مِنْ وَجْهِ الشَّرْعِ

quran_examples.ar: أُو۟لَـٰٓئِكَ لَهُمْ نَصِيبٌۭ مِّمَّا كَسَبُوا۟ ۚ وَٱللَّهُ سَرِيعُ ٱلْحِسَابِ
quran_examples.en: These have a portion of what they have earned, and Allah is swift in reckoning
quran_examples.context: Every soul receives what it earned

hadith.ar: كُلُّ ابْنِ آدَمَ خَطَّاءٌ، وَخَيْرُ الْخَطَّائِينَ التَّوَّابُونَ
hadith.en: Every son of Adam is a sinner, and the best of sinners are those who repent

shades.name_en: al-Kasb — Earning as the Foundation of Accountability
shades.name_ar: الْكَسْبُ — تَكَلُّفُ تَحْصِيلِ الشَّيْءِ بِسَعْيٍ، وَأَصْلُ الْمَسْؤُولِيَّةِ
shades.explanation: The kasb (earning) is the Quran's central concept for the moral responsibility of every human soul. The verse 2:202 establishes the principle: «these have a portion of what they have earned, and Allah is swift in reckoning» — every soul is precisely accountable for its kasb. The kasb is not only what one does but also what one intends, what one says, what one feels — the comprehensive concept of moral acquisition. The hadith — «kullu ibn ādama khāṭiʾ» (every son of Adam is a sinner) — establishes the universal need for taubah to compensate for human kasb al-khāṭiʾ (acquisition of error).
shades.hadith_ar: كُلُّ ابْنِ آدَمَ خَطَّاءٌ، وَخَيْرُ الْخَطَّائِينَ التَّوَّابُونَ
shades.hadith_en: Every son of Adam is a sinner, and the best of sinners are those who repent

meaning.en: Coming, bringing. The variant form of jāʾa — to come or bring something, particularly at the appointed time.
meaning.ar: الْمَجِيءُ، وَهُوَ قَرِيبٌ مِنْ جَاءَ، وَلَكِنَّهُ يُفِيدُ التَّعَجُّلَ فِي الْمَجِيءِ أَحْيَانًا

lexical_analysis.al_raghib: جِيءٌ: مَصْدَرُ جَاءَ بِمَعْنَى الْمَجِيءِ. وَجِيءٌ بِالشَّيْءِ: إِحْضَارُهُ

quran_examples.ar: قَالَ عِفۡرِيتٌۭ مِّنَ ٱلۡجِنِّ أَنَا۠ ءَاتِيكَ بِهِۦ قَبۡلَ أَن تَقُومَ مِن مَّقَامِكَ ۖ وَإِنِّى عَلَيۡهِ لَقَوِىٌ أَمِينٌ
quran_examples.en: An ʿifrīt of the jinn said: I will bring it to you before you rise from your seat, and I am strong and trustworthy
quran_examples.context: The throne of Bilqis brought by the ʿifrīt

hadith.ar: أَتَاكُمْ رَسُولُنَا يُبَيِّنُ لَكُمْ ۖ فَوَلَّوْا وَأَعْرَضُوا وَقَالُوا اللَّهُ جَاءَ بِالْحَقِّ
hadith.en: Our messenger came to make clear to you, but you turned away and said: Allah has brought the truth

shades.name_en: al-Jīʾ — The Arrival of the Decree and the Eschatological Coming
shades.name_ar: الْجِيءُ — حُضُورُ الشَّيْءِ، وَمَجِيءُ الْأَمْرِ وَقْتَ وَقُوعِهِ
shades.explanation: The jīʾ is the variant/intensive form of jāʾa — emphasizing the act of coming or bringing. The Quran's most striking uses of jīʾ appear in eschatological contexts: «when they see what they were promised, they will know who is weaker in helpers and fewer in numbers» (72:24), and in the description of the angels' gathering on the Last Day. The jīʾ is the moment of arrival — when what was promised becomes present, what was hidden becomes manifest, what was distant draws near.
shades.hadith_ar: أَتَاكُمْ رَسُولُنَا يُبَيِّنُ لَكُمْ
shades.hadith_en: Our messenger came to make clear to you

meaning.en: Brother. The variant form of akh — brother; the root also produces the plural ikhwah.
meaning.ar: الْأَخُ مِنَ النَّسَبِ أَوْ فِي الدِّينِ

lexical_analysis.ibn_faris: الْأَخُ: هُوَ وَلَدُ الْأَبَوَيْنِ أَوْ أَحَدِهِمَا
lexical_analysis.al_raghib: الْأَخُ: هُوَ الَّذِي يَشْتَرِكُ مَعَكَ فِي الْأَبَوَيْنِ أَوْ أَحَدِهِمَا أَوْ فِي الرَّضَاعِ أَوْ فِي الْإِيمَانِ

quran_examples.ar: كُتِبَ عَلَيْكُمۡ إِذَا حَضَرَ أَحَدَكُمُ ٱلْمَوۡتُ إِن تَرَكَ خَيۡرًا ٱلۡوَصِيَّةُ لِلۡوَٰلِدَيۡنِ وَٱلۡأَقۡرَبِينَ بِٱلۡمَعۡرُوفِ حَقًّا عَلَى ٱلۡمُتَّقِينَ
quran_examples.en: Prescribed for you when death approaches one of you, if he leaves wealth, is the bequest for parents and relatives according to what is fair

hadith.ar: لَا تَقَاطَعُوا وَلَا تَدَابَرُوا وَلَا تَبَاغَضُوا وَكُونُوا عِبَادَ اللَّهِ إِخْوَانًا
hadith.en: Do not cut off one another, do not turn away from one another, do not hate one another — be O servants of Allah, brothers

shades.name_en: al-Akh — Brotherhood in Faith as the New Kinship
shades.name_ar: الْأَخُ — نَسِيبٌ فِي الْإِسْلَامِ، وَرَابِطٌ بَيْنَ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ
shades.explanation: The akh (brother) in the Quran operates in two dimensions: al-akh bil-nasab (brother by blood/kinship) and al-akh bil-īmān (brother by faith). The verse 49:10 — «innamā l-muʾminūna ikhwatun» (the believers are brothers) — establishes the brotherhood of faith as the fundamental social bond of the Muslim ummah, transcending all blood and tribal ties. The brotherhood of faith is to be expressed in ṭalāqah (helpful cooperation), ʿadl (justice), and rafq (compassion). Al-Ghazālī's famous advice — «treat your brother as a brother in kindness» — summarizes the akh ethical ideal.
shades.hadith_ar: لَا تَقَاطَعُوا وَلَا تَدَابَرُوا وَلَا تَبَاغَضُوا وَكُونُوا عِبَادَ اللَّهِ إِخْوَانًا
shades.hadith_en: Do not cut off one another, do not turn away from one another, do not hate one another — be O servants of Allah, brothers

meaning.en: Error, mistake. The root denotes the act of erring or making a mistake — particularly unintentional.
meaning.ar: الْخَطَأُ: ضِدُّ الصَّوَابِ، وَهُوَ الَّذِي يَفْعَلُهُ الْإِنْسَانُ عَنْ غَيْرِ قَصْدٍ

lexical_analysis.ibn_faris: الْخَطَأُ: ضِدُّ الصَّوَابِ. وَهُوَ مِمَّا لَا اخْتِيَارَ فِيهِ لِصَاحِبِهِ
lexical_analysis.al_raghib: الْخَطَأُ: الْوُقُوعُ فِي الشَّيْءِ عَلَى غَيْرِ قَصْدٍ. وَهُوَ فِي الْأَخْلَاقِ ضِدُّ الْإِصَابَةِ

quran_examples.ar: وَمَا كَانَ لِمُؤْمِنٍ أَن يَقْتُلَ مُؤْمِنًا إِلَّا خَطَـًۭٔا ۚ وَمَن قَتَلَ مُؤْمِنًا خَطَـًٔا فَتَحۡرِيرُ رَقَبَةٍۢ مُّؤۡمِنَةٍۢ وَدِيَةٌۭ مُّسَلَّمَةٌ إِلَىٰٓ أَهۡلِهِۦٓ إِلَّآ أَن يَصَّدَّقُوا۟
quran_examples.en: It was not for a believer to kill a believer except by mistake — and whoever kills a believer by mistake must free a believing slave and pay compensation
quran_examples.context: The accidental killing of a believer

hadith.ar: رُفِعَ عَنْ أُمَّتِي الْخَطَأُ وَالنِّسْيَانُ وَمَا اسْتُكْرِهُوا عَلَيْهِ
hadith.en: My ummah is absolved of error, forgetfulness, and what they were forced to do

shades.name_en: al-Khaṭāʾ — Errors as Covered and Forgivable
shades.name_ar: الْخَطَأُ — الْوُقُوعُ فِي الشَّيْءِ عَلَى غَيْرِ قَصْدٍ، مَحْفُوفٌ بِالرَّفْعِ عَنِ الْأُمَّةِ
shades.explanation: The khaṭāʾ (error, mistake) in the Quran is distinguished from al-ʿamd (deliberate sin). The verse 4:92 establishes the legal framework: killing by mistake (khaṭāʾ) has different consequences than intentional killing (ʿamd). The hadith qudsī — «my ummah is absolved of error, forgetfulness, and what they are forced to do» — establishes the divine mercy that covers unintentional errors. The khaṭāʾ is the natural state of the human being, but it is divinely excused when accompanied by taubah and ʿamal al-ṣāliḥ.
shades.hadith_ar: رُفِعَ عَنْ أُمَّتِي الْخَطَأُ وَالنِّسْيَانُ وَمَا اسْتُكْرِهُوا عَلَيْهِ
shades.hadith_en: My ummah is absolved of error, forgetfulness, and what they were forced to do

meaning.en: Soul, spirit; rest, comfort. The root denotes the breath of life — the soul/spirit bestowed by Allah — and the rest that comes from divine mercy.
meaning.ar: الرُّوحُ: النَّفْسُ، وَجَوْهَرُ الْحَيَاةِ الَّذِي بِهِ كَانَ الْإِنْسَانُ حَيًّا

lexical_analysis.ibn_faris: الرُّوحُ: الرِّيحُ. وَالْأَرْوَاحُ: الْأَنْفُسُ. وَالرُّوحُ: جِبْرِيلُ
lexical_analysis.al_raghib: الرُّوحُ: اسْمٌ لِجَوْهَرٍ حَيَوِيٍّ عَقْلَانِيٍّ، مَجَرَّدٍ عَنِ الْمَادَّةِ، وَهُوَ مَدَارُ الْإِدْرَاكِ وَالْحَيَاةِ

quran_examples.ar: إِنَّا أَنزَلْنَـٰهُ فِى لَيْلَةِ ٱلْقَدْرِ
quran_examples.en: Indeed We sent it (the Quran) down on the Night of Power
quran_examples.context: The Quran as al-Ruḥ — the Spirit that gives life

hadith.ar: إِنَّ الرُّوحَ الْأَمِينَ يُنْزِلُ عَلَى قَلْبِي
hadith.en: The faithful Spirit (Gabriel) descends upon my heart

shades.name_en: ar-Rūḥ — The Divine Spirit, Gabriel, and the Breath of Life
shades.name_ar: الرُّوحُ — جَوْهَرُ الْحَيَاةِ الَّذِي يَأْتِي مِنَ اللَّهِ، وَالْمَلَكُ الْأَمِينُ
shades.explanation: The rūḥ (spirit/soul) is one of the most profound concepts in the Quran. The verse 17:85 asks the unanswerable question: «and they ask you about the rūḥ — say: the rūḥ is from the affair of my Lord» — emphasizing that its nature is beyond human comprehension. The rūḥ has multiple referents in the Quran: (1) The rūḥ al-amīn (Gabriel — 26:193, 16:102) — the faithful spirit who brings revelation; (2) The rūḥ from Allah breathed into Adam (15:29, 32:9) — the divine source of human life; (3) The rūḥ al-qudus (Holy Spirit — 2:87, 5:110) — the divine sanctifying spirit; (4) ʿĪsā ibn Maryam is called al-Rūḥ from Allah (4:171). The rūḥ is the secret of human life, the bearer of the divine breath that distinguishes the living from the dead.
shades.hadith_ar: إِنَّ الرُّوحَ الْأَمِينَ يُنْزِلُ عَلَى قَلْبِي
shades.hadith_en: The faithful Spirit (Gabriel) descends upon my heart

meaning.en: Hot water, boiling; beloved friend (h-am-im). The root denotes hot/burning water and the intimate intimate companion.
meaning.ar: الْحَمِيمُ: الْمَاءُ الْحَارُّ، أَوِ الصَّدِيقُ الْحَمِيمُ

lexical_analysis.ibn_faris: الْحَمِيمُ: الْمَاءُ الْحَارُّ. وَالْحَمِيمُ: الصَّدِيقُ الْمُحِبُّ
lexical_analysis.al_raghib: الْحَمِيمُ: الْمَاءُ الْحَارُّ الْبَالِغُ الْحَرَارَةَ. وَكُلُّ صَدِيقٍ مُحِبٍّ فَهُوَ حَمِيمٌ

quran_examples.ar: يَطُوفُونَ بَيْنَهَا وَبَيۡنَ حَمِيمٍ ءَانٍۢ
quran_examples.en: They will circulate between it (fire) and hot boiling water (ḥamīm)
quran_examples.context: The hellfire alternating with scalding water

hadith.ar: إِنَّ لَكَ فِي كُلِّ صَلَاةٍ رَكْعَتَيْنِ وَتَسْلِيمَتَيْنِ وَتَسْبِيحَ وَتَحْمِيدٍ حَمِيمٌ يَوْمَ الْقِيَامَةِ
hadith.en: In every prayer there are two rakʿahs and two salams and tasbīḥ and taḥmīd — these are ḥamīm on the Day of Resurrection

shades.name_en: al-Ḥamīm — Boiling Water of Hell and the Beloved Friend
shades.explanation: The ḥamīm in the Quran has two distinct meanings. First, the boiling scalding water — the punishment of Hellfire that the disbelievers drink (47:15). The verses 55:44-46 describe the oscillation between drinking the boiling ḥamīm and the most foul discharge of the damned. Second, the intimate companion or beloved friend (ḥamīm). The verse 68:4 establishes that the Prophet's role-model among those who will come to him on the Last Day is the one who has a clean heart toward him. The semantic bridge between the two meanings is intensity — of heat in the physical, of intimacy in the relational.
shades.hadith_ar: إِنَّ لَكَ فِي كُلِّ صَلَاةٍ ... حَمِيمٌ يَوْمَ الْقِيَامَةِ
shades.hadith_en: In every prayer there are tasbīḥ and taḥmīd — these are ḥamīm on the Day of Resurrection

meaning.en: Fear, terror, dread. The root denotes the fear that paralyzes or moves the soul — particularly the spiritual fear of the divine.

lexical_analysis.ibn_faris: الرَّهْبُ: الْخَوْفُ مَعَ تَعَظُّمٍ لِلْمَخُوفِ مِنْهُ
lexical_analysis.al_raghib: الرَّهْبُ: الْخَوْفُ الْمُصَاحِبُ لِتَعْظِيمِ الْمَرْهُوبِ مِنْهُ. وَهُوَ أَقْوَى مِنَ الْخَوْفِ الْمُجَرَّدِ

quran_examples.ar: ٱقۡتَرَبَ لِلنَّاسِ حِسَـٰبُهُمۡ وَهُمۡ فِى غَفۡلَةٍۢ مُّعۡرِضُونَ
quran_examples.en: The reckoning of people has drawn near, and they are in heedlessness turning away
quran_examples.context: The Quranic opening of judgment warning

hadith.ar: مَنْ رَأَى مِنْكُمْ مُنْكَرًا فَلْيُغَيِّرْهُ بِيَدِهِ، فَإِنْ لَمْ يَسْتَطِعْ فَبِلِسَانِهِ، فَإِنْ لَمْ يَسْتَطِعْ فَبِقَلْبِهِ
hadith.en: Whoever among you sees an evil — let him change it with his hand; if he cannot, with his tongue; if he cannot, with his heart

shades.name_en: ar-Rahb — Terror of the Lord and the Spiritual Response
shades.name_ar: الرَّهْبُ — الْفَزَعُ مِنْ عَظَمَةِ الْمَرْهُوبِ، وَخَوْفُ الْقَلْبِ مِنَ اللَّهِ
shades.explanation: The rahb (terror, dread) in the Quran is a stronger form of fear — the inner state that accompanies recognition of divine majesty. The verse 59:2 — the cause of the hypocrites' flight after Uhud — is rendered as rahb in some readings, conveying the complete panic that accompanied the divine punishment. The verse 8:26 promises that after the period of weakness there would come a time when Allah would give the believers «bah wa rahb» — power and terror in their enemies. The rahb is the awe that the divine inspires — a terror that is not merely physical but existential.
shades.hadith_ar: مَنْ رَأَى مِنْكُمْ مُنْكَرًا فَلْيُغَيِّرْهُ
shades.hadith_en: Whoever among you sees an evil — let him change it

meaning.en: Rain. The root denotes the water that falls from the sky — particularly as divine mercy or punishment.
meaning.ar: الْمَطَرُ: الْمَاءُ الَّذِي يَنْزِلُ مِنَ السَّمَاءِ

lexical_analysis.ibn_faris: الْمَطَرُ: مَا تَسَاقَطَ مِنَ السَّمَاءِ مِنَ الْمَاءِ. وَالْأَمْطَارُ: جَمْعُ الْمَطَرِ
lexical_analysis.al_raghib: الْمَطَرُ: الْمَاءُ الَّذِي يَنْزِلُ مِنَ السَّحَابِ. وَيُسْتَعْمَلُ فِي الرَّحْمَةِ وَالْعَذَابِ

quran_examples.ar: أَوۡ كَصَيِّبٍۢ مِّنَ ٱلسَّمَآءِ فِيهِ ظُلُمَـٰتٌۭ وَرَعۡدٌۭ وَبَرۡقٌۭ يَجۡعَلُونَ أَصَـٰبِعَهُمۡ فِىٓ ءَاذَانِهِم مِّنَ ٱلصَّوَٰعِقِ حَذَرَ ٱلۡمَوۡتِ
quran_examples.en: Or like rain from the sky in which is darkness and thunder and lightning — they put their fingers in their ears from the thunderclaps, fearing death
quran_examples.context: The parable of the downpour — religious response

hadith.ar: تُفْتَحُ أَبْوَابُ السَّمَاءِ بِنَصْفِ اللَّيْلِ فَيَنْزِلُ اللَّهُ إِلَى السَّمَاءِ الدُّنْيَا
hadith.en: The gates of heaven are opened at the middle of the night and Allah descends to the lowest heaven

shades.name_en: al-Maṭar — Rain as Divine Mercy and Wrath
shades.name_ar: الْمَطَرُ — الْمَاءُ النَّازِلُ مِنَ السَّمَاءِ، رَحْمَةً أَوْ عَذَابًا
shades.explanation: The maṭar (rain) in the Quran is a divine gift — water that falls from the sky to give life to the dead earth. The verse 2:19 establishes rain as one of the central parables of the divine — the downpour that brings life to the earth is parallel to the revelation that brings life to the heart. The verse 4:102 describes the maṭar al-khaif (rain of fear) — a divine punishment that descended on those who disobeyed. Al-Ghazālī (Iḥyāʾ, Book of Reverence for Prayer) uses rain as the central metaphor for divine mercy: just as the land receives the rain without effort, so the heart receives the revelation when it is open.
shades.hadith_ar: تُفْتَحُ أَبْوَابُ السَّمَاءِ بِنَصْفِ اللَّيْلِ
shades.hadith_en: The gates of heaven are opened at the middle of the night

meaning.en: To pass by, to command. The root denotes both transit (passing through) and direction (ordering).
meaning.ar: مَرَّ: جَاوَزَ مَكَانًا، أَوْ أَمَرَ وَكَلَّفَ

lexical_analysis.ibn_faris: الْمُرُورُ: الْجَوَازُ. وَأَمَرَّ الشَّيْءَ: جَعَلَهُ مُسْتَمِرًّا
lexical_analysis.al_raghib: الْمَرُّ: الْمُرُورُ وَالْجَوَازُ. وَالْأَمْرُ: الْطَّلَبُ مَعَ اسْتِعْلَاءِ صِفَةِ الْوَجْهِ

quran_examples.ar: فَلَمَّا رَأَوۡهُ عَارِضًۭا يَسۡتَقۡبِلُ أَوۡدِيَتَهُمۡ قَالُوا۟ هَـٰذَا عَارِضٌۭ مُّمۡطِرُنَا ۚ بَلۡ هُوَ مَا ٱسۡتَعۡجَلۡتُم بِهِۦ رِيحٌۭ فِيهَا عَذَابٌ أَلِيمٌ
quran_examples.en: When they saw it as a cloud approaching their valleys, they said: This is a cloud that will give us rain. Rather, it is what you hastened — a wind in which is painful punishment
quran_examples.context: The punishment of the people who asked for rain as punishment

hadith.ar: إِنَّ اللَّهَ كَتَبَ الْإِحْسَانَ عَلَى كُلِّ شَيْءٍ
hadith.en: Allah has prescribed ihsan on everything

shades.name_en: al-Marr — The Passage of Time and the Command of Authority
shades.name_ar: الْمَرُّ — مُرُورُ الزَّمَانِ، وَمَرُّ الْأَوَامِرِ، وَجَوَازُ الْحَالَاتِ
shades.explanation: The marr (passage, transit) in the Quran denotes both the passing of time (marr al-shay' — time passes) and the transiting of creatures across space (people passing by, time passing). The verse 46:24-25 uses the marr to describe the punishment cloud that came to the people of Aad — what they thought was rain was, in fact, the divine punishment. The passage of time, similarly, can carry either blessing (when lived in righteousness) or curse (when wasted in heedlessness). The verse 36:67 — «and if We willed, We would have transformed them in their place» — uses the form 'amarra (to cause to pass through) — another form of the root.
shades.hadith_ar: إِنَّ اللَّهَ كَتَبَ الْإِحْسَانَ عَلَى كُلِّ شَيْءٍ
shades.hadith_en: Allah has prescribed ihsan on everything

meaning.en: Word, speech. The root denotes a single utterance — particularly the divine word, the prophetic speech, or the uttered expression.
meaning.ar: الْكَلِمَةُ: الْقَوْلُ الْمُفْرَدُ، أَوِ الْجُمْلَةُ الْمُفِيدَةُ

lexical_analysis.ibn_faris: الْكَلِمُ: مِنَ الْقَوْلِ. وَيُسْتَعْمَلُ فِي الْكَلَامِ الْمُفْرَدِ وَالْجُمْلَةِ
lexical_analysis.al_raghib: الْكَلِمَةُ: اسْمٌ لِلْقَوْلِ الَّذِي يَسْتَقِلُّ بِالْمَعْنَى. وَهِيَ فِي اللَّهِ: قَوْلُهُ الْقَائِمُ بِذَاتِهِ

quran_examples.ar: وَإِذِ ٱبۡتَلَىٰٓ إِبۡرَٰهِـٰمَ رَبُّهُۥ بِكَلِمَـٰتٍۢ فَأَتَمَّهُنَّ
quran_examples.en: When Abraham was tested by his Lord with words, and he fulfilled them
quran_examples.context: Ibrahim's trial with the words of pilgrimage

hadith.ar: كَلِمَتَانِ خَفِيفَتَانِ عَلَى اللِّسَانِ، ثَقِيلَتَانِ فِي الْمِيزَانِ: سُبْحَانَ اللَّهِ وَبِحَمْدِهِ، سُبْحَانَ اللَّهِ الْعَظِيمِ
hadith.en: Two words that are light on the tongue, heavy on the scale: glory and praise be to Allah, glory to Allah the Great

shades.name_en: al-Kalimah — The Divine Word, the Prophetic Word, the Spoken Word
shades.name_ar: الْكَلِمَةُ — الْقَوْلُ الَّذِي يَسْتَقِلُّ بِالْمَعْنَى، مِنَ اللَّهِ أَوِ الْعَبْدِ
shades.explanation: The kalimah (word) in the Quran has multiple dimensions. (1) Kalimat Allāh — the divine word, which is eternal, all-encompassing, and infallible (2:124 — the words Ibrahim was tested with). (2) Kalimat al-tawḥīd — the declaration of faith (lā ilāha illā Allāh) which is the most noble word. (3) Kalimat al-sayyi' and kalimat al-ḥasanah — the evil and good words, respectively (41:33). (4) Kalimat al-fāsiq — the word of the rebellious (9:80). (5) The kalima as a specific utterance — the hadith «two words light on the tongue» refers to the daily dhikr as kalimāt. The kalimah is the basic unit of speech, the smallest meaningful utterance.
shades.hadith_ar: كَلِمَتَانِ خَفِيفَتَانِ عَلَى اللِّسَانِ، ثَقِيلَتَانِ فِي الْمِيزَانِ
shades.hadith_en: Two words that are light on the tongue, heavy on the scale

meaning.en: Boiling, hot, blazing. The root denotes the violent intensity of heat — particularly of hellfire.
meaning.ar: الْفَوْرُ: شِدَّةُ الْغَلَيَانِ، وَهُوَ الْحَرَارَةُ الشَّدِيدَةُ

lexical_analysis.ibn_faris: الْفَوْرُ: شِدَّةُ الْحَرَارَةِ. وَالْفَوْرُ: الْغَلَيَانُ الشَّدِيدُ
lexical_analysis.al_raghib: الْفَوْرُ: شِدَّةُ حَرَارَةِ النَّارِ إِذَا أُوقِدَتْ. وَيُسْتَعْمَلُ أَيْضًا لِلْإِسْرَاعِ

quran_examples.ar: وَإِذۡ قَالَ رَبُّكَ لِجِبۡرِيلَ إِنِّي مَعَكُمۡ لَئِن ثَبَّتُّمُ وَإِن تَقَوۡلُوا۟ لِلَّذِينَ أُوتُوا۟ ٱلۡكِتَـٰبَ
quran_examples.en: When your Lord said to Gabriel: Indeed I am with you. If you remain firm and say to those who have been given the Book...
quran_examples.context: Divine support to the believers at Badr

hadith.ar: صُومُوا تَصِحُّوا
hadith.en: Fast so you may be healthy

shades.name_en: al-Fawr — The Blazing Intensity of the Fire and Immediate Action
shades.name_ar: الْفَوْرُ — شِدَّةُ الْحَرَارَةِ، وَالْإِسْرَاعُ فِي الْفِعْلِ
shades.explanation: The fawr in the Quran has two semantic dimensions. First, the violent intensity of heat — the blazing of fire (warith fuwwar — the scorching fire). Second, the immediacy of action — the doing of something right away (al-fawr — the immediate). The verse 2:93 uses the verb thabattum (to be firm, to be steadfast), related to the concept of stability rather than quick action. The fawr is thus a powerful Quranic concept: it is the heat that punishes and the immediacy that rewards.
shades.hadith_ar: صُومُوا تَصِحُّوا
shades.hadith_en: Fast so you may be healthy

meaning.en: To follow, pursue, narrate, tell. The root denotes the pursuit of information or events — particularly the narration of the prophets' stories.

lexical_analysis.ibn_faris: الْقَصُّ: الْأَثَرُ يُتْبَعُ. وَالْقَصَصُ: جَمْعُ قِصَّةٍ
lexical_analysis.al_raghib: الْقَصَصُ: الْأَخْبَارُ الْمَاضِيَةُ تُتْلَى بِطَرِيقِ التَّبَعِ. وَيُسْتَعْمَلُ لِكُلِّ خَبَرٍ مَاضٍ

quran_examples.ar: إِنَّ هَـٰذَا لَهُوَ ٱلۡقَصَصُ ٱلۡحَقُّ ۚ وَمَا مِنۡ إِلَـٰهٍ إِلَّا ٱللَّهُ
quran_examples.en: Indeed this is the true narrative (al-qaṣaṣ al-ḥaqq) — and there is no god but Allah
quran_examples.context: The Quran's claim that its stories of prophets are true

hadith.ar: حَدِّثُوا عَنْ بَنِي إِسْرَائِيلَ وَلَا حَرَجَ
hadith.en: Narrate from the Children of Israel — there is no blame

shades.name_en: al-Qaṣaṣ — The True Story and Its Lessons
shades.name_ar: الْقَصَصُ — الْأَخْبَارُ الْمَاضِيَةُ الَّتِي تَحْمِلُ دُرُوسًا
shades.explanation: The qaṣaṣ (stories, narratives) in the Quran is one of its major rhetorical and theological methods. The verse 12:3 — «naḥnu naquṣṣu ʿalayka aḥsana l-qaṣaṣ» (We narrate to you the best of stories) — establishes the Quran's narratives as divinely authoritative. Al-Ghazālī (Jawāhir al-Qur'ān) argues that the qaṣaṣ of the prophets serves three purposes: (1) ʿibra (lesson) — the moral lesson extracted from the prophets' stories; (2) khabar (information) — accurate historical narrative; (3) baraka (blessing) — the spiritual blessing of contemplating the prophets' lives. The qaṣaṣ is the Quran's evidence for the historical reality of the prophetic mission and the moral framework it offers.
shades.hadith_ar: حَدِّثُوا عَنْ بَنِي إِسْرَائِيلَ وَلَا حَرَجَ
shades.hadith_en: Narrate from the Children of Israel — there is no blame

meaning.en: Thread, cord. The root denotes a thin string or cord — used metaphorically for the continuity of life and the breaching of the Day of Judgment.

lexical_analysis.ibn_faris: الْخَيْطُ: السَّيْرُ الَّذِي يُلَفُّ أَوْ يُنْسَجُ. وَكُلُّ مَا تَمَدَّدَ مِنَ الشَّيْءِ الرَّفِيعِ فَهُوَ خَيْطٌ
lexical_analysis.al_raghib: الْخَيْطُ: اسْمٌ لِمَا تَأْسِسَ مِنَ الشَّيْءِ الرَّفِيعِ. وَقَدْ يُسْتَعْمَلُ لِلْخَاصِّ مِنَ الْمَوْصُولِ

quran_examples.ar: أَوۡ كَصَيِّبٍۢ مِّنَ ٱلسَّمَآءِ فِيهِ ظُلُمَـٰتٌۭ وَرَعۡدٌۭ وَبَرۡقٌۭ يَجۡعَلُونَ أَصَـٰبِعَهُمۡ فِىٓ ءَاذَانِهِم مِّنَ ٱلصَّوَٰعِقِ حَذَرَ ٱلۡوَتُ
quran_examples.en: Or like rain from the sky with darkness and thunder and lightning
quran_examples.context: The parable of the downpour with thunder

hadith.ar: لَا يَقُصُّ عَلَيْنَا إِلَّا أَبُو هُرَيْرَةَ، فَإِنَّهُ لَا يَزَالُ يُحَدِّثُ عَنْ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ
hadith.en: None used to narrate to us except Abu Hurayra — he never stopped narrating from the Messenger of Allah

shades.name_en: al-Khayṭ — The Thread of Life and the Distinction of Lines
shades.name_ar: الْخَيْطُ — الشَّيْءُ الرَّفِيعُ الْمَفْتُولُ، وَاسْتَعْمَالُهُ فِي فَقْدِ الْأَبْصَارِ مَعَ ضَعْفِ النَّظَرِ
shades.explanation: The khayṭ (thread) in the Quran is used in two distinct senses. First, the white thread distinguished from the black thread (the dawn of Ramadan — 2:187). Second, the relativity of human judgment of the size of a mote or thread of a date seed (2:235). The khayṭ is the thinnest of threads — used metaphorically for the most subtle distinctions. The verse 4:23 establishes prohibitions about marrying certain kin — the khayṭ al-washl (extended relation) being the most distant.
shades.hadith_ar: لَا يَقُصُّ عَلَيْنَا إِلَّا أَبُو هُرَيْرَةَ
shades.hadith_en: None used to narrate to us except Abu Hurayra

meaning.en: To set up, erect; affliction, fatigue. The root denotes both the placing of something in position and the experience of toil or hardship.
meaning.ar: نَصَبَ: أَوْقَفَ الشَّيْءَ مُنْتَصِبًا، أَوْ أَتْعَبَهُ إِتْعَابًا شَدِيدًا

lexical_analysis.ibn_faris: النَّصْبُ: الْإِتْعَابُ. وَالنَّصْبُ: ضِدُّ الرَّاحَةِ
lexical_analysis.al_raghib: النَّصْبُ: الْإِتْعَابُ. وَيُسْتَعْمَلُ فِي التَّعَبِ الْمُفْرِطِ، وَفِي نَصْبِ الشَّيْءِ وَإِقَامَتِهِ

quran_examples.ar: وَمِنْهُم مَّن يَقُولُ رَبَّنَآ ءَاتِنَا فِى ٱلدُّنْيَا حَسَنَةًۭ وَفِى ٱلْـَٔاخِرَةِ حَسَنَةًۭ وَقِنَا عَذَابَ ٱلنَّارِ
quran_examples.en: And among them are those who say: Our Lord, give us good in this world and good in the Hereafter, and protect us from the punishment of the Fire
quran_examples.context: The dua of those seeking refuge from hardship

hadith.ar: مَنْ أَحَبَّ أَنْ يُسْرَعَ لَهُ فِي رِزْقِهِ، أَوْ يُمْدَّ لَهُ فِي أَثَرِهِ، فَلْيَصِلْ رَحِمَهُ
hadith.en: Whoever would love to have his sustenance expanded and his lifespan lengthened — let him maintain his family ties

shades.name_en: an-Naṣb — Affliction, Toil, and the Weariness of the Soul
shades.explanation: The naṣb (affliction, fatigue, weariness) is the state of the soul suffering hardship, toil, or anguish. The verse 2:201 — the petition for hasana in both worlds and protection from Hellfire — acknowledges the naṣb of the human condition. Al-Ghazālī (Iḥyāʾ, Book of Patience) treats naṣb as the necessary condition of human existence — there is no worldly life without it. The wise response to naṣb is not avoidance but endurance, not complaint but acceptance, not bitterness but gratitude for what is preserved through the hardship.
shades.hadith_ar: مَنْ أَحَبَّ أَنْ يُسْرَعَ لَهُ فِي رِزْقِهِ، أَوْ يُمْدَّ لَهُ فِي أَثَرِهِ، فَلْيَصِلْ رَحِمَهُ
shades.hadith_en: Whoever would love to have his sustenance expanded — let him maintain his family ties

meaning.en: Selecting, choosing, electing. The root denotes the deliberate choice of someone or something — particularly the divine choice of prophets and the elite among the believers.

lexical_analysis.ibn_faris: النَّجْبُ: خِيَارُ الْأَشْيَاءِ. وَالْأَنْجَبُ: خَالِصُ الشَّيْءِ وَأَفْضَلُهُ
lexical_analysis.al_raghib: الِاجْتِبَاءُ: الِاخْتِيَارُ لِفَضْلِ الشَّيْءِ عَلَى غَيْرِهِ. وَاجْتَبَاهُ: اخْتَارَهُ

quran_examples.ar: إِنَّ اللَّهَ اصْطَفَىٰٓ ءَادَمَ وَنُوحًۭا وَءَالَ إِبۡرَٰهِـ۰مَ وَءَالَ عِمۡرَٰنَ عَلَى ٱلۡعَـٰلَمِينَ
quran_examples.en: Indeed Allah chose Adam, Noah, the family of Abraham, and the family of Imran over all the worlds
quran_examples.context: The divine selection of certain lineages for prophethood

hadith.ar: إِنَّ اللَّهَ اصْطَفَىٰٓ ءَادَمَ وَنُوحًۭا وَءَالَ إِبۡرَٰهِـ۰مَ وَءَالَ عِمۡرَٰنَ عَلَى ٱلۡعَـٰلَمِينَ
hadith.en: Indeed Allah chose Adam, Noah, the family of Abraham, and the family of Imran over the worlds

shades.name_en: al-Istifāʾ — Divine Selection of the Best Among Creation
shades.name_ar: الِاجْتِبَاءُ — اخْتِيَارُ اللَّهِ لِأَفْضَلِ الْخَلْقِ لِرِسَالَتِهِ
shades.explanation: The istifāʾ (selection) in the Quran is the divine act of choosing specific individuals for specific missions. The verse 3:33 — «inn Allāha iṣṭafā ādama wa-nūḥan wa-āla ibrāhīma wa-āla ʿimrāna ʿalā l-ʿālamīn» — establishes the divine selection of prophetic lineages for carrying the message of tawḥīd. The istifāʾ is not arbitrary — it is based on divine wisdom that recognizes the capacity of the chosen one to bear the trust. Ibn ʿArabī (al-Futūḥāt) develops a metaphysics of istifāʾ: the divine names chose certain servants to manifest their attributes in creation — Adam for al-Khalīfah, Noah for al-Nabī, Abraham for al-Khalīl, Muhammad for al-Raḥma.
shades.hadith_ar: إِنَّ اللَّهَ اصْطَفَىٰٓ ءَادَمَ وَنُوحًۭا وَءَالَ إِبۡرَٰهِـ۰مَ وَءَالَ عِمۡرَٰنَ عَلَى ٱلۡعَـٰلَمِينَ
shades.hadith_en: Indeed Allah chose Adam, Noah, the family of Abraham, and the family of Imran over the worlds

meaning.en: Randomly, without thought, groundlessly. The root denotes acting without knowledge or deliberation — particularly in matters of religion and faith.
meaning.ar: الْجَزَافُ: الْبُتُ بِلَا تَأَمُّلٍ، أَوِ الْقَوْلُ بِلَا عِلْمٍ

lexical_analysis.ibn_faris: الْجَزَافُ: الْكَلَامُ فِيمَا لَا يُدْرَكُ وَلَا يُعْلَمُ مَعْنَاهُ
lexical_analysis.al_raghib: الْجَزَافُ: الْقَوْلُ بِلَا رَوِيَّةٍ، مِنَ التَّقَحُّمِ فِيمَا لَا يَعْلَمُ. وَيُسْتَعْمَلُ فِي الذَّمِّ

quran_examples.ar: لَا تُؤَاخِذۡنَا إِن نَّسِينَآ أَوۡ أَخۡطَأۡنَا
quran_examples.en: Do not hold us accountable for our forgetfulness or our errors
quran_examples.context: The Prophet's request to his Lord

hadith.ar: مَنْ أَفْتَى بِغَيْرِ عِلْمٍ كَانَ إِثْمُهُ عَلَى مَنْ أَفْتَاهُ
hadith.en: Whoever gives a religious ruling without knowledge — the sin is upon the one who issued it

shades.name_en: al-Jazf — Acting Without Knowledge and the Prohibition of Ignorant Speech
shades.name_ar: الْجَزَافُ — الْقَوْلُ بِلَا عِلْمٍ، وَالْتَّقَحُّمُ فِيمَا لَا يُدْرَكُ
shades.explanation: The jazf (acting without knowledge) in the Quran appears in the verse 5:4 — the Prophet's supplication for protection from this state. Al-jazf is one of the most severely condemned states — speaking or acting without knowledge in matters of religion, especially. The hadith «man aftā bi-ghayri ʿilmin kāna ithmuhu ʿalā man aftāh» (whoever gives a fatwa without knowledge, his sin is upon him) is a foundational principle of Islamic jurisprudence. The opposite is al-tafaqquh (deep understanding) and al-tathabbut (verification) — to know before one speaks.
shades.hadith_ar: مَنْ أَفْتَى بِغَيْرِ عِلْمٍ كَانَ إِثْمُهُ عَلَى مَنْ أَفْتَاهُ
shades.hadith_en: Whoever gives a religious ruling without knowledge — the sin is upon the one who issued it

meaning.en: Hope, expectation. The root denotes a state of hopeful expectation — particularly of divine mercy.

lexical_analysis.ibn_faris: الرَّجَاءُ: الْأَمَلُ. وَرَجَوْتُ: أَمَّلْتُ
lexical_analysis.al_raghib: الرَّجَاءُ: تَوَقُّعُ الشَّيْءِ الْمَحْبُوبِ مَعَ طَلَبِهِ

quran_examples.ar: وَلَا تُفۡسِدُوا۟ فِى ٱلۡأَرۡضِ بَعۡدَ إِصۡلَـٰحِهَا وَٱدۡعُوهُ خَوۡفًۭا وَطَمَعًا ۖ إِنَّ رَحۡمَتَ ٱللَّهِ قَرِيبٌۭ مِّنَ ٱلۡمُحۡسِنِينَ
quran_examples.en: Do not corrupt the earth after its reformation. Call upon Him with fear and hope — indeed Allah's mercy is near to those who do good
quran_examples.context: The duality of khawf and raja'

hadith.ar: لَا يَمُوتَنَّ أَحَدُكُمْ وَلَا يُبَالِيَ بِأَيِّ وَادٍ رَكِبَاهُ، إِنْ سَلِمَ أَمْرَهُ كَانَ مِمَّنْ رَجَا رَبَّهُ
hadith.en: None of you should die except hoping for the best from his Lord

shades.name_en: ar-Rajāʾ — Hope as One of the Two Wings of the Spiritual Life
shades.name_ar: الرَّجَاءُ — التَّوَقُّعُ، الْأَمَلُ، أَحَدُ جَنَاحَيِ الطَّيَرَانِ إِلَى اللَّهِ
shades.explanation: The rajāʾ (hope) is paired with khawf (fear) throughout the Quran as the two wings of the spiritual journey. The verse 7:56 — «invoke Him with khawf and rajāʾ» — establishes that both are essential postures of the soul before Allah. Al-Ghazālī (Iḥyāʾ, Book of Hope) treats rajāʾ as a divine gift, not a human achievement — the soul that has rajāʾ has been given it by Allah as a sign of His pleasure. The rajāʾ without action is delusion; the action without rajāʾ is despair. The hadith — «none of you should die except hoping for the best from his Lord» — establishes rajāʾ as the final state of the soul at death.
shades.hadith_ar: لَا يَمُوتَنَّ أَحَدُكُمْ وَلَا يُبَالِيَ بِأَيِّ وَادٍ رَكِبَاهُ، إِنْ سَلِمَ أَمْرُهُ كَانَ مِمَّنْ رَجَا رَبَّهُ
shades.hadith_en: None of you should die except hoping for the best from his Lord

meaning.en: Poverty, need. The root denotes the state of being in need — the opposite of ghinā (self-sufficiency).

lexical_analysis.ibn_faris: الْفَقْرُ: ضِدُّ الْغِنَى. وَالْفَقِيرُ: الَّذِي لَا يَجِدُ شَيْئًا
lexical_analysis.al_raghib: الْفَقْرُ: الِاحْتِيَاجُ إِلَى الشَّيْءِ مَعَ عَدَمِهِ. وَالْفَقِيرُ: الَّذِي لَا شَيْءَ لَهُ. وَالْمِسْكِينُ: مَنْ لَهُ شَيْءٌ مَعَ قِلَّتِهِ

quran_examples.ar: لِّلْفُقَرَآءِ ٱلَّذِينَ أُحۡصِرُوا۟ فِى سَبِيلِ ٱللَّهِ لَا يَسۡتَطِيعُونَ ضَرۡبًۭا فِى ٱلۡأَرۡضِ يَحۡسَبُهُمُ ٱلۡجَاهِلُ أَغۡنيَآءَ مِنَ ٱلتَّعَفُّفِ
quran_examples.en: Charity is for the poor who have been restricted in Allah's way, unable to travel through the earth — the ignorant person thinks them rich because of their modesty
quran_examples.context: The category of poor in the zakāh system

hadith.ar: لَيْسَ الْمِسْكِينُ الَّذِي تَرُدُّهُ اللُّقْمَةُ وَاللُّقْمَتَانِ، وَلَكِنَّ الْمِسْكِينَ الَّذِي لَا يَجِدُ غِنًى يُغْنِيهِ، وَلَا يُفْطَنُ بِهِ فَيُتَصَدَّقَ عَلَيْهِ وَلَا يَقُومُ فَيَسْأَلَ النَّاسَ
hadith.en: The poor person is not the one who can be turned away with one or two morsels of food — the poor person is the one who has no means, who does not appear to be given charity, and who does not go around asking people

shades.name_en: al-Faqr — Poverty as the Human Condition Before Allah
shades.name_ar: الْفَقْرُ — الْحَاجَةُ، وَالِاحْتِيَاجُ إِلَى غَيْرِ الذَّاتِ
shades.explanation: The faqr (poverty, need) in the Quran is both a social condition and a spiritual reality. As a social condition, the faqrūn (poor) are specified categories of zakāh recipients (9:60), deserving of care from the community. As a spiritual reality, the Quran's foundational statement is the verse 35:15 — «yā ayyuhā l-insānu innaka kādiḥun ilā rabbika kadhan fa-mulāqīhi» (O man, you are laboring toward your Lord, and you will meet Him) — the entire human life is a journey of need, dependent on Allah. Al-Ghazālī (Iḥyāʾ, Book of Reliance on Allah) argues that faqr (need) is the essential human state — the one who recognizes his poverty before Allah is the one who will receive divine ghinā (sufficiency).
shades.hadith_ar: لَيْسَ الْمِسْكِينُ الَّذِي تَرُدُّهُ اللُّقْمَةُ وَاللُّقْمَتَانِ
shades.hadith_en: The poor person is not the one who can be turned away with one or two morsels of food

meaning.en: To dislike, hate, detest. The root denotes the negative emotional response of aversion — the opposite of raghbah (desire).

lexical_analysis.ibn_faris: الْكُرْهُ: ضِدُّ الْحُبِّ. وَالْكَرَاهِيَةُ: ضِدُّ الْمَحَبَّةِ
lexical_analysis.al_raghib: الْكَرَاهَةُ: نَفْسُ الْمَكْرُوهِ. وَهِيَ ضِدُّ الْمَحَبَّةِ. وَقَدْ تَكُونُ مَحْمُودَةً إِذَا كَانَ الْمَكْرُوهُ مَذْمُومًا

quran_examples.ar: وَعَسَىٰٓ أَن تَكْرَهُوا۟ شَيۡـًۭٔا وَهُوَ خَيۡرٌۭ لَّكُمۡ ۖ وَعَسَىٰٓ أَن تُحِبُّوا۟ شَيۡـًۭٔا وَهُوَ شَرٌّۭ لَّكُمۡ
quran_examples.en: Perhaps you hate something and it is good for you, and perhaps you love something and it is bad for you

hadith.ar: لَا يُؤْمِنُ أَحَدُكُمْ حَتَّى يُحِبَّ لِأَخِيهِ مَا يُحِبُّ لِنَفْسِهِ
hadith.en: None of you truly believes until he loves for his brother what he loves for himself

shades.name_en: al-Karāhiyah — Dislike That May Be Good or Bad
shades.name_ar: الْكَرَاهَةُ — نَفْسُ الْمَكْرُوهِ، قَدْ تَكُونُ خَيْرًا أَوْ شَرًّا
shades.explanation: The karāhiyah (dislike) in the Quran is the negative counterpart of love and preference. The verse 2:216 establishes that human dislike may hide divine goodness, and vice versa. The hadith of the Prophet — «la yaqʾAllāhu li-man ʿaṣāhu» (Allah does not bless the one who disobeys Him) — implicit in the karāhiyah structure is that the soul's natural dislike of pain is beneficial when it leads to repentance, but harmful when it leads to despair. The karāhiyah that is praised is the dislike of sin and wrongdoing; the karāhiyah that is condemned is the dislike of divine decree (kufr bil-qadar — disbelief in the divine decree).
shades.hadith_ar: لَا يُؤْمِنُ أَحَدُكُمْ حَتَّى يُحِبَّ لِأَخِيهِ مَا يُحِبُّ لِنَفْسِهِ
shades.hadith_en: None of you truly believes until he loves for his brother what he loves for himself

meaning.en: State, condition, situation. The root denotes a particular state or circumstance — particularly one that is transitional or temporary.
meaning.ar: الْحَالُ: الْوَقْتُ الَّذِي يَقَعُ فِيهِ الشَّيْءُ، أَوِ الْوَصْفُ الْعَارِضُ

lexical_analysis.ibn_faris: الْحَوْلُ: السَّنَةُ. وَالْحَالُ: الَّذِي يَحُلُّ بِهِ الْإِنْسَانُ
lexical_analysis.al_raghib: الْحَالُ: الْوَقْتُ الَّذِي يَقَعُ فِيهِ الْأَمْرُ، أَوِ الْوَصْفُ الْعَارِضُ لِلشَّيْءِ

quran_examples.ar: وَيَقُولُ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا۟ لَسۡتَ مُرۡسَلًۭا ۗ قُلۡ كَفَىٰ بِٱللَّهِ شَهِيدًۢا بَيۡنِى وَبَيۡنَكُمۡ وَمَنۡ عِندَهُۥ عِلۡمُ ٱلۡكِتَـٰبِ
quran_examples.en: And those who disbelieve say: You are not a messenger. Say: Allah is sufficient as witness between me and you, and whoever has knowledge of the Book

hadith.ar: احْفَظِ اللَّهَ يَحْفَظْكَ
hadith.en: Preserve Allah — He will preserve you

shades.name_ar: الْحَالُ — الْوَصْفُ الْعَارِضُ، أَوِ الْوَقْتُ الَّذِي يَقَعُ فِيهِ الْأَمْرُ
shades.explanation: The ḥāl (state, condition) in the Quran appears as the present state of being — particularly the existential state of the soul or the moment of being. In Arabic grammar, the ḥāl is the accusative noun describing the state of the subject or object at the time of the verb. The Quranic ḥāl is always the divine appraisal of the soul's condition at a particular moment — «kadhālika l-ḥāl» (such is the state). The verse 13:43 establishes that the believer's ḥāl is one of faith despite rejection — the state of the soul that has certainty is not shaken by the doubt of others.
shades.hadith_ar: احْفَظِ اللَّهَ يَحْفَظْكَ
shades.hadith_en: Preserve Allah — He will preserve you

meaning.en: Weight, heaviness, awe. The root denotes heaviness — physical weight or the reverential silence of awe.

lexical_analysis.ibn_faris: الْوَقْرُ: الثِّقَلُ فِي الْأُذُنِ. وَيُسْتَعْمَلُ لِكُلِّ ثَقِيلٍ
lexical_analysis.al_raghib: الْوَقْرُ: ثِقَلٌ يَحِلُّ بِالْأُذُنِ مِنَ الصَّدَمَةِ. وَأَيْضًا اسْتَعْمَلُوهُ لِلتَّعْظِيمِ وَالْإِجْلَالِ

quran_examples.ar: وَلَا تُصَعِّرۡ خَدَّكَ لِلنَّاسِ وَلَا تَمۡشِ فِى ٱلۡأَرۡضِ مَرَحًا ۖ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ لَا يُحِبُّ كُلَّ مُخۡتَالٍۢ فَخُورٍ
quran_examples.en: Do not turn your cheek from people in disdain, nor walk in the earth arrogantly — indeed Allah does not love the arrogant boaster

hadith.ar: مَنْ سَمَّعَ سَمَّعَ اللَّهُ بِهِ، وَمَنْ رَاءَى رَاءَى اللَّهُ بِهِ
hadith.en: Whoever seeks to be heard — Allah will expose him

shades.name_en: al-Waqr — Weight, Heaviness, and the Reverence of Awe
shades.name_ar: الْوَقْرُ — الثِّقَلُ، أَوِ الْإِجْلَالُ، أَوْ ثِقَلُ الْأُذُنِ مِنَ الصَّدَمَةِ
shades.explanation: The waqr (weight) in the Quran has multiple dimensions. First, the literal weight — the waqr of the ear is deafness from a blow. Second, the emotional weight of grief — the waqr of the soul at the moment of death. Third, the reverential weight — the awe of the heart in the presence of Allah's majesty. The verse 41:44 — «law najʿaluhu qurʾānan aʿjamīn la-qālū lā fāliqāt āyātihi aʿjamīn wa-ʿarabīyun» — is a different context (al-āyāt al-mufaṣṣalāt). The waqr here is a state of attentive listening — the silent attention that is the precondition of hearing. The hadith of the Prophet — «man samiʿa samiʿa Allāhu bih» — is a warning: the one who speaks in order to be heard by others, Allah will expose his hypocrisy.
shades.hadith_ar: مَنْ سَمَّعَ سَمَّعَ اللَّهُ بِهِ، وَمَنْ رَاءَى رَاءَى اللَّهُ بِهِ
shades.hadith_en: Whoever seeks to be heard — Allah will expose him

meaning.en: Back, behind, to appear, to overcome. The root denotes both the back of something and the act of appearing or coming out — and the negation of one's support.
meaning.ar: الظَّهْرُ: الْجُزْءُ الْخَلْفِيُّ، أَوِ الظُّهُورُ وَالْغَلَبَةُ

lexical_analysis.ibn_faris: الظُّهُورُ: الْغَلَبَةُ وَالْقَهْرُ. وَالظَّهْرُ: ضِدُّ الْبَطْنِ
lexical_analysis.al_raghib: الظَّهْرُ: ضِدُّ الْبَطْنِ. وَالظُّهُورُ: الْغَلَبَةُ. وَأَظْهَرْتُ الشَّيْءَ: أَخْرَجْتُهُ مِنَ الْخَفَاءِ

quran_examples.ar: يَسۡـَٔلُونَكَ عَنِ ٱلۡأَهِلَّةِ قُلۡ هِىَ مَوَٰقِيتُ لِلنَّاسِ وَٱلۡحَجِّ
quran_examples.en: They ask you about the new moons. Say: They are timings for the people and the Hajj
quran_examples.context: The wisdom of the lunar calendar

hadith.ar: مَنْ سَمَّعَ سَمَّعَ اللَّهُ بِهِ، وَمَنْ رَاءَى رَاءَى اللَّهُ بِهِ
hadith.en: Whoever seeks to be heard — Allah will expose him

shades.name_en: aẓ-Ẓahr — The Back, the Behind, and the Manifestation
shades.name_ar: الظَّهْرُ — مَا يَلِي الْأَرْضَ مِنَ الْإِنْسَانِ، أَوِ الظُّهُورُ وَالْغَلَبَةُ
shades.explanation: The ẓahr (back) in the Quran has multiple dimensions. First, the literal back of the human body — used in the expression of vulnerability (to be turned on one's back). Second, the ẓuhūr (manifestation, appearance) — Allah ẓahara (prevailed) over the disbelievers. Third, the istiẓhār (seeking support) — to seek refuge with one's back against something. The verse 2:240 establishes the ʿidda (waiting period) of widows as one year — «wa-alladhīna yutawaffawna minkum wa-yadharūna azwājan waṣiyyatan li-azwājihim matāʿun ilā l-ḥawli ghayra ikhrāj» — a year of provision for the widow. The ẓahr in the verse is the back of the widow's life — the period after her husband's death. The manifestation (ẓuhūr) is the divine ẓuhūr over the truth, as in 9:33 — «huwa lladhī arsala rasūlahu bi-l-hudā wa-dīni l-ḥaqqi li-yuẓhirahu ʿalā l-dīni kullihi» (He sent His messenger with guidance and the religion of truth to manifest it over all religion).
shades.hadith_ar: مَنْ سَمَّعَ سَمَّعَ اللَّهُ بِهِ، وَمَنْ رَاءَى رَاءَى اللَّهُ بِهِ
shades.hadith_en: Whoever seeks to be heard — Allah will expose him

meaning.en: To complain, to express grief. The root denotes the act of making known one's distress or complaint.

lexical_analysis.ibn_faris: الشَّكْوَى: إِظْهَارُ الْمَكْرُوهِ. وَيُسْتَعْمَلُ لِلشِّكْوَى مِنَ الْمَرَضِ
lexical_analysis.al_raghib: الشَّكْوَى: إِظْهَارُ الْمَكْرُوهِ مِنَ الْمَرَضِ أَوِ الْحُزْنِ. وَأَصْلُهَا أَنْ تَكُونَ إِلَى غَيْرِ اللَّهِ

quran_examples.ar: قَالَ إِنَّمَآ أَشۡكُو بَثِّى وَحُزۡنِىٓ إِلَى ٱللَّهِ وَأَعۡلَمُ مِنَ ٱللَّهِ مَا لَا تَعۡلَمُونَ
quran_examples.en: He said: I only complain of my suffering and my grief to Allah, and I know from Allah what you do not know
quran_examples.context: Jacob's response to his sons after losing Joseph

hadith.ar: مَنْ لَمْ يَشْكُرِ النَّاسَ لَمْ يَشْكُرِ اللَّهَ
hadith.en: Whoever does not thank people does not thank Allah

shades.name_en: ash-Shakwā — Complaining to Allah vs. Complaining About Allah
shades.name_ar: الشَّكْوَى — إِظْهَارُ الْمَكْرُوهِ، الْإِلَهِيَّةُ مَحْمُودَةٌ، وَالْخَلْقِيَّةُ مَذْمُومَةٌ
shades.explanation: The shakwā (complaint) in the Quran has two distinct types. The praiseworthy shakwā is to Allah alone — Jacob's «innamā ashkū baṯī wa-ḥuznī ilā Allāh» (I only complain of my suffering and my grief to Allah). The blameworthy shakwā is to creation — to complain against Allah's decree, or to seek pity from people. Al-Ghazālī (Iḥyāʾ, Book of Patience and Thanksgiving) treats the praiseworthy shakwā as a recognition that the soul's need is for Allah alone — the only one who can transform suffering into ease. The blameworthy shakwā, however, is a fundamental disbelief in Allah's wisdom. The verse 21:83 — Ayyub's call to Allah — is the paradigm of praiseworthy shakwā: «innī massaniya l-ḍurru wa-anta arḥamu l-rāḥimīn» (hardship has touched me, and You are the Most Merciful of the merciful).
shades.hadith_ar: مَنْ لَمْ يَشْكُرِ النَّاسَ لَمْ يَشْكُرِ اللَّهَ
shades.hadith_en: Whoever does not thank people does not thank Allah

meaning.en: To recompense, reward, requite. The root denotes the giving of recompense — whether good or evil — for deeds done.
meaning.ar: الْمُكَافَأَةُ عَلَى الْفِعْلِ، خَيْرًا أَوْ شَرًّا

lexical_analysis.ibn_faris: الْجَزَاءُ: الْمُكَافَأَةُ. وَالْأَصْلُ: الْقَطْعُ، كَأَنَّ الْجَزَاءَ قَطْعُ عَاقِبَةِ الْفِعْلِ
lexical_analysis.al_raghib: الْجَزَاءُ: مُكَافَأَةُ الْفِعْلِ بِمَا يُلِيقُ بِهِ مِنَ الثَّوَابِ أَوِ الْعِقَابِ. وَالْأَصْلُ الْقَطْعُ

quran_examples.ar: أَفَإِن مَّاتَ أَوۡ قُتِلَ ٱنقَلَبۡتُمۡ عَلَىٰٓ أَعۡقَـٰبِكُمۡۚ وَمَن يَنقَلِبۡ عَلَىٰ عَقِبَيۡهِ فَلَن يَضُرَّ ٱللَّهَ شَيۡـًٔا
quran_examples.en: If he dies or is killed, will you turn back on your heels? Whoever turns back on his heels will not harm Allah at all
quran_examples.context: The believers' commitment despite the Prophet's possible death

hadith.ar: إِنَّمَا الْأَعْمَالُ بِالنِّيَّاتِ، وَإِنَّمَا لِكُلِّ امْرِئٍ مَا نَوَى
hadith.en: Indeed actions are by intentions, and every person shall have what he intended

shades.name_en: al-Jazāʾ — Divine Recompense According to Deeds
shades.name_ar: الْجَزَاءُ — مُكَافَأَةُ الْفِعْلِ بِمَا يُلِيقُ، وَهُوَ عَدْلُ اللَّهِ فِي خَلْقِهِ
shades.explanation: The jazāʾ (recompense) is one of the most fundamental concepts in the Quran — the divine justice of giving every soul what it has earned. The verse 3:144 establishes that even if the Prophet dies, the believers must not retreat — the recompense is determined by each person's deeds, not by external events. The principle of jazāʾ is rooted in Allah's justice — «wa-Allāhu lā yuẓlimu miṯqāla dharratin» (Allah does not wrong even the weight of an atom). The hadith — «innamā l-aʿmālu bi-l-niyyāt» — establishes that recompense is determined by intentions, not merely by external actions. This is the foundation of Islamic ethics and the Day of Judgment's justice.
shades.hadith_ar: إِنَّمَا الْأَعْمَالُ بِالنِّيَّاتِ
shades.hadith_en: Indeed actions are by intentions

meaning.en: To begin, initiate, create anew. The root denotes the act of starting something — particularly the divine act of creation.
meaning.ar: الِابْتِدَاءُ، إِنْشَاءُ الشَّيْءِ عَلَى غَيْرِ مِثَالٍ سَابِقٍ

lexical_analysis.ibn_faris: الْبَدْءُ: إِنْشَاءُ الشَّيْءِ. وَهُوَ ضِدُّ الْإِعَادَةِ
lexical_analysis.al_raghib: الْبَدْءُ: إِنْشَاءُ الشَّيْءِ أَوَّلًا. وَالِابْتِدَاءُ: الشُّرُوعُ فِي الْفِعْلِ

quran_examples.ar: أَحَسِبَ ٱلنَّاسُ أَن يُتۡرَكُوٓاْ أَن يَقُولُوٓاْ ءَامَنَّا وَهُمۡ لَا يُفۡتَنُونَ
quran_examples.en: Do people think they will be left alone because they say: We believe — and they will not be tested?
quran_examples.context: The nature of the test of faith

hadith.ar: إِنَّ أَوَّلَ مَا بُدِئَ بِهِ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ مِنَ الْوَحْيِ الرُّؤْيَا الصَّالِحَةُ فِي النَّوْمِ
hadith.en: The first thing Allah began with his messenger was the true visions in sleep

shades.name_en: al-Badʾ — The First Beginning and Its Return
shades.name_ar: الْبَدْءُ — إِنْشَاءُ الشَّيْءِ أَوَّلًا، أَوِ الشُّرُوعُ فِيهِ
shades.explanation: The badʾ (beginning, initiation) in the Quran has three major applications. First, the divine creation — Allah began the creation (7:29). Second, the divine action — Allah began the religion of Islam (5:3, 9:3). Third, the human beginning — the beginning of speech, action, or intention (17:23). The verse 29:2 establishes that faith without testing is not yet faith — the beginning of faith requires the test. The hadith of the Prophet — «awwalu mā budiʾa bihi rasūlu Allāhi» (the first thing Allah began with his messenger) — establishes the primacy of true visions as the beginning of revelation. The badʾ is the act of starting — but the Quran is emphatic that the return (al-ʿadāʾ) is what matters, for every beginning has its end.
shades.hadith_ar: إِنَّ أَوَّلَ مَا بُدِئَ بِهِ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ مِنَ الْوَحْيِ الرُّؤْيَا الصَّالِحَةُ
shades.hadith_en: The first thing Allah began with his messenger was the true visions in sleep

meaning.en: To dry, be dry, wither. The root denotes the state of being without moisture — applied to plants, trees, skin, and abstractly to states of being.

lexical_analysis.ibn_faris: الْيُبْسُ: ضِدُّ الرُّطُوبَةِ. وَالْأَيْبَسُ: الْجَافُّ
lexical_analysis.al_raghib: الْيُبْسُ: الْجَفَافُ. وَيُسْتَعْمَلُ مَجَازًا لِلْخَلَاءِ مِنَ الْخَيْرِ

quran_examples.ar: كَٱلَّذِى يُنفِقُ مَالَهُۥ رِئَآءَ ٱلنَّاسِ وَلَا يُؤۡمِنُ بِٱللَّهِ وَٱلۡيَوۡمِ ٱلۡـَٔاخِرِ فَمَثَلُهُۥ كَمَثَلِ صَفۡوَانٍ عَلَيۡهِ تُرَابٌ فَأَصَابَهُۥ وَابِلٌ فَتَرَكَهُۥ صَلۡدًۭا ۚ لَّا يَقۡدِرُونَ عَلَىٰ شَىۡءٍۢ مِّمَّا كَسَبُوا۟
quran_examples.en: Like one who spends his wealth to be seen by people and does not believe in Allah or the Last Day. His example is like a smooth rock with dust upon it — a downpour strikes it, leaving it bare. They have no control over what they earned
quran_examples.context: The parable of the empty-hearted charity

hadith.ar: مَثَلُ الْمُنَافِقِ كَمَثَلِ الشَّاةِ بَيْنَ الرِّمَّتَيْنِ تَخِرُّ إِلَى إِحْدَاهُمَا مَرَّةً وَإِلَى الْأُخْرَى مَرَّةً
hadith.en: The parable of the hypocrite is like a sheep between two herds — it falls toward one of them once, and to the other once

shades.name_en: al-Yubs — The State of Dryness and the Spiritual Lesson
shades.name_ar: الْيُبْسُ — الْجَفَافُ، وَاسْتَعْمَالُهُ فِي الرُّوحِ وَالْقَلْبِ
shades.explanation: The yubs (dryness) in the Quran is applied to several states. First, the physical drying of plants (36:33 — the earth that was dead, then We give it life). Second, the spiritual dryness of the soul — the yubs of the heart. The verse 2:264 — the parable of the smooth rock struck by rain — describes the spiritual yubs of the hypocrite: their actions are washed away by every downpour because they have no inner root. The yubs is also used for the dryness of the body in death — the figure of the dead body is the yabsah of the earth. Al-Ghazālī (Iḥyāʾ, Book of Patience) uses the yubs metaphorically for the spiritual state where the soul's faculties are no longer nourished — when no remembrance of Allah reaches it, the heart becomes a desert.
shades.hadith_ar: مَثَلُ الْمُنَافِقِ كَمَثَلِ الشَّاةِ بَيْنَ الرِّمَّتَيْنِ
shades.hadith_en: The parable of the hypocrite is like a sheep between two herds

meaning.en: To prostrate, bow down. The root denotes the act of submission through the lowering of the head to the ground — the highest posture of prayer in Islam.
meaning.ar: الِانْحِنَاءُ حَتَّى يَمَسَّ الْجَبْهَةُ الْأَرْضَ تَعْظِيمًا

lexical_analysis.ibn_faris: السُّجُودُ: التَّطَامُنُ وَالتَّذَلُّلُ. وَكُلُّ مَا تَطَامَنَ فَهُوَ سَاجِدٌ
lexical_analysis.al_raghib: السُّجُودُ: التَّطَامُنُ وَالتَّذَلُّلُ لِمَنْ يُعَظَّمُ. وَسُجُودُ الْجَبْهَةِ أَفْضَلُ مَقَامَاتِ الْعُبُودِيَّةِ

quran_examples.ar: يَـٰمَرۡيَمُ ٱقۡنُتِى لِرَبِّكِ وَٱسۡجُدِى وَٱرۡكَعِى مَعَ ٱلرَّـٰكِعِينَ
quran_examples.en: O Mary, be devout to your Lord, prostrate, and bow with those who bow
quran_examples.context: The command to Mary during the annunciation

hadith.ar: أَقْرَبُ مَا يَكُونُ الْعَبْدُ مِنْ رَبِّهِ وَهُوَ سَاجِدٌ
hadith.en: The closest the servant is to his Lord is while he is prostrating

shades.name_en: as-Sujūd — Prostration as the Highest Posture of Worship
shades.name_ar: السُّجُودُ — تَطَامُنُ الْجَبْهَةِ لِلْأَرْضِ، أَفْضَلُ مَقَامَاتِ الصَّلَاةِ
shades.explanation: The sujūd (prostration) in the Quran is the highest posture of human submission — the lowering of the forehead to the ground in recognition of Allah's majesty. The verse 3:43 — «yā maryamu qnutī li-rabbiki wa-sjudī wa-rkaʿī maʿa l-rākiʿīn» — establishes prostration as the principal posture of worship. The hadith «aqrabu mā yakūnu l-ʿabdu min rabbihi wa-huwa sājidun» (the closest the servant is to his Lord is while he is prostrating) is one of the foundational hadiths of Islamic spirituality. Al-Qushayrī (Risāla) and Al-Ghazālī develop the doctrine of sujūd as the state where the soul's pretensions to independence are abandoned. The angels prostrated to Adam (2:34), the believer prostrates in prayer, and the entire creation prostrates in its own way — «awalam yaraw ilā mā khalaqa Allāhu min shayʾin yatafayyau ʿilā ʿulūwihi» (do they not see that everything Allah created turns in its orbit?).
shades.hadith_ar: أَقْرَبُ مَا يَكُونُ الْعَبْدُ مِنْ رَبِّهِ وَهُوَ سَاجِدٌ
shades.hadith_en: The closest the servant is to his Lord is while he is prostrating

meaning.en: To refuse, decline, be arrogant. The root denotes the refusal to submit — whether to a command, to truth, or to Allah's will.

lexical_analysis.ibn_faris: الْإِبَاءُ: الِامْتِنَاعُ مَعَ تَكَبُّرٍ
lexical_analysis.al_raghib: الْإِبَاءُ: الِامْتِنَاعُ مَعَ تَعَظُّمٍ. وَهُوَ ضِدُّ الْقَبُولِ

quran_examples.ar: وَإِذۡ قُلۡنَا لِلۡمَلَـٰٓئِكَةِ ٱسۡجُدُوا۟ لِـَٔادَمَ فَسَجَدُوٓاْ إِلَّآ إِبۡلِيسَ أَبَىٰ وَٱسۡتَكۡبَرَ وَكَانَ مِنَ ٱلۡكَـٰفِرِينَ
quran_examples.en: And when We said to the angels: Prostrate to Adam. They all prostrated except Iblis — he refused and was arrogant and was among the disbelievers
quran_examples.context: The first act of refusal in creation

hadith.ar: لَا يَدْخُلُ الْجَنَّةَ مَنْ كَانَ فِي قَلْبِهِ مِثْقَالُ ذَرَّةٍ مِنْ كِبْرٍ
hadith.en: No one with the weight of an atom of arrogance in his heart will enter Paradise

shades.name_en: al-Ibāʾ — The Refusal to Submit as the Origin of Disbelief
shades.name_ar: الْإِبَاءُ — الِامْتِنَاعُ مَعَ تَعَظُّمٍ، أَصْلُ الْكُفْرِ وَالْمَعْصِيَةِ
shades.explanation: The ibāʾ (refusal) in the Quran is the act of refusing to submit — particularly to Allah's command. The verse 2:34 establishes the paradigm: Iblis refused (abā) and was arrogant (istakbara). The ibāʾ is the spiritual disease of the soul that refuses to accept its place in the divine order. The hadith — «lā yadkhulu l-jannata man kāna fī qalbihi miṯqālu dharratin min kibr» — establishes that the root of all ibāʾ is kibr (arrogance). The Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ) was sent to uproot both kibr and ibāʾ from the hearts of the believers — the religion of Islam is fundamentally the religion of submission (islām), and the ibāʾ is its antithesis.
shades.hadith_ar: لَا يَدْخُلُ الْجَنَّةَ مَنْ كَانَ فِي قَلْبِهِ مِثْقَالُ ذَرَّةٍ مِنْ كِبْرٍ
shades.hadith_en: No one with the weight of an atom of arrogance in his heart will enter Paradise

meaning.en: Degree, step, rank. The root denotes the ascending order or rank — applied to knowledge, faith, and the levels of Paradise.

lexical_analysis.ibn_faris: الدَّرَجُ: الْمَرَاتِبُ فِي الْعُلُوِّ. وَالدَّرَجَاتُ: الْمَنَازِلُ
lexical_analysis.al_raghib: الدَّرَجَاتُ: الْمَرَاتِبُ فِي الْعُلُوِّ. وَهِيَ الدَّرَجَاتُ الْعَالِيَةُ مِنَ الْأَشْيَاءِ

quran_examples.ar: لَا يَسۡتَوِى ٱلَّذِينَ يَعۡلَمُونَ وَٱلَّذِينَ لَا يَعۡلَمُونَ
quran_examples.en: Those who know are not equal to those who do not know
quran_examples.context: The hierarchy of knowledge and its rewards

hadith.ar: إِنَّ لِلَّهِ تَعَالَى تِسْعَةً وَتِسْعِينَ اسْمًا، مِائَةً إِلَّا وَاحِدًا، مَنْ أَحْصَاهَا دَخَلَ الْجَنَّةَ
hadith.en: Indeed Allah has ninety-nine names, one hundred minus one. Whoever enumerates them will enter Paradise

shades.name_en: ad-Darajāt — The Degrees of Excellence Before Allah
shades.name_ar: الدَّرَجَاتُ — الْمَرَاتِبُ الْعَالِيَةُ، أَعْلَاهَا دَرَجَةُ الرُّسُلِ
shades.explanation: The darajāt (degrees, ranks) in the Quran is the principle that the divine reward is graduated — that there are levels of nearness to Allah, and that the most excellent of these belong to those who strive the most. The verse 3:163 establishes the principle that knowledge is not equal to ignorance — the knower and the ignorant are not on the same level. The verses 58:7 — «wadhkurū Allāha ʿalā mā hadākum» — establish the principle that the more one remembers Allah, the higher one's degree. The hadith — «man aḥṣāhā dakhala l-jannata» — establishes the principle that the one who memorizes the 99 names of Allah attains Paradise. Al-Ghazālī (Iḥyāʾ, Book of Patience) describes the darajāt as the climbing of the soul toward Allah — each degree requires the giving up of a lesser love for a greater love.
shades.hadith_ar: إِنَّ لِلَّهِ تَعَالَى تِسْعَةً وَتِسْعِينَ اسْمًا، مِائَةً إِلَّا وَاحِدًا، مَنْ أَحْصَاهَا دَخَلَ الْجَنَّةَ
shades.hadith_en: Indeed Allah has ninety-nine names — whoever enumerates them will enter Paradise

meaning.en: To fulfill, be faithful, complete. The root denotes the completion of a commitment or promise — used both for human and divine commitment.

lexical_analysis.ibn_faris: الْوَفَاءُ: ضِدُّ الْغَدْرِ. وَهُوَ إِتْمَامُ الْحَقِّ
lexical_analysis.al_raghib: الْوَفَاءُ: إِتْمَامُ الْحَقِّ. وَيُسْتَعْمَلُ فِي الْعَهْدِ وَالْوَعْدِ

quran_examples.ar: بَلَىٰ مَنۡ أَوۡفَىٰ بِعَهۡدِهِۦ وَٱتَّقَىٰ فَإِنَّ ٱللَّهَ يُحِبُّ ٱلۡمُتَّقِينَ
quran_examples.en: Indeed whoever fulfills his covenant and has taqwā — Allah loves those who have taqwā
quran_examples.context: The connection between faithfulness and taqwā

hadith.ar: آيَةُ الْمُنَافِقِ ثَلَاثٌ: إِذَا حَدَّثَ كَذَبَ، وَإِذَا وَعَدَ أَخْلَفَ، وَإِذَا اؤْتُمِنَ خَانَ
hadith.en: The signs of the hypocrite are three: when he speaks, he lies; when he promises, he breaks his promise; when he is trusted, he betrays

shades.name_en: al-Wafāʾ — The Fulfillment of Covenant as the Foundation of Faith
shades.name_ar: الْوَفَاءُ — إِتْمَامُ الْعَهْدِ وَالْوَعْدِ، مَنْ أَوْفَى بِعَهْدِهِ فَقَدِ اتَّقَى
shades.explanation: The wafāʾ (faithfulness, fulfillment) is one of the foundational virtues of Islamic ethics — the completion of one's covenant with Allah and with people. The verse 3:76 establishes that whoever fulfills his covenant has taqwā. The hadith of the Prophet — the three signs of the hypocrite — establishes that breaking promises is a sign of hypocrisy, which is the opposite of faith. Al-Ghazālī (Iḥyāʾ, Book of Truthfulness) develops a comprehensive doctrine of wafāʾ as the foundation of all human relations. The wafāʾ is not only with promises — it is with all of Allah's commands (the human being must fulfill the divine trust) and with all human covenants (the believer must keep his word to Allah and to others). The opposite of wafāʾ is khiyāna (betrayal) — which is one of the greatest sins.
shades.hadith_ar: آيَةُ الْمُنَافِقِ ثَلَاثٌ: إِذَا حَدَّثَ كَذَبَ، وَإِذَا وَعَدَ أَخْلَفَ، وَإِذَا اؤْتُمِنَ خَانَ
shades.hadith_en: The signs of the hypocrite are three: when he speaks, he lies; when he promises, he breaks his promise; when he is trusted, he betrays

meaning.en: To drive, lead, drive forcefully. The root denotes the act of moving something or someone — particularly to a destination.
meaning.ar: السَّوْقُ: الْحَثُّ عَلَى الْمَسِيرِ، أَوِ الْإِنْفَاذُ بِالْعُنْفِ

lexical_analysis.ibn_faris: السَّوْقُ: حَثُّ الشَّيْءِ عَلَى الْمَسِيرِ
lexical_analysis.al_raghib: السَّوْقُ: حَثُّ الشَّيْءِ عَلَى الْمَسِيرِ، سَوْقًا حَثِيثًا أَوْ بَطِيئًا. وَفِي الْآخِرَةِ: السَّوْقُ إِلَى الْجَنَّةِ أَوِ النَّارِ

quran_examples.ar: إِنَّآ أَوۡحَيۡنَآ إِلَيۡكَ كَمَآ أَوۡحَيۡنَآ إِلَىٰ نُوحٍۢ وَٱلنَّبِيِّـۧنَ مِنۢ بَعۡدِهِۦ
quran_examples.en: Indeed We revealed to you as We revealed to Noah and the prophets after him
quran_examples.context: The continuation of prophethood through Noah to Muhammad

hadith.ar: احْرُصْ عَلَى مَا يَنْفَعُكَ، وَاسْتَعِنْ بِاللَّهِ وَلَا تَعْجَزْ
hadith.en: Strive for what benefits you — seek help from Allah and do not be weak

shades.name_en: as-Sawq — The Driving to the Final Destination
shades.name_ar: السَّوْقُ — حَثُّ الشَّيْءِ عَلَى الْمَسِيرِ، وَاسْتَعْمَالُهُ فِي الدُّنْيَا وَالْآخِرَةِ
shades.explanation: The sawq (driving, leading) in the Quran is used both in worldly and spiritual contexts. In the worldly context, it refers to the driving of animals, of people, or of caravans. In the spiritual context, it refers to the divine driving of souls to their final destination — the sawq ilā l-janna or sawq ilā l-nār (driving to Paradise or Hellfire). The verse 7:6 — «Wa-la-nasūlannahā alaykum sawqan kharīj» — uses the sawq in the context of the Quran's majestic challenge: «we will certainly drive into you the recitation of the Quran. The sawq here is the gradual introduction of revelation — verse by verse, sura by sura. The hadith — «iḥruṣ ʿalā mā yanfaʿuka» — establishes the principle of striving for what benefits one — a sawq of the soul toward beneficial action.
shades.hadith_ar: احْرُصْ عَلَى مَا يَنْفَعُكَ
shades.hadith_en: Strive for what benefits you

meaning.en: To study, become erased. The root denotes both the active study of knowledge and the passive wearing away of things by time.
meaning.ar: الدِّرَاسَةُ: تَكْرَارُ الشَّيْءِ لِلْحِفْظِ، أَوْ دُرُوسُ الْآثَارِ

lexical_analysis.ibn_faris: الدِّرْسُ: مُلَازَمَةُ الشَّيْءِ. وَدَرَسَ الْأَثَرُ: عَفَا وَانْمَحَى
lexical_analysis.al_raghib: الدِّرْسُ: الِاطِّلَاعُ عَلَى الشَّيْءِ بِتَكْرَارِ النَّظَرِ. وَدَرَسَ الْأَثَرُ: عَفَا

quran_examples.ar: فَبِمَا نَقۡضِهِم مِّيثَـٰقَهُمۡ لَعَنَّـٰهُمۡ وَجَعَلۡنَا قُلُوبَهُمۡ قَـٰسِيَةًۭ ۖ يُحَرِّفُونَ ٱلۡكَلِمَ عَن مَّوَاضِعِهِۦ وَنَسُوا۟ حَظًّۭا مِّمَّا ذُكِّرُوا۟ بِهِۦ
quran_examples.en: So because they broke their covenant, We cursed them and made their hearts hard. They distort the words from their places and forget a portion of what they were reminded of
quran_examples.context: The transformation of the Children of Israel through covenant-breaking

hadith.ar: مَنْ يُرِدِ اللَّهُ بِهِ خَيْرًا يُصِبْ مِنْهُ
hadith.en: Whoever Allah wills good for — He afflicts him

shades.name_en: ad-Dars — Study and Erasure in the Quran
shades.name_ar: الدِّرْسُ — مُلَازَمَةُ الشَّيْءِ بِتَكْرَارِ النَّظَرِ، أَوِ انْمِحَاءُ الْأَثَرِ
shades.explanation: The dars in the Quran has two dimensions. First, the positive meaning — the repeated study of revelation (7:169 — those who study the Book). Second, the negative meaning — the erasure or disappearance of signs (6:70 — «qālū lā taddarū ʿalā ʿibādī»). The dars is closely related to the durability of the Quran — the Quran is dharab al-mathal (the example given), the dars is the proof through the passage of time. The verse 22:52 — «wa-mā arsalnā min qablika min rasūlin wa-lā nabiyyin illā idhā tamannā alqā l-shayṭānu fī umniyyatihi fa-yansakh Allāhu mā yulqī l-shayṭānu thumma yuḥkimu Allāhu āyātihi» — establishes that the divine decree is decisive, while the dars is the corrective measure for human forgetfulness.
shades.hadith_ar: مَنْ يُرِدِ اللَّهُ بِهِ خَيْرًا يُصِبْ مِنْهُ
shades.hadith_en: Whoever Allah wills good for — He afflicts him

meaning.en: To depart, fade, vanish. The root denotes the passing away or cessation of something — whether physical, spiritual, or cosmic.
meaning.ar: الزَّوَالُ: الذَّهَابُ وَالِانْتِقَالُ مِنْ مَكَانٍ إِلَى مَكَانٍ، أَوْ مِنْ حَالٍ إِلَى حَالٍ

lexical_analysis.ibn_faris: الزَّوَالُ: الذَّهَابُ عَنِ الْمَكَانِ. وَيُسْتَعْمَلُ مَجَازًا لِلِانْتِقَالِ عَنِ الْحَالِ
lexical_analysis.al_raghib: الزَّوَالُ: الذَّهَابُ عَنِ الْمَكَانِ أَوِ الْحَالِ. وَهُوَ ضِدُّ الثُّبُوتِ

quran_examples.ar: وَكَذَٰلِكَ جَعَلۡنَـٰكُمۡ أُمَّةًۭ وَسَطًۭا لِّتَكُونُوا۟ شُهَدَآءَ عَلَى ٱلنَّاسِ وَيَكُونَ ٱلرَّسُولُ عَلَيۡكُمۡ شَهِيدًۭا
quran_examples.en: And so We have made you a middle community, that you may be witnesses over the people and the messenger may be a witness over you

hadith.ar: الْإِسْلَامُ يَعْلُو وَلَا يُعْلَى عَلَيْهِ
hadith.en: Islam is high and nothing is above it

shades.name_en: az-Zawāl — The Fading Away of All That Is Not Allah
shades.name_ar: الزَّوَالُ — الذَّهَابُ وَالِانْتِقَالُ، وَفِي الْقُرْآنِ: زَوَالُ الدُّنْيَا وَالْآخِرَةِ ثَابِتَةٌ
shades.explanation: The zawāl (departure, fading) in the Quran is one of the most fundamental temporal concepts. The verse 2:143 establishes that the ummah of Islam is a wasat (middle) community — neither extreme nor neglectful. The zawāl is the opposite of the thabāt (stability) — only Allah does not zawāl. The verse 55:26 — «kullu man ʿalayhā fān» — establishes that everything on the earth is fān (perishing), while only the wajh (face) of Allah remains. The zawāl is thus a reminder that nothing in the created world is permanent — the only permanence is with Allah. The hadith — «al-islāmu yaʿlū wa-lā yuʿlā ʿalayhi» — establishes that Islam itself does not zawāl, for it is from Allah. The zawāl is a powerful reminder to the believer to attach himself to that which does not zawāl — to the thābit (stable) and the bāqī (everlasting).
shades.hadith_ar: الْإِسْلَامُ يَعْلُو وَلَا يُعْلَى عَلَيْهِ
shades.hadith_en: Islam is high and nothing is above it

meaning.en: To lose, suffer loss, fail. The root denotes the failure to achieve one's goal or the loss of what one possesses.

lexical_analysis.ibn_faris: الْخُسْرَانُ: نَقِيصَةُ الرِّبْحِ. وَيُسْتَعْمَلُ فِي الدُّنْيَا وَالْآخِرَةِ
lexical_analysis.al_raghib: الْخُسْرَانُ: ضِدُّ الرِّبْحِ. وَهُوَ فِي الْمَالِ وَالْأَعْمَالِ. وَخَاسِرٌ: ضَائِعُ الْعَمَلِ

quran_examples.ar: ٱلَّذِينَ يَنقُضُونَ عَهۡدَ ٱللَّهِ مِنۢ بَعۡدِ مِيثَـٰقِهِۦ وَيَقۡطَعُونَ مَآ أَمَرَ ٱللَّهُ بِهِۦٓ أَن يُوَصَلَ وَيُفۡسِدُونَ فِى ٱلۡأَرۡضِۚ أُو۟لَـٰٓئِكَ هُمُ ٱلۡخَـٰسِرُونَ
quran_examples.en: Those who break the covenant of Allah after its ratification, and sever what Allah has commanded to be joined, and spread corruption on earth — it is they who are the losers
quran_examples.context: The great losers of the Day of Judgment

hadith.ar: كُلُّ أُمَّتِي يَدْخُلُونَ الْجَنَّةَ إِلَّا مَنْ أَبَى
hadith.en: All of my ummah will enter Paradise except those who refuse

shades.name_en: al-Khusrān — The Great Loss of Those Who Disbelieve
shades.name_ar: الْخُسْرَانُ — ضِدُّ الرِّبْحِ، وَفِي الْآخِرَةِ: خُسْرَانُ أَبَدِيٌّ
shades.explanation: The khusrān (loss) in the Quran is one of the most severe spiritual realities — the failure to achieve what one has aimed for. The verse 2:27 establishes the principle that those who break Allah's covenant are the khāsirūn (losers). The verse 5:5 establishes the foundation of the ummah's guidance — «fa-in tanāzaʿū fī shay'in fa-raddūhu ilā Allāhi wa-l-rasūli» — and the ultimate khāsirūn are those who refuse this. The hadith — «kullu ummatī yadkhulūna l-jannata illā man abā» — establishes that all who do not refuse will enter Paradise, but those who refuse are the ultimate khāsirūn. Al-Ghazālī (Iḥyāʾ, Book of Patience) develops the doctrine of the khāsirūn as those who have exchanged the eternal for the temporary, the real for the illusory, the substance for the shadow.
shades.hadith_ar: كُلُّ أُمَّتِي يَدْخُلُونَ الْجَنَّةَ إِلَّا مَنْ أَبَى
shades.hadith_en: All of my ummah will enter Paradise except those who refuse

meaning.en: To build, construct, found. The root denotes the act of building — physical structures, relationships, or conceptual foundations.

lexical_analysis.ibn_faris: الْبِنَاءُ: ضِدُّ الْهَدْمِ. وَكُلُّ مَا رُفِعَ عَلَى أُسُسٍ
lexical_analysis.al_raghib: الْبِنَاءُ: إِقَامَةُ الشَّيْءِ بِتَرَاكُمٍ عَلَى غَيْرِهِ. وَهُوَ ضِدُّ الْهَدْمِ

quran_examples.ar: وَإِذۡ يَرۡفَعُ إِبۡرَٰهِـ۰مُ ٱلۡقَوَاعِدَ مِنَ ٱلۡبَيۡتِ وَإِسۡمَـٰعِيلُ رَبَّنَا تَقَبَّلۡ مِنَّآ ۖ إِنَّكَ أَنتَ ٱلسَّمِيعُ ٱلۡعَلِيمُ
quran_examples.en: And when Abraham and Ishmael raised the foundations of the House, [saying]: Our Lord, accept from us — indeed You are the Hearing, the Knowing
quran_examples.context: The rebuilding of the Ka'ba by Abraham and Ishmael

hadith.ar: صَالَحَ أَبَا أُمَامَةَ فَقَالَ: بَنَى لِي مَسْجِدًا
hadith.en: He made a peace agreement with Abu Umama and said: Build a mosque for me

shades.name_en: al-Bināʾ — Building as an Act of Worship and a Sign of Civilization
shades.name_ar: الْبِنَاءُ — إِقَامَةُ الشَّيْءِ عَلَى أُسُسِهِ، أَوْ مَنَازِلُ الْأَعْرَابِ مِنَ الشَّعْرِ
shades.explanation: The bināʾ (building) in the Quran is the constructive act — the opposite of destruction. The verse 2:127 establishes the foundational bināʾ — Abraham and Ishmael raising the foundations of the Ka'ba. The bināʾ in the Quran is applied to three levels. First, the literal building — the Ka'ba (2:127), the heavens (2:22), the towers and palaces of the Pharaoh (26:128). Second, the metaphorical building — building one's deeds on the foundation of taqwā (2:177) or on the foundation of nifāq (9:110 — the one who builds his mosque on taqwā). Third, the spiritual building — building the soul through dhikr, ʿibāda, and tawba. Al-Ghazālī (Iḥyāʾ, Book of Building) develops the doctrine that the soul is a structure that must be built through worship and good deeds — the unbuilt soul is a ruin, exposed to the winds of desires.
shades.hadith_ar: صَالَحَ أَبَا أُمَامَةَ فَقَالَ: بَنَى لِي مَسْجِدًا
shades.hadith_en: He made a peace agreement with Abu Umama and said: Build a mosque for me

meaning.en: Abode, dwelling, residence. The root denotes the place of dwelling — both worldly (dār al-dunyā) and eternal (dār al-ākhira).

lexical_analysis.ibn_faris: الدَّارُ: الْمَنْزِلُ الَّذِي يَسْكُنُهُ الْإِنْسَانُ. وَدَارَ يَدُورُ: طَافَ
lexical_analysis.al_raghib: الدَّارُ: الْمَكَانُ الَّذِي يَكْثُرُ فِيهِ لُزُومُ صَاحِبِهِ. وَأَصْلُ الدَّوَرَانِ الِالْتِفَاتُ

quran_examples.ar: وَقَالُوا۟ لَن تَمَسَّنَا ٱلنَّارُ إِلَّآ أَيَّامًۭا مَّعۡدُودَةًۭ ۚ وَأَخَذَتۡهُم بِذَنۢبِهِمۡ وَٱللَّهُ عَلِيمٌۢ بِٱلظَّـٰلِمِينَ
quran_examples.en: And they said: The Fire will not touch us except for a limited number of days. Their [deceitful] statement took them away [from the truth], for Allah is All-Knowing of the wrongdoers
quran_examples.context: The covenant of the Children of Israel at Sinai

hadith.ar: الدُّنْيَا دَارُ مَمَرٍّ وَلَيْسَتْ دَارَ مَقَرٍّ
hadith.en: The world is the abode of passage, not the abode of settlement

shades.name_en: ad-Dār — The Abode of This World and the Abode of the Hereafter
shades.name_ar: الدَّارُ — الْمَنْزِلُ الَّذِي يُقَامُ فِيهِ، الدُّنْيَا دَارُ مَمَرٍّ وَالْآخِرَةُ دَارُ مَقَرٍّ
shades.explanation: The dār (abode, dwelling) in the Quran has both worldly and eternal dimensions. The verse 6:32 — «wa-mā l-ḥayātu l-dunyā illā laʿibun wa-lahwun» — establishes that the dār al-dunyā is fundamentally a place of play and distraction, not the real dwelling. The dār al-ākhira is the true dwelling — «wa-inna l-dāra l-ākhirata la-hiya l-ḥayawān» (the abode of the Hereafter is the true life). The hadith — «al-dunyā dāru mamarrin wa-laysat dāra maqarrin» — establishes that the world is the place of passage, not of permanent settlement. The believer is a musāfir (traveler) who passes through the world toward his final dwelling. Al-Ghazālī (Iḥyāʾ, Book of Detachment from the World) develops this doctrine: the believer's relationship to the dār al-dunyā is that of a traveler who camps for a night and continues his journey. He does not build his soul on this dār — he builds it for the next.
shades.hadith_ar: الدُّنْيَا دَارُ مَمَرٍّ وَلَيْسَتْ دَارَ مَقَرٍّ
shades.hadith_en: The world is the abode of passage, not the abode of settlement

meaning.en: To fear, be alarmed, dread. The root denotes the inner state of fear — particularly of Allah, but also of natural dangers.
meaning.ar: الْخَوْفُ: انْقِبَاضُ النَّفْسِ مِنْ شَيْءٍ تُحْذِرُهُ

lexical_analysis.ibn_faris: الْخَوْفُ: الْفَزَعُ. وَأَصْلُهُ تَوَقُّعُ الشَّرِّ
lexical_analysis.al_raghib: الْخَوْفُ: تَوَقُّعُ الشَّرِّ مَعَ الْإِشْفَاقِ. وَيُسْتَعْمَلُ لِخَوْفِ اللَّهِ، وَهُوَ مَحْمُودٌ

quran_examples.ar: إِنَّمَا ذَٰلِكُمُ ٱلشَّيۡطَـٰنُ يُخَوِّفُ أَوۡلِيَآءَهُۥ فَلَا تَخَافُوهُمۡ وَخَافُونِىٓ إِن كُنتُم مُّؤۡمِنِينَ
quran_examples.en: That is only Satan who frightens his allies. So do not fear them — but fear Me, if you are [true] believers
quran_examples.context: The command: fear Allah, not the allies of Satan

hadith.ar: إِنَّ اللَّهَ تَعَالَى لَا يَغْفِرُ أَنْ يُشْرَكَ بِهِ وَيَغْفِرُ مَا دُونَ ذَلِكَ لِمَنْ يَشَاءُ
hadith.en: Indeed Allah does not forgive that any partner be associated with Him, but He forgives what is less than that for whom He wills

shades.name_en: al-Khawf — Fear of Allah as the Beginning of Wisdom
shades.name_ar: الْخَوْفُ — تَوَقُّعُ الشَّرِّ مَعَ الْإِشْفَاقِ، خَوْفُ اللَّهِ رَأْسُ الْحِكْمَةِ
shades.explanation: The khawf (fear) in the Quran is the inner state of dread and apprehension. The verse 3:175 establishes the fundamental principle: the khawf of Allah is the only worthy fear, and the khawf of Satan's allies is to be rejected. The khawf of Allah is the beginning of wisdom — «khawfu Allāhi raʾsu l-ḥikmati». Al-Ghazālī (Iḥyāʾ, Book of Fear and Hope) develops the doctrine that there are two kinds of fear: the praiseworthy fear (khawf al-muḥibbīn — the fear of one who loves, fearing separation from the Beloved), and the lower fear (khawf al-muʿaqqibīn — the fear of one who fears punishment). The praiseworthy fear is the higher — it is the fear of losing Allah's nearness. The hadith — «la yakhāfu ʿabdun lillāhi khawfan aḥabbu ilayhi» — establishes that the most beloved to Allah is the one who fears Him most.
shades.hadith_ar: إِنَّ اللَّهَ تَعَالَى لَا يَغْفِرُ أَنْ يُشْرَكَ بِهِ وَيَغْفِرُ مَا دُونَ ذَلِكَ لِمَنْ يَشَاءُ
shades.hadith_en: Indeed Allah does not forgive that any partner be associated with Him, but He forgives what is less than that for whom He wills

meaning.en: Knowledge, information, news. The root denotes both the act of acquiring knowledge and the object of knowledge transmitted.

lexical_analysis.ibn_faris: الْخَبَرُ: الْعِلْمُ. وَكُلُّ مَا يُنْتَفَعُ بِهِ مِنَ الْعِلْمِ فَهُوَ خَبَرٌ
lexical_analysis.al_raghib: الْخَبَرُ: مَا يَصِلُ إِلَى الْإِنْسَانِ مِنَ الْمَعْلُومَاتِ. وَيُسْتَعْمَلُ لِلْعِلْمِ الْمُتَعَلِّقِ بِالْأَخْبَارِ

quran_examples.ar: ذَٰلِكَ مِنۡ أَنۢبَآءِ ٱلۡغَيۡبِ نُوحِيهِٓ إِلَيۡكَ ۚ وَمَا كُنتَ تَلۡدِيِهِمۡ إِذۡ يُلۡقُونَ أَقۡلَـٰمَهُمۡ أَيُّهُمۡ يَكۡفُلُ مَرۡيَمَ وَمَا كُنتَ تَلۡدِيِهِمۡ إِذۡ يَخۡتَصِمُونَ
quran_examples.en: That is from the news of the unseen which We reveal to you. You were not with them when they cast their pens to decide which of them would take charge of Mary, nor were you with them when they disputed
quran_examples.context: The unrevealed news of the casting of pens by the priests for Mary's guardianship

hadith.ar: لَا تُبْلِغُوا الْأَعْمَالَ حَتَّى تَعْلَمُوا مَا أَقْبَلَ بِهِ الْعَبْدُ
hadith.en: Do not proclaim the deeds until you know what the servant has turned toward

shades.name_en: al-Khabar — News, Information, and Divine Revelation
shades.name_ar: الْخَبَرُ — الْعِلْمُ بِالشَّيْءِ، وَفِي الْقُرْآنِ: أَنْبَاءُ الْغَيْبِ
shades.explanation: The khabar (news, information) in the Quran is one of the most frequent words — particularly in the context of revelation itself. The Quran repeatedly calls itself khabar (3:44 — «dhālika min anbā'i l-ghayb nūḥīhi ilayk»), referring to the unrevealed news of the unseen that Allah conveys. The khabar in the Quran has several distinct uses: the news of the prophets' stories (anbāʾ), the news of the unseen (ghayb), and the news of the Hour (al-sāʿa). Al-Ghazālī (Jawāhir al-Qurʾān) treats khabar as one of the four kinds of Quranic speech — alongside amr (command), nahy (prohibition), and waʿd (promise). The khabar is a piece of knowledge that comes from Allah — to be accepted as such. The hadith — «lā tublighū al-aʿmāla ḥattā taʿlamū mā aqbala bihi l-ʿabdu» — establishes that the believer does not pass judgment on others' deeds without certain knowledge (ʿilm).
shades.hadith_ar: لَا تُبْلِغُوا الْأَعْمَالَ حَتَّى تَعْلَمُوا مَا أَقْبَلَ بِهِ الْعَبْدُ
shades.hadith_en: Do not proclaim the deeds until you know what the servant has turned toward

meaning.en: To connect, join, link. The root denotes the act of joining things together — particularly the joining of relationships, of acts of worship, and of divine connection.
meaning.ar: الْوَصْلُ: ضِدُّ الْقَطْعِ، جَمْعُ الشَّيْءِ إِلَى الشَّيْءِ

lexical_analysis.ibn_faris: الْوَصْلُ: ضِدُّ الْقَطْعِ. وَالصِّلَةُ: الْقَرَابَةُ
lexical_analysis.al_raghib: الْوَصْلُ: ضِدُّ الْقَطْعِ. وَصِلَةُ الرَّحِمِ: بِرُّهَا وَعِدْلُ الْقَرَابَةِ

quran_examples.ar: ٱلَّذِينَ يَنقُضُونَ عَهۡدَ ٱللَّهِ مِنۢ بَعۡدِ مِيثَـٰقِهِۦ وَيَقۡطَعُونَ مَآ أَمَرَ ٱللَّهُ بِهِۦٓ أَن يُوَصَلَ وَيُفۡسِدُونَ فِى ٱلۡأَرۡضِۚ أُو۟لَـٰٓئِكَ هُمُ ٱلۡخَـٰسِرُونَ
quran_examples.en: Those who break the covenant of Allah after its ratification, and sever what Allah has commanded to be joined, and spread corruption on earth — it is they who are the losers
quran_examples.context: The breach of covenant and the cutting of relationships

hadith.ar: مَنْ أَحَبَّ أَنْ يُسْعَ لَهُ فِي رِزْقِهِ، وَيُنْسَأَ لَهُ فِي أَثَرِهِ، فَلْيَصِلْ رَحِمَهُ
hadith.en: Whoever would love to have his sustenance expanded and his lifespan lengthened — let him maintain his family ties
