shades.name_en: al-Waṣl — The Joining of What Allah Has Commanded to Be Joined
shades.name_ar: الْوَصْلُ — ضِدُّ الْقَطْعِ، وَصِلَةُ الرَّحِمِ أَفْضَلُ الْوَصَايَا
shades.explanation: The waṣl (joining) in the Quran is one of the most fundamental ethical commands — to join what Allah has commanded to be joined. The verse 2:27 establishes that those who sever (yaqṭaʿūn) what Allah has commanded to be joined (mā amara Allāhu bihi an yuwaṣala) are the khāsirūn (losers). The waṣl in the Quran includes: the joining of family ties (ṣilat al-rahim), the joining of the Quran's verses, the joining of belief with action, and the joining of the believer with Allah. The hadith — «man aḥabba an yubsaʿa lahu fī rizqihi wa-yunsaʾa lahu fī atharihi falyaṣil rahma-hu» — establishes that the ṣilat al-rahim is one of the most effective means of expanding one's sustenance and lengthening one's lifespan.
shades.hadith_ar: مَنْ أَحَبَّ أَنْ يُسْعَ لَهُ فِي رِزْقِهِ، وَيُنْسَأَ لَهُ فِي أَثَرِهِ، فَلْيَصِلْ رَحِمَهُ
shades.hadith_en: Whoever would love to have his sustenance expanded — let him maintain his family ties

meaning.en: To separate, distinguish, divide. The root denotes the act of making distinct or separate — and by extension, fear (when the soul is separated from its source of comfort).
meaning.ar: الْفَرْقُ: ضِدُّ الْجَمْعِ، تَمْيِيزُ الشَّيْءِ عَنْ غَيْرِهِ

lexical_analysis.ibn_faris: الْفَرْقُ: تَمْيِيزُ الشَّيْءِ عَنْ غَيْرِهِ. وَالْفَزَعُ: خِلَافُهُ، أَيْ خِلَافُ الْأَمْنِ
lexical_analysis.al_raghib: الْفَرْقُ: تَمْيِيزُ الشَّيْءِ مِنْ غَيْرِهِ. وَالْفَزَعُ: الِاضْطِرَابُ مِنَ الرَّوْعِ. وَقَدْ يَتَقَارَبَانِ

quran_examples.ar: وَإِذۡ فَرَقۡنَا بِكُمُ ٱلۡبَحۡرَ فَأَنجَيۡنَـٰكُمۡ وَأَغۡرَقۧنَآ ءَالَ فِرۡعَوۡنَ وَأَنتُمۡ تَنظُرُونَ
quran_examples.en: And [recall] when We parted the sea for you and saved you and drowned the people of Pharaoh while you were looking on
quran_examples.context: The parting of the Red Sea

hadith.ar: كُنَّا إِذَا أَصَابَتْنَا مُصِيبَةٌ قُلْنَا هَذِهِ أَمَّتِي وَهَذَا دِينِي
hadith.en: When a calamity struck us, we said: This is my ummah and this is my religion

shades.name_en: al-Furqān — The Distinguishing Criterion and the Discriminating Judgment
shades.name_ar: الْفَرْقُ — تَمْيِيزُ الشَّيْءِ مِنْ غَيْرِهِ، أَوِ الْفَزَعُ مِنَ الْأَمْنِ
shades.explanation: The farq (distinguishing, separation) in the Quran has two major uses. First, the act of distinguishing — Allah yufarriqu (distinguishes) between truth and falsehood. The Quran itself is called al-Furqān (the Distinguishing Criterion) — «tabāraka lladhī nazzala l-furqāna ʿalā ʿabdihi» (blessed is He who sent down the Furqān to His servant). Second, the act of parting — the parting of the Red Sea (faraqnā) is the great miracle of Moses. The firaq (separation, parting) can also refer to the Day of Judgment — the separation of the believers from the disbelievers. Al-Ghazālī (Jawāhir al-Qurʾān) treats al-Furqān as one of the names of the Quran — the criterion that distinguishes truth from falsehood, guidance from misguidance.
shades.hadith_ar: كُنَّا إِذَا أَصَابَتْنَا مُصِيبَةٌ قُلْنَا هَذِهِ أَمَّتِي وَهَذَا دِينِي
shades.hadith_en: When a calamity struck us, we said: This is my ummah and this is my religion

meaning.en: To purify, refine, be pure. The root denotes the act of purifying — particularly the refining of gold from dross, or the soul from impurities.
meaning.ar: الصَّفْوُ: الْخُلُوصُ مِنَ الشَّوْبِ، نَقَاءُ الشَّيْءِ مِمَّا يُخَالِطُهُ

lexical_analysis.ibn_faris: الصَّفْوُ: الْخُلُوصُ. وَالصَّفِيُّ: الْخَالِصُ مِنْ كُلِّ شَيْءٍ
lexical_analysis.al_raghib: الصَّفْوُ: نَقَاءُ الشَّيْءِ مِمَّا يُخَالِطُهُ مِنَ الشَّوْبِ. وَصَفَوْتُ الشَّيْءَ: أَخْلَصْتُهُ

quran_examples.ar: مَّا كَانَ ٱللَّهُ لِيَذَرَ ٱلۡمُؤۡمِنِينَ عَلَىٰ مَآ أَنتُمۡ عَلَيۡهِ حَتَّىٰ يَمِيزَ ٱلۡخَبِيثَ مِنَ ٱلطَّيِّبِ
quran_examples.en: Allah would not leave the believers in the state you are in until He distinguishes the bad from the good
quran_examples.context: The divine testing to distinguish the sincere from the insincere

hadith.ar: إِنَّ اللَّهَ لَا يَنْظُرُ إِلَى صُوَرِكُمْ وَلَا إِلَى أَمْوَالِكُمْ، وَلَكِنْ يَنْظُرُ إِلَى قُلُوبِكُمْ وَأَعْمَالِكُمْ
hadith.en: Allah does not look at your forms nor your wealth, but He looks at your hearts and your deeds

shades.name_en: aṣ-Ṣafw — The Purity of Refined Love and Pure Intent
shades.name_ar: الصَّفْوُ — الْخُلُوصُ مِنَ الشَّوْبِ، صَفْوُ الْقَلْبِ مِنَ الشِّرْكِ
shades.explanation: The ṣafw (purity, refinement) in the Quran is the act of being pure from impurities — particularly the refinement of the soul from shirk (associating partners with Allah). The verse 3:179 establishes that Allah distinguishes (yamīz) the bad (khabīth) from the good (ṭayyib) through tests — the ṣafw of the soul is not automatic, but is the result of divine trial. The aṣfiyāʾ (the chosen pure ones) are the prophets and the awliyāʾ (the friends of Allah). The hadith — «inn Allāha lā yanẓuru ilā ṣuwarikum wa-lā ilā amwālikum, wa-lākin yanẓuru ilā qulūbikum wa-aʿmālikum» — establishes that Allah's sight is on the heart and its purity, not on the outward form. The ṣafw of the heart is the foundation of all spiritual attainment.
shades.hadith_ar: إِنَّ اللَّهَ لَا يَنْظُرُ إِلَى صُوَرِكُمْ وَلَا إِلَى أَمْوَالِكُمْ، وَلَكِنْ يَنْظُرُ إِلَى قُلُوبِكُمْ وَأَعْمَالِكُمْ
shades.hadith_en: Allah does not look at your forms nor your wealth, but He looks at your hearts and your deeds

meaning.en: To understand, comprehend. The root denotes the deep, intuitive understanding — beyond mere hearing or knowing.
meaning.ar: الْفَهْمُ: إِدْرَاكُ الشَّيْءِ بِالْقَلْبِ، أَعَمُّ مِنَ الْعِلْمِ

lexical_analysis.ibn_faris: الْفَهْمُ: الْعِلْمُ الَّذِي يَصِلُ إِلَى الْقَلْبِ
lexical_analysis.al_raghib: الْفَهْمُ: الْعِلَمُ الْمُؤَدِّي إِلَى مَعْرِفَةِ الشَّيْءِ بِطَرِيقِ الْإِدْرَاكِ

quran_examples.ar: فَفَهَّمۡنَـٰهَا سُلَيۡمَـٰنَ ۚ وَكُلًّا ءَاتَيۡنَا حُكۡمًا وَعِلۡمًا
quran_examples.en: And We gave Solomon [correct] understanding of it, and to each We gave judgment and knowledge
quran_examples.context: Solomon's superior understanding of the case of the two mothers and their child

hadith.ar: مَنْ يُرِدِ اللَّهُ بِهِ خَيْرًا يُفَقِّهْهُ فِي الدِّينِ
hadith.en: Whoever Allah wills good for — He grants him understanding (fiqh) of the religion

shades.name_en: al-Fahm — Deep Understanding as a Divine Gift
shades.name_ar: الْفَهْمُ — إِدْرَاكُ الشَّيْءِ بِالْقَلْبِ، أَعَمُّ مِنَ الْعِلْمِ وَأَخَصُّ مِنَ الْفِقْهِ
shades.explanation: The fahm (understanding) in the Quran is the deepest form of comprehension — the heart's reception of meaning. The verse 21:79 establishes that Solomon was given fahm (deep understanding) of the case — and to each of the prophets was given hukm (judgment) and ʿilm (knowledge). The fahm is distinct from ʿilm — it is the ʿilm that has penetrated the heart. The hadith — «man yuridi Allāhu bihi khayran yufaqqih-hu fī l-dīn» — establishes that fiqh (deep understanding) of the religion is the mark of divine goodness. Al-Ghazālī (Jawāhir al-Qurʾān) treats fahm as the precondition of ijtihād (independent reasoning) — the one who has fahm understands the divine wisdom behind the command, not merely the command itself.
shades.hadith_ar: مَنْ يُرِدِ اللَّهُ بِهِ خَيْرًا يُفَقِّهْهُ فِي الدِّينِ
shades.hadith_en: Whoever Allah wills good for — He grants him fiqh of the religion

meaning.en: To return, go back, revert. The root denotes the act of returning — whether physically, temporally, or spiritually.

lexical_analysis.ibn_faris: الرُّجُوعُ: الْعَوْدُ. وَكُلُّ مَا عُدْتَ إِلَيْهِ فَقَدْ رَجَعْتَ إِلَيْهِ
lexical_analysis.al_raghib: الرُّجُوعُ: الْعَوْدُ إِلَى الشَّيْءِ. وَفِي الشَّرْعِ: الْعَوْدُ إِلَى اللَّهِ بِالتَّوْبَةِ

quran_examples.ar: وَإِذۡ قَالَ مُوسَىٰ لِقَوۡمِهِۦ يَـٰقَوۡمِ إِنَّكُمۡ ظَلَمۡتُمۡ أَنفُسَكُم بِٱتِّخَاذِكُمُ ٱلۡعِجۡلَ فَتُوبُوٓاْ إِلَىٰ بَارِئِكُمۡ فَٱقۡتُلُوٓاْ أَنفُسَكُمۡ
quran_examples.en: And when Moses said to his people: O my people, you have wronged yourselves by taking the calf [for worship]. So repent to your Creator and kill yourselves
quran_examples.context: Moses' call to repentance after the worship of the calf

hadith.ar: كُلُّ بَنِي آدَمَ خَطَّاءٌ، وَخَيْرُ الْخَطَّائِينَ التَّوَّابُونَ
hadith.en: All the children of Adam are sinners, and the best of sinners are those who repent

shades.name_ar: الرُّجُوعُ — الْعَوْدُ، أَفْضَلُ الرُّجُوعِ الرُّجُوعُ إِلَى اللَّهِ
shades.explanation: The rujūʿ (return) in the Quran is the most fundamental spiritual movement — the return to Allah. The verse 2:54 establishes the principle that when the soul errs (worshipping the calf), it must return (tubū) to Allah and submit to His command. The rujūʿ in the Quran has several dimensions: the return of the soul to its Lord at death («Allāhu yatawaffā l-anfusa ḥīna mawtihā» — 3:145), the return to Allah on the Day of Judgment («ilā Allāhi masīruhum» — 3:28), the return to Allah through tawba (repentance), and the return through dhikr (remembrance). The hadith — «kullu banī ādama khaṭṭāʾun, wa-khayru l-khaṭṭāʾīna l-tawwābūn» — establishes that the human soul's fundamental movement is to err and to return — and the best of the erring are those who return often.
shades.hadith_ar: كُلُّ بَنِي آدَمَ خَطَّاءٌ، وَخَيْرُ الْخَطَّائِينَ التَّوَّابُونَ
shades.hadith_en: All the children of Adam are sinners, and the best of sinners are those who repent

meaning.en: To touch, afflict, reach. The root denotes physical contact or the experience of something reaching one.
meaning.ar: الْمَسُّ: إِصَابَةُ الشَّيْءِ، جِسِّيًّا أَوْ مَعْنَوِيًّا

lexical_analysis.ibn_faris: الْمَسُّ: إِصَابَةُ الشَّيْءِ بِالْحِسِّ. وَمَسَّهُ الشَّيْءُ: أَصَابَهُ
lexical_analysis.al_raghib: الْمَسُّ: إِصَابَةُ الشَّيْءِ لِلشَّيْءِ. وَيَتَقَيَّدُ تَارَةً بِالْحِسِّ الظَّاهِرِ، وَتَارَةً بِالْمَعْنَوِيِّ

quran_examples.ar: ٱلَّذِينَ يَأۡكُلُونَ ٱلرِّبَوٰاْ لَا يَقُومُونَ إِلَّا كَمَا يَقُومُ ٱلَّذِى يَتَخَبَّطُهُ ٱلشَّيۡطَـٰنُ مِنَ ٱلۡمَسِّ
quran_examples.en: Those who consume ribā will not stand except as one who is beaten by Satan into insanity. That is because they say: Trade is [just] like ribā
quran_examples.context: The parable of the consumer of ribā

hadith.ar: مَا أَصَابَ الْمُسْلِمَ مِنْ نَصَبٍ وَلَا وَصَبٍ وَلَا هَمٍّ وَلَا حَزَنٍ وَلَا أَذًى وَلَا غَمٍّ حَتَّى الشَّوْكَةُ يُشَاكُهَا إِلَّا كَفَّرَ اللَّهُ بِهَا مِنْ خَطَايَاهُ
hadith.en: No Muslim is afflicted with fatigue, illness, worry, grief, harm, or anxiety — not even a thorn that pricks him — except that Allah will expiate some of his sins through it

shades.name_en: al-Mass — The Touch of Trial and the Touch of Grace
shades.name_ar: الْمَسُّ — إِصَابَةُ الشَّيْءِ، مَسُّ الضُّرِّ أَوْ مَسُّ النَّعْمَاءِ
shades.explanation: The mass (touch, affliction) in the Quran has several dimensions. First, the physical touch — the touch of the hand, the touch of the foot, the touch of the head (in wudu). Second, the touch of trial — the verse 2:275 establishes that those who consume ribā are touched (yamasūhūn) by Satan's disturbance. Third, the touch of divine punishment — the 'adhab al-mass (the painful punishment) is the fire's touch. The hadith — «mā aṣāba l-muslim min naṣabin wa-lā waṣabin wa-lā hammin wa-lā ḥuznin wa-lā adhan wa-lā ghammin ḥattā l-shawkata yushākuhā illā kaffara Allāhu bihā min khaṭāyāhu» — establishes that every touch of hardship for the Muslim is an expiation of sins. The mass is thus both a warning and a mercy — a touch that purifies.
shades.hadith_ar: مَا أَصَابَ الْمُسْلِمَ مِنْ نَصَبٍ وَلَا وَصَبٍ وَلَا هَمٍّ وَلَا حَزَنٍ وَلَا أَذًى وَلَا غَمٍّ حَتَّى الشَّوْكَةُ يُشَاكُهَا إِلَّا كَفَّرَ اللَّهُ بِهَا مِنْ خَطَايَاهُ
shades.hadith_en: No Muslim is afflicted with fatigue, illness, worry, grief, harm, or anxiety — not even a thorn that pricks him — except that Allah will expiate some of his sins through it

meaning.en: To be pleased, satisfied, content. The root denotes the positive state of approval — the acceptance of what comes from Allah.

lexical_analysis.ibn_faris: الرِّضَا: الرَّاحَةُ. وَالرَّضِيَ الشَّيْءَ: أَحَبَّهُ وَارْتَاحَ إِلَيْهِ
lexical_analysis.al_raghib: الرِّضَا: الرَّاحَةُ لِلشَّيْءِ. وَهُوَ ضِدُّ السُّخْطِ. وَيُسْتَعْمَلُ لِرِضَا اللَّهِ عَنِ الْعَبْدِ، وَرِضَا الْعَبْدِ عَنِ اللَّهِ

quran_examples.ar: وَعَدَ ٱللَّهُ ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوا۟ مِنكُمۡ وَعَمِلُوا۟ ٱلصَّـٰلِحَـٰتِ لَيَسۡتَخۡلِفَنَّهُمۡ فِى ٱلۡأَرۡضِ
quran_examples.en: Allah has promised those who believe and do righteous deeds that He will surely make them successors in the earth
quran_examples.context: The divine promise of khilāfa to the believers

hadith.ar: مَنْ رَضِيَ بِقَسْمِ اللَّهِ كَانَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ رَاضِيًا
hadith.en: Whoever is pleased with Allah's decree — Allah will be pleased with him

shades.name_en: ar-Riḍā — The Divine Pleasure and Human Contentment
shades.name_ar: الرِّضَا — الرَّاحَةُ لِلشَّيْءِ، أَعْلَى مَرَاتِبِ الْعُبُودِيَّةِ
shades.explanation: The riḍā (pleasure, contentment) in the Quran is the highest state of the soul — the acceptance of what Allah has decreed. The verse 2:38 establishes the divine promise (waʿd) — those who believe and do righteous deeds will have khilāfa on the earth, with Allah's riḍā. The riḍā is both the divine pleasure (riḍā Allāh) and the human contentment (riḍā al-ʿabd). The hadith — «man raḍiya bi-qaṣmi Allāh kāna Allāhu ʿanhu rāḍiyā» — establishes that the believer's contentment with Allah's decree brings about Allah's pleasure. Al-Qushayrī (Risāla) develops the doctrine of riḍā as one of the stations of the wayfarers (sālikīn) — the highest station before riḍā is the tawakkul (reliance on Allah).
shades.hadith_ar: مَنْ رَضِيَ بِقَسْمِ اللَّهِ كَانَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ رَاضِيًا
shades.hadith_en: Whoever is pleased with Allah's decree — Allah will be pleased with him

meaning.en: Hot wind, intense heat, scorching. The root denotes the violent heat — both physical (the hot wind of the desert) and spiritual (the heat of punishment).
meaning.ar: الْحَمِيمُ: الشَّدِيدُ الْحَرَارَةِ مِنَ الْمَاءِ أَوِ الرِّيحِ

lexical_analysis.ibn_faris: الْحَمِيمُ: الْمَاءُ الشَّدِيدُ الْحَرَارَةِ. وَيُسْتَعْمَلُ لِلرِّيحِ الشَّدِيدَةِ الْحَرَارَةِ
lexical_analysis.al_raghib: الْحَمِيمُ: الشَّدِيدُ الْحَرَارَةِ. وَيُسْتَعْمَلُ لِلْمَاءِ وَالرِّيحِ

quran_examples.ar: مَثَلُ مَا يُنفِقُونَ فِى هَـٰذِهِ ٱلۡحَيَوٰةِ ٱلدُّنْيَا كَمَثَلِ رِيحٍ فِيهَا صِرٌّ أَصَابَتۡ حَرۡثَ قَوۡمٍۢ ظَلَمُوٓاْ أَنفُسَهُمۡ فَأَهۡلَكَتۡهُۥ ۚ وَمَا ظَلَمَهُمُ ٱللَّهُ وَلَـٰكِنۡ أَنفُسَهُمۡ يَظۡلِمُونَ
quran_examples.en: The example of what they spend in this worldly life is like a wind containing frost which struck the harvest of a people who wronged themselves and destroyed it. Allah did not wrong them — they wrong themselves
quran_examples.context: The parable of the cold frost

hadith.ar: أَهْلُ النَّارِ كُلُّ عَامٍ يَغْتَمِرُونَ فِيهِ سَبْعِينَ خَرِيفًا
hadith.en: The people of Hell drink boiling water (ḥamīm) that tears their bowels

shades.name_en: al-Ḥamīm — The Boiling Water and the Hot Wind
shades.name_ar: الْحَمِيمُ — الشَّدِيدُ الْحَرَارَةِ، شَرَابُ أَهْلِ النَّارِ
shades.explanation: The ḥamīm (boiling water, hot wind) in the Quran is one of the punishments of the Hereafter — the drink of the people of Hellfire. The verse 3:117 uses the related ṣirr (frost) in the parable of the wind that destroys the harvest. The ḥamīm is mentioned in multiple suras — the ablution of the people of Hell (al-wuṣūl) is with ḥamīm, and the cool shade of Paradise is with the kaʾs (cup) of non-intoxicating wine. The hadith — «ahlu l-nāri kullu ʿāmin yaqtamirūna fīhi sabʿīna kharīfā» — establishes that the people of Hell undergo tremendous heat for thousands of years. The ḥamīm is the antithesis of the barīd (coolness) that is the natural state of the believer in Paradise.
shades.hadith_ar: أَهْلُ النَّارِ كُلُّ عَامٍ يَغْتَمِرُونَ فِيهِ سَبْعِينَ خَرِيفًا
shades.hadith_en: The people of Hell drink boiling water that tears their bowels

meaning.en: To call, summon, supplicate. The root denotes the act of calling upon someone — particularly the calling upon Allah in supplication.
meaning.ar: الدُّعَاءُ: الْمُنَادَاةُ، وَطَلَبُ الْإِقْبَالِ عَلَى الْمَدْعُوِّ

lexical_analysis.ibn_faris: الدُّعَاءُ: النِّدَاءُ. وَيَتَقَيَّدُ تَارَةً بِالطَّلَبِ وَتَارَةً بِغَيْرِ الطَّلَبِ
lexical_analysis.al_raghib: الدُّعَاءُ: اسْمٌ لِطَلَبِ الْإِقْبَالِ عَلَى الْمَدْعُوِّ بِقَوْلٍ أَوْ فِعْلٍ. وَالدُّعَاءُ إِلَى اللَّهِ أَفْضَلُ الطَّاعَاتِ

quran_examples.ar: وَإِذَا سَأَلَكَ عِبَادِى عَنِّى فَإِنِّى قَرِيبٌ ۖ أُجِيبُ دَعۡوَةَ ٱلدَّاعِ إِذَا دَعَانِ
quran_examples.en: And when My servants ask you about Me — indeed I am near. I respond to the call of the caller when he calls upon Me
quran_examples.context: Allah's nearness to the supplicating servant

hadith.ar: الدُّعَاءُ هُوَ الْعِبَادَةُ
hadith.en: Supplication is worship

shades.name_en: ad-Duʿāʾ — The Calling Upon Allah as the Essence of Worship
shades.name_ar: الدُّعَاءُ — طَلَبُ الْإِقْبَالِ عَلَى الْمَدْعُوِّ، أَفْضَلُ الْعِبَادَاتِ
shades.explanation: The duʿāʾ (calling, supplication) in the Quran is one of the most fundamental acts of worship — the calling upon Allah. The verse 2:186 establishes the principle that Allah is near (qarīb) and answers the call (ujību daʿwata l-dāʿ). The duʿāʾ in the Quran has two dimensions: the duʿāʾ bi-l-fi'l (the call to action, such as calling to prayer) and the duʿāʾ bi-l-qalb (the inner supplication). The hadith — «al-duʿāʾu huwa l-ʿibāda» — establishes that supplication is the essence of worship. Al-Ghazālī (Iḥyāʾ, Book of Duʿāʾ) develops the doctrine that duʿāʾ is the highest manifestation of tawḥīd — it is the confession that only Allah has the power to grant and to avert.
shades.hadith_ar: الدُّعَاءُ هُوَ الْعِبَادَةُ
shades.hadith_en: Supplication is worship

meaning.en: To be fair, give half. The root denotes the act of giving the half-share — and more broadly, the principle of justice.

lexical_analysis.ibn_faris: النِّصْفُ: أَحَدُ الشَّيْئَيْنِ الْمُتَسَاوِيَيْنِ. وَيُسْتَعْمَلُ لِلْعَدْلِ
lexical_analysis.al_raghib: النِّصْفُ: الْحَظُّ مِنَ الشَّيْءِ. وَيُسْتَعْمَلُ لِلْعَدْلِ بَيْنَ الشَّيْئَيْنِ

quran_examples.ar: وَإِنۡ خِفۡتُمۡ أَلَّا تُقۡسِطُوا۟ فِى ٱلۡيَتَـٰمَىٰ فَٱنكِحُوا۟ مَا طَابَ لَكُم مِّنَ ٱلنِّسَآءِ مَثۡنَىٰ وَثُلَـٰثَ وَرُبَـٰعَ
quran_examples.en: And if you fear that you will not deal justly with the orphans, then marry [other] women as you may, two and three and four
quran_examples.context: The command to deal justly with orphans

hadith.ar: إِنَّ الْمُقْسِطِينَ عِنْدَ اللَّهِ عَلَى مَنَابِرَ مِنْ نُورٍ
hadith.en: The just will be on pulpits of light before Allah

shades.name_en: an-Niṣf — The Half-Share and the Principle of Justice
shades.name_ar: النِّصْفُ — أَحَدُ الشَّيْئَيْنِ الْمُتَسَاوِيَيْنِ، وَالْعَدْلُ بَيْنَهُمَا
shades.explanation: The niṣf (half) in the Quran is the half-share in inheritance and the principle of fairness (ʿadl). The verse 4:11 establishes the inheritance shares — the male gets the equivalent of two females' share («yidhūna l-dhukūr naṣīf»). The niṣf in the Quran is also used for the fairness of transaction (6:152 — «wa-niṣfi l-waʾdi»). The hadith — «inna l-muqsitīna ʿinda Allāhi ʿalā manābira min nūr» — establishes that the just are on pulpits of light on the Day of Judgment. Al-Ghazālī (Iḥyāʾ, Book of Justice) develops the doctrine that justice is the foundation of all human relations — without justice, neither the family nor the society can stand.
shades.hadith_ar: إِنَّ الْمُقْسِطِينَ عِنْدَ اللَّهِ عَلَى مَنَابِرَ مِنْ نُورٍ
shades.hadith_en: The just will be on pulpits of light before Allah

meaning.en: To follow, pursue, come after. The root denotes the act of coming after — and by extension, the act of following someone or something.

lexical_analysis.ibn_faris: الِاتِّبَاعُ: التَّوَخِّي لِسُلُوكِ طَرِيقِ الْمَتْبُوعِ. وَالتَّبِيعُ: الِاسْتِدْلَالُ بِآثَارِ الْأَشْيَاءِ
lexical_analysis.al_raghib: التَّابِعُ: الْجَائِي بَعْدَ غَيْرِهِ. وَاتَّبَعْتُهُ: سِرْتُ خَلْفَهُ، أَوْ قَصَّيْتُ أَثَرَهُ

quran_examples.ar: وَكَذَٰلِكَ جَعَلۡنَـٰكُمۡ أُمَّةًۭ وَسَطًۭا لِّتَكُونُوا۟ شُهَدَآءَ عَلَى ٱلنَّاسِ وَيَكُونَ ٱلرَّسُولُ عَلَيۡكُمۡ شَهِيدًۭا
quran_examples.en: And so We have made you a middle community, that you may be witnesses over the people and the messenger may be a witness over you
quran_examples.context: The middle ummah, called to follow the divine guidance

hadith.ar: مَنْ سَنَّ سُنَّةً حَسَنَةً فَلَهُ أَجْرُهَا وَأَجْرُ مَنْ عَمِلَ بِهَا إِلَى يَوْمِ الْقِيَامَةِ
hadith.en: Whoever establishes a good sunna will have its reward and the reward of those who act upon it until the Day of Judgment

shades.name_en: at-Tabaʿ — The Following as the Highest Act of Faith
shades.name_ar: التَّبَعُ — الْجَاءُ بَعْدَ الْغَيْرِ، وَاتِّبَاعُ الرَّسُولِ أَفْضَلُ الطَّاعَاتِ
shades.explanation: The tabaʿ (following) in the Quran is the fundamental movement of faith — following the divine guidance. The verse 2:143 establishes the principle that the ummah is a middle community — they follow (yattabiʿūn) the divine path. The tabaʿ in the Quran has several dimensions: the following of the messenger («ittabiʿū lladhī unzila ilaykum» — 2:174), the following of truth («wa-alladhīna ihtadaw zādat-hum hudā» — 47:17), and the following of one's desires («wa-man arāda l-ākhirata wa-saʿā lahā saʿyaha» — 17:19). The hadith — «man sanna sunnatan ḥasanatan falahu ajruhā wa-ajru man ʿamila bihā» — establishes that the one who establishes a good sunna (way) has a continuing reward as long as others follow it.
shades.hadith_ar: مَنْ سَنَّ سُنَّةً حَسَنَةً فَلَهُ أَجْرُهَا وَأَجْرُ مَنْ عَمِلَ بِهَا
shades.hadith_en: Whoever establishes a good sunna will have its reward and the reward of those who act upon it

meaning.en: Comfort, rest, ease. The root denotes the state of relief from difficulty — and by extension, the good news of ease.

lexical_analysis.ibn_faris: الرَّوْحُ: الرَّاحَةُ. وَالرَّاحَةُ: ضِدُّ التَّعَبِ
lexical_analysis.al_raghib: الرَّوْحُ: الرَّاحَةُ بَعْدَ الضِّيقِ. وَالرَّاحَةُ: ضِدُّ التَّعَبِ

quran_examples.ar: يُرِيدُ ٱللَّهُ بِكُمُ ٱلۡيُسۡرَ وَلَا يُرِيدُ بِكُمُ ٱلۡعُسۡرَ
quran_examples.en: Allah intends for you ease and does not intend for you hardship
quran_examples.context: The divine intent of ease for the believers

hadith.ar: مَعَ الْعُسْرِ يُسْرًا، إِنَّ مَعَ الْعُسْرِ يُسْرًا
hadith.en: With hardship comes ease — indeed with hardship comes ease

shades.name_ar: الرَّاحَةُ — ضِدُّ التَّعَبِ، وَالرَّاحَةُ الْأَبَدِيَّةُ فِي الْجَنَّةِ
shades.explanation: The rāḥa (rest, comfort) in the Quran is one of the divine gifts to the believer — the rest after toil. The verse 2:185 establishes the principle that Allah intends ease (yusr) for the believer, not hardship (ʿusr). The rāḥa is both physical (rest of the body) and spiritual (tranquility of the soul). The verse 16:97 establishes the rāḥa of the righteous — «man ʿamila ṣāliḥan min dhakarin aw unthā wa-huwa muʾminun fa-la-nuḥyiyannahu ḥayātan ṭayyibah» (whoever does righteous deeds, male or female, while a believer — We will surely grant them a good life). The hadith — «maʿa l-ʿusri yusran, inna maʿa l-ʿusri yusran» — establishes that with every hardship comes ease. Al-Ghazālī (Iḥyāʾ, Book of Patience) treats the rāḥa as the divine gift that comes after sabr (patience) — the one who is patient in hardship receives the rāḥa of ease.
shades.hadith_ar: مَعَ الْعُسْرِ يُسْرًا، إِنَّ مَعَ الْعُسْرِ يُسْرًا
shades.hadith_en: With hardship comes ease — indeed with hardship comes ease

meaning.en: Righteous, kindness, dutiful. The root denotes the act of being righteous — particularly the dutiful kindness to parents and relatives.
meaning.ar: الْبِرُّ: الطَّاعَةُ مَعَ مَزِيدِ الْإِحْسَانِ، وَصِلَةُ الرَّحِمِ

lexical_analysis.ibn_faris: الْبِرُّ: الطَّاعَةُ. وَهُوَ أَعَمُّ مِنَ الْإِحْسَانِ. وَالْبَرُّ: الْوَاسِعُ الْخَيْرِ
lexical_analysis.al_raghib: الْبِرُّ: طَاعَةُ اللَّهِ مَعَ مَحَبَّةٍ. وَهُوَ أَعَمُّ مِنَ الْإِحْسَانِ

quran_examples.ar: وَإِذۡ أَخَذۡنَا مِيثَـٰقَ بَنِىٓ إِسۡرَٰٓءِيلَ لَا تَعۡبُدُونَ إِلَّا ٱللَّهَ وَبِٱلۡوَٰلِدَيۡنِ إِحۡسَانًا وَذِى ٱلۡقُرۡبَىٰ وَٱلۡيَتَـٰمَىٰ وَٱلۡمَسَـٰكِينِ
quran_examples.en: And [recall] when We took the covenant from the Children of Israel: You shall not worship except Allah, and to parents do good, and to relatives, orphans, and the needy
quran_examples.context: The covenant of the Children of Israel

hadith.ar: الْجَنَّةُ تَحْتَ أَقْدَامِ الْأُمَّهَاتِ
hadith.en: Paradise is beneath the feet of mothers

shades.name_en: al-Birr — Righteous Obedience to Allah and Dutiful Kindness
shades.name_ar: الْبِرُّ — طَاعَةُ اللَّهِ مَعَ مَحَبَّةٍ، أَعَمُّ مِنَ الْإِحْسَانِ
shades.explanation: The birr (righteousness, dutiful kindness) in the Quran is one of the most comprehensive ethical concepts — it includes all forms of obedience to Allah, kindness to parents, kindness to relatives, and good deeds in general. The verse 2:83 establishes the covenant that includes birr — «wa-bi-l-wālidayni iḥsānan» (and to parents do good). The birr in the Quran is wider than iḥsān (goodness) — birr is the totality of obedience and dutiful kindness. The hadith — «al-jannatu taḥta aqḍāmi l-ummahāt» — establishes that Paradise is beneath the feet of mothers — a paradigm of birr. Al-Ghazālī (Iḥyāʾ, Book of Etiquette) treats birr as the foundation of all ethics — the one who has birr to his parents, relatives, and Allah has the foundation of all virtue.
shades.hadith_ar: الْجَنَّةُ تَحْتَ أَقْدَامِ الْأُمَّهَاتِ
shades.hadith_en: Paradise is beneath the feet of mothers

meaning.en: To compel, force, drive. The root denotes the forcing or driving of someone — particularly the forcing of actions contrary to one's will.

lexical_analysis.ibn_faris: الْإِيصَارُ: الْحَثُّ الشَّدِيدُ. وَكُلُّ مَنْ حَمَلَ غَيْرَهُ عَلَى شَيْءٍ فَقَدْ آصَرَهُ
lexical_analysis.al_raghib: الْإِيصَارُ: الْحَثُّ الشَّدِيدُ بِحَقٍّ أَوْ لِغَرَضٍ. وَأَصَرَّهُ: أَلْزَمَهُ

quran_examples.ar: وَإِن كُنتُمۡ عَلَىٰ سَفَرٍ وَلَمۡ تَجِدُوا۟ كَاتِبًۭا فَرِهَـٰنٌۭ مَّقۡبُوضَةٌۭ
quran_examples.en: And if you are on a journey and cannot find a scribe, then a security deposit [should be] taken
quran_examples.context: The rules of debt and security on a journey

hadith.ar: لَا يَدْخُلُ الْجَنَّةَ مَنْ كَانَ فِي قَلْبِهِ مِثْقَالُ حَبَّةٍ مِنْ خَرْدَلٍ مِنْ كِبْرٍ
hadith.en: No one with the weight of a mustard seed of arrogance will enter Paradise

shades.name_en: al-Īṣār — The Compelling Force and the Pledge
shades.name_ar: الْإِيصَارُ — الْحَثُّ الشَّدِيدُ، أَوْ مَا يُلْزِمُ بِهِ نَفْسَهُ مِنَ النَّذْرِ
shades.explanation: The īṣār (compelling, pledge) in the Quran has two main uses. First, the literal force — the forcing of someone to do something. Second, the religious pledge — what one binds himself to do, particularly in the context of vows and covenants. The verse 5:49 establishes the principle that the believer's pledge (īṣār) is a matter of conscience — they must follow the divine law even if it contradicts the pledge. The hadith — «lā yadkhulu l-jannata man kāna fī qalbihi miṯqālu ḥabbatin min khardalin min kibr» — establishes that no arrogant person enters Paradise. The īṣār in the spiritual sense is the binding of the soul to a particular commitment — a voluntary commitment that becomes a sacred bond.
shades.hadith_ar: لَا يَدْخُلُ الْجَنَّةَ مَنْ كَانَ فِي قَلْبِهِ مِثْقَالُ حَبَّةٍ مِنْ خَرْدَلٍ مِنْ كِبْرٍ
shades.hadith_en: No one with the weight of a mustard seed of arrogance will enter Paradise

meaning.en: To be beautiful, shine, be radiant. The root denotes beauty and radiance — particularly of face or appearance.

lexical_analysis.ibn_faris: الْبَهَاءُ: الْجَمَالُ. وَتَبَاهَى الشَّيْءُ: تَجَمَّلَ
lexical_analysis.al_raghib: الْبَهَاءُ: الْجَمَالُ الَّذِي يَلِيقُ بِهِ التَّبَاهِي. وَتَبَاهَى: افْتَخَرَ بِجَمَالِهِ

quran_examples.ar: وَإِذۡ قَالَ عِيسَى ٱبۡنُ مَرۡيَمَ يَـٰبَنِىٓ إِسۡرَٰٓءِيلَ إِنِّى رَسُولُ ٱللَّهِ إِلَيۡكُم مُّصَدِّقًۭا لِّمَا بَيۡنَ يَدَىَّ مِنَ ٱلتَّوۡرَىٰةِ وَمُبَشِّرًۢا بِرَسُولٍۢ يَأۡتِى مِنۢ بَعۡدِى ٱسۡمُهُۥٓ أَحۡمَدُ
quran_examples.en: And when Jesus, son of Mary, said: O Children of Israel, indeed I am the messenger of Allah to you, confirming what came before me of the Torah and bringing good tidings of a messenger to come after me whose name is Ahmad
quran_examples.context: The prophecy of Ahmad in the Gospel

hadith.ar: كَانَ وَجْهُ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ مِثْلَ الْقَمَرِ
hadith.en: The face of the Messenger of Allah was like the moon

shades.name_en: al-Bahāʾ — The Beauty and Radiance of Light
shades.name_ar: الْبَهَاءُ — الْجَمَالُ وَالْحُسْنُ، الْإِشْرَاقُ الَّذِي يَأْخُذُ الْقَلْبَ
shades.explanation: The bahāʾ (beauty, radiance) in the Quran is one of the divine attributes — the radiant beauty of Allah's creation. The verse 61:6 establishes the prophecy of Ahmad in the Gospel — the coming of a prophet whose name is Ahmad. The bahāʾ in the Quran is closely related to nūr (light) — the beauty of the believer is the light of his faith. The hadith of the Prophet — «kāna wajhu rasūli Allāhi mithla l-qamar» (the face of the Messenger of Allah was like the moon) — establishes that the beauty of the Prophet was a manifestation of divine beauty. Al-Ghazālī (Jawāhir al-Qurʾān) develops the doctrine that the bahāʾ of the believer is a reflection of his inner state — the one whose heart is illuminated has a face that shines.
shades.hadith_ar: كَانَ وَجْهُ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ مِثْلَ الْقَمَرِ
shades.hadith_en: The face of the Messenger of Allah was like the moon

meaning.en: To pasture, graze, watch over. The root denotes the act of pasturing animals — and by extension, the watchful care of a shepherd.

lexical_analysis.ibn_faris: الرَّعْيُ: أَكْلُ الْمَاشِيَةِ مِنَ الْعُشْبِ. وَالرَّاعِي: حَافِظُهَا
lexical_analysis.al_raghib: الرَّعْيُ: أَكْلُ الْبَهِيمَةِ مِنَ النَّبَاتِ. وَالرَّاعِي: حَافِظُ الْمَاشِيَةِ. وَقِيلَ: كُلُّ حَافِظٍ رَاعٍ

quran_examples.ar: وَأَنَّ ٱقۡصُدۡ فِى مَشۡيِكَ وَٱغۡضُضۡ مِن صَوۡتِكَ ۚ إِنَّ أَنكَرَ ٱلۡأَصۡوَٰتِ لَصَوۡتُ ٱلۡحَمِيرِ
quran_examples.en: And be moderate in your pace and lower your voice. Indeed the most disagreeable of sounds is the voice of donkeys
quran_examples.context: The Prophet's command to Luqman about his manner and voice

hadith.ar: كُلُّكُمْ رَاعٍ وَكُلُّكُمْ مَسْئُولٌ عَنْ رَعِيَّتِهِ
hadith.en: Each of you is a shepherd and each of you is responsible for his flock

shades.name_en: ar-Raʿy — Pasturage and the Shepherd's Responsibility
shades.name_ar: الرَّعْيُ — الرِّعَايَةُ، وَكُلُّ رَاعٍ مَسْئُولٌ عَنْ رَعِيَّتِهِ
shades.explanation: The raʿy (pasturage, shepherd's care) in the Quran is the watchful care of the shepherd for his flock — and by extension, the responsibility of every leader for those under his care. The verse 20:14 establishes the principle of moderation in movement and voice — Luqman's advice to his son. The raʿy in the Quran is closely related to wilāya (guardianship) and imāma (leadership). The hadith — «kullukum rāʿin wa-kullukum masʾūlun ʿan raʿiyyatihi» (each of you is a shepherd and each of you is responsible for his flock) — is one of the foundational hadiths of Islamic governance. It establishes that the leader, the father, the husband, and the teacher are all rāʿūn (shepherds) responsible for their raʿiyya (flock). Al-Māwardī (al-Aḥkām al-Sulṭāniyya) develops this hadith as the foundation of political theory in Islam.
shades.hadith_ar: كُلُّكُمْ رَاعٍ وَكُلُّكُمْ مَسْئُولٌ عَنْ رَعِيَّتِهِ
shades.hadith_en: Each of you is a shepherd and each of you is responsible for his flock

meaning.en: To last forever, be perpetual, be eternal. The root denotes the state of permanence and eternity — particularly of the Hereafter.

lexical_analysis.ibn_faris: الدَّوَامُ: الْبَقَاءُ. وَكُلُّ مَا دَامَ فَقَدْ بَقِيَ
lexical_analysis.al_raghib: الدَّوَامُ: الْبَقَاءُ عَلَى الْحَالِ. وَدَامَ الشَّيْءُ: لَمْ يَزُلْ

quran_examples.ar: كُلُّ مَنۡ عَلَيۡهَا فَانٍۭ ۖ وَيَبۡقَىٰ وَجۡهُ رَبِّكَ ذُو ٱلۡجَلَـٰلِ وَٱلۡإِكۡرَامِ
quran_examples.en: Everyone upon the earth will perish, and there will remain the Face of your Lord, Owner of Majesty and Honor
quran_examples.context: The impermanence of all that is on earth

hadith.ar: كُلُّ شَيْءٍ يَهْلِكُ إِلَّا وَجْهَهُ
hadith.en: Everything perishes except His Face

shades.name_en: ad-Dawām — The Perpetuity of Allah and the Passing of Creation
shades.name_ar: الدَّوَامُ — الْبَقَاءُ، وَحَقِيقَةُ الدَّوَامِ لِلَّهِ وَحْدَهُ
shades.explanation: The dawām (perpetuity, permanence) in the Quran is the attribute that belongs to Allah alone. The verse 55:26 establishes the fundamental principle — «kullu man ʿalayhā fān» (everyone upon the earth will perish) and «wa-yabqā wajhu rabbika» (the Face of your Lord will remain). The dawām is the opposite of fanāʾ (passing away). The hadith — «kullu shayʾin yahliku illā wajhahu» (everything perishes except His Face) — establishes that only Allah has true perpetuity. Al-Ghazālī (Maqāṣid al-Falāsifa) treats the dawām as one of the divine attributes — Allah is al-Bāqī (the Everlasting), the One whose existence has no beginning and no end.
shades.hadith_ar: كُلُّ شَيْءٍ يَهْلِكُ إِلَّا وَجْهَهُ
shades.hadith_en: Everything perishes except His Face

meaning.en: Equal, same, even. The root denotes the state of equality or sameness — and by extension, the middle or common.

lexical_analysis.ibn_faris: السَّوَاءُ: الْوَسَطُ. وَسَوَاءٌ: وَسَطُ الشَّيْءِ
lexical_analysis.al_raghib: السَّوَاءُ: الْوَسَطُ الَّذِي يَسْتَوِي فِيهِ الْجَانِبَانِ. وَاسْتَوَى الشَّيْءُ: اعْتَدَلَ

quran_examples.ar: قُلۡ يَـٰٓأَهۡلَ ٱلۡكِتَـٰبِ تَعَالَوۡاْ إِلَىٰ كَلِمَةٍۢ سَوَآءٍۭ بَيۡنَنَا وَبَيۡنَكُمۡ أَلَّا نَعۡبُدَ إِلَّا ٱللَّهَ وَلَا نُشۡرِكَ بِهِۦ شَيۡـًٔا
quran_examples.en: Say: O People of the Book, come to a word common between us and you — that we worship none but Allah and do not associate anything with Him
quran_examples.context: The call to a common word with the People of the Book

hadith.ar: نَحْنُ مَعَاشِرَ الْأَنْبِيَاءِ لَا نُورَثُ، مَا تَرَكْنَاهُ صَدَقَةٌ
hadith.en: We prophets do not leave inheritance; what we leave is charity

shades.name_en: as-Sawāʾ — The Common Word and the State of Equality
shades.name_ar: السَّوَاءُ — الْوَسَطُ أَوِ الِاسْتِوَاءُ، كَلِمَةُ السَّوَاءِ هِيَ التَّوْحِيدُ
shades.explanation: The sawāʾ (equal, middle, common) in the Quran is the state of being equal or even — and by extension, the middle way. The verse 3:64 establishes the famous kalimatu sawāʾ (the common word) — the call to the People of the Book to come to a word that is common between Muslims and them. The kalimatu sawāʾ is the foundation of inter-religious dialogue: «an lā naʿbuda illā Allāha wa-lā nushrika bihi shayʾan» (we worship none but Allah and associate nothing with Him). The sawāʾ is the principle of equality — between believers and disbelievers in the judgment of justice, between spouses in the rights of marriage, and between peoples in the fundamental rights of humanity.
shades.hadith_ar: نَحْنُ مَعَاشِرَ الْأَنْبِيَاءِ لَا نُورَثُ، مَا تَرَكْنَاهُ صَدَقَةٌ
shades.hadith_en: We prophets do not leave inheritance; what we leave is charity

meaning.en: High, elevated, exalted. The root denotes elevation or loftiness — and by extension, the height of virtue or excellence.

lexical_analysis.ibn_faris: السَّنَاءُ: الْعُلُوُّ. وَكُلُّ مَا عَلَا فَهُوَ سَنِيٌّ
lexical_analysis.al_raghib: السَّنَاءُ: الْعُلُوُّ فِي الْفَضْلِ. وَسَنِيٌّ: شَرِيفٌ

quran_examples.ar: إِنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ يَكۡتُمُونَ مَآ أَنزَلَ ٱللَّهُ مِنَ ٱلۡكِتَـٰبِ وَيَشۡتَرُونَ بِهِۦ ثَمَنًۭا قَلِيلًا أُو۟لَـٰٓئِكَ مَا يَأۡكُلُونَ فِى بُطُونِهِمۡ إِلَّا ٱلنَّارَ
quran_examples.en: Indeed those who conceal what Allah has sent down of the Book and exchange it for a small price — those consume nothing but fire into their bellies
quran_examples.context: The condemnation of those who conceal the Book

hadith.ar: إِنَّ اللَّهَ رَفِيعُ الدَّرَجَاتِ
hadith.en: Indeed Allah is the Owner of High Ranks

shades.explanation: The sanāʾ (elevation, loftiness) in the Quran denotes the state of being elevated or exalted. The verse 2:174 condemns those who conceal the divine revelation — their consumption is only fire, not the sanāʾ of legitimate sustenance. The sanāʾ is the divine rank — the elevation that Allah grants to those whom He pleases. The hadith — «inna Allāha rafīqu l-darajāt» — establishes that Allah is the owner of high ranks. Al-Ghazālī (Jawāhir al-Qurʾān) treats the sanāʾ as the spiritual elevation that the believer attains through devotion — the closer to Allah, the higher the sanāʾ.
shades.hadith_ar: إِنَّ اللَّهَ رَفِيعُ الدَّرَجَاتِ
shades.hadith_en: Indeed Allah is the Owner of High Ranks

meaning.en: To make sacred, forbid, declare unlawful. The root denotes the prohibition of something — and by extension, the declaration of it as sacred and inviolable.
meaning.ar: التَّحْرِيمُ: التَّسْلِيطُ عَلَى الِامْتِنَاعِ، وَجَعْلُ الشَّيْءِ حَرَامًا

lexical_analysis.ibn_faris: التَّحْرِيمُ: مَنْعُ الْإِنْسَانِ مِنَ الشَّيْءِ. وَالْحَرَامُ: الْمَمْنُوعُ
lexical_analysis.al_raghib: التَّحْرِيمُ: التَّسْلِيطُ عَلَى الِامْتِنَاعِ مِنَ الشَّيْءِ. وَالْحَرَامُ: الْمَمْنُوعُ الَّذِي لَا يَحِلُّ الْإِقْدَامُ عَلَيْهِ

quran_examples.ar: إِنَّمَا حَرَّمَ عَلَيۡكُمُ ٱلۡمَيۡتَةَ وَٱلدَّمَ وَلَحۡمَ ٱلۡخِنزِيرِ وَمَآ أُهِلَّ بِهِۦ لِغَيۡرِ ٱللَّهِ
quran_examples.en: He has only forbidden to you the dead animal, blood, the flesh of swine, and that which has been dedicated to other than Allah

hadith.ar: إِنَّ اللَّهَ حَرَّمَ عَلَيْكُمْ عُقُوقَ الْأُمَّهَاتِ وَمَنْعًا وَهَاتِ
hadith.en: Allah has forbidden for you the disobedience of mothers, and to withhold (what you owe), and to demand (what you don't deserve)

shades.name_en: al-Taḥrīm — The Prohibition and the Sacred
shades.name_ar: التَّحْرِيمُ — مَنْعُ الشَّيْءِ وَتَحْرِيمُهُ، وَالْحَرَامُ مِنَ الطَّعَامِ وَالشَّرَابِ وَالْفِعْلِ
shades.explanation: The taḥrīm (prohibition, sanctification) in the Quran is one of the most fundamental legal concepts — the declaration of something as forbidden. The verse 2:173 establishes the forbidden foods in Islam — the mayta (dead animal), dam (blood), laḥm al-khinzīr (pork), and that which has been dedicated to other than Allah. The taḥrīm is the opposite of ibāḥa (permission). The hadith — «inna Allāha ḥarrama ʿalaykum ʿuqūqa l-ummahāti» — establishes that Allah has forbidden certain social evils as well — disobedience to mothers, withholding (what one owes), and demanding (what one does not deserve). Al-Ghazālī (Iḥyāʾ, Book of Lawful and Unlawful) treats the taḥrīm as a divine protection — what Allah has forbidden is forbidden for a reason (the protection of the soul, the mind, the wealth, the honor, or the lineage).
shades.hadith_ar: إِنَّ اللَّهَ حَرَّمَ عَلَيْكُمْ عُقُوقَ الْأُمَّهَاتِ
shades.hadith_en: Allah has forbidden for you the disobedience of mothers

meaning.en: To be patient, persevere, endure. The root denotes the act of remaining steadfast in the face of hardship — and is one of the most important Quranic virtues.
meaning.ar: الصَّبْرُ: حَبْسُ النَّفْسِ عَنِ الْجَزَعِ، وَالتَّمَاسُكُ فِي الْبَلَاءِ

lexical_analysis.ibn_faris: الصَّبْرُ: حَبْسُ النَّفْسِ عَنِ الْفَزَعِ. وَالصَّبُورُ: الَّذِي لَا يَسْتَعْجِلُ
lexical_analysis.al_raghib: الصَّبْرُ: حَبْسُ النَّفْسِ عَلَى مَا يَقْتَضِيهِ الْحَظُّ الْعَقْلِيُّ وَالشَّرْعِيُّ، أَوْ حَبْسُهَا عَمَّا يَنْهَى الْعَقْلُ وَالشَّرْعُ عَنْهُ

quran_examples.ar: يَـٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوا۟ ٱصۡبِرُوا۟ وَصَابِرُوا۟ وَرَابِطُوا۟ وَٱتَّقُوا۟ ٱللَّهَ لَعَلَّكُمۡ تُفۡلِحُونَ
quran_examples.en: O you who believe, persevere and endure and remain stationed and fear Allah that you may succeed
quran_examples.context: The command to patience and perseverance

hadith.ar: مَا يُصِيبُ الْمُسْلِمَ مِنْ نَصَبٍ وَلَا وَصَبٍ وَلَا هَمٍّ وَلَا حَزَنٍ وَلَا أَذًى وَلَا غَمٍّ حَتَّى الشَّوْكَةُ يُشَاكُهَا إِلَّا كَفَّرَ اللَّهُ بِهَا مِنْ خَطَايَاهُ
hadith.en: No Muslim is afflicted with fatigue, illness, worry, grief, harm, or anxiety — not even a thorn that pricks him — except that Allah will expiate some of his sins through it

shades.name_en: aṣ-Ṣabr — Patience as the Foundation of Faith
shades.name_ar: الصَّبْرُ — حَبْسُ النَّفْسِ عَنِ الْجَزَعِ، نِصْفُ الْإِيمَانِ
shades.explanation: The ṣabr (patience, perseverance) in the Quran is one of the most fundamental virtues — half of faith according to the hadith. The verse 2:153 establishes the famous command: «ṣbirū wa-ṣābirū wa-rābiṭū» (be patient, persevere, and remain stationed). The ṣabr in the Quran has three dimensions according to Al-Ghazālī: ṣabr ʿalā l-ṭāʿa (patience in obedience), ṣabr ʿan l-maʿṣiya (patience against disobedience), and ṣabr ʿalā l-balāʾ (patience in the face of trials). The hadith — «mā yuṣību l-muslim min naṣabin» — establishes that every hardship for the Muslim is an expiation of sins through patience. The ṣabr is thus the foundation of the spiritual life — without it, no virtue can be sustained.
shades.hadith_ar: مَا يُصِيبُ الْمُسْلِمَ مِنْ نَصَبٍ وَلَا وَصَبٍ وَلَا هَمٍّ وَلَا حَزَنٍ وَلَا أَذًى وَلَا غَمٍّ حَتَّى الشَّوْكَةُ يُشَاكُهَا إِلَّا كَفَّرَ اللَّهُ بِهَا مِنْ خَطَايَاهُ
shades.hadith_en: No Muslim is afflicted with fatigue — not even a thorn that pricks him — except that Allah will expiate some of his sins through it

meaning.en: To be eager, anxious, in a hurry. The root denotes the state of being eager — and by extension, the haste to do something.
meaning.ar: الْعَجَلَةُ: الِاسْتِعْجَالُ، طَلَبُ الشَّيْءِ قَبْلَ أَوَانِهِ

lexical_analysis.ibn_faris: الْعَجَلَةُ: الِاسْتِعْجَالُ. وَكُلُّ مَنْ طَلَبَ الشَّيْءَ قَبْلَ أَوَانِهِ فَقَدْ أَعْجَلَ
lexical_analysis.al_raghib: الْعَجَلَةُ: طَلَبُ الشَّيْءِ قَبْلَ وَقْتِهِ. وَهِيَ مَذْمُومَةٌ عِنْدَ طَلَبِ الشَّيْءِ قَبْلَ أَوَانِهِ، مَحْمُودَةٌ عِنْدَ الْإِنَابَةِ إِلَى اللَّهِ

quran_examples.ar: وَمَا لَكُمۡ لَا تُقَـٰتِلُونَ فِى سَبِيلِ ٱللَّهِ وَٱلۡمُسۡتَضۡعَفِينَ مِنَ ٱلرِّجَالِ وَٱلنِّسَآءِ وَٱلۡوِلۡدَٰنِ ٱلَّذِينَ يَقُولُونَ رَبَّنَآ أَخۡرِجۡنَا مِنۡ هَـٰذِهِ ٱلۡقَرۡيَةِ ٱلظَّالِمِ أَهۡلُهَا
quran_examples.en: And why should you not fight in the cause of Allah and the oppressed men, women, and children who say: Our Lord, take us out of this city whose people are wrongdoers
quran_examples.context: The call to fight for the oppressed

hadith.ar: الْعَجَلَةَ الْعَجَلَةَ، فَإِنَّمَا هَلَكَ مَنْ كَانَ قَبْلَكُمْ بِالْعَجَلَةِ
hadith.en: Beware of haste, for indeed those before you perished because of haste

shades.name_en: al-ʿAjala — The Haste and the Divine Wisdom
shades.name_ar: الْعَجَلَةُ — طَلَبُ الشَّيْءِ قَبْلَ أَوَانِهِ، مَذْمُومَةٌ عِنْدَ التَّكَلُّفِ مَحْمُودَةٌ عِنْدَ التَّوْبَةِ
shades.explanation: The ʿajala (haste) in the Quran is one of the human traits most criticized in the Quran. The verse 2:85 implicitly addresses haste — the call to fight in Allah's way is for the patient, not the hasty. The ʿajala is contrasted with sabr (patience) and taʾakhkhur (taking one's time). The hadith — «al-ʿajalata al-ʿajalata» — is the Prophet's warning that haste led to the destruction of past nations. Al-Ghazālī (Iḥyāʾ, Book of Discipline of the Soul) treats the ʿajala as one of the diseases of the soul — the soul that is in haste does not consider, does not consult, does not wait for divine wisdom. The cure for ʿajala is the tafakkur (reflection) and the taḥammul (forbearance).
shades.hadith_ar: الْعَجَلَةَ الْعَجَلَةَ، فَإِنَّمَا هَلَكَ مَنْ كَانَ قَبْلَكُمْ بِالْعَجَلَةِ
shades.hadith_en: Beware of haste, for indeed those before you perished because of haste

meaning.en: To read, recite, gather. The root denotes the act of reading — particularly the recitation of the Quran.
meaning.ar: الْقِرَاءَةُ: النُّطْقُ بِالْكَلَامِ الْمَكْتُوبِ أَوِ الْمَحْفُوظِ

lexical_analysis.ibn_faris: الْقِرَاءَةُ: جَمْعُ الْحُرُوفِ وَالْكَلِمَاتِ. وَالْقُرْآنُ: الْمَقْرُوءُ
lexical_analysis.al_raghib: الْقِرَاءَةُ: جَمْعُ الْحُرُوفِ الْمُتَفَرِّقَةِ فِي النُّطْقِ. وَالْقُرْآنُ: مَقْرُوءٌ، اسْمٌ لِهَذَا الْكِتَابِ

quran_examples.ar: ٱقۡرَأۡ بِٱسۡمِ رَبِّكَ ٱلَّذِى خَلَقَ
quran_examples.en: Read in the name of your Lord who created
quran_examples.context: The first revelation — the command to read

hadith.ar: اقْرَأُوا الْقُرْآنَ فَإِنَّهُ يَأْتِي يَوْمَ الْقِيَامَةِ شَفِيعًا لِأَصْحَابِهِ
hadith.en: Recite the Quran, for it will come on the Day of Judgment as an intercessor for its companions

shades.name_en: al-Qirāʾa — The Recitation of the Quran
shades.name_ar: الْقِرَاءَةُ — جَمْعُ الْحُرُوفِ، وَالْقُرْآنُ اسْمٌ لِلْكِتَابِ الْمَقْرُوءِ
shades.explanation: The qirāʾa (recitation, reading) in the Quran is the foundational act of revelation — the first word was iqraʾ (read!). The verse 96:1 establishes the principle that the Quran is to be recited — «iqraʾ bi-smi rabbika lladhī khalaq» (read in the name of your Lord who created). The qirāʾa in the Quran has two dimensions: the act of recitation by the reciter (qāriʾ) and the act of being read (maqrūʾ). The Quran is called al-Qurʾān (the Recitation) precisely because it is read and recited. The hadith — «iqraʾū l-Qurʾāna fa-innahu yaʾtī yawma l-qiyāmati shafīʿan li-aṣḥābihi» — establishes that the recitation of the Quran is the intercession for its people on the Day of Judgment. Al-Bukhārī (Sahih) dedicated a chapter to faḍāʾil al-Qurʾān (the virtues of the Quran) — the recitation of the Quran is among the greatest acts of worship.
shades.hadith_ar: اقْرَأُوا الْقُرْآنَ فَإِنَّهُ يَأْتِي يَوْمَ الْقِيَامَةِ شَفِيعًا لِأَصْحَابِهِ
shades.hadith_en: Recite the Quran, for it will come on the Day of Judgment as an intercessor for its companions

meaning.en: To succeed, attain, escape. The root denotes the achievement of one's goal — or the escape from danger.
meaning.ar: النَّجَاةُ: السَّلَامَةُ مِنَ الْمَكْرُوهِ، وَالْفَوْزُ بِالْمَطْلُوبِ

lexical_analysis.ibn_faris: النَّجَاةُ: السَّلَامَةُ مِنَ الْهَلَكَةِ. وَالنَّاجِي: السَّالِمُ
lexical_analysis.al_raghib: النَّجَاةُ: السَّلَامَةُ مِنَ الشِّدَّةِ. وَأَصْلُهُ الْخَلَاصُ مِنَ الْمَكْرُوهِ

quran_examples.ar: وَٱعۡتَصِمُوا۟ بِحَبۡلِ ٱللَّهِ جَمِيعًۭا وَلَا تَفَرَّقُوا۟ ۚ وَٱذۡكُرُوا۟ نِعۡمَتَ ٱللَّهِ عَلَيۡكُمۡ إِذۡ كُنتُمۡ أَعۡدَآءً فَأَلَّفَ بَيۡنَ قُلُوبِكُمۡ فَأَصۡبَحۡتُم بِنِعۡمَتِهِۦٓ إِخۡوَٰنًا
quran_examples.en: And hold firmly to the rope of Allah all together and do not become divided. And remember the favor of Allah upon you — when you were enemies and He brought your hearts together and you became, by His favor, brothers
quran_examples.context: The command to hold the rope of Allah

hadith.ar: مَنْ عَمِلَ عَمَلًا لَيْسَ عَلَيْهِ أَمْرُنَا فَهُوَ رَدٌّ
hadith.en: Whoever does a deed that is not from us, it is rejected

shades.name_en: an-Najāḥ — The Success and the Salvation
shades.name_ar: النَّجَاةُ — السَّلَامَةُ مِنَ الْمَكْرُوهِ، أَفْضَلُ النَّجَاحِ نَجَاةُ الْآخِرَةِ
shades.explanation: The najāḥ (success, salvation) in the Quran is the achievement of one's goal — particularly the salvation from Hellfire. The verse 3:103 establishes the famous command to hold the ḥabl Allāh (the rope of Allah) — the collective unity that is the path to salvation. The najāḥ in the Quran is the opposite of khalāṣ (destruction). The hadith — «man ʿamila ʿamalan laysa ʿalayhi amrunā fa-huwa radḍ» — establishes that only deeds aligned with the Sunna are accepted. Al-Ghazālī (Iḥyāʾ, Book of Trust in Allah) develops the doctrine that the najāḥ is achieved through tawḥīd (affirmation of unity), tawakkul (reliance on Allah), and ʿamal ṣāliḥ (righteous deeds).
shades.hadith_ar: مَنْ عَمِلَ عَمَلًا لَيْسَ عَلَيْهِ أَمْرُنَا فَهُوَ رَدٌّ
shades.hadith_en: Whoever does a deed that is not from us, it is rejected

meaning.en: Single, alone, alone (one). The root denotes the state of being alone — particularly the oneness of Allah.
meaning.ar: الْفَرْدُ: الْوَاحِدُ الَّذِي لَيْسَ مَعَهُ غَيْرُهُ

lexical_analysis.ibn_faris: الْفَرْدُ: الْوَاحِدُ. وَالْأَفْرَادُ: جَمْعُ فَرِيدٍ
lexical_analysis.al_raghib: الْفَرْدُ: الْوَاحِدُ الَّذِي لَيْسَ مَعَهُ ثَانٍ

quran_examples.ar: وَإِنۡ خِفۡتُمۡ أَلَّا تُقۡسِطُوا۟ فِى ٱلۡيَتَـٰمَىٰ فَٱنكِحُوا۟ مَا طَابَ لَكُم مِّنَ ٱلنِّسَآءِ مَثۡنَىٰ وَثُلَـٰثَ وَرُبَـٰعَ
quran_examples.en: And if you fear that you will not deal justly with the orphans, then marry [other] women as you may, two and three and four
quran_examples.context: The permission of plural marriage with justice

hadith.ar: يَا بَنِي عَبْدِ مُنَافٍ، إِنَّكُمْ لَمْ تُبَارِكُمْ سَوْءَةً قَطُّ
hadith.en: O sons of Abd Manaf, you have never suffered evil alone

shades.name_en: al-Fard — The Single and the Unique
shades.name_ar: الْفَرْدُ — الْوَاحِدُ الَّذِي لَيْسَ مَعَهُ ثَانٍ
shades.explanation: The fard (single, alone) in the Quran is the state of being alone — and particularly the divine attribute of waḥdāniyya (oneness). The verse 4:3 mentions the odd and even numbers (mathnā wa-thulātha wa-rubāʿ) — the context of marriage but also implicitly the divine unity. The fard is closely related to tawḥīd — the affirmation of Allah's oneness. Al-Ghazālī (Jawāhir al-Qurʾān) treats the fard as the divine attribute that excludes plurality — the divine essence is fard (one) and there is no like Him. The fard in the Quran is the basis of the theological concept of tawḥīd — the oneness of Allah.
shades.hadith_ar: يَا بَنِي عَبْدِ مُنَافٍ، إِنَّكُمْ لَمْ تُبَارِكُمْ سَوْءَةً قَطُّ
shades.hadith_en: O sons of Abd Manaf, you have never suffered evil alone

meaning.en: To heal, cure. The root denotes the act of healing — and by extension, the divine mercy that brings healing to the soul and body.

lexical_analysis.ibn_faris: الشِّفَاءُ: الْبُرْءُ مِنَ الْمَرَضِ. وَشَفَيْتُهُ: أَبَرَأْتُهُ
lexical_analysis.al_raghib: الشِّفَاءُ: الْبُرْءُ مِنَ الْمَرَضِ. وَاسْتَعْمَلُوهُ مَجَازًا لِكُلِّ مَا يَزُولُ بِهِ الشَّرُّ

quran_examples.ar: يَـٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلنَّاسُ قَدۡ جَآءَتۡكُم مَّوۡعِظَةٌۭ مِّن رَّبِّكُمۡ وَشِفَآءٌۭ لِّمَا فِى ٱلصُّدُورِ وَهُدًۭى وَرَحۡمَةٌۭ لِّلۡمُؤۡمِنِينَ
quran_examples.en: O mankind, there has come to you an admonition from your Lord and a healing for what is in the breasts — a guidance and a mercy for the believers
quran_examples.context: The Quran as healing for the soul

hadith.ar: مَا أَنْزَلَ اللَّهُ دَاءً إِلَّا أَنْزَلَ لَهُ شِفَاءً
hadith.en: Allah has not sent down a disease except that He has also sent down its cure

shades.name_ar: الشِّفَاءُ — الْبُرْءُ مِنَ الْمَرَضِ، وَالْقُرْآنُ شِفَاءٌ لِلصُّدُورِ
shades.explanation: The shifāʾ (healing) in the Quran is one of the divine attributes — Allah is al-Shāfī (the Healer). The verse 10:57 establishes that the Quran itself is shifāʾ (healing) for what is in the breasts — the spiritual and psychological healing. The shifāʾ is closely related to ʿāfiya (well-being) and ʿifāʾ (cure). The hadith — «mā anzala Allāhu dāʾan illā anzala lahu shifāʾan» — establishes that Allah has not sent down any disease except that He has also sent down its cure. Al-Ghazālī (Iḥyāʾ, Book of Medicine of the Heart) treats the shifāʾ as both physical and spiritual — the physical shifāʾ is the cure of the body, while the spiritual shifāʾ is the cure of the soul. The Quran is the ultimate shifāʾ for the soul — its recitation brings the soul from the darkness of sin to the light of taqwā.
shades.hadith_ar: مَا أَنْزَلَ اللَّهُ دَاءً إِلَّا أَنْزَلَ لَهُ شِفَاءً
shades.hadith_en: Allah has not sent down a disease except that He has also sent down its cure

meaning.en: Head, chief, beginning. The root denotes the uppermost part of the body — and by extension, the chief or beginning of something.
meaning.ar: الرَّأْسُ: أَعْلَى الشَّيْءِ، أَوِ الْقَائِمُ عَلَيْهِ

lexical_analysis.ibn_faris: الرَّأْسُ: أَعْلَى الشَّيْءِ. وَالرَّئِيسُ: الْقَائِمُ بِأَمْرِ الْقَوْمِ
lexical_analysis.al_raghib: الرَّأْسُ: عُضْوٌ مَعْلُومٌ. وَقِيلَ: الرَّئِيسُ: الَّذِي يَرْأَسُ الْقَوْمَ، أَيْ يَفُوقُهُمْ

quran_examples.ar: فَمَن كَانَ مِنكُم مَّرِيضًا أَو بِهِۦٓ أَذًۭى مِّن رَّأۡسِهِۦ فَفِدۡيَةٌۭ مِّن صِيَامٍ أَوۡ صَدَقَةٍ أَوۡ نُسُكٍۢ
quran_examples.en: And whoever is ill or has an ailment of the head must pay a fidya from fasting or charity or sacrifice
quran_examples.context: The compensation for shaving the head during Hajj

hadith.ar: إِنَّ لِكُلِّ أَمَّةٍ أَمِينًا، وَأَمِينُ هَذِهِ الْأُمَّةِ أَبُو عُبَيْدَةَ بْنُ الْجَرَّاحِ
hadith.en: Every community has an amin (trustworthy), and the amin of this ummah is Abu Ubayda ibn al-Jarrah

shades.name_en: ar-Raʾs — The Head and the Chief
shades.name_ar: الرَّأْسُ — أَعْلَى الشَّيْءِ، وَالرَّئِيسُ: مَنْ يَفُوقُ الْقَوْمَ فَضْلًا
shades.explanation: The raʾs (head) in the Quran is the uppermost part of the body — and by extension, the beginning, the chief, or the leader. The verse 2:196 establishes the fiḍya (compensation) for those who shave their head during Hajj due to illness — the head is the site of ihrām's most significant action. The raʾs in the Quran is the symbolic seat of the soul's consciousness — the place where the judgment of the soul is made. The hadith — «inna li-kulli ummatin amīnan» — establishes the amīn (trustworthy chief) as essential for every community. Al-Māwardī (al-Aḥkām al-Sulṭāniyya) develops the doctrine of the raʾs al-dawla (the head of state) — the imām or caliph as the raʾs of the Islamic political community.
shades.hadith_ar: إِنَّ لِكُلِّ أَمَّةٍ أَمِينًا، وَأَمِينُ هَذِهِ الْأُمَّةِ أَبُو عُبَيْدَةَ بْنُ الْجَرَّاحِ
shades.hadith_en: Every community has an amin — and the amin of this ummah is Abu Ubayda ibn al-Jarrah

meaning.en: Empty, void, travel. The root denotes both emptiness and travel — particularly the travel of leaving a place.
meaning.ar: السَّفَرُ: الْبُرُوزُ عَنِ الْمَكَانِ، وَالسَّفَرُ: الْمَتَاعُ الْمُسْتَعْمَلُ

lexical_analysis.ibn_faris: السَّفَرُ: الْقَطْعُ. وَيُسْتَعْمَلُ لِلْمُسَافِرِ لِأَنَّهُ يَقْطَعُ الْمَسَافَةَ
lexical_analysis.al_raghib: السَّفَرُ: قَطْعُ الْمَسَافَةِ. وَالسَّفَرُ: كِتَابٌ ضَخْمٌ، أَوِ الْمَتَاعُ

quran_examples.ar: أَيَّامًۭا مَّعۡدُودَٰتٍۢ ۗ فَمَن كَانَ مِنكُم مَّرِيضًا أَوۡ عَلَىٰ سَفَرٍۢ فَعِدَّةٌۭ مِّنۡ أَيَّامٍ أُخَرَ
quran_examples.en: [A limited number of days]. So whoever among you is ill or on a journey [during them] — then an equal number of days [are to be made up]
quran_examples.context: The concession for the traveler during Ramadan

hadith.ar: سَافِرُوا تَصِحُّوا وَتُغْنَمُوا
hadith.en: Travel, and you will be healthy and gain provision

shades.name_en: as-Safar — The Journey and the Travel
shades.name_ar: السَّفَرُ — قَطْعُ الْمَسَافَةِ، وَالسَّفَرُ: الْمُسَافِرُ لِقَطْعِهِ الْمَسَافَةَ
shades.explanation: The safar (journey, travel) in the Quran is the act of traveling from one place to another — and by extension, the journey of life toward the Hereafter. The verse 2:184 establishes the concession for the traveler (musāfir) — he may break the fast of Ramadan and make up the days later. The safar is one of the conditions that allows shortening the prayer (qaṣr). The hadith — «sāfirū taṣiḥḥū wa-tughnamū» — establishes that travel is a means of both physical health and spiritual provision. Al-Ghazālī (Iḥyāʾ, Book of Travel) treats the safar as the journey of the soul toward Allah — every step taken with sincere intention is a worship.
shades.hadith_ar: سَافِرُوا تَصِحُّوا وَتُغْنَمُوا
shades.hadith_en: Travel, and you will be healthy and gain provision

meaning.en: To go out, exit, emerge. The root denotes the act of exiting from a place — and by extension, leaving a state.
meaning.ar: الْخُرُوجُ: الْإِنْفِصَالُ عَنِ الشَّيْءِ، مُتَوَجِّهًا إِلَى غَيْرِهِ

lexical_analysis.ibn_faris: الْخُرُوجُ: ضِدُّ الدُّخُولِ. وَكُلُّ مَنْ خَرَجَ مِنْ مَكَانٍ فَقَدْ خَرَجَ
lexical_analysis.al_raghib: الْخُرُوجُ: انْفِصَالُ الشَّيْءِ عَنْ غَيْرِهِ. وَفِي الشَّرْعِ: خُرُوجُ الْإِنْسَانِ مِنْ بَيْتِهِ لِلصَّلَاةِ

quran_examples.ar: يَـٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلنَّاسُ إِنَّ وَعۡدَ ٱللَّهِ حَقٌّۭ ۖ فَلَا تَغُرَّنَّكُمُ ٱلۡحَيَوٰةُ ٱلدُّنۡيَا وَلَا يَغُرَّنَّكُم بِٱللَّهِ ٱلۡغَرُورُ
quran_examples.en: O mankind, the promise of Allah is true. So let not the worldly life delude you, nor let the Deceiver delude you about Allah
quran_examples.context: The warning against the deceptions of the worldly life

hadith.ar: الْمُسْلِمُ مَنْ سَلِمَ الْمُسْلِمُونَ مِنْ لِسَانِهِ وَيَدِهِ، وَالْمُهَاجِرُ مَنْ هَجَرَ مَا نَهَى اللَّهُ عَنْهُ
hadith.en: The Muslim is the one from whose tongue and hand other Muslims are safe; and the muhajir is the one who abandons what Allah has forbidden

shades.name_en: al-Khurūj — The Exit from the World and Toward Allah
shades.name_ar: الْخُرُوجُ — ضِدُّ الدُّخُولِ، خُرُوجُ الْمُهَاجِرِ مِنَ الشِّرْكِ إِلَى الْإِسْلَامِ
shades.explanation: The khurūj (exit) in the Quran is one of the most frequent words — particularly in the context of hijra (migration) and resurrection (kharaja min al-qabr). The verse 2:20 establishes the principle that the worldly life is deceptive — the believer should not be deceived by it. The khurūj in the Quran is the exit from the worldly life (mamāt, death) and the exit from the grave (al-ba's, resurrection). The hadith — «al-muslimu man salima l-muslimūna min lisānihi wa-yadihi» — establishes that the muhājir is the one who abandons what Allah has forbidden. Al-Ghazālī (Iḥyāʾ) develops the doctrine that the khurūj in this world is the preparation for the khurūj in the next — every step taken in obedience is a step closer to the resurrection.
shades.hadith_ar: الْمُسْلِمُ مَنْ سَلِمَ الْمُسْلِمُونَ مِنْ لِسَانِهِ وَيَدِهِ، وَالْمُهَاجِرُ مَنْ هَجَرَ مَا نَهَى اللَّهُ عَنْهُ
shades.hadith_en: The Muslim is the one from whose tongue and hand other Muslims are safe; and the muhajir is the one who abandons what Allah has forbidden

meaning.en: To be good, be righteous, be fit. The root denotes goodness, righteousness, and the state of being sound.

lexical_analysis.ibn_faris: الصَّلَاحُ: ضِدُّ الْفَسَادِ. وَصَلَحَ الشَّيْءُ: حَسُنَ
lexical_analysis.al_raghib: الصَّلَاحُ: اسْتِقَامَةُ الْحَالِ. وَيُقَالُ: صَلَحَ لِكَذَا: أَيْ لَاقَ

quran_examples.ar: وَإِذَا قِيلَ لَهُمۡ لَا تُفۡسِدُوا۟ فِى ٱلۡأَرۡضِ قَالُوٓاْ إِنَّمَا نَحۡنُ مُصۡلِحُونَ
quran_examples.en: And when it is said to them: Do not cause corruption on the earth, they say: We are but reformers
quran_examples.context: The hypocrites claiming to be reformers

hadith.ar: الْمُسْلِمُ مَنْ سَلِمَ الْمُسْلِمُونَ مِنْ لِسَانِهِ وَيَدِهِ، وَالْمُهَاجِرُ مَنْ هَجَرَ مَا نَهَى اللَّهُ عَنْهُ
hadith.en: The Muslim is the one from whose tongue and hand other Muslims are safe; and the muhajir is the one who abandons what Allah has forbidden

shades.name_en: aṣ-Ṣalāḥ — The Righteousness as the State of Soundness
shades.name_ar: الصَّلَاحُ — اسْتِقَامَةُ الْحَالِ، أَصْلُ الْإِصْلَاحِ فِي الْإِسْلَامِ
shades.explanation: The ṣalāḥ (righteousness) in the Quran is the state of being sound and good — the opposite of fasād (corruption). The verse 2:11 establishes the principle that the hypocrites falsely claim to be muṣliḥūn (reformers) when they are actually mufsidūn (corrupters). The ṣalāḥ in the Quran is closely related to ṣāliḥ (righteous) and iṣlāḥ (reformation). The hadith — «al-muslimu man salima l-muslimūna» — establishes that the Muslim is the one who makes others safe from his tongue and hand. Al-Ghazālī (Iḥyāʾ, Book of Etiquette) treats the ṣalāḥ as the comprehensive state of the soul — when the soul is in ṣalāḥ, all its faculties are in harmony.
shades.hadith_ar: الْمُسْلِمُ مَنْ سَلِمَ الْمُسْلِمُونَ مِنْ لِسَانِهِ وَيَدِهِ، وَالْمُهَاجِرُ مَنْ هَجَرَ مَا نَهَى اللَّهُ عَنْهُ
shades.hadith_en: The Muslim is the one from whose tongue and hand other Muslims are safe; and the muhajir is the one who abandons what Allah has forbidden

meaning.en: To raise, elevate, lift up. The root denotes the act of raising — and by extension, the elevation in rank or status.
meaning.ar: الرَّفْعُ: ضِدُّ الْوَضْعِ، تَصْعِيدُ الشَّيْءِ إِلَى فَوْقُ

lexical_analysis.ibn_faris: الرَّفْعُ: ضِدُّ الْوَضْعِ. وَكُلُّ تَصْعِيدٍ رَفْعٌ
lexical_analysis.al_raghib: الرَّفْعُ: ضِدُّ الْوَضْعِ. وَقِيلَ: الرَّفْعُ فِي الشَّرَفِ أَعَمُّ مِنَ الْعُلُوِّ فِي الْمَكَانِ

quran_examples.ar: وَعَلَّمَ ءَادَمَ ٱلۡأَسۡمَآءَ كُلَّهَا ثُمَّ عَرَضَهُمۡ عَلَى ٱلۡمَلَـٰٓئِكَةِ فَقَالَ أَنۢبِـُٔونِى بِأَسۡمَآءِ هَـٰٓؤُلَآءِ إِن كُنتُمۡ صَـٰدِقِينَ
quran_examples.en: And He taught Adam the names — all of them — and then presented them to the angels and said: Inform Me of the names of these, if you are truthful
quran_examples.context: The teaching of the names to Adam and his elevation

hadith.ar: إِنَّ اللَّهَ رَفِيعُ الدَّرَجَاتِ
hadith.en: Indeed Allah is the Owner of High Ranks

shades.name_en: ar-Rafʿ — The Elevation and the Raising
shades.name_ar: الرَّفْعُ — تَصْعِيدُ الشَّيْءِ إِلَى فَوْقُ، رَفْعُ الْمَكَانِ وَالرُّتْبَةِ
shades.explanation: The rafʿ (raising, elevation) in the Quran is the act of raising — and by extension, the elevation in rank. The verse 2:31 establishes that Adam was taught the names and elevated above the angels. The rafʿ in the Quran has several dimensions: the physical rafʿ (raising of the heavens), the spiritual rafʿ (elevation of the soul through good deeds), and the social rafʿ (elevation of the community of Islam). The hadith — «inna Allāha rafīqu l-darajāt» — establishes that Allah is the owner of high ranks. Al-Ghazālī (Jawāhir al-Qurʾān) treats the rafʿ as the divine act of lifting the soul from the darkness of sin to the light of taqwā.
shades.hadith_ar: إِنَّ اللَّهَ رَفِيعُ الدَّرَجَاتِ
shades.hadith_en: Indeed Allah is the Owner of High Ranks

meaning.en: To be clear, to manifest, to come out. The root denotes the act of becoming clear or manifest — and the ascension of stars.
meaning.ar: الْبُرُوجُ: الظُّهُورُ، وَالْبُرُوجُ: الْمَنَازِلُ الْعَالِيَةُ مِنَ السَّمَاءِ

lexical_analysis.ibn_faris: الْبُرُوجُ: طُلُوعُ الْكَوَاكِبِ. وَيُسْتَعْمَلُ لِكُلِّ ظَاهِرٍ مُشْرِقٍ
lexical_analysis.al_raghib: الْبُرُوجُ: الْقُصُورُ الْعَالِيَةُ. وَبُرُوجُ السَّمَاءِ: نُجُومُهَا الْعَالِيَةُ

quran_examples.ar: أَيۡنَمَا تَكُونُوا۟ يُدۡرِككُمُ ٱلۡمَوۡتُ وَلَوۡ كُنتُمۡ فِى بُرُوجٍۢ مُشَيَّدَةٍۢ
quran_examples.en: Wherever you may be, death will overtake you, even if you should be within towers of great height

hadith.ar: كَانَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ إِذَا أَوَى إِلَى فِرَاشِهِ نَامَ عَلَى شِقِّهِ الْأَيْمَنِ
hadith.en: When the Messenger of Allah went to bed, he slept on his right side

shades.name_en: al-Burūj — The Constellations and the Towers
shades.name_ar: الْبُرُوجُ — الْكَوَاكِبُ الثَّابِتَةُ فِي مَسَارِهَا، أَوِ الْقُصُورُ الْعَالِيَةُ
shades.explanation: The burūj (constellations, towers) in the Quran refers to the fixed constellations of the stars — the zodiac signs and the major stellar formations. The verse 4:78 uses the burūj metaphorically for high towers — to emphasize that no place is safe from death. The burūj in the Quran is one of the signs (āyāt) of Allah in the heavens — the verse 85:1 — «wa-l-samāʾi dhāti l-burūj» (by the sky with its constellations) — establishes the burūj as a divine creation. Al-Ghazālī (Jawāhir al-Qurʾān) treats the burūj as a sign of divine wisdom — the precise positioning of stars in the heavens reflects the divine knowledge that orders the cosmos.
shades.hadith_ar: كَانَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ إِذَا أَوَى إِلَى فِرَاشِهِ نَامَ عَلَى شِقِّهِ الْأَيْمَنِ
shades.hadith_en: When the Messenger of Allah went to bed, he slept on his right side

meaning.en: To swear, take an oath. The root denotes the act of swearing — particularly the taking of a solemn oath by Allah.
meaning.ar: الْقَسَمُ: الْحَلِفُ، وَإِقْسَامُ اللَّهِ عَلَى الشَّيْءِ: إِخْبَارٌ عَنْ عَظَمَتِهِ

lexical_analysis.ibn_faris: الْقَسَمُ: الْحَلِفُ. وَكُلُّ مَنْ حَلَفَ فَقَدْ أَقْسَمَ
lexical_analysis.al_raghib: الْقَسَمُ: التَّحَدُّثُ بِالْحَلِفِ عَلَى الشَّيْءِ. وَهُوَ مِنَ اللَّهِ تَعَالَى: الْإِخْبَارُ عَلَى وَجْهِ التَّعْظِيمِ لِلشَّيْءِ

quran_examples.ar: لَآ أُقۡسِمُ بِيَوۡمِ ٱلۡقِيَـٰمَةِ
quran_examples.en: I swear by the Day of Resurrection
quran_examples.context: The divine oath by the Day of Resurrection

hadith.ar: مَنْ حَلَفَ فَقَالَ: لَا وَالَّذِي نَفْسِي بِيَدِهِ، أَوْ بَلَى، فَقَدْ أَوْجَبَ
hadith.en: Whoever swears and says: No, by Him in whose hand is my soul — or yes — has incurred

shades.name_ar: الْقَسَمُ — التَّحَدُّثُ بِالْحَلِفِ، وَإِقْسَامُ اللَّهِ تَعْظِيمٌ لِلْمَقْسَمِ بِهِ
shades.explanation: The qasam (oath) in the Quran is the solemn declaration by which Allah swears by His creation to emphasize the truth of what He says. The verse 75:1 — «lā uqsimu bi-yawmi l-qiyāma» — establishes the principle that the divine oath is for emphasis, not because the oath is necessary. The qasam in the Quran is divided into two types: the qasam bi-llāh (oath by Allah, which is forbidden to creation) and the qasam bi-makhlūq (oath by created things, which Allah does for emphasis). The hadith — «man halafa fa-qāla: lā wa-lladhī nafsī bi-yadihi» — establishes the rulings on human oaths. Al-Ghazālī (Jawāhir al-Qurʾān) treats the qasam in the Quran as a sign of the importance of what is being sworn — the things by which Allah swears (the Day of Judgment, the soul, the night, etc.) are all essential to the divine wisdom.
shades.hadith_ar: مَنْ حَلَفَ فَقَالَ: لَا وَالَّذِي نَفْسِي بِيَدِهِ، أَوْ بَلَى، فَقَدْ أَوْجَبَ
shades.hadith_en: Whoever swears and says: No, by Him in whose hand is my soul — has incurred

meaning.en: To give to drink, water. The root denotes the act of providing drink — particularly water for the thirsty.

lexical_analysis.ibn_faris: السَّقْيُ: شُرْبُ الْمَاءِ. وَسَقَيْتُهُ: أَنَالْتُهُ الْمَاءَ
lexical_analysis.al_raghib: السَّقْيُ: إِنَالَةُ الْمَاءِ. وَأَسْقَيْتُهُ: إِذَا جَعَلْتَ لَهُ سَقْيًا

quran_examples.ar: وَإِذِ ٱسۡتَسۡقَىٰ مُوسَىٰ لِقَوۡمِهِۦ فَقُلۡنَا ٱضۡرِب بِّعَصَاكَ ٱلۡحَجَرَ ۖ فَٱنفَجَرَتۡ مِنۡهُ ٱثۡنَتَا عَشَرَةَ عَيۡنًا
quran_examples.en: And when Moses asked for water for his people, We said: Strike with your staff the stone. And there gushed forth from it twelve springs
quran_examples.context: The miracle of the twelve springs for the Children of Israel

hadith.ar: أَيُّمَا رَجُلٍ مِنْ أُمَّتِي أَطْعَمَ مُسْلِمًا شَيْئًا حَتَّى يُدْخِلَهُ فِي جَوْفِهِ، كَانَ لَهُ بَرَاءَةٌ مِنَ النَّارِ
hadith.en: Whoever from my ummah feeds a Muslim until he is full — he will have immunity from the Fire

shades.name_ar: السَّقْيُ — إِنَالَةُ الْمَاءِ، وَسَقْيُ الْكَرِيمِ فِي الْآخِرَةِ أَفْضَلُ الْأَعْمَالِ
shades.explanation: The saqy (giving to drink) in the Quran is one of the most fundamental acts of charity — particularly in the desert context. The verse 2:60 establishes the miracle of the twelve springs — when Moses struck the rock for his people. The saqy in the Quran is both physical (giving water to the thirsty) and spiritual (quenching the thirst of the soul with the water of tawḥīd). The hadith — «ayyumu rajulin min ummatī aṭʿama musliman» — establishes that feeding and giving drink to a Muslim is among the most beloved deeds. Al-Ghazālī (Iḥyāʾ, Book of Charitable Acts) treats the saqy as one of the most enduring forms of charity — the saqiyya (water-drawer) and the birka (water-well) are among the most beloved endowments (waqf) in Islamic civilization.
shades.hadith_ar: أَيُّمَا رَجُلٍ مِنْ أُمَّتِي أَطْعَمَ مُسْلِمًا شَيْئًا حَتَّى يُدْخِلَهُ فِي جَوْفِهِ، كَانَ لَهُ بَرَاءَةٌ مِنَ النَّارِ
shades.hadith_en: Whoever from my ummah feeds a Muslim until he is full — he will have immunity from the Fire

meaning.en: To try, test, experience. The root denotes the act of testing or experiencing — particularly the test of hardship.
meaning.ar: التَّجْرِبَةُ: الِاخْتِبَارُ، وَالْإِيقَاعُ فِي الْأَشْيَاءِ لِمَعْرِفَةِ حَقِيقَتِهَا

lexical_analysis.ibn_faris: التَّجْرِبَةُ: مُبَاشَرَةُ الشَّيْءِ. وَيُسْتَعْمَلُ لِلِاخْتِبَارِ
lexical_analysis.al_raghib: التَّجْرِبَةُ: الِاخْتِبَارُ. وَكُلُّ مَنْ عَرَّضَ شَيْئًا لِلْآخَرِ حَتَّى يَتَبَيَّنَ حَالُهُ فَقَدْ جَرَّبَهُ

quran_examples.ar: أَمۡ حَسِبۡتُمۡ أَن تُتۡرَكُوا۟ وَلَمَّا يَعۡلَمِ ٱللَّهُ ٱلَّذِينَ جَـٰهَدُوا۟ مِنكُمۡ وَلَمۡ يَتَّخِذُوا۟ مِن دُونِ ٱللَّهِ وَلَا رَسُولِهِۦ وَلَا ٱلۡمُؤۡمِنِينَ وَلِيجَةًۭ ۚ وَٱللَّهُ خَبِيرٌۢ بِمَا تَعۡمَلُونَ
quran_examples.en: Or have you thought that you would be left [as you are] while Allah has not yet made evident those who strive among you and have not taken besides Allah, His Messenger, and the believers as intimates?

hadith.ar: لَا يَزَالُ الْبَلَاءُ بِالْمُؤْمِنِ وَالْمُؤْمِنَةِ حَتَّى يَلْقَى اللَّهَ وَمَا عَلَيْهِ خَطِيئَةٌ
hadith.en: The trial continues to befall the believer and the believerah until they meet Allah without any sin

shades.name_en: at-Tajruba — The Testing and the Experience
shades.name_ar: التَّجْرِبَةُ — الِاخْتِبَارُ، كُلُّ مُسْلِمٍ يُجَرَّبُ بِالْمَصَائِبِ لِيَتَزَكَّى
shades.explanation: The tajruba (testing, experience) in the Quran is the act of putting something to the test — particularly the believer being tested through hardship. The verse 9:16 establishes that Allah will test the believers — the test is the means of distinguishing the sincere from the insincere. The tajruba in the Quran is one of the foundational principles of Islamic theology — the life of this world is a test (al-dunya mātaḥ). The hadith — «lā yazālu l-balāʾu bi-l-muʾmini» — establishes that trials continue for the believer until they meet Allah sinless. Al-Ghazālī (Iḥyāʾ, Book of Patience) treats the tajruba as the divine pedagogy — the believer is like a sword that needs to be sharpened by hardship.
shades.hadith_ar: لَا يَزَالُ الْبَلَاءُ بِالْمُؤْمِنِ وَالْمُؤْمِنَةِ حَتَّى يَلْقَى اللَّهَ وَمَا عَلَيْهِ خَطِيئَةٌ
shades.hadith_en: The trial continues to befall the believer until they meet Allah without any sin

meaning.en: To restrain, refrain, withhold. The root denotes the act of restraining — and by extension, the act of protection.
meaning.ar: الْكَفُّ: ضِدُّ الْبَسْطِ، حَبْسُ الشَّيْءِ وَإِمْسَاكُهُ

lexical_analysis.ibn_faris: الْكَفُّ: ضِدُّ الْبَسْطِ. وَكَفَّ الشَّيْءَ: حَبَسَهُ
lexical_analysis.al_raghib: الْكَفُّ: إِمْسَاكُ الشَّيْءِ. وَيُسْتَعْمَلُ مَجَازًا لِمَنْ حَبَسَ نَفْسَهُ عَنِ الشَّيْءِ

quran_examples.ar: أُحِلَّ لَكُمۡ لَيۡلَةَ ٱلصِّيَامِ ٱلرَّفَثُ إِلَىٰ نِسَآئِكُمۡ هُنَّ لِبَاسٌۭ لَّكُمۡ وَأَنتُمۡ لِبَاسٌۭ لَّهُنَّ ۗ عَلِمَ ٱللَّهُ أَنَّكُمۡ كُنتُمۡ تَخۡتَانُونَ أَنفُسَكُمۡ فَتَابَ عَلَيۡكُمۡ وَعَفَا عَنكُمۡ ۖ فَٱلۡـَٔنَ بَـٰشِرُوهُنَّ وَٱبۡتَغُوا۟ مَا كَتَبَ ٱللَّهُ لَكُمۡ
quran_examples.en: It has been made permissible for you, during the nights of fasting, to have intimacy with your wives. They are a covering for you and you are a covering for them. Allah knew that you used to betray yourselves, so He accepted your repentance and forgave you. So now, have relations with them and seek that which Allah has decreed for you
quran_examples.context: The permission for intimacy during the nights of Ramadan

hadith.ar: مَنْ رَأَى مِنْكُمْ مُنْكَرًا فَلْيُغَيِّرْهُ بِيَدِهِ، فَإِنْ لَمْ يَسْتَطِعْ فَبِلِسَانِهِ، فَإِنْ لَمْ يَسْتَطِعْ فَبِقَلْبِهِ
hadith.en: Whoever among you sees an evil, let him change it with his hand; if he cannot, then with his tongue; if he cannot, then with his heart

shades.name_en: al-Kaff — The Restraint and the Protection
shades.name_ar: الْكَفُّ — ضِدُّ الْبَسْطِ، كَفُّ الْأَذَى وَكَفُّ النَّفْسِ عَنِ الشَّهْوَةِ
shades.explanation: The kaff (restraint, protection) in the Quran is one of the most frequent ethical concepts — the act of restraining oneself from evil. The verse 2:187 establishes the permission for intimacy during the nights of Ramadan — a balance between worship and the legitimate needs of life. The kaff in the Quran has several dimensions: kaff al-aḍā (restraint from harm), kaff al-nafs (restraint of the self from desire), and kaff al-yad (restraint of the hand). The hadith — «man raʾā munkaran fa-l-yughayyir-hu» — establishes the obligation of changing evil according to one's capacity — first with the hand, then with the tongue, then with the heart. Al-Ghazālī (Iḥyāʾ, Book of Patience) treats the kaff as the foundation of taqwā — the one who can restrain the self has the foundation of all virtue.
shades.hadith_ar: مَنْ رَأَى مِنْكُمْ مُنْكَرًا فَلْيُغَيِّرْهُ بِيَدِهِ، فَإِنْ لَمْ يَسْتَطِعْ فَبِلِسَانِهِ، فَإِنْ لَمْ يَسْتَطِعْ فَبِقَلْبِهِ
shades.hadith_en: Whoever among you sees an evil, let him change it with his hand; if he cannot, then with his tongue; if he cannot, then with his heart

meaning.en: Eye, spring, source. The root denotes both the organ of sight and the spring of water — and by extension, the watchful observation.
meaning.ar: الْعَيْنُ: حَاسَّةُ الْبَصَرِ، أَوْ مَنْبَعُ الْمَاءِ

lexical_analysis.ibn_faris: الْعَيْنُ: حَاسَّةُ الرُّؤْيَةِ. وَيُسْتَعْمَلُ لِمَنْبَعِ الْمَاءِ
lexical_analysis.al_raghib: الْعَيْنُ: حَاسَّةُ الْبَصَرِ. وَيُسْتَعْمَلُ لِلْمَنْبَعِ مِنَ الْمَاءِ أَيْضًا. وَالْعَيْنُ: الرَّقِيبُ عَلَى الشَّيْءِ

quran_examples.ar: وَكَتَبۡنَا عَلَيۡهِمۡ فِيهَآ أَنَّ ٱلنَّفۡسَ بِٱلنَّفۡسِ وَٱلۡعَيۡنَ بِٱلۡعَيۡنِ وَٱلۡأَنفَ بِٱلۡأَنفِ وَٱلۡأُذُنَ بِٱلۡأُذُنِ وَٱلسِّنَّ بِٱلسِّنِّ
quran_examples.en: And We ordained for them therein: a life for a life, an eye for an eye, a nose for a nose, an ear for an ear, a tooth for a tooth

hadith.ar: الْحَيَاءُ مِنَ الْإِيمَانِ، وَالْإِيمَانُ فِي الْجَنَّةِ، وَالْبَذَاءُ مِنَ الْجَفَاءِ، وَالْجَفَاءُ فِي النَّارِ
hadith.en: Modesty is from faith, and faith is in Paradise; obscenity is from coarseness, and coarseness is in the Fire

shades.name_en: al-ʿAyn — The Eye and the Spring
shades.name_ar: الْعَيْنُ — حَاسَّةُ الْبَصَرِ، وَالْعَيْنُ: الرَّقِيبُ، وَعَيْنُ الْمَاءِ: مَنْبَعُهُ
shades.explanation: The ʿayn (eye, spring) in the Quran has two distinct uses: the organ of sight (chāsira al-baṣar) and the spring of water (manbaʿ al-mā'). The verse 5:45 establishes the principle of qiṣāṣ (retribution) — al-ʿayn bi-l-ʿayn (an eye for an eye) — the Torah's law of equal retaliation. The ʿayn in the Quran is closely related to al-baṣar (sight) and al-ruʾyā (vision). The hadith — «al-ḥayāʾu mina l-īmān» — establishes that modesty is from faith. Al-Ghazālī (Iḥyāʾ, Book of Etiquette) treats the ʿayn as the gate through which most sins enter the soul — the one who guards the ʿayn has guarded the heart.
shades.hadith_ar: الْحَيَاءُ مِنَ الْإِيمَانِ، وَالْإِيمَانُ فِي الْجَنَّةِ، وَالْبَذَاءُ مِنَ الْجَفَاءِ، وَالْجَفَاءُ فِي النَّارِ
shades.hadith_en: Modesty is from faith, and faith is in Paradise; obscenity is from coarseness, and coarseness is in the Fire

meaning.en: To force, compel, tyrannize. The root denotes the act of forcing or compelling — and by extension, the tyranny of one over another.

lexical_analysis.ibn_faris: الْجَبْرُ: الْقَهْرُ. وَالْجَبَّارُ: الَّذِي يَجْبُرُ خَلْقَهُ عَلَى مَا يُرِيدُ
lexical_analysis.al_raghib: الْجَبْرُ: إِجْبَارُ الْإِنْسَانِ عَلَى الشَّيْءِ قَهْرًا. وَالْجَبَّارُ: الَّذِي يَجْبُرُ النَّاسَ عَلَى أَمْرِهِ

quran_examples.ar: وَإِذۡ قَالَ مُوسَىٰ لِقَوۡمِهِۦ يَـٰقَوۡمِ إِنَّكُمۡ ظَلَمۡتُمۡ أَنفُسَكُم بِٱتِّخَاذِكُمُ ٱلۡعِجۡلَ فَتُوبُوٓاْ إِلَىٰ بَارِئِكُمۡ فَٱقۡتُلُوٓاْ أَنفُسَكُمۡ
quran_examples.en: And when Moses said to his people: O my people, you have wronged yourselves by taking the calf [for worship]. So repent to your Creator and kill yourselves
quran_examples.context: Moses' call to repentance after the worship of the calf

hadith.ar: مَا نَقَصَتْ صَدَقَةٌ مِنْ مَالٍ
hadith.en: Charity does not decrease wealth

shades.name_en: al-Jabr — The Force and the Compulsion
shades.name_ar: الْجَبْرُ — الْقَهْرُ عَلَى الشَّيْءِ، جَبْرُ الْقَلْبِ وَجَبْرُ الْكَسْرِ
shades.explanation: The jabr (compulsion, force) in the Quran is the act of forcing or compelling — used both for divine jabar (compelling creation) and human jabar (tyranny). The verse 2:54 establishes that the soul that worships the calf has wronged itself — and must return to Allah. The jabr in the Quran is the opposite of ikhtiyār (free choice). The jabr is closely related to jabr al-kalb (healing the heart) and jabr al-kawn (restoring the cosmos). The hadith — «mā naqaṣat ṣadaqatun min mālin» — establishes that charity does not decrease wealth, contrary to the human belief that giving means losing. Al-Ghazālī (Iḥyāʾ, Book of Reliance on Allah) treats the jabr as the divine attribute — Allah is al-Jabbār, the Compeller, who orders creation as He wills.
shades.hadith_ar: مَا نَقَصَتْ صَدَقَةٌ مِنْ مَالٍ
shades.hadith_en: Charity does not decrease wealth

meaning.en: Severity, might, force. The root denotes the severity of combat — and by extension, the might of Allah.
meaning.ar: الْبَأْسُ: الشِّدَّةُ، أَوِ الْحَرْبُ، أَوِ الْجِدُّ فِي الْأَمْرِ

lexical_analysis.ibn_faris: الْبَأْسُ: الشِّدَّةُ فِي الْحَرْبِ. وَيُسْتَعْمَلُ لِكُلِّ شِدَّةٍ
lexical_analysis.al_raghib: الْبَأْسُ: الشِّدَّةُ فِي الْحَرْبِ. وَقِيلَ: هُوَ مُبَالَغَةُ الْبُؤْسِ، أَوِ الشِّدَّةِ فِي الْجِهَادِ

quran_examples.ar: لَّيۡسَ ٱلۡبِرَّ أَن تُوَلُّوا۟ وُجُوهَكُمۡ قِبَلَ ٱلۡمَشۡرِقِ وَٱلۡمَغۡرِبِ وَلَـٰكِنَّ ٱلۡبِرَّ مَنۡ ءَامَنَ بِٱللَّهِ وَٱلۡيَوۡمِ ٱلۡـَٔاخِرِ وَٱلۡمَلَـٰٓئِكَةِ وَٱلۡكِتَـٰبِ وَٱلنَّبِيِّـۧنَ وَءَاتَى ٱلۡمَالَ عَلَىٰ حُبِّهِۦ ذَوِى ٱلۡقُرۡبَىٰ وَٱلۡيَتَـٰمَىٰ وَٱلۡمَسَـٰكِينَ وَٱبۡنَ ٱلسَّبِيلِ وَٱلسَّآئِلِينَ وَفِى ٱلرِّقَابِ وَأَقَامَ ٱلصَّلَوٰةَ وَءَاتَى ٱلزَّكَوٰةَ وَٱلۡمُوفُونَ بِعَهۡدِهِمۡ إِذَا عَـٰهَدُوا۟ وَٱلصَّـٰبِرِينَ فِى ٱلۡبَأۡسَآءِ وَٱلضَّرَّآءِ وَحِينَ ٱلۡبَأۡسِ
quran_examples.en: Righteousness is not that you turn your faces toward the east or the west, but [true] righteousness is [in] one who believes in Allah, the Last Day, the angels, the Book, and the prophets, and gives wealth in spite of love for it to relatives, orphans, the needy, the traveler, those who ask [for help], and for freeing captives; and who establishes prayer and gives zakāh; and [those who] fulfill their promise when they promise; and [those who] are patient in poverty and hardship and during battle

hadith.ar: مَنْ قَاتَلَ دُونَ مَالِهِ فَقُتِلَ فَهُوَ شَهِيدٌ
hadith.en: Whoever fights for his wealth and is killed — he is a martyr

shades.name_en: al-Baʾs — The Severity and the Strength in Battle
shades.name_ar: الْبَأْسُ — الشِّدَّةُ فِي الْحَرْبِ، أَوِ الْجِدُّ فِي الْأَمْرِ
shades.explanation: The baʾs (severity, might) in the Quran is the severity of combat — and by extension, the divine might. The verse 2:177 establishes the principle that true righteousness is not merely outward — it includes being patient in baʾsāʾ (hardship) and ḍarrāʾ (poverty) and ḥīn al-baʾs (the time of battle). The baʾs in the Quran is the force that the believer must mobilize in the face of trials. The hadith — «man qātala dūna mālihi fa-huwa shahīd» — establishes that fighting for one's wealth is a path to martyrdom. Al-Māwardī (al-Aḥkām al-Sulṭāniyya) develops the doctrine that the imām is the commander of the baʾs — the leader who organizes the jihād of the community.
shades.hadith_ar: مَنْ قَاتَلَ دُونَ مَالِهِ فَقُتِلَ فَهُوَ شَهِيدٌ
shades.hadith_en: Whoever fights for his wealth and is killed — he is a martyr

meaning.en: To commit immorality, to flow, to sin openly. The root denotes the act of committing major sins — and by extension, the flow of water.
meaning.ar: الْفُجُورُ: ضِدُّ الْبِرِّ، الْخُرُوجُ عَنِ الْحَقِّ، أَوِ انْفِجَارُ الْمَاءِ

lexical_analysis.ibn_faris: الْفُجُورُ: ضِدُّ الْبِرِّ. وَفَجَرَ الْمَاءَ: فَتَحَهُ. وَفَجَّرَهُ: أَكْثَرَ انْفِجَارَهُ
lexical_analysis.al_raghib: الْفُجُورُ: الْمَيْلُ عَنِ الْحَقِّ. وَيُسْتَعْمَلُ لِانْفِجَارِ الْمَاءِ

quran_examples.ar: وَلَا تَسۡتَوۡى ٱلۡحَسَنَةُ وَلَا ٱلسَّيِّئَةُ ۚ ٱدۡفَعۡ بِٱلَّتِى هِىَ أَحۡسَنُ فَإِذَا ٱلَّذِى بَيۡنَكَ وَبَيۡنَهُۥ عَدَـٰوَةٌۭ كَأَنَّهُۥ وَلِىٌّ حَمِيمٌۭ
quran_examples.en: And not equal are the good deed and the bad. Repel [evil] by that [deed] which is better; and thereupon the one whom between you and him is enmity [will become] as though he was a devoted friend
quran_examples.context: The principle of repelling evil with good

hadith.ar: مَا أَصَابَكَ لَمْ يَكُنْ لِيُخْطِئَكَ، وَمَا أَخْطَأَكَ لَمْ يَكُنْ لِيُصِيبَكَ
