hadith.en: What befalls you was not meant to miss you, and what misses you was not meant to befall you

shades.name_en: al-Fujūr — The Open Sin and the Flowing of Water
shades.name_ar: الْفُجُورُ — الْمَيْلُ عَنِ الْحَقِّ، أَوِ انْفِجَارُ الْمَاءِ مِنَ الْأَرْضِ
shades.explanation: The fujūr (immorality, open sin) in the Quran is the state of being openly sinful — the opposite of taqwā. The verse 4:19 establishes the principle that the good deed and the bad are not equal — the believer must repel evil with good. The fujūr in the Quran is the explicit declaration of sin — fujūr vs. taqwā (verse 91:7-8 — «wa-nafsī wa-mā sawwāhā, fa-alḥamāhā fujūrahā wa-taqwāhā» — by the soul and what shaped it, and inspired it with its immorality and its taqwā). The hadith — «mā aṣābaka lam yakun li-yukhṭiʾaka» — establishes divine wisdom in what befalls the believer. Al-Ghazālī (Iḥyāʾ, Book of Disciplining the Soul) treats the fujūr as one of the states of the soul that the believer must overcome — through tazkiya (purification), the soul rises from fujūr to taqwā.
shades.hadith_ar: مَا أَصَابَكَ لَمْ يَكُنْ لِيُخْطِئَكَ، وَمَا أَخْطَأَكَ لَمْ يَكُنْ لِيُصِيبَكَ
shades.hadith_en: What befalls you was not meant to miss you, and what misses you was not meant to befall you

meaning.en: To reason, understand, use the intellect. The root denotes the use of the intellect — and by extension, the faculty of reason.
meaning.ar: الْعَقْلُ: حَبْسُ النَّفْسِ عَنِ الْهَلَكِ، أَوِ إِدْرَاكُ الْأَشْيَاءِ عَلَى حَقَائِقِهَا

lexical_analysis.ibn_faris: الْعَقْلُ: حِفْظُ الْقَلْبِ الشَّيْءَ. وَعَقَلْتُ الشَّيْءَ: إِذَا عَلِمْتَهُ
lexical_analysis.al_raghib: الْعَقْلُ: الْقُوَّةُ الْمُدْرِكَةُ لِحَقَائِقِ الْأَشْيَاءِ. وَقِيلَ: حِبْسُ النَّفْسِ عَنِ الْهَلَكِ

quran_examples.ar: أَفَتَطۡمَعُونَ أَن يُؤۡمِنُوا۟ لَكُمۡ وَقَدۡ كَانَ فَرِيقٌۭ مِّنۡهُمۡ يَسۡمَعُونَ كَلَـٰمَ ٱللَّهِ ثُمَّ يُحَرِّفُونَهُۥ مِنۢ بَعۡدِ مَا عَقَلُوهُ وَهُمۡ يَعۡلَمُونَ
quran_examples.en: Do you covet [the hope] that they would believe for you while a party of them used to hear the word of Allah and then distort it after they had understood it while they were knowing?
quran_examples.context: The condemnation of the People of the Book who distorted revelation

hadith.ar: إِنَّمَا الْأَعْمَالُ بِالنِّيَّاتِ، وَإِنَّمَا لِكُلِّ امْرِئٍ مَا نَوَى
hadith.en: Indeed actions are by intentions, and every person shall have what he intended

shades.name_en: al-ʿAql — The Intellect as the Divine Light
shades.name_ar: الْعَقْلُ — الْقُوَّةُ الْمُدْرِكَةُ لِحَقَائِقِ الْأَشْيَاءِ، أَفْضَلُ نِعَمِ اللَّهِ عَلَى الْإِنْسَانِ
shades.explanation: The ʿaql (intellect, reason) in the Quran is one of the most divine gifts to humanity — the faculty that distinguishes humans from animals. The verse 2:75 establishes the principle that the People of the Book distorted the revelation after they had ʿaqalū-hu (understood it) — the ʿaql is the precondition of understanding. The ʿaql in the Quran is closely related to al-fahm (comprehension) and al-dhikr (remembrance). The hadith — «innamā l-aʿmālu bi-l-niyyāt» — establishes that actions are by intentions — the ʿaql is what discerns the intentions. Al-Ghazālī (Miʿyār al-ʿIlm, Jawāhir al-Qurʾān) treats the ʿaql as the noor (light) of the heart — the faculty by which the soul recognizes Allah.
shades.hadith_ar: إِنَّمَا الْأَعْمَالُ بِالنِّيَّاتِ
shades.hadith_en: Indeed actions are by intentions

meaning.en: To despair, lose hope. The root denotes the state of hopelessness — the loss of expectation of good.

lexical_analysis.ibn_faris: الْيَأْسُ: الْقُنُوطُ. وَكُلُّ قَنَطَ فَقَدْ يَئِسَ
lexical_analysis.al_raghib: الْيَأْسُ: انْقِطَاعُ الرَّجَاءِ عَنِ الشَّيْءِ. وَالْقُنُوطُ: الْيَأْسُ مَعَ تَقَصِيرٍ

quran_examples.ar: وَلَوۡ أَنَّآ كَتَبۡنَا عَلَيۡهِمۡ أَنِ ٱقۡتُلُوٓاْ أَنفُسَكُمۡ أَوِ ٱخۡرُجُواْ مِن دِيَـٰرِكُمۡ مَّا فَعَلُوهُ إِلَّا قَلِيلٌۭ مِّنۡهُمۡ ۖ وَلَوۡ أَنَّهُمۡ فَعَلُوا۟ مَا يُوعَظُونَ بِهِۦ لَكَانَ خَيۡرًۭا لَّهُمۡ وَأَشَدَّ تَثۡبِيتًا
quran_examples.en: And if We had decreed upon them: Kill yourselves or leave your homes, they would not have done it, except for a few of them. And if they had done what they were instructed with, it would have been better for them and a firmer position
quran_examples.context: The conditional compliance of the People of the Book

hadith.ar: لَا يَمُوتَنَّ أَحَدُكُمْ إِلَّا وَهُوَ يُحْسِنُ الظَّنَّ بِاللَّهِ
hadith.en: Let none of you die except with a good opinion of Allah

shades.name_en: al-Yaʾs — The Despair and Its Prohibition
shades.name_ar: الْيَأْسُ — انْقِطَاعُ الرَّجَاءِ، وَهُوَ مِنَ الذُّنُوبِ الْكَبِيرَةِ
shades.explanation: The yaʾs (despair, hopelessness) in the Quran is the state of losing hope — and one of the major sins. The verse 2:64 establishes that even the most difficult divine commands would be hard for the People of the Book — except for the few. The yaʾs in the Quran is closely related to al-qunūṭ (despair with inadequacy) — both are condemned in Islamic theology. The hadith — «lā yamūtanna aḥadukum illā wa-huwa yuḥsinu l-ẓanna bi-Allāh» — establishes that the believer must always have good opinion of Allah, never despairing of His mercy. Al-Ghazālī (Iḥyāʾ, Book of Hope and Fear) treats the yaʾs as a grave spiritual disease — it leads to abandonment of worship and surrender to despair. The cure for yaʾs is the dhikr of Allah — the remembrance of His mercy and power.
shades.hadith_ar: لَا يَمُوتَنَّ أَحَدُكُمْ إِلَّا وَهُوَ يُحْسِنُ الظَّنَّ بِاللَّهِ
shades.hadith_en: Let none of you die except with a good opinion of Allah

meaning.en: Cause, reason, means. The root denotes the means or cause by which something is achieved.

lexical_analysis.ibn_faris: السَّبَبُ: الْحَبْلُ. وَكُلُّ طَرِيقٍ يُتَوَصَّلُ بِهِ إِلَى الشَّيْءِ فَهُوَ سَبَبٌ
lexical_analysis.al_raghib: السَّبَبُ: الْوَصْلَةُ إِلَى الشَّيْءِ. وَقِيلَ: السَّبَبُ: الْحَبْلُ الَّذِي يُرْتَقَى بِهِ إِلَى الشَّيْءِ

quran_examples.ar: وَإِذَا رَءَاكَ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُوٓاْ إِن يَتَّخِذُونَكَ إِلَّا هُزُوًا أَهَـٰذَا ٱلَّذِى يَذۡكُرُ ءَالِهَتَكُمۡ وَهُم بِذِكۡرِ ٱلرَّحۡمَـٰنِ هُمۡ كَـٰفِرُونَ
quran_examples.en: And when those who disbelieve see you, they take you not except in ridicule: Is this the one who mentions your gods? And they are, at the mention of the Most Merciful, disbelievers
quran_examples.context: The mockery of the Prophet by the disbelievers

hadith.ar: الْحَلَالُ بَيِّنٌ وَالْحَرَامُ بَيِّنٌ وَبَيْنَهُمَا مُشْتَبِهَاتٌ لَا يَعْلَمُهُنَّ كَثِيرٌ مِنَ النَّاسِ
hadith.en: The lawful is clear and the unlawful is clear, and between them are doubtful things which many people do not know

shades.name_en: as-Sabab — The Cause and the Means
shades.name_ar: السَّبَبُ — الْوَصْلَةُ إِلَى الشَّيْءِ، وَسَبَبُ الْخَيْرِ: طَرِيقُهُ
shades.explanation: The sabab (cause, means) in the Quran is the means or path by which one achieves a goal. The verse 2:166 establishes the principle that the disbelievers ridicule the Prophet — but the sabab of divine victory will come. The sabab in the Quran is closely related to al-ʿilla (cause) and al-wasila (means). The hadith — «al-ḥalālu bayyinun wa-l-ḥarāmu bayyinun» — establishes that there are doubtful matters between the lawful and unlawful — these are the ambiguous asbāb (means) that require careful judgment. Al-Ghazālī (Miʿyār al-ʿIlm) treats the sabab as a fundamental principle of legal reasoning — the asbāb are the premises that lead to the hukm.
shades.hadith_ar: الْحَلَالُ بَيِّنٌ وَالْحَرَامُ بَيِّنٌ وَبَيْنَهُمَا مُشْتَبِهَاتٌ لَا يَعْلَمُهُنَّ كَثِيرٌ مِنَ النَّاسِ
shades.hadith_en: The lawful is clear and the unlawful is clear, and between them are doubtful things which many people do not know

meaning.en: To be content, satisfied. The root denotes the state of contentment with what one has — and by extension, the satisfaction of need.

lexical_analysis.ibn_faris: الْقُنُوعُ: الرِّضَا بِالْحَالِ. وَكُلُّ مَنْ رَضِيَ بِمَا لَهُ فَهُوَ قَنِعٌ
lexical_analysis.al_raghib: الْقَنَاعَةُ: الرِّضَا بِالْبُلُوغِ مِنْ غَيْرِ زِيَادَةٍ. وَهِيَ مِنَ الْأَخْلَاقِ الْحَمِيدَةِ

quran_examples.ar: وَإِذۡ قَالَ إِبۡرَٰهِـ۰مُ رَبِّ ٱجۡعَلۡ هَـٰذَا بَلَدًا ءَامِنًا وَٱرۡزُقۡ أَهۡلَهُۥ مِنَ ٱلثَّمَرَٰتِ مَنۡ ءَامَنَ مِنۡهُم بِٱللَّهِ وَٱلۡيَوۡمِ ٱلۡـَٔاخِرِ
quran_examples.en: And when Abraham said: My Lord, make this a secure city and provide its people with fruits — whoever of them believes in Allah and the Last Day
quran_examples.context: Abraham's prayer for the inhabitants of Mecca

hadith.ar: لَيْسَ الْغِنَى عَنْ كَثْرَةِ الْعَرَضِ، وَلَكِنَّ الْغِنَى غِنَى النَّفْسِ
hadith.en: Richness is not in having many possessions, but richness is the richness of the soul

shades.name_en: al-Qanāʿa — The Contentment of the Soul
shades.name_ar: الْقَنَاعَةُ — الرِّضَا بِالْبُلُوغِ مِنْ غَيْرِ زِيَادَةٍ، وَهِيَ خُلُقُ الْأَقْطَابِ
shades.explanation: The qanāʿa (contentment) in the Quran is the state of being satisfied with what one has — a virtue of the soul. The verse 2:126 establishes Abraham's prayer for the people of Mecca — he asks for both security and sustenance, showing that the believer seeks from Allah but is also content. The qanāʿa in the Quran is closely related to al-ʿafāf (chastity) and al-zuhd (asceticism). The hadith — «laysa l-ghinā ʿan kathrat al-ʿaraḍ» — establishes that true richness is the richness of the soul, not of possessions. Al-Ghazālī (Iḥyāʾ, Book of Disciplining the Soul) treats the qanāʿa as one of the stations of the wayfarers to Allah — the one who is content with what Allah has given is free from the chains of greed.
shades.hadith_ar: لَيْسَ الْغِنَى عَنْ كَثْرَةِ الْعَرَضِ، وَلَكِنَّ الْغِنَى غِنَى النَّفْسِ
shades.hadith_en: Richness is not in having many possessions, but richness is the richness of the soul

meaning.en: To divide, distribute, swear. The root denotes the act of dividing or distributing — and by extension, the act of swearing an oath.

lexical_analysis.ibn_faris: الْقَسْمُ: التَّقْسِيمُ. وَقَسَمْتُ الشَّيْءَ: فَرَّقْتُهُ
lexical_analysis.al_raghib: الْقَسْمُ: التَّقْسِيمُ. وَالْقَسَمُ: الْحَلِفُ. وَقِيلَ: الْقَسَمُ: الْحَظُّ

quran_examples.ar: وَإِذَا حَضَرَ ٱلۡقِسۡمَةَ أُو۟لُوا۟ ٱلۡقُرۡبَىٰ وَٱلۡيَتَـٰمَىٰ وَٱلۡمَسَـٰكِينُ فَٱرۡزُقُوهُم مِّنۡهُ وَقُولُوا۟ لَهُمۡ قَوۡلًا مَّعۡرُوفًا
quran_examples.en: And when [other] relatives and orphans and the needy are present at the [time of] division, then provide for them [something] out of it and speak to them words of appropriate kindness

hadith.ar: إِنَّ اللَّهَ قَسَمَ بَيْنَكُمْ أَخْلَاقَكُمْ
hadith.en: Indeed Allah has divided your dispositions among you

shades.name_en: al-Qasm — The Division and the Oath
shades.explanation: The qasm (division, oath) in the Quran is the act of dividing or swearing. The verse 4:8 establishes the principle that relatives and orphans should be given from the inheritance before it is distributed — even though they are not legal heirs. The qasm in the Quran is both the legal division of property and the divine oath (when Allah swears by His creation). The hadith — «inna Allāha qasama baynakum akhlāqakum» — establishes that Allah has divided the dispositions of people among them. Al-Ghazālī (Iḥyāʾ) treats the qasm as a divine attribute — Allah is the One who distributes sustenance, rizq, and provisions according to His wisdom.
shades.hadith_ar: إِنَّ اللَّهَ قَسَمَ بَيْنَكُمْ أَخْلَاقَكُمْ
shades.hadith_en: Indeed Allah has divided your dispositions among you

meaning.en: Horn, century, generation. The root denotes both the horn of an animal and a generation or century of people.
meaning.ar: الْقَرْنُ: حَافِرُ الْحَيَوَانِ، أَوِ الطَّائِفَةُ مِنَ النَّاسِ يَقْتَرِنُونَ فِي زَمَانٍ

lexical_analysis.ibn_faris: الْقَرْنُ: حَافِرُ الْحَيَوَانِ. وَاسْتُعْمِلَ لِطَائِفَةٍ مِنَ النَّاسِ يَقْتَرِنُونَ فِي زَمَانٍ
lexical_analysis.al_raghib: الْقَرْنُ: مَا يُسَمَّى بِهِ حَافِرُ الْحَيَوَانِ. وَقِيلَ: الْقَرْنُ مِنَ النَّاسِ: أَقْرَانُهُمْ فِي الزَّمَانِ

quran_examples.ar: وَعَلَّمَ ءَادَمَ ٱلۡأَسۡمَآءَ كُلَّهَا ثُمَّ عَرَضَهُمۡ عَلَى ٱلۡمَلَـٰٓئِكَةِ فَقَالَ أَنۢبِـُٔونِى بِأَسۡمَآءِ هَـٰٓؤُلَآءِ إِن كُنتُمۡ صَـٰدِقِينَ
quran_examples.en: And He taught Adam the names — all of them — and then presented them to the angels and said: Inform Me of the names of these, if you are truthful
quran_examples.context: The teaching of the names to Adam

hadith.ar: خَيْرُ النَّاسِ قَرْنِي، ثُمَّ الَّذِينَ يَلُونَهُمْ، ثُمَّ الَّذِينَ يَلُونَهُمْ
hadith.en: The best of people is my generation, then those who follow them, then those who follow them

shades.name_en: al-Qarn — The Generation and the Era
shades.name_ar: الْقَرْنُ — مَنْ يَقْتَرِنُ فِي الزَّمَانِ، وَالْقَرْنُ أَيْضًا: الْحَافِرُ
shades.explanation: The qarn (horn, generation) in the Quran is both a physical horn and a generation of people. The verse 2:31 establishes the teaching of the names to Adam — the beginning of human generations. The qarn in the Quran is closely related to al-jīl (generation) and al-ʿaṣr (era). The hadith — «khayru l-nāsi qarnī» — establishes that the best generation is the generation of the Prophet, then those who follow them. The hadith of the Prophet — that each generation is followed by one worse than it — establishes the principle of declining generations. Al-Ghazālī (Iḥyāʾ, Book of Etiquette) treats the qarn as a temporal container — the people of each era share particular characteristics that distinguish them from other eras.
shades.hadith_ar: خَيْرُ النَّاسِ قَرْنِي، ثُمَّ الَّذِينَ يَلُونَهُمْ، ثُمَّ الَّذِينَ يَلُونَهُمْ
shades.hadith_en: The best of people is my generation, then those who follow them

meaning.en: Far away, wilderness. The root denotes a place that is far from civilization — and by extension, the open desert.

lexical_analysis.ibn_faris: الْبَدَدُ: الْبُعْدُ. وَالْبَدَدُ: الْمَكَانُ الْبَعِيدُ
lexical_analysis.al_raghib: الْبَدَدُ: الْبُعْدُ. وَيُسْتَعْمَلُ لِلْمَوْضِعِ الْبَعِيدِ مِنَ الْعُمْرَانِ

quran_examples.ar: قَالَ فَإِنَّهَا مُحَرَّمَةٌ عَلَيۡهِمۡ أَرۡبَعِينَ سَنَةًۭ يَتِيهُونَ فِى ٱلۡأَرۡضِ ۚ فَلَا تَأۡسَ عَلَى ٱلۡقَوۡمِ ٱلۡفَـٰسِقِينَ
quran_examples.en: He said: Then it [the land] is forbidden to them for forty years — they will wander throughout the land. So do not grieve over the defiantly disobedient people
quran_examples.context: The wandering of the Children of Israel in the desert

hadith.ar: إِنَّ اللَّهَ يُحِبُّ الْعَبْدَ التَّقِيَّ الْغَنِيَّ الْخَفِيَّ
hadith.en: Indeed Allah loves the servant who is pious, self-sufficient, and obscure

shades.name_en: al-Badad — The Wilderness and the Distance
shades.name_ar: الْبَدَدُ — الْبُعْدُ مِنَ الْعُمْرَانِ، أَوِ الْمَكَانُ الْبَعِيدُ
shades.explanation: The badd (wilderness, distance) in the Quran is the open desert — the place far from civilization. The verse 5:26 establishes that the Children of Israel would wander in the desert for forty years — the divine punishment for rejecting the Holy Land. The badd in the Quran is closely related to al-ṣaḥrāʾ (desert) and al-qif (wilderness). The hadith — «inna Allāha yuḥibbu l-ʿabda l-taqiyya l-ghaniyya l-khafiyya» — establishes that Allah loves the self-sufficient servant who does not beg from others. Al-Ghazālī (Iḥyāʾ, Book of Zuhd) treats the badd as the place of the truthful seekers — those who flee from the fitna of civilization to seek Allah's face.
shades.hadith_ar: إِنَّ اللَّهَ يُحِبُّ الْعَبْدَ التَّقِيَّ الْغَنِيَّ الْخَفِيَّ
shades.hadith_en: Indeed Allah loves the servant who is pious, self-sufficient, and obscure

meaning.en: To make pilgrimage, to intend. The root denotes the act of pilgrimage to the Sacred House — and by extension, the intention to do something.
meaning.ar: الْحَجُّ: الْقَصْدُ إِلَى مَكَانٍ مُعَظَّمٍ، أَوْ إِلَى عَمَلٍ مَخْصُوصٍ

lexical_analysis.ibn_faris: الْحَجُّ: الْقَصْدُ. وَيُسْتَعْمَلُ لِقَصْدِ الْبَيْتِ
lexical_analysis.al_raghib: الْحَجُّ: الْقَصْدُ إِلَى مَكَانٍ شَرِيفٍ أَوْ عَمَلٍ مَخْصُوصٍ. وَفِي الْعُرْفِ: الْإِتْيَانُ إِلَى الْبَيْتِ الْحَرَامِ

quran_examples.ar: رَبَّنَا وَٱجۡعَلۡنَا مُسۡلِمَيۡنِ لَكَ وَمِن ذُرِّيَّتِنَآ أُمَّةًۭ مُّسۡلِمَةًۭ لَّكَ وَأَرِنَا مَنَاسِكَنَا وَتُبۡ عَلَيۡنَآ ۖ إِنَّكَ أَنتَ ٱلتَّوَّابُ ٱلرَّحِيمُ
quran_examples.en: Our Lord, and make us Muslims [in submission] to You and from our descendants a Muslim nation [in submission] to You. And show us our rites and accept our repentance. Indeed, You are the Accepting of Repentance, the Merciful
quran_examples.context: Abraham's prayer for the rituals of Hajj

hadith.ar: مَنْ حَجَّ فَلَمْ يَرْفُثْ وَلَمْ يَفْسُقْ رَجَعَ كَيَوْمِ وَلَدَتْهُ أُمُّهُ
hadith.en: Whoever performs Hajj and does not commit obscenity or sin will return as on the day his mother bore him

shades.name_en: al-Ḥajj — The Pilgrimage and the Intention
shades.name_ar: الْحَجُّ — الْقَصْدُ إِلَى بَيْتِ اللَّهِ الْحَرَامِ، خَامِسُ أَرْكَانِ الْإِسْلَامِ
shades.explanation: The ḥajj (pilgrimage) in the Quran is the fifth pillar of Islam — the act of pilgrimage to the Sacred House in Mecca. The verse 2:128 establishes Abraham's prayer for the rites of Hajj — the foundation of the hajj ritual. The ḥajj in the Quran is closely related to al-ʿumra (lesser pilgrimage) and al-ziyāra (visitation). The hadith — «man ḥajja fa-lam yarfuth wa-lam yafsuq» — establishes that whoever performs Hajj without obscenity or sin returns as on the day his mother bore him. Al-Māwardī (al-Aḥkām al-Sulṭāniyya) treats the ḥajj as one of the most important acts of Islam — the imām must facilitate the Hajj for those who are able. Al-Ghazālī (Iḥyāʾ, Book of Pilgrimage) treats the ḥajj as the inner pilgrimage of the soul — the outward journey to Mecca symbolizes the inner journey of the soul to Allah.
shades.hadith_ar: مَنْ حَجَّ فَلَمْ يَرْفُثْ وَلَمْ يَفْسُقْ رَجَعَ كَيَوْمِ وَلَدَتْهُ أُمُّهُ
shades.hadith_en: Whoever performs Hajj and does not commit obscenity or sin will return as on the day his mother bore him

meaning.en: To protect, preserve, guard. The root denotes the act of protecting or guarding — particularly the divine preservation of revelation.
meaning.ar: الْحِفْظُ: ضِدُّ النِّسْيَانِ، رِعَايَةُ الشَّيْءِ مِنَ الضَّيَاعِ

lexical_analysis.ibn_faris: الْحِفْظُ: ضِدُّ النِّسْيَانِ. وَكُلُّ مَا حَفِظْتَهُ فَقَدْ رَعَيْتَهُ
lexical_analysis.al_raghib: الْحِفْظُ: رِعَايَةُ الشَّيْءِ مِمَّا يُفْسِدُهُ. وَفِي الشَّرْعِ: حِفْظُ اللَّهِ الْقُرْآنَ مِنَ التَّحْرِيفِ

quran_examples.ar: وَكَذَٰلِكَ جَعَلۡنَـٰكُمۡ أُمَّةًۭ وَسَطًۭا لِّتَكُونُوا۟ شُهَدَآءَ عَلَى ٱلنَّاسِ وَيَكُونَ ٱلرَّسُولُ عَلَيۡكُمۡ شَهِيدًۭا
quran_examples.en: And so We have made you a middle community, that you may be witnesses over the people and the messenger may be a witness over you

hadith.ar: احْفَظِ اللَّهَ يَحْفَظْكَ، احْفَظِ اللَّهَ تَجِدْهُ أَمَامَكَ
hadith.en: Preserve Allah — He will preserve you. Preserve Allah — you will find Him before you

shades.name_ar: الْحِفْظُ — رِعَايَةُ الشَّيْءِ، حِفْظُ اللَّهِ لِعِبَادِهِ وَحِفْظُ الْقُرْآنِ
shades.explanation: The ḥifẓ (preservation, protection) in the Quran is one of the divine attributes — Allah is al-Ḥāfiẓ (the Preserver). The verse 2:143 establishes the principle of the ummah — the middle community that Allah preserves for the testimony. The ḥifẓ in the Quran is applied both to divine preservation of creation and to human preservation of divine commands. The hadith — «iḥfaẓ Allāh yaḥfaẓak» — establishes that the one who preserves Allah's commands will be preserved by Allah. Al-Ghazālī (Miʿyār al-ʿIlm, Jawāhir al-Qurʾān) treats the ḥifẓ as the foundation of ʿilm — the preservation of knowledge is the preservation of the religion.
shades.hadith_ar: احْفَظِ اللَّهَ يَحْفَظْكَ
shades.hadith_en: Preserve Allah — He will preserve you

meaning.en: To corrupt, be evil. The root denotes the act of corruption — whether moral, religious, or social.
meaning.ar: الْفَسَادُ: الْخُرُوجُ عَنِ الِاعْتِدَالِ، أَوْ ضِدُّ الصَّلَاحِ

lexical_analysis.ibn_faris: الْفَسَادُ: خِلَافُ الصَّلَاحِ. وَيُسْتَعْمَلُ فِي الْأَشْيَاءِ الْمُخْتَلِفَةِ
lexical_analysis.al_raghib: الْفَسَادُ: خُرُوجُ الشَّيْءِ عَنِ الِاسْتِقَامَةِ. وَأَصْلُهُ: الْفَسَادُ فِي الثَّمَرَةِ، ثُمَّ اسْتُعْمِلَ فِي الْأَخْلَاقِ

quran_examples.ar: وَإِذَا قِيلَ لَهُمۡ لَا تُفۡسِدُوا۟ فِى ٱلۡأَرۡضِ قَالُوٓاْ إِنَّمَا نَحۡنُ مُصۡلِحُونَ
quran_examples.en: And when it is said to them: Do not cause corruption on the earth, they say: We are but reformers

hadith.ar: صِنْفَانِ مِنْ أُمَّتِي لَيْسَ لَهُمَا نَصِيبٌ فِي الْإِسْلَامِ: الْمُرْجِئَةُ وَالْقَدَرِيَّةُ
hadith.en: Two groups from my ummah have no share in Islam: the Murji'ah and the Qadariyyah

shades.name_en: al-Fasād — The Corruption of the Earth
shades.name_ar: الْفَسَادُ — خُرُوجُ الشَّيْءِ عَنِ الِاسْتِقَامَةِ، وَالْإِفْسَادُ فِي الْأَرْضِ أَعْظَمُ الذُّنُوبِ
shades.explanation: The fasād (corruption) in the Quran is the state of disorder and evil — the opposite of ṣalāḥ. The verse 2:11 establishes that the hypocrites falsely claim to be reformers while they are corrupters. The ifsād (corruption-making) in the earth is one of the greatest sins in Islam — it is the spread of evil and the destruction of order. The hadith — «al-fasādu fī al-arḍ» (corruption in the earth) is mentioned in the Quran as the action of those who disbelieve and reject the divine commands. Al-Ghazālī (Iḥyāʾ, Book of Enjoining Good and Forbidding Evil) treats the ifsād as the greatest sin against the community — the one who spreads corruption destroys the foundations of human society.
shades.hadith_ar: صِنْفَانِ مِنْ أُمَّتِي لَيْسَ لَهُمَا نَصِيبٌ فِي الْإِسْلَامِ: الْمُرْجِئَةُ وَالْقَدَرِيَّةُ
shades.hadith_en: Two groups from my ummah have no share in Islam: the Murji'ah and the Qadariyyah

meaning.en: To be forbearing, clement. The root denotes the quality of clemency — the restraint of anger and the giving of time.
meaning.ar: الْحِلْمُ: ضِبْطُ النَّفْسِ عَنِ الْغَضَبِ، وَالْإِمْهَالُ فِي الْعُقُوبَةِ

lexical_analysis.ibn_faris: الْحِلْمُ: ضِبْطُ النَّفْسِ عَنِ الْغَضَبِ. وَالْحَلِيمُ: الَّذِي لَا يَسْتَعْجِلُ الْعُقُوبَةَ
lexical_analysis.al_raghib: الْحِلْمُ: ضِبْطُ النَّفْسِ عَنِ اسْتِفْزَازِ الْغَضَبِ. وَهُوَ مِنَ الصِّفَاتِ الْحَمِيدَةِ

quran_examples.ar: وَلَا تُعۡرِمُوا۟ عُقۡدَةَ ٱلنِّكَاحِ حَتَّىٰ يَبۡلُغَ ٱلۡكِتَـٰبُ أَجَلَهُۥ ۚ وَٱعۡلَمُوٓاْ أَنَّ ٱللَّهَ يَعۡلَمُ مَا فِىٓ أَنفُسِكُمۡ فَٱحۡذَرُوهُ ۚ وَٱعۡلَمُوٓاْ أَنَّ ٱللَّهَ غَفُورٌ حَلِيمٌۭ
quran_examples.en: And do not determine to contract a marriage until the [waiting] period has reached its end. And know that Allah knows what is within yourselves, so beware of Him. And know that Allah is Forgiving and Forbearing
quran_examples.context: The waiting period and Allah's forbearance

hadith.ar: إِنَّ اللَّهَ عَزَّ وَجَلَّ حَلِيمٌ يُحِبُّ الْحِلْمَ
hadith.en: Indeed Allah is Forbearing and loves forbearance

shades.name_ar: الْحِلْمُ — ضِبْطُ النَّفْسِ عَنِ اسْتِفْزَازِ الْغَضَبِ، خُلُقٌ رَفِيعٌ مِنْ أَخْلَاقِ اللَّهِ
shades.explanation: The ḥilm (forbearance, clemency) in the Quran is one of the divine attributes — Allah is al-Ḥalīm (the Forbearing). The verse 2:235 establishes the principle of patience in marriage and the warning of Allah's knowledge of the self — the ḥilm is closely tied to forgiveness (ghufrān). The ḥilm in the Quran is closely related to al-ṣabr (patience) and al-mālāh (giving time). The hadith — «inna Allāha ʿazza wa-jalla ḥalīmun yuḥibbu l-ḥilm» — establishes that Allah is forbearing and loves forbearance. Al-Ghazālī (Iḥyāʾ, Book of Patience) treats the ḥilm as one of the most noble virtues — the one who is forbearing has conquered the lower self.
shades.hadith_ar: إِنَّ اللَّهَ عَزَّ وَجَلَّ حَلِيمٌ يُحِبُّ الْحِلْمَ
shades.hadith_en: Indeed Allah is Forbearing and loves forbearance

meaning.en: To be kind, gentle, compassionate. The root denotes the quality of gentleness — particularly the gentle treatment of others.

lexical_analysis.ibn_faris: الرِّفْقُ: ضِدُّ الْعُنْفِ. وَالرَّفِيقُ: الْمُرَافِقُ عَلَى الرِّفْقِ
lexical_analysis.al_raghib: الرِّفْقُ: لِينُ الْجَانِبِ وَتَرْكُ الْإِيجَاعِ. وَهُوَ مِنْ أَخْلَاقِ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ

quran_examples.ar: وَإِذۡ أَخَذۡنَا مِيثَـٰقَ بَنِىٓ إِسۡرَٰٓءِيلَ لَا تَعۡبُدُونَ إِلَّا ٱللَّهَ وَبِٱلۡوَٰلِدَيۡنِ إِحۡسَانًا وَذِى ٱلۡقُرۡبَىٰ وَٱلۡيَتَـٰمَىٰ وَٱلۡمَسَـٰكِينِ وَقُولُوا۟ لِلنَّاسِ حُسۡنًۭا وَأَقِيمُوا۟ ٱلصَّلَوٰةَ وَءَاتُوا۟ ٱلزَّكَوٰةَ ثُمَّ تَوَلَّيۡتُمۡ إِلَّا قَلِيلًۭا مِّنكُمۡ وَأَنتُمۡ مُعۡرِضُونَ
quran_examples.en: And [recall] when We took the covenant from the Children of Israel: You shall not worship except Allah, and to parents do good, and to relatives, orphans, and the needy. And speak to people good [words] and establish prayer and give zakāh. Then you turned away, except a few of you, and you were refusing
quran_examples.context: The covenant of the Children of Israel

hadith.ar: إِنَّ الرِّفْقَ لَا يَكُونُ فِي شَيْءٍ إِلَّا زَانَهُ، وَلَا يُنْزَعُ مِنْ شَيْءٍ إِلَّا شَانَهُ
hadith.en: Indeed gentleness does not enter anything except that it adorns it, and it is not removed from anything except that it disgraces it

shades.name_en: ar-Rifq — The Gentleness in All Affairs
shades.name_ar: الرِّفْقُ — لِينُ الْجَانِبِ، الرِّفْقُ لَا يَكُونُ فِي شَيْءٍ إِلَّا زَانَهُ
shades.explanation: The rifq (gentleness) in the Quran is one of the virtues that the believer must cultivate — the opposite of ʿunf (violence). The verse 2:83 establishes the principle of speaking good words to people — the rifq in speech is one of the marks of the believers. The rifq in the Quran is closely related to al-ḥilm (forbearance) and al-līn (softness). The hadith — «inna l-rifqa lā yakūnu fī shayʾin illā zānahu» — establishes that gentleness adorns everything. Al-Ghazālī (Iḥyāʾ, Book of Etiquette) treats the rifq as the foundation of all social relations — the one who is gentle with others has the closest character to the Prophet.
shades.hadith_ar: إِنَّ الرِّفْقَ لَا يَكُونُ فِي شَيْءٍ إِلَّا زَانَهُ
shades.hadith_en: Indeed gentleness does not enter anything except that it adorns it

meaning.en: To stand, stop, attend. The root denotes the act of standing — particularly the standing before Allah in prayer and judgment.
meaning.ar: الْوُقُوفُ: الْقِيَامُ فِي مَكَانٍ، أَوْ الْوُقُوفُ لِلتَّعَلُّمِ

lexical_analysis.ibn_faris: الْوُقُوفُ: الْقِيَامُ. وَأَوْقَفْتُ الشَّيْءَ: جَعَلْتُهُ وَاقِفًا
lexical_analysis.al_raghib: الْوُقُوفُ: الْقِيَامُ فِي الْمَكَانِ. وَقَدْ يُسْتَعْمَلُ لِلْوُقُوفِ عَلَى الْحَقِّ لِلتَّعَرُّفِ

quran_examples.ar: وَأَنَّ هَـٰذَا صِرَٰطِى مُسۡتَقِيمًۭا فَٱتَّبِعُوهُ ۖ وَلَا تَتَّبِعُوا۟ ٱلسُّبُلَ فَتَفَرَّقَ بِكُمۡ عَن سَبِيلِهِۦ ۚ ذَٰلِكُمۡ وَصَّىٰكُم بِهِۦ لَعَلَّكُمۡ تَتَّقُونَ
quran_examples.en: And that this is My path, which is straight, so follow it; and do not follow [other] ways, for there will separate you from His way. This He has instructed you that you may become righteous

hadith.ar: صَلُّوا كَمَا رَأَيْتُمُونِي أُصَلِّي
hadith.en: Pray as you have seen me pray

shades.name_ar: الْوُقُوفُ — الْقِيَامُ، خَاصَّةً الْوُقُوفُ فِي الصَّلَاةِ وَالْوُقُوفُ بِعَرَفَاتٍ
shades.explanation: The wuqūf (standing, attending) in the Quran is the act of standing before Allah — particularly in the prayer and on the Day of Judgment. The verse 2:144 establishes the principle of the straight path — the believer must follow it and not deviate. The wuqūf in the Quran is also the standing at ʿArafāt during Hajj. The hadith — «ṣallū kamā raʾaytumūnī uṣallī» — establishes that the prayer is performed by following the Prophet's example. Al-Ghazālī (Iḥyāʾ, Book of Prayer) treats the wuqūf in prayer as the most fundamental standing — the believer stands before Allah and recites the divine words.
shades.hadith_ar: صَلُّوا كَمَا رَأَيْتُمُونِي أُصَلِّي
shades.hadith_en: Pray as you have seen me pray

meaning.en: To be time, due, ready. The root denotes the state of time being due or ready — and by extension, the moment when something must happen.
meaning.ar: الْحِينُ: الْوَقْتُ، أَوِ الْوَقْتُ الَّذِي حَانَ فِيهِ الشَّيْءُ

lexical_analysis.ibn_faris: الْحِينُ: الْوَقْتُ مِنَ الدَّهْرِ. وَقِيلَ: كُلُّ وَقْتٍ يُسَمَّى حِينًا
lexical_analysis.al_raghib: الْحِينُ: الْوَقْتُ الطَّوِيلُ. وَقِيلَ: الزَّمَانُ الَّذِي يَحِلُّ فِيهِ الْأَمْرُ

quran_examples.ar: ثُمَّ أَنزَلَ عَلَيۡكُم مِّنۢ بَعۡدِ ٱلۡغَمِّ أَمَنَةًۭ نُّعَاسًۭا يَغۡشَىٰ طَآئِفَةًۭ مِّنكُمۡ ۖ وَطَآئِفَةٌ قَدۡ أَهَمَّتۡهُمۡ أَنفُسُهُمۡ يَظُنُّونَ بِٱللَّهِ غَيۡرَ ٱلۡحَقِّ ظَنَّ ٱلۡجَـٰهِلِيَّةِ ۖ يَقُولُونَ هَل لَّنَا مِنَ ٱلۡأَمۡرِ مِن شَىۡءٍۢ ۚ قُلۡ إِنَّ ٱلۡأَمۡرَ كُلَّهُۥ لِلَّهِ
quran_examples.en: Then after distress, He sent down upon you security [in the form of] drowsiness, overcoming some of you, while others were disturbed by their own souls, thinking wrongly of Allah — the thought of ignorance. They say: Is there anything we have a share in this affair? Say: Indeed the affair belongs entirely to Allah
quran_examples.context: The Battle of Uhud and the doubt of some

hadith.ar: كَانَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ إِذَا صَلَّى رَفَعَ يَدَيْهِ حَذْوَ مَنْكِبَيْهِ
hadith.en: When the Messenger of Allah prayed, he would raise his hands level with his shoulders

shades.name_en: al-Ḥīn — The Time and the Moment
shades.name_ar: الْحِينُ — الزَّمَانُ الَّذِي يَحِلُّ فِيهِ الْأَمْرُ، أَوِ الْوَقْتُ الْمُقَدَّرُ
shades.explanation: The ḥīn (time, moment) in the Quran is the appointed time for something to happen. The verse 3:154 establishes the principle that all matters belong to Allah — the ḥīn of distress is followed by the ḥīn of relief. The ḥīn in the Quran is closely related to al-āna (now) and al-waqt (time). The hadith — «kāna rasūl Allāhi iḍā ṣallā rafʿa yadayhi ḥadhwa mankabayhi» — establishes the practice of the Prophet in prayer. Al-Ghazālī (Jawāhir al-Qurʾān) treats the ḥīn as a divine appointment — every moment is ordained by Allah for something specific to happen.
shades.hadith_ar: كَانَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ إِذَا صَلَّى رَفَعَ يَدَيْهِ حَذْوَ مَنْكِبَيْهِ
shades.hadith_en: When the Messenger of Allah prayed, he would raise his hands level with his shoulders

meaning.en: To prevent, forbid, withhold. The root denotes the act of preventing — particularly the divine prevention or human withholding of help.
meaning.ar: الْمَنْعُ: ضِدُّ الْإِعْطَاءِ، حَبْسُ الشَّيْءِ عَمَّنْ يَسْتَحِقُّهُ

lexical_analysis.ibn_faris: الْمَنْعُ: ضِدُّ الْإِعْطَاءِ. وَمَنَعْتُ الشَّيْءَ: حَبَسْتُهُ
lexical_analysis.al_raghib: الْمَنْعُ: ضِدُّ الْبَذْلِ. وَكُلُّ مَنْ حَبَسَ شَيْئًا عَنْ غَيْرِهِ فَقَدْ مَنَعَهُ

quran_examples.ar: وَلَقَدۡ جَآءَكُمۡ مُوسَىٰ مِن قَبۡلُ وَأَنتُمۡ تَظۡلِمُونَ فَلَقَدۡ كَانُوا۟ مِّنكُمۡ حِزۡبًۭا يُسَـٰرِعُونَ فِى ٱلۡكُفۡرِ وَيُسۡعَوۡنَ فِى ٱلۡخَرَابِ
quran_examples.en: And Moses had certainly come to you before with clear evidences, but you had taken the calf in his absence and you had been wrongdoers. So We took your covenant and raised over you the Mount, [saying]: Take what We have given you with determination and listen. They said: We hear and disobey
quran_examples.context: The covenant of the Children of Israel and their breaking it

hadith.ar: مَنْ يَهْدِهِ اللَّهُ فَهُوَ الْمُهْتَدِ وَمَنْ يُضْلِلْ فَلَنْ تَجِدَ لَهُ وَلِيًّا مُّرْشِدًا
hadith.en: Whoever Allah guides — he is the guided one, and whoever He leads astray — you will never find for him any protecting friend to lead [him] to right guidance

shades.name_en: al-Manʿ — The Prevention and the Withholding
shades.name_ar: الْمَنْعُ — حَبْسُ الشَّيْءِ عَنْ غَيْرِهِ، مَنْعُ الشَّيْطَانِ لِلْخَيْرِ
shades.explanation: The manʿ (prevention, withholding) in the Quran is the act of withholding something — whether divine or human. The verse 2:89 establishes the principle that the People of the Book had Moses come to them with clear signs — yet they took the calf and were wrongdoers. The manʿ in the Quran is closely related to al-bukhl (stinginess) and al-iʿrāḍ (turning away). The hadith — «man yahdihi Allāhu fa-huwa l-muhtadī» — establishes that divine guidance is the ultimate determinant. Al-Ghazālī (Iḥyāʾ, Book of Etiquette) treats the manʿ as a vice of the soul — the one who withholds help from others is trapped in the vice of stinginess, while the generous believer gives without stint.
shades.hadith_ar: مَنْ يَهْدِهِ اللَّهُ فَهُوَ الْمُهْتَدِ
shades.hadith_en: Whoever Allah guides — he is the guided one

meaning.en: To argue, dispute, debate. The root denotes the act of arguing — particularly the intellectual disputation of matters.

lexical_analysis.ibn_faris: الْحُجَّةُ: الْبُرْهَانُ. وَحَاجَجْتُهُ: جَادَلْتُهُ بِالْحُجَجِ
lexical_analysis.al_raghib: الْمُحَاجَّةُ: الْمُجَادَلَةُ بِالْحُجَجِ. وَالْحُجَّةُ: الْبُرْهَانُ الَّذِي يُفِيضُ عَلَى الْمُقَامِ

quran_examples.ar: ذَٰلِكَ ٱلۡكِتَـٰبُ لَا رَيۡبَ ۛ فِيهِ ۛ هُدًۭى لِّلۡمُتَّقِينَ
quran_examples.en: This is the Book about which there is no doubt, a guidance for those conscious of Allah

hadith.ar: جَادِلُوا عَنْ أَهْلِ الْبِدَعِ
hadith.en: Argue against the people of innovation

shades.name_en: al-Ḥujja — The Argument and the Proof
shades.explanation: The ḥujja (proof, argument) in the Quran is the divine proof — the evidence that establishes the truth. The verse 2:2 establishes the Quran itself as the huda (guidance) and the Burhān (proof). The ḥujja in the Quran is closely related to al-bayyin (clear evidence) and al-burhān (proof). The hadith — «jādilū ʿan ahli l-bidaʿ» — establishes the principle of arguing against the people of innovation. Al-Ghazālī (Jawāhir al-Qurʾān, Miʿyār al-ʿIlm) treats the ḥujja as the foundation of ʿilm — the one who has the ḥujja has the argument, and the one without the ḥujja has no argument.
shades.hadith_ar: جَادِلُوا عَنْ أَهْلِ الْبِدَعِ
shades.hadith_en: Argue against the people of innovation

meaning.en: To be in difficulty, distress. The root denotes the state of being unable to move forward — and by extension, the settled suffering.

lexical_analysis.ibn_faris: الشَّحْبُ: جَذْبُ الشَّيْءِ بِحِدَّةٍ. وَشَحَبَهُ: جَذَبَهُ وَسَحَبَهُ
lexical_analysis.al_raghib: الشَّحْبُ: جَذْبُ الشَّيْءِ فِي حِدَّةٍ. وَقَدْ يُسْتَعْمَلُ لِلْمَسْحُوبِ فِي الْبُعْدِ

quran_examples.ar: وَإِذَا طَلَّقۡتُمُ ٱلنِّسَآءَ فَبَلَغۡنَ أَجَلَهُنَّ فَلَا تَعۡضُلُوهُنَّ أَن يَنكِحۡنَ أَزۡوَاجَهُنَّ إِذَا تَرَاضَوۡاْ بَيۡنَهُم بِٱلۡمَعۡرُوفِ
quran_examples.en: And when you divorce women and they have fulfilled their term, do not prevent them from remarrying their [former] husbands if they agree among themselves on an acceptable basis
quran_examples.context: The rules of divorce and remarriage

hadith.ar: لَا يَزَالُ الْبَلَاءُ بِالْمُؤْمِنِ وَالْمُؤْمِنَةِ حَتَّى يَلْقَى اللَّهَ وَمَا عَلَيْهِ خَطِيئَةٌ
hadith.en: The trial continues to befall the believer until they meet Allah without any sin

shades.name_en: ash-Shaḥb — The Dragging and the Severance
shades.name_ar: الشَّحْبُ — الْجَذْبُ بِحِدَّةٍ، أَوِ الْبُعْدُ بِعُنْفٍ
shades.explanation: The shaḥb (dragging, severance) in the Quran is the state of being pulled or dragged away. The verse 2:231 establishes the principle that divorced women must not be prevented from remarrying if they agree — and the shaḥb is the violent prevention. The shaḥb in the Quran is closely related to al-jadhb (dragging) and al-qaṭʿ (severing). The hadith of trials establishes the general principle of divine wisdom in human affairs. Al-Ghazālī (Iḥyāʾ) treats the shaḥb as the spiritual state of being pulled away from Allah — the soul that is dragged by its desires away from the divine path.
shades.hadith_ar: لَا يَزَالُ الْبَلَاءُ بِالْمُؤْمِنِ وَالْمُؤْمِنَةِ حَتَّى يَلْقَى اللَّهَ وَمَا عَلَيْهِ خَطِيئَةٌ
shades.hadith_en: The trial continues to befall the believer until they meet Allah without any sin

meaning.en: To say, speak. The root denotes the act of speaking or uttering words — and by extension, the content of speech.
meaning.ar: الْقَوْلُ: اللَّفْظُ الدَّالُّ عَلَى مَا فِي النَّفْسِ

lexical_analysis.ibn_faris: الْقَوْلُ: كُلُّ لَفْظَةٍ تَدُلُّ عَلَى مَعْنًى. وَقَالَ: نَطَقَ
lexical_analysis.al_raghib: الْقَوْلُ: كَلَامٌ يَدُلُّ عَلَى مَعْنًى مِنَ الْمَعَانِي بِاللَّفْظِ. وَهُوَ أَعَمُّ مِنَ الْكَلَامِ

quran_examples.ar: ٱلَّذِينَ يُؤۡمِنُونَ بِٱلۡغَيۡبِ وَيُقِيمُونَ ٱلصَّلَوٰةَ وَمِمَّا رَزَقۡنَـٰهُمۡ يُنفِقُونَ
quran_examples.en: Who believe in the unseen and establish prayer and spend from what We have provided them

hadith.ar: إِنَّ اللَّهَ لَمْ يَدَعْ شَيْئًا يَحْتَاجُ إِلَيْهِ الْعِبَادُ فِي دِينِهِمْ إِلَّا بَيَّنَهُ لَهُمْ
hadith.en: Allah has not left anything that the servants need in their religion without making it clear

shades.name_en: al-Qawl — The Speech and the Word
shades.name_ar: الْقَوْلُ — اللَّفْظُ الدَّالُّ عَلَى مَا فِي النَّفْسِ، وَهُوَ أَعَمُّ مِنَ الْكَلَامِ
shades.explanation: The qawl (speech) in the Quran is the most frequent word — the act of uttering words. The verse 2:3 establishes the principle that the believers believe in the unseen and establish prayer. The qawl in the Quran is both divine (Allah's speech to the prophets) and human (the speech of the believers). The hadith — «inna Allāha lam yadʿ shayʾan yaḥtāju ilayhi l-ʿibādu fī dīnihim illā bayyana-hu lahum» — establishes that Allah has made clear everything the servants need for their religion. Al-Ghazālī (Iḥyāʾ, Book of Etiquette) treats the qawl as one of the most important acts — the tongue must speak only what is good, and the silent tongue is better than the harmful one.
shades.hadith_ar: إِنَّ اللَّهَ لَمْ يَدَعْ شَيْئًا يَحْتَاجُ إِلَيْهِ الْعِبَادُ فِي دِينِهِمْ إِلَّا بَيَّنَهُ لَهُمْ
shades.hadith_en: Allah has not left anything that the servants need in their religion without making it clear

meaning.en: To punish, chastise, torment. The root denotes the infliction of punishment — and by extension, the divine chastisement for sin.

lexical_analysis.ibn_faris: الْعَذَابُ: الْعُقُوبَةُ. وَعَذَّبْتُهُ: أَوْقَعْتُ بِهِ الْعَذَابَ
lexical_analysis.al_raghib: الْعَذَابُ: الْإِيلَامُ الْمُسْتَوْجَبُ بِالذَّنْبِ. وَيُسْتَعْمَلُ مَجَازًا لِكُلِّ مَا يَتَأَلَّمُ مِنْهُ الْإِنْسَانُ

quran_examples.ar: خَتَمَ ٱللَّهُ عَلَىٰ قُلُوبِهِمۡ وَعَلَىٰ سَمۡعِهِمۡ ۖ وَعَلَىٰٓ أَبۡصَـٰرِهِمۡ غِشَـٰوَةٌۭ ۖ وَلَهُمۡ عَذَابٌ عَظِيمٌۭ
quran_examples.en: Allah has set a seal upon their hearts and upon their hearing, and over their vision is a veil. And for them is a great punishment
quran_examples.context: The seal upon the hearts of the disbelievers

hadith.ar: إِنَّ اللَّهَ لَيُمْلِي لِلظَّالِمِ حَتَّى إِذَا أَخَذَهُ لَمْ يُفْلِتْهُ
hadith.en: Allah gives respite to the wrongdoer until He seizes him and he cannot escape

shades.name_ar: الْعَذَابُ — الْعُقُوبَةُ، وَالْعَذَابُ الْأَشَدُّ: عَذَابُ الْآخِرَةِ
shades.explanation: The ʿadhāb (punishment) in the Quran is the divine chastisement — the consequence of sin and disobedience. The verse 2:7 establishes the principle that Allah has set a seal upon the hearts of the disbelievers — and they have a great punishment. The ʿadhāb in the Quran is the most severe consequence of divine justice — the punishment of the Hereafter. The hadith — «inna Allāha layumillī li-l-ẓālim» — establishes that Allah gives respite to the wrongdoer, but when He seizes him, he cannot escape. Al-Ghazālī (Iḥyāʾ, Book of Patience) treats the ʿadhāb as the consequence of turning away from Allah — the more one turns away, the closer one comes to divine punishment. The cure is to turn back to Allah in taubah (repentance).
shades.hadith_ar: إِنَّ اللَّهَ لَيُمْلِي لِلظَّالِمِ حَتَّى إِذَا أَخَذَهُ لَمْ يُفْلِتْهُ
shades.hadith_en: Allah gives respite to the wrongdoer until He seizes him and he cannot escape

meaning.en: To be poor, destitute, in need. The root denotes the state of poverty — and by extension, the spiritual poverty of the soul before Allah.
meaning.ar: الْفَقْرُ: ضِدُّ الْغِنَى، وَالْحَاجَةُ إِلَى الشَّيْءِ

lexical_analysis.ibn_faris: الْفَقْرُ: ضِدُّ الْغِنَى. وَالْفَقِيرُ: الَّذِي لَا شَيْءَ لَهُ
lexical_analysis.al_raghib: الْفَقْرُ: ضِدُّ الْغِنَى. وَهُوَ عَلَى ثَلَاثَةِ أَضْرُبٍ: فَقْرُ الْمَالِ، وَفَقْرُ النَّفْسِ، وَفَقْرُ الْقَلْبِ

quran_examples.ar: لَّيۡسَ ٱلۡبِرَّ أَن تُوَلُّوا۟ وُجُوهَكُمۡ قِبَلَ ٱلۡمَشۡرِقِ وَٱلۡمَغۡرِبِ وَلَـٰكِنَّ ٱلۡبِرَّ مَنۡ ءَامَنَ بِٱللَّهِ وَٱلۡيَوۡمِ ٱلۡـَٔاخِرِ وَٱلۡمَلَـٰٓئِكَةِ وَٱلۡكِتَـٰبِ وَٱلنَّبِيِّـۧنَ وَءَاتَى ٱلۡمَالَ عَلَىٰ حُبِّهِۦ ذَوِى ٱلۡقُرۡبَىٰ وَٱلۡيَتَـٰمَىٰ وَٱلۡمَسَـٰكِينَ وَٱبۡنَ ٱلسَّبِيلِ وَٱلسَّآئِلِينَ وَفِى ٱلرِّقَابِ وَأَقَامَ ٱلصَّلَوٰةَ وَءَاتَى ٱلزَّكَوٰةَ وَٱلۡمُوفُونَ بِعَهۡدِهِمۡ إِذَا عَـٰهَدُوا۟ وَٱلصَّـٰبِرِينَ فِى ٱلۡبَأۡسَآءِ وَٱلضَّرَّآءِ وَحِينَ ٱلۡبَأۡسِ
quran_examples.en: Righteousness is not that you turn your faces toward the east or the west, but [true] righteousness is [in] one who believes in Allah, the Last Day, the angels, the Book, and the prophets, and gives wealth in spite of love for it to relatives, orphans, the needy, the traveler, those who ask [for help], and for freeing captives; and who establishes prayer and gives zakāh; and [those who] fulfill their promise when they promise; and [those who] are patient in poverty and hardship and during battle

hadith.ar: لَبِسُوا الصُّوفَ عَلَى لُبُودِ الْجُنُوبِ، أَوْ بُطُونِ الرَّحَالِ، يَقُولُونَ: سَيِّدُنَا رَبُّنَا
hadith.en: They wore wool on the inside of their garments (against their skin), and they would say: Our Lord, forgive us our sins

shades.name_ar: الْفَقْرُ — الْحَاجَةُ، الْإِنْسَانُ فَقِيرٌ إِلَى اللَّهِ فِي كُلِّ حَالٍ
shades.explanation: The faqr (poverty) in the Quran is both material and spiritual — the state of being in need of Allah. The verse 2:177 establishes the principle of righteousness — which includes being patient in faqr (poverty). The faqr in the Quran is closely related to al-ʿafāf (chastity, refraining) and al-zuhd (asceticism). The hadith of the early Sufis — «labisū l-ṣūf ʿalā l-junūb» — establishes the practice of voluntary poverty for the sake of Allah. Al-Ghazālī (Iḥyāʾ, Book of Trust in Allah) treats the faqr al-nafs as the spiritual state of the one who depends entirely on Allah — the one who knows that all provision comes from Allah alone.
shades.hadith_ar: لَبِسُوا الصُّوفَ عَلَى لُبُودِ الْجُنُوبِ، أَوْ بُطُونِ الرَّحَالِ، يَقُولُونَ: سَيِّدُنَا رَبُّنَا
shades.hadith_en: They wore wool on the inside of their garments, and they would say: Our Lord, forgive us our sins

meaning.en: To try, test, afflict. The root denotes the act of testing — particularly the divine test of the believer through trials.

lexical_analysis.ibn_faris: الْبَلْوُ: الِاخْتِبَارُ. وَبَلَوْتُ الشَّيْءَ: اخْتَبَرْتُهُ
lexical_analysis.al_raghib: الْبَلْوُ: الِاخْتِبَارُ. وَيُسْتَعْمَلُ لِكُلِّ مَا يُبْتَلَى بِهِ الْإِنْسَانُ مِنَ الشَّدَائِدِ وَالنِّعَمِ

quran_examples.ar: وَعَلَّمَ ءَادَمَ ٱلۡأَسۡمَآءَ كُلَّهَا ثُمَّ عَرَضَهُمۡ عَلَى ٱلۡمَلَـٰٓئِكَةِ فَقَالَ أَنۢبِـُٔونِى بِأَسۡمَآءِ هَـٰٓؤُلَآءِ إِن كُنتُمۡ صَـٰدِقِينَ
quran_examples.en: And He taught Adam the names — all of them — and then presented them to the angels and said: Inform Me of the names of these, if you are truthful
quran_examples.context: The test of the angels by the command to prostrate to Adam

hadith.ar: إِنَّمَا الْبَلَاءُ بِالْعَبْدِ فِي الْوَلَدِ وَالْمَالِ
hadith.en: Trials come to the servant in his child and his wealth

shades.name_en: al-Balāʾ — The Test and the Affliction
shades.name_ar: الْبَلْوُ — الِاخْتِبَارُ، بَلْوُ الْإِنْسَانِ فِي نَفْسِهِ وَمَالِهِ وَوَلَدِهِ
shades.explanation: The balāʾ (test, affliction) in the Quran is the divine test — the trial through which Allah distinguishes the sincere from the insincere. The verse 2:31 establishes the test of the angels — the command to prostrate to Adam was a test. The balāʾ in the Quran is both material and spiritual — the test through wealth, children, health, or faith. The hadith — «innama l-balāʾu bi-l-ʿabdi fī l-waladi wa-l-māl» — establishes that trials come to the believer through his children and wealth. Al-Ghazālī (Iḥyāʾ, Book of Patience) treats the balāʾ as the divine pedagogical tool — the believer is refined through tests, and the one who is patient in tests is the one who has faith.
shades.hadith_ar: إِنَّمَا الْبَلَاءُ بِالْعَبْدِ فِي الْوَلَدِ وَالْمَالِ
shades.hadith_en: Trials come to the servant in his child and his wealth

meaning.en: To ride, embark, mount. The root denotes the act of mounting a vehicle or animal — and by extension, the act of undertaking a journey.
meaning.ar: الرُّكُوبُ: الْجُلُوسُ عَلَى الظَّهْرِ مِنَ الدَّابَّةِ أَوِ السَّفِينَةِ

lexical_analysis.ibn_faris: الرُّكُوبُ: الْجُلُوسُ عَلَى الظَّهْرِ. وَالْمَرْكَبُ: مَا يُرْكَبُ عَلَيْهِ
lexical_analysis.al_raghib: الرُّكُوبُ: الِاسْتِوَاءُ عَلَى الظَّهْرِ. وَيُسْتَعْمَلُ لِكُلِّ مَا يُرْكَبُ، وَلَوْ كَانَ سَفِينَةً أَوْ فَرَسًا

quran_examples.ar: فَإِنۡ خِفۡتُمۡ فَرِجَالًا أَوۡ رُكۡبَانًاۭ ۖ فَإِذَآ أَمِنتُمۡ فَٱذۡكُرُوا۟ ٱللَّهَ كَمَا عَلَّمَكُم مَّا لَمۡ تَكُونُوا۟ تَعۡلَمُونَ
quran_examples.en: And if you are in fear — then [pray] on foot or riding. But when you are secure, then remember Allah, as He has taught you that which you did not know
quran_examples.context: The permission to pray while traveling

hadith.ar: لَا تُسَافِرُوا إِلَّا فِي ثَلَاثٍ: مَسْجِدٍ جَامِعٍ، أَوْ مَدْرَسَةٍ، أَوْ بَيْتٍ عَلَى شَطِّ نَهْرٍ جَارٍ
hadith.en: Do not travel except to three places: a congregational mosque, a school, or a house on the bank of a flowing river

shades.name_en: ar-Rukūb — The Riding and the Journey
shades.name_ar: الرُّكُوبُ — الْجُلُوسُ عَلَى الظَّهْرِ، الرَّكْبُ: الْمَسَافِرُونَ عَلَى الْمَرَاكِبِ
shades.explanation: The rukūb (riding) in the Quran is the act of mounting a vehicle or animal. The verse 2:239 establishes the principle that the prayer may be shortened when traveling — and the prayer may be performed on foot or riding. The rukūb in the Quran is closely related to al-safar (travel) and al-masīr (walking). Al-Ghazālī (Iḥyāʾ, Book of Etiquette) treats the rukūb as a manifestation of divine blessing — the animals and vehicles that carry us are all gifts from Allah. The one who rides should remember Allah and not be arrogant.
shades.hadith_ar: لَا تُسَافِرُوا إِلَّا فِي ثَلَاثٍ: مَسْجِدٍ جَامِعٍ، أَوْ مَدْرَسَةٍ، أَوْ بَيْتٍ عَلَى شَطِّ نَهْرٍ جَارٍ
shades.hadith_en: Do not travel except to three places

meaning.en: To beware, fear, be cautious. The root denotes the state of being cautious or wary — particularly the spiritual caution of the soul.

lexical_analysis.ibn_faris: الْحَذَرُ: الْحِذْيَانُ. وَكُلُّ مَا يَتَحَرَّزُ مِنْ شَيْءٍ فَقَدْ حَذِرَهُ
lexical_analysis.al_raghib: الْحَذَرُ: التَّحَرُّزُ مِنَ الْمَكْرُوهِ. وَهُوَ ضِدُّ الْغَفْلَةِ

quran_examples.ar: ثُمَّ قَضَىٰٓ أَجَلًۭا ۖ وَأَجَلٌۭ مُّسَمًّى عِندَهُۥ ۚ ثُمَّ أَنتُمۡ تَمۡتَرُونَ
quran_examples.en: Then He decreed a term, a specified term. And to Allah is the [final] return. Then you will be disputing about it
quran_examples.context: The fixed term of life and the resurrection

hadith.ar: إِيَّاكَ وَالْحَذَرَ، فَإِنَّ الْحَذَرَ لَا يُغْنِي مِنَ الْقَدَرِ
hadith.en: Beware of caution, for caution does not avert the divine decree

shades.name_en: al-Ḥadhar — The Caution and the Watchfulness
shades.name_ar: الْحَذَرُ — التَّحَرُّزُ مِنَ الشَّرِّ، الْحَذَرُ الشَّرْعِيُّ مِنَ الذُّنُوبِ
shades.explanation: The ḥadhar (caution, wariness) in the Quran is the state of being careful — particularly the spiritual caution against sin. The verse 2:56 establishes the principle of the appointed term of life — the ḥadhar of Allah is fixed, and the believer must be cautious about the Hereafter. The ḥadhar in the Quran is closely related to al-khawf (fear) and al-muhādhara (preparing). The hadith — «iyyāka wa-l-ḥadhar» — establishes that excessive caution cannot avert the divine decree. Al-Ghazālī (Iḥyāʾ, Book of Trust in Allah) treats the ḥadhar as the necessary caution without excessive anxiety — the believer must be cautious about the consequences of actions, while maintaining tawakkul (trust in Allah).
shades.hadith_ar: إِيَّاكَ وَالْحَذَرَ، فَإِنَّ الْحَذَرَ لَا يُغْنِي مِنَ الْقَدَرِ
shades.hadith_en: Beware of caution, for caution does not avert the divine decree

meaning.en: To be pure, clear, serene. The root denotes the state of purity and serenity — particularly the clear state of the heart or the sky.
meaning.ar: الصَّفْوُ: ضِدُّ الْكَدَرِ، نَقَاءُ الشَّيْءِ مِمَّا يُخَالِطُهُ

lexical_analysis.ibn_faris: الصَّفْوُ: ضِدُّ الْكَدَرِ. وَصَفَا الشَّيْءُ: خَلَصَ مِنَ الْغَشِّ
lexical_analysis.al_raghib: الصَّفْوُ: النَّقَاءُ مِنَ الْكَدَرِ. وَيُسْتَعْمَلُ لِكُلِّ مَا خَلَصَ مِنَ الشَّوْبِ

quran_examples.ar: ثُمَّ قَسَتۡ قُلُوبُكُم مِّنۢ بَعۡدِ ذَٰلِكَ فَهِىَ كَٱلۡحِجَارَةِ أَوۡ أَشَدُّ قَسۡوَةًۭ ۚ وَإِنَّ مِنَ ٱلۡحِجَارَةِ لَمَا يَتَفَجَّرُ مِنۡهُ ٱلۡأَنۡهَـٰرُ
quran_examples.en: Then your hearts became hardened after that, being like stones or even harder. For indeed, there are stones from which rivers burst forth

hadith.ar: صِفْ لِي رَبَّكَ، قَالَ: لَا تُطِيقُونَ
hadith.en: Describe to me your Lord — He said: You will not be able to

shades.name_en: aṣ-Ṣafw — The Purity of Heart and Sky
shades.name_ar: الصَّفْوُ — نَقَاءُ الشَّيْءِ مِنَ الْكَدَرِ، صَفَاءُ الْقَلْبِ مِنَ الشِّرْكِ
shades.explanation: The ṣafw (purity, serenity) in the Quran is the state of being pure and free from impurities. The verse 2:74 establishes the principle that hearts may become hardened like stones — but stones may also have water flow through them. The ṣafw in the Quran is closely related to al-naqāʾ (purity) and al-ṭahāra (cleanliness). The hadith — «ṣif lī rabbaka» — establishes that the divine reality is beyond description — the human tongue cannot fully describe the ṣafw of Allah. Al-Ghazālī (Miʿyār al-ʿIlm) treats the ṣafw as the state of the soul free from the impurities of sin and doubt — the one who has ṣafw has the foundation of the spiritual life.
shades.hadith_ar: صِفْ لِي رَبَّكَ، قَالَ: لَا تُطِيقُونَ
shades.hadith_en: Describe to me your Lord — He said: You will not be able to

meaning.en: To die, pass away. The root denotes the departure of the soul from the body — and by extension, the cessation of worldly life.
meaning.ar: الْمَوْتُ: خِلَافُ الْحَيَاةِ، انْفِصَالُ الرُّوحِ عَنِ الْجَسَدِ

lexical_analysis.ibn_faris: الْمَوْتُ: خِلَافُ الْحَيَاةِ. وَمَاتَ: ذَهَبَتْ حَيَاتُهُ
lexical_analysis.al_raghib: الْمَوْتُ: خُرُوجُ الرُّوحِ مِنَ الْجَسَدِ. وَالْمَوْتُ الشَّرْعِيُّ: خُرُوجُ الرُّوحِ بِقَبْضِ مَلَكِ الْمَوْتِ

quran_examples.ar: كَيۡفَ تَكۡفُرُونَ بِٱللَّهِ وَكُنتُمۡ أَمۡوَ٭تًۭا فَأَحۡيَـٰكُمۡ ۖ ثُمَّ يُمِيتُكُمۡ ثُمَّ يُحۡيِيكُمۡ ثُمَّ إِلَيۡهِ تُرۡجَعُونَ
quran_examples.en: How can you disbelieve in Allah while you were dead and He gave you life; then He will cause you to die, then He will give you life, then to Him you will be returned
quran_examples.context: The divine gift of life and the certainty of death

hadith.ar: كُنْ فِي الدُّنْيَا كَأَنَّكَ غَرِيبٌ أَوْ عَابِرُ سَبِيلٍ
hadith.en: Be in the world as if you are a stranger or a traveler

shades.name_en: al-Mawt — The Death and the Hereafter
shades.name_ar: الْمَوْتُ — خُرُوجُ الرُّوحِ مِنَ الْجَسَدِ، كُلُّ نَفْسٍ ذَائِقَةُ الْمَوْتِ
shades.explanation: The mawt (death) in the Quran is the most certain fact of life — «kullu nafsin dhāʾiqatu l-mawt» (every soul will taste death). The verse 2:28 establishes the principle that Allah gives life and causes death — the divine cycle. The mawt in the Quran is not annihilation but transition — the departure of the soul to the barzakh (intermediate realm). The hadith — «kun fī l-dunyā ka-annaka gharīb» — establishes the attitude of the believer toward the world — as a stranger or traveler. Al-Ghazālī (Iḥyāʾ, Book of Remembrance of Death) treats the mawt as the most important reality that the believer must constantly remember — the one who remembers death is detached from the world, while the one who forgets death is trapped in it.
shades.hadith_ar: كُنْ فِي الدُّنْيَا كَأَنَّكَ غَرِيبٌ أَوْ عَابِرُ سَبِيلٍ
shades.hadith_en: Be in the world as if you are a stranger or a traveler

meaning.en: To be merciful, compassionate. The root denotes the quality of mercy — the most important attribute of Allah.
meaning.ar: الرَّحْمَةُ: رِقَّةُ الْقَلْبِ، وَالْإِرَادَةُ لِلْإِحْسَانِ إِلَى الْمَرْحُومِ

lexical_analysis.ibn_faris: الرَّحْمَةُ: رِقَّةُ الْقَلْبِ. وَالرَّحْمَنُ: ذُو الرَّحْمَةِ
lexical_analysis.al_raghib: الرَّحْمَةُ: رَأْفَةٌ تَقْتَضِي الْإِحْسَانَ إِلَى الْمَرْحُومِ. وَهِيَ أَفْعَلُ الصِّفَاتِ الْإِلَهِيَّةِ

quran_examples.ar: وَإِذۡ قَالَ رَبُّكَ لِلۡمَلَـٰٓئِكَةِ إِنِّى جَاعِلٌۭ فِى ٱلۡأَرۡضِ خَلِيفَةًۭ ۖ قَالُوٓاْ أَتَجۡعَلُ فِيهَا مَن يُفۡسِدُ فِيهَا وَيَسۡفِكُ ٱلدِّمَآءَ وَنَحۡنُ نُسَبِّحُ بِحَمۡدِكَ وَنُقَدِّسُ لَكَ ۖ قَالَ إِنِّىٓ أَعۡلَمُ مَا لَا تَعۡلَمُونَ
quran_examples.en: And [mention] when your Lord said to the angels: Indeed I am going to place upon the earth a vicegerent. They said: Will You place upon it one who causes corruption therein and sheds blood, while we declare Your praise and sanctify You? Allah said: Indeed, I know that which you do not know

hadith.ar: إِنَّ لِلَّهِ مِائَةَ رَحْمَةٍ، أَنْزَلَ مِنْهَا رَحْمَةً وَاحِدَةً بَيْنَ الْجِنِّ وَالْإِنْسِ وَالْبَهَائِمِ وَالْهَوَامِّ، فَبِهَا يَتَعَاطَفُونَ، وَأَخَّرَ اللَّهُ تِسْعًا وَتِسْعِينَ رَحْمَةً يَرْحَمُ بِهَا عِبَادَهُ يَوْمَ الْقِيَامَةِ
hadith.en: Indeed Allah has one hundred mercies, of which He sent down one mercy among jinn, humans, animals, and insects — by which they are kind to one another. And Allah has kept ninety-nine mercies for His servants on the Day of Judgment

shades.name_ar: الرَّحْمَةُ — رَأْفَةٌ تَقْتَضِي الْإِحْسَانَ، رَحْمَةُ اللَّهِ أَفْضَلُ مِنْ كُلِّ شَيْءٍ
shades.explanation: The raḥma (mercy) in the Quran is the most important divine attribute — Allah is al-Raḥmān (the Most Merciful), al-Raḥīm (the Especially Merciful). The verse 2:64 establishes the principle of the divine vicegerency — Adam was placed on the earth with Allah's mercy. The raḥma in the Quran is the mercy that encompasses all things — the divine mercy that gives life to the dead. The hadith — «inna lillāhi miʾata raḥma» — establishes that Allah has one hundred mercies, of which He sent only one to the world, and reserved ninety-nine for the Day of Judgment. Al-Ghazālī (Jawāhir al-Qurʾān) treats the raḥma as the foundation of all divine attributes — without raḥma, the divine attributes would be terrifying, but with raḥma, they become merciful.
shades.hadith_ar: إِنَّ لِلَّهِ مِائَةَ رَحْمَةٍ، أَنْزَلَ مِنْهَا رَحْمَةً وَاحِدَةً
shades.hadith_en: Indeed Allah has one hundred mercies, of which He sent down one mercy

meaning.en: To think, reckon, account. The root denotes the act of calculating or reckoning — and by extension, the divine accounting of deeds.

lexical_analysis.ibn_faris: الْحِسَابُ: عَدُّ الشَّيْءِ. وَكُلُّ مَنْ أَحْصَى شَيْئًا فَقَدْ حَسَبَهُ
lexical_analysis.al_raghib: الْحِسَابُ: الْإِحْصَاءُ. وَيُسْتَعْمَلُ مَجَازًا لِلْكِفَايَةِ، كَقَوْلِهِمْ: حَسْبِيَ اللَّهُ، أَيْ كَافَانِي

quran_examples.ar: تِلۡكَ عَشَرَةٌۭ كَامِلَةٌۭ ۖ ذَٰلِكَ لِمَن لَّمۡ يَكُنۡ أَهۡلُهُ حَاضِرِى ٱلۡمَسۡجِدِ ٱلۡحَرَامِ ۚ وَٱتَّقُوا۟ ٱللَّهَ وَٱعۡلَمُوٓا۟ أَنَّ ٱللَّهَ شَدِيدُ ٱلۡعِقَابِ
quran_examples.en: These are ten complete [days] — that is for whoever is not resident near the Sacred Mosque. And fear Allah and know that Allah is severe in penalty

hadith.ar: مَنْ حَاسَبَ نَفْسَهُ فِي الدُّنْيَا شَغَلَهُ عَنِ اللَّهِ
hadith.en: Whoever holds himself to account in this world will be too busy for Allah

shades.name_en: al-Ḥisāb — The Reckoning and the Account
shades.name_ar: الْحِسَابُ — الْإِحْصَاءُ، حِسَابُ اللَّهِ لِلْعِبَادِ يَوْمَ الْقِيَامَةِ
shades.explanation: The ḥisāb (reckoning, account) in the Quran is the divine accounting — the Day of Judgment when every soul will be reckoned with. The verse 2:202 establishes the principle that those who live near the Sacred Mosque have a different rule — and the ḥisāb of Allah is severe. The ḥisāb in the Quran is closely related to al-jazāʾ (recompense) and al-mīzān (balance). The hadith — «man ḥāsaba nafsahu fī l-dunyā» — establishes that the one who holds himself accountable in this world will be freed from the divine reckoning. Al-Ghazālī (Iḥyāʾ, Book of Accountability) treats the ḥisāb as a lifelong duty — the believer must continually examine his deeds and intentions.
shades.hadith_ar: مَنْ حَاسَبَ نَفْسَهُ فِي الدُّنْيَا شَغَلَهُ عَنِ اللَّهِ
shades.hadith_en: Whoever holds himself to account in this world will be too busy for Allah

meaning.en: I, me, myself. The root denotes the first person singular pronoun — the self, the ego.
meaning.ar: الْأَنَا: ضَمِيرُ الْمُتَكَلِّمِ، يَدُلُّ عَلَى الذَّاتِ الْمُتَكَلِّمِ

lexical_analysis.ibn_faris: الْأَنَا: الضَّمِيرُ الْمُتَكَلِّمُ بِهِ عَنْ نَفْسِهِ
lexical_analysis.al_raghib: الْأَنَا: ضَمِيرُ الْمُتَكَلِّمِ عَنْ نَفْسِهِ. وَهُوَ فِي الشَّرْعِ: الدَّالُّ عَلَى الذَّاتِ الْمُتَكَلِّمِ

quran_examples.ar: وَمِنۡهُمۡ أُمِّيُّونَ لَا يَعۡلَمُونَ ٱلۡكِتَـٰبَ إِلَّا أَمَانِىَّ وَإِنۡ هُمۡ إِلَّا يَظُنُّونَ
quran_examples.en: And among them are unlettered ones who do not know the Scripture except in wishful thinking, but they are only assuming
quran_examples.context: The unlettered Arabs and their ignorance of the Book

hadith.ar: أَنَا رَسُولُ اللَّهِ إِلَيْكُمْ حَقًّا
hadith.en: I am the Messenger of Allah to you, truly

shades.name_en: al-Anā — The Self and the Ego
shades.name_ar: الْأَنَا — ضَمِيرُ الْمُتَكَلِّمِ، الَّذِي يَدُلُّ عَلَى الذَّاتِ الْمُتَكَلِّمِ
shades.explanation: The anā (I, the ego) in the Quran is the first-person pronoun — used both by humans and by Allah (when speaking in the divine speech of the Quran). The verse 2:78 establishes that some people have the Book only in wishful thinking — but the anā of the human is often the source of error. The anā in the Quran has a particular force when Allah speaks — «ana Allāh» — establishing divine identity. The hadith — «ana rasūl Allāh ilaykum» — establishes the Prophet's mission by his declaration of his identity. Al-Ghazālī (Iḥyāʾ, Book of Disciplining the Soul) treats the anā (ego) as the most fundamental obstacle to spiritual progress — the one who overcomes the anā is the one who has attained.
shades.hadith_ar: أَنَا رَسُولُ اللَّهِ إِلَيْكُمْ حَقًّا
shades.hadith_en: I am the Messenger of Allah to you, truly

meaning.en: To ask, question, request. The root denotes the act of asking or questioning — particularly the seeking of knowledge or help.

lexical_analysis.ibn_faris: الْمَسْأَلَةُ: طَلَبُ الشَّيْءِ. وَسَأَلَهُ: طَلَبَ مِنْهُ
lexical_analysis.al_raghib: الْمَسْأَلَةُ: طَلَبُ الشَّيْءِ بِقَوْلٍ أَوْ فِعْلٍ. وَالِاسْتِفْهَامُ: طَلَبُ الْفَهْمِ

quran_examples.ar: وَإِذۡ أَخَذۡنَا مِيثَـٰقَ بَنِىٓ إِسۡرَٰٓءِيلَ لَا تَعۡبُدُونَ إِلَّا ٱللَّهَ وَبِٱلۡوَٰلِدَيۡنِ إِحۡسَانًا وَذِى ٱلۡقُرۡبَىٰ وَٱلۡيَتَـٰمَىٰ وَٱلۡمَسَـٰكِينِ وَقُولُوا۟ لِلنَّاسِ حُسۡنًۭا وَأَقِيمُوا۟ ٱلصَّلَوٰةَ وَءَاتُوا۟ ٱلزَّكَوٰةَ ثُمَّ تَوَلَّيۡتُمۡ إِلَّا قَلِيلًۭا مِّنكُمۡ وَأَنتُمۡ مُعۡرِضُونَ
quran_examples.en: And [recall] when We took the covenant from the Children of Israel: You shall not worship except Allah, and to parents do good, and to relatives, orphans, and the needy. And speak to people good [words] and establish prayer and give zakāh. Then you turned away, except a few of you, and you were refusing
quran_examples.context: The covenant of the Children of Israel

hadith.ar: سَلُوا اللَّهَ مِنْ فَضْلِهِ، فَإِنَّهُ يُحِبُّ أَنْ يُسْأَلَ
hadith.en: Ask Allah for His bounty, for He loves to be asked

shades.name_en: as-Suʾāl — The Asking and the Request
shades.name_ar: الْمَسْأَلَةُ — طَلَبُ الشَّيْءِ، سُؤَالُ اللَّهِ أَفْضَلُ الْعِبَادَاتِ
shades.explanation: The suʾāl (asking, requesting) in the Quran is one of the fundamental acts of worship — the asking of Allah for one's needs. The verse 2:83 establishes the covenant with the Children of Israel — and they were commanded to fulfill it. The suʾāl in the Quran is the asking of Allah for guidance, sustenance, and forgiveness. The hadith — «salū Allāh min faḍlihi» — establishes that Allah loves to be asked and that asking is one of the most beloved acts of worship. Al-Ghazālī (Iḥyāʾ, Book of Duʿāʾ) treats the suʾāl as the essential act of ʿubūdiyya (servitude) — the one who asks Allah is acknowledging his need and His generosity.
shades.hadith_ar: سَلُوا اللَّهَ مِنْ فَضْلِهِ، فَإِنَّهُ يُحِبُّ أَنْ يُسْأَلَ
shades.hadith_en: Ask Allah for His bounty, for He loves to be asked

meaning.en: To come, bring, arrive. The root denotes the arrival or coming — and by extension, the divine decree that comes to pass.

lexical_analysis.ibn_faris: الْمَجِيءُ: ضِدُّ الذَّهَابِ. وَجَأْتُ: أَتَيْتُ
lexical_analysis.al_raghib: الْمَجِيءُ: الْإِتْيَانُ. وَقِيلَ: الْإِقْبَالُ عَلَى الشَّيْءِ

quran_examples.ar: وَلَقَدۡ جَآءَكُم مُّوسَىٰ مِن قَبۡلُ وَأَنتُمۡ ظَـٰلِمُونَ
quran_examples.en: And Moses had certainly come to you before while you were wrongdoers
quran_examples.context: The coming of Moses to the Children of Israel

hadith.ar: جَاءَ الْحَقُّ وَزَهَقَ الْبَاطِلُ
hadith.en: Truth has come and falsehood has perished

shades.name_en: al-Majīʾ — The Coming and the Arrival
shades.name_ar: الْمَجِيءُ — الْإِتْيَانُ، مَجِيءُ الْحَقِّ وَمَجِيءُ الْآخِرَةِ
shades.explanation: The majīʾ (coming, arrival) in the Quran is the arrival of the divine decree — and the certainty that what Allah has promised will come to pass. The verse 2:89 establishes the principle that Moses came to the Children of Israel while they were wrongdoers — and the majīʾ of the messenger is the arrival of truth. The majīʾ in the Quran is closely related to al-wuṣūl (arrival) and al-nuzūl (descent). The hadith — «jāʾa l-ḥaqqu wa-zahaqa l-bāṭil» — establishes that truth has come and falsehood has perished. Al-Ghazālī (Jawāhir al-Qurʾān) treats the majīʾ as the divine arrival — the one who awaits Allah's majīʾ with patience is the one who has faith.
shades.hadith_ar: جَاءَ الْحَقُّ وَزَهَقَ الْبَاطِلُ
shades.hadith_en: Truth has come and falsehood has perished

meaning.en: Honorable, noble, high. The root denotes the state of nobility or honor — particularly the high rank or status.

lexical_analysis.ibn_faris: الشَّرَفُ: الْعُلُوُّ. وَالشَّرِيفُ: الْعَالِي
lexical_analysis.al_raghib: الشَّرَفُ: الْفَضْلُ الْمُشْرِفُ. وَقِيلَ: الشَّرَفُ: الْعُلُوُّ فِي الشَّرَفِ

quran_examples.ar: تَبَـٰرَكَ ٱسۡمُ رَبِّكَ ذِى ٱلۡجَلَـٰلِ وَٱلۡإِكۡرَامِ
quran_examples.en: Blessed be the name of your Lord, Owner of Majesty and Honor
quran_examples.context: The closing of surah al-Rahman — the divine majesty and honor

hadith.ar: إِنَّ اللَّهَ يُحِبُّ مَعَالِيَ الْأَخْلَاقِ وَيَكۡرَهُ سَفۡسَافَهَا
hadith.en: Indeed Allah loves high morals and hates low ones

shades.name_en: ash-Sharaf — The Honor and the Nobility
shades.name_ar: الشَّرَفُ — الْعُلُوُّ، وَالشَّرَفُ الْحَقِيقِيُّ: شَرَفُ التَّقْوَى
shades.explanation: The sharaf (honor, nobility) in the Quran is closely tied to the divine attributes — Allah is dhū l-jalāli wa-l-ikrām (Owner of Majesty and Honor). The verse 55:78 establishes that the name of Allah is blessed — the source of all honor and majesty. The sharaf in the Quran is closely related to al-faḍl (virtue) and al-karāma (dignity). The hadith — «inna Allāha yuḥibbu maʿālī l-akhlāq» — establishes that Allah loves high morals. Al-Ghazālī (Iḥyāʾ, Book of Etiquette) treats the sharaf as the elevation of the soul — the one who has taqwā has the true sharaf, regardless of lineage or wealth.
shades.hadith_ar: إِنَّ اللَّهَ يُحِبُّ مَعَالِيَ الْأَخْلَاقِ
shades.hadith_en: Indeed Allah loves high morals

meaning.en: To be near, approach. The root denotes the state of nearness — particularly the nearness to Allah through worship.

lexical_analysis.ibn_faris: الْقُرْبُ: ضِدُّ الْبُعْدِ. وَقَرُبَ الشَّيْءُ: دَنَا
lexical_analysis.al_raghib: الْقُرْبُ: ضِدُّ الْبُعْدِ. وَقُرْبُ الْإِنْسَانِ مِنَ اللَّهِ: إِقْبَالُهُ عَلَيْهِ بِالطَّاعَةِ

quran_examples.ar: وَإِذَا سَأَلَكَ عِبَادِى عَنِّى فَإِنِّى قَرِيبٌ ۖ أُجِيبُ دَعۡوَةَ ٱلدَّاعِ إِذَا دَعَانِ
quran_examples.en: And when My servants ask you about Me — indeed I am near. I respond to the call of the caller when he calls upon Me
quran_examples.context: Allah's nearness to the supplicating servant

hadith.ar: أَقْرَبُ مَا يَكُونُ الْعَبْدُ مِنْ رَبِّهِ وَهُوَ سَاجِدٌ
hadith.en: The closest the servant is to his Lord is while he is prostrating

shades.name_ar: الْقُرْبُ — ضِدُّ الْبُعْدِ، وَأَقْرَبُ مَا يَكُونُ الْعَبْدُ مِنْ رَبِّهِ فِي السُّجُودِ
shades.explanation: The qurb (nearness, approach) in the Quran is the spiritual nearness to Allah — the highest goal of the soul. The verse 2:186 establishes that Allah is near (qarīb) — and He responds to the call of the caller. The qurb in the Quran is closely related to al-wuṣūl (arrival) and al-muqābala (meeting). The hadith — «aqrabu mā yakūnu l-ʿabdu min rabbihi wa-huwa sājid» — establishes that the closest the servant is to his Lord is while he is prostrating. Al-Ghazālī (Iḥyāʾ, Book of Remembrance of Allah) treats the qurb as the highest spiritual station — the one who has attained qurb has achieved the goal of the spiritual journey.
shades.hadith_ar: أَقْرَبُ مَا يَكُونُ الْعَبْدُ مِنْ رَبِّهِ وَهُوَ سَاجِدٌ
shades.hadith_en: The closest the servant is to his Lord is while he is prostrating

meaning.en: To be rich, content, free from need. The root denotes the state of richness — and the divine attribute of being in no need of creation.
meaning.ar: الْغِنَى: ضِدُّ الْفَقْرِ، الِاسْتِغْنَاءُ عَنْ غَيْرِهِ

lexical_analysis.ibn_faris: الْغِنَى: ضِدُّ الْفَقْرِ. وَاسْتَغْنَى الشَّيْءُ: اسْتَغْنَى عَنْ غَيْرِهِ
lexical_analysis.al_raghib: الْغِنَى: ضِدُّ الْفَقْرِ. وَهُوَ اسْتِغْنَاءُ الشَّيْءِ عَمَّا يَحْتَاجُ إِلَيْهِ

quran_examples.ar: يَـٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوٓاْ أَنفِقُوا۟ مِن طَيِّبَـٰتِ مَا كَسَبۡتُمۡ وَمِمَّآ أَخۡرَجۡنَا لَكُم مِّنَ ٱلۡأَرۡضِ ۖ وَلَا تَيَمَّمُوا۟ ٱلۡخَبِيثَ مِنۡهُ تُنفِقُونَ وَلَسۡتُم بِـَٔاخِذِيهِ إِلَّآ أَن تُغۡمِضُوا۟ فِيهِ ۚ وَٱعۡلَمُوٓاْ أَنَّ ٱللَّهَ غَنِىٌّ حَمِيدٌ
quran_examples.en: O you who have believed, spend from the good things which you have earned and from that which We have produced for you from the earth. And do not aim toward the defective therefrom, spending [only upon it] while you would not take it [yourself] except with closed eyes. And know that Allah is Free of need and Praiseworthy
quran_examples.context: The command to spend and the divine freedom from need

hadith.ar: لَا تَسْأَلُوا النَّاسَ أَشْيَاءَهُمْ، فَإِنَّهُ مَنْ سَأَلَ النَّاسَ شَيْئًا مِنْ غَيْرِ مَسْأَلَةٍ، أَتَى يَوْمَ الْقِيَامَةِ وَفِي وَجْهِهِ خَمْشَةٌ
hadith.en: Do not ask people for their things, for whoever asks people for something without need will come on the Day of Judgment with his face scratched

shades.name_en: al-Ghinā — The Richness of Allah and the Self-Sufficiency of the Believer
shades.name_ar: الْغِنَى — اسْتِغْنَاءُ الشَّيْءِ عَمَّا سِوَاهُ، اللَّهُ غَنِيٌّ حَمِيدٌ
shades.explanation: The ghinā (richness, self-sufficiency) in the Quran is one of the divine attributes — Allah is al-Ghanī (the Self-Sufficient). The verse 2:267 establishes that Allah is free of need (ghanī) and praiseworthy (ḥamīd) — even though He commands spending. The ghinā in the Quran is the state of being in no need — and the human ghinā comes from taqwā (piety). The hadith — «lā tasʾalū al-nāsa ashyāʾahum» — establishes that the believer should not beg from people — true ghinā is in the heart. Al-Ghazālī (Iḥyāʾ, Book of Trust in Allah) treats the ghinā as the spiritual state of the heart — the one who is ghanī from people is ghanī from need.
shades.hadith_ar: لَا تَسْأَلُوا النَّاسَ أَشْيَاءَهُمْ
shades.hadith_en: Do not ask people for their things

meaning.en: To take, seize, hold. The root denotes the act of taking or seizing — and by extension, the divine taking of the soul at death.
meaning.ar: الْأَخْذُ: ضِدُّ الْإِعْطَاءِ، ضَبْطُ الشَّيْءِ وَحَيَازَتُهُ

lexical_analysis.ibn_faris: الْأَخْذُ: ضِدُّ الْإِعْطَاءِ. وَأَخَذْتُ الشَّيْءَ: حَوَزْتُهُ
lexical_analysis.al_raghib: الْأَخْذُ: ضِدُّ الْإِعْطَاءِ. وَقِيلَ: اسْتِيفَاءُ الشَّيْءِ مَعَ ضَبْطٍ

quran_examples.ar: وَإِذۡ أَخَذۡنَا مِيثَـٰقَ بَنِىٓ إِسۡرَٰٓءِيلَ لَا تَعۡبُدُونَ إِلَّا ٱللَّهَ وَبِٱلۡوَٰلِدَيۡنِ إِحۡسَانًا وَذِى ٱلۡقُرۡبَىٰ وَٱلۡيَتَـٰمَىٰ وَٱلۡمَسَـٰكِينِ وَقُولُوا۟ لِلنَّاسِ حُسۡنًۭا وَأَقِيمُوا۟ ٱلصَّلَوٰةَ وَءَاتُوا۟ ٱلزَّكَوٰةَ ثُمَّ تَوَلَّيۡتُمۡ إِلَّا قَلِيلًۭا مِّنكُمۡ وَأَنتُمۡ مُعۡرِضُونَ
quran_examples.en: And [recall] when We took the covenant from the Children of Israel: You shall not worship except Allah, and to parents do good, and to relatives, orphans, and the needy. And speak to people good [words] and establish prayer and give zakāh. Then you turned away, except a few of you, and you were refusing
quran_examples.context: The covenant of the Children of Israel

hadith.ar: إِنَّ اللَّهَ لَا يَأْخُذُ بِالظِّنَّةِ، وَلَا يُؤَاخِذُ بِالْحَدْسِ، وَيُحِبُّ التَّثَبُّتَ
hadith.en: Indeed Allah does not punish based on suspicion, and He does not punish based on guessing, and He loves verification

shades.name_en: al-Akhdh — The Taking and the Seizing
shades.name_ar: الْأَخْذُ — ضِبْطُ الشَّيْءِ، أَخْذُ اللَّهِ لِلْأَعْمَالِ يَوْمَ الْقِيَامَةِ
shades.explanation: The akhdh (taking, seizing) in the Quran is one of the most frequent words — the act of taking or seizing. The verse 2:83 establishes the principle of the covenant — Allah took (akhadhnā) the covenant from the Children of Israel. The akhdh in the Quran is both divine (Allah takes the covenant, the soul at death) and human (the human takes, the human seizes). The hadith — «inna Allāha lā ya'khudhu bi-l-ẓann» — establishes that Allah does not punish based on suspicion — He acts with justice. Al-Ghazālī (Miʿyār al-ʿIlm) treats the akhdh as the act of binding — the one who takes a covenant is bound by it, and the one who seizes must seize with justice.
shades.hadith_ar: إِنَّ اللَّهَ لَا يَأْخُذُ بِالظِّنَّةِ
shades.hadith_en: Indeed Allah does not punish based on suspicion

meaning.en: To be high, exalted, elevated. The root denotes the state of being high — and by extension, the divine exaltation above the creation.
meaning.ar: الْعُلُوُّ: ضِدُّ السُّفُولِ، الرِّفْعَةُ فَوْقَ غَيْرِهِ

lexical_analysis.ibn_faris: الْعُلُوُّ: ضِدُّ السُّفُلِ. وَعَلَا: ارْتَفَعَ
lexical_analysis.al_raghib: الْعُلُوُّ: ضِدُّ السُّفُولِ. وَهُوَ مَجَازٌ لِلتَّفَوُّقِ فِي الشَّرَفِ

quran_examples.ar: ٱللَّهُ لَآ إِلَـٰهَ إِلَّا هُوَ ٱلۡحَىُّ ٱلۡقَيُّومُ ۚ لَا تَأۡخُذُهُۥ سِنَةٌۭ وَلَا نَوۡمٌۭ ۚ لَّهُۥ مَا فِى ٱلسَّمَـٰوَٰتِ وَمَا فِى ٱلۡأَرۡضِ ۗ مَن ذَا ٱلَّذِى يَشۡفَعُ عِندَهُۥٓ إِلَّا بِإِذۡنِهِۦ ۚ يَعۡلَمُ مَا بَيۡنَ أَيۡدِيهِمۡ وَمَا خَلۡفَهُمۡ ۖ وَلَا يُحِيطُونَ بِشَىۡءٍۢ مِّنۡ عِلۡمِهِۦٓ إِلَّا بِمَا شَآءَ ۚ وَسِعَ كُرۡسِيُّهُ ٱلسَّمَـٰوَٰتِ وَٱلۡأَرۡضَ ۖ وَلَا يَـُٔودُهُۥ حِفۡظُهُمَا ۚ وَهُوَ ٱلۡعَلِىُّ ٱلۡعَظِيمُ
quran_examples.en: Allah — there is no deity except Him, the Ever-Living, the Sustainer of existence. Neither drowsiness overtakes Him nor sleep. To Him belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth. Who is it that can intercede with Him except by His permission? He knows what is before them and what will be after them, and they encompass not a thing of His knowledge except for what He wills. His Kursi extends over the heavens and the earth, and their preservation tires Him not. And He is the Most High, the Grand

hadith.ar: إِنَّ اللَّهَ عَزَّ وَجَلَّ إِذَا تَفَضَّلَ عَلَى عَبْدِهِ بِفَضْلِهِ أَحَبَّ أَنْ يَرَى أَثَرَهُ عَلَيْهِ
hadith.en: Indeed Allah, when He grants a bounty to His servant, loves to see its effect on him

shades.name_ar: الْعُلُوُّ — ضِدُّ السُّفُولِ، اللهُ الْعَلِيُّ الْعَظِيمُ
shades.explanation: The ʿulūw (highness, exaltedness) in the Quran is the divine attribute — Allah is al-ʿAlī (the Most High). The verse 2:255 establishes the Āyat al-Kursī — and concludes «wa-huwa l-ʿaliyyu l-ʿaẓīm» (He is the Most High, the Grand). The ʿulūw in the Quran is closely related to al-kibriyāʾ (greatness) and al-jalāl (majesty). The hadith — «inna Allāha ʿazza wa-jalla iḍā tafaḍḍala ʿalā ʿabdihi bi-faḍlihi aḥabba an yarā atharahu ʿalayh» — establishes that Allah loves to see the effect of His bounty on His servant. Al-Ghazālī (Jawāhir al-Qurʾān) treats the ʿulūw as the divine attribute — Allah is above the creation in essence, in attributes, and in actions.
shades.hadith_ar: إِنَّ اللَّهَ عَزَّ وَجَلَّ إِذَا تَفَضَّلَ عَلَى عَبْدِهِ بِفَضْلِهِ أَحَبَّ أَنْ يَرَى أَثَرَهُ عَلَيْهِ
shades.hadith_en: Indeed Allah, when He grants a bounty to His servant, loves to see its effect on him

meaning.en: To please, satisfy, be content. The root denotes the state of satisfaction — and by extension, the divine pleasure with the believer.

lexical_analysis.ibn_faris: الرِّضَا: ضِدُّ السُّخْطِ. وَرَضِيتُ: ارْتَحْتُ لَهُ
lexical_analysis.al_raghib: الرِّضَا: ضِدُّ السُّخْطِ. وَهُوَ الرَّاحَةُ لِلشَّيْءِ مَعَ قَبُولِهِ

quran_examples.ar: وَمِنَ ٱلنَّاسِ مَن يَشۡرِى نَفۡسَهُ ٱبۡتِغَآءَ مَرۡضَاتِ ٱللَّهِ ۚ وَٱللَّهُ رَءُوفٌۢ بِٱلۡعِبَادِ
quran_examples.en: And among the people is he who sells himself, seeking means to the approval of Allah. And Allah is Kind to [His] servants

hadith.ar: إِنَّ اللَّهَ رَفِيقٌ يُحِبُّ الرِّفْقَ فِي الْأَمْرِ كُلِّهِ
hadith.en: Indeed Allah is gentle and loves gentleness in all matters

shades.name_en: al-Riḍā — The Satisfaction and the Pleasure
shades.name_ar: الرِّضَا — ضِدُّ السُّخْطِ، الرِّضَا مِنَ اللَّهِ أَفْضَلُ الْأَعْمَالِ
shades.explanation: The riḍā (satisfaction, pleasure) in the Quran is the divine state of satisfaction with the believer — and the believer's satisfaction with Allah. The verse 2:207 establishes the principle of self-sacrifice for Allah's pleasure — and Allah is ra'ūf (kind) to the servants. The riḍā in the Quran is the highest state of the believer — the riḍā of Allah with the servant and the riḍā of the servant with Allah. The hadith — «inna Allāha raḥīmun yuḥibbu l-ri'fa» — establishes that Allah loves gentleness. Al-Ghazālī (Iḥyāʾ, Book of Satisfaction) treats the riḍā as the highest station of the soul — the one who is riḍā has accepted divine decree in all its forms.
shades.hadith_ar: إِنَّ اللَّهَ رَفِيقٌ يُحِبُّ الرِّفْقَ فِي الْأَمْرِ كُلِّهِ
shades.hadith_en: Indeed Allah is gentle and loves gentleness in all matters

meaning.en: Wage, reward, recompense. The root denotes the wage or recompense — particularly the divine reward for good deeds.

lexical_analysis.ibn_faris: الْأَجْرُ: الْجَزَاءُ عَلَى الْعَمَلِ. وَأَجَرْتُهُ: أَعْطَيْتُهُ الْأَجْرَ
lexical_analysis.al_raghib: الْأَجْرُ: الْعِوَضُ عَلَى عَمَلٍ. وَفِي الشَّرْعِ: ثَوَابُ اللَّهِ تَعَالَى عَلَى الطَّاعَةِ

quran_examples.ar: إِنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوا۟ وَٱلَّذِينَ هَادُوا۟ وَٱلنَّصَـٰرَىٰ وَٱلصَّـٰبِـِٔينَ مَنۡ ءَامَنَ بِٱللَّهِ وَٱلۡيَوۡمِ ٱلۡـَٔاخِرِ وَعَمِلَ صَـٰلِحًۭا فَلَهُمۡ أَجۡرُهُمۡ عِندَ رَبِّهِمۡ وَلَا خَوۡفٌ عَلَيۡهِمۡ وَلَا هُمۡ يَحۡزَنُونَ
quran_examples.en: Indeed those who believed and those who were Jews or Christians or Sabeans [before Prophet Muhammad] — those [among them] who believed in Allah and the Last Day and did righteous deeds — will be rewarded by their Lord, and there will be no fear concerning them, nor will they grieve
quran_examples.context: The universal reward of faith and good deeds

hadith.ar: إِنَّ لِلَّهِ مِائَةَ رَحْمَةٍ، أَنْزَلَ مِنْهَا رَحْمَةً وَاحِدَةً
hadith.en: Allah has one hundred mercies, of which He sent down one

shades.name_en: al-Ajr — The Reward and the Recompense
shades.name_ar: الْأَجْرُ — الْجَزَاءُ عَلَى الْعَمَلِ، أَجْرُ اللَّهِ أَفْضَلُ الْأُجُورِ
shades.explanation: The ajr (reward, wage) in the Quran is the divine recompense for good deeds — the wage of the believer. The verse 2:62 establishes that those who believed and did righteous deeds will be rewarded — and there will be no fear or grief for them. The ajr in the Quran is closely related to al-thawāb (reward) and al-jazāʾ (recompense). The hadith of the Prophet establishes that Allah has one hundred mercies — of which one is in the world, and the rest are reserved for the Day of Judgment. Al-Ghazālī (Iḥyāʾ, Book of Reward) treats the ajr as the divine gift — the one who works for Allah will receive from Allah what is beyond all human expectation.
shades.hadith_ar: إِنَّ لِلَّهِ مِائَةَ رَحْمَةٍ، أَنْزَلَ مِنْهَا رَحْمَةً وَاحِدَةً
shades.hadith_en: Allah has one hundred mercies, of which He sent down one

meaning.en: To wish, want, will. The root denotes the act of willing — and by extension, the divine will that orders all things.

lexical_analysis.ibn_faris: الْمَشِيئَةُ: إِرَادَةُ الشَّيْءِ. وَشَاءَ الشَّيْءَ: أَرَادَهُ
lexical_analysis.al_raghib: الْمَشِيئَةُ: إِرَادَةُ الشَّيْءِ مَعَ الْإِقْبَالِ إِلَيْهِ. وَالشَّيْءُ: هُوَ الْمَوْجُودُ الَّذِي يُمْكِنُ وُقُوعُهُ

quran_examples.ar: قَالُوا۟ ٱدۡعُ لَنَا رَبَّكَ يُبَيِّن لَّنَا مَا هِىَۦ ۖ قَالَ إِنَّهُۥ يَقُولُ إِنَّهَا بَقَرَةٌۭ لَا فَارِضٌۭ وَلَا بِكۡرٌ ۚ عَوَانٌۢ بَيۡنَ ذَٰلِكَ ۖ فَٱفۡعَلُواْ مَا تُؤۡمَرُونَ
quran_examples.en: They said: Call upon your Lord to make clear to us what she is. He said: He says: She is a cow neither old nor young, but [of] middle age. So do what you are commanded
quran_examples.context: The cow of the Children of Israel

hadith.ar: مَا شَاءَ اللَّهُ كَانَ، وَمَا لَمْ يَشَأْ لَمْ يَكُنْ
hadith.en: What Allah wills happens, and what He does not will does not happen

shades.name_ar: الْمَشِيئَةُ — إِرَادَةُ الشَّيْءِ، مَشِيئَةُ اللَّهِ أَزَلِيَّةٌ
shades.explanation: The mashīʾa (will, willing) in the Quran is the most frequent divine attribute — Allah wills (sha') all things. The verse 2:70 establishes the principle that the cow of the Children of Israel was specified by Allah — «fāfiḍun wa-lā bikrun» (neither old nor young). The mashīʾa in the Quran is closely related to al-irāda (willing) and al-qaḍāʾ (decreeing). The hadith — «mā shāʾa Allāhu kān» — establishes that what Allah wills happens, and what He does not will does not happen. Al-Ghazālī (Jawāhir al-Qurʾān) treats the mashīʾa as the foundational divine attribute — Allah's will is the source of all existence, and nothing happens except by His will.
shades.hadith_ar: مَا شَاءَ اللَّهُ كَانَ، وَمَا لَمْ يَشَأْ لَمْ يَكُنْ
shades.hadith_en: What Allah wills happens, and what He does not will does not happen

meaning.en: To hate, dislike. The root denotes the state of aversion — and by extension, the divine hatred of sin.

lexical_analysis.ibn_faris: الْحَوْبُ: الْمَقْتُ. وَحَابَ الشَّيْءَ: كَرِهَهُ
lexical_analysis.al_raghib: الْحَوْبُ: مَكْرُوهٌ يَلْحَقُ الْإِنْسَانَ. وَقِيلَ: الْإِثْمُ

quran_examples.ar: وَلَقَدۡ جَآءَكُم مُّوسَىٰ مِن قَبۡلُ وَأَنتُمۡ ظَـٰلِمُونَ
quran_examples.en: And Moses had certainly come to you before while you were wrongdoers
quran_examples.context: The coming of Moses to the Children of Israel

hadith.ar: إِنَّ اللَّهَ لَا يَقْبَلُ صَالِحَ الْعَمَلِ مِنَ الْمُرَائِي
hadith.en: Indeed Allah does not accept the righteous deed of the one who shows off

shades.name_en: al-Ḥawb — The Hatred and the Dislike
shades.name_ar: الْحَوْبُ — الْمَقْتُ، مَا يَلْحَقُ الْإِنْسَانَ مِنَ الذَّنْبِ
shades.explanation: The ḥawb (hatred, dislike) in the Quran is the state of aversion — particularly the divine hatred of sin. The verse 2:89 establishes that the Children of Israel had Moses come to them while they were wrongdoers — and their state was one of falsehood. The ḥawb in the Quran is closely related to al-makrūh (hated) and al-muʿaṭṭal (detestable). The hadith — «inna Allāha lā yaqbal ṣāliḥ al-ʿamali mina l-murāʾī» — establishes that Allah does not accept the deed of the one who shows off — the riyaʾ is a form of spiritual ḥawb. Al-Ghazālī (Iḥyāʾ, Book of Sincerity) treats the ḥawb as the inner disease that destroys the deed — the one who seeks the pleasure of people in their worship has the ḥawb in their heart.
shades.hadith_ar: إِنَّ اللَّهَ لَا يَقْبَلُ صَالِحَ الْعَمَلِ مِنَ الْمُرَائِي
shades.hadith_en: Indeed Allah does not accept the righteous deed of the one who shows off

meaning.en: To be noble, generous, honored. The root denotes the state of nobility and generosity — and by extension, the divine generosity.
