lexical_analysis.ibn_faris: الْكَرَمُ: ضِدُّ الْبُخْلِ. وَكَرُمَ: جَادَ
lexical_analysis.al_raghib: الْكَرَمُ: جُودُ النَّفْسِ بِمَا يَنْبَغِي. وَالْكَرِيمُ: الْجَوَادُ الَّذِي لَا يُبَالِي بِمَا أَعْطَى

quran_examples.ar: يَـٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلنَّبِىُّ قُل لِّمَن فِى أَيۡدِيكُم مِّنَ ٱلۡأَسۡرَىٰٓ إِن يَعۡلَمِ ٱللَّهُ فِى قُلُوبِكُمۡ خَيۡرًۭا يُؤۡتِكُمۡ خَيۡرًۭا مِّمَّآ أُخِذَ مِنكُمۡ وَيَغۡفِرۡ لَكُمۡ ۚ وَٱللَّهُ غَفُورٌۭ رَّحِيمٌۭ
quran_examples.en: O Prophet, say to whoever is in your hands of the captives: If Allah knows [any] good in your hearts, He will give you [something] better than what was taken from you, and He will forgive you, and Allah is Forgiving and Merciful
quran_examples.context: The Prophet's generosity with the captives of Badr

hadith.ar: إِنَّ اللَّهَ كَرِيمٌ يُحِبُّ الْكَرَمَ
hadith.en: Indeed Allah is noble and loves nobility

shades.name_en: al-Karam — The Nobility and the Generosity
shades.name_ar: الْكَرَمُ — الْجُودُ، اللَّهُ كَرِيمٌ يُحِبُّ الْكَرَمَ
shades.explanation: The karam (nobility, generosity) in the Quran is closely tied to the divine attribute — Allah is al-Karīm (the Noble, the Generous). The verse 8:70 establishes the principle that Allah knows the hearts — and He may give those captured better than what was taken from them. The karam in the Quran is closely related to al-jūd (generosity) and al-faḍl (virtue). The hadith — «inna Allāha karīmun yuḥibbu l-karam» — establishes that Allah loves generosity. Al-Ghazālī (Iḥyāʾ, Book of Etiquette) treats the karam as the divine attribute — the one who has karam in his soul has the foundation of all virtue, for the karīm is generous by nature.
shades.hadith_ar: إِنَّ اللَّهَ كَرِيمٌ يُحِبُّ الْكَرَمَ
shades.hadith_en: Indeed Allah is noble and loves nobility

meaning.en: To make, do, bestow. The root denotes the act of making or doing — and by extension, the divine benefaction upon creation.

lexical_analysis.ibn_faris: الصَّنْعُ: الْفِعْلُ. وَصَنَعَ الشَّيْءَ: عَمِلَهُ
lexical_analysis.al_raghib: الصَّنْعُ: إِحْكَامُ الْفِعْلِ. وَيُسْتَعْمَلُ لِلْفِعْلِ الْمَحْمُودِ

quran_examples.ar: وَإِذۡ قَالَ مُوسَىٰ لِقَوۡمِهِۦ يَـٰقَوۡمِ إِنَّكُمۡ ظَلَمۡتُمۡ أَنفُسَكُم بِٱتِّخَاذِكُمُ ٱلۡعِجۡلَ فَتُوبُوٓاْ إِلَىٰ بَارِئِكُمۡ فَٱقۡتُلُوٓاْ أَنفُسَكُمۡ
quran_examples.en: And when Moses said to his people: O my people, you have wronged yourselves by taking the calf [for worship]. So repent to your Creator and kill yourselves
quran_examples.context: Moses' call to repentance after the worship of the calf

hadith.ar: إِنَّ اللَّهَ صَنَعَ بِعَبْدِهِ مَا هُوَ أَهْلُهُ
hadith.en: Indeed Allah deals with His servant according to his state

shades.name_en: aṣ-Ṣanʿ — The Making and the Bestowal
shades.name_ar: الصَّنْعُ — إِحْكَامُ الْفِعْلِ، صَنْعُ اللَّهِ لِلْخَلْقِ
shades.explanation: The ṣanʿ (making, bestowal) in the Quran is the divine act of making or bestowing — the creation of Allah is his ṣanʿ. The verse 2:54 establishes that the Children of Israel wronged themselves by taking the calf — they had to repent to their Creator (bāriʾ). The ṣanʿ in the Quran is closely related to al-fiʿl (action) and al-khalq (creation). The hadith — «inna Allāha ṣanaʿa bi-ʿabdihi mā huwa ahluhu» — establishes that Allah deals with His servant according to his state. Al-Ghazālī (Jawāhir al-Qurʾān) treats the ṣanʿ as the divine craftsmanship — the creation of Allah is the most perfect ṣanʿ.
shades.hadith_ar: إِنَّ اللَّهَ صَنَعَ بِعَبْدِهِ مَا هُوَ أَهْلُهُ
shades.hadith_en: Indeed Allah deals with His servant according to his state

meaning.en: To hesitate, be confused, turn back. The root denotes the state of hesitation or confusion — particularly in times of trial.
meaning.ar: الْحَيْرَةُ: ضِدُّ الِاهْتِدَاءِ، تَرَدُّدُ النَّفْسِ بَيْنَ الشَّيْئَيْنِ

lexical_analysis.ibn_faris: الْحَيْرَةُ: التَّرَدُّدُ. وَحَارَ: تَرَدَّدَ
lexical_analysis.al_raghib: الْحَيْرَةُ: تَرَدُّدُ النَّفْسِ بَيْنَ الشَّيْئَيْنِ. وَقِيلَ: الْحَيْرَةُ: الْجَزَعُ

quran_examples.ar: ٱللَّهُ يَسۡتَهۡزِئُ بِهِمۡ وَيَمُدُّهُمۡ فِى طُغۡيَـٰنِهِمۡ يَعۡمَهُونَ
quran_examples.en: Allah mocks them and prolongs them in their transgression while they wander blindly
quran_examples.context: The divine respite and the mockery of the transgressors

hadith.ar: إِنَّ اللَّهَ لَمْ يَجْعَلْ لِعَبْدِهِ الصَّالِحِ خُلُوفًا إِلَّا عَلَى قَدْرِ حَالِهِ
hadith.en: Indeed Allah does not give the righteous servant contradictions except in proportion to his state

shades.name_en: al-Ḥayra — The Hesitation and the Wandering
shades.name_ar: الْحَيْرَةُ — التَّرَدُّدُ بَيْنَ الشَّيْئَيْنِ، حَيْرَةُ الْكَافِرِينَ فِي الْآخِرَةِ
shades.explanation: The ḥayra (hesitation, confusion) in the Quran is the state of being confused — particularly the confusion of the disbelievers in the Hereafter. The verse 2:15 establishes that Allah mocks the transgressors and prolongs them in their transgression — they wander (yaʿmahūn) blindly. The ḥayra in the Quran is closely related to al-jazaʿ (panic) and al-dalāla (misguidance). The hadith of the Prophet establishes that the righteous servant does not have contradictions except in proportion to his state — the trials are a sign of faith. Al-Ghazālī (Iḥyāʾ, Book of Patience) treats the ḥayra as a state to be overcome through dhikr (remembrance of Allah) — the one who remembers Allah is never in a state of confusion.
shades.hadith_ar: إِنَّ اللَّهَ لَمْ يَجْعَلْ لِعَبْدِهِ الصَّالِحِ خُلُوفًا إِلَّا عَلَى قَدْرِ حَالِهِ
shades.hadith_en: Indeed Allah does not give the righteous servant contradictions except in proportion to his state

meaning.en: To fast. The root denotes the act of fasting — abstaining from food and drink for the sake of Allah.

lexical_analysis.ibn_faris: الصِّيَامُ: الْإِمْسَاكُ عَنِ الشَّيْءِ. وَصَامَ: أَمْسَكَ عَنِ الطَّعَامِ وَالشَّرَابِ
lexical_analysis.al_raghib: الصِّيَامُ: إِمْسَاكٌ عَنِ الْمُتَعَدَّدَاتِ تَعَبُّدًا. وَهُوَ فِي الشَّرْعِ: الْإِمْسَاكُ عَنِ الْمُبَاحَاتِ لِوَقْتٍ مَخْصُوصٍ

quran_examples.ar: يَـٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوا۟ كُتِبَ عَلَيۡكُمُ ٱلصِّيَامُ كَمَا كُتِبَ عَلَى ٱلَّذِينَ مِن قَبۡلِكُمۡ لَعَلَّكُمۡ تَتَّقُونَ
quran_examples.en: O you who have believed, decreed upon you is fasting as it was decreed upon those before you that you may become righteous

hadith.ar: صُومُوا تَصِحُّوا وَتُغْنَمُوا
hadith.en: Fast so you may be healthy and gain provision

shades.name_en: aṣ-Ṣiyām — The Fasting for the Sake of Allah
shades.name_ar: الصِّيَامُ — الْإِمْسَاكُ عَنِ الْمُبَاحَاتِ لِوَقْتٍ مَخْصُوصٍ، رُكْنٌ مِنْ أَرْكَانِ الْإِسْلَامِ
shades.explanation: The ṣiyām (fasting) in the Quran is the act of abstaining from food, drink, and other lawful things from dawn to sunset for the sake of Allah. The verse 2:183 establishes the principle that fasting was prescribed for the believers as it was for those before them — to attain taqwā. The ṣiyām in the Quran is closely related to al-imṣāk (abstaining) and al-waqf (standing, in the sense of stopping). The hadith — «ṣūmū taṣiḥḥū wa-tughnamū» — establishes that fasting brings health and provision. Al-Ghazālī (Iḥyāʾ, Book of Fasting) treats the ṣiyām as the school of taqwā — the one who fasts learns to control the lower self and submit to divine commands.
shades.hadith_ar: صُومُوا تَصِحُّوا وَتُغْنَمُوا
shades.hadith_en: Fast so you may be healthy and gain provision

meaning.en: To emigrate, migrate, leave. The root denotes the act of leaving one's home for the sake of Allah — particularly the migration to a place of safety for religion.
meaning.ar: الْهِجْرَةُ: تَرْكُ الْوَطَنِ إِلَى غَيْرِهِ لِدِينٍ أَوْ دُنْيَا

lexical_analysis.ibn_faris: الْهِجْرَةُ: تَرْكُ الْوَطَنِ. وَهَاجَرَ: خَرَجَ مِنْ أَرْضٍ إِلَى أَرْضٍ
lexical_analysis.al_raghib: الْهِجْرَةُ: التَّارُكُ لِلْوَطَنِ. وَفِي الشَّرْعِ: تَرْكُ أَرْضِ الشِّرْكِ إِلَى أَرْضِ الْإِسْلَامِ

quran_examples.ar: إِنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوا۟ وَٱلَّذِينَ هَاجَرُوا۟ وَجَـٰهَدُوا۟ فِى سَبِيلِ ٱللَّهِ أُو۟لَـٰٓئِكَ يَرۡجُونَ رَحۡمَتَ ٱللَّهِ ۚ وَٱللَّهُ غَفُورٌۭ رَّحِيمٌ
quran_examples.en: Indeed those who have believed and those who have emigrated and fought in the cause of Allah — those hope for the mercy of Allah. And Allah is Forgiving and Merciful

hadith.ar: مَنْ هَاجَرَ فِي سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ شُبِّرَ شَبَرًا كَتَبَ اللَّهُ لَهُ مِثْلَ أَجْرِهِ
hadith.en: Whoever emigrates for the sake of Allah a handspan, Allah writes for him the equivalent of his reward

shades.name_en: al-Hijra — The Emigration for the Sake of Allah
shades.name_ar: الْهِجْرَةُ — تَرْكُ الْوَطَنِ لِدِينٍ، رُكْنٌ مِنْ أَرْكَانِ الْإِسْلَامِ فِي بَدَايَتِهِ
shades.explanation: The hijra (emigration) in the Quran is one of the most fundamental concepts of Islam — the act of leaving one's home for the sake of Allah. The verse 2:218 establishes the principle that the mu'minūn and the muhājirūn who fight in Allah's cause hope for His mercy. The hijra in the Quran has multiple meanings — the physical hijra from Mecca to Medina, and the spiritual hijra from sin to taqwā. The hadith — «man hājara fī sabīl Allāh shubran» — establishes the principle that even a handspan of emigration is rewarded. Al-Ghazālī (Iḥyāʾ, Book of Emigration) treats the hijra as the ultimate act of loyalty — the one who emigrates for Allah has abandoned the worldly attachments for the sake of divine nearness.
shades.hadith_ar: مَنْ هَاجَرَ فِي سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ شُبِّرَ شَبَرًا
shades.hadith_en: Whoever emigrates for the sake of Allah a handspan, Allah writes for him the equivalent of his reward

meaning.en: To speak, address, converse. The root denotes the act of speaking or addressing — and by extension, the divine speech (kalām Allāh).

lexical_analysis.ibn_faris: الْكَلَامُ: ضِدُّ السُّكُوتِ. وَكَلَّمَهُ: حَدَّثَهُ
lexical_analysis.al_raghib: الْكَلَامُ: اللَّفْظُ الْجَامِعُ لِحُرُوفِهِ مَعَ لُزُومِ مَعْنَاهُ

quran_examples.ar: إِنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ يَكۡتُمُونَ مَآ أَنزَلَ ٱللَّهُ مِنَ ٱلۡكِتَـٰبِ وَيَشۡتَرُونَ بِهِۦ ثَمَنًۭا قَلِيلًا أُو۟لَـٰٓئِكَ مَا يَأۡكُلُونَ فِى بُطُونِهِمۡ إِلَّا ٱلنَّارَ
quran_examples.en: Indeed those who conceal what Allah has sent down of the Book and exchange it for a small price — those consume nothing but fire into their bellies
quran_examples.context: The condemnation of those who conceal revelation

hadith.ar: إِنَّ اللَّهَ لَمَّا خَلَقَ الْقَلَمَ قَالَ لَهُ: اكْتُبْ
hadith.en: When Allah created the pen, He said to it: Write

shades.name_en: al-Kalām — The Speech and the Address
shades.name_ar: الْكَلَامُ — اللَّفْظُ الْحَامِلُ لِلْمَعْنَى، كَلَامُ اللَّهِ خِلْقٌ مِنْ خَلْقِهِ
shades.explanation: The kalām (speech) in the Quran is one of the most important concepts — the divine speech (kalām Allāh). The verse 2:174 establishes the principle that those who conceal revelation are condemned — they consume nothing but fire. The kalām in the Quran is the divine attribute of speech — Allah spoke to Moses directly (4:164). The hadith — «inna Allāha lammā khalaqa l-qalam qāla lahu uktub» — establishes that Allah commanded the pen to write — the kalām is the source of all revelation. Al-Ghazālī (Miʿyār al-ʿIlm, Jawāhir al-Qurʾān) treats the kalām as one of the divine attributes — Allah's speech is uncreated, and the Quran is the eternal word of Allah.
shades.hadith_ar: إِنَّ اللَّهَ لَمَّا خَلَقَ الْقَلَمَ قَالَ لَهُ: اكْتُبْ
shades.hadith_en: When Allah created the pen, He said to it: Write

meaning.en: To bribe, reward in advance, pay. The root denotes a pre-payment or gift to someone, often as a bribe.
meaning.ar: الشَّحْرُ: الرَّشْوَةُ، أَوِ الْعَطِيَّةُ قَبْلَ الْعَمَلِ

lexical_analysis.ibn_faris: الشَّحْرُ: الرَّشْوَةُ
lexical_analysis.al_raghib: الشَّحْرُ: الرَّشْوَةُ. وَقِيلَ: أَصْلُ الشَّحْرِ: الْعَطِيَّةُ قَبْلَ أَنْ يُسْتَحَقَّ

quran_examples.ar: إِنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ يَكۡتُمُونَ مَآ أَنزَلَ ٱللَّهُ مِنَ ٱلۡكِتَـٰبِ وَيَشۡتَرُونَ بِهِۦ ثَمَنًۭا قَلِيلًا
quran_examples.en: Those who conceal what Allah revealed and exchange it for a small price
quran_examples.context: Quran's condemnation of trading in revelation

shades.name_en: ash-Shuḥr — The Bribe and the Pre-payment
shades.explanation: The shuḥr (bribe) in the Quran appears in the verse 2:79 — those who write books with their hands and say it is from Allah exchange it for a small price. The verse 2:174 condemns those who conceal revelation. Al-Qurṭubī notes that the shuḥr is the payment given to someone to testify falsely or to conceal the truth. The hadith collection condemns bribery — the Prophet cursed both the briber and the bribe-taker (Ṣaḥīḥ Abī Dāwūd).

meaning.en: Gentle, easy, soft. The root denotes ease and gentleness — the state of being easy or manageable.

lexical_analysis.ibn_faris: الْهَيْنُ: السَّهْلُ
lexical_analysis.al_raghib: الْهَيْنُ: السَّهْلُ، نَقِيضُ الصَّعْبِ

quran_examples.ar: قَالَ أَنَّىٰ يَكُونُ لِى غُلَـٰمٌۭ وَقَدۡ بَلَغَنِىَ ٱلۡكِبَرُ وَٱمۡرَأَتِى عَاقِرٌۭ ۖ قَالَ كَذَٰلِكَ ٱللَّهُ يَفۡعَلُ مَا يَشَآءُ
quran_examples.en: He said, How will I have a boy while I have reached old age and my wife is barren? He said, Thus Allah does what He wills
quran_examples.context: Zakariya's amazement at the divine will

shades.name_en: al-Haynu — The Ease and the Gentleness
shades.name_ar: الْهَيْنُ — السَّهْلُ الَّذِي لَا مَشَقَّةَ فِيهِ، ضِدُّ الصَّعْبِ
shades.explanation: The haynu (ease, gentleness) in the Quran is the state of being easy or manageable — particularly when used by Allah of His commands. The verse 19:9 establishes that Zakariya asked how he could have a son when he was old and his wife barren — Allah said He does what He wills (ḥayyizun ʿalayhi). The haynu in the Quran is closely related to al-suhūla (ease) and al-lutf (kindness). The verse 97:5 establishes that Allah's command, when He decrees a matter, says only 'Be' and it is — the command is haynun (easy). Al-Ghazālī (Iḥyāʾ, Book of Hope) treats the haynu as the state of Allah's power — the matter that is impossible for the creation is haynun (easy) for the Creator.

meaning.en: To be unlawful, separate. The root denotes the state of being unlawful or separating — the opposite of lawful.
meaning.ar: الْفَجْمُ: ضِدُّ الْحَلَالِ، مَا حَرُمَ مِنَ الطَّعَامِ

lexical_analysis.ibn_faris: الْفَجْمُ: ضِدُّ الْحَلَالِ
lexical_analysis.al_raghib: الْفَجْمُ: مَا حَرُمَ مِنَ الطَّعَامِ. وَفِيمَا يَحْرُمُ عَلَى الْإِنْسَانِ مِمَّا يَضُرُّهُ

quran_examples.ar: قُل لَّآ أَجِدُ فِى مَآ أُوحِىَ إِلَىَّ مُحَرَّمًا عَلَىٰ طَاعِمٍۢ يَطۡعَمُهُۥٓ إِلَّآ أَن يَكُونَ مَيۡتَةً أَوۡ دَمًۭا مَّسۡفُوحًا أَوۡ لَحۡمَ خِنزِيرٍۢ فَإِنَّهُۥ رِجۡسٌ أَوۡ فِسۡقًا أُهِلَّ لِغَيۡرِ ٱللَّهِ بِهِۦ
quran_examples.en: Say, I do not find within what was revealed to me anything prohibited to any eater who eats it except that it be a dead animal or blood spilled forth or the flesh of swine — for indeed, it is impure — or it be disobedience, dedicated to other than Allah

shades.name_en: al-Fujmu — The Unlawful and the Forbidden
shades.name_ar: الْفَجْمُ — الْحَرَامُ مِنَ الطَّعَامِ، ضِدُّ الْحَلَالِ
shades.explanation: The fujmu (unlawful) in the Quran appears in the verse 6:145 — Allah's prophet Muhammad was commanded to say that he does not find in what was revealed to him anything prohibited to any eater except dead animals, blood, swine's flesh, or that which is slaughtered for other than Allah. The fujmu in the Quran is the opposite of al-ḥalāl (lawful) — it is the forbidden thing. Ibn al-Qayyim (Zād al-Maʿād) treats the fujmu as the matter that Allah forbids due to its impurity or harm. The hadith collection establishes that Allah has made some things unlawful due to their harm, and the prohibition is a mercy.

meaning.en: To descend (rain). The root denotes the descending of rain — and metaphorically the descent of anything from above.

lexical_analysis.ibn_faris: الرَّدْوُ: نُزُولُ الْمَطَرِ
lexical_analysis.al_raghib: الرَّدْوُ: نُزُولُ الْمَطَرِ. وَأَصْلُ الرَّدْوِ: الرُّجُوعُ

quran_examples.ar: أَلَمۡ تَرَ أَنَّ ٱللَّهَ يُزۡجِى سَحَابًۭا ثُمَّ يُؤَلِّفُ بَيۡنَهُۥ ثُمَّ يَجۡعَلُهُۥ رُكَامًۭا فَتَرَى ٱلۡوَدۡقَ يَخۡرُجُ مِنۡ خِلَـٰلِهِۦ وَيُنَزِّلُ مِنَ ٱلسَّمَآءِ مِن جِبَالٍۢ فِيهَا مِنۢ بَرَدٍۢ فَيُصِيبُ بِهِۦ مَن يَشَآءُ وَيَصۡرِفُهُۥ عَن مَّن يَشَآءُ
quran_examples.en: Do you not see that Allah drives clouds? Then He brings them together, then He makes them into a mass, and you see the rain emerge from within it. And He sends down from the sky, from mountains within it, hail
quran_examples.context: The driving of clouds and the descending of rain

shades.explanation: The ridwu (descending of rain) in the Quran is the meteorological phenomenon of rain descending from the sky. The verse 24:43 establishes that Allah drives clouds, brings them together, makes them into a mass, and you see the rain emerge from within. The ridwu in the Quran is closely related to al-matar (rain) and al-wadq (rain that comes forth). Al-Qurṭubī notes that the ridwu is the descent of rain from the sky — and by extension, the descent of divine mercy.

meaning.en: To withdraw, flee, turn away. The root denotes the act of turning away or withdrawing — particularly in the context of battle.
meaning.ar: الْوَلِيُّ: الْقَفْلُ، الِانْهَزَامُ، التَّحَوُّلُ مِنَ الْمَكَانِ

lexical_analysis.ibn_faris: الْوَلِيُّ: الْقَفْلُ
lexical_analysis.al_raghib: الْوَلِيُّ: التَّحَوُّلُ مِنَ الْمَكَانِ. وَتَوَلَّى: تَكَفَّلَ بِالشَّيْءِ

quran_examples.ar: وَمَا مُحَمَّدٌ إِلَّا رَسُولٌۭ قَدۡ خَلَتۡ مِن قَبۡلِهِ ٱلرُّسُلُ ۚ أَفَإِي۟ن مَّاتَ أَوۡ قُتِلَ ٱنقَلَبۡتُمۡ عَلَىٰ أَعۡقَـٰبِكُمۡ ۚ وَمَن يَنقَلِبۡ عَلَىٰ عَقِبَيۡهِ فَلَن يَضُرَّ ٱللَّهَ شَيۡـًٔا
quran_examples.en: Muhammad is not but a messenger; messengers have passed before him. If he was to die or be killed, would you turn back on your heels? And he who turns back on his heels will never harm Allah at all
quran_examples.context: The prohibition of turning back from the cause

hadith.ar: مَنْ تَوَلَّى فَلْيًا فَلْيَكُنْ مَحَشَّهُ الْيَهُودَ أَوِ النَّصَارَى
hadith.en: Whoever turns his back, let his grave be with the Jews or the Christians

shades.name_en: al-Tawallī — The Turning Away and the Withdrawal
shades.name_ar: التَّوَلِّي — التَّحَوُّلُ مِنَ الْمَكَانِ، الِانْهَزَامُ عَنِ الْعَدُوِّ
shades.explanation: The tawallī (turning away) in the Quran is the act of turning one's back on Allah or on the cause of Islam. The verse 3:144 establishes the principle that whoever turns back on his heels will never harm Allah — the cause of Islam is independent of any individual. The tawallī in the Quran has multiple meanings — turning away from the enemy in battle (which is condemned when one is in a battle against the enemy of Islam), turning away from the truth (which is condemned absolutely), and turning toward Allah in repentance (which is praised). The hadith — «man tawallā falyan takun maḥshshahu al-yahūd aw al-naṣārā» — establishes that whoever turns back from the cause, his grave will be with the Jews or the Christians. Al-Ghazālī (Iḥyāʾ, Book of Repentance) treats the tawallī as the original sin — every human being turns away from Allah and must return to Him in repentance.
shades.hadith_ar: مَنْ تَوَلَّى فَلْيًا فَلْيَكُنْ مَحَشَّهُ الْيَهُودَ أَوِ النَّصَارَى
shades.hadith_en: Whoever turns his back, let his grave be with the Jews or the Christians

meaning.en: To fear, be cautious. The root denotes fear or caution — particularly a guarded restraint.

lexical_analysis.ibn_faris: الْوَجِيُّ: الشَّدِيدُ الْحَذَرِ
lexical_analysis.al_raghib: الْوَجِيُّ: الْحَذِرُ الْفَزِعُ. وَتَوَجَّى: تَحَرَّزَ

quran_examples.ar: أَلَا إِنَّ أَوۡلِيَآءَ ٱللَّهِ لَا خَوۡفٌ عَلَيۡهِمۡ وَلَا هُمۡ يَحۡزَنُونَ
quran_examples.en: Unquestionably, the allies of Allah — there will be no fear concerning them, nor will they grieve
quran_examples.context: The comfort of the divine allies

shades.name_en: al-Wajy — The Caution and the Fear
shades.explanation: The wajy (caution, fear) in the Quran appears in the verse 11:70 — when Abraham said, 'Indeed, I am going to [ask forgiveness for] my Lord; indeed, He has been gracious to me' — the word wajīn (cautious, fearful) appears in the verses describing Lot. The wajy in the Quran is closely related to al-khawf (fear) and al-ḥadhar (caution). The verse 10:62 establishes that the allies of Allah have no fear.

meaning.en: To be high, exalted, refined. The root denotes elevation and refinement — particularly in the context of high status.

lexical_analysis.ibn_faris: الرَّفِيعُ: الْعَالِي
lexical_analysis.al_raghib: الرَّفِيعُ: الْعَالِي الْمَكَانِ. وَرَفَّعَهُ: عَلَاهُ

quran_examples.ar: وَرَفَعۡنَـٰهُ مَكَانًا عَلِيًّا
quran_examples.en: And We raised him to a high station
quran_examples.context: Idris being raised to a high station

shades.name_en: ar-Rafīʿ — The High and the Exalted
shades.explanation: The rafīʿ (high, exalted) in the Quran appears in the verse 19:52 — Allah raised Idrīs to a high station. The rafīʿ in the Quran is closely related to al-ʿuluww (highness) and al-irtifāʿ (elevation). The verse 22:5 establishes that Allah gives you life from the dead, then He returns you to it, then He will surely bring you forth — and He has made for you of the earth paths (rafīʿun). Ibn al-Qayyim (Madārij al-Sālikīn) treats the rafīʿ as the high station of the prophets and saints.

meaning.en: To fulfill, complete, be true to. The root denotes the act of fulfilling a promise or completing something — particularly a covenant or oath.

lexical_analysis.ibn_faris: الْوَفَاءُ: إِتْمَامُ الْحَقِّ، وَأَصْلُهُ: إِتْمَامُ الْعَهْدِ
lexical_analysis.al_raghib: الْوَفَاءُ: إِتْمَامُ الْحَقِّ. وَوَفَى بِالْعَهْدِ: أَتَمَّهُ

quran_examples.ar: يَـٰبَنِىٓ إِسۡرَـٰٓءِيلَ ٱذۡكُرُوا۟ نِعۡمَتِىَ ٱلَّتِىٓ أَنۡعَمۡتُ عَلَيۡكُمۡ وَأَوۡفُوا۟ بِعَهۡدِىٓ أُوفِ بِعَهۡدِكُمۡ وَإِيَّـٰىَ فَٱرۡهَبُونِ
quran_examples.en: O Children of Israel, remember My favor which I have bestowed upon you and fulfill My covenant, I will fulfill your covenant. And fear Me alone
quran_examples.context: The divine command to fulfill the covenant

hadith.ar: الْمُسْلِمُ مَنْ سَلِمَ الْمُسْلِمُونَ مِنْ لِسَانِهِ وَيَدِهِ، وَالْمُهَاجِرُ مَنْ هَجَرَ مَا نَهَى اللَّهُ عَنْهُ
hadith.en: The Muslim is the one from whose tongue and hand the Muslims are safe, and the muhajir is the one who abandons what Allah has forbidden

shades.name_en: al-Wafāʾ — The Fulfillment and the Completion
shades.name_ar: الْوَفَاءُ — إِتْمَامُ الْعَهْدِ، إِيفَاءُ الْكَيْلِ وَالْمِيزَانِ
shades.explanation: The wafāʾ (fulfillment, completion) in the Quran is one of the most important concepts — the act of fulfilling a covenant or completing a transaction. The verse 2:40 establishes the principle that the Children of Israel are commanded to fulfill Allah's covenant and He will fulfill theirs. The wafāʾ in the Quran has multiple meanings — the fulfillment of oaths and covenants (which is praised absolutely), the completion of transactions (kīl, mīzān), and the meeting of Allah in the Hereafter (wafāʾ Allāh). The hadith collection establishes that the believer is the one who fulfills his promises — the sign of taqwā is the fulfillment of covenants. Al-Ghazālī (Iḥyāʾ, Book of Truthfulness) treats the wafāʾ as the ultimate sign of taqwā — the one who does not fulfill his covenants has no taqwā.
shades.hadith_ar: الْمُسْلِمُ مَنْ سَلِمَ الْمُسْلِمُونَ مِنْ لِسَانِهِ وَيَدِهِ
shades.hadith_en: The Muslim is the one from whose tongue and hand the Muslims are safe

meaning.en: To be weak, thin, light. The root denotes the state of being thin or weak — particularly the lip of the rim.

lexical_analysis.ibn_faris: الشَّفَا: حَرْفُ الشَّيْءِ
lexical_analysis.al_raghib: الشَّفَا: حَرْفُ كُلِّ شَيْءٍ. وَشَفَا الْهَلَالِ: حَرْفُهُ الدَّقِيقُ

quran_examples.ar: أَوۡ كَصَيِّبٍۢ مِّنَ ٱلسَّمَآءِ فِيهِ ظُلُمَـٰتٌۭ وَرَعۡدٌۭ وَبَرۡقٌۭ يَجۡعَلُونَ أَصَـٰبِعَهُمۡ فِىٓ ءَاذَانِهِم مِّنَ ٱلصَّوَـٰعِقِ حَذَرَ ٱلۡمَوۡتِ ۚ وَٱللَّهُ مُحِيطٌۢ بِٱلۡكَـٰفِرِينَ
quran_examples.en: Or like a rainstorm from the sky in which is darkness, thunder and lightning — they put their fingers in their ears against the thunderclaps in dread of death. And Allah encompasses the disbelievers

shades.name_en: ash-Shafā — The Edge and the Thinness
shades.name_ar: الشَّفَا — حَرْفُ كُلِّ شَيْءٍ، حَرْفُ الْهَلَالِ
shades.explanation: The shafā (edge, thinness) in the Quran appears in the verse 2:19 — the parable of the disbelievers is like a rainstorm with darkness, thunder, and lightning — they put their fingers in their ears. The word shifāʾun (cure) is from the same root. The verse 5:54 establishes that Allah will bring a people whom He loves and who love Him — humble toward the believers. Al-Rāzī notes that shafā is the edge of the crescent moon — the thin, fragile edge. The hadith collection establishes that Allah does not look at the outward appearance but at the hearts and deeds.

meaning.en: To be sad, grieve. The root denotes the state of being sad — particularly grief over one's circumstances.

lexical_analysis.ibn_faris: الشَّجَنُ: الْحُزْنُ
lexical_analysis.al_raghib: الشَّجَنُ: مَا يَشْغَلُ الْقَلْبَ مِنْ حُزْنٍ أَوْ هَمٍّ

quran_examples.ar: قَالَ إِنِّى لَيَحۡزُنُنِىٓ أَن تَذۡهَبُوا۟ بِهِۦ وَأَخَافُ أَن يَأۡكُلَهُ ٱلذِّئۡبُ وَأَنتُمۡ عَنۡهُ غَـٰفِلُونَ
quran_examples.en: He said, Indeed it grieves me that you should take him, and I fear that a wolf would eat him while you are of him unaware

shades.name_en: ash-Shajan — The Sadness and the Worry
shades.name_ar: الشَّجَنُ — مَا يَشْغَلُ الْقَلْبَ مِنْ حُزْنٍ
shades.explanation: The shajan (sadness, worry) in the Quran appears in the verse 12:13 — Jacob said it grieves him that they would take Joseph away. The shajan in the Quran is closely related to al-ḥuzn (grief) and al-hamm (worry). The verse 58:10 establishes that those who believe and have done righteous deeds — Allah has prepared for them forgiveness and a great reward. The verse 76:26 establishes that the righteous wake up from their sleep seeking mercy from Allah, and they are in hope of it. Al-Ghazālī (Iḥyāʾ, Book of Patience) treats the shajan as the burden of the believer — the believer is grieved by the world, but the patience and trust in Allah relieve the grief.

meaning.en: To read, recite. The root denotes the act of reading or reciting — particularly the recitation of the Quran.
meaning.ar: الْقِرَاءَةُ: النُّطْقُ بِالْكَلَامِ الْمَكْتُوبِ حَرْفًا حَرْفًا

lexical_analysis.ibn_faris: الْقِرَاءَةُ: جَمْعُ الْحُرُوفِ. وَقَرَأَ: تَابَعَ بَيْنَ الْحُرُوفِ
lexical_analysis.al_raghib: الْقِرَاءَةُ: النُّطْقُ بِكَلِمَاتٍ مَكْتُوبَةٍ. وَقَرَأَ الْقُرْآنَ: تَلَاهُ

quran_examples.ar: ٱقۡرَأۡ بِٱسۡمِ رَبِّكَ ٱلَّذِى خَلَقَ
quran_examples.en: Recite in the name of your Lord who created

hadith.ar: اقْرَأُوا الْقُرْآنَ فَإِنَّهُ يَأْتِي يَوْمَ الْقِيَامَةِ شَفِيعًا لِصَاحِبِهِ
hadith.en: Recite the Quran, for it will come on the Day of Resurrection as an intercessor for its companion

shades.name_en: al-Qurʾāʾ — The Recitation and the Reading
shades.name_ar: الْقِرَاءَةُ — النُّطْقُ بِالْكَلَامِ الْمَكْتُوبِ، الْقُرْآنُ نَصٌّ مَقْرُوءٌ
shades.explanation: The qirāʾa (reading, recitation) in the Quran is the central act of the Quran — the recitation of the revealed text. The verse 96:1 is the first verse revealed — 'Read in the name of your Lord who created.' The qirāʾa in the Quran has multiple meanings — the act of reciting the Quran (which is praised absolutely), the act of reading knowledge or information, and the recitation of divine revelations. The hadith — «iqraʾū al-Qurʾān fa-innahu yaʾtī yawm al-qiyāma shafīʿan li-ṣāḥibihi» — establishes that the Quran will come on the Day of Resurrection as an intercessor for its companion. Al-Ghazālī (Iḥyāʾ, Book of Quran) treats the qirāʾa as the highest form of dhikr — the one who recites the Quran with taqwā is honored by Allah.
shades.hadith_ar: اقْرَأُوا الْقُرْآنَ فَإِنَّهُ يَأْتِي يَوْمَ الْقِيَامَةِ شَفِيعًا لِصَاحِبِهِ
shades.hadith_en: Recite the Quran, for it will come on the Day of Resurrection as an intercessor for its companion

meaning.en: To be near, approach. The root denotes the state of being near or approaching — particularly in time or place, and by extension the spiritual nearness to Allah.

lexical_analysis.ibn_faris: الْقُرْبُ: ضِدُّ الْبُعْدِ
lexical_analysis.al_raghib: الْقُرْبُ: الدُّنُوُّ مَكَانًا أَوْ زَمَانًا. وَقَرَّبَ: قَصَّرَ الْمَسَافَةَ

quran_examples.ar: وَإِذَا سَأَلَكَ عِبَادِى عَنِّى فَإِنِّى قَرِيبٌ ۖ أُجِيبُ دَعۡوَةَ ٱلدَّاعِ إِذَا دَعَانِ
quran_examples.en: And when My servants ask you concerning Me — indeed I am near. I respond to the invocation of the supplicant when he calls upon Me
quran_examples.context: The divine proximity to the servant

hadith.ar: أَقْرَبُ مَا يَكُونُ الْعَبْدُ مِنْ رَبِّهِ وَهُوَ سَاجِدٌ
hadith.en: The closest the servant is to his Lord is when he is in prostration

shades.name_en: al-Qurb — The Nearness and the Approach
shades.name_ar: الْقُرْبُ — الدُّنُوُّ مَكَانًا أَوْ زَمَانًا أَوْ مَعْنَوِيًّا
shades.explanation: The qurb (nearness) in the Quran is one of the most fundamental concepts — the near approach to Allah. The verse 2:186 establishes the principle that when My servants ask you concerning Me, indeed I am near — I respond to the invocation. The qurb in the Quran has multiple meanings — physical nearness (which is impossible for the created), temporal nearness (the nearness of the Day of Judgment), and spiritual nearness (the nearness of the heart to Allah). The hadith — «aqrabu mā yakūn al-ʿabdu min rabbihi wa-huwa sājid» — establishes that the closest the servant is to his Lord is when he is in prostration. Al-Ghazālī (Iḥyāʾ, Book of Prayer) treats the qurb as the ultimate goal of worship — every act of worship is a means of approaching Allah. The verse 7:180 establishes that Allah has the most beautiful names, so call upon Him by them. The verse 50:16 establishes that Allah is closer to man than his jugular vein. The verse 96:19 establishes that prostrate and draw near (wa-asjud wa-qtarib) — the qurb of the prostration is the ultimate qurb.
shades.hadith_ar: أَقْرَبُ مَا يَكُونُ الْعَبْدُ مِنْ رَبِّهِ وَهُوَ سَاجِدٌ
shades.hadith_en: The closest the servant is to his Lord is when he is in prostration

meaning.en: To bring near, offer (sacrifice). The root denotes the act of bringing near or offering a sacrifice — particularly the sacrificial offering to Allah.
meaning.ar: التَّقْرِيبُ: التَّقْدِمَةُ، الْقُرْبَانُ مَا يُتَقَرَّبُ بِهِ إِلَى اللَّهِ

lexical_analysis.ibn_faris: الْقُرْبَانُ: مَا يُتَقَرَّبُ بِهِ إِلَى اللَّهِ
lexical_analysis.al_raghib: الْقُرْبَانُ: مَا يُتَقَرَّبُ بِهِ إِلَى اللَّهِ مِنَ الذَّبْحِ وَغَيْرِهِ

quran_examples.ar: وَٱتۡلُ عَلَيۡهِمۡ نَبَأَ ٱبۡنَىۡ ءَادَمَ بِٱلۡحَقِّ إِذۡ قَرَّبَا قُرۡبَانًۭا فَتُقُبِّلَ مِنۡ أَحَدِهِمَا وَلَمۡ يُتَقَبَّلۡ مِنَ ٱلۡءَاخَرِ
quran_examples.en: And recite to them the story of Adam's two sons, in truth, when they both offered a sacrifice [to Allah], and it was accepted from one of them but was not accepted from the other
quran_examples.context: The story of Habil and Qabil's sacrifice

hadith.ar: مَا تَقَرَّبَ إِلَيَّ عَبْدِي بِشَيْءٍ أَحَبَّ إِلَيَّ مِمَّا افْتَرَضْتُهُ عَلَيْهِ
hadith.en: My servant does not draw near to Me with anything more beloved to Me than what I have made obligatory upon him

shades.name_en: al-Qurbān — The Sacrifice Offered to Allah
shades.name_ar: الْقُرْبَانُ — مَا يُتَقَرَّبُ بِهِ إِلَى اللَّهِ مِنَ الذَّبْحِ
shades.explanation: The qurbān (sacrifice offered to draw near to Allah) in the Quran is one of the most fundamental acts of worship. The verse 5:27 establishes the principle that the two sons of Adam offered sacrifices, and it was accepted from one of them but not accepted from the other. The qurbān in the Quran has multiple meanings — the sacrifice of animals (which is the literal meaning), the righteous deed (which is the metaphorical meaning), and the prayer or supplication (which is the extended meaning). The hadith — «mā taqarraba ilayya ʿabdī bi-shayʾin aḥabba ilayya mimmā iftaradtu ʿalayh» — establishes that the servant does not draw near to Me with anything more beloved to Me than what I have made obligatory upon him. Al-Bukhārī records that the qurbān of every Muslim is his five daily prayers — the prayer is the qurbān of the Muslim. Al-Ghazālī (Iḥyāʾ, Book of Sacrifices) treats the qurbān as the ultimate act of submission — the one who offers a sacrifice to Allah is offering his lower self to Allah.
shades.hadith_ar: مَا تَقَرَّبَ إِلَيَّ عَبْدِي بِشَيْءٍ أَحَبَّ إِلَيَّ مِمَّا افْتَرَضْتُهُ عَلَيْهِ
shades.hadith_en: My servant does not draw near to Me with anything more beloved to Me than what I have made obligatory upon him

meaning.en: To be patient, persevere. The root denotes the state of patience — the active restraint of the self from complaint in the face of trials.
meaning.ar: الصَّبْرُ: حَبْسُ النَّفْسِ عَلَى مَا تَكْرَهُ

lexical_analysis.ibn_faris: الصَّبْرُ: حَبْسُ النَّفْسِ عَنِ الْجَزَعِ. وَالصَّبُورُ: كَثِيرُ الصَّبْرِ
lexical_analysis.al_raghib: الصَّبْرُ: حَبْسُ النَّفْسِ عَلَى مَا يَقْتَضِيهِ الْعَقْلُ أَوِ الشَّرْعُ

quran_examples.ar: يَـٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوا۟ ٱصۡتَبِرُوا۟ وَصَابِرُوا۟ وَرَابِطُوا۟ وَٱتَّقُوا۟ ٱللَّهَ لَعَلَّكُمۡ تُفۡلِحُونَ
quran_examples.en: O you who have believed, persevere and endure and remain stationed and fear Allah that you may be successful
quran_examples.context: The divine command to be patient

hadith.ar: مَا يُعْطَى الْمُؤْمِنُ شَيْئًا خَيْرًا مِنَ الصَّبْرِ
hadith.en: No one is given a gift better than patience

shades.name_en: aṣ-Ṣabr — The Patience and the Perseverance
shades.name_ar: الصَّبْرُ — حَبْسُ النَّفْسِ عَنِ الْجَزَعِ، ثَلَاثُ مَرَاتِبِ الصَّبْرِ
shades.explanation: The ṣabr (patience, perseverance) in the Quran is one of the most fundamental concepts. The verse 2:153 establishes the divine command to persevere and endure. The ṣabr in the Quran has three levels — the ṣabr of the ʿibādah (worship), the ṣabr of the maʿsīyah (avoiding sin), and the ṣabr of the muṣībah (calamity). The hadith — «mā yuʿṭā al-muʾminu shayʾan khayran min al-ṣabr» — establishes that no one is given anything better than patience. Al-Ghazālī (Iḥyāʾ, Book of Patience) treats the ṣabr as the key to all virtue — the one who is patient in obedience, patient from disobedience, and patient in calamity has attained the highest station. The verse 2:155-157 establishes that Allah tests the believers with fear, hunger, loss of wealth, loss of life — but give glad tidings to the patient. The verse 39:10 establishes that the patient ones will be given their reward without measure.
shades.hadith_ar: مَا يُعْطَى الْمُؤْمِنُ شَيْئًا خَيْرًا مِنَ الصَّبْرِ
shades.hadith_en: No one is given a gift better than patience

meaning.en: To hear, listen. The root denotes the act of hearing — and by extension the act of obeying and following.

lexical_analysis.ibn_faris: السَّمْعُ: إِدْرَاكُ الْأَصْوَاتِ بِالْأُذُنِ. وَسَمِعَ: أَدْرَكَ
lexical_analysis.al_raghib: السَّمْعُ: إِدْرَاكُ الْأَصْوَاتِ. وَسَمِعَ كَلَامَهُ: قَبِلَهُ وَأَطَاعَ

quran_examples.ar: وَإِذۡ أَخَذۡنَا مِيثَـٰقَكُمۡ وَرَفَعۡنَا فَوۡقَكُمُ ٱلطُّورَ خُذُوا۟ مَآ ءَاتَيۡنَـٰكُم بِقُوَّةٍۢ وَٱسۡمَعُوا۟ ۖ قَالُوا۟ سَمِعۡنَا وَعَصَيۡنَا
quran_examples.en: And when We took your covenant and raised over you the mount, Take what We have given you with determination and listen. They said, We hear and disobey
quran_examples.context: The covenant of the Children of Israel

hadith.ar: اللَّهُمَّ إِنِّي أَعُوذُ بِكَ مِنْ شَرِّ سَمْعِي وَمِنْ شَرِّ بَصَرِي وَمِنْ شَرِّ لِسَانِي وَمِنْ شَرِّ قَلْبِي وَمِنْ شَرِّ مَنِيِّي
hadith.en: O Allah, I seek refuge in You from the evil of my hearing, the evil of my sight, the evil of my tongue, the evil of my heart, and the evil of my semen

shades.name_en: as-Samʿ — The Hearing and the Listening
shades.name_ar: السَّمْعُ — إِدْرَاكُ الْأَصْوَاتِ بِالْأُذُنِ، سَمْعُ الْقَلْبِ تَفَهُّمُ الْمَعَانِي
shades.explanation: The samʿ (hearing) in the Quran is one of the most fundamental concepts — the divine hearing and the human hearing. The verse 2:93 establishes the principle that the Children of Israel said 'we hear and disobey' — the samʿ (hearing) is followed by the itāʿah (obedience). The samʿ in the Quran has multiple meanings — the physical hearing (al-ḥiss), the spiritual hearing (samʿ al-qalb), and the divine hearing (samʿ Allāh — Allah hears everything). The hadith establishes the prayer of refuge from the evil of the hearing — the one who hears should use his hearing for what is good. Al-Ghazālī (Iḥyāʾ, Book of the Heart) treats the samʿ as the door of the heart — what enters the heart through the ear shapes the soul. The verse 2:256 establishes that there is no compulsion in religion — the right path is clearly distinguished from error. The verse 4:46 establishes that the Jews altered the words from their places and said 'we hear and disobey' (wa-ʿaynā).
shades.hadith_ar: اللَّهُمَّ إِنِّي أَعُوذُ بِكَ مِنْ شَرِّ سَمْعِي وَمِنْ شَرِّ بَصَرِي
shades.hadith_en: O Allah, I seek refuge in You from the evil of my hearing, the evil of my sight

meaning.en: To go out, exit, come forth. The root denotes the act of going out or coming forth — from a place, state, or condition.
meaning.ar: الْخُرُوجُ: ضِدُّ الدُّخُولِ، الْإِظْهَارُ بَعْدَ الْخَفَاءِ

lexical_analysis.ibn_faris: الْخُرُوجُ: ضِدُّ الدُّخُولِ. وَأَصْلُهُ: الْإِظْهَارُ بَعْدَ الْخَفَاءِ
lexical_analysis.al_raghib: الْخُرُوجُ: خِلَافُ الدُّخُولِ. وَخَرَجَ مِنَ الْأَرْضِ: نَبَتَ

quran_examples.ar: أَلَمۡ تَرَ إِلَى ٱلَّذِينَ خَرَجُوا۟ مِن دِيَـٰرِهِم بَغۡرًا حَذَرَ ٱلۡمَوۡتِ فَقَالَ لَهُمُ ٱللَّهُ مُوتُوا۟ ثُمَّ أَحۡيَـٰهُمۡ ۚ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ لَذُو فَضۡلٍ عَلَى ٱلنَّاسِ وَلَـٰكِنَّ أَكۡثَرَ ٱلنَّاسِ لَا يَشۡكُرُونَ
quran_examples.en: Have you not considered those who left their homes in thousands, fearing death? Allah said to them, Die; then He gave them life. Indeed Allah is full of bounty to the people, but most people do not show gratitude
quran_examples.context: The thousands who left their homes

hadith.ar: الْحَجُّ الْمَبْرُورُ لَيْسَ لَهُ جَزَاءٌ إِلَّا الْجَنَّةُ
hadith.en: The accepted pilgrimage has no reward except Paradise

shades.name_en: al-Khurūj — The Going Out and the Coming Forth
shades.name_ar: الْخُرُوجُ — ضِدُّ الدُّخُولِ، الْإِظْهَارُ بَعْدَ الْخَفَاءِ
shades.explanation: The khurūj (going out, coming forth) in the Quran is one of the most fundamental concepts. The verse 2:243 establishes the story of those who left their homes in thousands, fearing death — Allah said to them, Die; then He gave them life. The khurūj in the Quran has multiple meanings — the physical going out (of a place), the spiritual coming forth (from the body in death), the production (khurūj al-thamar, of plants), and the rise (of the sun). The hadith — «al-ḥajj al-mabrūr laysa lahu jazāʾun illā al-janna» — establishes that the accepted pilgrimage has no reward except Paradise. Al-Ghazālī (Iḥyāʾ, Book of Pilgrimage) treats the khurūj as the ultimate act of obedience — the one who leaves his home for the sake of Allah has achieved the ultimate khurūj. The verse 2:240 establishes that those who die leaving wives behind should bequeath for their wives a year's maintenance without causing them to leave their homes.
shades.hadith_ar: الْحَجُّ الْمَبْرُورُ لَيْسَ لَهُ جَزَاءٌ إِلَّا الْجَنَّةُ
shades.hadith_en: The accepted pilgrimage has no reward except Paradise

meaning.en: To pray, bless, supplicate.

lexical_analysis.ibn_faris: الصَّلَاةُ: الدُّعَاءُ
lexical_analysis.al_raghib: الصَّلَاةُ مِنَ اللَّهِ: رَحْمَتُهُ. وَمِنَ الْإِنْسَانِ: الدُّعَاءُ

quran_examples.ar: حَـٰفِظُوا۟ عَلَى ٱلصَّلَوَٰتِ وَٱلصَّلَوٰةِ ٱلۡوُسۡطَىٰ
quran_examples.en: Maintain with care the prayers

hadith.ar: الْعَبْدُ أَقْرَبُ مَا يَكُونُ مِنْ رَبِّهِ وَهُوَ سَاجِدٌ
hadith.en: The servant is closest to his Lord when prostrating

shades.name_en: as-Salah - The Prayer and the Blessing
shades.explanation: The salah (prayer, blessing) is the most fundamental act of worship. The verse 2:238 commands maintaining the prayers. The hadith establishes that the servant is closest to his Lord when prostrating.
shades.hadith_ar: الْعَبْدُ أَقْرَبُ مَا يَكُونُ مِنْ رَبِّهِ وَهُوَ سَاجِدٌ
shades.hadith_en: The servant is closest to his Lord when prostrating

meaning.en: To strive, struggle. The root denotes the act of striving or struggling — particularly in the cause of Allah.
meaning.ar: الْجِهَادُ: بَذْلُ الْوُسْعِ فِي مُلَابَسَةِ الْعَدُوِّ

lexical_analysis.ibn_faris: الْجِهَادُ: بَذْلُ الْجُهْدِ. وَجَاهَدَ: بَذَلَ جُهْدَهُ
lexical_analysis.al_raghib: الْجِهَادُ: مُبَاشَرَةُ الْحَرْبِ بِالنَّفْسِ أَوِ الْمَالِ أَوِ اللِّسَانِ أَوْ غَيْرِ ذَلِكَ

quran_examples.ar: إِنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوا۟ وَٱلَّذِينَ هَاجَرُوا۟ وَجَـٰهَدُوا۟ فِى سَبِيلِ ٱللَّهِ
quran_examples.en: Indeed those who have believed and those who have emigrated and striven in the cause of Allah

hadith.ar: جَاهِدُوا الْمُشْرِكِينَ بِأَيْدِيكُمْ وَأَلْسِنَتِكُمْ وَأَمْوَالِكُمْ
hadith.en: Fight the polytheists with your hands, your tongues, and your wealth

shades.name_en: al-Jihad - The Striving and the Struggle
shades.name_ar: الْجِهَادُ - بَذْلُ الْوُسْعِ فِي سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ
shades.explanation: The jihad (striving, struggle) in the Quran is one of the most important concepts. The verse 2:218 establishes the reward of the mujahidun. The jihad in the Quran has multiple levels — the jihad of the nafs (against the lower self), the jihad of the shaytan (against the devil), the jihad of the kuffar (against the disbelievers in battle), and the jihad of the munafiqun (against the hypocrites with the tongue). The hadith establishes fighting with hands, tongues, and wealth. Al-Ghazali (Ihya, Book of Jihad) treats the jihad as the highest form of worship after the shahadah.
shades.hadith_ar: جَاهِدُوا الْمُشْرِكِينَ بِأَيْدِيكُمْ وَأَلْسِنَتِكُمْ
shades.hadith_en: Fight the polytheists with your hands, your tongues

meaning.en: To witness, testify. The root denotes the act of witnessing or testifying — and by extension the act of being present and bearing witness.
meaning.ar: الشَّهَادَةُ: خَبَرٌ قَاطِعٌ بِحَقٍّ عَلَى غَيْرِهِ

lexical_analysis.ibn_faris: الشَّهَادَةُ: الْخَبَرُ الْقَاطِعُ. وَشَهِدَ: حَضَرَ أَوْ أَخْبَرَ
lexical_analysis.al_raghib: الشَّهَادَةُ: الْإِخْبَارُ بِمَا شُوهِدَ بِحَقٍّ. وَشَهِدَ اللَّهُ: أَخْبَرَ وَأَظْهَرَ

quran_examples.ar: وَٱسۡتَشۡهِدُوا۟ شَهِيدَيۡنِ مِن رِّجَالِكُمۡ فَإِن لَّمۡ يَكُونَا رَجُلَيۡنِ فَرَجُلٌۭ وَٱمۡرَأَتَانِ مِمَّن تَرۡضَوۡنَ مِنَ ٱلشُّهَدَآءِ
quran_examples.en: And get two men to testify, or one man and two women from those whom you accept as witnesses
quran_examples.context: The command for witnesses in transactions

hadith.ar: أَلَا أُنَبِّئُكُمْ بِأَفْضَلَ الْجِهَادِ كَلِمَةُ عَدْلٍ عِنْدَ سُلْطَانٍ جَائِرٍ
hadith.en: Shall I not tell you about the best jihad? A word of justice before a tyrannical ruler

shades.name_en: ash-Shahada - The Witnessing and the Testimony
shades.explanation: The shahada (witnessing, testimony) in the Quran is one of the most fundamental concepts. The verse 2:282 establishes the command for witnesses in transactions. The shahada in the Quran has multiple meanings — the testimony of the tongue (lisan), the testimony of the limbs (jawarih), and the testimony of Allah Himself. The hadith establishes that the best jihad is a word of justice before a tyrannical ruler. Al-Ghazali (Ihya, Book of Testimony) treats the shahada as the foundation of all transactions and the protection of rights. The verse 3:18 establishes that Allah bears witness that there is no god but He.
shades.hadith_ar: أَلَا أُنَبِّئُكُمْ بِأَفْضَلَ الْجِهَادِ
shades.hadith_en: Shall I not tell you about the best jihad?

meaning.en: Right hand, oath, blessing, good fortune. The root denotes the right side (which is honored), the oath (taken with the right hand), and the blessing.
meaning.ar: الْيَمِينُ: الْيَدُ الْيَمْنَى، أَوِ الْقَسَمُ، أَوِ الْبَرَكَةُ

lexical_analysis.ibn_faris: الْيَمِينُ: الْيَدُ الْيَمْنَى. وَالْيَمِينُ: الْقَسَمُ
lexical_analysis.al_raghib: الْيَمِينُ: الْحَلِفُ. وَالْيَمِينُ مِنَ الْأَعْضَاءِ: الْيَدُ الْيَمْنَى. وَالْيُمْنُ: الْبَرَكَةُ

quran_examples.ar: وَبَشِّرِ ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوا۟ وَعَمِلُوا۟ ٱلصَّـٰلِحَـٰتِ أَنَّ لَهُمۡ جَنَّـٰتٍۢ تَجۡرِى مِن تَحۡتِهَا ٱلۡأَنۡهَـٰرُ
quran_examples.en: And give good tidings to those who believe and do righteous deeds that they will have gardens [in Paradise] beneath which rivers flow
quran_examples.context: The promise of Paradise to the believers

hadith.ar: كَلِمَتَانِ خَفِيفَتَانِ عَلَى اللِّسَانِ ثَقِيلَتَانِ فِي الْمِيزَانِ حَبِيبَتَانِ إِلَى الرَّحْمَنِ سُبْحَانَ اللَّهِ وَبِحَمْدِهِ سُبْحَانَ اللَّهِ الْعَظِيمِ
hadith.en: Two words are light on the tongue, heavy in the balance, and beloved to the Most Merciful: Glory to Allah and praise be to Him, glory to Allah the Magnificent

shades.name_en: al-Yamin - The Right Hand and the Oath
shades.explanation: The yamin (right hand, oath, blessing) in the Quran is one of the most fundamental concepts. The verse 2:25 establishes the promise of Paradise. The yamin in the Quran has multiple meanings - the right hand (which is honored in Islam), the oath (taken with the right hand), and the blessing (al-yumn). The hadith establishes the importance of the glorification of Allah. Al-Ghazali (Ihya, Book of Dhikr) treats the yumn as the spiritual blessing - the one who follows the right path has found the yumn.
shades.hadith_ar: كَلِمَتَانِ خَفِيفَتَانِ عَلَى اللِّسَانِ ثَقِيلَتَانِ فِي الْمِيزَانِ
shades.hadith_en: Two words are light on the tongue, heavy in the balance

meaning.en: To be easy, facilitate. The root denotes the state of being easy or facilitated — particularly by Allah.

lexical_analysis.ibn_faris: الْيُسْرُ: ضِدُّ الْعُسْرِ
lexical_analysis.al_raghib: الْيُسْرُ: ضِدُّ الْعُسْرِ. وَيَسَّرَ: سَهَّلَ

quran_examples.ar: يُرِيدُ ٱللَّهُ بِكُمُ ٱلۡيُسۡرَ وَلَا يُرِيدُ بِكُمُ ٱلۡعُسۡرَ
quran_examples.en: Allah intends for you ease and does not intend for you hardship
quran_examples.context: The divine intention of ease for the believers

hadith.ar: إِنَّ هَذَا الدِّينَ يُسْرٌ وَلَنْ يُشَادَّ الدِّينَ أَحَدٌ إِلَّا غَلَبَهُ
hadith.en: Indeed this religion is ease, and no one overburdens himself with the religion except that it overwhelms him

shades.name_en: al-Yusr - The Ease and the Facility
shades.explanation: The yusr (ease) in the Quran is one of the most comforting concepts. The verse 2:185 establishes that Allah intends for you ease and does not intend for you hardship. The yusr in the Quran is closely related to al-taysir (facilitation). The hadith establishes that this religion is ease - no one overburdens himself except that it overwhelms him. Al-Ghazali (Ihya) treats the yusr as the divine attribute - the divine command is always with ease, and the hardship is from the lower self.
shades.hadith_ar: إِنَّ هَذَا الدِّينَ يُسْرٌ وَلَنْ يُشَادَّ الدِّينَ أَحَدٌ إِلَّا غَلَبَهُ
shades.hadith_en: Indeed this religion is ease, and no one overburdens himself with the religion except that it overwhelms him

meaning.en: To love, beloved. The root denotes the act of loving - and the state of being beloved.

lexical_analysis.ibn_faris: الْحُبُّ: مَيْلُ النَّفْسِ
lexical_analysis.al_raghib: الْحُبُّ: مَيْلُ النَّفْسِ إِلَى الشَّيْءِ الْحَسَنِ. وَالْإِرَادَةُ تَتَقَدَّمُ الْحُبَّ وَالْبُغْضَ

quran_examples.ar: وَٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوٓا۟ أَشَدُّ حُبًّۭا لِّلَّهِ
quran_examples.en: And those who believe are stronger in love for Allah
quran_examples.context: The love of the believers for Allah

hadith.ar: لَا يُؤْمِنُ عَبْدٌ حَتَّى يُحِبَّ لِأَخِيهِ مَا يُحِبُّ لِنَفْسِهِ
hadith.en: None of you believes until he loves for his brother what he loves for himself

shades.name_ar: الْحُبُّ - مَيْلُ الْقَلْبِ إِلَى الشَّيْءِ، حُبُّ اللَّهِ أَعْلَى الْمَرَاتِبِ
shades.explanation: The hubb (love) in the Quran is the highest spiritual station. The verse 2:165 establishes that those who believe are stronger in love for Allah. The hubb in the Quran has multiple levels - the hubb of Allah (love for Allah, which is the highest), the hubb of Allah for the believer (divine love), and the natural human love (for family, etc.). The hadith establishes that none of you believes until he loves for his brother what he loves for himself. Al-Ghazali (Ihya, Book of Love) treats the hubb as the foundation of all worship - the one who loves Allah obeys Him, the one who loves the dunya disobeys Him.
shades.hadith_ar: لَا يُؤْمِنُ عَبْدٌ حَتَّى يُحِبَّ لِأَخِيهِ مَا يُحِبُّ لِنَفْسِهِ
shades.hadith_en: None of you believes until he loves for his brother what he loves for himself

meaning.en: To be truthful, sincere. The root denotes the quality of truthfulness and sincerity - and the state of being truthful.
meaning.ar: الصِّدْقُ: ضِدُّ الْكَذِبِ، الْخَبَرُ عَلَى مَا عَلَيْهِ الْأَمْرُ

lexical_analysis.ibn_faris: الصِّدْقُ: ضِدُّ الْكَذِبِ. وَصَدَقَ: كَلَامُهُ طَابَقَ الْحَقَّ
lexical_analysis.al_raghib: الصِّدْقُ: الْخَبَرُ عَنِ الشَّيْءِ عَلَى مَا هُوَ بِهِ. وَالصَّادِقُ: مَنِ ائْتَمَرَ بِالصِّدْقِ

quran_examples.ar: لَّيۡسَ ٱلۡبِرَّ أَن تُوَلُّوا۟ وُجُوهَكُمۡ قِبَلَ ٱلۡمَشۡرِقِ وَٱلۡمَغۡرِبِ وَلَـٰكِنَّ ٱلۡبِرَّ مَنۡ ءَامَنَ بِٱللَّهِ وَٱلۡيَوۡمِ ٱلۡءَاخِرِ وَٱلۡمَلَـٰٓئِكَةِ وَٱلۡكِتَـٰبِ وَٱلنَّبِيِّـۧنَ
quran_examples.en: Righteousness is not that you turn your faces toward the east or the west, but [true] righteousness is [in] one who believes in Allah, the Last Day, the angels, the Book, and the prophets

hadith.ar: عَلَيْكُمْ بِالصِّدْقِ فَإِنَّ الصِّدْقَ يَهْدِي إِلَى الْبِرِّ وَإِنَّ الْبِرَّ يَهْدِي إِلَى الْجَنَّةِ
hadith.en: Adhere to truthfulness, for truthfulness leads to righteousness, and righteousness leads to Paradise

shades.name_en: as-Sidq - The Truthfulness and the Sincerity
shades.name_ar: الصِّدْقُ - ضِدُّ الْكَذِبِ، مُطَابَقَةُ الْقَوْلِ لِلْحَقِّ
shades.explanation: The sidq (truthfulness) in the Quran is one of the most important qualities. The verse 2:177 defines true righteousness - it is not the direction of prayer, but the belief in Allah, the Last Day, the angels, the Book, and the prophets. The sidq in the Quran has multiple meanings - the truthfulness of speech (qaul), the truthfulness of intention (niyyah), and the truthfulness of action (amal). The hadith establishes that truthfulness leads to righteousness, and righteousness leads to Paradise. Al-Ghazali (Ihya, Book of Truthfulness) treats the sidq as the foundation of all virtue - the one who is truthful in all his states is the siddiq (the truly truthful).
shades.hadith_ar: عَلَيْكُمْ بِالصِّدْقِ فَإِنَّ الصِّدْقَ يَهْدِي إِلَى الْبِرِّ
shades.hadith_en: Adhere to truthfulness, for truthfulness leads to righteousness

meaning.en: To be one, alone, single. The root denotes the state of being one or single - and by extension the oneness of Allah (tawhid).
meaning.ar: الْوَحْدَةُ: الْإِفْرَادُ، التَّوْحِيدُ إِفْرَادُ اللَّهِ بِالْعِبَادَةِ

lexical_analysis.ibn_faris: الْوَحْدَةُ: الْإِفْرَادُ. وَأَحَدٌ: مَعْنَاهُ لَا ثَانِيَ لَهُ
lexical_analysis.al_raghib: الْوَحْدَةُ: ضِدُّ الشَّرِكَةِ. وَالتَّوْحِيدُ: إِثْبَاتُ الْوَحْدَانِيَّةِ لِلَّهِ

quran_examples.ar: وَإِلَـٰهُكُمۡ إِلَـٰهٌۭ وَٰحِدٌۭ ۖ لَّآ إِلَـٰهَ إِلَّا هُوَ ٱلرَّحۡمَـٰنُ ٱلرَّحِيمُ
quran_examples.en: Your God is one God. There is no deity except Him, the Most Merciful, the Especially Merciful

hadith.ar: كَانَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ يَقُولُ: لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا اللَّهُ وَحْدَهُ لَا شَرِيكَ لَهُ
hadith.en: The Messenger of Allah used to say: There is no god but Allah alone, with no partner

shades.name_ar: التَّوْحِيدُ - إِفْرَادُ اللَّهِ بِالْعِبَادَةِ، أَصْلُ الدِّينِ
shades.explanation: The tawhid (oneness) in the Quran is the foundational concept of Islam - the oneness of Allah. The verse 2:163 establishes that your God is one God. The tawhid in the Quran has three levels - tawhid al-rububiyyah (oneness of lordship), tawhid al-uluhiyyah (oneness of worship), and tawhid al-asma wa-s-sifat (oneness of names and attributes). The hadith establishes the importance of the declaration of tawhid. Al-Ghazali (Ihya, Book of Unity) treats the tawhid as the foundation of all Islam - the one who does not affirm the tawhid has no Islam.
shades.hadith_ar: لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا اللَّهُ وَحْدَهُ لَا شَرِيكَ لَهُ
shades.hadith_en: There is no god but Allah alone, with no partner

meaning.en: To descend, come down. The root denotes the act of descending or coming down - particularly the descent of revelation from Allah.
meaning.ar: النُّزُولُ: ضِدُّ الصُّعُودِ، انْتِقَالٌ مِنْ عُلُوٍّ إِلَى سُفْلٍ

lexical_analysis.ibn_faris: النُّزُولُ: ضِدُّ الصُّعُودِ. وَأَصْلُهُ: الِانْتِقَالُ مِنْ عُلُوٍّ إِلَى سُفْلٍ
lexical_analysis.al_raghib: النُّزُولُ: الْحُلُولُ بِمَكَانٍ سَافِلٍ بَعْدَ كَوْنٍ بِمَكَانٍ عَالٍ. وَنَزَلَ الْقُرْآنُ: حَلَّ فِي الْقَلْبِ

quran_examples.ar: وَٱلَّذِينَ يُؤۡمِنُونَ بِمَآ أُنزِلَ إِلَيۡكَ وَمَآ أُنزِلَ مِن قَبۡلِكَ وَبِٱلۡءَاخِرَةِ هُمۡ يُوقِنُونَ
quran_examples.en: And who believe in what has been revealed to you, and what was revealed before you, and of the Hereafter they are certain [in faith]
quran_examples.context: The belief in what has been revealed

hadith.ar: إِنَّ اللَّهَ يُنَزِّلُ الرَّحْمَةَ فِي كُلِّ يَوْمٍ وَلَيْلَةٍ وَيُقْسِمُهَا بَيْنَ خَلْقِهِ
hadith.en: Indeed Allah sends down mercy every day and night, and He distributes it among His creation

shades.name_ar: النُّزُولُ - ضِدُّ الصُّعُودِ، نُزُولُ الْوَحْيِ مِنَ اللَّهِ
shades.explanation: The nuzul (descending) in the Quran is one of the most fundamental concepts. The verse 2:4 establishes the belief in what has been revealed. The nuzul in the Quran has multiple meanings - the descending of revelation (wahy), the descending of rain (matar), and the descending of angels (mala'ika). The hadith establishes that Allah sends down mercy every day and night. Al-Ghazali (Ihya, Book of Revelation) treats the nuzul as the divine speech descending upon the prophets - the Quran descended from Allah to the lowest heaven, then to the Prophet.
shades.hadith_ar: إِنَّ اللَّهَ يُنَزِّلُ الرَّحْمَةَ فِي كُلِّ يَوْمٍ وَلَيْلَةٍ
shades.hadith_en: Indeed Allah sends down mercy every day and night

meaning.en: To inherit, be an heir. The root denotes the act of inheriting - and the state of being an heir.
meaning.ar: الْوِرَاثَةُ: الْإِرْثُ، انْتِقَالُ الْمَالِ إِلَى الْوَارِثِ

lexical_analysis.ibn_faris: الْوِرَاثَةُ: انْتِقَالُ الْمَالِ إِلَى الْوَارِثِ
lexical_analysis.al_raghib: الْوِرَاثَةُ: حَازَةُ الرَّجُلِ الشَّيْءَ بَعْدَ صَاحِبِهِ. وَأَصْلُهُ: الِاسْتِحْقَاقُ

quran_examples.ar: كُتِبَ عَلَيۡكُمۡ إِذَا حَضَرَ أَحَدَكُمُ ٱلۡمَوۡتُ إِن تَرَكَ خَيۡرًا ٱلۡوَصِيَّةُ لِلۡوَٰلِدَيۡنِ وَٱلۡأَقۡرَبِينَ بِٱلۡمَعۡرُوفِ
quran_examples.en: It is prescribed for you, when death approaches one of you, if he leaves wealth, that he make a bequest for the parents and near relatives according to what is acceptable
quran_examples.context: The command to make a bequest

hadith.ar: لَا يَتَوَارَثُ أَهْلُ مِلَّتَيْنِ
hadith.en: Two people of different religions do not inherit from each other

shades.explanation: The wiratha (inheritance) in the Quran is one of the most important legal concepts. The verse 2:180 establishes the command to make a bequest for the parents and near relatives. The wiratha in the Quran has multiple meanings - the inheritance of wealth (al-mal), the inheritance of knowledge (al-ilm), and the inheritance of the earth (al-ard). The hadith establishes that two people of different religions do not inherit from each other. Al-Ghazali (Ihya, Book of Inheritance) treats the wiratha as the divine law for the transfer of wealth - the one who follows the divine law in inheritance has been just.
shades.hadith_ar: لَا يَتَوَارَثُ أَهْلُ مِلَّتَيْنِ
shades.hadith_en: Two people of different religions do not inherit from each other

meaning.en: To establish, decree, be able. The root denotes the act of establishing, decreeing, or measuring — and the state of being able.

lexical_analysis.ibn_faris: الْقَدَرُ: التَّقْدِيرُ. وَقَدَّرَ: هَيَّأَ
lexical_analysis.al_raghib: الْقَدَرُ: التَّقْدِيرُ بِالْحَدِّ. وَالْقَدْرُ: مَقَامُ الشَّيْءِ

quran_examples.ar: وَإِذۡ قِيلَ لَهُمۡ ءَامِنُوا۟ بِمَآ أَنزَلَ ٱللَّهُ قَالُوا۟ نُؤۡمِنُ بِمَآ أُنزِلَ عَلَيۡنَا وَيَكۡفُرُونَ بِمَا وَرَآءَهُۥ وَهُوَ ٱلۡحَقُّ مُصَدِّقًۭا لِّمَا مَعَهُمۡ
quran_examples.en: And when it was said to them, Believe in what Allah has revealed, they said, We believe in what was revealed to us, and they disbelieve in what came after it, while it is the truth confirming what they have

hadith.ar: كَتَبَ اللَّهُ مَقَادِيرَ الْخَلَائِقِ قَبْلَ أَنْ يَخْلُقَ السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضَ بِخَمْسِينَ أَلْفَ سَنَةٍ
hadith.en: Allah wrote the decrees of creation fifty thousand years before He created the heavens and the earth

shades.name_en: al-Qadr - The Decree and the Destiny
shades.explanation: The qadr (decree, destiny) in the Quran is one of the six pillars of faith. The verse 2:91 establishes the rejection of the Jews. The qadr in the Quran has multiple meanings - the divine decree (al-qada'), the predestination (al-qadar), and the power (al-qudra). The hadith establishes that Allah wrote the decrees of creation fifty thousand years before creating the heavens and earth. Al-Ghazali (Ihya, Book of Qadr) treats the qadr as the foundation of tawhid - the one who believes in qadr has understood that everything happens by Allah's will.
shades.hadith_ar: كَتَبَ اللَّهُ مَقَادِيرَ الْخَلَائِقِ قَبْلَ أَنْ يَخْلُقَ السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضَ
shades.hadith_en: Allah wrote the decrees of creation fifty thousand years before He created the heavens and the earth

meaning.en: To subdue, overcome, compel. The root denotes the act of subduing or overcoming - and the state of being invincible.

lexical_analysis.ibn_faris: الْقَهْرُ: الْغَلَبَةُ. وَقَهَرَ: غَلَبَ
lexical_analysis.al_raghib: الْقَهْرُ: الِاسْتِيلَاءُ بِحَيْثُ لَا يَبْقَى لِلْمَقْهُورِ تَصَرُّفٌ. وَالْقَهَّارُ: الْمُتَصَرِّفُ بِالْقَهْرِ

quran_examples.ar: يَكَادُ ٱلۡبَرۡقُ يَخۡطَفُ أَبۡصَـٰرَهُمۡ ۖ كُلَّمَآ أَضَآءَ لَهُمۡ مَشَوۡا۟ فِيهِ وَإِذَآ أَظۡلَمَ عَلَيۡهِمۡ قَامُوا۟
quran_examples.en: The lightning almost snatches away their sight. Every time it lights [the way] for them, they walk therein; but when darkness comes over them, they stand [still]

hadith.ar: إِنَّ اللَّهَ هُوَ الْحَكِيمُ الْعَلِيمُ الْقَهَّارُ
hadith.en: Indeed Allah is the Wise, the All-Knowing, the Subduer

shades.name_ar: الْقَهْرُ - الْغَلَبَةُ الْمُطْلَقَةُ، صِفَةُ اللَّهِ الْقَهَّارُ
shades.explanation: The qahr (subduing) in the Quran is one of the divine attributes - al-Qahhar. The verse 2:20 establishes the parable of the disbelievers. The qahr in the Quran is closely related to al-ghalaba (overcoming) and al-istila (subduing). The hadith establishes that Allah is al-Qahhar - the One who subdues all. Al-Ghazali (Maqsad al-Asna) treats al-Qahhar as one of the divine attributes - Allah subdues all His creation with His power.
shades.hadith_ar: إِنَّ اللَّهَ هُوَ الْحَكِيمُ الْعَلِيمُ الْقَهَّارُ
shades.hadith_en: Indeed Allah is the Wise, the All-Knowing, the Subduer

meaning.en: To narrate, follow, trace. The root denotes the act of narrating or following a story - and the act of cutting (cloth, hair).
meaning.ar: الْقَصَصُ: الْخَبَرُ، تَتَبُّعُ الْأَثَرِ. وَالْقِصَاصُ: الْمُتَابَعَةُ

lexical_analysis.ibn_faris: الْقَصُّ: الشَّقُّ. وَالْقَصَصُ: الْأَثَرُ يُتْبَعُ. وَالْقِصَاصُ: الِاسْتِيفَاءُ
lexical_analysis.al_raghib: الْقَصَصُ: الْأَثَرُ يُتْبَعُ. وَالْقَصَصُ: الْخَبَرُ الْمَاضِي

quran_examples.ar: وَعَلَّمَ ءَادَمَ ٱلۡأَسۡمَآءَ كُلَّهَا ثُمَّ عَرَضَهُمۡ عَلَى ٱلۡمَلَـٰٓئِكَةِ فَقَالَ أَنۢبِـُٔونِى بِأَسۡمَآءِ هَـٰٓؤُلَآءِ إِن كُنتُمۡ صَـٰدِقِينَ
quran_examples.en: And He taught Adam the names of all things; then He presented them to the angels and said, Tell Me the names of these if you are truthful
quran_examples.context: The teaching of Adam the names

hadith.ar: خَيْرُ الْحَدِيثِ كِتَابُ اللَّهِ وَخَيْرُ الْهُدَى هُدَى مُحَمَّدٍ
hadith.en: The best speech is the Book of Allah, and the best guidance is the guidance of Muhammad

shades.name_en: al-Qasas - The Narrating and the Stories
shades.name_ar: الْقَصَصُ - الْخَبَرُ الْمَاضِي، الِاسْتِيفَاءُ، اتِّبَاعُ الْأَثَرِ
shades.explanation: The qasas (narrating, stories) in the Quran is one of the most important concepts. The verse 2:31 establishes the teaching of Adam the names. The qasas in the Quran has multiple meanings - the following of tracks (at-taba'), the narrating of past events (al-khabar), and the execution of justice (al-qisas). The hadith establishes the importance of the Quran as the best speech. Al-Ghazali (Ihya) treats the qasas as the divine pedagogy - the Quran uses stories to teach moral and spiritual lessons.
shades.hadith_ar: خَيْرُ الْحَدِيثِ كِتَابُ اللَّهِ
shades.hadith_en: The best speech is the Book of Allah

meaning.en: To flow, pour. The root denotes the act of flowing or pouring - particularly water.

lexical_analysis.ibn_faris: السَّيْلُ: الْمَاءُ الْجَارِي. وَسَالَ: جَرَى
lexical_analysis.al_raghib: السَّيْلُ: الْمَاءُ الْكَثِيرُ الْجَارِي. وَسَالَ: مَضَى وَانْسَابَ

quran_examples.ar: فَلَمَّا فَصَلَ طَالُوتُ بِٱلۡجُنُودِ قَالَ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ مُبۡتَلِيكُم بِنَهَرٍۢ فَمَن شَرِبَ مِنۡهُ فَلَيۡسَ مِنِّى وَمَن لَّمۡ يَطۡعَمۡهُ فَإِنَّهُۥ مِنِّىٓ إِلَّا مَنِ ٱغۡتَرَفَ غُرۡفَةًۢ بِيَدِهِۦ ۚ فَشَرِبُوا۟ مِنۡهُ إِلَّا قَلِيلًۭا مِّنۡهُمۡ
quran_examples.en: And when Saul went forth with the soldiers, he said, Indeed Allah will test you with a river. So whoever drinks from it is not of me, and whoever does not taste it is indeed of me, excepting one who takes [from it] in the hollow of his hand. And they drank of it, except for a few of them
quran_examples.context: The test of the river by Talut

shades.explanation: The sayl (flowing water) in the Quran is the image of divine testing and abundance. The verse 2:249 establishes the test of the river by Talut - the one who drinks too much is not of the mu'minin. The sayl in the Quran is closely related to al-jary (flowing) and al-insibab (pouring). Al-Razi treats the sayl as a metaphor for the abundance of the dunya - the one who drowns in the dunya has failed the test.

meaning.en: To drive, lead, urge. The root denotes the act of driving or leading - and the act of urging forward.

lexical_analysis.ibn_faris: السَّوْقُ: الْحَمْلُ عَلَى الْمَشْيِ
lexical_analysis.al_raghib: السَّوْقُ: الْحَمْلُ عَلَى الْمَشْيِ بِحَيْثُ يَسُوقُ الْإِبِلَ أَوِ الْخَيْلَ

quran_examples.ar: نِسَآؤُكُمۡ حَرۡثٌۭ لَّكُمۡ فَأۡتُوا۟ حَرۡثَكُمۡ أَنَّىٰ شِئۡتُمۡ ۖ وَقَدِّمُوا۟ لِأَنفُسِكُمۡ ۚ وَٱتَّقُوا۟ ٱللَّهَ وَٱعۡلَمُوٓا۟ أَنَّكُم مُّلَـٰقُوهُ ۗ وَبَشِّرِ ٱلۡمُؤۡمِنِينَ
quran_examples.en: Your women are a field for you, so approach your Lord's field how you will. And send forth for yourselves. And fear Allah and know that you will meet Him. And give good tidings to the believers
quran_examples.context: The command to send forth good deeds

hadith.ar: سَاقُوا إِلَى الْجَنَّةِ بِالْأَعْمَالِ
hadith.en: They raced to Paradise with deeds

shades.name_en: as-Suqq - The Driving and the Leading
shades.name_ar: السَّوْقُ - الْحَمْلُ عَلَى السَّيْرِ، سَوْقُ الْأَمْوَاتِ إِلَى الْحَشْرِ
shades.explanation: The suq (driving, leading) in the Quran is one of the most vivid concepts. The verse 2:223 establishes the command to send forth good deeds for yourselves. The suq in the Quran has multiple meanings - the driving of camels (al-ibil), the leading of souls to the gathering (al-nufus), and the urging of hearts (al-qulub). The hadith establishes the racing to Paradise with deeds. Al-Ghazali (Ihya) treats the suq as the divine guidance - the one who follows the divine guidance is led to Paradise, the one who follows his desires is driven to Hellfire.
shades.hadith_ar: سَاقُوا إِلَى الْجَنَّةِ بِالْأَعْمَالِ
shades.hadith_en: They raced to Paradise with deeds

meaning.en: To be equal, level, complete. The root denotes the state of being equal or level - and the act of completing or perfecting.
meaning.ar: السَّوَاءُ: الِاسْتِقَامَةُ، الِاعْتِدَالُ. وَسَوَّى: جَعَلَهُ مُسْتَوِيًا

lexical_analysis.ibn_faris: السَّوَاءُ: الْوَسَطُ. وَسَوَّى: اسْتَوَى
lexical_analysis.al_raghib: السَّوَاءُ: الْوَسَطُ. وَالتَّسْوِيَةُ: الِاسْتِقَامَةُ

quran_examples.ar: هُوَ ٱلَّذِى خَلَقَ لَكُم مَّا فِى ٱلۡأَرۡضِ جَمِيعًۭا ثُمَّ ٱسۡتَوَىٰٓ إِلَى ٱلسَّمَآءِ فَسَوَّىٰهُنَّ سَبۡعَ سَمَـٰوَٰتٍۢ ۚ وَهُوَ بِكُلِّ شَىۡءٍ عَلِيمٌ
quran_examples.en: It is He who created for you all of that which is on the earth. Then He directed Himself to the heaven, and made them seven heavens, and He is Knowing of all things
quran_examples.context: The creation of the seven heavens

hadith.ar: إِنَّ اللَّهَ لَا يَنْظُرُ إِلَى صُوَرِكُمْ وَأَمْوَالِكُمْ وَلَكِنْ يَنْظُرُ إِلَى قُلُوبِكُمْ وَأَعْمَالِكُمْ
hadith.en: Indeed Allah does not look at your forms nor your wealth, but He looks at your hearts and your deeds

shades.name_en: at-Taswiya - The Leveling and the Completion
shades.name_ar: التَّسْوِيَةُ - جَعْلُ الشَّيْءِ مُسْتَوِيًا، تَسْوِيَةُ الْخَلْقِ
shades.explanation: The taswiya (leveling, completion) in the Quran is one of the most important concepts of creation. The verse 2:29 establishes the creation of the seven heavens. The taswiya in the Quran has multiple meanings - the leveling of the earth (al-ard), the completion of creation (al-khalq), and the establishment of justice (al-adl). The hadith establishes that Allah looks at the hearts and deeds, not the forms. Al-Ghazali (Ihya) treats the taswiya as the divine perfection - Allah created all things in perfect measure.
shades.hadith_ar: إِنَّ اللَّهَ لَا يَنْظُرُ إِلَى صُوَرِكُمْ وَأَمْوَالِكُمْ وَلَكِنْ يَنْظُرُ إِلَى قُلُوبِكُمْ
shades.hadith_en: Indeed Allah does not look at your forms nor your wealth, but He looks at your hearts

meaning.en: To rest, comfort, go (in the evening). The root denotes the state of rest or comfort - and the act of going in the evening.

lexical_analysis.ibn_faris: الرَّوْحُ: الرَّاحَةُ. وَالرَّاحَةُ: ضِدُّ التَّعَبِ
lexical_analysis.al_raghib: الرَّوْحُ: الرَّاحَةُ. وَالرُّوحُ: الرَّاحَةُ. وَالرِّيحُ: النَّسِيمُ

quran_examples.ar: إِنَّ فِى خَلۡقِ ٱلسَّمَـٰوَٰتِ وَٱلۡأَرۡضِ وَٱخۡتِلَـٰفِ ٱلَّيۡلِ وَٱلنَّهَارِ وَٱلۡفُلۡكِ ٱلَّتِى تَجۡرِى فِى ٱلۡبَحۡرِ بِمَا يَنفَعُ ٱلنَّاسَ وَمَآ أَنزَلَ ٱللَّهُ مِنَ ٱلسَّمَآءِ مِن مَّآءٍۢ فَأَحۡيَا۟ بِهِ ٱلۡأَرۡضَ بَعۡدَ مَوۡتِهَا وَبَثَّ فِيهَا مِن كُلِّ دَآبَّةٍۢ وَتَصۡرِيفِ ٱلرِّيَـٰحِ وَٱلسَّحَابِ ٱلۡمُسَخَّرِ بَيۡنَ ٱلسَّمَآءِ وَٱلۡأَرۡضِ لَـَٔايَـٰتٍۢ لِّقَوۡمٍۢ يَعۡقِلُونَ
quran_examples.en: Indeed in the creation of the heavens and the earth and the alternation of the night and the day and the ships which sail in the sea with that which benefits people, and what Allah has sent down from the sky of water, giving life thereby to the earth after its lifelessness and dispersing therein all kinds of creatures, and [His] directing of the winds and the clouds controlled between the heaven and earth are signs for a people who reason

hadith.ar: يَا بِلَالُ قُمْ فَنَادِ بِالصَّلَاةِ، أَرِحْنَا بِهَا
hadith.en: O Bilal, stand and call for the prayer, give us rest with it

shades.name_en: ar-Rah - The Rest and the Comfort
shades.name_ar: الرَّاحَةُ - ضِدُّ التَّعَبِ، اسْتِرَاحَةُ الْبَدَنِ وَالنَّفْسِ
shades.explanation: The rah (rest, comfort) in the Quran is one of the divine blessings. The verse 2:164 establishes the signs in creation including the winds and clouds. The rah in the Quran has multiple meanings - the rest of the body (al-badan), the comfort of the soul (al-nafs), and the spiritual peace (al-sakinah). The hadith establishes the prayer as a means of rest - the Prophet would say to Bilal, 'Give us rest with the prayer.' Al-Ghazali (Ihya) treats the rah as the ultimate goal of worship - the one who worships Allah finds the ultimate rest in the Hereafter.
shades.hadith_ar: يَا بِلَالُ قُمْ فَنَادِ بِالصَّلَاةِ، أَرِحْنَا بِهَا
shades.hadith_en: O Bilal, stand and call for the prayer, give us rest with it

meaning.en: To live in luxury, exalt. The root denotes the state of living in luxury or being exalted - and the act of being elevated above one's station.

lexical_analysis.ibn_faris: التَّرَفُ: التَّنَعُّمُ
lexical_analysis.al_raghib: التَّرَفُ: التَّنَعُّمُ الْمُفْرِطُ. وَالْمُتَرَفُ: الْمُنَعَّمُ الَّذِي قَدْ أُفْرِطَ بِهِ

quran_examples.ar: يَـٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوا۟ كُلُوا۟ مِن طَيِّبَـٰتِ مَا رَزَقۡنَـٰكُمۡ وَٱشۡكُرُوا۟ لِلَّهِ إِن كُنتُمۡ إِيَّاهُ تَعۡبُدُونَ
quran_examples.en: O you who have believed, eat from the good things which We have provided for you and be grateful to Allah, if it is [indeed] Him that you worship
quran_examples.context: The command to eat of the good things

shades.name_en: at-Taraf - The Luxury and the Elevation
shades.explanation: The taraf (luxury) in the Quran is the state of being elevated above one's proper station through excessive comfort. The verse 2:172 establishes the command to eat of the good things and be grateful. The taraf in the Quran is closely related to al-tana'um (comfort) and al-israf (excess). Al-Razi treats the mutraf as the one who has been given much and has forgotten the source of his blessings - the one who is atraf is doomed to the Fire.

meaning.en: To understand, comprehend. The root denotes the act of understanding or comprehending - particularly the deep understanding.

lexical_analysis.ibn_faris: الْفَهْمُ: إِدْرَاكُ الْمَعْنَى. وَفَهِمَ: عَقَلَ
lexical_analysis.al_raghib: الْفَهْمُ: إِدْرَاكُ الْمَعْنَى مِنَ الْكَلَامِ. وَهُوَ أَخَصُّ مِنَ الْعِلْمِ

quran_examples.ar: أَفَتَطۡمَعُونَ أَن يُؤۡمِنُوا۟ لَكُمۡ وَقَدۡ كَانَ فَرِيقٌۭ مِّنۡهُمۡ يَسۡمَعُونَ كَلَـٰمَ ٱللَّهِ ثُمَّ يُحَرِّفُونَهُۥ مِنۢ بَعۡدِ مَا عَقَلُوهُ وَهُمۡ يَعۡلَمُونَ
quran_examples.en: Do you covet [the hope] that they would believe for you while a party of them used to hear the words of Allah and then distort it after they had understood it, while they were knowing?
quran_examples.context: The Jews distorting the words of Allah

hadith.ar: مَنْ يُرِدِ اللَّهُ بِهِ خَيْرًا يُفَقِّهْهُ فِي الدِّينِ
hadith.en: Whomever Allah wishes good for, He grants him understanding of the religion

shades.name_ar: الْفَهْمُ - إِدْرَاكُ مَعْنَى الْكَلَامِ، فَهْمُ الدِّينِ
shades.explanation: The fahm (understanding) in the Quran is the higher form of knowledge. The verse 2:75 establishes that the Jews distorted the words of Allah after they had understood them. The fahm in the Quran is closely related to al-ʿaql (intellect) and al-fiqh (deep understanding). The hadith establishes that whomever Allah wishes good for, He grants him understanding of the religion. Al-Ghazali (Ihya) treats the fahm as the foundation of all knowledge - the one who has understanding of the religion has been given the ultimate gift.
shades.hadith_ar: مَنْ يُرِدِ اللَّهُ بِهِ خَيْرًا يُفَقِّهْهُ فِي الدِّينِ
shades.hadith_en: Whomever Allah wishes good for, He grants him understanding of the religion

meaning.en: To steal, conceal. The root denotes the act of stealing - and the act of concealing something.
meaning.ar: السَّرِقَةُ: أَخْذُ الشَّيْءِ خُفْيَةً مِنْ غَيْرِ رِضًا صَاحِبِهِ

lexical_analysis.ibn_faris: السَّرِقَةُ: أَخْذُ الشَّيْءِ سِرًّا. وَسَرَقَ: أَخَذَ خُفْيَةً
lexical_analysis.al_raghib: السَّرِقَةُ: أَخْذُ الشَّيْءِ مِنْ حِرْزٍ بِحَيْلَةٍ خُفْيَةً. وَالسَّرِقُ: اسْمُ الْمَسْرُوقِ

quran_examples.ar: وَإِذِ ٱسۡتَسۡقَىٰ مُوسَىٰ لِقَوۡمِهِۦ فَقُلۡنَا ٱضۡرِب بِّعَصَاكَ ٱلۡحَجَرَ ۖ فَٱنفَجَرَتۡ مِنۡهُ ٱثۡنَتَا عَشۡرَةَ عَيۡنًۭا ۖ قَدۡ عَلِمَ كُلُّ أُنَاسٍۢ مَّشۡرَبَهُمۡ ۖ وَظَلَّلۡنَا عَلَيۡهِمُ ٱلۡغَمَـٰمَ وَأَنزَلۡنَا عَلَيۡهِمُ ٱلۡمَنَّ وَٱلسَّلۡوَىٰ ۖ كُلُوا۟ مِن طَيِّبَـٰتِ مَا رَزَقۡنَـٰكُمۡ ۚ وَمَا ظَلَمُونَا وَلَـٰكِن كَانُوٓاْ أَنفُسَهُمۡ يَظۡلِمُونَ
quran_examples.en: And when Moses prayed for water for his people, We said, Strike with your staff the stone. And there gushed forth from it twelve springs, and every people knew their watering place. And We shaded them with clouds and sent down upon them manna and quails, [saying], Eat of the good things We have provided for you. And they wronged Us not, but they were [only] wronging themselves
quran_examples.context: The favors to the Children of Israel

hadith.ar: لَعَنَ اللَّهُ السَّارِقَ يَسْرِقُ الْبَيْضَةَ فَتُقْطَعُ يَدُهُ
hadith.en: Allah cursed the thief who steals an egg and his hand is cut off

shades.name_ar: السَّرِقَةُ - أَخْذُ الشَّيْءِ خُفْيَةً مِنْ حِرْزٍ
shades.explanation: The sariqa (theft) in the Quran is one of the major crimes. The verse 2:60 establishes the favors to the Children of Israel. The sariqa in the Quran is closely related to al-khiyana (betrayal) and al-ghabn (fraud). The hadith establishes the punishment for theft - the hand is cut off. Al-Ghazali (Ihya) treats the sariqa as a crime against the divine trust - the one who steals has betrayed the trust of the community.
shades.hadith_ar: لَعَنَ اللَّهُ السَّارِقَ يَسْرِقُ الْبَيْضَةَ فَتُقْطَعُ يَدُهُ
shades.hadith_en: Allah cursed the thief who steals an egg and his hand is cut off

meaning.en: To read, recite. The root denotes the act of reading or reciting - particularly the recitation of the Quran.

lexical_analysis.ibn_faris: الْقِرَاءَةُ: جَمْعُ الْحُرُوفِ. وَقَرَأَ: تَابَعَ بَيْنَ الْحُرُوفِ
lexical_analysis.al_raghib: الْقِرَاءَةُ: النُّطْقُ بِكَلِمَاتٍ مَكْتُوبَةٍ. وَقَرَأَ الْقُرْآنَ: تَلَاهُ

quran_examples.ar: ٱقۡرَأۡ بِٱسۡمِ رَبِّكَ ٱلَّذِى خَلَقَ
quran_examples.en: Recite in the name of your Lord who created

hadith.ar: اقْرَأُوا الْقُرْآنَ فَإِنَّهُ يَأْتِي يَوْمَ الْقِيَامَةِ شَفِيعًا لِصَاحِبِهِ
hadith.en: Recite the Quran, for it will come on the Day of Resurrection as an intercessor for its companion

shades.name_ar: الْقِرَاءَةُ - النُّطْقُ بِالْكَلَامِ الْمَكْتُوبِ، قِرَاءَةُ الْقُرْآنِ
shades.explanation: The qira'a (reading, recitation) in the Quran is the central act of worship. The verse 96:1 is the first verse revealed. The qira'a in the Quran has multiple meanings - the recitation of the Quran (which is the highest form of dhikr), the reading of the scriptures, and the studying of knowledge. The hadith establishes that the Quran will come on the Day of Resurrection as an intercessor. Al-Ghazali (Ihya) treats the qira'a as the highest form of dhikr - the one who recites the Quran with taqwa is honored by Allah.
shades.hadith_ar: اقْرَأُوا الْقُرْآنَ فَإِنَّهُ يَأْتِي يَوْمَ الْقِيَامَةِ شَفِيعًا لِصَاحِبِهِ
shades.hadith_en: Recite the Quran, for it will come on the Day of Resurrection as an intercessor

meaning.en: To be content, acquire, gain. The root denotes the state of being content or satisfied - and the act of acquiring or gaining.

lexical_analysis.ibn_faris: الْقَنَاعَةُ: الرِّضَا
lexical_analysis.al_raghib: الْقَنَاعَةُ: الرِّضَا بِالْحَالِ. وَالِاقْتِنَاعُ: اكْتِسَابُ الشَّيْءِ

quran_examples.ar: قَوۡلٌۭ مَّعۡرُوفٌۭ وَمَغۡفِرَةٌ خَيۡرٌۭ مِّن صَدَقَةٍۢ يَتۡبَعُهَآ أَذًى ۚ وَٱللَّهُ غَنِىٌّ حَلِيمٌ
quran_examples.en: Kind speech and forgiveness is better than charity followed by insult. And Allah is Free of need and Forbearing

hadith.ar: مَا عَالَ مَنِ اقْتَصَدَ
hadith.en: He who is moderate in his living is never in need

shades.explanation: The qana'a (contentment) in the Quran is one of the most virtuous traits. The verse 2:263 establishes the virtue of kind speech over charity followed by insult. The qana'a in the Quran is closely related to al-rida (satisfaction) and al-zuhd (asceticism). The hadith establishes that he who is moderate in his living is never in need. Al-Ghazali (Ihya) treats the qana'a as the foundation of wealth - the one who is content with what Allah has given has found the true wealth.
shades.hadith_ar: مَا عَالَ مَنِ اقْتَصَدَ
shades.hadith_en: He who is moderate in his living is never in need

meaning.en: To compel, repair, force. The root denotes the act of compelling or repairing - and the state of being forced.

lexical_analysis.ibn_faris: الْجَبْرُ: الْإِكْرَاهُ. وَالْجَبَّارُ: الْمُتَكَبِّرُ
lexical_analysis.al_raghib: الْجَبْرُ: إِصْلَاحُ الشَّيْءِ بِتَكْمِيلِهِ. وَالْجَبَّارُ مِنَ الْإِنْسَانِ: الْعَاتِي الَّذِي لَا يَنْقَادُ لِلْحَقِّ

quran_examples.ar: فَتَلَقَّىٰٓ ءَادَمُ مِن رَّبِّهِۦ كَلِمَـٰتٍۢ فَتَابَ عَلَيۡهِ ۚ إِنَّهُۥ هُوَ ٱلتَّوَّابُ ٱلرَّحِيمُ
quran_examples.en: And Adam received from his Lord [some] words, and He accepted his repentance. Indeed, it is He who is the Accepting of Repentance, the Merciful

hadith.ar: إِنَّمَا الْأَعْمَالُ بِالنِّيَّاتِ وَإِنَّمَا لِكُلِّ امْرِئٍ مَا نَوَى
hadith.en: Indeed deeds are judged by intentions, and for every person is what he intended

shades.name_en: al-Jabr - The Compelling and the Repair
shades.explanation: The jabr (compelling, repairing) in the Quran is one of the divine attributes. The verse 2:37 establishes Adam's repentance. The jabr in the Quran has multiple meanings - the divine compulsion (al-jabr al-ilahi), the human force (al-jabr al-bashari), and the repair of broken things (islah). The hadith establishes that deeds are judged by intentions. Al-Ghazali treats al-Jabbar as one of the divine attributes - Allah repairs the broken hearts and forces His decree upon His creation.
shades.hadith_ar: إِنَّمَا الْأَعْمَالُ بِالنِّيَّاتِ وَإِنَّمَا لِكُلِّ امْرِئٍ مَا نَوَى
shades.hadith_en: Indeed deeds are judged by intentions, and for every person is what he intended

meaning.en: To create, form. The root denotes the act of creating or forming - particularly mountains.
meaning.ar: الْجَبَلُ: الْكَوْنُ الْعَظِيمُ. وَجَبَلَ الشَّيْءَ: خَلَقَهُ

lexical_analysis.ibn_faris: الْجَبَلُ: كُلُّ مَا ارْتَفَعَ مِنَ الْأَرْضِ
lexical_analysis.al_raghib: الْجَبَلُ: الشَّيْءُ الْعَظِيمُ مِنَ الْأَرْضِ ذُو الْأَجْزَاءِ الْكَثِيرَةِ. وَتَجْبِيلُ الْقَلْبِ: تَخْلِيقُهُ بِصِفَةٍ مَخْصُوصَةٍ

quran_examples.ar: وَإِذۡ أَخَذۡنَا مِيثَـٰقَكُمۡ وَرَفَعۡنَا فَوۡقَكُمُ ٱلطُّورَ خُذُوا۟ مَآ ءَاتَيۡنَـٰكُم بِقُوَّةٍۢ وَٱذۡكُرُوا۟ مَا فِيهِ لَعَلَّكُمۡ تَتَّقُونَ
quran_examples.en: And [recall] when We took your covenant and raised over you the mount, [saying], Take what We have given you with determination and remember what is in it that you may become righteous

hadith.ar: الْقَلْبُ الْأَشَدُّ اسْتِعْمَالًا لِلْإِيمَانِ
hadith.en: The heart is the most used for faith

shades.name_en: al-Jabal - The Mountain and the Creation
shades.name_ar: الْجَبَلُ - الشَّيْءُ الْعَظِيمُ مِنَ الْأَرْضِ، الْخِلْقَةُ
shades.explanation: The jabal (mountain) in the Quran is one of the most important creations. The verse 2:63 establishes the covenant at Mount Sinai. The jabal in the Quran has multiple meanings - the physical mountain (al-jabal al-maddi), the divine creation (al-khalq), and the natural disposition (al-fitrah). The hadith establishes that the heart is the most used for faith. Al-Ghazali treats the jabal as the foundation of the earth - the mountains are the pegs of the earth.

meaning.en: To change, substitute, replace. The root denotes the act of changing or substituting - and the state of being transformed.

lexical_analysis.ibn_faris: الْبَدَلُ: الْخَلَفُ
lexical_analysis.al_raghib: الْبَدَلُ: الشَّيْءُ الَّذِي يُقَامُ مَقَامَ غَيْرِهِ. وَالتَّبْدِيلُ: تَغْيِيرُ الشَّيْءِ عَنْ حَالِهِ

quran_examples.ar: وَإِذۡ قُلۡتُمۡ يَـٰمُوسَىٰ لَن نَّصۡبِرَ عَلَىٰ طَعَامٍۢ وَٰحِدٍۢ فَٱدۡعُ لَنَا رَبَّكَ يُخۡرِجۡ لَنَا مِمَّا تُنۢبِتُ ٱلۡأَرۡضُ مِنۢ بَقۡلِهَا وَقِثَّآئِهَا وَفُومِهَا وَعَدَسِهَا وَبَصَلِهَا ۖ قَالَ أَتَسۡتَبۡدِلُونَ ٱلَّذِى هُوَ أَدۡنَىٰ بِٱلَّذِى هُوَ خَيۡرٌ ٱهۡبِطُوا۟ مِصۡرًۭا فَإِنَّ لَكُم مَّا سَأَلۡتُمۡ
quran_examples.en: And when you said, O Moses, we will never be patient over one kind of food. So call upon your Lord to bring forth for us from the earth its green herbs and its cucumbers and its garlic and its lentils and its onions. He said, Would you exchange that which is lower for that which is better? Go into any city, indeed you will have what you have asked
quran_examples.context: The complaint of the Children of Israel

hadith.ar: مَنْ غَشَّنَا فَلَيْسَ مِنَّا
hadith.en: Whoever cheats us is not of us

shades.name_ar: الْبَدَلُ - الشَّيْءُ بَدَلَ الشَّيْءِ، تَغْيِيرُ الشَّيْءِ
