meaning.en: To be stingy, miserly. The root denotes the state of being stingy or miserly - and the refusal to give.
meaning.ar: الْبُخْلُ: ضِدُّ الْجُودِ، ضِيقُ النَّفْسِ عَنِ الْإِنْفَاقِ

lexical_analysis.ibn_faris: الْبُخْلُ: ضِيقُ النَّفْسِ عَنِ الْإِنْفَاقِ
lexical_analysis.al_raghib: الْبُخْلُ: ضِيقُ النَّفْسِ عَنِ الْإِنْفَاقِ لِمَا يَجِبُ إِنْفَاقُهُ. وَالْبَخِيلُ: ضِدُّ الْجَوَادِ

quran_examples.ar: يَـٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوٓاْ أَنفِقُوا۟ مِن طَيِّبَـٰتِ مَا كَسَبۡتُمۡ وَمِمَّآ أَخۡرَجۡنَا لَكُم مِّنَ ٱلۡأَرۡضِ ۖ وَلَا تَيَمَّمُوا۟ ٱلۡخَبِيثَ مِنۡهُ تُنفِقُونَ
quran_examples.en: O you who have believed, spend of the good things which you have earned and of that which We have produced for you from the earth. And do not aim toward spending the bad of it
quran_examples.context: The command to spend in charity

hadith.ar: سُبْحَانَ اللَّهِ وَبِحَمْدِهِ سُبْحَانَ اللَّهِ الْعَظِيمِ
hadith.en: Glory to Allah and praise be to Him, glory to Allah the Magnificent

shades.explanation: The bukhl (stinginess) in the Quran is one of the major sins. The verse 2:267 establishes the command to spend in charity of the good things. The bukhl in the Quran has multiple meanings - the stinginess of wealth (bukhl al-mal), the stinginess of knowledge (bukhl al-'ilm), and the stinginess of greeting (bukhl al-salam). The hadith establishes the glorification of Allah. Al-Ghazali (Ihya) treats the bukhl as the disease of the soul - the one who overcomes bukhl has found the ultimate generosity.
shades.hadith_ar: سُبْحَانَ اللَّهِ وَبِحَمْدِهِ
shades.hadith_en: Glory to Allah and praise be to Him

meaning.en: To forbid, drive away, repel. The root denotes the act of forbidding or driving away - particularly from the truth.

lexical_analysis.ibn_faris: النَّهْيُ: ضِدُّ الْأَمْرِ
lexical_analysis.al_raghib: النَّهْيُ: الطَّلَبُ بِالتَّرْكِ. وَالنَّهْرُ: الطَّرْدُ بِشِدَّةٍ

quran_examples.ar: وَإِذۡ قُلۡتُمۡ يَـٰمُوسَىٰ لَن نَّصۡبِرَ عَلَىٰ طَعَامٍۢ وَٰحِدٍۢ
quran_examples.en: And when you said, O Moses, we will never be patient over one kind of food
quran_examples.context: The complaint of the Children of Israel

hadith.ar: إِذَا أَمَرْتُكُمْ بِأَمْرٍ فَأْتُوا مِنْهُ مَا اسْتَطَعْتُمْ
hadith.en: When I command you to do something, do of it what you are able

shades.explanation: The nahy (forbidding) in the Quran is one of the divine acts. The verse 2:61 establishes the complaint of the Children of Israel. The nahy in the Quran has multiple meanings - the divine forbidding (al-nahy al-ilahi), the human forbidding (al-nahy al-bashari), and the self-forbidding (al-nahy al-nafsi). The hadith establishes that when the Prophet commands you to do something, do of it what you are able. Al-Ghazali treats the nahy as the divine prohibition - the one who avoids what Allah has forbidden has found the ultimate taqwa.
shades.hadith_ar: إِذَا أَمَرْتُكُمْ بِأَمْرٍ فَأْتُوا مِنْهُ مَا اسْتَطَعْتُمْ
shades.hadith_en: When I command you to do something, do of it what you are able

meaning.en: To pair, marry, match. The root denotes the act of pairing or matching - and the state of being married.

lexical_analysis.ibn_faris: الزَّوْجُ: النَّظِيرُ. وَتَزَوَّجَ: اتَّخَذَ زَوْجَةً
lexical_analysis.al_raghib: الزَّوْجُ: كُلُّ وَاحِدٍ مِنْ خِلَافَيِ الشَّيْءِ. وَالزَّوْجَةُ: الْمَرْأَةُ

quran_examples.ar: فَإِن طَلَّقَهَا فَلَا تَحِلُّ لَهُۥ مِنۢ بَعۡدُ حَتَّىٰ تَنكِحَ زَوۡجًا غَيۡرَهُۥ
quran_examples.en: And if he divorces her, she is not lawful to him afterward until she marries a husband other than him
quran_examples.context: The ruling on remarriage after divorce

hadith.ar: الْإِسْلَامُ بُنِيَ عَلَى خَمْسٍ
hadith.en: Islam is built on five

shades.name_ar: الزَّوْجُ - النَّظِيرُ، كُلُّ وَاحِدٍ مِنِ اثْنَيْنِ
shades.explanation: The zawj (pair, mate) in the Quran is one of the divine creations. The verse 2:230 establishes the ruling on remarriage after divorce. The zawj in the Quran has multiple meanings - the husband (al-zawj al-rajul), the wife (al-zawj al-mar'a), and the pair of everything (al-zawj min al-ashya'). The hadith establishes the five pillars of Islam. Al-Ghazali treats the zawj as the divine pairing - the one who finds the righteous zawj has been blessed by Allah.
shades.hadith_ar: الْإِسْلَامُ بُنِيَ عَلَى خَمْسٍ
shades.hadith_en: Islam is built on five

meaning.en: To repent, return. The root denotes the act of repenting or returning - and the divine acceptance of repentance.

lexical_analysis.ibn_faris: التَّوْبَةُ: الرُّجُوعُ عَنِ الذَّنْبِ
lexical_analysis.al_raghib: التَّوْبَةُ: الرُّجُوعُ عَنِ الْمَعْصِيَةِ إِلَى الطَّاعَةِ. وَتَابَ اللَّهُ عَلَى عَبْدِهِ: رَجَعَ عَلَيْهِ بِرَحْمَتِهِ

quran_examples.ar: فَتَلَقَّىٰٓ ءَادَمُ مِن رَّبِّهِۦ كَلِمَـٰتٍۢ فَتَابَ عَلَيۡهِ ۚ إِنَّهُۥ هُوَ ٱلتَّوَّابُ ٱلرَّحِيمُ
quran_examples.en: And Adam received from his Lord [some] words, and He accepted his repentance. Indeed, it is He who is the Accepting of Repentance, the Merciful

hadith.ar: إِنَّ اللَّهَ يَقْبَلُ تَوْبَةَ الْعَبْدِ مَا لَمْ يُغَرْغِرْ
hadith.en: Indeed Allah accepts the repentance of His servant as long as he does not reach the death rattle

shades.name_ar: التَّوْبَةُ - الرُّجُوعُ عَنِ الذَّنْبِ إِلَى الطَّاعَةِ
shades.explanation: The tawba (repentance) in the Quran is one of the most fundamental concepts. The verse 2:37 establishes Adam's repentance - Allah accepted his repentance. The tawba in the Quran has multiple meanings - the human repentance (al-tawba al-bashariyyah), the divine acceptance (al-tawba al-ilahiyyah), and the turning of the heart (al-tawba al-qalbiyyah). The hadith establishes that Allah accepts the repentance of His servant as long as he does not reach the death rattle. Al-Ghazali (Ihya, Book of Repentance) treats the tawba as the return to Allah - the one who repents has found the ultimate salvation.
shades.hadith_ar: إِنَّ اللَّهَ يَقْبَلُ تَوْبَةَ الْعَبْدِ مَا لَمْ يُغَرْغِرْ
shades.hadith_en: Indeed Allah accepts the repentance of His servant as long as he does not reach the death rattle

meaning.en: To divide, distribute, swear. The root denotes the act of dividing or distributing - and the act of swearing.

lexical_analysis.ibn_faris: الْقِسْمَةُ: التَّقْسِيمُ. وَقَسَمَ: حَلَفَ
lexical_analysis.al_raghib: الْقِسْمَةُ: التَّقْسِيمُ. وَالْقَسَمُ: الْيَمِينُ

quran_examples.ar: ٱلَّذِينَ يَأۡكُلُونَ ٱلرِّبَوٰا۟ لَا يَقُومُونَ إِلَّا كَمَا يَقُومُ ٱلَّذِى يَتَخَبَّطُهُ ٱلشَّيۡطَـٰنُ مِنَ ٱلۡمَسِّ ۚ ذَٰلِكَ بِأَنَّهُمۡ قَالُوٓاْ إِنَّمَا ٱلۡبَيۡعُ مِثۡلُ ٱلرِّبَوٰا۟ ۗ وَأَحَلَّ ٱللَّهُ ٱلۡبَيۡعَ وَحَرَّمَ ٱلرِّبَوٰا۟
quran_examples.en: Those who consume interest cannot stand [on the Day of Resurrection] except as one stands who is being beaten by Satan into insanity. That is because they say, Trade is [just] like interest. But Allah has permitted trade and has forbidden interest

hadith.ar: إِنَّمَا الْأَعْمَالُ بِالنِّيَّاتِ
hadith.en: Indeed deeds are judged by intentions

shades.explanation: The qasm (dividing, swearing) in the Quran is one of the divine acts. The verse 2:275 establishes the prohibition of interest. The qasm in the Quran has multiple meanings - the divine division (al-qasm al-ilahi - the distribution of provision), the human division (al-qasm al-bashari), and the oath (al-qasm al-yamin). The hadith establishes that deeds are judged by intentions. Al-Ghazali treats the qasm as the divine decree - the distribution of provision and fate is from Allah alone.
shades.hadith_ar: إِنَّمَا الْأَعْمَالُ بِالنِّيَّاتِ
shades.hadith_en: Indeed deeds are judged by intentions

meaning.en: To be half, just. The root denotes the state of being half - and the act of being just.

lexical_analysis.ibn_faris: النِّصْفُ: نِصْفُ الشَّيْءِ. وَالنَّصَفَةُ: الْعَدْلُ
lexical_analysis.al_raghib: النِّصْفُ: نِصْفُ الشَّيْءِ. وَالنَّصَفُ: الْعَدْلُ. وَالنَّصِيفُ: حِجَارَةٌ تُنْصَبُ فِي الْمَاءِ

quran_examples.ar: وَإِن طَلَّقۡتُمُوهُنَّ مِن قَبۡلِ أَن تَمَسُّوهُنَّ وَقَدۡ فَرَضۡتُمۡ لَهُنَّ فَرِيضَةًۭ فَنِصۡفُ مَا فَرَضۡتُمۡ إِلَّآ أَن يَعۡفُونَ أَوۡ يَعۡفُوَا۟ ٱلَّذِى بِيَدِهِۦ عُقۡدَةُ ٱلنِّكَاحِ
quran_examples.en: And if you divorce them before you have touched them and you have already specified for them an obligation, then [give] half of what you specified - unless they forego the payment or the one in whose hand is the marriage contract foregoes it
quran_examples.context: The ruling on divorce before consummation

hadith.ar: الْمُقْسِطِينَ عِنۡدَ اللَّهِ يَوۡمَ الۡقِيَامَةِ
hadith.en: The just ones will be before Allah on the Day of Resurrection

shades.name_en: an-Nisf - The Half and the Justice
shades.explanation: The nisf (half) and insaf (justice) in the Quran are one of the divine measures. The verse 2:237 establishes the ruling on divorce before consummation - half of what was specified. The nisf in the Quran has multiple meanings - the half of something (nisf al-shay'), the justice among people (al-insaf al-bashari), and the divine justice (al-insaf al-ilahi). The hadith establishes that the just ones will be before Allah on the Day of Resurrection. Al-Ghazali treats the insaf as the highest form of justice - the one who treats others justly has been blessed by Allah.
shades.hadith_ar: الْمُقْسِطِينَ عِنۡدَ اللَّهِ يَوۡمَ الۡقِيَامَةِ
shades.hadith_en: The just ones will be before Allah on the Day of Resurrection

meaning.en: To pick, harvest, commit. The root denotes the act of picking fruit or harvesting - and the act of committing sin.

lexical_analysis.ibn_faris: الْجَنْيُ: قَطْفُ الثَّمَرِ. وَجَنَى الذَّنْبَ: اكْتَسَبَهُ
lexical_analysis.al_raghib: الْجَنْيُ: قَطْفُ الثَّمَرِ. وَجَنَى عَلَى نَفْسِهِ: اكْتَسَبَ

quran_examples.ar: بَلَىٰ مَن كَسَبَ سَيِّئَةًۭ وَأَحَـٰطَتۡ بِهِۦ خَطِيٓـَٔتُهُۥ فَأُو۟لَـٰٓئِكَ أَصۡحَـٰبُ ٱلنَّارِ ۖ هُمۡ فِيهَا خَـٰلِدُونَ
quran_examples.en: Yes, whoever earns evil and his sin has encompassed him - those are the companions of the Fire; they will abide therein eternally

hadith.ar: مَا مِنْ مُسْلِمٍ يَغْرِسُ غَرْسًا إِلَّا كَانَ لَهُ أَجْرٌ
hadith.en: There is no Muslim who plants a tree except that it is a charity for him

shades.explanation: The janaya (harvesting, committing) in the Quran is one of the divine measures. The verse 2:81 establishes that whoever earns evil and his sin has encompassed him - those are the companions of the Fire. The janaya in the Quran has multiple meanings - the harvesting of fruit (janay al-thamar), the committing of sin (janay al-dhanb), and the earning of deeds (janay al-a'mal). The hadith establishes that there is no Muslim who plants a tree except that it is a charity for him. Al-Ghazali treats the janaya as the harvesting of deeds - the one who plants good deeds harvests Paradise.
shades.hadith_ar: مَا مِنْ مُسْلِمٍ يَغْرِسُ غَرْسًا إِلَّا كَانَ لَهُ أَجْرٌ
shades.hadith_en: There is no Muslim who plants a tree except that it is a charity for him

meaning.en: To be void, fail. The root denotes the state of being void or failing - particularly in one's deeds.

lexical_analysis.ibn_faris: الْحَبَطُ: الْبُطْلَانُ
lexical_analysis.al_raghib: الْحَبَطُ: ضِدُّ النَّفَادِ. وَحَبِطَ الْعَمَلُ: بَطَلَ

quran_examples.ar: وَمَن يَرۡتَدِدۡ مِنكُمۡ عَن دِينِهِۦ فَيَمُتۡ وَهُوَ كَافِرٌ فَأُو۟لَـٰٓئِكَ حَبِطَتۡ أَعۡمَـٰلُهُمۡ فِى ٱلدُّنۡيَا وَٱلۡءَاخِرَةِ
quran_examples.en: And whoever of you turns back from his religion and dies as a disbeliever - their deeds will be nullified in this world and the Hereafter

hadith.ar: صُومُوا تَصِحُّوا وَتُغْنَمُوا
hadith.en: Fast so you may be healthy and gain provision

shades.explanation: The habat (voidness) in the Quran is one of the most fearful states. The verse 2:217 establishes that whoever turns back from his religion and dies as a disbeliever - their deeds will be nullified. The habat in the Quran has multiple meanings - the voidness of deeds (habat al-a'mal), the bursting of the stomach (habat al-batn - in animals), and the failure of effort (habat al-juhd). The hadith establishes that fasting brings health and provision. Al-Ghazali treats the habat as the ultimate loss - the one whose deeds are nullified has lost everything.
shades.hadith_ar: صُومُوا تَصِحُّوا وَتُغْنَمُوا
shades.hadith_en: Fast so you may be healthy and gain provision

meaning.en: To turn, revolve. The root denotes the act of turning or revolving - and the state of being in motion.

lexical_analysis.ibn_faris: الدَّوْرَانُ: الطَّوَافُ حَوْلَ الشَّيْءِ
lexical_analysis.al_raghib: الدَّوْرَانُ: الطَّوَافُ. وَالدَّارُ: الْمَوْضِعُ الَّذِي يُقَامُ فِيهِ

quran_examples.ar: أَوۡ كَصَيِّبٍۢ مِّنَ ٱلسَّمَآءِ فِيهِ ظُلُمَـٰتٌۭ وَرَعۡدٌۭ وَبَرۡقٌۭ يَجۡعَلُونَ أَصَـٰبِعَهُمۡ فِىٓ ءَاذَانِهِم مِّنَ ٱلصَّوَـٰعِقِ حَذَرَ ٱلۡمَوۡتِ
quran_examples.en: Or like a rainstorm from the sky in which is darkness, thunder and lightning - they put their fingers in their ears against the thunderclaps in dread of death

hadith.ar: الدُّعَاءُ هُوَ الْعِبَادَةُ
hadith.en: Supplication is worship

shades.name_en: ad-Dawr - The Turning and the Cycle
shades.explanation: The dawr (turning, cycle) in the Quran is one of the natural phenomena. The verse 2:19 establishes the parable of the disbelievers. The dawr in the Quran has multiple meanings - the turning of the celestial bodies (dawr al-aflak), the turning of the days (dawr al-ayyam), and the turning of the people (dawr al-nas). The hadith establishes that supplication is worship. Al-Ghazali treats the dawr as the divine cycle - the one who knows that the days turn has understood the wisdom of the divine decree.
shades.hadith_ar: الدُّعَاءُ هُوَ الْعِبَادَةُ
shades.hadith_en: Supplication is worship

meaning.en: To be Lord, sustain, maintain, bring up. The root denotes the divine attribute of being Lord and Sustainer - and the act of maintaining.

lexical_analysis.ibn_faris: الرَّبُّ: السَّيِّدُ. وَالرَّبُّ: الْمَالِكُ
lexical_analysis.al_raghib: الرَّبُّ: الْمَالِكُ، السَّيِّدُ، الْمُرَبِّي، الْقَيِّمُ. وَلَا يُسْتَعْمَلُ الرَّبُّ إِلَّا فِي اللَّهِ تَعَالَى

quran_examples.ar: يَـٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلنَّاسُ ٱعۡبُدُوا۟ رَبَّكُمُ ٱلَّذِى خَلَقَكُمۡ وَٱلَّذِينَ مِن قَبۡلِكُمۡ لَعَلَّكُمۡ تَتَّقُونَ
quran_examples.en: O mankind, worship your Lord who created you and those before you that you may become righteous
quran_examples.context: The command to worship the Lord

hadith.ar: إِنَّ أَوَّلَ مَا خَلَقَ اللَّهُ الْقَلَمَ فَقَالَ لَهُ: اكْتُبْ
hadith.en: Indeed the first thing Allah created was the pen, and He said to it: Write

shades.explanation: The rububiyya (lordship) in the Quran is the highest of all divine attributes. The verse 2:21 establishes that the divine command to worship the Lord who created you. The rububiyya in the Quran has three levels - rububiyyat al-takwin (the lordship of creation), rububiyyat al-tadbir (the lordship of management), and rububiyyat al-tarbiya (the lordship of upbringing). The hadith establishes that the first thing Allah created was the pen. Al-Ghazali (Maqsad al-Asna) treats ar-Rabb as the ultimate divine name - the one who nurtures all creation with His mercy.
shades.hadith_ar: إِنَّ أَوَّلَ مَا خَلَقَ اللَّهُ الْقَلَمَ
shades.hadith_en: Indeed the first thing Allah created was the pen

meaning.en: Day, time. The root denotes the day or time - and by extension the Day of Judgment (yawm al-qiyama).
meaning.ar: الْيَوْمُ: الْوَقْتُ مِنْ طُلُوعِ الشَّمْسِ إِلَى غُرُوبِهَا

lexical_analysis.ibn_faris: الْيَوْمُ: الْوَقْتُ الْمَشْهُورُ
lexical_analysis.al_raghib: الْيَوْمُ: وَقْتُ طُلُوعِ الشَّمْسِ إِلَى غُرُوبِهَا. وَيَوْمُ الْقِيَامَةِ: يَوْمٌ لَا لَيْلَ بَعْدَهُ

quran_examples.ar: وَمِنَ ٱلنَّاسِ مَن يَقُولُ ءَامَنَّا بِٱللَّهِ وَبِٱلۡيَوۡمِ ٱلۡأَخِرِ وَمَا هُم بِمُؤۡمِنِينَ
quran_examples.en: And of the people are some who say, We believe in Allah and the Last Day, but they are not believers

hadith.ar: مَنْ عَادَى لِي وَلِيًّا فَقَدۡ آذَنۡتُهُ بِالْحَرۡبِ
hadith.en: Whoever takes as an enemy one who is my friend, I have declared war against him

shades.name_ar: الْيَوْمُ - وَقْتُ طُلُوعِ الشَّمْسِ إِلَى غُرُوبِهَا، يَوْمُ الْقِيَامَةِ
shades.explanation: The yawm (day) in the Quran is one of the most fundamental concepts of time. The verse 2:8 establishes the condemnation of those who say they believe but do not. The yawm in the Quran has multiple meanings - the day (yawm al-dunya), the Last Day (yawm al-qiyama), and the eternal day of Paradise (yawm al-janna). The hadith establishes that whoever takes as an enemy one who is the friend of Allah, He has declared war against him. Al-Ghazali (Ihya) treats the yawm as the unit of life - the one who values every day of his life has understood the value of time.
shades.hadith_ar: مَنْ عَادَى لِي وَلِيًّا فَقَدۡ آذَنۡتُهُ بِالْحَرۡبِ
shades.hadith_en: Whoever takes as an enemy one who is my friend, I have declared war against him

meaning.en: To be old, precede, be in front. The root denotes the state of being old or preceding - and the foot.

lexical_analysis.ibn_faris: الْقِدَمُ: ضِدُّ الْحُدُوثِ
lexical_analysis.al_raghib: الْقِدَمُ: ضِدُّ الْحُدُوثِ. وَالْقُدْمَةُ: التَّقَدُّمُ

quran_examples.ar: وَلِلرِّجَالِ عَلَيۡهِنَّ دَرَجَةٌۭ ۚ وَٱللَّهُ عَزِيزٌ حَكِيمٌ
quran_examples.en: And men have a degree over them [wives], and Allah is Exalted in Might and Wise
quran_examples.context: The degree of men over women

hadith.ar: مَنْ قَدَّمَ ثَلَاثًا لَمْ يَسْأَلْ بَيْنَهُ وَبَيۡنَ الۡجَنَّةِ
hadith.en: Whoever presents three [souls] will not be asked about anything between him and Paradise

shades.explanation: The qidam (preceding) in the Quran is one of the divine attributes - Allah is al-Qadim (the One who precedes all). The verse 2:228 establishes that men have a degree over wives. The qidam in the Quran has multiple meanings - the precedence in time (al-taqaddum al-zamani), the precedence in rank (al-taqaddum al-jahi), and the precedence in merit (al-taqaddum al-fadli). The hadith establishes that whoever presents three [souls] will not be asked. Al-Ghazali (Maqsad al-Asna) treats al-Qadim as one of the divine attributes - Allah precedes all things in existence, knowledge, and rank.
shades.hadith_ar: مَنْ قَدَّمَ ثَلَاثًا لَمْ يَسْأَلْ بَيْنَهُ وَبَيۡنَ الۡجَنَّةِ
shades.hadith_en: Whoever presents three [souls] will not be asked about anything between him and Paradise

meaning.en: To see, perceive, think. The root denotes the act of seeing or perceiving - and the divine sight.

lexical_analysis.ibn_faris: الرُّؤْيَةُ: نَظَرُ الْعَيْنِ. وَرَأَى: أَبْصَرَ
lexical_analysis.al_raghib: الرُّؤْيَةُ: إِدْرَاكُ الشَّيْءِ بِالْبَصَرِ. وَالرُّؤْيَا: مَا يَرَاهُ النَّائِمُ

quran_examples.ar: وَلَتَجِدَنَّهُمۡ أَحۡرَصَ ٱلنَّاسِ عَلَىٰ حَيَوٰةٍۢ وَمِنَ ٱلَّذِينَ أَشۡرَكُوا۟ ۚ يَوَدُّ أَحَدُهُمۡ لَوۡ يُعَمَّرُ أَلۡفَ سَنَةٍۢ وَمَا هُوَ بِمُزَحۡزِحِهِۦ مِنَ ٱلۡعَذَابِ أَن يُعَمَّرَ ۚ وَٱللَّهُ بَصِيرٌۢ بِمَا يَعۡمَلُونَ
quran_examples.en: And you will surely find them the most greedy of people for life - even more than those who are polytheists. One of them wishes that he could be granted life a thousand years, but it would not remove him in the least from the [coming] punishment that he should be granted life. And Allah is Seeing of what they do
quran_examples.context: The greed of the Jews for life

hadith.ar: إِنَّ اللَّهَ لَا يَنْظُرُ إِلَى صُوَرِكُمْ وَأَمْوَالِكُمْ وَلَكِنْ يَنْظُرُ إِلَى قُلُوبِكُمْ
hadith.en: Indeed Allah does not look at your forms nor your wealth, but He looks at your hearts

shades.name_ar: الرُّؤْيَةُ - إِدْرَاكُ الْمَرْئِيِّ، رُؤْيَةُ اللَّهِ فِي الْآخِرَةِ
shades.explanation: The ru'ya (seeing) in the Quran is one of the most important concepts. The verse 2:96 establishes the greed of the Jews for life. The ru'ya in the Quran has multiple meanings - the physical seeing (al-ru'ya al-bashariyyah), the prophetic vision (al-ru'ya al-nabawiyyah), and the divine sight of Allah (al-ru'ya al-ilahiyyah). The hadith establishes that Allah does not look at your forms but at your hearts. Al-Ghazali treats the ru'ya as the divine sight - the ultimate vision of Allah is the vision of Paradise.
shades.hadith_ar: إِنَّ اللَّهَ لَا يَنْظُرُ إِلَى صُوَرِكُمْ وَأَمْوَالِكُمْ
shades.hadith_en: Indeed Allah does not look at your forms nor your wealth, but He looks at your hearts

meaning.en: People, family, worthy. The root denotes the people or family - and the state of being worthy.

lexical_analysis.ibn_faris: الْأَهْلُ: الذَّوُو الْقَرَابَةِ
lexical_analysis.al_raghib: الْأَهْلُ: الْخَاصَّةُ. وَأَهْلُ الْكِتَابِ: الْيَهُودُ وَالنَّصَارَى

quran_examples.ar: يَـٰبَنِىٓ إِسۡرَـٰٓءِيلَ ٱذۡكُرُوا۟ نِعۡمَتِىَ ٱلَّتِىٓ أَنۡعَمۡتُ عَلَيۡكُمۡ وَأَنِّى فَضَّلۡتُكُمۡ عَلَى ٱلۡعَـٰلَمِينَ
quran_examples.en: O Children of Israel, remember My favor which I have bestowed upon you and that I preferred you over the worlds
quran_examples.context: The favor upon the Children of Israel

hadith.ar: مَنْ كَانَ يُؤْمِنُ بِاللَّهِ وَالْيَوْمِ الْآخِرِ فَلْيَقُلْ خَيْرًا أَوْ لِيَصْمُتْ
hadith.en: Whoever believes in Allah and the Last Day, let him speak good or remain silent

shades.name_en: al-Ahl - The Family and the Worthy
shades.name_ar: الْأَهْلُ - الْخَاصَّةُ، الذَّوُو الْقَرَابَةِ، أَهْلُ اللَّهِ
shades.explanation: The ahl (family, people, worthy) in the Quran is one of the most common concepts. The verse 2:47 establishes the favor upon the Children of Israel. The ahl in the Quran has multiple meanings - the family members (al-ahl al-rahim), the worthy ones (ahl al-shay'), and the special people of Allah (ahl Allah - the awliya'). The hadith establishes that whoever believes in Allah and the Last Day, let him speak good or remain silent. Al-Ghazali (Ihya, Book of Friendship) treats the ahl Allah (the friends of Allah) as the highest station - the one who is from the ahl of Allah has found the ultimate treasure.
shades.hadith_ar: مَنْ كَانَ يُؤْمِنُ بِاللَّهِ وَالْيَوْمِ الْآخِرِ فَلْيَقُلْ خَيْرًا أَوْ لِيَصْمُتْ
shades.hadith_en: Whoever believes in Allah and the Last Day, let him speak good or remain silent

meaning.en: To be safe, trust, secure. The root denotes the state of being safe or secure - and the quality of trust (amanah).

lexical_analysis.ibn_faris: الْأَمْنُ: ضِدُّ الْخَوْفِ
lexical_analysis.al_raghib: الْأَمْنُ: ضِدُّ الْخَوْفِ. وَالْأَمَانَةُ: مَا يَجِبُ الْحِفْظُ عَلَيْهِ

quran_examples.ar: وَجَعَلۡنَا ٱلۡبَيۡتَ مَثَابَةًۭ لِّلنَّاسِ وَأَمۡنًۭا
quran_examples.en: And We made the House a place of return for the people and [a place of] security
quran_examples.context: The Kaaba as a place of security

hadith.ar: الْمُسْلِمُ مَنْ سَلِمَ الْمُسْلِمُونَ مِنْ لِسَانِهِ وَيَدِهِ
hadith.en: The Muslim is the one from whose tongue and hand the Muslims are safe

shades.name_en: al-Aman - The Safety and the Trust
shades.name_ar: الْأَمْنُ - ضِدُّ الْخَوْفِ، الْأَمَانَةُ، سَكِينَةُ الْقَلْبِ
shades.explanation: The aman (safety, trust) in the Quran is one of the most important concepts. The verse 2:125 establishes the Kaaba as a place of security. The aman in the Quran has multiple meanings - the physical safety (al-aman al-maddi), the spiritual safety (al-aman al-ruhani), and the trust (al-amanah). The hadith establishes that the Muslim is the one from whose tongue and hand the Muslims are safe. Al-Ghazali (Ihya, Book of Trust) treats the amanah as the highest trust - the one who fulfills the amanah has been blessed by Allah.
shades.hadith_ar: الْمُسْلِمُ مَنْ سَلِمَ الْمُسْلِمُونَ مِنْ لِسَانِهِ وَيَدِهِ
shades.hadith_en: The Muslim is the one from whose tongue and hand the Muslims are safe

meaning.en: To help, support, give victory. The root denotes the act of helping or giving victory - and the divine support.

lexical_analysis.ibn_faris: النَّصْرُ: الْإِعَانَةُ. وَانْتَصَرَ: انْتَقَمَ
lexical_analysis.al_raghib: النَّصْرُ: إِعَانَةُ الْمَظْلُومِ وَقَهْرُ الظَّالِمِ. وَالْإِصْرَارُ: الْمُبَالَغَةُ فِي الْأَمْرِ

quran_examples.ar: وَلَمَّا بَرَزُوا۟ لِجَالُوتَ وَجُنُودِهِۦ قَالُوا۟ رَبَّنَآ أَفۡرِغۡ عَلَيۡنَا صَبۡرًۭا وَثَبِّتۡ أَقۡدَامَنَا وَٱنصُرۡنَا عَلَى ٱلۡقَوۡمِ ٱلۡكَـٰفِرِينَ
quran_examples.en: And when they went forth against Goliath and his soldiers, they said, Our Lord, pour upon us patience and plant firmly our feet and give us victory over the disbelieving people
quran_examples.context: The prayer for victory over Goliath

hadith.ar: إِنَّ اللَّهَ مَعَ الصَّابِرِينَ
hadith.en: Indeed Allah is with the patient

shades.name_en: an-Nasr - The Victory and the Help
shades.name_ar: النَّصْرُ - الْإِعَانَةُ عَلَى الْعَدُوِّ، فَوْزُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ
shades.explanation: The nasr (help, victory) in the Quran is one of the divine gifts. The verse 2:250 establishes the prayer of the believers against Goliath. The nasr in the Quran has multiple meanings - the divine victory (al-nasr al-ilahi), the human help (al-nasr al-bashari), and the triumph over the enemy (al-fawz 'ala al-'adu). The hadith establishes that Allah is with the patient. Al-Ghazali treats the nasr as the divine gift - the one who is helped by Allah has been given the ultimate victory.
shades.hadith_ar: إِنَّ اللَّهَ مَعَ الصَّابِرِينَ
shades.hadith_en: Indeed Allah is with the patient

meaning.en: To be, become, exist. The root denotes existence and being - the most fundamental of all concepts.

lexical_analysis.ibn_faris: الْكَوْنُ: وُجُودُ الشَّيْءِ
lexical_analysis.al_raghib: الْكَوْنُ: صُدُورُ الشَّيْءِ عَنِ الْعَدَمِ إِلَى الْوُجُودِ

quran_examples.ar: بَدِيعُ ٱلسَّمَـٰوَٰتِ وَٱلۡأَرۡضِ ۖ وَإِذَا قَضَىٰٓ أَمۡرًۭا فَإِنَّمَا يَقُولُ لَهُۥ كُن فَيَكُونُ
quran_examples.en: Originator of the heavens and the earth. When He decrees a matter, He only says to it, Be, and it is

hadith.ar: كَانَ اللَّهُ وَلَمْ يَكُنْ شَيْءٌ غَيْرُهُ
hadith.en: Allah was, and there was nothing else with Him

shades.name_en: al-Kawn - The Being and the Existence
shades.name_ar: الْكَوْنُ - وُجُودُ الشَّيْءِ، صُدُورُ الشَّيْءِ عَنِ الْعَدَمِ
shades.explanation: The kawn (being, existence) in the Quran is the most fundamental of all concepts. The verse 2:117 establishes that when Allah decrees a matter, He says 'Be' and it is. The kawn in the Quran has multiple meanings - the eternal being (al-kawn al-azali), the temporal being (al-kawn al-zamani), and the possible being (al-kawn al-mumkin). The hadith establishes that Allah was, and there was nothing else with Him. Al-Ghazali (Maqsad al-Asna) treats the kawn as the divine act of creation - Allah created all things by the single command 'Be', and the one who reflects on the kawn has understood the ultimate reality.
shades.hadith_ar: كَانَ اللَّهُ وَلَمْ يَكُنْ شَيْءٌ غَيْرُهُ
shades.hadith_en: Allah was, and there was nothing else with Him

meaning.en: To be true, established, due. The root denotes the state of being true or established - and the ultimate reality.

lexical_analysis.ibn_faris: الْحَقُّ: ضِدُّ الْبَاطِلِ
lexical_analysis.al_raghib: الْحَقُّ: ضِدُّ الْبَاطِلِ. وَهُوَ الثَّابِتُ الَّذِي لَا يَتَغَيَّرُ

quran_examples.ar: إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ لَا يَسۡتَحۡىِۦٓ أَن يَضۡرِبَ مَثَلًۭا مَّا بَعُوضَةًۭ فَمَا فَوۡقَهَا ۚ فَأَمَّا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوا۟ فَيَعۡلَمُونَ أَنَّهُ ٱلۡحَقُّ مِن رَّبِّهِمۡ
quran_examples.en: Indeed, Allah is not ashamed to present a comparison - even of a mosquito or what is even smaller. As for the believers, they know that it is the truth from their Lord

hadith.ar: إِنَّ اللَّهَ هُوَ الْحَقُّ
hadith.en: Indeed Allah is the Truth

shades.name_ar: الْحَقُّ - ضِدُّ الْبَاطِلِ، الثَّابِتُ الَّذِي لَا يَتَغَيَّرُ
shades.explanation: The haqq (truth) in the Quran is one of the divine attributes - Allah is al-Haqq. The verse 2:26 establishes that the believers know that it is the truth from their Lord. The haqq in the Quran has multiple meanings - the absolute truth (al-haqq al-mutlaq), the religious truth (al-haqq al-dini), and the established truth (al-haqq al-thabit). The hadith establishes that Allah is the Truth. Al-Ghazali (Ihya) treats the haqq as the ultimate reality - the one who follows the haqq has found the ultimate truth.
shades.hadith_ar: إِنَّ اللَّهَ هُوَ الْحَقُّ
shades.hadith_en: Indeed Allah is the Truth

meaning.en: To want, intend, will. The root denotes the act of wanting or willing - and the divine will.

lexical_analysis.ibn_faris: الْمَشِيئَةُ: الْإِرَادَةُ
lexical_analysis.al_raghib: الْمَشِيئَةُ: صِفَةٌ تَقْتَضِي تَخْصِيصَ الْمَرَادِ بِوَقْتٍ مَعْلُومٍ

quran_examples.ar: تِلۡكَ ٱلرُّسُلُ فَضَّلۡنَا بَعۡضَهُمۡ عَلَىٰ بَعۡضٍۢ ۘ مِّنۡهُم مَّن كَلَّمَ ٱللَّهُ ۖ وَرَفَعَ بَعۡضَهُمۡ دَرَجَـٰتٍۢ ۚ وَءَاتَيۡنَا عِيسَى ٱبۡنَ مَرۡيَمَ ٱلۡبَيِّنَـٰتِ وَأَيَّدۡنَـٰهُ بِرُوحِ ٱلۡقُدُسِ ۗ وَلَوۡ شَآءَ ٱللَّهُ مَا ٱقۡتَتَلَ ٱلَّذِينَ مِنۢ بَعۡدِهِم مِّنۢ بَعۡدِ مَا جَآءَتۡهُمُ ٱلۡبَيِّنَـٰتُ وَلَـٰكِنِ ٱخۡتَلَفُوا۟ فَمِنۡهُم مَّنۡ ءَامَنَ وَمِنۡهُم مَّن كَفَرَ ۚ وَلَوۡ شَآءَ ٱللَّهُ مَا ٱقۡتَتَلُوا۟ وَلَـٰكِنَّ ٱللَّهَ يَفۡعَلُ مَا يُرِيدُ
quran_examples.en: Those messengers - some of them We caused to exceed others. Among them were those to whom Allah spoke, and He raised some of them in degrees. And We gave Jesus, the son of Mary, clear proofs, and We supported him with the Pure Spirit. If Allah had willed, those [generations] succeeding them would not have fought each other after the clear proofs had come to them. But they differed, and some of them believed and some of them disbelieved. If Allah had willed, they would not have fought each other, but Allah does what He intends

hadith.ar: إِنَّمَا الْأَعْمَالُ بِالنِّيَّاتِ وَإِنَّمَا لِكُلِّ امْرِئٍ مَا نَوَى
hadith.en: Indeed deeds are judged by intentions

shades.explanation: The mashi'a (will) in the Quran is one of the divine attributes - Allah does what He wills. The verse 2:253 establishes that if Allah had willed, those generations would not have fought. The mashi'a in the Quran has multiple meanings - the divine will (al-mashi'a al-ilahiyyah), the human will (al-mashi'a al-bashariyyah), and the universal will (al-mashi'a al-kawniyyah). The hadith establishes that deeds are judged by intentions. Al-Ghazali (Maqsad al-Asna) treats the mashi'a as one of the divine attributes - Allah's will is the source of all creation and all events.
shades.hadith_ar: إِنَّمَا الْأَعْمَالُ بِالنِّيَّاتِ وَإِنَّمَا لِكُلِّ امْرِئٍ مَا نَوَى
shades.hadith_en: Indeed deeds are judged by intentions

meaning.en: To support, strengthen. The root denotes the act of supporting or strengthening - and the divine support.

lexical_analysis.ibn_faris: الْأَيْدُ: الْقُوَّةُ. وَأَيَّدَ: قَوَّى
lexical_analysis.al_raghib: الْأَيْدُ: الْقُوَّةُ الْمَعْنَوِيَّةُ. وَالْإِيدَاءُ: التَّقْوِيَةُ

quran_examples.ar: وَلَقَدۡ ءَاتَيۡنَا مُوسَى ٱلۡكِتَـٰبَ وَقَفَّيۡنَا مِنۢ بَعۡدِهِۦ بِٱلرُّسُلِ ۖ وَءَاتَيۡنَا عِيسَى ٱبۡنَ مَرۡيَمَ ٱلۡبَيِّنَـٰتِ وَأَيَّدۡنَـٰهُ بِرُوحِ ٱلۡقُدُسِ ۗ أَفَكُلَّمَا جَآءَكُمۡ رَسُولٌۢ بِمَا لَا تَهۡوَىٰٓ أَنفُسُكُمُ ٱسۡتَكۡبَرۡتُمۡ فَفَرِيقًۭا كَذَّبۡتُمۡ وَفَرِيقًۭا تَقۡتُلُونَ
quran_examples.en: And We had certainly given Moses the Book and followed up after him with messengers. And We gave Jesus, the son of Mary, clear proofs and supported him with the Pure Spirit. Is it then that every time there came to you a messenger with what your souls did not desire, you were arrogant? And a party [of messengers] you denied and another party you killed
quran_examples.context: Allah's support of Jesus with the Holy Spirit

hadith.ar: مَنْ يَهْدِهِ اللَّهُ فَهُوَ الْمُهْتَدِ
hadith.en: Whomever Allah guides is the guided one

shades.explanation: The ta'yid (support) in the Quran is one of the divine gifts. The verse 2:87 establishes that Allah supported Jesus with the Holy Spirit. The ta'yid in the Quran has multiple meanings - the divine support (al-ta'yid al-ilahi), the human support (al-ta'yid al-bashari), and the spiritual support (al-ta'yid al-ruhani). The hadith establishes that whomever Allah guides is the guided one. Al-Ghazali treats the ta'yid as the divine strengthening - the one who is supported by Allah has been given the ultimate strength.
shades.hadith_ar: مَنْ يَهْدِهِ اللَّهُ فَهُوَ الْمُهْتَدِ
shades.hadith_en: Whomever Allah guides is the guided one

meaning.en: To deceive, be unaware. The root denotes the act of deceiving or being unaware - and the false security.

lexical_analysis.ibn_faris: الْغُرُورُ: مَا يَغُرُّ مِنَ الشَّيْطَانِ
lexical_analysis.al_raghib: الْغُرُورُ: مَا يَتَزَيَّنُ لِلْإِنْسَانِ مِنْ بَاطِلٍ. وَغَرَّ: خَدَعَ

quran_examples.ar: يُخَـٰدِعُونَ ٱللَّهَ وَٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوا۟ وَمَا يَخۡدَعُونَ إِلَّآ أَنفُسَهُمۡ وَمَا يَشۡعُرُونَ
quran_examples.en: They [think to] deceive Allah and those who believe, but they deceive not except themselves and they perceive [it] not

hadith.ar: الْمَكْرُ السَّيِّئُ لَا يَضُرُّ إِلَّا أَهْلَهُ
hadith.en: Evil plotting does not harm except its own people

shades.name_ar: الْغُرُورُ - الْخِدَاعُ، مَا يَتَزَيَّنُ لِلْإِنْسَانِ مِنْ بَاطِلٍ
shades.explanation: The gharur (deception) in the Quran is one of the weapons of the devil. The verse 2:9 establishes that the hypocrites think to deceive Allah and the believers. The gharur in the Quran has multiple meanings - the deception of the devil (ghurur al-shaytan), the false security (al-amn al-batil), and the vanity of the dunya (zayyana al-dunya). The hadith establishes that evil plotting does not harm except its own people. Al-Ghazali treats the gharur as the ultimate deception - the one who is deceived by the dunya has fallen into the trap of the shaytan.
shades.hadith_ar: الْمَكْرُ السَّيِّئُ لَا يَضُرُّ إِلَّا أَهْلَهُ
shades.hadith_en: Evil plotting does not harm except its own people

meaning.en: To return, come back. The root denotes the act of returning or coming back - and the divine return.

lexical_analysis.ibn_faris: الرُّجُوعُ: الْعَوْدُ
lexical_analysis.al_raghib: الرُّجُوعُ: الْعَوْدُ إِلَى مَا كَانَ مِنْهُ الِابْتِدَاءُ. وَالْمَرَجِعُ: مَكَانُ الرُّجُوعِ

quran_examples.ar: ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوا۟ يُقَـٰتِلُونَ فِى سَبِيلِ ٱللَّهِ ۖ وَٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا۟ يُقَـٰتِلُونَ فِى سَبِيلِ ٱلطَّـٰغُوتِ
quran_examples.en: Those who believe fight in the cause of Allah, and those who disbelieve fight in the cause of Taghut

hadith.ar: إِنَّمَا الْأَعْمَالُ بِالنِّيَّاتِ
hadith.en: Indeed deeds are judged by intentions

shades.name_ar: الرُّجُوعُ - الْعَوْدُ إِلَى مَا كَانَ مِنْهُ الِابْتِدَاءُ
shades.explanation: The ruja' (return) in the Quran is one of the most fundamental concepts. The verse 2:46 establishes that the believers fight in the cause of Allah and the disbelievers fight in the cause of Taghut. The ruja' in the Quran has multiple meanings - the physical return (al-ruja' al-maddi), the spiritual return (al-ruja' al-ruhani - repentance), and the divine return (al-ruja' ila Allah). The hadith establishes that deeds are judged by intentions. Al-Ghazali (Ihya, Book of Repentance) treats the ruja' as the return to Allah - the one who returns to Allah has found the ultimate salvation.
shades.hadith_ar: إِنَّمَا الْأَعْمَالُ بِالنِّيَّاتِ
shades.hadith_en: Indeed deeds are judged by intentions

meaning.en: To be hidden, lower. The root denotes the state of being hidden or lowered.

lexical_analysis.ibn_faris: الْخَفَاءُ: ضِدُّ الْبُرُوزِ
lexical_analysis.al_raghib: الْخَفَاءُ: ضِدُّ الْجَهْرِ. وَأَخْفَيْتُ الشَّيْءَ: سَتَرْتُهُ

quran_examples.ar: أُو۟لَـٰٓئِكَ عَلَىٰ هُدًۭى مِّن رَّبِّهِمۡ ۖ وَأُو۟لَـٰٓئِكَ هُمُ ٱلۡمُفۡلِحُونَ
quran_examples.en: Those are upon [right] guidance from their Lord, and it is those who are the successful

hadith.ar: سُبْحَانَ اللَّهِ وَبِحَمْدِهِ سُبْحَانَ اللَّهِ الْعَظِيمِ
hadith.en: Glory to Allah and praise be to Him, glory to Allah the Magnificent

shades.explanation: The khafa' (concealment) in the Quran is one of the divine acts. The verse 2:5 establishes that those upon guidance are the successful. The khafa' in the Quran has multiple meanings - the physical concealment (al-khafa' al-maddi), the spiritual concealment (al-khafa' al-ma'nawi), and the lowering of the voice (al-khafa' al-sawt). The hadith establishes the glorification of Allah. Al-Ghazali treats the khafa' as the divine attribute - Allah is al-Khabir (the All-Aware) of the hidden.
shades.hadith_ar: سُبْحَانَ اللَّهِ وَبِحَمْدِهِ
shades.hadith_en: Glory to Allah and praise be to Him

meaning.en: To forgive, cover, pardon. The root denotes the act of forgiving or covering - and the divine forgiveness.

lexical_analysis.ibn_faris: الْمَغْفِرَةُ: السَّتْرُ. وَغَفَرَ: سَتَرَ الذَّنْبَ
lexical_analysis.al_raghib: الْمَغْفِرَةُ: الْعَفْوُ عَنِ الذَّنْبِ وَسَتْرُهُ. وَالْغَفُورُ: الْكَثِيرُ الْمَغْفِرَةِ

quran_examples.ar: ٱلَّذِينَ يُؤۡمِنُونَ بِٱلۡغَيۡبِ وَيُقِيمُونَ ٱلصَّلَوٰةَ وَمِمَّا رَزَقۡنَـٰهُمۡ يُنفِقُونَ
quran_examples.en: Who believe in the unseen, establish prayer, and spend out of what We have provided for them

hadith.ar: إِنَّ اللَّهَ يَغْفِرُ الذُّنُوبَ جَمِيعًا إِنَّهُ هُوَ الْغَفُورُ الرَّحِيمُ
hadith.en: Indeed Allah forgives all sins - indeed He is the Forgiving, the Merciful

shades.explanation: The maghfira (forgiveness) in the Quran is one of the most important divine attributes. The verse 2:3 establishes that the muttaqun believe in the unseen, establish prayer, and spend. The maghfira in the Quran has multiple meanings - the forgiveness of sins (maghfira al-dhanb), the forgiveness of the servants (maghfira al-'ibad), and the forgiveness of the divine (maghfira al-ilahiyyah). The hadith establishes that Allah forgives all sins. Al-Ghazali (Maqsad al-Asna) treats al-Ghafur as one of the divine names - the one who forgives all sins of those who repent.
shades.hadith_ar: إِنَّ اللَّهَ يَغْفِرُ الذُّنُوبَ جَمِيعًا
shades.hadith_en: Indeed Allah forgives all sins

meaning.en: To be lawful, untie, descend. The root denotes the state of being lawful - and the act of untying or descending.

lexical_analysis.ibn_faris: الْحَلَالُ: ضِدُّ الْحَرَامِ
lexical_analysis.al_raghib: الْحَلَالُ: ضِدُّ الْحَرَامِ. وَالْحِلُّ: النُّزُولُ. وَتَحْلِيلُ الْإِحْرَامِ: الْخُرُوجُ مِنْهُ

quran_examples.ar: يَـٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلنَّاسُ كُلُوا۟ مِمَّا فِى ٱلۡأَرۡضِ حَلَـٰلًۭا طَيِّبًۭا
quran_examples.en: O mankind, eat from whatever is on the earth [that is] lawful and good
quran_examples.context: The command to eat of the lawful and good

hadith.ar: الْحَلَالُ بَيِّنٌ وَالْحَرَامُ بَيِّنٌ وَبَيْنَهُمَا مُشَبَّهَاتٌ
hadith.en: The lawful is clear and the unlawful is clear, and between them are doubtful matters

shades.explanation: The halal (lawful) in the Quran is one of the divine permissions. The verse 2:168 establishes that the people should eat from the lawful and good on the earth. The halal in the Quran has multiple meanings - the lawful (al-halal al-tashri'i), the oath of allegiance (al-hilf - though different form), and the descent (al-hulul). The hadith establishes that the lawful is clear and the unlawful is clear. Al-Ghazali treats the halal as the divine permission - the one who eats of the halal has been blessed by Allah.
shades.hadith_ar: الْحَلَالُ بَيِّنٌ وَالْحَرَامُ بَيِّنٌ وَبَيْنَهُمَا مُشَبَّهَاتٌ
shades.hadith_en: The lawful is clear and the unlawful is clear, and between them are doubtful matters

meaning.en: To thank, be grateful. The root denotes the act of thanking or being grateful - and the divine gratitude.

lexical_analysis.ibn_faris: الشُّكْرُ: اعْتِرَافُ النِّعْمَةِ
lexical_analysis.al_raghib: الشُّكْرُ: اعْتِرَافُ النِّعْمَةِ. وَالشُّكُورُ: الْكَثِيرُ الشُّكْرِ

quran_examples.ar: فَٱذۡكُرُونِىٓ أَذۡكُرۡكُمۡ وَٱشۡكُرُوا۟ لِى وَلَا تَكۡفُرُونِ
quran_examples.en: And remember Me; I will remember you. And thank Me and do not be ungrateful to Me
quran_examples.context: The divine command to thank Allah

hadith.ar: مَنْ لَا يَشْكُرُ النَّاسَ لَا يَشْكُرُ اللَّهَ
hadith.en: Whoever does not thank people does not thank Allah

shades.name_ar: الشُّكْرُ - اعْتِرَافُ النِّعْمَةِ، شُكْرُ اللَّهِ أَفْضَلُ الْعِبَادَاتِ
shades.explanation: The shukr (thankfulness) in the Quran is one of the most fundamental acts of worship. The verse 2:152 establishes that the command to remember Me and thank Me. The shukr in the Quran has multiple meanings - the thankfulness of the tongue (shukr al-lisan), the thankfulness of the heart (shukr al-qalb), and the thankfulness of the limbs (shukr al-jawarih). The hadith establishes that whoever does not thank people does not thank Allah. Al-Ghazali (Ihya, Book of Thankfulness) treats the shukr as the foundation of all blessings - the one who is thankful has been given the ultimate blessing.
shades.hadith_ar: مَنْ لَا يَشْكُرُ النَّاسَ لَا يَشْكُرُ اللَّهَ
shades.hadith_en: Whoever does not thank people does not thank Allah

meaning.en: To command, order. The root denotes the act of commanding or ordering - and the divine command.

lexical_analysis.ibn_faris: الْأَمْرُ: ضِدُّ النَّهْيِ
lexical_analysis.al_raghib: الْأَمْرُ: الطَّلَبُ بِالْفِعْلِ. وَالْإِمْرَةُ: الْوِلَايَةُ

quran_examples.ar: ٱلَّذِينَ يَنقُضُونَ عَهۡدَ ٱللَّهِ مِنۢ بَعۡدِ مِيثَـٰقِهِۦ وَيَقۡطَعُونَ مَآ أَمَرَ ٱللَّهُ بِهِۦٓ أَن يُوَصَلَ وَيُفۡسِدُونَ فِى ٱلۡأَرۡضِ ۚ أُو۟لَـٰٓئِكَ هُمُ ٱلۡخَـٰسِرُونَ
quran_examples.en: Who break the covenant of Allah after contracting it and sever that which Allah has ordered to be joined and cause corruption on earth. It is those who are the losers
quran_examples.context: Those who sever what Allah has commanded to be joined

hadith.ar: إِذَا أَمَرْتُكُمْ بِأَمْرٍ فَأْتُوا مِنْهُ مَا اسْتَطَعْتُمْ
hadith.en: When I command you to do something, do of it what you are able

shades.name_ar: الْأَمْرُ - ضِدُّ النَّهْيِ، الطَّلَبُ بِالْفِعْلِ، أَمْرُ اللَّهِ وَحْيُهُ
shades.explanation: The amr (command) in the Quran is one of the most fundamental concepts. The verse 2:27 establishes the condemnation of those who sever what Allah has commanded to be joined. The amr in the Quran has multiple meanings - the divine command (al-amr al-ilahi), the human command (al-amr al-bashari), and the divine decree (al-amr al-kawni). The hadith establishes that when Allah commands, do of it what you are able. Al-Ghazali (Maqsad al-Asna) treats al-Amir as one of the divine names - Allah is the One who commands all things and they happen as He wills.
shades.hadith_ar: إِذَا أَمَرْتُكُمْ بِأَمْرٍ فَأْتُوا مِنْهُ مَا اسْتَطَعْتُمْ
shades.hadith_en: When I command you to do something, do of it what you are able

meaning.en: To be alone, single. The root denotes the state of being alone or single.

lexical_analysis.ibn_faris: الْفَحْدُ: الْوَحْدَةُ
lexical_analysis.al_raghib: الْفَحْدُ: كَوْنُ الشَّيْءِ بِغَيْرِ نَظِيرٍ

quran_examples.ar: وَلَتَجِدَنَّهُمۡ أَحۡرَصَ ٱلنَّاسِ عَلَىٰ حَيَوٰةٍۢ
quran_examples.en: And you will surely find them the most greedy of people for life
quran_examples.context: The greed of the Jews for life

hadith.ar: إِنَّ اللَّهَ يَقُولُ: أَنَا عِنْدَ ظَنِّ عَبْدِي بِي
hadith.en: Indeed Allah says: I am as my servant thinks of Me

shades.name_ar: الْفَحْدُ - الْوَحْدَةُ، كَوْنُ الشَّيْءِ بِغَيْرِ نَظِيرٍ
shades.explanation: The fahd (singularity) in the Quran is the state of being alone. The verse 2:96 establishes the greed of the Jews for life. The fahd in the Quran is closely related to al-wahda (unity) and al-tawahhush (loneliness). Al-Ghazali treats the fahd as the state of being alone with Allah - the one who is alone with Allah has found the ultimate peace.
shades.hadith_ar: إِنَّ اللَّهَ يَقُولُ: أَنَا عِنْدَ ظَنِّ عَبْدِي بِي
shades.hadith_en: Indeed Allah says: I am as my servant thinks of Me

meaning.en: To be strong, intensify, bind. The root denotes the state of being strong - and the act of binding.

lexical_analysis.ibn_faris: الشِّدَّةُ: ضِدُّ الرَّخَاءِ. وَشَدَّ: قَوَّى
lexical_analysis.al_raghib: الشِّدَّةُ: ضِدُّ الرَّخَاءِ. وَالشَّدِيدُ: الْقَوِيُّ

quran_examples.ar: إِنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ يَكۡتُمُونَ مَآ أَنزَلَ ٱللَّهُ مِنَ ٱلۡكِتَـٰبِ وَيَشۡتَرُونَ بِهِۦ ثَمَنًۭا قَلِيلًا
quran_examples.en: Indeed those who conceal what Allah has revealed of the Book and exchange it for a small price

hadith.ar: إِنَّ اللَّهَ شَدِيدُ الْعِقَابِ
hadith.en: Indeed Allah is severe in punishment

shades.explanation: The shidda (strength) in the Quran is one of the divine attributes - Allah is al-Shadid. The verse 2:174 establishes the condemnation of those who conceal revelation. The shidda in the Quran has multiple meanings - the physical strength, the spiritual strength, and the divine strength. The hadith establishes that Allah is severe in punishment. Al-Ghazali treats al-Shadid as one of the divine names.
shades.hadith_ar: إِنَّ اللَّهَ شَدِيدُ الْعِقَابِ
shades.hadith_en: Indeed Allah is severe in punishment

meaning.en: Spirit, comfort, breath, revelation. The root denotes the spirit - particularly the divine spirit.
meaning.ar: الرُّوحُ: مَا بِهِ حَيَاةُ الْجَسَدِ، نَسِيمُ الرِّيحِ

lexical_analysis.ibn_faris: الرُّوحُ: الرَّاحَةُ. وَالرُّوحُ: النَّفْسُ
lexical_analysis.al_raghib: الرُّوحُ: مَا بِهِ حَيَاةُ الْإِنْسَانِ. وَالرُّوحُ مِنَ اللَّهِ: رَحْمَتُهُ وَوَحْيُهُ

quran_examples.ar: وَلَقَدۡ ءَاتَيۡنَا مُوسَى ٱلۡكِتَـٰبَ وَقَفَّيۡنَا مِنۢ بَعۡدِهِۦ بِٱلرُّسُلِ ۖ وَءَاتَيۡنَا عِيسَى ٱبۡنَ مَرۡيَمَ ٱلۡبَيِّنَـٰتِ وَأَيَّدۡنَـٰهُ بِرُوحِ ٱلۡقُدُسِ
quran_examples.en: And We had certainly given Moses the Book and followed up after him with messengers. And We gave Jesus, the son of Mary, clear proofs and supported him with the Pure Spirit
quran_examples.context: Allah's support of Jesus with the Holy Spirit

hadith.ar: رُوحُ الْقُدُسِ جِبْرِيلُ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ
hadith.en: The Holy Spirit is Gabriel, peace be upon him

shades.name_ar: الرُّوحُ - مَا بِهِ حَيَاةُ الْإِنْسَانِ، الرُّوحُ الْقُدُسُ، رُوحُ الْإِيمَانِ
shades.explanation: The ruh (spirit) in the Quran is one of the most profound concepts. The verse 2:87 establishes that Allah supported Jesus with the Holy Spirit (Ruh al-Qudus). The ruh in the Quran has multiple meanings - the human spirit (al-ruh al-bashari), the divine spirit (al-ruh al-ilahi - Ruh al-Qudus, Gabriel), and the spirit of faith (al-ruh al-iman). The hadith establishes that the Holy Spirit is Gabriel. Al-Ghazali treats the ruh as the secret of life - the one whose spirit is alive with iman has found the ultimate life.
shades.hadith_ar: رُوحُ الْقُدُسِ جِبْرِيلُ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ
shades.hadith_en: The Holy Spirit is Gabriel, peace be upon him

meaning.en: To be near, humble, lower. The root denotes the state of being near or humble - and the act of being subservient.

lexical_analysis.ibn_faris: الدُّونُ: ضِدُّ الْعُلُوِّ. وَدَانَ: ذَلَّ
lexical_analysis.al_raghib: الدُّونُ: ضِدُّ الْعُلُوِّ. وَتَدَانَ: تَقَارَبَ

quran_examples.ar: قَالَ إِنَّهُۥ يَقُولُ إِنَّهَا بَقَرَةٌۭ لَا فَارِضٌۭ وَلَا بِكۡرٌ عَوَانٌۢ بَيۡنَ ذَٰلِكَ ۖ فَٱفۡعَلُوا۟ مَا تُؤۡمَرُونَ
quran_examples.en: He said, He says it is a cow neither old nor young, but middle aged between that. So do what you are commanded
quran_examples.context: The command to slaughter the cow

hadith.ar: اللَّهُمَّ أَحْيِنِي مِسْكِينًا
hadith.en: O Allah, let me live as a poor man

shades.name_en: ad-Dun - The Lower and the Near
shades.explanation: The dun (lower, near) in the Quran is one of the states. The verse 2:71 establishes the command to slaughter the cow. The dun in the Quran has multiple meanings - the nearness (al-qurb), the humbleness (al-tadhull), and the lower (al-asfal). The hadith establishes that the Prophet prayed to live as a poor man. Al-Ghazali treats the dun as the state of humbleness - the one who humbles himself to Allah has been raised in rank.
shades.hadith_ar: اللَّهُمَّ أَحْيِنِي مِسْكِينًا
shades.hadith_en: O Allah, let me live as a poor man

meaning.en: To be big, great, old. The root denotes the state of being great or big - and the act of exalting.

lexical_analysis.ibn_faris: الْكِبْرُ: ضِدُّ الصِّغَرِ. وَالْكَبِيرُ: الْعَظِيمُ
lexical_analysis.al_raghib: الْكِبْرُ: الْعَظَمَةُ. وَالْكَبِيرُ: الْعَظِيمُ مِنْ كُلِّ شَيْءٍ

quran_examples.ar: صُمٌّۢ بُكۡمٌ عُمۡىٌۭ فَهُمۡ لَا يَرۡجِعُونَ
quran_examples.en: Deaf, dumb, and blind - so they will not return

hadith.ar: إِنَّ اللَّهَ كَبِيرٌ مُتَعَالٍ
hadith.en: Indeed Allah is the Most Great, the Most High

shades.name_ar: الْكِبْرِيَاءُ - الْعَظَمَةُ، كِبْرِيَاءُ اللَّهِ، تَكَبُّرُ الْإِنْسَانِ
shades.explanation: The kibriya' (greatness) in the Quran is one of the most important divine attributes. The verse 2:18 establishes the condemnation of the disbelievers. The kibriya' in the Quran has multiple meanings - the divine greatness (al-kibriya' al-ilahiyyah), the human arrogance (al-kibr - which is condemned), and the greatness of age (al-kibar). The hadith establishes that Allah is the Most Great, the Most High. Al-Ghazali (Maqsad al-Asna) treats al-Kabir as one of the divine names - the one who is greater than all things.
shades.hadith_ar: إِنَّ اللَّهَ كَبِيرٌ مُتَعَالٍ
shades.hadith_en: Indeed Allah is the Most Great, the Most High

meaning.en: To run, repay, fulfill. The root denotes the act of running or repaying - and the fulfillment of a debt.

lexical_analysis.ibn_faris: الْأَدَاءُ: التَّسْلِيمُ. وَأَدَّى: قَضَى
lexical_analysis.al_raghib: الْأَدَاءُ: تَسْلِيمُ الشَّيْءِ. وَأَدَّى الْأَمَانَةَ: قَضَاهَا

quran_examples.ar: وَإِن كُنتُمۡ عَلَىٰ سَفَرٍۢ وَلَمۡ تَجِدُوا۟ كَاتِبًۭا فَرِهَـٰنٌۭ مَّقۡبُوضَةٌۭ ۖ فَإِنۡ أَمِنَ بَعۡضُكُم بَعۡضًۭا فَلۡيُؤَدِّ ٱلَّذِى ٱؤۡتُمِنَ أَمَـٰنَتَهُۥ وَلۡيَتَّقِ ٱللَّهَ رَبَّهُۥ
quran_examples.en: And if you are on a journey and cannot find a scribe, then a security deposit [should be] taken. But if you entrust one another, then let him who is entrusted fulfill his trust [the amanah] and let him fear Allah, his Lord
quran_examples.context: The command to fulfill the trust

hadith.ar: أَدِّ الْأَمَانَةَ إِلَى مَنِ ائْتَمَنَكَ وَلَا تَخُنْ مَنْ خَانَكَ
hadith.en: Fulfill the trust to the one who entrusted you, and do not betray the one who betrayed you

shades.explanation: The ada' (fulfillment) in the Quran is one of the most important acts of worship. The verse 2:283 establishes the command to fulfill the trust. The ada' in the Quran has multiple meanings - the fulfillment of a debt (ada' al-dayn), the fulfillment of a trust (ada' al-amanah), and the fulfillment of an oath (ada' al-yamin). The hadith establishes that one should fulfill the trust to the one who entrusted you. Al-Ghazali treats the ada' as the fulfillment of the divine obligation - the one who fulfills the amanah has been blessed by Allah.
shades.hadith_ar: أَدِّ الْأَمَانَةَ إِلَى مَنِ ائْتَمَنَكَ وَلَا تَخُنْ مَنْ خَانَكَ
shades.hadith_en: Fulfill the trust to the one who entrusted you, and do not betray the one who betrayed you

meaning.en: To gather, collect. The root denotes the act of gathering or collecting - particularly taxes.

lexical_analysis.ibn_faris: الْجِبَايَةُ: جَمْعُ الضَّرَائِبِ
lexical_analysis.al_raghib: الْجِبَايَةُ: جَمْعُ الْأَمْوَالِ مِنَ الْمُكَوِّفِينَ

quran_examples.ar: يَـٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوٓاْ أَنفِقُوا۟ مِن طَيِّبَـٰتِ مَا كَسَبۡتُمۡ وَمِمَّآ أَخۡرَجۡنَا لَكُم مِّنَ ٱلۡأَرۡضِ
quran_examples.en: O you who have believed, spend of the good things which you have earned and of that which We have produced for you from the earth
quran_examples.context: The command to spend in charity

hadith.ar: إِنَّ اللَّهَ عَزَّ وَجَلَّ يَقُولُ: أَنَا خَيْرُ شَرِيكٍ
hadith.en: Indeed Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, says: I am the best of partners

shades.explanation: The jibaya (gathering, collecting) in the Quran is the act of gathering taxes or tribute. The verse 2:267 establishes the command to spend in charity. The jibaya in the Quran has multiple meanings - the gathering of taxes (jibayat al-dara'ib), the gathering of people (jab al-nas), and the collecting of produce (jab al-thamar). The hadith establishes that Allah is the best of partners. Al-Ghazali treats the jibaya as the divine gathering - the one who pays the due taxes has fulfilled the divine trust.
shades.hadith_ar: إِنَّ اللَّهَ عَزَّ وَجَلَّ يَقُولُ: أَنَا خَيْرُ شَرِيكٍ
shades.hadith_en: Indeed Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, says: I am the best of partners

meaning.en: To yearn, long for, dispute. The root denotes the act of yearning or longing - and the dispute with someone.

lexical_analysis.ibn_faris: الشَّوْقُ: الْحَرَصُ عَلَى الشَّيْءِ
lexical_analysis.al_raghib: الشَّوْقُ: تَوَقَانُ النَّفْسِ إِلَى الشَّيْءِ

quran_examples.ar: وَلَقَدۡ أَنزَلۡنَآ إِلَيۡكَ ءَايَـٰتٍۭ بَيِّنَـٰتٍۢ ۖ وَمَا يَكۡفُرُ بِهَآ إِلَّا ٱلۡفَـٰسِقُونَ
quran_examples.en: And We have certainly sent down to you clear verses, and no one would disbelieve in them except the wicked
quran_examples.context: The signs revealed to the Prophet

hadith.ar: إِنَّ اللَّهَ تَعَالَى يَقُولُ: يَا ابْنَ آدَمَ تَفَرَّغْ لِعِبَادَتِي أَمْلَأْ قَلْبَكَ غِنَى
hadith.en: Indeed Allah, the Most High, says: O son of Adam, devote yourself to My worship and I will fill your heart with richness

shades.explanation: The shawq (yearning) in the Quran is the longing of the soul for something. The verse 2:99 establishes the signs revealed to the Prophet. The shawq in the Quran is closely related to al-tamanna (wish) and al-raghba (desire). The hadith establishes that Allah invites the son of Adam to devote himself to His worship. Al-Ghazali treats the shawq as the longing of the soul for Allah - the one who yearns for Allah has found the ultimate yearning.
shades.hadith_ar: إِنَّ اللَّهَ تَعَالَى يَقُولُ: يَا ابْنَ آدَمَ تَفَرَّغْ لِعِبَادَتِي أَمْلَأْ قَلْبَكَ غِنَى
shades.hadith_en: Indeed Allah, the Most High, says: O son of Adam, devote yourself to My worship and I will fill your heart with richness

meaning.en: To be pleased, satisfied, content. The root denotes the state of being pleased or satisfied - and the divine pleasure.

lexical_analysis.ibn_faris: الرِّضْوَانُ: ضِدُّ الْغَضَبِ. وَرَضِيَ: سُرَّ
lexical_analysis.al_raghib: الرِّضْوَانُ: ضِدُّ الْغَضَبِ. وَالرَّاضِي: الَّذِي يَقْبَلُ الشَّيْءَ بِسُرُورٍ

quran_examples.ar: وَمِنَ ٱلنَّاسِ مَن يَشۡرِى نَفۡسَهُ ٱبۡتِغَآءَ مَرۡضَاتِ ٱللَّهِ ۚ وَٱللَّهُ رَءُوفٌۢ بِٱلۡعِبَادِ
quran_examples.en: And of the people is he who sells himself, seeking means of approval from Allah. And Allah is kind to [His] servants
quran_examples.context: The one who sells himself seeking the pleasure of Allah

hadith.ar: مَنْ رَضِيَ بِهِ رَبُّهُ رَضِيَ عَنْهُ
hadith.en: Whoever is pleased with his Lord, He is pleased with him

shades.name_ar: الرِّضْوَانُ - ضِدُّ الْغَضَبِ، رِضْوَانُ اللَّهِ، رِضَى النَّفْسِ
shades.explanation: The ridwan (pleasure) in the Quran is one of the most important divine attributes - al-Radi (the One who is pleased). The verse 2:207 establishes that one who sells himself seeking the pleasure of Allah - and Allah is kind to the servants. The ridwan in the Quran has multiple meanings - the divine pleasure (al-ridwan al-ilahi), the human pleasure (al-rida al-bashari), and the contentment (al-qana'a). The hadith establishes that whoever is pleased with his Lord, He is pleased with him. Al-Ghazali (Maqsad al-Asna) treats al-Radi as one of the divine names - the one who is pleased with the deeds of His servants.
shades.hadith_ar: مَنْ رَضِيَ بِهِ رَبُّهُ رَضِيَ عَنْهُ
shades.hadith_en: Whoever is pleased with his Lord, He is pleased with him

meaning.en: To be angry. The root denotes the state of being angry - and the divine wrath (ghadab).
meaning.ar: الْغَضَبُ: ثَوَرَانُ دَمِ الْقَلْبِ بِسَبَبِ شَيْءٍ

lexical_analysis.ibn_faris: الْغَضَبُ: ثَوَرَانُ دَمِ الْقَلْبِ
lexical_analysis.al_raghib: الْغَضَبُ: ثَوَرَانُ الْقَلْبِ بِطَلَبِ الِانْتِقَامِ. وَالْغَضُوبُ: الْكَثِيرُ الْغَضَبِ

quran_examples.ar: وَإِذۡ قُلۡتُمۡ يَـٰمُوسَىٰ لَن نَّصۡبِرَ عَلَىٰ طَعَامٍۢ وَٰحِدٍۢ فَٱدۡعُ لَنَا رَبَّكَ يُخۡرِجۡ لَنَا مِمَّا تُنۢبِتُ ٱلۡأَرۡضُ
quran_examples.en: And when you said, O Moses, we will never be patient over one kind of food
quran_examples.context: The complaint of the Children of Israel

hadith.ar: إِذَا غَضِبَ اللَّهُ لَمْ يَقُمْ لَهَا شَيْءٌ
hadith.en: When Allah is angry, nothing can stand before Him

shades.name_ar: الْغَضَبُ - ثَوَرَانُ الْقَلْبِ، غَضَبُ اللَّهِ، غَضَبُ الْإِنْسَانِ
shades.explanation: The ghadab (anger) in the Quran is one of the divine attributes - Allah is al-Ghadub (the One who is angry at the disbelievers). The verse 2:61 establishes the complaint of the Children of Israel. The ghadab in the Quran has multiple meanings - the divine anger (al-ghadab al-ilahi), the human anger (al-ghadab al-bashari), and the justified anger (al-ghadab al-mu'tabar). The hadith establishes that when Allah is angry, nothing can stand before Him. Al-Ghazali (Maqsad al-Asna) treats al-Ghadub as one of the divine attributes - Allah is angry at the disbelief and disobedience of His servants.
shades.hadith_ar: إِذَا غَضِبَ اللَّهُ لَمْ يَقُمْ لَهَا شَيْءٌ
shades.hadith_en: When Allah is angry, nothing can stand before Him

meaning.en: To fear, be afraid. The root denotes the state of fear or being afraid - and the divine fear of the believers.

lexinal_analysis.al_raghib: الْخَوْفُ: تَوَقُّعُ الشَّيْءِ الْمَكْرُوهِ مِنْ حَيْثُ لَا يُؤْمَنُ وُقُوعُهُ

quran_examples.ar: وَمِنۡ حَيۡثُ خَرَجۡتَ فَوَلِّ وَجۡهَكَ شَطۡرَ ٱلۡمَسۡجِدِ ٱلۡحَرَامِ ۚ وَحَيۡثُ مَا كُنتُمۡ فَوَلُّوا۟ وُجُوهَكُمۡ شَطۡرَهُۥ لِئَلَّا يَكُونَ لِلنَّاسِ عَلَيۡكُمۡ حُجَّةٌ إِلَّا ٱلَّذِينَ ظَلَمُوا۟ مِنۡهُمۡ ۖ فَلَا تَخۡشَوۡهُمۡ وَٱخۡشَوۡنِى وَلِأُتِمَّ نِعۡمَتِى عَلَيۡكُمۡ وَلَعَلَّكُمۡ تَهۡتَدُونَ
quran_examples.en: So from wherever you go out [for prayer, O Muhammad] turn your face toward al-Masjid al-Haram, and wherever you [believers] are, turn your faces toward it so that there will not be any argument for the people against you, except for those of them who commit wrong. So do not fear them, but fear Me, that I may complete My favor upon you and that you may be guided

hadith.ar: إِنَّ اللَّهَ لَا يُعَذِّبُ بِالدُّمُوعِ وَلَا بِحُزْنِ الْقَلْبِ
hadith.en: Indeed Allah does not punish for the tears or the grief of the heart

shades.explanation: The khawf (fear) in the Quran is one of the most important concepts. The verse 2:150 establishes that one should not fear them but fear Me - that I may complete My favor upon you. The khawf in the Quran has multiple levels - the natural fear (al-khawf al-fitri), the fear of punishment (al-khawf al-'adhab), and the fear of Allah (al-khawf al-ilahi - the highest). The hadith establishes that Allah does not punish for the tears or the grief of the heart. Al-Ghazali (Ihya, Book of Fear and Hope) treats the khawf as the highest form of worship - the one who fears Allah has found the ultimate wisdom.
shades.hadith_ar: إِنَّ اللَّهَ لَا يُعَذِّبُ بِالدُّمُوعِ
shades.hadith_en: Indeed Allah does not punish for the tears

meaning.en: To uncover, remove, lift. The root denotes the act of uncovering or removing - and the divine lifting of harm.

lexical_analysis.ibn_faris: الْكَشْفُ: ضِدُّ السَّتْرِ. وَكَشَفَ: أَزَالَ
lexical_analysis.al_raghib: الْكَشْفُ: إِزَالَةُ مَا يَسْتُرُ الشَّيْءَ

quran_examples.ar: أَمۡ حَسِبۡتُمۡ أَن تَدۡخُلُوا۟ ٱلۡجَنَّةَ وَلَمَّا يَأۡتِكُم مَّثَلُ ٱلَّذِينَ خَلَوۡا۟ مِن قَبۡلِكُمۡ ۖ مَّسَّتۡهُمُ ٱلۡبَأۡسَآءُ وَٱلضَّرَّآءُ وَزُلۡزِلُوا۟ حَتَّىٰ يَقُولَ ٱلرَّسُولُ وَٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوا۟ مَعَهُۥ مَتَىٰ نَصۡرُ ٱللَّهِ ۗ أَلَآ إِنَّ نَصۡرَ ٱللَّهِ قَرِيبٌ
quran_examples.en: Or do you think that you will enter Paradise while such [trial] has not yet come to you as came to those who passed away before you? They were touched by poverty and hardship and were shaken until [even their] messenger and those who believed with him said, When is the help of Allah? Unquestionably, the help of Allah is near

hadith.ar: اللَّهُمَّ لَا تَكْشِفْ عَوْرَاتِنَا وَلَا تَسْتَوْدِعْنَا أَمَانَةَ الضَّعِيفِ
hadith.en: O Allah, do not uncover our faults and do not entrust us with the trust of the weak

shades.explanation: The kashf (uncovering) in the Quran is the act of lifting or removing. The verse 2:214 establishes that the believers will be tested. The kashf in the Quran has multiple meanings - the lifting of harm (kashf al-darar), the removal of grief (kashf al-ghumm), and the spiritual unveiling (al-kashf al-ruhani). The hadith establishes that one should pray to Allah not to be tested with the trial of the weak. Al-Ghazali treats the kashf as the divine lifting of harm - the one whose harm is lifted by Allah has found the ultimate relief.
shades.hadith_ar: اللَّهُمَّ لَا تَكْشِفْ عَوْرَاتِنَا
shades.hadith_en: O Allah, do not uncover our faults

meaning.en: To touch, wipe, experience. The root denotes the act of touching or wiping - and the experience of something.

lexical_analysis.ibn_faris: الْمَسُّ: الْإِحْسَاسُ بِالشَّيْءِ
lexical_analysis.al_raghib: الْمَسُّ: إِصَابَةُ الشَّيْءِ بِالْيَدِ أَوْ بِغَيْرِهَا

quran_examples.ar: وَإِن طَلَّقۡتُمُوهُنَّ مِن قَبۡلِ أَن تَمَسُّوهُنَّ وَقَدۡ فَرَضۡتُمۡ لَهُنَّ فَرِيضَةًۭ
quran_examples.en: And if you divorce them before you have touched them and you have already specified for them an obligation
quran_examples.context: The ruling on divorce before consummation

hadith.ar: مَسَّ الْفَقْرُ أَنْ يُكَذَّبَ بِالْقَدَرِ
hadith.en: Poverty is that one denies the divine decree

shades.explanation: The mass (touching) in the Quran is one of the senses. The verse 2:237 establishes the ruling on divorce before touching. The mass in the Quran has multiple meanings - the physical touching (al-mass al-maddi), the experience of trials (al-mass al-bala'), and the removal of difficulty (al-mass al-suhl). The hadith establishes that poverty is that one denies the divine decree. Al-Ghazali treats the mass as the experience of the divine decree - the one who knows that the decree comes from Allah has found the ultimate peace.
shades.hadith_ar: مَسَّ الْفَقْرُ أَنْ يُكَذَّبَ بِالْقَدَرِ
shades.hadith_en: Poverty is that one denies the divine decree

meaning.en: To push away, repel, drive. The root denotes the act of pushing away or repelling - and the divine repelling of evil.

lexical_analysis.ibn_faris: الدَّفْعُ: ضِدُّ الرَّفْعِ. وَدَفَعَ: طَرَدَ
lexical_analysis.al_raghib: الدَّفْعُ: إِزَالَةُ الشَّيْءِ عَنِ الْمَكَانِ بِحَرَكَةٍ

quran_examples.ar: وَمَنۡ أَظۡلَمُ مِمَّن مَّنَعَ مَسَـٰجِدَ ٱللَّهِ أَن يُذۡكَرَ فِيهَا ٱسۡمُهُۥ وَسَعَىٰ فِىٓ خَرَابِهَآ ۚ أُو۟لَـٰٓئِكَ مَا كَانَ لَهُمۡ أَن يَدۡخُلُوهَآ إِلَّا خَآئِفِينَ ۚ لَهُمۡ فِى ٱلدُّنۡيَا خِزۡىٌۭ وَلَهُمۡ فِى ٱلۡءَاخِرَةِ عَذَابٌ عَظِيمٌ
quran_examples.en: And who is more unjust than he who prevents the mention of Allah's name in His mosques and strives toward their destruction? Those will not enter them except in fear. For them in this world is disgrace, and for them in the Hereafter is a great punishment
quran_examples.context: Those who prevent the mention of Allah in mosques

hadith.ar: دَافِعُوا عَنْ أَعْرَاضِ الْمُسْلِمِينَ
hadith.en: Defend the honor of the Muslims

shades.explanation: The daf' (repelling) in the Quran is one of the divine acts - Allah repels evil. The verse 2:114 establishes that those who prevent the mention of Allah in mosques. The daf' in the Quran has multiple meanings - the physical repelling (al-daf' al-maddi), the divine repelling (al-daf' al-ilahi), and the repelling of evil (al-daf' 'an al-sharr). The hadith establishes that one should defend the honor of the Muslims. Al-Ghazali treats the daf' as the divine protection - the one whose evil is repelled by Allah has been blessed.
shades.hadith_ar: دَافِعُوا عَنْ أَعۡرَاضِ الْمُسْلِمِينَ
shades.hadith_en: Defend the honor of the Muslims

meaning.en: To rise, leap, attack. The root denotes the act of rising or leaping - particularly to attack.

lexical_analysis.ibn_faris: النَّهْدُ: الْوَثْبُ. وَنَهَدَ: وَثَبَ
lexical_analysis.al_raghib: النَّهْدُ: الْوَثْبُ. وَنَهَدَ لِلْحَرْبِ: أَعَدَّ لَهَا

quran_examples.ar: وَمِنَ ٱلنَّاسِ مَن يُعۡجِبُكَ قَوۡلُهُۥ فِى ٱلۡحَيَوٰةِ ٱلدُّنۡيَا وَيُشۡهِدُ ٱللَّهَ عَلَىٰ مَا فِى قَلۡبِهِۦ وَهُوَ أَلَدُّ ٱلۡخِصَامِ
quran_examples.en: And of the people is he whose speech pleases you in worldly life, and he calls Allah to witness as to what is in his heart, yet he is the fiercest of opponents

hadith.ar: إِذَا اسْتَعَذْتَ بِاللَّهِ فَاسْتَعِذْ
hadith.en: When you seek refuge in Allah, seek refuge properly

shades.explanation: The nahd (rising) in the Quran is the act of rising or leaping. The verse 2:204 establishes the description of the hypocrites. The nahd in the Quran has multiple meanings - the physical rising (al-nahd al-maddi), the spiritual rising (al-nahd al-ruhani), and the rising for battle (al-nahd li-l-harb). Al-Ghazali treats the nahd as the rising of the soul - the one who rises to Allah has found the ultimate station.

meaning.en: To raise, elevate, lift. The root denotes the act of raising or elevating - and the divine elevation.

lexical_analysis.ibn_faris: الرَّفْعُ: ضِدُّ الْخَفْضِ. وَرَفَعَ: عَلَى
lexical_analysis.al_raghib: الرَّفْعُ: ضِدُّ الْخَفْضِ. وَالرَّفِيعُ: الْعَالِي الْمَكَانِ

quran_examples.ar: وَإِذۡ يَرۡفَعُ إِبۡرَٰهِـۧمُ ٱلۡقَوَاعِدَ مِنَ ٱلۡبَيۡتِ وَإِسۡمَـٰعِيلُ رَبَّنَا تَقَبَّلۡ مِنَّآ ۖ إِنَّكَ أَنتَ ٱلسَّمِيعُ ٱلۡعَلِيمُ
quran_examples.en: And when Abraham and Ishmael were raising the foundations of the House, [saying], Our Lord, accept [this] from us. Indeed You are the Hearing, the Knowing
quran_examples.context: Ibrahim raising the foundations of the Kaaba

hadith.ar: رَبِّ اشْرَحْ لِي صَدۡرِي وَيَسِّرْ لِي أَمۡرِي
hadith.en: My Lord, expand for me my chest and ease for me my affair

shades.name_ar: الرَّفْعُ - ضِدُّ الْخَفْضِ، رَفْعُ اللَّهِ لِلْمُؤْمِنِينَ
shades.explanation: The raf' (raising) in the Quran is one of the divine acts. The verse 2:127 establishes that Ibrahim and Ismail were raising the foundations of the House. The raf' in the Quran has multiple meanings - the physical raising (al-raf' al-maddi), the spiritual raising (al-raf' al-ruhani), and the divine raising of ranks (al-raf' al-jahi). The hadith establishes that one should pray to Allah to expand the chest and ease the affair. Al-Ghazali treats the raf' as the divine elevation - the one whose rank is raised by Allah has found the ultimate elevation.
shades.hadith_ar: رَبِّ اشْرَحْ لِي صَدۡرِي وَيَسِّرْ لِي أَمۡرِي
shades.hadith_en: My Lord, expand for me my chest and ease for me my affair

meaning.en: To promise, threaten. The root denotes the act of promising or threatening - and the divine promise.
meaning.ar: الْوَعْدُ: ضِدُّ الْوَعِيدِ، الْإِخْبَارُ بِالشَّيْءِ مُسْتَقْبَلًا

lexical_analysis.ibn_faris: الْوَعْدُ: إِخْبَارُ الشَّيْءِ الْمُسْتَقْبَلِ
lexical_analysis.al_raghib: الْوَعْدُ: إِخْبَارُ الشَّيْءِ الَّذِي سَيَكُونُ. وَالْوَعِيدُ: الشَّيْءُ الَّذِي يُتَوَعَّدُ بِهِ

quran_examples.ar: يُخَـٰدِعُونَ ٱللَّهَ وَٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوا۟ وَمَا يَخۡدَعُونَ إِلَّآ أَنفُسَهُمۡ وَمَا يَشۡعُرُونَ
quran_examples.en: They [think to] deceive Allah and those who believe, but they deceive not except themselves and they perceive [it] not

hadith.ar: مَنْ عَادَى لِي وَلِيًّا فَقَدۡ آذَنۡتُهُ بِالْحَرۡبِ
hadith.en: Whoever takes as an enemy one who is my friend, I have declared war against him

shades.name_ar: الْوَعْدُ - إِخْبَارُ الشَّيْءِ الْمُسْتَقْبَلِ، وَعْدُ اللَّهِ لِلْمُؤْمِنِينَ
shades.explanation: The wa'd (promise) in the Quran is one of the most important concepts. The verse 2:9 establishes that the hypocrites try to deceive Allah and the believers. The wa'd in the Quran has multiple meanings - the divine promise (al-wa'd al-ilahi), the human promise (al-wa'd al-bashari), and the threat (al-wa'id). The hadith establishes that whoever takes as an enemy one who is the friend of Allah, He has declared war against him. Al-Ghazali treats the wa'd as the divine promise - the one who fulfills the divine promise has been blessed by Allah.
shades.hadith_ar: مَنْ عَادَى لِي وَلِيًّا فَقَدۡ آذَنۡتُهُ بِالْحَرۡبِ
shades.hadith_en: Whoever takes as an enemy one who is my friend, I have declared war against him

meaning.en: To protect, preserve, guard. The root denotes the act of protecting or preserving - and the divine protection.

lexical_analysis.ibn_faris: الْوِقَايَةُ: الْحِفْظُ. وَوَقَى: صَانَ
lexical_analysis.al_raghib: الْوِقَايَةُ: الْحِفْظُ مِنَ الشَّيْءِ. وَتَقَوَّى: اتَّخَذَ وَقَايَةً مِنَ الْعَذَابِ

quran_examples.ar: وَإِذۡ وَٰعَدۡنَا مُوسَىٰٓ أَرۡبَعِينَ لَيۡلَةًۭ ثُمَّ ٱتَّخَذۡتُمُ ٱلۡعِجۡلَ مِنۢ بَعۡدِهِۦ وَأَنتُمۡ ظَـٰلِمُونَ
quran_examples.en: And [recall] when We made an appointment with Moses for forty nights. Then you took [for yourselves] the calf after him, while you were wrongdoers
quran_examples.context: The appointment of Moses on Mount Sinai

hadith.ar: مَنْ لَمْ يَهْتَمَّ بِأَمۡرِ الْمُسْلِمِينَ فَلَيۡسَ مِنْهُمْ
hadith.en: Whoever does not care about the affairs of the Muslims is not of them

shades.name_ar: التَّقْوَى - اتِّخَاذُ الْوِقَايَةِ، الْحِفْظُ مِنَ الذُّنُوبِ
shades.explanation: The taqwa (piety) in the Quran is the most fundamental concept of the religion. The verse 2:51 establishes that Moses was given the appointment of forty nights. The taqwa in the Quran has multiple levels - the taqwa of the common people (al-taqwa al-'amma - avoiding the major sins), the taqwa of the elite (al-taqwa al-khassa - avoiding all sins), and the taqwa of the elite of the elite (al-taqwa al-khassa al-khassa - being aware of everything besides Allah). The hadith establishes that whoever does not care about the affairs of the Muslims is not of them. Al-Ghazali (Ihya, Book of Piety) treats the taqwa as the foundation of all religion - the one who has taqwa has found the ultimate treasure.
shades.hadith_ar: مَنْ لَمْ يَهْتَمَّ بِأَمۡرِ الْمُسْلِمِينَ فَلَيۡسَ مِنْهُمْ
shades.hadith_en: Whoever does not care about the affairs of the Muslims is not of them

meaning.en: To be full, satisfied. The root denotes the state of being full or satisfied - particularly with food.

lexical_analysis.ibn_faris: الشِّبَعُ: ضِدُّ الْجُوعِ
lexical_analysis.al_raghib: الشِّبَعُ: ضِدُّ الْجُوعِ. وَأَشْبَعَ: أَوْصَلَ إِلَى الشِّبَعِ

quran_examples.ar: وَظَلَّلۡنَا عَلَيۡكُمُ ٱلۡغَمَـٰمَ وَأَنزَلۡنَا عَلَيۡكُمُ ٱلۡمَنَّ وَٱلسَّلۡوَىٰ ۖ كُلُوا۟ مِن طَيِّبَـٰتِ مَا رَزَقۡنَـٰكُمۡ ۚ وَمَا ظَلَمُونَا وَلَـٰكِن كَانُوٓاْ أَنفُسَهُمۡ يَظۡلِمُونَ
quran_examples.en: And We shaded you with clouds and sent down upon you manna and quails, [saying], Eat of the good things We have provided for you. And they wronged Us not, but they were [only] wronging themselves
quran_examples.context: The favors to the Children of Israel

hadith.ar: مَا مَلأَ آدَمِيٌّ وِعَاءً شَرًّا مِنْ بَطۡنٍ
hadith.en: No human fills a vessel worse than his stomach

shades.name_ar: الشِّبَعُ - ضِدُّ الْجُوعِ، شِبَعُ الْبَطۡنِ، شِبَعُ الْقَلۡبِ
shades.explanation: The shiba' (fullness) in the Quran is the state of being full. The verse 2:57 establishes that Allah shaded the Children of Israel with clouds and sent down manna and quails. The shiba' in the Quran has multiple meanings - the physical fullness (al-shiba' al-maddi), the spiritual fullness (al-shiba' al-ruhani), and the fullness of the heart (al-shiba' al-qalb). The hadith establishes that no human fills a vessel worse than his stomach. Al-Ghazali treats the sari' (fasting) as the opposite of shiba' - the one who eats moderately has found the ultimate health.
shades.hadith_ar: مَا مَلأَ آدَمِيٌّ وِعَاءً شَرًّا مِنۡ بَطۡنٍ
shades.hadith_en: No human fills a vessel worse than his stomach

meaning.en: To be wounded, hurt. The root denotes the state of being wounded or hurt.

lexical_analysis.ibn_faris: الْقَرْحُ: الْجُرۡحُ
lexical_analysis.al_raghib: الْقَرْحُ: الْجُرۡحُ فِي الْجِسْمِ. وَالْقُرْحَةُ: الشَّجَّةُ فِي الرَّأْسِ

quran_examples.ar: وَلَا تَقُولُوا۟ لِمَن يُقۡتَلُ فِى سَبِيلِ ٱللَّهِ أَمۡوَٰتٌۢ ۚ بَلۡ أَحۡيَآءٌۭ وَلَـٰكِن لَّا تَشۡعُرُونَ
quran_examples.en: And do not say about those who are killed in the way of Allah, They are dead. Rather, they are alive, but you do not perceive
quran_examples.context: The shuhada are alive with their Lord

hadith.ar: مَا أَصَابَكَ لَمْ يَكُنْ لِيُخْطِئَكَ وَمَا أَخْطَأَكَ لَمْ يَكُنْ لِيُصِيبَكَ
hadith.en: What befalls you was not meant to miss you, and what missed you was not meant to befall you

shades.explanation: The qarh (wound) in the Quran is the state of being wounded. The verse 2:154 establishes that those killed in the way of Allah are not dead but alive. The qarh in the Quran has multiple meanings - the physical wound (al-qarh al-maddi), the spiritual wound (al-qarh al-ruhani), and the wound of the heart (al-qarh al-qalb). The hadith establishes that what befalls you was not meant to miss you. Al-Ghazali treats the qarh as the test of the believer - the one who is wounded by trials has found the ultimate patience.
shades.hadith_ar: مَا أَصَابَكَ لَمْ يَكُنْ لِيُخْطِئَكَ
shades.hadith_en: What befalls you was not meant to miss you

meaning.en: To split, create, originate. The root denotes the act of splitting or creating - and the divine creation.

lexical_analysis.ibn_faris: الْفَطْرُ: الشَّقُّ. وَفَطَرَ: خَلَقَ
lexical_analysis.al_raghib: الْفَطْرُ: الشَّقُّ. وَفَطَرَ السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضَ: خَلَقَهُمَا

quran_examples.ar: هُوَ ٱلَّذِى خَلَقَ لَكُم مَّا فِى ٱلۡأَرۡضِ جَمِيعًۭا ثُمَّ ٱسۡتَوَىٰٓ إِلَى ٱلسَّمَآءِ فَسَوَّىٰهُنَّ سَبۡعَ سَمَـٰوَٰتٍۢ ۚ وَهُوَ بِكُلِّ شَىۡءٍ عَلِيمٌ
quran_examples.en: It is He who created for you all of that which is on the earth. Then He directed Himself to the heaven, and made them seven heavens, and He is Knowing of all things
quran_examples.context: The creation of the heavens and earth

hadith.ar: صُومُوا يَوْمَ عَاشُورَاءَ
hadith.en: Fast the day of Ashura

shades.name_ar: الْفِطْرُ - الشَّقُّ، الْخَلۡقُ، فِطۡرُ اللَّهِ الَّتِي فَطَرَ النَّاسَ عَلَيۡهَا
shades.explanation: The fitr (origination, splitting) in the Quran is one of the most important divine acts. The verse 2:29 establishes the creation of the heavens and earth. The fitr in the Quran has multiple meanings - the splitting of the sky (fatr al-sama'), the creation of the universe (fatr al-kawn), and the natural disposition (al-fitra - the fitrah of man). The hadith establishes that one should fast the day of Ashura. Al-Ghazali (Maqsad al-Asna) treats al-Fatir as one of the divine names - the One who splits the dawn and creates the universe.
shades.hadith_ar: صُومُوا يَوْمَ عَاشُورَاءَ
shades.hadith_en: Fast the day of Ashura

meaning.en: To limit, delimit, define. The root denotes the act of limiting or defining - and the divine limits.

lexical_analysis.ibn_faris: الْحَدُّ: الْفَاصِلُ. وَحَدَّ: فَصَلَ
lexical_analysis.al_raghib: الْحَدُّ: الْحَاجِزُ بَيْنَ الشَّيْئَيْنِ. وَحُدُودُ اللَّهِ: مَا حَرَّمَهُ

quran_examples.ar: أُحِلَّ لَكُمۡ لَيۡلَةَ ٱلصِّيَامِ ٱلرَّفَثُ إِلَىٰ نِسَآئِكُمۡ
quran_examples.en: It has been made permissible for you the night preceding fasting to go to your wives
quran_examples.context: The permission during the night of fasting

hadith.ar: مَنْ عَمِلَ عَمَلًا لَيۡسَ عَلَيۡهِ أَمۡرُنَا فَهُوَ رَدٌّ
hadith.en: Whoever does a deed that is not from our affair, it is rejected

shades.name_ar: الْحُدُودُ - الْحَوَاجِزُ، حُدُودُ اللَّهِ، الْحَدُّ الشَّرۡعِيُّ
shades.explanation: The hudud (limits) in the Quran are the divine limits that the believer should not transgress. The verse 2:187 establishes the permission during the night of fasting. The hudud in the Quran has multiple meanings - the divine limits (hudud Allah), the legal punishments (al-hudud al-shar'iyyah), and the boundaries of the religion (hudud al-din). The hadith establishes that whoever does a deed that is not from our affair, it is rejected. Al-Ghazali treats the hudud as the divine limits - the one who respects the limits of Allah has found the ultimate taqwa.
shades.hadith_ar: مَنْ عَمِلَ عَمَلًا لَيۡسَ عَلَيۡهِ أَمۡرُنَا فَهُوَ رَدٌّ
shades.hadith_en: Whoever does a deed that is not from our affair, it is rejected

meaning.en: To be present, witness. The root denotes the state of being present or witnessing.

lexical_analysis.ibn_faris: الشُّهُودُ: الْحُضُورُ
lexical_analysis.al_raghib: الشُّهُودُ: الْحُضُورُ. وَالْمَشْهَدُ: مَكَانُ الْحُضُورِ

quran_examples.ar: أَمۡ كُنتُمۡ شُهَدَآءَ إِذۡ حَضَرَ يَعۡقُوبَ ٱلۡمَوۡتُ إِذۡ قَالَ لِبَنِيهِ مَا تَعۡبُدُونَ مِنۢ بَعۡدِىۦ قَالُوا۟ نَعۡبُدُ إِلَـٰهَكَ وَإِلَـٰهَ ءَابَآئِكَ إِبۡرَٰهِـۧمَ وَإِسۡمَـٰعِيلَ وَإِسۡحَـٰقَ إِلَـٰهًۭا وَٰحِدًۭا وَنَحۡنُ لَهُۥ مُسۡلِمُونَ
quran_examples.en: Or were you witnesses when death approached Jacob, when he said to his sons, What will you worship after me? They said, We will worship your God and the God of your fathers, Abraham and Ishmael and Isaac - one God. And we are Muslims [in submission] to Him
quran_examples.context: The covenant of Jacob with his sons

hadith.ar: الْمُسْلِمُ مَنْ سَلِمَ الْمُسْلِمُونَ مِنْ لِسَانِهِ وَيَدِهِ
hadith.en: The Muslim is the one from whose tongue and hand the Muslims are safe

shades.explanation: The shuhud (presence) in the Quran is the state of being present or witnessing. The verse 2:133 establishes the covenant of Jacob with his sons. The shuhud in the Quran has multiple meanings - the physical presence (al-shuhud al-maddi), the spiritual presence (al-shuhud al-ruhani), and the witnessing for the truth (al-shuhud li-l-haqq). The hadith establishes that the Muslim is the one from whose tongue and hand the Muslims are safe. Al-Ghazali treats the shuhud as the witnessing of the heart - the one whose heart is present with Allah has found the ultimate reality.
shades.hadith_ar: الْمُسْلِمُ مَنْ سَلِمَ الْمُسْلِمُونَ مِنْ لِسَانِهِ وَيَدِهِ
shades.hadith_en: The Muslim is the one from whose tongue and hand the Muslims are safe

meaning.en: To be clear, manifest, reveal. The root denotes the state of being clear or manifest.

lexical_analysis.ibn_faris: الْجَلَاءُ: الِانْكِشَافُ. وَجَلَا: كَشَفَ
lexical_analysis.al_raghib: الْجَلَاءُ: الِانْكِشَافُ. وَجَلَا الشَّيْءَ: كَشَفَهُ

quran_examples.ar: وَلَقَدۡ أَنزَلۡنَآ إِلَيۡكَ ءَايَـٰتٍۭ بَيِّنَـٰتٍۢ ۖ وَمَا يَكۡفُرُ بِهَآ إِلَّا ٱلۡفَـٰسِقُونَ
quran_examples.en: And We have certainly sent down to you clear verses, and no one would disbelieve in them except the wicked
quran_examples.context: The signs revealed to the Prophet

hadith.ar: لَوْ لَمْ تُذْنِبُوا لَذَهَبَ اللَّهُ بِكُمْ وَلَجَاءَ بِقَوْمٍ يُذْنِبُونَ
hadith.en: If you did not sin, Allah would take you away and bring a people who do sin

shades.name_ar: الْجَلَاءُ - الِانْكِشَافُ، جَلَاءُ الْحَقِّ عَنِ الْبَاطِلِ
shades.explanation: The jala' (manifestation) in the Quran is the state of being clear or manifest. The verse 2:99 establishes the clear verses sent down to the Prophet. The jala' in the Quran is closely related to al-wuduh (clarity) and al-zuhur (manifestation). The hadith establishes that if you did not sin, Allah would take you away. Al-Ghazali treats the jala' as the manifestation of the truth - the truth is always clear, and the one who follows the truth has found the ultimate guidance.
shades.hadith_ar: لَوْ لَمۡ تُذْنِبُوا لَذَهَبَ اللَّهُ بِكُمۡ وَلَجَاءَ بِقَوۡمٍۢ يُذْنِبُونَ
shades.hadith_en: If you did not sin, Allah would take you away and bring a people who do sin

meaning.en: To be good, right, fit. The root denotes the state of being good or right.

lexical_analysis.ibn_faris: الصَّوْلُ: الشَّجَاعَةُ. وَصَالَ: شَجُعَ
lexical_analysis.al_raghib: الصَّوْلُ: الشَّجَاعَةُ. وَصَالَ: أَقْبَلَ

quran_examples.ar: لِّلۡفُقَرَآءِ ٱلَّذِينَ أُحۡصِرُوا۟ فِى سَبِيلِ ٱللَّهِ لَا يَسۡتَطِيعُونَ ضَرۡبًۭا فِى ٱلۡأَرۡضِ يَحۡسَبُهُمُ ٱلۡجَاهِلُ أَغۡنيَآءَ مِنَ ٱلتَّعَفُّفِ تَعۡرِفُهُم بِسِيمَـٰهُمۡ لَا يَسۡـَٔلُونَ ٱلنَّاسَ إِلۡحَافًۭا ۚ وَمَا تُنفِقُوا۟ مِنۡ خَيۡرٍۢ فَإِنَّ ٱللَّهَ بِهِۦ عَلِيمٌ
quran_examples.en: [Charity is] for the poor who have been restricted for the cause of Allah, unable to move about in the land. An ignorant [person] would think them self-sufficient because of their restraint, but you will know them by their [characteristic] sign - they do not ask people persistently [or at all]. And whatever you spend of good - indeed, Allah is Knowing of it

hadith.ar: إِنَّ اللَّهَ يَحِبُّ إِذَا عَمِلَ أَحَدُكُمْ عَمَلًا أَنْ يُتْقِنَهُ
hadith.en: Indeed Allah loves that when one of you does a deed, he does it with excellence

shades.explanation: The sawl (bravery) in the Quran is the state of being brave and strong. The verse 2:273 establishes the charity for the poor.
