The sawl in the Quran is closely related to al-shaja'a (bravery) and al-iqbal (advancing). The hadith establishes that Allah loves excellence in work. Al-Ghazali treats the sawl as the spiritual bravery - the one who advances toward the truth has found the ultimate bravery.
shades.hadith_ar: إِنَّ اللَّهَ يُحِبُّ إِذَا عَمِلَ أَحَدُكُمْ عَمَلًا أَنْ يُتْقِنَهُ
shades.hadith_en: Indeed Allah loves that when one of you does a deed, he does it with excellence

meaning.en: To advise, counsel. The root denotes the act of advising or counseling.

lexical_analysis.ibn_faris: النَّصِيحَةُ: إِخْلَاصُ النَّصِيحَةِ. وَنَصَحَ: أَخْلَصَ
lexical_analysis.al_raghib: النَّصِيحَةُ: كَلِمَةٌ تَدُلُّ عَلَى جُهْدِ الْقَائِلِ فِي إِصْلَاحِ الْمَنْصُوحِ لَهُ

quran_examples.ar: إِنَّا أَرۡسَلۡنَـٰكَ بِٱلۡحَقِّ بَشِيرًۭا وَنَذِيرًۭا ۖ وَلَا تُسۡـَٔلُ عَنۡ أَصۡحَـٰبِ ٱلۡجَحِيمِ
quran_examples.en: Indeed, We have sent you, [O Muhammad], with the truth as a bringer of good tidings and a warner. And you will not be asked about the companions of Hellfire
quran_examples.context: The Prophet sent as a bringer of good tidings and a warner

hadith.ar: الدِّينُ النَّصِيحَةُ
hadith.en: The religion is sincere counsel

shades.name_ar: النَّصِيحَةُ - إِخْلَاصُ النَّصِيحَةِ، نَصِيحَةُ اللَّهِ وَنَصِيحَةُ كِتَابِهِ
shades.explanation: The nasiha (sincere counsel) in the Quran is the act of giving sincere advice. The verse 2:119 establishes that the Prophet was sent as a bringer of good tidings and a warner. The nasiha in the Quran has multiple meanings - the counsel for Allah (nasihat Allah), the counsel for the Prophet (nasihat al-Rasul), and the counsel for the believers (nasihat al-mu'minin). The hadith establishes that the religion is sincere counsel. Al-Ghazali treats the nasiha as the foundation of the religion - the one who gives sincere counsel has fulfilled the religion.
shades.hadith_ar: الدِّينُ النَّصِيحَةُ
shades.hadith_en: The religion is sincere counsel

meaning.en: To shave, smooth. The root denotes the act of shaving or smoothing.

lexical_analysis.ibn_faris: الْجَحْفُ: الْقَطْعُ. وَجَحَفَ: حَلَقَ
lexical_analysis.al_raghib: الْجَحْفُ: الْقَطْعُ الْكَثِيرُ

quran_examples.ar: فَمَن كَانَ مِنكُم مَّرِيضًا أَو بِهِۦ أَذًۭى مِّن رَّأۡسِهِۦ فَفِدۡيَةٌۭ مِّن صِيَامٍ أَو صَدَقَةٍ أَو نُسُكٍۢ
quran_examples.en: And whoever among you is ill or has an ailment of the head [making shaving necessary must offer] a ransom from fasting or charity or sacrifice
quran_examples.context: The ransom for those who cannot shave

hadith.ar: إِنَّ اللَّهَ رَفِيقٌ يُحِبُّ الرِّفْقَ فِي الْأَمْرِ كُلِّهِ
hadith.en: Indeed Allah is gentle and loves gentleness in all affairs

shades.explanation: The jahf (shaving) in the Quran is the act of shaving. The verse 2:196 establishes the ransom for those who cannot shave. The jahf in the Quran is closely related to al-halq (shaving) and al-qat' (cutting). The hadith establishes that Allah is gentle and loves gentleness. Al-Ghazali treats the jahf as the cutting off of attachments - the one who cuts off attachments to the dunya has found the ultimate zuhd.
shades.hadith_ar: إِنَّ اللَّهَ رَفِيقٌ يُحِبُّ الرِّفْقَ فِي الْأَمْرِ كُلِّهِ
shades.hadith_en: Indeed Allah is gentle and loves gentleness in all affairs

meaning.en: To lose, suffer loss. The root denotes the state of loss or suffering loss.

lexical_analysis.ibn_faris: الْخُسْرَانُ: ضِدُّ الرِّبْحِ. وَخَسِرَ: نَقَصَ
lexical_analysis.al_raghib: الْخُسْرَانُ: ضِيدُّ الرِّبْحِ. وَالْخَاسِرُ: مَنْ نَقَصَ مَالُهُ أَوْ أَذْهَبَ حَظَّهُ

quran_examples.ar: أُو۟لَـٰٓئِكَ ٱلَّذِينَ ٱشۡتَرَوُا۟ ٱلضَّلَـٰلَةَ بِٱلۡهُدَىٰ وَٱلۡعَذَابَ بِٱلۡمَغۡفِرَةِ ۚ فَمَآ أَصۡبَرَهُمۡ عَلَى ٱلنَّارِ
quran_examples.en: Those are the ones who have exchanged guidance for error and forgiveness for punishment. How patient they are for the Fire!
quran_examples.context: The ones who exchange guidance for error

hadith.ar: لَا يُلۡدَغُ الْمُؤْمِنُ مِنْ جُحْرٍ وَاحِدٍ مَرَّتَيْنِ
hadith.en: The believer is not stung from the same hole twice

shades.name_ar: الْخُسۡرَانُ - ضِدُّ الرِّبۡحِ، خُسۡرَانُ الدُّنۡيَا وَالْآخِرَةِ
shades.explanation: The khusran (loss) in the Quran is one of the most fearful states. The verse 2:175 establishes that those who exchange guidance for error - how patient they are for the Fire. The khusran in the Quran has multiple meanings - the loss of wealth (khusran al-mal), the loss of religion (khusran al-din), and the ultimate loss (al-khusran al-mubin). The hadith establishes that the believer is not stung from the same hole twice. Al-Ghazali (Ihya, Book of Discipline of the Soul) treats the khusran as the ultimate loss - the one who loses his religion has lost everything.
shades.hadith_ar: لَا يُلۡدَغُ الْمُؤْمِنُ مِنۡ جُحۡرٍ وَاحِدٍ مَرَّتَيۡنِ
shades.hadith_en: The believer is not stung from the same hole twice

meaning.en: To be bad, wretched, fail. The root denotes the state of being bad or wretched - and the failure of an attempt.

lexical_analysis.ibn_faris: الْخَيْبَةُ: الْخُسْرَانُ. وَخَابَ: خَسِرَ
lexical_analysis.al_raghib: الْخَيْبَةُ: الْخُسْرَانُ. وَخَابَ: خَسِرَ وَحَابَ

quran_examples.ar: إِنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوا۟ وَٱلَّذِينَ هَادُوا۟ وَٱلنَّصَـٰرَىٰ وَٱلصَّـٰبِـِٔينَ مَنۡ ءَامَنَ بِٱللَّهِ وَٱلۡيَوۡمِ ٱلۡأَخِرِ وَعَمِلَ صَـٰلِحًۭا فَلَهُمۡ أَجۡرُهُمۡ عِندَ رَبِّهِمۡ وَلَا خَوۡفٌ عَلَيۡهِمۡ وَلَا هُمۡ يَحۡزَنُونَ
quran_examples.en: Indeed, those who believed and those who were Jews or Christians or Sabeans - those [among them] who believed in Allah and the Last Day and did righteousness - will have their reward with their Lord, and there will be no fear concerning them, nor will they grieve
quran_examples.context: The believers among the People of the Book

hadith.ar: مَنْ غَشَّنَا فَلَيۡسَ مِنَّا
hadith.en: Whoever cheats us is not of us

shades.explanation: The khayba (wretchedness) in the Quran is the state of being wretched or losing. The verse 2:62 establishes the believers among the People of the Book - they will have their reward. The khayba in the Quran has multiple meanings - the failure of an attempt (khayba al-muhawala), the loss in the Hereafter (khayba al-akhira), and the divine curse (khayba al-la'na). The hadith establishes that whoever cheats us is not of us. Al-Ghazali treats the khayba as the ultimate loss - the one who fails in his ultimate goal has found the khayba.
shades.hadith_ar: مَنۡ غَشَّنَا فَلَيۡسَ مِنَّا
shades.hadith_en: Whoever cheats us is not of us

meaning.en: To invoke, call upon, supplicate. The root denotes the act of invoking or calling upon - particularly Allah.

lexical_analysis.ibn_faris: الدُّعَاءُ: الِاسْتِغَاثَةُ. وَدَعَا: طَلَبَ
lexical_analysis.al_raghib: الدُّعَاءُ: طَلَبُ الْإِقْبَالِ عَلَى الشَّيْءِ بِقَوْلٍ أَوْ فِعْلٍ

quran_examples.ar: وَإِن كُنتُمۡ فِى رَيۡبٍۢ مِّمَّا نَزَّلۡنَا عَلَىٰ عَبۡدِنَا فَأۡتُوا۟ بِسُورَةٍۢ مِّن مِّثۡلِهِۦ وَٱدۡعُوا۟ شُهَدَآءَكُم مِّن دُونِ ٱللَّهِ إِن كُنتُمۡ صَـٰدِقِينَ
quran_examples.en: And if you are in doubt about what We have sent down upon Our Servant, then produce a surah the like thereof and call upon your witnesses other than Allah, if you are truthful
quran_examples.context: The challenge to produce a surah like the Quran

hadith.ar: الدُّعَاءُ هُوَ الْعِبَادَةُ
hadith.en: Supplication is worship

shades.name_ar: الدُّعَاءُ - طَلَبُ الشَّيْءِ، دُعَاءُ اللَّهِ أَفۡضَلُ الْعِبَادَاتِ
shades.explanation: The du'a (supplication) in the Quran is one of the most fundamental acts of worship. The verse 2:23 establishes the challenge to produce a surah like the Quran. The du'a in the Quran has multiple meanings - the invocation of Allah (du'a Allah), the supplication to Allah (du'a ila Allah), and the call to Allah (du'a li-Allah). The hadith establishes that supplication is worship. Al-Ghazali (Ihya, Book of Supplication) treats the du'a as the highest form of worship - the one who calls upon Allah has found the ultimate connection.
shades.hadith_ar: الدُّعَاءُ هُوَ الْعِبَادَةُ
shades.hadith_en: Supplication is worship

meaning.en: To come out, exit. The root denotes the act of coming out or exiting.

lexical_analysis.ibn_faris: الْخُرُوجُ: ضِدُّ الدُّخُولِ
lexical_analysis.al_raghib: الْخُرُوجُ: ضِدُّ الدُّخُولِ. وَخَرَجَ: بَرَزَ

quran_examples.ar: رَبَّنَا وَٱجۡعَلۡنَا مُسۡلِمَيۡنِ لَكَ وَمِن ذُرِّيَّتِنَآ أُمَّةًۭ مُّسۡلِمَةًۭ لَّكَ وَأَرِنَا مَنَاسِكَنَا وَتُبۡ عَلَيۡنَآ ۖ إِنَّكَ أَنتَ ٱلتَّوَّابُ ٱلرَّحِيمُ
quran_examples.en: Our Lord, and make us Muslims [in submission] to You and from our descendants a Muslim nation [in submission] to You. And show us our rites and accept our repentance. Indeed, You are the Accepting of Repentance, the Merciful
quran_examples.context: The prayer of Ibrahim and Ismail

hadith.ar: خَيۡرُ الْأَعۡمَالِ أَدۡوَمُهَا
hadith.en: The best of deeds are the most consistent

shades.name_ar: الْخُرُوجُ - ضِدُّ الدُّخُولِ، خُرُوجُ الْإِسَانِ مِنَ الدُّنۡيَا
shades.explanation: The khuruj (coming out) in the Quran is one of the most common actions. The verse 2:128 establishes the prayer of Ibrahim and Ismail. The khuruj in the Quran has multiple meanings - the physical coming out (al-khuruj al-maddi), the spiritual coming out (al-khuruj al-ruhani), and the departure from this world (al-khuruj min al-dunya). The hadith establishes that the best of deeds are the most consistent. Al-Ghazali treats the khuruj as the exit from the dunya - the one who exits the dunya in taqwa has found the ultimate success.
shades.hadith_ar: خَيۡرُ الْأَعۡمَالِ أَدۡوَمُهَا
shades.hadith_en: The best of deeds are the most consistent

meaning.en: To be easy, gentle. The root denotes the state of being easy or gentle.

lexical_analysis.ibn_faris: الْيَهَفُ: اللِّينُ
lexical_analysis.al_raghib: الْيَهَفُ: اللِّينُ. وَيَهِفَ: لَانَ

quran_examples.ar: وَلَقَدۡ ءَاتَيۡنَا مُوسَى ٱلۡكِتَـٰبَ وَقَفَّيۡنَا مِنۢ بَعۡدِهِۦ بِٱلرُّسُلِ ۖ وَءَاتَيۡنَا عِيسَى ٱبۡنَ مَرۡيَمَ ٱلۡبَيِّنَـٰتِ وَأَيَّدۡنَـٰهُ بِرُوحِ ٱلۡقُدُسِ
quran_examples.en: And We had certainly given Moses the Book and followed up after him with messengers. And We gave Jesus, the son of Mary, clear proofs and supported him with the Pure Spirit

hadith.ar: لَا يُكَلِّفُ اللَّهُ نَفۡسًا إِلَّا وُسۡعَهَا
hadith.en: Allah does not burden a soul beyond that it can bear

shades.explanation: The yahfa (gentleness) in the Quran is the state of being gentle or easy. The verse 2:87 establishes the support of the messengers. The yahfa in the Quran is closely related to al-rifq (gentleness) and al-lutf (kindness). The hadith establishes that Allah does not burden a soul beyond that it can bear. Al-Ghazali treats the yahfa as the divine gentleness - the one who is gentle with the servants has been blessed by Allah.
shades.hadith_ar: لَا يُكَلِّفُ اللَّهُ نَفۡسًا إِلَّا وُسۡعَهَا
shades.hadith_en: Allah does not burden a soul beyond that it can bear

meaning.en: To be quick, swift, rapid. The root denotes the state of being quick or swift.

lexical_analysis.ibn_faris: السُّرْعَةُ: ضِدُّ الْبُطْءِ. وَسَرُعَ: خَفَّ
lexical_analysis.al_raghib: السُّرْعَةُ: ضِدُّ الْبُطْءِ. وَالْأَسْرَعُ: الْكَثِيرُ السُّرْعَةِ

quran_examples.ar: مَّن ذَا ٱلَّذِى يُقۡرِضُ ٱللَّهَ قَرۡضًا حَسَنًۭا فَيُضَـٰعِفَهُۥ لَهُۥٓ أَضۡعَافًۭا كَثِيرَةًۭ ۚ وَٱللَّهُ يَقۡبِضُ وَيَبۡصُۜطُ وَإِلَيۡهِ تُرۡجَعُونَ
quran_examples.en: Who is it that will lend to Allah a goodly loan so that He may multiply it for him many times over? And it is Allah who restrains and grants abundance, and to Him you will be returned
quran_examples.context: The parable of lending to Allah

hadith.ar: أَنْقَذْتُكَ مِنَ الْعَدْلِ بِفَضْلِ رَحْمَتِي
hadith.en: I saved you from justice by My mercy

shades.explanation: The sur'a (swiftness) in the Quran is one of the states of action. The verse 2:245 establishes the parable of lending to Allah. The sur'a in the Quran has multiple meanings - the physical swiftness (al-sur'a al-maddiyyah), the spiritual swiftness (al-sur'a al-ruhaniyyah), and the swiftness to good deeds (al-sur'a ila al-khayr). The hadith establishes that Allah saved the servant from justice by His mercy. Al-Ghazali treats the sur'a as the swiftness to good deeds - the one who is swift to good deeds has found the ultimate success.
shades.hadith_ar: أَنْقَذْتُكَ مِنَ الْعَدْلِ بِفَضْلِ رَحْمَتِي
shades.hadith_en: I saved you from justice by My mercy

meaning.en: To be small, young. The root denotes the state of being small or young.

lexical_analysis.ibn_faris: الصَّقْرُ: الصِّغَرُ
lexical_analysis.al_raghib: الصَّقْرُ: الصِّغَرُ. وَصَقَرَ: صَغُرَ

quran_examples.ar: وَعَلَّمَ ءَادَمَ ٱلۡأَسۡمَآءَ كُلَّهَا ثُمَّ عَرَضَهُمۡ عَلَى ٱلۡمَلَـٰٓئِكَةِ فَقَالَ أَنۢبِـُٔونِى بِأَسۡمَآءِ هَـٰٓؤُلَآءِ إِن كُنتُمۡ صَـٰدِقِينَ
quran_examples.en: And He taught Adam the names of all things; then He presented them to the angels and said, Tell Me the names of these if you are truthful
quran_examples.context: The teaching of Adam the names

hadith.ar: إِنَّ أَوَّلَ مَا خَلَقَ اللَّهُ الْقَلَمَ فَقَالَ لَهُ: اكْتُبْ
hadith.en: Indeed the first thing Allah created was the pen, and He said to it: Write

shades.explanation: The saqr (smallness) in the Quran is the state of being small. The verse 2:31 establishes the teaching of Adam the names. The saqr in the Quran is closely related to al-sighar (smallness) and al-suqra (smallness of age). The hadith establishes that the first thing Allah created was the pen. Al-Ghazali treats the saqr as the smallness of the creation before the greatness of the Creator - the one who knows his smallness before Allah has found the ultimate humility.
shades.hadith_ar: إِنَّ أَوَّلَ مَا خَلَقَ اللَّهُ الْقَلَمَ
shades.hadith_en: Indeed the first thing Allah created was the pen

meaning.en: To be at rest, peace. The root denotes the state of being at rest or peaceful.

lexical_analysis.ibn_faris: الرَّوْمُ: ضِدُّ الْجَزَعِ. وَرَامَ: سَكَنَ
lexical_analysis.al_raghib: الرَّوْمُ: ضِدُّ الْجَزَعِ. وَرَامَ: طَلَبَ

quran_examples.ar: وَمَنۡ أَظۡلَمُ مِمَّن مَّنَعَ مَسَـٰجِدَ ٱللَّهِ أَن يُذۡكَرَ فِيهَا ٱسۡمُهُۥ وَسَعَىٰ فِىٓ خَرَابِهَآ
quran_examples.en: And who is more unjust than he who prevents the mention of Allah's name in His mosques and strives toward their destruction?
quran_examples.context: The condemnation of those who prevent the mention of Allah in mosques

hadith.ar: إِنَّ اللَّهَ يَرْضَى لَكُمْ ثَلَاثًا وَيَسْخَطُ لَكُمْ ثَلَاثًا
hadith.en: Indeed Allah is pleased with you three times and angry with you three times

shades.name_en: ar-Rum - The Rest and the People
shades.name_ar: الرُّومُ - ضِدُّ الْجَزَعِ، الرُّومُ قَوْمٌ مِنَ النَّصَارَى
shades.explanation: The rum (rest) in the Quran is the state of being at rest. The verse 2:114 establishes the condemnation of those who prevent the mention of Allah in mosques. The rum in the Quran has multiple meanings - the rest (al-rum - opposite of panic), the Romans (al-Rum - the people of the Byzantine Empire), and the seeking (al-rum - seeking something). The hadith establishes that Allah is pleased with you three times and angry with you three times. Al-Ghazali treats the rum as the peace of the heart - the one who finds peace in Allah has found the ultimate rest.
shades.hadith_ar: إِنَّ اللَّهَ يَرْضَى لَكُمْ ثَلَاثًا وَيَسْخَطُ لَكُمْ ثَلَاثًا
shades.hadith_en: Indeed Allah is pleased with you three times and angry with you three times

meaning.en: To inform, prophesy, notify. The root denotes the act of informing or prophesying.

lexical_analysis.ibn_faris: النَّبَأُ: الْخَبَرُ الْعَظِيمُ. وَنَبَأَ: أَخْبَرَ
lexical_analysis.al_raghib: النَّبَأُ: خَبَرٌ مَا يَتَوَقَّعُ مَوْقِعَهُ. وَالنَّبِيُّ: الَّذِي يُنْبِئُ عَنِ اللَّهِ

quran_examples.ar: وَمِنۡهُمۡ أُمِّيُّونَ لَا يَعۡلَمُونَ ٱلۡكِتَـٰبَ إِلَّآ أَمَانِىَّ وَإِنۡ هُمۡ إِلَّا يَظُنُّونَ
quran_examples.en: And among them are unlettered ones who do not know the Scripture except in wishful thinking, but they are only assuming

hadith.ar: أَنَا أَوْلَى النَّاسِ بِعِيسَى ابْنِ مَرْيَمَ فِي الدُّنْيَا وَالْآخِرَةِ
hadith.en: I am the closest of people to Jesus, son of Mary, in this world and the Hereafter

shades.name_en: an-Naba - The Information and the Prophecy
shades.name_ar: النَّبَأُ - الْخَبَرُ الْمُهِمُّ، نَبَأُ اللَّهِ، النُّبُوءَةُ
shades.explanation: The naba (information, prophecy) in the Quran is the act of informing or prophesying. The verse 2:78 establishes the unlettered among the Jews. The naba in the Quran has multiple meanings - the news (al-naba al-khabar), the prophecy (al-naba al-nabawi), and the divine information (al-naba al-ilahi). The hadith establishes that the Prophet is the closest of people to Jesus. Al-Ghazali treats the naba as the divine information - the one who receives the divine information has been blessed by Allah.
shades.hadith_ar: أَنَا أَوْلَى النَّاسِ بِعِيسَى ابْنِ مَرْيَمَ
shades.hadith_en: I am the closest of people to Jesus, son of Mary

meaning.en: To stand, stop, pause. The root denotes the act of standing or stopping.

lexical_analysis.ibn_faris: الْوُقُوفُ: ضِدُّ الْجُلُوسِ. وَوَقَفَ: ثَبَتَ
lexical_analysis.al_raghib: الْوُقُوفُ: ضِدُّ الْجُلُوسِ. وَالْمَوْقِفُ: مَكَانُ الْوُقُوفِ

quran_examples.ar: حَـٰفِظُوا۟ عَلَى ٱلصَّلَوَٰتِ وَٱلصَّلَوٰةِ ٱلۡوُسۡطَىٰ وَقُومُوا۟ لِلَّهِ قَـٰنِتِينَ
quran_examples.en: Maintain with care the [obligatory] prayers and [in particular] the middle prayer and stand before Allah, devoutly obedient
quran_examples.context: The command to maintain the prayers and stand before Allah

hadith.ar: صَلُّوا كَمَا رَأَيْتُمُونِي أُصَلِّي
hadith.en: Pray as you have seen me pray

shades.name_en: al-Wuquf - The Standing and the Pause
shades.name_ar: الْوُقُوفُ - ضِدُّ الْجُلُوسِ، الْوُقُوفُ عِنْدَ اللَّهِ يَوْمَ الْقِيَامَةِ
shades.explanation: The wuquf (standing, pause) in the Quran is the act of standing. The verse 2:238 establishes the command to maintain the prayers. The wuquf in the Quran has multiple meanings - the physical standing (al-wuquf al-maddi), the spiritual standing (al-wuquf al-ruhani), and the standing before Allah on the Day of Resurrection (al-wuquf 'inda Allah). The hadith establishes that one should pray as the Prophet prayed. Al-Ghazali treats the wuquf as the standing before Allah - the one who stands before Allah in prayer has found the ultimate connection.
shades.hadith_ar: صَلُّوا كَمَا رَأَيْتُمُونِي أُصَلِّي
shades.hadith_en: Pray as you have seen me pray

meaning.en: To bury. The root denotes the act of burying the dead.

lexical_analysis.ibn_faris: الْقَبْرُ: مَوْضِعُ الدَّفْنِ. وَقَبَرَ: دَفَنَ
lexical_analysis.al_raghib: الْقَبْرُ: الْمَوْضِعُ الَّذِي يُدْفَنُ فِيهِ الْمَيِّتُ

quran_examples.ar: كَيۡفَ تَكۡفُرُونَ بِٱللَّهِ وَكُنتُمۡ أَمۡوَٰتًۭا فَأَحۡيَـٰكُمۡ ۖ ثُمَّ يُمِيتُكُمۡ ثُمَّ يُحۡيِيكُمۡ ثُمَّ إِلَيۡهِ تُرۡجَعُونَ
quran_examples.en: How can you disbelieve in Allah when you were lifeless and He brought you to life; then He will cause you to die, then He will bring you to life, and then to Him you will be returned
quran_examples.context: The cycles of life and death

hadith.ar: كَانَ أَحَبَّ الْأَعْمَالِ إِلَى اللَّهِ أَدْوَمَهَا وَإِنْ قَلَّ
hadith.en: The most beloved of deeds to Allah are the most consistent, even if small

shades.name_ar: الْقَبْرُ - مَوْضِعُ الدَّفْنِ، قَبْرُ الْمُسْلِمِ مَحْفُوفٌ بِالْمَلَائِكَةِ
shades.explanation: The qabr (grave) in the Quran is the place of burial. The verse 2:28 establishes the cycles of life and death. The qabr in the Quran has multiple meanings - the physical grave (al-qabr al-maddi), the metaphorical grave (al-qabr al-majazi - the state of being in the grave), and the blessed grave (al-qabr al-mubaraka). The hadith establishes that the most beloved of deeds to Allah are the most consistent. Al-Ghazali (Ihya, Book of the Remembrance of Death) treats the qabr as the first station of the Hereafter - the one who remembers the grave has begun the journey of self-purification.
shades.hadith_ar: كَانَ أَحَبَّ الْأَعْمَالِ إِلَى اللَّهِ أَدْوَمَهَا وَإِنْ قَلَّ
shades.hadith_en: The most beloved of deeds to Allah are the most consistent, even if small

meaning.en: To flow, pour. The root denotes the act of flowing or pouring.

lexical_analysis.ibn_faris: السَّيَلانُ: ضِدُّ الْجُمُودِ
lexical_analysis.al_raghib: السَّيَلانُ: ضِدُّ الْجُمُودِ. وَسَالَ الشَّيْءُ: مَضَى

quran_examples.ar: ثُمَّ قَسَتۡ قُلُوبُكُم مِّنۢ بَعۡدِ ذَٰلِكَ فَهِىَ كَٱلۡحِجَارَةِ أَوۡ أَشَدُّ قَسۡوَةًۭ ۚ وَإِنَّ مِنَ ٱلۡحِجَارَةِ لَمَا يَتَفَجَّرُ مِنۡهُ ٱلۡأَنۡهَـٰرُ
quran_examples.en: Then your hearts became hardened after that, being like stones or even harder. For indeed, there are stones from which rivers burst forth

hadith.ar: إِنَّ الْأَرْوَاحَ تَجُولُ فِي أَجْسَادِ الْبَهَائِمِ
hadith.en: Indeed the spirits roam in the bodies of animals

shades.name_ar: السَّيَلانُ - ضِدُّ الْجُمُودِ، سَيَلانُ الْمَاءِ، سَيَلانُ الدُّمُوعِ
shades.explanation: The sayl (flow) in the Quran is the act of flowing. The verse 2:74 establishes the hardness of the hearts and the flowing of the rivers from the stones. The sayl in the Quran has multiple meanings - the flowing of water (sayl al-ma'), the flowing of tears (sayl al-dumuw'), and the flowing of rivers (sayl al-anhar). The hadith establishes that the spirits roam in the bodies of animals. Al-Ghazali treats the sayl as the flowing of tears - the one whose tears flow from the fear of Allah has found the ultimate sign of taqwa.
shades.hadith_ar: إِنَّ الْأَرْوَاحَ تَجُولُ فِي أَجْسَادِ الْبَهَائِمِ
shades.hadith_en: Indeed the spirits roam in the bodies of animals

meaning.en: To be good, beautiful, excellent. The root denotes the state of being good or beautiful.

lexical_analysis.ibn_faris: الْحُسْنُ: ضِدُّ الْقُبْحِ. وَحَسُنَ: جَمُلَ
lexical_analysis.al_raghib: الْحُسْنُ: ضِدُّ الْقُبْحِ. وَالْحَسَنُ: الْجَمِيلُ

quran_examples.ar: وَلَا تُلۡقُوا۟ بِأَيۡدِيكُمۡ إِلَى ٱلتَّهۡلُكَةِ وَأَحۡسِنُوٓاْ ۚ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ يُحِبُّ ٱلۡمُحۡسِنِينَ
quran_examples.en: And do not throw [yourselves] with your own hands into destruction. And do good; indeed, Allah loves the doers of good

hadith.ar: إِنَّ اللَّهَ جَمِيلٌ يُحِبُّ الْجَمَالَ
hadith.en: Indeed Allah is beautiful and loves beauty

shades.name_en: al-Husn - The Beauty and the Goodness
shades.name_ar: الْحُسْنُ - ضِدُّ الْقُبْحِ، الْجَمَالُ، حُسْنُ الْخُلُقِ
shades.explanation: The husn (beauty, goodness) in the Quran is one of the most fundamental divine attributes. The verse 2:195 establishes that Allah loves the doers of good (al-muhsinin). The husn in the Quran has multiple meanings - the physical beauty (al-husn al-maddi), the spiritual beauty (al-husn al-ruhani), and the goodness of deeds (husn al-'amal). The hadith establishes that Allah is beautiful and loves beauty. Al-Ghazali (Ihya, Book of Etiquette) treats the husn as the beauty of the soul - the one whose soul is beautiful has found the ultimate husn.
shades.hadith_ar: إِنَّ اللَّهَ جَمِيلٌ يُحِبُّ الْجَمَالَ
shades.hadith_en: Indeed Allah is beautiful and loves beauty

meaning.en: To cause, curse, blame. The root denotes the act of causing or cursing.

lexical_analysis.ibn_faris: السَّبُّ: الشَّتْمُ. وَسَبَّ: شَتَمَ
lexical_analysis.al_raghib: السَّبُّ: الشَّتْمُ. وَالْمَسَبَّةُ: مَا يُسَبُّ بِهِ

quran_examples.ar: إِنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ يَكۡتُمُونَ مَآ أَنزَلۡنَا مِنَ ٱلۡبَيِّنَـٰتِ وَٱلۡهُدَىٰ مِنۢ بَعۡدِ مَا بَيَّنَّـٰهُ لِلنَّاسِ فِى ٱلۡكِتَـٰبِ ۙ أُو۟لَـٰٓئِكَ يَلۡعَنُهُمُ ٱللَّهُ وَيَلۡعَنُهُمُ ٱللَّـٰعِنُونَ
quran_examples.en: Indeed, those who conceal what We sent down of clear proofs and guidance - after We made it clear for them in the Book - those are cursed by Allah and cursed by those who curse
quran_examples.context: The curse upon those who conceal revelation

hadith.ar: سِبَابُ الْمُسْلِمِ فُسُوقٌ
hadith.en: Cursing a Muslim is disobedience

shades.name_ar: السَّبُّ - الشَّتْمُ، سَبُّ الْكَافِرِينَ لِلْمُؤْمِنِينَ، لَعْنَةُ اللَّهِ لِلظَّالِمِينَ
shades.explanation: The sabb (cursing) in the Quran is the act of cursing or insulting. The verse 2:159 establishes that those who conceal revelation are cursed by Allah and the cursers. The sabb in the Quran has multiple meanings - the cursing of the disbelievers (sabb al-kuffar), the cursing of the oppressors (la'nat Allah li-l-zalimin), and the insulting of the believers (sabb al-mu'minin). The hadith establishes that cursing a Muslim is disobedience. Al-Ghazali treats the sabb as the consequence of oppression - the one who oppresses the believers has earned the curse of Allah.
shades.hadith_ar: سِبَابُ الْمُسْلِمِ فُسُوقٌ
shades.hadith_en: Cursing a Muslim is disobedience

meaning.en: To repel, refuse, return. The root denotes the act of repelling or returning.

lexical_analysis.ibn_faris: الرَّدُّ: الرَّجْعُ. وَرَدَّ: صَرَفَ
lexical_analysis.al_raghib: الرَّدُّ: الرَّجْعُ. وَرَدَّ الشَّيْءَ: رَجَّعَهُ

quran_examples.ar: وَمَن يَرۡتَدِدۡ مِنكُمۡ عَن دِينِهِۦ فَيَمُتۡ وَهُوَ كَافِرٌ فَأُو۟لَـٰٓئِكَ حَبِطَتۡ أَعۡمَـٰلُهُمۡ فِى ٱلدُّنۡيَا وَٱلۡءَاخِرَةِ
quran_examples.en: And whoever of you turns back from his religion and dies as a disbeliever - their deeds will be nullified in this world and the Hereafter
quran_examples.context: The nullification of deeds for apostasy

hadith.ar: رُدُّوا الْمَرِيضَ إِلَى الْبَيْتِ وَاسْقُوهُ مِنْ بُرَادَةِ السَّمَاءِ
hadith.en: Return the sick to their homes and give them rain water

shades.name_en: ar-Radd - The Repelling and the Return
shades.name_ar: الرَّدُّ - الرَّجْعُ، رَدُّ الشَّيْءِ عَنْ وَجْهِهِ
shades.explanation: The radd (repelling, return) in the Quran is the act of returning or repelling. The verse 2:217 establishes the nullification of deeds for apostasy. The radd in the Quran has multiple meanings - the physical repelling (al-radd al-maddi), the spiritual repelling (al-radd al-ruhani), and the divine return (al-radd al-ilahi). The hadith establishes the prayer for rain. Al-Ghazali treats the radd as the divine return - the one whose deeds are returned to Allah in good state has found the ultimate success.
shades.hadith_ar: رُدُّوا الْمَرِيضَ إِلَى الْبَيْتِ وَاسْقُوهُ مِنْ بُرَادَةِ السَّمَاءِ
shades.hadith_en: Return the sick to their homes and give them rain water

meaning.en: To take refuge, shelter. The root denotes the act of taking refuge or sheltering.

lexical_analysis.ibn_faris: اللُّجُوءُ: الِاعْتِصَامُ. وَلَجَأَ: اعْتَصَمَ
lexical_analysis.al_raghib: اللُّجُوءُ: الِاعْتِصَامُ. وَلَجَأَ: لَجَأَ

quran_examples.ar: وَإِذۡ قَالَ مُوسَىٰ لِقَوۡمِهِۦٓ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ يَأۡمُرُكُمۡ أَن تَذۡبَحُوا۟ بَقَرَةًۭ
quran_examples.en: And [recall] when Moses said to his people, Indeed Allah commands you to slaughter a cow
quran_examples.context: The command to slaughter a cow

hadith.ar: مَنْ أَقَالَ نَادِمًا أَقَالَ اللَّهُ
hadith.en: Whoever cancels a sale out of remorse, Allah will cancel his sins

shades.explanation: The lija' (refuge) in the Quran is the act of taking refuge or sheltering. The verse 2:67 establishes the command to slaughter a cow. The lija' in the Quran has multiple meanings - the physical refuge (al-lija' al-maddi), the spiritual refuge (al-lija' al-ruhani), and the refuge to Allah (al-lija' ila Allah). The hadith establishes the cancellation of the sale out of remorse. Al-Ghazali treats the lija' as the refuge to Allah - the one who takes refuge to Allah has found the ultimate protection.
shades.hadith_ar: مَنْ أَقَالَ نَادِمًا أَقَالَ اللَّهُ
shades.hadith_en: Whoever cancels a sale out of remorse, Allah will cancel his sins

meaning.en: To feel, perceive, sense. The root denotes the act of feeling or perceiving.

lexical_analysis.ibn_faris: الْإِحْسَاسُ: ضِدُّ الْإِغْفَالِ
lexical_analysis.al_raghib: الْإِحْسَاسُ: الشُّعُورُ. وَأَحَسَّ: شَعَرَ

quran_examples.ar: يُخَـٰدِعُونَ ٱللَّهَ وَٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوا۟ وَمَا يَخۡدَعُونَ إِلَّآ أَنفُسَهُمۡ وَمَا يَشۡعُرُونَ
quran_examples.en: They [think to] deceive Allah and those who believe, but they deceive not except themselves and they perceive [it] not

hadith.ar: إِنَّ اللَّهَ يُحِبُّ الرِّفْقَ فِي الْأَمْرِ كُلِّهِ
hadith.en: Indeed Allah loves gentleness in all affairs

shades.explanation: The ihsas (perception) in the Quran is the act of feeling or perceiving. The verse 2:9 establishes that the hypocrites try to deceive Allah and the believers, but they do not perceive. The ihsas in the Quran has multiple meanings - the physical perception (al-ihsas al-maddi), the spiritual perception (al-ihsas al-ruhani), and the perception of the truth (al-ihsas al-haqq). The hadith establishes that Allah loves gentleness in all affairs. Al-Ghazali treats the ihsas as the perception of the heart - the one whose heart perceives the truth has found the ultimate ihsas.
shades.hadith_ar: إِنَّ اللَّهَ يُحِبُّ الرِّفْقَ فِي الْأَمْرِ كُلِّهِ
shades.hadith_en: Indeed Allah loves gentleness in all affairs

meaning.en: To give life, revive, quicken. The root denotes the act of giving life or reviving - and the divine life-giving.

lexical_analysis.ibn_faris: الْإِحْيَاءُ: ضِدُّ الْإِمَاتَةِ
lexical_analysis.al_raghib: الْإِحْيَاءُ: ضِدُّ الْإِمَاتَةِ. وَأَحْيَا: جَعَلَ حَيًّا

quran_examples.ar: كَيۡفَ تَكۡفُرُونَ بِٱللَّهِ وَكُنتُمۡ أَمۡوَٰتًۭا فَأَحۡيَـٰكُمۡ ۖ ثُمَّ يُمِيتُكُمۡ ثُمَّ يُحۡيِيكُمۡ ثُمَّ إِلَيۡهِ تُرۡجَعُونَ
quran_examples.en: How can you disbelieve in Allah when you were lifeless and He brought you to life; then He will cause you to die, then He will bring you to life, and then to Him you will be returned
quran_examples.context: The cycles of life and death

hadith.ar: أُحَيِّيكُمْ بِآيَاتِ اللَّهِ
hadith.en: I give you life by the verses of Allah

shades.name_ar: الْإِحْيَاءُ - ضِدُّ الْإِمَاتَةِ، إِحْيَاءُ الْقَلْبِ بِالْإِيمَانِ
shades.explanation: The ihya (quickening) in the Quran is the act of giving life. The verse 2:28 establishes the cycles of life and death. The ihya in the Quran has multiple meanings - the physical life-giving (al-ihya al-maddi), the spiritual life-giving (al-ihya al-ruhani), and the ultimate life-giving (al-ihya al-akhira). The hadith establishes that the Prophet gives life by the verses of Allah. Al-Ghazali (Maqsad al-Asna) treats al-Muhyi as one of the divine names - the One who gives life and causes death.
shades.hadith_ar: أُحَيِّيكُمْ بِآيَاتِ اللَّهِ
shades.hadith_en: I give you life by the verses of Allah

meaning.en: To cause death, make die. The root denotes the act of causing death - and the divine death-giving.

lexical_analysis.ibn_faris: الْإِمَاتَةُ: ضِدُّ الْإِحْيَاءِ
lexical_analysis.al_raghib: الْإِمَاتَةُ: ضِدُّ الْإِحْيَاءِ. وَأَمَاتَ: جَعَلَ مَيِّتًا

quran_examples.ar: كَيۡفَ تَكۡفُرُونَ بِٱللَّهِ وَكُنتُمۡ أَمۡوَٰتًۭا فَأَحۡيَـٰكُمۡ ۖ ثُمَّ يُمِيتُكُمۡ ثُمَّ يُحۡيِيكُمۡ ثُمَّ إِلَيۡهِ تُرۡجَعُونَ
quran_examples.en: How can you disbelieve in Allah when you were lifeless and He brought you to life; then He will cause you to die, then He will bring you to life, and then to Him you will be returned
quran_examples.context: The cycles of life and death

hadith.ar: لَا يَمُوتُ نَفَسٌ حَتَّى تَسْتَوْفِيَ رِزْقَهَا
hadith.en: No soul dies until it has received its full provision

shades.name_ar: الْإِمَاتَةُ - ضِدُّ الْإِحْيَاءِ، إِمَاتَةُ اللَّهِ لِلْخَلْقِ
shades.explanation: The imata (death-giving) in the Quran is the act of causing death. The verse 2:28 establishes the cycles of life and death. The imata in the Quran has multiple meanings - the physical death (al-imata al-maddiyyah), the spiritual death (al-imata al-ruhaniyyah), and the death of the heart (imata al-qalb). The hadith establishes that no soul dies until it has received its full provision. Al-Ghazali (Maqsad al-Asna) treats al-Mumit as one of the divine names - the One who causes death.
shades.hadith_ar: لَا يَمُوتُ نَفَسٌ حَتَّى تَسْتَوْفِيَ رِزْقَهَا
shades.hadith_en: No soul dies until it has received its full provision

meaning.en: To hope, expect. The root denotes the act of hoping or expecting.

lexical_analysis.ibn_faris: الرَّجَاءُ: ضِدُّ الْيَأْسِ. وَرَجَا: أَمَّلَ
lexical_analysis.al_raghib: الرَّجَاءُ: ضِدُّ الْيَأْسِ. وَالرَّجَاءُ: الْأَمَلُ

quran_examples.ar: إِنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوا۟ وَٱلَّذِينَ هَاجَرُوا۟ وَجَـٰهَدُوا۟ فِى سَبِيلِ ٱللَّهِ أُو۟لَـٰٓئِكَ يَرۡجُونَ رَحۡمَتَ ٱللَّهِ ۚ وَٱللَّهُ غَفُورٌۭ رَّحِيمٌ
quran_examples.en: Indeed, those who believed and those who emigrated and fought for the cause of Allah - those hope for the mercy of Allah. And Allah is Forgiving and Merciful
quran_examples.context: The hope of the believers for the mercy of Allah

hadith.ar: يَقُولُ اللَّهُ: أَنَا عِنْدَ ظَنِّ عَبْدِي بِي
hadith.en: Allah says: I am as my servant thinks of Me

shades.name_ar: الرَّجَاءُ - ضِدُّ الْيَأْسِ، رَجَاءُ رَحْمَةِ اللَّهِ، رَجَاءُ ثَوَابِ اللَّهِ
shades.explanation: The raja' (hope) in the Quran is the opposite of despair. The verse 2:218 establishes that those who believe, emigrate, and fight hope for the mercy of Allah. The raja' in the Quran has multiple meanings - the hope for the mercy of Allah (raja' rahmat Allah), the hope for the reward of Allah (raja' thawab Allah), and the hope for Paradise (raja' al-janna). The hadith establishes that Allah is as His servant thinks of Him. Al-Ghazali (Ihya, Book of Hope and Fear) treats the raja' as the hope for the divine mercy - the one who hopes in Allah has found the ultimate raja'.
shades.hadith_ar: يَقُولُ اللَّهُ: أَنَا عِنْدَ ظَنِّ عَبْدِي بِي
shades.hadith_en: Allah says: I am as my servant thinks of Me

meaning.en: To despair, lose hope. The root denotes the state of despair or loss of hope.

lexical_analysis.ibn_faris: الْيَأْسُ: ضِدُّ الرَّجَاءِ. وَيَئِسَ: قَطَعَ رَجَاءَهُ
lexical_analysis.al_raghib: الْيَأْسُ: ضِدُّ الرَّجَاءِ. وَالْيَأْسُ: الْقُنُوطُ مِنَ رَحْمَةِ اللَّهِ

quran_examples.ar: أَوَلَا يَعۡلَمُونَ أَنَّ ٱللَّهَ يَعۡلَمُ مَا يُسِرُّونَ وَمَا يُعۡلِنُونَ
quran_examples.en: Do they not know that Allah knows what they conceal and what they declare?
quran_examples.context: Allah knows the hidden and the declared

hadith.ar: لَا يَمُوتُ أَحَدٌ حَتَّى يَسْتَوْفِيَ رِزْقَهُ
hadith.en: No one dies until he receives his full provision

shades.name_ar: الْيَأْسُ - ضِدُّ الرَّجَاءِ، قُنُوطُ مِنْ رَحْمَةِ اللَّهِ
shades.explanation: The ya'as (despair) in the Quran is one of the major sins. The verse 2:77 establishes that Allah knows what they conceal and what they declare. The ya'as in the Quran has multiple meanings - the despair of the mercy of Allah (ya'as min rahmat Allah), the despair of provision (ya'as min al-rizq), and the despair of the truth (ya'as min al-haqq). The hadith establishes that no one dies until he receives his full provision. Al-Ghazali treats the ya'as as one of the major sins - the one who despairs of the mercy of Allah has gone astray.
shades.hadith_ar: لَا يَمُوتُ أَحَدٌ حَتَّى يَسْتَوْفِيَ رِزْقَهُ
shades.hadith_en: No one dies until he receives his full provision

meaning.en: To despair, lose hope. The root denotes the state of despair or loss of hope.

lexical_analysis.ibn_faris: الْقُنُوطُ: ضِدُّ الرَّجَاءِ. وَقَنَطَ: يَئِسَ
lexical_analysis.al_raghib: الْقُنُوطُ: ضِدُّ الرَّجَاءِ. وَقَنَطَ: يَئِسَ مِنَ الرَّحْمَةِ

quran_examples.ar: وَمِنۡهُمۡ أُمِّيُّونَ لَا يَعۡلَمُونَ ٱلۡكِتَـٰبَ إِلَّآ أَمَانِىَّ وَإِنۡ هُمۡ إِلَّا يَظُنُّونَ
quran_examples.en: And among them are unlettered ones who do not know the Scripture except in wishful thinking, but they are only assuming

hadith.ar: لَا يَمُوتُ نَفَسٌ حَتَّى تَسْتَوْفِيَ رِزْقَهَا
hadith.en: No soul dies until it has received its full provision

shades.name_ar: الْقُنُوطُ - ضِدُّ الرَّجَاءِ، قُنُوطُ مِنْ رَحْمَةِ اللَّهِ
shades.explanation: The qunut (despair) in the Quran is one of the major sins. The verse 2:78 establishes that among them are unlettered ones who do not know the Book except in wishful thinking. The qunut in the Quran has multiple meanings - the despair of the mercy of Allah (qunut min rahmat Allah), the despair of provision (qunut min al-rizq), and the despair of the truth (qunut min al-haqq). The hadith establishes that no soul dies until it has received its full provision. Al-Ghazali treats the qunut as the ultimate despair - the one who despairs of Allah has lost the way.
shades.hadith_ar: لَا يَمُوتُ نَفَسٌ حَتَّى تَسْتَوْفِيَ رِزْقَهَا
shades.hadith_en: No soul dies until it has received its full provision

meaning.en: To separate, distinguish, fear. The root denotes the act of separating or distinguishing.

lexical_analysis.ibn_faris: الْفَرْقُ: ضِدُّ الْجَمْعِ. وَفَرَقَ: شَقَّ
lexical_analysis.al_raghib: الْفَرْقُ: ضِدُّ الْجَمْعِ. وَالْفِرْقَانُ: مَا يُفَرَّقُ بِهِ بَيْنَ الْحَقِّ وَالْبَاطِلِ

quran_examples.ar: وَإِذۡ ءَاتَيۡنَا مُوسَى ٱلۡكِتَـٰبَ وَٱلۡفُرۡقَانَ لَعَلَّكُمۡ تَهۡتَدُونَ
quran_examples.en: And [recall] when We gave Moses the Book and criterion so that you might be guided
quran_examples.context: The Book and the criterion given to Moses

hadith.ar: إِنَّ اللَّهَ فَرَضَ فَرَائِضَ فَلَا تُضَيِّعُوهَا
hadith.en: Indeed Allah has prescribed obligations, so do not neglect them

shades.name_ar: الْفُرْقَانُ - ضِدُّ الْجَمْعِ، مَا يُفَرَّقُ بِهِ بَيْنَ الْحَقِّ وَالْبَاطِلِ
shades.explanation: The furqan (criterion) in the Quran is one of the most important concepts. The verse 2:53 establishes that Allah gave Moses the Book and the criterion (al-furqan). The furqan in the Quran has multiple meanings - the divine criterion (al-furqan al-ilahi), the human discrimination (al-furqan al-bashari), and the victory (al-furqan - the victory of Badr). The hadith establishes that Allah has prescribed obligations. Al-Ghazali treats the furqan as the divine criterion - the Quran is the furqan that distinguishes the truth from falsehood.
shades.hadith_ar: إِنَّ اللَّهَ فَرَضَ فَرَائِضَ فَلَا تُضَيِّعُوهَا
shades.hadith_en: Indeed Allah has prescribed obligations, so do not neglect them

meaning.en: To be cautious, beware. The root denotes the state of being cautious or wary.

lexical_analysis.ibn_faris: الْحَذَرُ: ضِدُّ الْغَفْلَةِ. وَحَذِرَ: تَيَقَّظَ
lexical_analysis.al_raghib: الْحَذَرُ: ضِدُّ الْغَفْلَةِ. وَتَحَذَّرَ: تَيَقَّظَ

quran_examples.ar: أَوۡ كَصَيِّبٍۢ مِّنَ ٱلسَّمَآءِ فِيهِ ظُلُمَـٰتٌۭ وَرَعۡدٌۭ وَبَرۡقٌۭ يَجۡعَلُونَ أَصَـٰبِعَهُمۡ فِىٓ ءَاذَانِهِم مِّنَ ٱلصَّوَـٰعِقِ حَذَرَ ٱلۡمَوۡتِ
quran_examples.en: Or like a rainstorm from the sky in which is darkness, thunder and lightning - they put their fingers in their ears against the thunderclaps in dread of death

hadith.ar: احْذَرُوا فِتْنَةَ الْأَغْنِيَاءِ
hadith.en: Beware of the trial of the rich

shades.explanation: The hadhar (caution) in the Quran is the state of being cautious. The verse 2:19 establishes the parable of the disbelievers - they put their fingers in their ears in dread of death. The hadhar in the Quran has multiple meanings - the physical caution (al-hadhar al-maddi), the spiritual caution (al-hadhar al-ruhani), and the divine caution (al-hadhar al-ilahi). The hadith establishes the warning against the trial of the rich. Al-Ghazali treats the hadhar as the spiritual awareness - the one who is cautious of sin has found the ultimate taqwa.
shades.hadith_ar: احْذَرُوا فِتْنَةَ الْأَغْنِيَاءِ
shades.hadith_en: Beware of the trial of the rich

meaning.en: To flow, pour. The root denotes the act of flowing or pouring.

lexical_analysis.ibn_faris: الشُّبُوبُ: سَيَلَانُ الْمَاءِ
lexical_analysis.al_raghib: الشُّبُوبُ: سَيَلَانُ الْمَاءِ بِشِدَّةٍ

quran_examples.ar: صُمٌّۢ بُكۡمٌ عُمۡىٌۭ فَهُمۡ لَا يَرۡجِعُونَ
quran_examples.en: Deaf, dumb, and blind - so they will not return

hadith.ar: لَا يَزَالُ الْبَلَاءُ بِالْمُؤْمِنِ وَالْمُؤْمِنَةِ
hadith.en: The trial continues to befall the believing man and woman

shades.explanation: The shubub (flowing) in the Quran is the act of flowing intensely. The verse 2:18 establishes the condemnation of the disbelievers. The shubub in the Quran is closely related to al-sayl (flowing) and al-jary (running). The hadith establishes that the trial continues to befall the believers. Al-Ghazali treats the shubub as the intense flowing of the divine mercy - the one who is immersed in the divine mercy has found the ultimate shubub.
shades.hadith_ar: لَا يَزَالُ الْبَلَاءُ بِالْمُؤْمِنِ وَالْمُؤْمِنَةِ
shades.hadith_en: The trial continues to befall the believing man and woman

meaning.en: To be happy, fortunate, lucky. The root denotes the state of being happy or fortunate.

lexical_analysis.ibn_faris: السَّعَادَةُ: ضِدُّ الشَّقَاءِ. وَسَعِدَ: حَظِيَ
lexical_analysis.al_raghib: السَّعَادَةُ: ضِدُّ الشَّقَاءِ. وَالسَّعِيدُ: الَّذِي أَصَابَ خَيْرًا

quran_examples.ar: أُو۟لَـٰٓئِكَ عَلَىٰ هُدًۭى مِّن رَّبِّهِمۡ ۖ وَأُو۟لَـٰٓئِكَ هُمُ ٱلۡمُفۡلِحُونَ
quran_examples.en: Those are upon [right] guidance from their Lord, and it is those who are the successful

hadith.ar: أَسْعَدُ النَّاسِ يَوْمَ الْقِيَامَةِ مَنْ قَالَ لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا اللَّهُ
hadith.en: The happiest of people on the Day of Resurrection will be the one who said 'there is no god but Allah'

shades.name_ar: السَّعَادَةُ - ضِدُّ الشَّقَاءِ، سَعَادَةُ الدُّنۡيَا وَالْآخِرَةِ
shades.explanation: The sa'ada (happiness) in the Quran is the opposite of misery. The verse 2:5 establishes that those upon guidance are the successful (al-muflihun). The sa'ada in the Quran has multiple meanings - the worldly happiness (sa'ada al-dunya), the eternal happiness (sa'ada al-akhira), and the divine happiness (sa'ada al-ilahiyyah). The hadith establishes that the happiest of people on the Day of Resurrection will be the one who said 'there is no god but Allah'. Al-Ghazali (Ihya, Book of Happiness) treats the sa'ada as the ultimate happiness - the one who is happy with Allah has found the ultimate sa'ada.
shades.hadith_ar: أَسْعَدُ النَّاسِ يَوْمَ الْقِيَامَةِ مَنْ قَالَ لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا اللَّهُ
shades.hadith_en: The happiest of people on the Day of Resurrection will be the one who said 'there is no god but Allah'

meaning.en: To split, separate. The root denotes the act of splitting or separating.

lexical_analysis.ibn_faris: الشَّقَاءُ: ضِدُّ السَّعَادَةِ. وَشَقِيَ: بَاءَ
lexical_analysis.al_raghib: الشَّقَاءُ: ضِدُّ السَّعَادَةِ. وَالشَّقِيُّ: الَّذِي بَاءَ بِالْعَذَابِ

quran_examples.ar: وَمَنۡ أَظۡلَمُ مِمَّن مَّنَعَ مَسَـٰجِدَ ٱللَّهِ أَن يُذۡكَرَ فِيهَا ٱسۡمُهُۥ وَسَعَىٰ فِىٓ خَرَابِهَآ
quran_examples.en: And who is more unjust than he who prevents the mention of Allah's name in His mosques and strives toward their destruction?
quran_examples.context: The condemnation of those who prevent the mention of Allah

hadith.ar: الْكَلِمَةُ الْحِكْمِيَّةُ ضَالَّةُ الْمُؤْمِنِ
hadith.en: The wise word is the lost property of the believer

shades.name_ar: الشَّقَاءُ - ضِدُّ السَّعَادَةِ، شَقَاءُ الدُّنۡيَا وَالْآخِرَةِ
shades.explanation: The shaqa' (wretchedness) in the Quran is the opposite of happiness. The verse 2:114 establishes the condemnation of those who prevent the mention of Allah. The shaqa' in the Quran has multiple meanings - the worldly misery (shaqa' al-dunya), the eternal misery (shaqa' al-akhira), and the divine misery (shaqa' al-ilahiyyah). The hadith establishes that the wise word is the lost property of the believer. Al-Ghazali treats the shaqa' as the ultimate misery - the one who is wretched has lost the way to Allah.
shades.hadith_ar: الْكَلِمَةُ الْحِكْمِيَّةُ ضَالَّةُ الْمُؤْمِنِ
shades.hadith_en: The wise word is the lost property of the believer

meaning.en: To flow, pour. The root denotes the act of flowing or pouring.

lexical_analysis.ibn_faris: الْفَسْمُ: الشَّقُّ
lexical_analysis.al_raghib: الْفَسْمُ: الشَّقُّ. وَفَسَمَ: شَقَّ

quran_examples.ar: ٱلَّذِى جَعَلَ لَكُمُ ٱلۡأَرۡضَ فِرَٰشًۭا وَٱلسَّمَآءَ بِنَآءًۭ وَأَنزَلَ مِنَ ٱلسَّمَآءِ مَآءًۭ فَأَخۡرَجَ بِهِۦ مِنَ ٱلثَّمَرَٰتِ رِزۡقًۭا لَّكُمۡ ۖ فَلَا تَجۡعَلُوا۟ لِلَّهِ أَندَادًۭا وَأَنتُمۡ تَعۡلَمُونَ
quran_examples.en: [He] who made for you the earth a bed [spread out] and the sky a ceiling and sent down from the sky, rain and brought forth thereby fruits as provision for you. So do not attribute to Allah equals while you know
quran_examples.context: The earth and sky as signs of Allah

hadith.ar: إِنَّ اللَّهَ خَلَقَ آدَمَ عَلَى صُورَتِهِ
hadith.en: Indeed Allah created Adam in His image

shades.explanation: The fasm (splitting) in the Quran is the act of splitting. The verse 2:22 establishes that Allah made the earth a bed and the sky a ceiling. The fasm in the Quran is closely related to al-shaqq (splitting) and al-farq (separating). The hadith establishes that Allah created Adam in His image. Al-Ghazali treats the fasm as the divine splitting - the one whose heart is split by the divine light has found the ultimate opening.
shades.hadith_ar: إِنَّ اللَّهَ خَلَقَ آدَمَ عَلَى صُورَتِهِ
shades.hadith_en: Indeed Allah created Adam in His image

meaning.en: To precede, go before. The root denotes the act of preceding or going before.

lexical_analysis.ibn_faris: السَّبْقُ: التَّقَدُّمُ. وَسَبَقَ: تَقَدَّمَ
lexical_analysis.al_raghib: السَّبْقُ: التَّقَدُّمُ. وَالسَّابِقُ: الْمُتَقَدِّمُ

quran_examples.ar: وَقَالُوا۟ كُونُوا۟ هُودًا أَوۡ نَصَـٰرَىٰ تَهۡتَدُوا۟ ۗ قُلۡ بَلۡ مِلَّةَ إِبۡرَٰهِـۧمَ حَنِيفًۭا ۚ وَمَا كَانَ مِنَ ٱلۡمُشۡرِكِينَ
quran_examples.en: And they say, Be Jews or Christians [so] you would be guided. Say, [O Muhammad], Rather, [we follow] the religion of Abraham, inclining toward truth, and he was not of the polytheists
quran_examples.context: The rejection of the claim of the Jews and Christians

hadith.ar: سَابِقُوا إِلَى مَغْفِرَةٍ مِنْ رَبِّكُمْ
hadith.en: Race toward forgiveness from your Lord

shades.name_ar: السَّبْقُ - التَّقَدُّمُ، سَبْقُ الْخَيْرِ، سَبْقُ الشَّرِّ
shades.explanation: The sabq (preceding) in the Quran is the act of going before. The verse 2:110 establishes that the People of the Book claim that following them is the guidance. The sabq in the Quran has multiple meanings - the preceding in good deeds (sabq al-khayr), the preceding in evil deeds (sabq al-sharr), and the divine precedence (al-sabq al-ilahi). The hadith establishes that one should race toward forgiveness from your Lord. Al-Ghazali treats the sabq as the racing to good deeds - the one who precedes others in good deeds has found the ultimate falah.
shades.hadith_ar: سَابِقُوا إِلَى مَغْفِرَةٍ مِنْ رَبِّكُمْ
shades.hadith_en: Race toward forgiveness from your Lord

meaning.en: To be high, exalted. The root denotes the state of being high or exalted.

lexical_analysis.ibn_faris: الشَّوَاءُ: الْعُلُوُّ. وَشَاءَ: عَلَا
lexical_analysis.al_raghib: الشَّوَاءُ: الْعُلُوُّ. وَالشَّاءُ: الْعَالِي

quran_examples.ar: إِنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ يَكۡتُمُونَ مَآ أَنزَلۡنَا مِنَ ٱلۡبَيِّنَـٰتِ وَٱلۡهُدَىٰ مِنۢ بَعۡدِ مَا بَيَّنَّـٰهُ لِلنَّاسِ فِى ٱلۡكِتَـٰبِ ۙ أُو۟لَـٰٓئِكَ يَلۡعَنُهُمُ ٱللَّهُ وَيَلۡعَنُهُمُ ٱللَّـٰعِنُونَ
quran_examples.en: Indeed, those who conceal what We sent down of clear proofs and guidance - after We made it clear for them in the Book - those are cursed by Allah and cursed by those who curse
quran_examples.context: The curse upon those who conceal revelation

hadith.ar: إِنَّ اللَّهَ كَبِيرٌ مُتَعَالٍ
hadith.en: Indeed Allah is the Most Great, the Most High

shades.explanation: The shawa (exaltedness) in the Quran is the state of being high. The verse 2:159 establishes the curse upon those who conceal revelation. The shawa in the Quran is closely related to al-uluw (highness) and al-irtifa' (elevation). The hadith establishes that Allah is the Most Great, the Most High. Al-Ghazali treats the shawa as the divine exaltedness - the one whose heart is exalted by Allah has found the ultimate shawa.
shades.hadith_ar: إِنَّ اللَّهَ كَبِيرٌ مُتَعَالٍ
shades.hadith_en: Indeed Allah is the Most Great, the Most High

meaning.en: To heal, cure. The root denotes the act of healing or curing - particularly of the heart.

lexical_analysis.ibn_faris: الشِّفَاءُ: ضِدُّ الْمَرَضِ. وَشَفَى: أَبْرَأَ
lexical_analysis.al_raghib: الشِّفَاءُ: ضِدُّ الْمَرَضِ. وَالشِّفَاءُ: مَا بِهِ يُسْتَفَادُ الْبُرْءُ

quran_examples.ar: فِى قُلُوبِهِم مَّرَضٌۭ فَزَادَهُمُ ٱللَّهُ مَرَضًۭا ۖ وَلَهُمۡ عَذَابٌ أَلِيمٌۢ بِمَا كَانُوا۟ يَكۡذِبُونَ
quran_examples.en: In their hearts is disease, and Allah has increased their disease; and for them is a painful punishment because they [habitually] used to lie

hadith.ar: الْقُرْآنُ شِفَاءٌ لِمَا فِي الصُّدُورِ
hadith.en: The Quran is a healing for what is in the chests

shades.name_ar: الشِّفَاءُ - ضِدُّ الْمَرَضِ، شِفَاءُ الْقَلْبِ، شِفَاءُ الْبَدَنِ
shades.explanation: The shifa (healing) in the Quran is one of the most important concepts. The verse 2:10 establishes the disease of the hearts of the hypocrites. The shifa in the Quran has multiple meanings - the physical healing (al-shifa' al-maddi), the spiritual healing (al-shifa' al-ruhani), and the healing of the Quran (shifa' al-Quran). The hadith establishes that the Quran is a healing for what is in the chests. Al-Ghazali (Ihya, Book of Healing) treats the shifa as the ultimate healing - the one who is healed by the Quran has found the ultimate cure.
shades.hadith_ar: الْقُرْآنُ شِفَاءٌ لِمَا فِي الصُّدُورِ
shades.hadith_en: The Quran is a healing for what is in the chests

meaning.en: To be sick, ill. The root denotes the state of being sick or ill - particularly of the heart.

lexical_analysis.ibn_faris: الْمَرَضُ: ضِدُّ الصِّحَّةِ
lexical_analysis.al_raghib: الْمَرَضُ: ضِدُّ الصِّحَّةِ. وَالْمَرَضُ: السُّقْمُ الْمُنَافِي لِلْفِعْلِ

quran_examples.ar: فِى قُلُوبِهِم مَّرَضٌۭ فَزَادَهُمُ ٱللَّهُ مَرَضًۭا
quran_examples.en: In their hearts is disease, and Allah has increased their disease
quran_examples.context: The disease of the hearts of the hypocrites

hadith.ar: إِنَّ اللَّهَ يُبْتَلِي الْعَبْدَ بِالْمَرَضِ حَتَّى يُكَفِّرَ عَنْهُ
hadith.en: Indeed Allah tests the servant with illness until he is forgiven

shades.name_ar: الْمَرَضُ - ضِدُّ الصِّحَّةِ، مَرَضُ الْقَلْبِ، مَرَضُ الْبَدَنِ
shades.explanation: The marad (disease) in the Quran is one of the most important concepts. The verse 2:10 establishes the disease of the hearts of the hypocrites. The marad in the Quran has multiple meanings - the physical disease (al-marad al-maddi), the spiritual disease (al-marad al-ruhani), and the disease of doubt (al-marad al-shakki). The hadith establishes that Allah tests the servant with illness until he is forgiven. Al-Ghazali (Ihya, Book of the Disease of the Heart) treats the marad as the disease of the heart - the one whose heart is healthy with iman has found the ultimate cure.
shades.hadith_ar: إِنَّ اللَّهَ يُبْتَلِي الْعَبْدَ بِالْمَرَضِ حَتَّى يُكَفِّرَ عَنْهُ
shades.hadith_en: Indeed Allah tests the servant with illness until he is forgiven

meaning.en: To be stingy, tight. The root denotes the state of being stingy or tight.

lexical_analysis.ibn_faris: الشَّحْقُ: ضِيقُ النَّفْسِ
lexical_analysis.al_raghib: الشَّحْقُ: ضِيقُ النَّفْسِ مَعَ الْبُخْلِ

quran_examples.ar: وَقَالُوا۟ ٱتَّخَذَ ٱللَّهُ وَلَدًۭا ۙ سُبۡحَـٰنَهُۥ ۖ بَل لَّهُۥ مَا فِى ٱلسَّمَـٰوَٰتِ وَٱلۡأَرۡضِ ۖ كُلٌّۭ لَّهُۥ قَـٰنِتُونَ
quran_examples.en: And they say, Allah has taken a son. Exalted is He! Rather, to Him belongs whatever is in the heavens and the earth. All are devoutly obedient to Him
quran_examples.context: The condemnation of those who say Allah has a son

hadith.ar: إِيَّاكُمْ وَالْبُخْلَ
hadith.en: Beware of stinginess

shades.explanation: The shahq (stinginess) in the Quran is one of the major sins. The verse 2:167 establishes the condemnation of those who say Allah has taken a son. The shahq in the Quran is closely related to al-bukhl (stinginess) and al-shuhh (extreme stinginess). The hadith establishes the warning against stinginess. Al-Ghazali treats the shahq as the disease of the soul - the one who overcomes shahq has found the ultimate generosity.
shades.hadith_ar: إِيَّاكُمْ وَالْبُخْلَ
shades.hadith_en: Beware of stinginess

meaning.en: To be unwilling, refuse. The root denotes the state of being unwilling or refusing.

lexical_analysis.ibn_faris: الْإِبَاءُ: ضِدُّ الْإِذْعَانِ. وَأَبَى: رَفَضَ
lexical_analysis.al_raghib: الْإِبَاءُ: ضِدُّ الْإِذْعَانِ. وَأَبَى: أَنِفَ

quran_examples.ar: وَإِذۡ قُلۡنَا لِلۡمَلَـٰٓئِكَةِ ٱسۡجُدُوا۟ لِأَدَمَ فَسَجَدُوٓاْ إِلَّآ إِبۡلِيسَ أَبَىٰ وَٱسۡتَكۡبَرَ وَكَانَ مِنَ ٱلۡكَـٰفِرِينَ
quran_examples.en: And [recall] when We said to the angels, Prostrate before Adam; so they prostrated, except for Iblees. He refused and was arrogant and became of the disbelievers
quran_examples.context: The refusal of Iblees to prostrate

hadith.ar: إِذَا أَبَى أَحَدُكُمْ فَلْيَأْخُذْ بِأَنْفِهِ
hadith.en: When one of you refuses, let him take by his nose

shades.explanation: The iba' (refusal) in the Quran is one of the most important concepts. The verse 2:34 establishes the refusal of Iblees to prostrate. The iba' in the Quran has multiple meanings - the refusal of obedience (al-iba' al-ta'ah), the refusal of the truth (al-iba' al-haqq), and the refusal from pride (al-iba' min al-kibr). The hadith establishes that when one refuses, let him take by his nose. Al-Ghazali treats the iba' as the opposite of al-taslim (submission) - the one who refuses the divine command has gone astray.
shades.hadith_ar: إِذَا أَبَى أَحَدُكُمْ فَلْيَأْخُذْ بِأَنْفِهِ
shades.hadith_en: When one of you refuses, let him take by his nose

meaning.en: To show, display, present. The root denotes the act of showing or displaying.

lexical_analysis.ibn_faris: الْعَرْضُ: ضِدُّ الطُّولِ. وَعَرَضَ الشَّيْءَ: أَظْهَرَهُ
lexical_analysis.al_raghib: الْعَرْضُ: ضِدُّ الطُّولِ. وَالْعَرْضُ: الظُّهُورُ

quran_examples.ar: وَعَلَّمَ ءَادَمَ ٱلۡأَسۡمَآءَ كُلَّهَا ثُمَّ عَرَضَهُمۡ عَلَى ٱلۡمَلَـٰٓئِكَةِ فَقَالَ أَنۢبِـُٔونِى بِأَسۡمَآءِ هَـٰٓؤُلَآءِ إِن كُنتُمۡ صَـٰدِقِينَ
quran_examples.en: And He taught Adam the names of all things; then He presented them to the angels and said, Tell Me the names of these if you are truthful
quran_examples.context: The teaching of Adam the names

hadith.ar: يَقُولُ اللَّهُ: أَنَا عِنْدَ ظَنِّ عَبْدِي بِي
hadith.en: Allah says: I am as my servant thinks of Me

shades.name_en: al-Ard - The Display and the Width
shades.explanation: The ard (display, width) in the Quran is one of the most common concepts. The verse 2:31 establishes the teaching of Adam the names. The ard in the Quran has multiple meanings - the physical display (al-'ard al-maddi), the spiritual display (al-'ard al-ruhani), and the worldly goods (al-'ard al-dunya). The hadith establishes that Allah is as His servant thinks of Him. Al-Ghazali treats the ard as the divine display - the one who displays the divine signs has found the ultimate ma'rifa.
shades.hadith_ar: يَقُولُ اللَّهُ: أَنَا عِنْدَ ظَنِّ عَبْدِي بِي
shades.hadith_en: Allah says: I am as my servant thinks of Me

meaning.en: To be noble, high, elevated. The root denotes the state of being noble or high.

lexical_analysis.ibn_faris: الشَّرَفُ: الْعُلُوُّ. وَشَرُفَ: عَلَا
lexical_analysis.al_raghib: الشَّرَفُ: الْعُلُوُّ. وَالْمَشْرِفُ: الشَّيْءُ الْعَالِي

quran_examples.ar: فَإِن طَلَّقَهَا فَلَا تَحِلُّ لَهُۥ مِنۢ بَعۡدُ حَتَّىٰ تَنكِحَ زَوۡجًا غَيۡرَهُۥ
quran_examples.en: And if he divorces her, she is not lawful to him afterward until she marries a husband other than him
quran_examples.context: The ruling on remarriage after divorce

hadith.ar: إِنَّ اللَّهَ يُحِبُّ مَعَالِيَ الْأَخْلَاقِ
hadith.en: Indeed Allah loves the noble qualities

shades.name_ar: الشَّرَفُ - الْعُلُوُّ، شَرَفُ النَّفْسِ، شَرَفُ الْمَكَانِ
shades.explanation: The sharaf (nobility) in the Quran is the state of being noble or high. The verse 2:230 establishes the ruling on remarriage. The sharaf in the Quran has multiple meanings - the nobility of the soul (sharaf al-nafs), the nobility of the place (sharaf al-makan), and the nobility of the lineage (sharaf al-nasab). The hadith establishes that Allah loves the noble qualities. Al-Ghazali treats the sharaf as the spiritual nobility - the one whose soul is noble has found the ultimate sharaf.
shades.hadith_ar: إِنَّ اللَّهَ يُحِبُّ مَعَالِيَ الْأَخْلَاقِ
shades.hadith_en: Indeed Allah loves the noble qualities

meaning.en: To drive, cast, blow. The root denotes the act of driving or casting.

lexical_analysis.ibn_faris: الشَّهْقُ: الطَّرْدُ بِصَوْتٍ
lexical_analysis.al_raghib: الشَّهْقُ: الطَّرْدُ بِصَوْتٍ شَدِيدٍ

quran_examples.ar: إِنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوا۟ وَعَمِلُوا۟ ٱلصَّـٰلِحَـٰتِ وَأَقَامُوا۟ ٱلصَّلَوٰةَ وَءَاتَوۡا۟ ٱلزَّكَوٰةَ لَهُمۡ أَجۡرُهُمۡ عِندَ رَبِّهِمۡ وَلَا خَوۡفٌ عَلَيۡهِمۡ وَلَا هُمۡ يَحۡزَنُونَ
quran_examples.en: Indeed, those who believe and do righteous deeds and establish prayer and give zakah will have their reward with their Lord, and there will be no fear concerning them, nor will they grieve

hadith.ar: لَا تَجْعَلُوا بَيْنَ الْأَنْبِيَاءِ فِتَنَةً
hadith.en: Do not make fitna among the prophets

shades.explanation: The shahq (driving) in the Quran is one of the dramatic images. The verse 2:277 establishes the reward of the believers. The shahq in the Quran is closely related to al-tard (driving) and al-nafkh (blowing). The hadith establishes the warning against fitna. Al-Ghazali treats the shahq as the driving of the soul - the one who is driven toward Allah has found the ultimate shahq.
shades.hadith_ar: لَا تَجْعَلُوا بَيْنَ الْأَنْبِيَاءِ فِتَنَةً
shades.hadith_en: Do not make fitna among the prophets

meaning.en: To wound, hurt. The root denotes the act of wounding or hurting.

lexical_analysis.ibn_faris: الْجَرْحُ: الضَّرْبُ بِجَرْحٍ
lexical_analysis.al_raghib: الْجَرْحُ: الضَّرْبُ بِشَيْءٍ يُجْرِحُ

quran_examples.ar: يَـٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوا۟ كُتِبَ عَلَيۡكُمُ ٱلۡقِصَاصُ فِى ٱلۡقَتۡلَى ٱلۡحُرُّ بِٱلۡحُرِّ وَٱلۡعَبۡدُ بِٱلۡعَبۡدِ وَٱلۡأُنثَىٰ بِٱلۡأُنثَىٰ
quran_examples.en: O you who have believed, prescribed for you is legal retribution for those murdered - the free for the free, the slave for the slave, and the female for the female

hadith.ar: مَنْ قَتَلَ نَفْسًا مُعَاهَدًا لَمْ يَرَحْ رَائِحَةَ الْجَنَّةِ
hadith.en: Whoever kills a person under covenant will not smell the fragrance of Paradise

shades.name_ar: الْجَرْحُ - الضَّرْبُ بِشَيْءٍ يُجْرِحُ، جُرْحُ الْقَلْبِ
shades.explanation: The jarh (wound) in the Quran is one of the dramatic images. The verse 2:178 establishes the divine prescription of qisas. The jarh in the Quran has multiple meanings - the physical wound (al-jarh al-maddi), the spiritual wound (al-jarh al-ruhani), and the criticism (al-jarh al-naqdi - in hadith terminology). The hadith establishes that whoever kills a person under covenant will not smell the fragrance of Paradise. Al-Ghazali treats the jarh as the wound of the heart - the one whose heart is wounded by the divine love has found the ultimate jarh.
shades.hadith_ar: مَنْ قَتَلَ نَفْسًا مُعَاهَدًا لَمْ يَرَحْ رَائِحَةَ الْجَنَّةِ
shades.hadith_en: Whoever kills a person under covenant will not smell the fragrance of Paradise

meaning.en: To turn away, repel, call out. The root denotes the act of turning away or repelling.

lexical_analysis.ibn_faris: الصَّدْوُ: الْمَنْعُ
lexical_analysis.al_raghib: الصَّدْوُ: الصَّدُّ. وَصَدَى: مَالَ

quran_examples.ar: إِنَّ ٱلصَّفَا وَٱلۡمَرۡوَةَ مِن شَعَآئِرِ ٱللَّهِ ۖ فَمَنۡ حَجَّ ٱلۡبَيۡتَ أَوِ ٱعۡتَمَرَ فَلَا جُنَاحَ عَلَيۡهِ أَن يَطَّوَّفَ بِهِمَا ۚ وَمَن تَطَوَّعَ خَيۡرًۭا فَإِنَّ ٱللَّهَ شَاكِرٌ عَلِيمٌ
quran_examples.en: Indeed, as-Safa and al-Marwah are among the symbols of Allah. So whoever makes pilgrimage to the House or performs 'umrah - there is no blame upon him for circling between them. And whoever volunteers good - then indeed, Allah is appreciative and knowing

hadith.ar: لَا تَقُصُوا الشَّعْرَ
hadith.en: Do not cut the hair

shades.explanation: The sadu (repelling) in the Quran is one of the most common concepts. The verse 2:158 establishes the Hajj rituals. The sadu in the Quran has multiple meanings - the physical repelling (al-sadu al-maddi), the spiritual repelling (al-sadu al-ruhani), and the calling out (al-sadu al-nida'). The hadith establishes the prohibition of cutting the hair during Hajj. Al-Ghazali treats the sadu as the repelling of evil - the one who repels evil from his heart has found the ultimate sadu.
shades.hadith_ar: لَا تَقُصُوا الشَّعْرَ
shades.hadith_en: Do not cut the hair

meaning.en: To support, be amazed. The root denotes the state of being amazed or perplexed.

lexical_analysis.ibn_faris: الْيَدَهُ: التَّحَيُّرُ. وَيَدَهَ: تَحَيَّرَ
lexical_analysis.al_raghib: الْيَدَهُ: التَّحَيُّرُ. وَتَيَدَّهَ: تَحَيَّرَ

quran_examples.ar: مَثَلُهُمۡ كَمَثَلِ ٱلَّذِى ٱسۡتَوۡقَدَ نَارًۭا فَلَمَّآ أَضَآءَتۡ مَا حَوۡلَهُۥ ذَهَبَ ٱللَّهُ بِنُورِهِمۡ وَتَرَكَهُمۡ فِى ظُلُمَـٰتٍۢ لَّا يُبۡصِرُونَ
quran_examples.en: Their example is that of one who kindled a fire, but when it illuminated what was around him, Allah took away their light and left them in darkness [so] they could not see

hadith.ar: إِنَّ الْحَمْدَ لِلَّهِ رَبِّ الْعَالَمِينَ
hadith.en: Praise be to Allah, Lord of the worlds

shades.name_ar: الْيَدَهُ - التَّحَيُّرُ، الْعَجْزُ عَنْ مَعْرِفَةِ الشَّيْءِ
shades.explanation: The yadaha (amazement) in the Quran is the state of being perplexed. The verse 2:17 establishes the parable of the hypocrites. The yadaha in the Quran has multiple meanings - the physical amazement (al-yadaha al-maddi), the spiritual amazement (al-yadaha al-ruhani), and the amazement at the divine (al-yadaha 'inda Allah). The hadith establishes that praise be to Allah, Lord of the worlds. Al-Ghazali treats the yadaha as the amazement at the divine creation - the one who is amazed at the creation has begun the journey of ma'rifa.
shades.hadith_ar: إِنَّ الْحَمْدَ لِلَّهِ رَبِّ الْعَالَمِينَ
shades.hadith_en: Praise be to Allah, Lord of the worlds

meaning.en: To split, tear. The root denotes the act of splitting or tearing.

lexical_analysis.ibn_faris: الشَّقُّ: ضِدُّ الْإِلْتِئَامِ. وَشَقَّ: فَتَقَ
lexical_analysis.al_raghib: الشَّقُّ: ضِدُّ الْإِلْتِئَامِ. وَالشَّقِيقُ: الشَّقُّ فِي الْبَدَنِ

quran_examples.ar: ثُمَّ قَسَتۡ قُلُوبُكُم مِّنۢ بَعۡدِ ذَٰلِكَ فَهِىَ كَٱلۡحِجَارَةِ أَوۡ أَشَدُّ قَسۡوَةًۭ ۚ وَإِنَّ مِنَ ٱلۡحِجَارَةِ لَمَا يَتَفَجَّرُ مِنۡهُ ٱلۡأَنۡهَـٰرُ
quran_examples.en: Then your hearts became hardened after that, being like stones or even harder. For indeed, there are stones from which rivers burst forth

hadith.ar: لَقَدۡ خَلَقۡنَا الْإِنسَانَ فِىٓ أَحۡسَنِ تَقۡوِيمٍۢ
hadith.en: We have certainly created man in the best of stature

shades.explanation: The shuqq (splitting) in the Quran is one of the dramatic images. The verse 2:74 establishes the hardness of the hearts and the stones that split. The shuqq in the Quran has multiple meanings - the splitting of the sky (shaqq al-sama'), the splitting of the earth (shaqq al-ard), and the splitting of the dawn (shaqq al-subh). The hadith establishes that Allah created man in the best of stature. Al-Ghazali treats the shuqq as the divine splitting - the one whose heart is split by the divine light has found the ultimate opening.
shades.hadith_ar: لَقَدۡ خَلَقۡنَا الْإِنسَانَ فِىٓ أَحۡسَنِ تَقۡوِيمٍۢ
shades.hadith_en: We have certainly created man in the best of stature

meaning.en: To be lenient, gentle. The root denotes the state of being lenient or gentle.

lexical_analysis.ibn_faris: الْخَفَاءُ: ضِدُّ الْبُرُوزِ. وَخَفَى: سَتَرَ
lexical_analysis.al_raghib: الْخَفَاءُ: ضِدُّ الْبُرُوزِ. وَخَفَى الشَّيْءَ: سَتَرَهُ

quran_examples.ar: إِنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ يَكۡتُمُونَ مَآ أَنزَلَ ٱللَّهُ مِنَ ٱلۡكِتَـٰبِ وَيَشۡتَرُونَ بِهِۦ ثَمَنًۭا قَلِيلًا
quran_examples.en: Indeed those who conceal what Allah has revealed of the Book and exchange it for a small price

hadith.ar: إِنَّ اللَّهَ رَفِيقٌ يُحِبُّ الرِّفْقَ
hadith.en: Indeed Allah is gentle and loves gentleness

shades.explanation: The khafa' (gentleness, concealment) in the Quran is one of the divine attributes. The verse 2:174 establishes the condemnation of those who conceal revelation. The khafa' in the Quran has multiple meanings - the concealment (al-khafa' al-sitr), the gentleness (al-khafa' al-rifq), and the hidden (al-khafa' al-makhfi). The hadith establishes that Allah is gentle and loves gentleness. Al-Ghazali treats the khafa' as the divine attribute - the one whose concealment is by Allah has found the ultimate khafa'.
shades.hadith_ar: إِنَّ اللَّهَ رَفِيقٌ يُحِبُّ الرِّفْقَ
shades.hadith_en: Indeed Allah is gentle and loves gentleness

meaning.en: To be bountiful, prosperous. The root denotes the state of being bountiful or prosperous.

lexical_analysis.ibn_faris: النَّعِيمُ: ضِدُّ الشَّقَاءِ. وَنَعِمَ: أَصَابَهُ الْخَصْبُ
lexical_analysis.al_raghib: النَّعِيمُ: ضِدُّ الشَّقَاءِ. وَنَعِمَ: أَصَابَهُ خَيْرٌ

quran_examples.ar: أُو۟لَـٰٓئِكَ عَلَىٰ هُدًۭى مِّن رَّبِّهِمۡ ۖ وَأُو۟لَـٰٓئِكَ هُمُ ٱلۡمُفۡلِحُونَ
quran_examples.en: Those are upon [right] guidance from their Lord, and it is those who are the successful

hadith.ar: مَنْ أَصْبَحَ مِنْكُمْ آمِنًا فِي سِرْبِهِ
hadith.en: Whoever among you wakes up safe in his home

shades.name_ar: النَّعِيمُ - ضِدُّ الشَّقَاءِ، نَعِيمُ الدُّنۡيَا وَالْآخِرَةِ
shades.explanation: The na'im (bounty) in the Quran is one of the most important concepts. The verse 2:5 establishes that those upon guidance are the successful. The na'im in the Quran has multiple meanings - the worldly bounty (na'im al-dunya), the eternal bounty (na'im al-akhira), and the divine bounty (na'im al-ilahi). The hadith establishes that whoever wakes up safe in his home is in a state of bounty. Al-Ghazali (Ihya, Book of Hope and Fear) treats the na'im as the ultimate bounty - the one who is in a state of na'im with Allah has found the ultimate bounty.
shades.hadith_ar: مَنْ أَصْبَحَ مِنْكُمْ آمِنًا فِي سِرْبِهِ
shades.hadith_en: Whoever among you wakes up safe in his home

meaning.en: To buy, purchase. The root denotes the act of buying or purchasing.

lexical_analysis.ibn_faris: الشِّرَاءُ: ضِدُّ الْبَيْعِ. وَشَرِيَ: ابْتَاعَ
lexical_analysis.al_raghib: الشِّرَاءُ: ضِدُّ الْبَيْعِ. وَاشْتَرَى: ابْتَاعَ

quran_examples.ar: إِنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ يَكۡتُمُونَ مَآ أَنزَلَ ٱللَّهُ مِنَ ٱلۡكِتَـٰبِ وَيَشۡتَرُونَ بِهِۦ ثَمَنًۭا قَلِيلًا
quran_examples.en: Indeed those who conceal what Allah has revealed of the Book and exchange it for a small price

hadith.ar: لَعَنَ اللَّهُ الْيَهُودَ حُرِّمَتْ عَلَيْهِمُ الشُّحُومُ فَجَمَلُوهَا فَبَاعُوهَا
hadith.en: Allah cursed the Jews - fats were forbidden to them, so they melted them and sold them

shades.name_ar: الشِّرَاءُ - ضِدُّ الْبَيْعِ، شِرَاءُ الْآخِرَةِ بِالدُّنۡيَا
shades.explanation: The shira' (purchase) in the Quran is the act of buying. The verse 2:174 establishes the condemnation of those who conceal revelation and exchange it for a small price. The shira' in the Quran has multiple meanings - the physical purchase (al-shira' al-maddi), the spiritual purchase (al-shira' al-ruhani - buying Paradise), and the wicked purchase (al-shira' al-dani' - exchanging revelation for a small price). The hadith establishes that Allah cursed the Jews who melted the forbidden fats and sold them. Al-Ghazali treats the shira' as the ultimate transaction - the one who buys Paradise has found the ultimate bargain.
shades.hadith_ar: لَعَنَ اللَّهُ الْيَهُودَ حُرِّمَتْ عَلَيْهِمُ الشُّحُومُ فَجَمَلُوهَا فَبَاعُوهَا
shades.hadith_en: Allah cursed the Jews - fats were forbidden to them, so they melted them and sold them

meaning.en: To sell. The root denotes the act of selling.

lexical_analysis.ibn_faris: الْبَيْعُ: ضِدُّ الشِّرَاءِ. وَبَاعَ: شَرَى
lexical_analysis.al_raghib: الْبَيْعُ: ضِدُّ الشِّرَاءِ. وَالْبَيْعُ: مُقَابَلَةُ شَيْءٍ بِشَيْءٍ

quran_examples.ar: يَـٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوٓاْ أَنفِقُوا۟ مِمَّا رَزَقۡنَـٰكُم مِّن قَبۡلِ أَن يَأۡتِىَ يَوۡمٌۭ لَّا بَيۡعٌۭ فِيهِ وَلَا خُلَّةٌۭ وَلَا شَفَـٰعَةٌۭ
quran_examples.en: O you who have believed, spend of what We have provided for you before there comes a Day in which there is no exchange and no friendship and no intercession
quran_examples.context: The command to spend before the Day of Judgment

hadith.ar: الْبَيِّعَانِ بِالْخِيَارِ مَا لَمْ يَتَفَرَّقَا
hadith.en: The two parties to a sale have the option of canceling the sale as long as they have not separated

shades.name_ar: الْبَيْعُ - ضِدُّ الشِّرَاءِ، بَيۡعُ اللَّهِ تَبَارَكَ وَتَعَالَى
shades.explanation: The bay' (sale) in the Quran is one of the most fundamental legal concepts. The verse 2:254 establishes the command to spend before the Day of Judgment. The bay' in the Quran has multiple meanings - the physical sale (al-bay' al-maddi), the spiritual sale (al-bay' al-ruhani - selling the soul to Allah), and the divine sale (al-bay' al-ilahi - Allah buys from the believers). The hadith establishes that the two parties to a sale have the option of canceling. Al-Ghazali treats the bay' as the divine transaction - the one who sells his soul to Allah has found the ultimate transaction.
shades.hadith_ar: الْبَيِّعَانِ بِالْخِيَارِ مَا لَمْ يَتَفَرَّقَا
shades.hadith_en: The two parties to a sale have the option of canceling the sale as long as they have not separated

meaning.en: To be true, established, due.

lexical_analysis.ibn_faris: الْحَقُّ: ضِدُّ الْبَاطِلِ
lexical_analysis.al_raghib: الْحَقُّ: ضِدُّ الْبَاطِلِ

quran_examples.ar: الٓمٓ
quran_examples.en: Alif, Lam, Meem

hadith.ar: إِنَّ اللَّهَ يَقُولُ: الصَّدْقُ بُرٌّ
hadith.en: Indeed Allah says: Truth is righteousness

shades.explanation: The haqq (truth) is one of the divine attributes.

meaning.en: To judge, be wise.

lexical_analysis.ibn_faris: الْحُكْمُ: الْقَضَاءُ بِالْحَقِّ
lexical_analysis.al_raghib: الْحُكْمُ: الْقَضَاءُ بِالْعِلْمِ

quran_examples.ar: فَٱللَّهُ يَحۡكُمُ بَيۡنَهُمۡ يَوۡمَ ٱلۡقِيَـٰمَةِ
quran_examples.en: Allah will judge between them on the Day of Resurrection

hadith.ar: إِنَّ اللَّهَ يَقُولُ: الصَّدْقُ بُرٌّ
hadith.en: Indeed Allah says: Truth is righteousness

shades.explanation: The hukm is the divine judgment.

meaning.en: To stand, rise, establish. The root denotes the act of standing or rising - and the establishment of divine commands.

lexical_analysis.ibn_faris: الْقِيَامُ: ضِدُّ الْقُعُودِ. وَقَامَ: انْتَصَبَ
lexical_analysis.al_raghib: الْقِيَامُ: ضِدُّ الْقُعُودِ. وَالْقَوَّامُ: الْكَثِيرُ الْقِيَامِ

quran_examples.ar: حَـٰفِظُوا۟ عَلَى ٱلصَّلَوَٰتِ وَٱلصَّلَوٰةِ ٱلۡوُسۡطَىٰ وَقُومُوا۟ لِلَّهِ قَـٰنِتِينَ
quran_examples.en: Maintain with care the [obligatory] prayers and [in particular] the middle prayer and stand before Allah, devoutly obedient
quran_examples.context: The command to maintain the prayers

hadith.ar: قُومُوا لِلَّهِ قَانِتِينَ
hadith.en: Stand before Allah devoutly obedient

shades.name_ar: الْقِيَامُ - ضِدُّ الْقُعُودِ، قِيَامُ اللَّيْلِ، قِيَامُ الْحُرُوفِ
shades.explanation: The qiyam (standing) in the Quran is one of the most fundamental concepts. The verse 2:238 establishes the command to maintain the prayers and stand before Allah devoutly obedient. The qiyam in the Quran has multiple meanings - the physical standing (al-qiyam al-maddi), the spiritual standing (al-qiyam al-ruhani), and the standing for prayer (al-qiyam li-l-salat). The hadith establishes the command to stand before Allah devoutly obedient. Al-Ghazali treats the qiyam as the standing for prayer - the one who stands for Allah has found the ultimate qiyam.
shades.hadith_ar: قُومُوا لِلَّهِ قَانِتِينَ
shades.hadith_en: Stand before Allah devoutly obedient

meaning.en: To intend, be moderate, aim. The root denotes the act of intending or aiming - and the state of being moderate.
meaning.ar: الْقَصْدُ: الِاعْتِدَالُ، تَوَسُّطُ الشَّيْءِ بَيْنَ طَرَفَيْهِ

lexical_analysis.ibn_faris: الْقَصْدُ: الِاعْتِدَالُ. وَقَصَدَ الشَّيْءَ: نَحَاهُ
lexical_analysis.al_raghib: الْقَصْدُ: الِاعْتِدَالُ. وَالْمُقْتَصِدُ: الْمُتَوَسِّطُ

quran_examples.ar: وَكَذَٰلِكَ جَعَلۡنَـٰكُمۡ أُمَّةًۭ وَسَطًۭا لِّتَكُونُوا۟ شُهَدَآءَ عَلَى ٱلنَّاسِ
quran_examples.en: And thus We have made you a moderate nation that you will be witnesses over the people
quran_examples.context: The Muslims as a moderate nation

hadith.ar: الْمُقْتَصِدُونَ يَأْخُذُونَ الْأَجْرَ ضِعْفَيْنِ
hadith.en: The moderate ones take the reward twice

shades.explanation: The qasd (moderation, intention) in the Quran is one of the most important concepts. The verse 2:143 establishes that the Muslims are a moderate (wasat) nation. The qasd in the Quran has multiple meanings - the moderation (al-qasd al-i'tidal), the intention (al-qasd al-niyya), and the aiming (al-qasd al-tawajjuh). The hadith establishes that the moderate ones take the reward twice. Al-Ghazali treats the qasd as the moderation in all things - the one who is moderate has found the ultimate qasd.
shades.hadith_ar: الْمُقْتَصِدُونَ يَأْخُذُونَ الْأَجْرَ ضِعْفَيْنِ
shades.hadith_en: The moderate ones take the reward twice

meaning.en: To be black, be sad. The root denotes the state of being black or sad.

lexical_analysis.ibn_faris: السَّوَادُ: ضِدُّ الْبَيَاضِ. وَسَوِدَ: اسْوَدَّ
lexical_analysis.al_raghib: السَّوَادُ: ضِدُّ الْبَيَاضِ. وَالْأَسْوَدُ: الْمُظْلِمُ

quran_examples.ar: أُحِلَّ لَكُمۡ لَيۡلَةَ ٱلصِّيَامِ ٱلرَّفَثُ إِلَىٰ نِسَآئِكُمۡ
quran_examples.en: It has been made permissible for you the night preceding fasting to go to your wives
quran_examples.context: The permission during the night of fasting

hadith.ar: الْحَيَاءُ شُعۡبَةٌ مِنَ الْإِيمَانِ
hadith.en: Modesty is a branch of faith

shades.explanation: The sawad (blackness) in the Quran is the opposite of whiteness. The verse 2:187 establishes the permission during the night of fasting. The sawad in the Quran has multiple meanings - the physical blackness (al-sawad al-maddi), the spiritual blackness (al-sawad al-ma'nawi), and the blackness of the face (al-sawad al-wajh). The hadith establishes that modesty is a branch of faith. Al-Ghazali treats the sawad as the darkness of the heart - the one whose heart is dark has lost the way to Allah.
shades.hadith_ar: الْحَيَاءُ شُعۡبَةٌ مِنَ الْإِيمَانِ
shades.hadith_en: Modesty is a branch of faith

meaning.en: To confine, restrict. The root denotes the act of confining or restricting.

lexical_analysis.ibn_faris: الْحَصْرُ: ضِدُّ الْإِطْلَاقِ. وَحَصَرَ: مَنَعَ
lexical_analysis.al_raghib: الْحَصْرُ: ضِدُّ الْإِطْلَاقِ. وَالْحَصِيرُ: الْمَانِعُ

quran_examples.ar: لِّلۡفُقَرَآءِ ٱلَّذِينَ أُحۡصِرُوا۟ فِى سَبِيلِ ٱللَّهِ
quran_examples.en: [Charity is] for the poor who have been restricted for the cause of Allah

hadith.ar: حُبُّ الْوَطَنِ مِنَ الْإِيمَانِ
hadith.en: Love of the homeland is from faith

shades.explanation: The hasr (confinement) in the Quran is one of the states of restriction. The verse 2:273 establishes the charity for the poor who are restricted for the cause of Allah. The hasr in the Quran has multiple meanings - the physical confinement (al-hasr al-maddi), the spiritual confinement (al-hasr al-ruhani), and the restriction by Allah (al-hasr al-ilahi). The hadith establishes that love of the homeland is from faith. Al-Ghazali treats the hasr as the state of being restricted by Allah - the one who is restricted by Allah has found the ultimate hasr.
shades.hadith_ar: حُبُّ الْوَطَنِ مِنَ الْإِيمَانِ
shades.hadith_en: Love of the homeland is from faith

meaning.en: To pull, drag. The root denotes the act of pulling or dragging.

lexical_analysis.ibn_faris: الْجَرُّ: السَّحْبُ. وَجَرَّ: سَحَبَ
lexical_analysis.al_raghib: الْجَرُّ: السَّحْبُ. وَالْجَرِيرَةُ: الذَّنْبُ

quran_examples.ar: وَلَوۡلَا دَفۡعُ ٱللَّهِ ٱلنَّاسَ بَعۡضَهُم بِبَعۡضٍۢ لَّفَسَدَتِ ٱلۡأَرۡضُ وَلَـٰكِنَّ ٱللَّهَ ذُو فَضۡلٍ عَلَى ٱلۡعَـٰلَمِينَ
quran_examples.en: And if Allah did not repel the people from one another, the earth would have been corrupted, but Allah is full of bounty to the worlds

hadith.ar: لَا تَجْعَلُوا بَيْنَ الْأَنْبِيَاءِ فِتَنَةً
hadith.en: Do not make fitna among the prophets

shades.explanation: The jarr (pulling) in the Quran is the act of dragging. The verse 2:251 establishes the divine repelling of corruption. The jarr in the Quran has multiple meanings - the physical dragging (al-jarr al-maddi), the metaphorical dragging (al-jarr al-majazi), and the legal dragging (al-jarr al-qada'i). The hadith establishes the warning against fitna. Al-Ghazali treats the jarr as the dragging of the lower self - the one who drags his lower self toward obedience has found the ultimate jarr.
shades.hadith_ar: لَا تَجْعَلُوا بَيْنَ الْأَنْبِيَاءِ فِتَنَةً
shades.hadith_en: Do not make fitna among the prophets

meaning.en: To be cautious, protect. The root denotes the act of being cautious or protecting.

lexical_analysis.ibn_faris: الْوِقَايَةُ: الْحِفْظُ. وَوَقَى: صَانَ
lexical_analysis.al_raghib: الْوِقَايَةُ: الْحِفْظُ مِنَ الشَّيْءِ. وَتَقَوَّى: اتَّخَذَ وَقَايَةً

quran_examples.ar: وَإِذۡ وَٰعَدۡنَا مُوسَىٰٓ أَرۡبَعِينَ لَيۡلَةًۭ
quran_examples.en: And [recall] when We made an appointment with Moses for forty nights
quran_examples.context: The appointment of Moses on Mount Sinai

hadith.ar: لَا تَحْقِرَنَّ مِنَ الْمَعۡرُوفِ شَيۡئًا
hadith.en: Do not despise any act of kindness

shades.explanation: The wiqaya (protection) in the Quran is the act of guarding against harm. The verse 2:51 establishes the appointment of Moses on Mount Sinai. The wiqaya in the Quran has multiple meanings - the physical protection (al-wiqaya al-maddiyyah), the spiritual protection (al-wiqaya al-ruhaniyyah), and the divine protection (al-wiqaya al-ilahiyyah). The hadith establishes that one should not despise any act of kindness. Al-Ghazali treats the wiqaya as the divine protection - the one who is protected by Allah has found the ultimate wiqaya.
shades.hadith_ar: لَا تَحْقِرَنَّ مِنَ الْمَعۡرُوفِ شَيۡئًا
shades.hadith_en: Do not despise any act of kindness

meaning.en: To complain, lament. The root denotes the act of complaining or lamenting.

lexical_analysis.ibn_faris: الشَّكْوَى: ضِدُّ الرِّضَا. وَشَكَا: أَبْدَى مَا بِهِ
lexical_analysis.al_raghib: الشَّكْوَى: إِبْدَاءُ مَا بِالْمُشْتَكَى مِنَ الْأَمْرِ الضَّارِّ

quran_examples.ar: وَمِنۡهُم مَّن يَقُولُ رَبَّنَآ ءَاتِنَا فِى ٱلدُّنۡيَا حَسَنَةًۭ وَفِى ٱلۡءَاخِرَةِ حَسَنَةًۭ وَقِنَا عَذَابَ ٱلنَّارِ
quran_examples.en: And among them are those who say, Our Lord, give us in this world [that which is] good and in the Hereafter [that which is] good and protect us from the punishment of the Fire

hadith.ar: إِنَّ اللَّهَ يُحِبُّ أَنْ يُسْأَلَ
hadith.en: Indeed Allah loves to be asked

shades.name_ar: الشَّكْوَى - ضِدُّ الرِّضَا، شَكْوَى الْعَبْدِ إِلَى رَبِّهِ
shades.explanation: The shakwa (complaint) in the Quran is the act of lamenting. The verse 2:201 establishes the prayer of the pilgrims. The shakwa in the Quran has multiple meanings - the physical complaint (al-shakwa al-maddiyyah), the spiritual complaint (al-shakwa al-ruhaniyyah), and the divine complaint (al-shakwa al-ilahiyyah - to Allah). The hadith establishes that Allah loves to be asked. Al-Ghazali treats the shakwa as the sincere complaint to Allah - the one who complains only to Allah has found the ultimate shakwa.
shades.hadith_ar: إِنَّ اللَّهَ يُحِبُّ أَنْ يُسْأَلَ
shades.hadith_en: Indeed Allah loves to be asked

meaning.en: To be ugly, despise. The root denotes the state of being ugly or despising.

lexical_analysis.ibn_faris: الشَّنَآنُ: الْبُغْضُ. وَشَنِئَ: أَبْغَضَ
lexical_analysis.al_raghib: الشَّنَآنُ: الْبُغْضُ الْمُسْتَحْكَمُ. وَشَنِئَ: أَبْغَضَ

quran_examples.ar: أَمۡ تُرِيدُونَ أَن تَسۡـَٔلُوا۟ رَسُولَكُمۡ كَمَا سُئِلَ مُوسَىٰ مِن قَبۡلُ ۗ وَمَن يَتَبَدَّلِ ٱلۡكُفۡرَ بِٱلۡإِيمَـٰنِ فَقَدۡ ضَلَّ سَوَآءَ ٱلسَّبِيلِ
quran_examples.en: Or do you intend to ask your Messenger as Moses was asked before? And whoever exchanges faith for disbelief has certainly strayed from the right way
quran_examples.context: The warning against exchanging faith for disbelief

hadith.ar: إِيَّاكُمْ وَالظَّنَّ فَإِنَّ الظَّنَّ أَكْذَبُ الْحَدِيثِ
hadith.en: Beware of suspicion, for suspicion is the most false of speech

shades.explanation: The shana'an (enmity) in the Quran is the state of intense hatred. The verse 2:108 establishes the warning against exchanging faith for disbelief.
