The shana'an in the Quran has multiple meanings - the personal enmity (al-shana'an al-shakhsi), the religious enmity (al-shana'an al-dini), and the divine enmity (al-shana'an al-ilahi). The hadith establishes that one should beware of suspicion. Al-Ghazali treats the shana'an as the disease of the heart - the one who overcomes shana'an has found the ultimate ihsan.
shades.hadith_ar: إِيَّاكُمْ وَالظَّنَّ فَإِنَّ الظَّنَّ أَكْذَبُ الْحَدِيثِ
shades.hadith_en: Beware of suspicion, for suspicion is the most false of speech

meaning.en: To be, exist, will.

lexical_analysis.ibn_faris: الْمَشِيئَةُ: الْإِرَادَةُ
lexical_analysis.al_raghib: الْمَشِيئَةُ: صِفَةٌ تَقْتَضِي تَخْصِيصَ الْمَرَادِ بِوَقْتٍ مَعْلُومٍ

quran_examples.ar: يَكَادُ ٱلۡبَرۡقُ يَخۡطَفُ أَبۡصَـٰرَهُمۡ
quran_examples.en: The lightning almost snatches away their sight

hadith.ar: إِنَّمَا الْأَعْمَالُ بِالنِّيَّاتِ
hadith.en: Indeed deeds are judged by intentions

shades.explanation: The mashi'a (will) is one of the divine attributes.
shades.hadith_ar: إِنَّمَا الْأَعْمَالُ بِالنِّيَّاتِ
shades.hadith_en: Indeed deeds are judged by intentions

meaning.en: To forbid, declare sacred. The root denotes the act of forbidding or declaring sacred.

lexical_analysis.ibn_faris: التَّحْكِيمُ: الْمَنْعُ. وَحَكَمَ: مَنَعَ
lexical_analysis.al_raghib: التَّحْكِيمُ: الْمَنْعُ. وَالْحَكِيمُ: الْمَانِعُ مِنَ الْقَبَائِحِ

quran_examples.ar: وَلِلرِّجَالِ عَلَيۡهِنَّ دَرَجَةٌۭ ۚ وَٱللَّهُ عَزِيزٌ حَكِيمٌ
quran_examples.en: And men have a degree over them [wives], and Allah is Exalted in Might and Wise
quran_examples.context: The degree of men over women

hadith.ar: الْحَلَالُ بَيِّنٌ وَالْحَرَامُ بَيِّنٌ
hadith.en: The lawful is clear and the unlawful is clear

shades.explanation: The tahrim (forbidding) in the Quran is the act of declaring something forbidden. The verse 2:228 establishes the degree of men over women. The tahrim in the Quran has multiple meanings - the divine forbidding (al-tahrim al-ilahi), the human forbidding (al-tahrim al-bashari), and the sacred (al-muharram). The hadith establishes that the lawful is clear and the unlawful is clear. Al-Ghazali treats the tahrim as the divine prohibition - the one who respects the tahrim of Allah has found the ultimate taqwa.
shades.hadith_ar: الْحَلَالُ بَيِّنٌ وَالْحَرَامُ بَيِّنٌ
shades.hadith_en: The lawful is clear and the unlawful is clear

meaning.en: To be sharp. The root denotes the state of being sharp.

lexical_analysis.ibn_faris: الْحَدَقُ: الشَّدِيدُ. وَحَدَقَ: اِحْتَدَقَ
lexical_analysis.al_raghib: الْحَدَقُ: الشَّدِيدُ. وَالْحَادِقُ: الشَّدِيدُ

quran_examples.ar: أَوۡ كَصَيِّبٍۢ مِّنَ ٱلسَّمَآءِ فِيهِ ظُلُمَـٰتٌۭ وَرَعۡدٌۭ وَبَرۡقٌۭ
quran_examples.en: Or like a rainstorm from the sky in which is darkness, thunder and lightning

hadith.ar: إِنَّ مَعَ الْعُسْرِ يُسْرًا
hadith.en: Indeed with hardship comes ease

shades.explanation: The hadaq (sharpness) in the Quran is the state of being sharp. The verse 2:19 establishes the parable of the disbelievers. The hadaq in the Quran is closely related to al-shiddah (severity) and al-quwwah (strength). The hadith establishes that with hardship comes ease. Al-Ghazali treats the hadaq as the sharpness of the heart - the one whose heart is sharp in faith has found the ultimate hadaq.
shades.hadith_ar: إِنَّ مَعَ الْعُسْرِ يُسْرًا
shades.hadith_en: Indeed with hardship comes ease

meaning.en: To forbid, abstain. The root denotes the act of forbidding or abstaining.

lexical_analysis.ibn_faris: النَّهْيُ: ضِدُّ الْأَمْرِ
lexical_analysis.al_raghib: النَّهْيُ: الطَّلَبُ بِالتَّرْكِ

quran_examples.ar: وَٱتَّبَعُوا۟ مَا تَتۡلُوا۟ ٱلشَّيَـٰطِينُ عَلَىٰ مُلۡكِ سُلَيۡمَـٰنَ
quran_examples.en: And they followed what the devils used to recite in the reign of Solomon

hadith.ar: مَا نَهَيْتُكُمْ عَنْهُ فَاجْتَنِبُوهُ
hadith.en: What I have forbidden you from, avoid it

shades.explanation: The nahl (forbidding) in the Quran is the act of forbidding. The verse 2:102 establishes the story of Solomon and the devils. The nahl in the Quran has multiple meanings - the divine forbidding (al-nahl al-ilahi), the human forbidding (al-nahl al-bashari), and the spiritual forbidding (al-nahl al-ruhani). The hadith establishes that what the Prophet has forbidden, one should avoid it. Al-Ghazali treats the nahl as the divine prohibition - the one who respects the nahl of Allah has found the ultimate taqwa.
shades.hadith_ar: مَا نَهَيْتُكُمْ عَنْهُ فَاجْتَنِبُوهُ
shades.hadith_en: What I have forbidden you from, avoid it

meaning.en: To betray, be treacherous. The root denotes the act of betrayal or treachery.

lexical_analysis.ibn_faris: الْخِيَانَةُ: نَقْضُ الْأَمَانَةِ
lexical_analysis.al_raghib: الْخِيَانَةُ: نَقْضُ الْأَمَانَةِ. وَخَانَ: غَدَرَ

quran_examples.ar: أُحِلَّ لَكُمۡ لَيۡلَةَ ٱلصِّيَامِ ٱلرَّفَثُ إِلَىٰ نِسَآئِكُمۡ ۚ هُنَّ لِبَاسٌۭ لَّكُمۡ وَأَنتُمۡ لِبَاسٌۭ لَّهُنَّ ۗ عَلِمَ ٱللَّهُ أَنَّكُمۡ كُنتُمۡ تَخۡتَانُونَ أَنفُسَكُمۡ
quran_examples.en: It has been made permissible for you the night preceding fasting to go to your wives. They are clothing for you, and you are clothing for them. Allah knows that you used to betray yourselves
quran_examples.context: The command not to betray during fasting

hadith.ar: إِيَّاكَ وَالْخِيَانَةَ فَإِنَّ الْخِيَانَةَ مَجْلَبَةٌ لِلْفَضِيحَةِ
hadith.en: Beware of betrayal, for betrayal leads to disgrace

shades.explanation: The khiyana (betrayal) in the Quran is one of the major sins. The verse 2:187 establishes the command not to betray during fasting. The khiyana in the Quran has multiple meanings - the betrayal of trust (khiyana al-amanah), the betrayal of the covenant (khiyana al-ahd), and the betrayal of the spouse (khiyana al-zawj). The hadith establishes that one should beware of betrayal. Al-Ghazali treats the khiyana as the ultimate betrayal of the divine trust - the one who betrays the trust has no din and no dunya.
shades.hadith_ar: إِيَّاكَ وَالْخِيَانَةَ فَإِنَّ الْخِيَانَةَ مَجْلَبَةٌ لِلْفَضِيحَةِ
shades.hadith_en: Beware of betrayal, for betrayal leads to disgrace

meaning.en: To be at fault, wrong. The root denotes the state of being at fault or doing wrong.

lexical_analysis.ibn_faris: الْخَطْأُ: ضِدُّ الْعَمْدِ. وَخَاطَ: أَخْطَأَ
lexical_analysis.al_raghib: الْخَطْأُ: ضِدُّ الْعَمْدِ. وَالْخَاطِئُ: مَنْ فَعَلَ الذَّنْبَ مِنْ غَيْرِ قَصْدٍ

quran_examples.ar: وَٱسۡتَشۡهِدُوا۟ شَهِيدَيۡنِ مِن رِّجَالِكُمۡ ۖ فَإِن لَّمۡ يَكُونَا رَجُلَيۡنِ فَرَجُلٌۭ وَٱمۡرَأَتَانِ مِمَّن تَرۡضَوۡنَ مِنَ ٱلشُّهَدَآءِ
quran_examples.en: And get two men to testify, or one man and two women from those whom you accept as witnesses
quran_examples.context: The command for witnesses in transactions

hadith.ar: رُفِعَ الْقَلَمُ عَنْ ثَلَاثَةٍ عَنِ النَّائِمِ حَتَّى يَسْتَيْقِظَ
hadith.en: The pen is lifted from three - from the sleeper until he awakens

shades.name_ar: الْخَطْأُ - ضِدُّ الْعَمْدِ، الْإِثْمُ غَيْرُ الْمُتَعَمَّدِ
shades.explanation: The khata' (error) in the Quran is the act of doing wrong unintentionally. The verse 2:282 establishes the command for witnesses. The khata' in the Quran has multiple meanings - the unintentional error (khata' ghayr mu'tamad), the intentional error (khata' mu'tamad), and the legal error (khata' al-qada'i). The hadith establishes that the pen is lifted from three. Al-Ghazali treats the khata' as the unintentional error - the one who repents from the khata' has been forgiven by Allah.
shades.hadith_ar: رُفِعَ الْقَلَمُ عَنْ ثَلَاثَةٍ عَنِ النَّائِمِ حَتَّى يَسْتَيْقِظَ
shades.hadith_en: The pen is lifted from three - from the sleeper until he awakens

meaning.en: To be in excess, be virtuous. The root denotes the state of being in excess or virtuous.

lexical_analysis.ibn_faris: الْفَضْلُ: ضِدُّ الْعَدْلِ. وَفَضَلَ: زَادَ
lexical_analysis.al_raghib: الْفَضْلُ: الزِّيَادَةُ عَلَى الْحَاجَةِ. وَفَضْلُ اللَّهِ: إِحْسَانُهُ

quran_examples.ar: وَلَوۡلَا دَفۡعُ ٱللَّهِ ٱلنَّاسَ بَعۡضَهُم بِبَعۡضٍۢ لَّفَسَدَتِ ٱلۡأَرۡضُ وَلَـٰكِنَّ ٱللَّهَ ذُو فَضۡلٍ عَلَى ٱلۡعَـٰلَمِينَ
quran_examples.en: And if Allah did not repel the people from one another, the earth would have been corrupted, but Allah is full of bounty to the worlds
quran_examples.context: The divine bounty to the worlds

hadith.ar: لَوْ أَنَّ لِي مِثْلَ أُحُدٍ ذَهَبًا لَأَحْبَبْتُ أَنْ لَا تَمُرَّ عَلَيَّ ثَلَاثَ لَيَالٍ وَعِنْدِي مِنْهُ شَيْءٌ
hadith.en: If I had gold like Mount Uhud, I would not like any to pass through my possession for three nights

shades.name_en: al-Fadl - The Virtue and the Bounty
shades.name_ar: الْفَضْلُ - ضِدُّ الْعَدْلِ، فَضْلُ اللَّهِ عَلَى عِبَادِهِ
shades.explanation: The fadl (virtue, bounty) in the Quran is one of the most important divine attributes - Allah is al-Faddal (the Most Generous). The verse 2:251 establishes the divine bounty to the worlds. The fadl in the Quran has multiple meanings - the physical bounty (al-fadl al-maddi), the spiritual bounty (al-fadl al-ruhani), and the divine bounty (al-fadl al-ilahi). The hadith establishes that the Prophet did not like to have gold for three nights. Al-Ghazali (Maqsad al-Asna) treats al-Faddal as one of the divine names - the One who is generous with His bounty.
shades.hadith_ar: لَوْ أَنَّ لِي مِثْلَ أُحُدٍ ذَهَبًا لَأَحْبَبْتُ أَنْ لَا تَمُرَّ عَلَيَّ ثَلَاثَ لَيَالٍ وَعِنْدِي مِنْهُ شَيْءٌ
shades.hadith_en: If I had gold like Mount Uhud, I would not like any to pass through my possession for three nights

meaning.en: To be empty, vacant. The root denotes the state of being empty or vacant.

lexical_analysis.ibn_faris: الْخُلُوُّ: ضِدُّ الِامْتِلَاءِ. وَخَلَا: فَرَغَ
lexical_analysis.al_raghib: الْخُلُوُّ: ضِدُّ الِامْتِلَاءِ. وَخَلَا الشَّيْءُ: خَلَصَ

quran_examples.ar: وَٱلَّذِينَ يُتَوَفَّوۡنَ مِنكُمۡ وَيَذَرُونَ أَزۡوَٰجًۭا يَتَرَبَّصۡنَ بِأَنفُسِهِنَّ أَرۡبَعَةَ أَشۡهُرٍۢ وَعَشۡرًۭا
quran_examples.en: And those who are taken in death among you and leave wives behind - they, [the wives, shall] wait four months and ten [days]

hadith.ar: إِنَّ اللَّهَ لَا يَمَلُّ حَتَّى تَمَلُّوا
hadith.en: Indeed Allah does not tire until you tire

shades.explanation: The khulaw (emptiness) in the Quran is the state of being empty. The verse 2:234 establishes the waiting period for widows. The khulaw in the Quran has multiple meanings - the physical emptiness (al-khulaw al-maddi), the temporal emptiness (al-khulaw al-zamani), and the spiritual emptiness (al-khulaw al-ruhani). The hadith establishes that Allah does not tire until you tire. Al-Ghazali treats the khulaw as the emptiness of the heart from the divine remembrance - the one whose heart is filled with Allah has found the ultimate fullness.
shades.hadith_ar: إِنَّ اللَّهَ لَا يَمَلُّ حَتَّى تَمَلُّوا
shades.hadith_en: Indeed Allah does not tire until you tire

meaning.en: To increase, grow, add. The root denotes the act of increasing or adding.

lexical_analysis.ibn_faris: الزِّيَادَةُ: ضِدُّ النُّقْصَانِ. وَزَادَ: نَمَى
lexical_analysis.al_raghib: الزِّيَادَةُ: ضِدُّ النُّقْصَانِ. وَزَادَ: كَثُرَ

quran_examples.ar: مَّن ذَا ٱلَّذِى يُقۡرِضُ ٱللَّهَ قَرۡضًا حَسَنًۭا فَيُضَـٰعِفَهُۥ لَهُۥٓ أَضۡعَافًۭا كَثِيرَةًۭ
quran_examples.en: Who is it that will lend to Allah a goodly loan so that He may multiply it for him many times over?
quran_examples.context: The parable of lending to Allah

hadith.ar: مَنْ يُرِدِ اللَّهُ بِهِ خَيْرًا يُصِبْ مِنْهُ
hadith.en: Whomever Allah wishes good for, He afflicts him

shades.name_ar: الزِّيَادَةُ - ضِدُّ النُّقْصَانِ، زِيَادَةُ اللَّهِ فِي الْخَلْقِ
shades.explanation: The ziyada (increase) in the Quran is one of the most important divine acts. The verse 2:245 establishes the parable of lending to Allah - He multiplies it many times over. The ziyada in the Quran has multiple meanings - the physical increase (al-ziyada al-maddiyyah), the spiritual increase (al-ziyada al-ruhaniyyah), and the divine increase (al-ziyada al-ilahiyyah). The hadith establishes that whomever Allah wishes good for, He afflicts him. Al-Ghazali treats the ziyada as the divine gift - the one who gives for the sake of Allah has been given the ultimate ziyada.
shades.hadith_ar: مَنْ يُرِدِ اللَّهُ بِهِ خَيْرًا يُصِبْ مِنْهُ
shades.hadith_en: Whomever Allah wishes good for, He afflicts him

meaning.en: To slip, err, deviate. The root denotes the act of slipping or deviating.

lexical_analysis.ibn_faris: الزَّلَلُ: ضِدُّ الثَّبَاتِ. وَزَلَّ: سَقَطَ
lexical_analysis.al_raghib: الزَّلَلُ: ضِدُّ الثَّبَاتِ. وَزَلَّ الشَّيْءُ: مَالَ

quran_examples.ar: فَأَزَلَّهُمَا ٱلشَّيۡطَـٰنُ عَنۡهَا فَأَخۡرَجَهُمَا مِمَّا كَانَا فِيهِ ۖ وَقُلۡنَا ٱهۡبِطُوا۟ بَعۡضُكُمۡ لِبَعۡضٍ عَدُوٌّۭ ۖ وَلَكُمۡ فِى ٱلۡأَرۡضِ مُسۡتَقَرٌّۭ وَمَتَـٰعٌ إِلَىٰ حِينٍۢ
quran_examples.en: But Satan caused them to slip out of it and removed them from that [condition] in which they had been. And We said, Go down, [all of you], as enemies to one another, and you will have upon the earth a place of settlement and provision for a time
quran_examples.context: The descent of Adam and his wife

hadith.ar: كُلُّ ابْنِ آدَمَ خَطَّاءٌ وَخَيْرُ الْخَطَّائِينَ التَّوَّابُونَ
hadith.en: Every son of Adam is a sinner, and the best of sinners are those who repent

shades.explanation: The zalal (slipping) in the Quran is the act of deviating. The verse 2:36 establishes that Satan caused Adam and his wife to slip. The zalal in the Quran has multiple meanings - the physical slip (al-zalal al-maddi), the spiritual slip (al-zalal al-ruhani), and the slip of the foot (zalal al-qadam). The hadith establishes that every son of Adam is a sinner, and the best of sinners are those who repent. Al-Ghazali treats the zalal as the slip of the heart - the one who is aware of the zalal has begun the journey of taqwa.
shades.hadith_ar: كُلُّ ابْنِ آدَمَ خَطَّاءٌ وَخَيْرُ الْخَطَّائِينَ التَّوَّابُونَ
shades.hadith_en: Every son of Adam is a sinner, and the best of sinners are those who repent

meaning.en: To be tight, restrained. The root denotes the state of being tight or restrained.

lexical_analysis.ibn_faris: الْحَكُّ: ضِدُّ الْإِرْخَاءِ. وَحَكَّ: شَدَّ
lexical_analysis.al_raghib: الْحَكُّ: ضِدُّ الْإِرْخَاءِ. وَالْحَكِيمُ: الشَّدِيدُ الْإِحْكَامِ

quran_examples.ar: وَٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوٓاْ أَشَدُّ حُبًّۭا لِّلَّهِ
quran_examples.en: And those who believe are stronger in love for Allah
quran_examples.context: The love of the believers for Allah

hadith.ar: لَا تَجْعَلُوا بَيْنَ الْأَنْبِيَاءِ فِتَنَةً
hadith.en: Do not make fitna among the prophets

shades.explanation: The hakw (tightness) in the Quran is the state of being tight. The verse 2:165 establishes that those who believe are stronger in love for Allah. The hakw in the Quran is closely related to al-shiddah (severity) and al-qahr (domination). The hadith establishes the warning against fitna. Al-Ghazali treats the hakw as the tightness of the heart toward Allah - the one whose heart is tight with the love of Allah has found the ultimate hakw.
shades.hadith_ar: لَا تَجْعَلُوا بَيْنَ الْأَنْبِيَاءِ فِتَنَةً
shades.hadith_en: Do not make fitna among the prophets

meaning.en: To be steadfast, persevering. The root denotes the state of being steadfast or persevering.

lexical_analysis.ibn_faris: الشَّدِيدُ: الشِّدَّةُ. وَشَبِدَ: اِشْتَدَّ
lexical_analysis.al_raghib: الشَّدِيدُ: الشَّدِيدُ الْقُوَّةِ

quran_examples.ar: وَمِنَ ٱلنَّاسِ مَن يَقُولُ ءَامَنَّا بِٱللَّهِ وَبِٱلۡيَوۡمِ ٱلۡأَخِرِ وَمَا هُم بِمُؤۡمِنِينَ
quran_examples.en: And of the people are some who say, We believe in Allah and the Last Day, but they are not believers

hadith.ar: مَنْ يَتَوَكَّلْ عَلَى اللَّهِ فَهُوَ حَسْبُهُ
hadith.en: Whoever relies upon Allah - then He is sufficient for him

shades.explanation: The shabada (steadfastness) is the state of being strong and persevering.
shades.hadith_ar: مَنْ يَتَوَكَّلْ عَلَى اللَّهِ فَهُوَ حَسْبُهُ
shades.hadith_en: Whoever relies upon Allah - then He is sufficient for him

meaning.en: To prostrate, bow down. The root denotes the act of prostrating or bowing down - and the ultimate submission to Allah.

lexical_analysis.ibn_faris: السُّجُودُ: التَّطَامَنُ. وَسَجَدَ: تَطَامَنَ
lexical_analysis.al_raghib: السُّجُودُ: ضِعْفُ الْخُضُوعِ. وَالسُّجُودُ لِلَّهِ: التَّطَامَنُ تَحْتَ الْأَمْرِ

quran_examples.ar: وَإِذۡ قُلۡنَا لِلۡمَلَـٰٓئِكَةِ ٱسۡجُدُوا۟ لِأَدَمَ فَسَجَدُوٓاْ إِلَّآ إِبۡلِيسَ أَبَىٰ وَٱسۡتَكۡبَرَ
quran_examples.en: And [recall] when We said to the angels, Prostrate before Adam; so they prostrated, except for Iblees. He refused and was arrogant
quran_examples.context: The prostration of the angels before Adam

hadith.ar: أَقْرَبُ مَا يَكُونُ الْعَبْدُ مِنْ رَبِّهِ وَهُوَ سَاجِدٌ
hadith.en: The closest the servant is to his Lord is when he is prostrating

shades.name_ar: السُّجُودُ - ضِعْفُ الْخُضُوعِ، أَقْرَبُ الْأَحْوَالِ إِلَى اللَّهِ
shades.explanation: The sujud (prostration) is the ultimate submission to Allah.
shades.hadith_ar: أَقْرَبُ مَا يَكُونُ الْعَبْدُ مِنْ رَبِّهِ وَهُوَ سَاجِدٌ
shades.hadith_en: The closest the servant is to his Lord is when he is prostrating

meaning.en: To bow, kneel. The root denotes the act of bowing or kneeling - particularly in prayer.

lexical_analysis.ibn_faris: الرُّكُوعُ: ضِدُّ الِاسْتِقَامَةِ. وَرَكَعَ: انْحَنَى
lexical_analysis.al_raghib: الرُّكُوعُ: ضِدُّ الِاسْتِقَامَةِ. وَالرَّاكِعُ: الْمُنْحَنِي

quran_examples.ar: وَأَقِيمُوا۟ ٱلصَّلَوٰةَ وَءَاتُوا۟ ٱلزَّكَوٰةَ وَٱرۡكَعُوا۟ مَعَ ٱلرَّـٰكِعِينَ
quran_examples.en: And establish prayer and give zakah and bow with those who bow [in worship and obedience]
quran_examples.context: The command to bow with those who bow

hadith.ar: صَلُّوا كَمَا رَأَيْتُمُونِي أُصَلِّي
hadith.en: Pray as you have seen me pray

shades.name_ar: الرُّكُوعُ - ضِدُّ الِاسْتِقَامَةِ، انْحِنَاءُ الظَّهْرِ فِي الصَّلَاةِ
shades.explanation: The ruku' (bowing) is the act of bending the back in prayer.
shades.hadith_ar: صَلُّوا كَمَا رَأَيْتُمُونِي أُصَلِّي
shades.hadith_en: Pray as you have seen me pray

meaning.en: To say, speak. The root denotes the act of saying or speaking - and the divine speech.

lexical_analysis.ibn_faris: الْقَوْلُ: ضِدُّ الْفِعْلِ. وَقَالَ: نَطَقَ
lexical_analysis.al_raghib: الْقَوْلُ: الْكَلَامُ بِحُرُوفٍ مَتَوَالِيَةٍ

quran_examples.ar: وَعَلَّمَ ءَادَمَ ٱلۡأَسۡمَآءَ كُلَّهَا ثُمَّ عَرَضَهُمۡ عَلَى ٱلۡمَلَـٰٓئِكَةِ
quran_examples.en: And He taught Adam the names of all things; then He presented them to the angels
quran_examples.context: The teaching of Adam the names

hadith.ar: كَلِمَتَانِ خَفِيفَتَانِ عَلَى اللِّسَانِ ثَقِيلَتَانِ فِي الْمِيزَانِ
hadith.en: Two words are light on the tongue, heavy in the balance

shades.name_ar: الْقَوْلُ - الْكَلَامُ، قَوْلُ اللَّهِ خِلْقٌ مِنْ خَلْقِهِ
shades.explanation: The qawl (speech) is one of the most fundamental human actions. The verse 2:31 establishes the teaching of Adam the names. The qawl in the Quran has multiple meanings - the human speech (al-qawl al-bashari), the divine speech (al-qawl al-ilahi), and the evil speech (al-qawl al-dani'). The hadith establishes the two words that are light on the tongue. Al-Ghazali treats the qawl as the divine speech - the Quran is the speech of Allah, and the one who recites it has found the ultimate qawl.
shades.hadith_ar: كَلِمَتَانِ خَفِيفَتَانِ عَلَى اللِّسَانِ ثَقِيلَتَانِ فِي الْمِيزَانِ
shades.hadith_en: Two words are light on the tongue, heavy in the balance

meaning.en: To do, act, perform. The root denotes the act of doing or acting - and the divine action.

lexical_analysis.ibn_faris: الْفِعْلُ: ضِدُّ الْقَوْلِ. وَفَعَلَ: عَمِلَ
lexical_analysis.al_raghib: الْفِعْلُ: الْعَمَلُ. وَفِعْلُ اللَّهِ: خَلْقُهُ وَتَصَرُّفُهُ

quran_examples.ar: إِنَّمَا يَقُولُ لَنَا كُنۡ فَيَكُونُ
quran_examples.en: He only says to it, Be, and it is

hadith.ar: كَلِمَةُ الْحَقِّ عَمَلًا بِهَا
hadith.en: A word of truth acted upon

shades.name_ar: الْفِعْلُ - الْعَمَلُ، فِعْلُ اللَّهِ، فِعْلُ الْعَبْدِ
shades.explanation: The fi'l (action) is the most fundamental of all human activities. The verse 2:170 establishes the divine action of saying 'Be'. The fi'l in the Quran has multiple meanings - the human action (al-fi'l al-bashari), the divine action (al-fi'l al-ilahi), and the evil action (al-fi'l al-dani'). The hadith establishes that the best speech is the word of truth acted upon. Al-Ghazali treats the fi'l as the divine action - the one whose action is righteous has found the ultimate fi'l.
shades.hadith_ar: كَلِمَةُ الْحَقِّ عَمَلًا بِهَا
shades.hadith_en: A word of truth acted upon

meaning.en: To gain, profit. The root denotes the act of gaining or profiting - and the divine profit.

lexical_analysis.ibn_faris: الرِّبْحُ: ضِدُّ الْخُسْرَانِ. وَرَبِحَ: زَادَ
lexical_analysis.al_raghib: الرِّبْحُ: ضِدُّ الْخُسْرَانِ. وَالرِّبْحُ: الْفَائِدَةُ

quran_examples.ar: أُو۟لَـٰٓئِكَ ٱشۡتَرَوُا۟ ٱلضَّلَـٰلَةَ بِٱلۡهُدَىٰ فَمَا رَبِحَتۡ تِجَـٰرَتُهُمۡ وَمَا كَانُوا۟ مُهۡتَدِينَ
quran_examples.en: Those are the ones who have exchanged guidance for error; so their transaction has brought no profit, nor were they guided
quran_examples.context: The condemnation of those who exchange guidance for error

hadith.ar: مَنْ غَشَّنَا فَلَيۡسَ مِنَّا
hadith.en: Whoever cheats us is not of us

shades.explanation: The ribh (profit) in the Quran is the gain of a transaction. The verse 2:16 establishes the condemnation of those who exchanged guidance for error - their transaction brought no profit. The ribh in the Quran has multiple meanings - the worldly profit (al-ribh al-dunya), the eternal profit (al-ribh al-akhira), and the loss of profit (al-khusrana - the opposite). The hadith establishes that whoever cheats is not of us. Al-Ghazali treats the ribh as the ultimate transaction - the one who buys Paradise has found the ultimate ribh.
shades.hadith_ar: مَنْ غَشَّنَا فَلَيۡسَ مِنَّا
shades.hadith_en: Whoever cheats us is not of us

meaning.en: To be soft, gentle, lax. The root denotes the state of being soft or gentle.

lexical_analysis.ibn_faris: الرَّخَاءُ: ضِدُّ الشِّدَّةِ. وَرَخُوَ: لَانَ
lexical_analysis.al_raghib: الرَّخَاءُ: ضِدُّ الشِّدَّةِ. وَرَخَا: لَانَ

quran_examples.ar: يَـٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوا۟ كُتِبَ عَلَيۡكُمُ ٱلۡقِصَاصُ فِى ٱلۡقَتۡلَى
quran_examples.en: O you who have believed, prescribed for you is legal retribution for those murdered

hadith.ar: مَنْ لَا يَرْحَمْ لَا يُرْحَمْ
hadith.en: Whoever does not show mercy will not be shown mercy

shades.explanation: The rakha' (softness) in the Quran is the state of being soft.
shades.hadith_ar: مَنْ لَا يَرْحَمْ لَا يُرْحَمْ
shades.hadith_en: Whoever does not show mercy will not be shown mercy

meaning.en: To fear, be afraid. The root denotes the state of fear.

lexical_analysis.ibn_faris: الْخَوْفُ: ضِدُّ الْأَمْنِ. وَخَافَ: أَشْفَقَ
lexical_analysis.al_raghib: الْخَوْفُ: ضِدُّ الْأَمْنِ. وَخَافَ: تَوَقَّعَ الشَّيْءَ

quran_examples.ar: فَلَا تَخۡشَوۡهُمۡ وَٱخۡشَوۡنِى وَلِأُتِمَّ نِعۡمَتِى عَلَيۡكُمۡ
quran_examples.en: So do not fear them, but fear Me, that I may complete My favor upon you

hadith.ar: مَنْ خَافَ أَدْلَجَ
hadith.en: Whoever fears, departs at night

shades.explanation: The khawf (fear) is one of the most fundamental concepts.
shades.hadith_ar: مَنْ خَافَ أَدْلَجَ
shades.hadith_en: Whoever fears, departs at night

meaning.en: To begin, create, originate. The root denotes the act of beginning or creating.

lexical_analysis.ibn_faris: الْبَدْءُ: ضِدُّ الْإِعَادَةِ. وَبَدَأَ: اِبْتَدَأَ
lexical_analysis.al_raghib: الْبَدْءُ: الِابْتِدَاءُ. وَبَدَأَ الشَّيْءَ: أَنْشَأَهُ

quran_examples.ar: وَإِذۡ قَالَ رَبُّكَ لِلۡمَلَـٰٓئِكَةِ إِنِّى جَاعِلٌۭ فِى ٱلۡأَرۡضِ خَلِيفَةًۭ
quran_examples.en: And when your Lord said to the angels, I will make upon the earth a vicegerent
quran_examples.context: The creation of Adam as a vicegerent

hadith.ar: بَدَأَ الْإِسْلَامُ غَرِيبًا وَسَيَعُودُ غَرِيبًا
hadith.en: Islam began as a stranger and will return as a stranger

shades.explanation: The bad' (beginning) in the Quran is the act of originating. The verse 2:29 establishes that Allah will make upon the earth a vicegerent. The bad' in the Quran has multiple meanings - the divine beginning (al-bad' al-ilahi), the human beginning (al-bad' al-bashari), and the beginning of creation (bad' al-khalq). The hadith establishes that Islam began as a stranger. Al-Ghazali treats the bad' as the divine creation - the one who reflects on the bad' has begun the journey of ma'rifa.
shades.hadith_ar: بَدَأَ الْإِسْلَامُ غَرِيبًا
shades.hadith_en: Islam began as a stranger

meaning.en: To return, repeat. The root denotes the act of returning or repeating.

lexical_analysis.ibn_faris: الْعَوْدُ: الرُّجُوعُ. وَعَادَ: رَجَعَ
lexical_analysis.al_raghib: الْعَوْدُ: الرُّجُوعُ. وَالْمَوْعُودُ: الَّذِي يُرْجَعُ إِلَيْهِ

quran_examples.ar: وَمَن يَرۡتَدِدۡ مِنكُمۡ عَن دِينِهِۦ فَيَمُتۡ وَهُوَ كَافِرٌ
quran_examples.en: And whoever of you turns back from his religion and dies as a disbeliever
quran_examples.context: The nullification of deeds for apostasy

hadith.ar: تَابَ اللَّهُ عَلَى مَنْ تَابَ
hadith.en: Allah accepts the repentance of the one who repents

shades.explanation: The awd (return) in the Quran is the act of returning. The verse 2:217 establishes that whoever turns back from his religion and dies as a disbeliever - their deeds are nullified. The awd in the Quran has multiple meanings - the physical return (al-awd al-maddi), the spiritual return (al-awd al-ruhani), and the habitual return (al-i'tiyad - to be accustomed). The hadith establishes that Allah accepts the repentance of the one who repents. Al-Ghazali treats the awd as the spiritual return - the one who returns to Allah has found the ultimate awd.
shades.hadith_ar: تَابَ اللَّهُ عَلَى مَنْ تَابَ
shades.hadith_en: Allah accepts the repentance of the one who repents

meaning.en: To complete, perfect. The root denotes the act of completing or perfecting.

lexical_analysis.ibn_faris: التَّمَامُ: ضِدُّ النُّقْصَانِ. وَتَمَّمَ: أَتَمَّ
lexical_analysis.al_raghib: التَّمَامُ: ضِدُّ النُّقْصَانِ. وَتَمَّمَ الشَّيْءَ: أَكْمَلَهُ

quran_examples.ar: وَلِتُكَمِّلُوا ٱلۡعِدَّةَ وَلِتُكَبِّرُوا۟ ٱللَّهَ عَلَىٰ مَا هَدَىٰكُمۡ وَلَعَلَّكُمۡ تَشۡكُرُونَ
quran_examples.en: And [We] intended to complete the count and to glorify Allah for that [to] which He has guided you and perhaps you would be grateful
quran_examples.context: The completion of the count of Ramadan

hadith.ar: مَنْ صَامَ رَمَضَانَ إِيمَانًا وَاحْتِسَابًا غُفِرَ لَهُ مَا تَقَدَّمَ مِنْ ذَنْبِهِ
hadith.en: Whoever fasts Ramadan out of faith and seeking reward, his past sins will be forgiven

shades.explanation: The tamam (completion) in the Quran is the act of perfecting. The verse 2:185 establishes the completion of the count of Ramadan. The tamam in the Quran has multiple meanings - the physical completion (al-tamam al-maddi), the spiritual completion (al-tamam al-ruhani), and the divine completion (al-tamam al-ilahi). The hadith establishes that whoever fasts Ramadan out of faith has his past sins forgiven. Al-Ghazali treats the tamam as the divine perfection - the one who has attained the tamam of faith has found the ultimate perfection.
shades.hadith_ar: مَنْ صَامَ رَمَضَانَ إِيمَانًا وَاحْتِسَابًا
shades.hadith_en: Whoever fasts Ramadan out of faith and seeking reward

meaning.en: To dispute, argue. The root denotes the act of disputing or arguing.

lexical_analysis.ibn_faris: الْحَكُّ: الْجَرْحُ. وَتَحَاكَمَا: اخْتَصَمَا
lexical_analysis.al_raghib: الْحَكُّ: الْجَرْحُ بِالْحِجَارَةِ. وَالْحَاكُّ: الْجَارِحُ

quran_examples.ar: فَإِن لَّمۡ تَفۡعَلُوا۟ وَلَن تَفۡعَلُوا۟ فَٱتَّقُوا۟ ٱلنَّارَ ٱلَّتِى وَقُودُهَا ٱلنَّاسُ وَٱلۡحِجَارَةُ أُعِدَّتۡ لِلۡكَـٰفِرِينَ
quran_examples.en: But if you do not - and you will never be able to - then fear the Fire, whose fuel is men and stones, prepared for the disbelievers

hadith.ar: لَا تَجْعَلُوا بَيْنَ الْأَنْبِيَاءِ فِتَنَةً
hadith.en: Do not make fitna among the prophets

shades.explanation: The haku (dispute) in the Quran is the act of arguing.
shades.hadith_ar: لَا تَجْعَلُوا بَيْنَ الْأَنْبِيَاءِ فِتَنَةً
shades.hadith_en: Do not make fitna among the prophets

meaning.en: To forbid, make sacred. The root denotes the act of forbidding or making sacred.

lexical_analysis.ibn_faris: التَّحْرِيمُ: ضِدُّ التَّحْلِيلِ. وَحَرَّمَ: مَنَعَ
lexical_analysis.al_raghib: التَّحْرِيمُ: ضِدُّ التَّحْلِيلِ. وَالْحَرَامُ: الْمَمْنُوعُ

quran_examples.ar: إِنَّمَا حَرَّمَ عَلَيۡكُمُ ٱلۡمَيۡتَةَ وَٱلدَّمَ وَلَحۡمَ ٱلۡخِنزِيرِ وَمَآ أُهِلَّ بِهِۦ لِغَيۡرِ ٱللَّهِ
quran_examples.en: He has only forbidden to you dead animals, blood, the flesh of swine, and that which has been dedicated to other than Allah
quran_examples.context: The divine prohibition of certain foods

hadith.ar: إِنَّ اللَّهَ حَرَّمَ عَلَيْكُمْ عُقُوقَ الْأُمَّهَاتِ
hadith.en: Indeed Allah has forbidden you from disobeying the mothers

shades.name_ar: التَّحْرِيمُ - ضِدُّ التَّحْلِيلِ، حَرَامُ اللَّهِ، الْحَرَمُ الْمَكِّيُّ
shades.explanation: The harama (prohibition) in the Quran is the divine act of forbidding. The verse 2:173 establishes that Allah has only forbidden to you dead animals, blood, the flesh of swine, and that which has been dedicated to other than Allah. The harama in the Quran has multiple meanings - the divine prohibition (al-tahrim al-ilahi), the sacred (al-haram - the Sacred Mosque), and the prohibited (al-muharram). The hadith establishes that Allah has forbidden disobeying the mothers. Al-Ghazali treats the harama as the divine prohibition - the one who respects the harama of Allah has found the ultimate taqwa.
shades.hadith_ar: إِنَّ اللَّهَ حَرَّمَ عَلَيْكُمْ عُقُوقَ الْأُمَّهَاتِ
shades.hadith_en: Indeed Allah has forbidden you from disobeying the mothers

meaning.en: To be sweet, pleasant. The root denotes the state of being sweet or pleasant.

lexical_analysis.ibn_faris: الْحَلَاوَةُ: ضِدُّ الْمُرَارَةِ. وَحَلَا: حَلَاوَةٌ
lexical_analysis.al_raghib: الْحَلَاوَةُ: ضِدُّ الْمُرَارَةِ

quran_examples.ar: كُتِبَ عَلَيۡكُمُ ٱلۡقِتَالُ وَهُوَ كُرۡهٌۭ لَّكُمۡ ۖ وَعَسَىٰٓ أَن تَكۡرَهُوا۟ شَيۡـًۭٔا وَهُوَ خَيۡرٌۭ لَّكُمۡ ۖ وَعَسَىٰٓ أَن تُحِبُّوا۟ شَيۡـًۭٔا وَهُوَ شَرٌّۭ لَّكُمۡ ۚ وَٱللَّهُ يَعۡلَمُ وَأَنتُمۡ لَا تَعۡلَمُونَ
quran_examples.en: Fighting has been enjoined upon you while it is hateful to you. Perhaps you hate a thing and it is good for you; and perhaps you love a thing and it is bad for you. And Allah knows, while you know not
quran_examples.context: The divine wisdom in the commands

hadith.ar: احْرِصْ عَلَى مَا يَنْفَعُكَ وَاسْتَعِنْ بِاللَّهِ وَلَا تَعْجَزْ
hadith.en: Be keen on what benefits you, seek help from Allah, and do not despair

shades.explanation: The halawa (sweetness) in the Quran is the state of being sweet.
shades.hadith_ar: احْرِصْ عَلَى مَا يَنْفَعُكَ
shades.hadith_en: Be keen on what benefits you

meaning.en: To surround, enclose. The root denotes the act of surrounding or enclosing.

lexical_analysis.ibn_faris: الْحَوْيُ: الْجَمْعُ. وَحَوَى الشَّيْءَ: جَمَعَهُ
lexical_analysis.al_raghib: الْحَوْيُ: ضِدُّ النَّشْرِ. وَتَحَوَّى: تَقَبَّضَ

quran_examples.ar: أَوۡ كَصَيِّبٍۢ مِّنَ ٱلسَّمَآءِ فِيهِ ظُلُمَـٰتٌۭ وَرَعۡدٌۭ وَبَرۡقٌۭ
quran_examples.en: Or like a rainstorm from the sky in which is darkness, thunder and lightning

hadith.ar: إِنَّ اللَّهَ يُحِبُّ الْعَبْدَ التَّقِيَّ الْغَنِيَّ الْخَفِيَّ
hadith.en: Indeed Allah loves the servant who is pious, self-sufficient, and hidden

shades.explanation: The hawi (enclosing) in the Quran is the act of surrounding.
shades.hadith_ar: إِنَّ اللَّهَ يُحِبُّ الْعَبْدَ التَّقِيَّ الْغَنِيَّ الْخَفِيَّ
shades.hadith_en: Indeed Allah loves the servant who is pious, self-sufficient, and hidden

meaning.en: To be cowardly. The root denotes the state of being cowardly.

lexical_analysis.ibn_faris: الْبَوَالُ: الْهَلَاكُ. وَبَالَ: هَلَكَ
lexical_analysis.al_raghib: الْبَوَالُ: الْهَلَاكُ. وَبَالَ: هَلَكَ مَالُهُ

quran_examples.ar: فَٱتَّقُوا۟ ٱلنَّارَ ٱلَّتِى وَقُودُهَا ٱلنَّاسُ وَٱلۡحِجَارَةُ
quran_examples.en: Then fear the Fire, whose fuel is men and stones

hadith.ar: لَا تَجْعَلُوا بَيْنَ الْأَنْبِيَاءِ فِتَنَةً
hadith.en: Do not make fitna among the prophets

shades.explanation: The bawal (cowardice) in the Quran is the state of being cowardly.
shades.hadith_ar: لَا تَجْعَلُوا بَيْنَ الْأَنْبِيَاءِ فِتَنَةً
shades.hadith_en: Do not make fitna among the prophets

meaning.en: To praise, commend. The root denotes the act of praising or commending.

lexical_analysis.ibn_faris: الْحَمْدُ: ضِدُّ الذَّمِّ. وَحَمَدَ: ثَنَى بِالْجَمِيلِ
lexical_analysis.al_raghib: الْحَمْدُ: الثَّنَاءُ بِالْجَمِيلِ. وَالْحَمِيدُ: الْمَحْمُودُ

quran_examples.ar: وَإِذۡ قَالَ رَبُّكَ لِلۡمَلَـٰٓئِكَةِ إِنِّى جَاعِلٌۭ فِى ٱلۡأَرۡضِ خَلِيفَةًۭ ۖ قَالُوٓاْ أَتَجۡعَلُ فِيهَا مَن يُفۡسِدُ فِيهَا وَيَسۡفِكُ ٱلدِّمَآءَ
quran_examples.en: And when your Lord said to the angels, I will make upon the earth a vicegerent, they said, Will You place upon it one who causes corruption therein and sheds blood
quran_examples.context: The announcement of the creation of Adam

hadith.ar: الْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ رَبِّ الْعَالَمِينَ
hadith.en: Praise be to Allah, Lord of the worlds

shades.name_ar: الْحَمْدُ - ضِدُّ الذَّمِّ، الْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ رَبِّ الْعَالَمِينَ
shades.explanation: The hamd (praise) in the Quran is one of the most fundamental acts of worship. The verse 2:30 establishes the announcement of the creation of Adam. The hamd in the Quran has multiple meanings - the human praise (al-hamd al-bashari), the divine praise (al-hamd al-ilahi), and the universal praise (al-hamd al-kawni - all creation praises Allah). The hadith establishes that the best dhikr is al-hamdu lillah. Al-Ghazali (Ihya, Book of the Etiquette of Eating) treats the hamd as the highest form of dhikr - the one who praises Allah has found the ultimate hamd.
shades.hadith_ar: الْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ رَبِّ الْعَالَمِينَ
shades.hadith_en: Praise be to Allah, Lord of the worlds

meaning.en: To deny, disbelieve. The root denotes the act of denying or disbelieving.

lexical_analysis.ibn_faris: الْحُكْرُ: الْمَنْعُ. وَحَكَرَ: مَنَعَ
lexical_analysis.al_raghib: الْحُكْرُ: ضِدُّ الْبُخْلِ. وَتَحَكَّرَ: امْتَنَعَ

quran_examples.ar: إِنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ يَكۡتُمُونَ مَآ أَنزَلَ ٱللَّهُ مِنَ ٱلۡكِتَـٰبِ وَيَشۡتَرُونَ بِهِۦ ثَمَنًۭا قَلِيلًا
quran_examples.en: Indeed those who conceal what Allah has revealed of the Book and exchange it for a small price

hadith.ar: مَنْ لَا يَشْكُرُ النَّاسَ لَا يَشْكُرُ اللَّهَ
hadith.en: Whoever does not thank people does not thank Allah

shades.explanation: The hukr (stinginess) in the Quran is closely related to al-bukhl.
shades.hadith_ar: مَنْ لَا يَشْكُرُ النَّاسَ لَا يَشْكُرُ اللَّهَ
shades.hadith_en: Whoever does not thank people does not thank Allah

meaning.en: To move, shake. The root denotes the act of moving or shaking.

lexical_analysis.ibn_faris: الْحَرَكَةُ: ضِدُّ السُّكُونِ. وَحَرَكَ: أَزَالَ السُّكُونَ
lexical_analysis.al_raghib: الْحَرَكَةُ: ضِدُّ السُّكُونِ. وَتَحَرَّكَ: تَحَرَّكَ

quran_examples.ar: أَلَمۡ تَرَ إِلَى ٱلَّذِينَ خَرَجُوا۟ مِن دِيَـٰرِهِم بَغۡرًا حَذَرَ ٱلۡمَوۡتِ فَقَالَ لَهُمُ ٱللَّهُ مُوتُوا۟ ثُمَّ أَحۡيَـٰهُمۡ ۚ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ لَذُو فَضۡلٍ عَلَى ٱلنَّاسِ وَلَـٰكِنَّ أَكۡثَرَ ٱلنَّاسِ لَا يَشۡكُرُونَ
quran_examples.en: Have you not considered those who left their homes in thousands, fearing death? Allah said to them, Die; then He gave them life. Indeed Allah is full of bounty to the people, but most people do not show gratitude
quran_examples.context: The story of the thousands who left their homes

hadith.ar: الْأَرْوَاحُ جُنُودٌ مُجَنَّدَةٌ
hadith.en: The souls are like conscripted soldiers

shades.explanation: The haraka (movement) in the Quran is the act of moving.
shades.hadith_ar: الْأَرْوَاحُ جُنُودٌ مُجَنَّدَةٌ
shades.hadith_en: The souls are like conscripted soldiers

meaning.en: To be giddy, deceive, be jealous. The root denotes the state of being giddy or jealous.

lexical_analysis.ibn_faris: الْغِلُّ: الْحِقْدُ فِي الصَّدْرِ. وَغَلَّ: حَقَدَ
lexical_analysis.al_raghib: الْغِلُّ: الْحِقْدُ فِي الصَّدْرِ. وَالْغُلُّ: ضِدُّ الْوَفَاءِ

quran_examples.ar: وَدَّ كَثِيرٌۭ مِّنۡ أَهۡلِ ٱلۡكِتَـٰبِ لَوۡ يَرُدُّونَكُم مِّنۢ بَعۡدِ إِيمَـٰنِكُمۡ كُفَّارًا حَسَدًۭا مِّنۡ عِندِ أَنفُسِهِم مِّنۢ بَعۡدِ مَا تَبَيَّنَ لَهُمُ ٱلۡحَقُّ
quran_examples.en: Many of the People of the Book wish they could turn you back to disbelief after your faith had been established, out of envy from themselves, even after the truth had become clear to them
quran_examples.context: The envy of the People of the Book

hadith.ar: لَا تَجْعَلُوا بَيْنَ الْأَنْبِيَاءِ فِتَنَةً
hadith.en: Do not make fitna among the prophets

shades.name_ar: الْغِلُّ - ضِدُّ الْوَفَاءِ، الْحِقْدُ فِي الصَّدْرِ
shades.explanation: The ghil (enmity) in the Quran is the state of holding grudges.
shades.hadith_ar: لَا تَجْعَلُوا بَيْنَ الْأَنْبِيَاءِ فِتَنَةً
shades.hadith_en: Do not make fitna among the prophets

meaning.en: To be light, fall. The root denotes the state of being light or falling.

lexical_analysis.ibn_faris: الْهَوْفُ: الضَّعْفُ. وَهَافَ: سَقَطَ
lexical_analysis.al_raghib: الْهَوْفُ: الضَّعْفُ. وَتَهَافَتِ الْأَشْجَارُ: تَسَاقَطَتْ

quran_examples.ar: وَلِكُلٍّۢ وِجۡهَةٌ هُوَ مُوَلِّيهَا ۖ فَٱسۡتَبِقُوا۟ ٱلۡخَيۡرَٰتِ
quran_examples.en: For each [religious following] is a direction toward which it faces. So race to [all that is] good
quran_examples.context: The diversity of religions and the race to good deeds

hadith.ar: احْرِصْ عَلَى مَا يَنْفَعُكَ وَاسْتَعِنْ بِاللَّهِ وَلَا تَعْجَزْ
hadith.en: Be keen on what benefits you, seek help from Allah, and do not despair

shades.explanation: The haw (falling) in the Quran is the state of falling.
shades.hadith_ar: احْرِصْ عَلَى مَا يَنْفَعُكَ
shades.hadith_en: Be keen on what benefits you

meaning.en: To cut, peel. The root denotes the act of cutting or peeling - and the gathering of fruit.

lexical_analysis.ibn_faris: الْخَرْفُ: قَطْفُ الثَّمَرِ
lexical_analysis.al_raghib: الْخَرْفُ: الْقَطْفُ. وَخَرَفَ الثَّمَرَ: قَطَفَهُ

quran_examples.ar: ٱلَّذِينَ يَأۡكُلُونَ ٱلرِّبَوٰا۟ لَا يَقُومُونَ إِلَّا كَمَا يَقُومُ ٱلَّذِى يَتَخَبَّطُهُ ٱلشَّيۡطَـٰنُ مِنَ ٱلۡمَسِّ ۚ ذَٰلِكَ بِأَنَّهُمۡ قَالُوٓاْ إِنَّمَا ٱلۡبَيۡعُ مِثۡلُ ٱلرِّبَوٰا۟ ۗ وَأَحَلَّ ٱللَّهُ ٱلۡبَيۡعَ وَحَرَّمَ ٱلرِّبَوٰا۟
quran_examples.en: Those who consume interest cannot stand [on the Day of Resurrection] except as one stands who is being beaten by Satan into insanity. That is because they say, Trade is [just] like interest. But Allah has permitted trade and has forbidden interest

hadith.ar: لَا تَجْعَلُوا بَيْنَ الْأَنْبِيَاءِ فِتَنَةً
hadith.en: Do not make fitna among the prophets

shades.explanation: The kharf (picking) in the Quran is the act of picking fruit.
shades.hadith_ar: لَا تَجْعَلُوا بَيْنَ الْأَنْبِيَاءِ فِتَنَةً
shades.hadith_en: Do not make fitna among the prophets

meaning.en: To delay, hinder. The root denotes the act of delaying or hindering.

lexical_analysis.ibn_faris: الْعَوْقُ: ضِدُّ التَّقَدُّمِ. وَعَاقَ: حَبَسَ
lexical_analysis.al_raghib: الْعَوْقُ: ضِدُّ التَّقَدُّمِ. وَعَاقَ الشَّيْءَ: حَبَسَهُ

quran_examples.ar: وَٱلَّذِينَ يُتَوَفَّوۡنَ مِنكُمۡ وَيَذَرُونَ أَزۡوَٰجًا وَصِيَّةًۭ لِّأَزۡوَٰجِهِم مَّتَـٰعًا إِلَى ٱلۡحَوۡلِ غَيۡرَ إِخۡرَاجٍۢ ۚ فَإِنۡ خَرَجۡنَ فَلَا جُنَاحَ عَلَيۡكُمۡ فِى مَا فَعَلۡنَ فِىٓ أَنفُسِهِنَّ مِن مَّعۡرُوفٍۢ ۗ وَٱللَّهُ عَزِيزٌ حَكِيمٌ
quran_examples.en: And those who are taken in death among you and leave wives behind - they, [the wives, shall] wait four months and ten [days]. And when they have fulfilled their term, then there is no blame upon you for what they do with themselves in an acceptable manner

hadith.ar: لَا تَجْعَلُوا بَيْنَ الْأَنْبِيَاءِ فِتَنَةً
hadith.en: Do not make fitna among the prophets

shades.explanation: The awq (delay) in the Quran is the act of delaying.
shades.hadith_ar: لَا تَجْعَلُوا بَيْنَ الْأَنْبِيَاءِ فِتَنَةً
shades.hadith_en: Do not make fitna among the prophets

meaning.en: To be hot, burning. The root denotes the state of being hot or burning.

lexical_analysis.ibn_faris: الْحَمَامُ: الْمَوْتُ. وَحَمَّ: قَصَدَ
lexical_analysis.al_raghib: الْحَمَامُ: الْمَوْتُ. وَالْحَامُّ: الْمَوْتُ

quran_examples.ar: أَوۡ كَٱلَّذِى مَرَّ عَلَىٰ قَرۡيَةٍۢ وَهِىَ خَاوِيَةٌ عَلَىٰ عُرُوشِهَا قَالَ أَنَّىٰ يُحۡيِۦ هَـٰذِهِ ٱللَّهُ بَعۡدَ مَوۡتِهَا ۖ فَأَمَاتَهُ ٱللَّهُ مِا۟ئَةَ عَامٍۢ ثُمَّ بَعَثَهُۥ
quran_examples.en: Or [consider such an example] as he who passed by a township which had fallen into ruin. He said, How will Allah bring this to life after its death? So Allah caused him to die for a hundred years; then He revived him
quran_examples.context: The story of the man who died and was revived

hadith.ar: لَا تَجْعَلُوا بَيْنَ الْأَنْبِيَاءِ فِتَنَةً
hadith.en: Do not make fitna among the prophets

shades.explanation: The hamim (hot water) in the Quran is the boiling water of Hellfire.
shades.hadith_ar: لَا تَجْعَلُوا بَيْنَ الْأَنْبِيَاءِ فِتَنَةً
shades.hadith_en: Do not make fitna among the prophets

meaning.en: To do, act, work. The root denotes the act of doing or working.

lexical_analysis.ibn_faris: الْعَمَلُ: ضِدُّ الْقَوْلِ. وَعَمِلَ: فَعَلَ
lexical_analysis.al_raghib: الْعَمَلُ: كُلُّ فِعْلٍ يَفْعَلُهُ الْإِنْسَانُ مِنْ قَوْلٍ أَوْ فِعْلٍ

quran_examples.ar: وَبَشِّرِ ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوا۟ وَعَمِلُوا۟ ٱلصَّـٰلِحَـٰتِ أَنَّ لَهُمۡ جَنَّـٰتٍۢ
quran_examples.en: And give good tidings to those who believe and do righteous deeds that they will have gardens [in Paradise]
quran_examples.context: The good tidings for the believers who do righteous deeds

hadith.ar: إِنَّمَا الْأَعْمَالُ بِالنِّيَّاتِ
hadith.en: Indeed deeds are judged by intentions

shades.explanation: The 'amal (deed) in the Quran is the act of doing. The verse 2:25 establishes the good tidings for the believers who do righteous deeds. The 'amal in the Quran has multiple meanings - the righteous deed (al-'amal al-salih), the evil deed (al-'amal al-sayyi'), and the divine deed (al-'amal al-ilahi). The hadith establishes that deeds are judged by intentions. Al-Ghazali (Ihya, Book of Etiquette) treats the 'amal as the outward action - the one whose deeds are righteous has found the ultimate 'amal.
shades.hadith_ar: إِنَّمَا الْأَعْمَالُ بِالنِّيَّاتِ
shades.hadith_en: Indeed deeds are judged by intentions

meaning.en: To know, recognize. The root denotes the act of knowing or recognizing.

lexical_analysis.ibn_faris: الْمَعْرِفَةُ: ضِدُّ الْإِنْكَارِ. وَعَرَفَ: عَلِمَ
lexical_analysis.al_raghib: الْمَعْرِفَةُ: عِلْمُ الشَّيْءِ بِتَصَوُّرِهِ. وَالْمَعْرُوفُ: الْمَحْمُودُ

quran_examples.ar: وَلَقَدۡ صَدَقَكُمُ ٱللَّهُ وَعۡدَهُۥٓ إِذۡ تَحُسُّونَهُم بِإِذۡنِهِۦ ۖ حَتَّىٰٓ إِذَا فَشِلۡتُمۡ وَتَنَـٰزَعۡتُمۡ فِى ٱلۡأَمۡرِ وَعَصَيۡتُم مِّنۢ بَعۡدِ مَآ أَرَىٰكُم مَّا تُحِبُّونَ
quran_examples.en: And Allah had certainly fulfilled His promise to you when you were killing them by His permission until [the time] when you lost courage and fell to disputing about the order and disobeyed after He had shown you that which you love
quran_examples.context: The promise of Allah and the slip of the believers

hadith.ar: مَنْ عَرَفَ نَفْسَهُ فَقَدْ عَرَفَ رَبَّهُ
hadith.en: Whoever knows himself knows his Lord

shades.name_ar: الْمَعْرِفَةُ - ضِدُّ الْإِنْكَارِ، عِلْمُ الشَّيْءِ بِتَصَوُّرِهِ
shades.explanation: The ma'rifa (knowledge, recognition) in the Quran is one of the highest stations.
shades.hadith_ar: مَنْ عَرَفَ نَفْسَهُ فَقَدْ عَرَفَ رَبَّهُ
shades.hadith_en: Whoever knows himself knows his Lord

meaning.en: To dispute, argue. The root denotes the act of disputing or arguing.

lexical_analysis.ibn_faris: الشِّجَارُ: الْخُصُومَةُ. وَشَجَرَ: اخْتَصَمَ
lexical_analysis.al_raghib: الشِّجَارُ: الْخُصُومَةُ. وَتَشَاجَرُوا: تَخَاصَمُوا

quran_examples.ar: وَإِذۡ قَالَ رَبُّكَ لِلۡمَلَـٰٓئِكَةِ إِنِّى جَاعِلٌۭ فِى ٱلۡأَرۡضِ خَلِيفَةًۭ
quran_examples.en: And when your Lord said to the angels, I will make upon the earth a vicegerent
quran_examples.context: The announcement of the creation of Adam

hadith.ar: لَا تَجْعَلُوا بَيْنَ الْأَنْبِيَاءِ فِتَنَةً
hadith.en: Do not make fitna among the prophets

shades.explanation: The shajar (dispute) in the Quran is the act of disputing.
shades.hadith_ar: لَا تَجْعَلُوا بَيْنَ الْأَنْبِيَاءِ فِتَنَةً
shades.hadith_en: Do not make fitna among the prophets

meaning.en: To drown, sink. The root denotes the state of drowning or sinking.
meaning.ar: الْغَرَقُ: الْغَوْصُ فِي الْمَاءِ حَتَّى الْمَوْتِ

lexical_analysis.ibn_faris: الْغَرَقُ: الْغَوْصُ فِي الْمَاءِ. وَغَرِقَ: غَرَقَ
lexical_analysis.al_raghib: الْغَرَقُ: الْغَوْصُ فِي الْمَاءِ. وَأَغْرَقَ: أَغْرَقَ

quran_examples.ar: وَإِذۡ فَرَقۡنَا بِكُمُ ٱلۡبَحۡرَ فَأَنجَيۡنَـٰكُمۡ وَأَغۡرَقۡنَآ ءَالَ فِرۡعَوۡنَ
quran_examples.en: And [recall] when We parted the sea for you and saved you and drowned the people of Pharaoh
quran_examples.context: The parting of the sea and the drowning of Pharaoh's people

hadith.ar: لَوْ أَنَّ لِلَّهَ عَمَلًا لَكَانَ الْمَوْتُ
hadith.en: If Allah had a deed, it would be death

shades.name_ar: الْغَرَقُ - الْغَوْصُ فِي الْمَاءِ، إِغْرَاقُ اللَّهِ لِلْكَافِرِينَ
shades.explanation: The gharaq (drowning) in the Quran is the act of sinking in water.
shades.hadith_ar: لَوْ أَنَّ لِلَّهَ عَمَلًا لَكَانَ الْمَوْتُ
shades.hadith_en: If Allah had a deed, it would be death

meaning.en: To live, be alive. The root denotes life and existence.
meaning.ar: الْحَيَاةُ: ضِدُّ الْمَوْتِ، وُجُودُ الْحَيَوِيَّةِ وَالْحَرَكَةِ

lexical_analysis.ibn_faris: الْحَيُّ: الْحَيَاةُ نَقِيضُ الْمَوْتِ. قَالَ: حَيِيَ، يَحْيَا
lexical_analysis.al_raghib: الْحَيَاةُ: النَّامُ الْمُتَنَفِّسُ. وَالْحَيُّ مِنَ اللَّهِ: الدَّائِمُ الْحَيَاةِ الَّذِي لَا يَمُوتُ

quran_examples.ar: ٱللَّهُ لَآ إِلَـٰهَ إِلَّا هُوَ ٱلۡحَىُّ ٱلۡقَيُّومُۚ
quran_examples.en: Allah - there is no deity except Him, the Ever-Living, the Sustainer of existence

quran_examples.ar: كَيۡفَ تَكۡفُرُونَ بِٱللَّهِ وَكُنتُمۡ أَمۡوَٰتًۭا فَأَحۡيَـٰكُمۡۖ ثُمَّ يُمِيتُكُمۡ ثُمَّ يُحۡيِيكُمۡ
quran_examples.en: How can you disbelieve in Allah when you were lifeless and He brought you to life; then He will cause you to die and then bring you back to life
quran_examples.context: The beginning and end of life

hadith.ar: يَا حَيُّ يَا قَيُّومُ، بِرَحْمَتِكَ أَسْتَغِيثُ
hadith.en: O Ever-Living, O Sustainer, by Your mercy I seek help

hadith.ar: كُونُوا عَلَى الْحَيَاةِ الدُّنْيَا أَشَدَّ حِرْصًا مِنْكُمْ عَلَى الْآخِرَةِ
hadith.en: You are more eager for the life of this world than for the Hereafter

shades.name_ar: الْحَيُّ - الْقَيُّومُ بِذَاتِهِ، الَّذِي لَا يَمُوتُ
shades.explanation: al-Hayy (The Ever-Living) is one of the most majestic Names of Allah. The root hy-y denotes life and existence. Al-Hayy is the One whose life is perfect, complete, and unending — without beginning, without end, without any defect. He is eternally alive, and all life flows from Him. The hadith Qudsi states: 'O My servants, if the first of you and the last of you and the jinn and mankind all stood in one place and asked of Me, I would give to each one what he asked — that would not diminish what is with Me except as a needle dipped in the sea.' This Name is paired with al-Qayyum in the Throne Verse.
shades.hadith_ar: الْحَيُّ عَلَى الْحَيِّ لَا يَمُوتُ، وَالْحَيَاةُ لَا تَزَالُ فِي الْأَزَلِ
shades.hadith_en: The Ever-Living upon the Ever-Living does not die, and life never ceases in eternity

shades.name_ar: الْحَيَوَانُ - كُلُّ مَا تَتَنَفَّسُ فِيهِ الرُّوحُ
shades.explanation: al-Hayawan (the living creature) is derived from the same root. In Quran 29:64 it refers to the abode of eternal life — 'the life of this world is but amusement and diversion, but the Hereafter is the abode of perpetuity (al-hayawan) for those who fear Allah.' Classical exegetes distinguish dunya (lower, fleeting life) from hayawan (permanent, eternal life in the hereafter). Ibn al-Qayyim explains hayawan is the eternal life that never ends — the special life of Paradise for the people of taqwa.
shades.hadith_ar: الدُّنْيَا مَنْزِلُ عَارِيَةٍ، وَالْآخِرَةُ مَنْزِلُ بَقَاءٍ
shades.hadith_en: This world is a borrowed dwelling, and the Hereafter is the dwelling of permanence

shades.explanation: Hayat (life) is the antithesis of mawt (death). In the Quran, Allah gives life and causes death, and He is described as al-Muhyi (the Giver of Life). Hayat in the Quran includes three levels: the hayat al-dunya (life of this world — temporary), the hayat al-tawwa (repentance, regeneration — 4:17, 6:122), and the hayat al-akhira (life of the Hereafter — eternal). The dunya life is often described as play, amusement, and vanity compared to the hayat al-akhira. The hadith states: 'The life of the believer is the seed of his death' — the dunya life plants the seed for the eternal harvest.
shades.hadith_ar: حَيَاتُ الْمُؤْمِنِ بَذْرُ مَوْتِهِ
shades.hadith_en: The believer's life is the seed of his death

shades.name_en: Hayy al-Mayyit - Bringing the Dead to Life
shades.name_ar: إِحْيَاءُ الْمَوْتَى - إِنْبَاثُ الْحَيَاةِ فِي الْهَيَاكِلِ الْمَيْتَةِ
shades.explanation: Ihya al-mayyit (bringing the dead to life) is one of Allah's greatest signs. In the Quran, this is demonstrated through: (1) the creation of Adam from lifeless clay, (2) the reviving of the People of the Cave after long sleep, (3) the slain heifer whose parts spoke after being struck, (4) the bird made alive again by Ibrahim in 2:260, (5) Jesus's revival of the dead by Allah's permission, and (6) the splitting of the earth over the dead on the Day of Judgment. Each of these signs demonstrates that Allah is al-Muhyi, the One who gives life to that which is dead. The believer's heart is also considered dead and is brought to life by faith and remembrance of Allah.
shades.hadith_ar: إِنَّ اللَّهَ يُحْيِي الْمَوْتَى وَيُنْبِتُ الْأَرْضَ بَعْدَ مَوْتِهَا
shades.hadith_en: Indeed Allah gives life to the dead and brings forth the earth after its death

meaning.en: To follow, succeed. The root denotes the act of following or coming after.
meaning.ar: التَّبَعُ: وُصُولُ الشَّيْءِ بِالشَّيْءِ، التَّالِي لَهُ

lexical_analysis.ibn_faris: التَّبَعُ: قُفُولُ الشَّيْءِ الشَّيْءَ. قَالَ: تَبِعَ، يَتْبَعُ، تَبَعًا
lexical_analysis.al_raghib: التَّابِعُ: الْقَافِي الْآخَرَ. وَالتَّبَعُ: الْآخِرُ مِنْ كُلِّ شَيْءٍ

quran_examples.ar: وَكَذَٰلِكَ جَعَلۡنَـٰكُمۡ أُمَّةًۭ وَسَطًۭا لِّتَكُونُوا۟ شُهَدَآءَ عَلَى ٱلنَّاسِ
quran_examples.en: And thus We have made you a middle nation that you will be witnesses over the people
quran_examples.context: The ummah of the middle way

quran_examples.ar: ٱلَّذِينَ يَتَّبِعُونَ ٱلرَّسُولَ ٱلنَّبِىَّ ٱلۡأُمِّىَّ
quran_examples.en: Those who follow the Messenger, the unlettered Prophet
quran_examples.context: The description of the righteous who follow the Prophet

hadith.ar: مَنْ أَحْدَثَ فِي أَمْرِنَا هَذَا مَا لَيْسَ مِنْهُ فَهُوَ رَدٌّ
hadith.en: Whoever introduces into this affair of ours what is not from it, it is rejected

hadith.ar: الْيَهُودُ وَالنَّصَارَى لَا يَصْبُغُونَ رُءُوسَهُمْ فَكُونُوا تَبَعًا لِلْيَهُودِ وَالنَّصَارَى
hadith.en: The Jews and Christians do not dye their hair, so be followers of them

shades.name_ar: التَّابِعُ - مَنْ يَتْبَعُ غَيْرَهُ، التَّالِي لَهُ
shades.explanation: at-Taba'iyya (the following) is the act of following. In the Quran, taba'a often appears in the context of following truth or falsehood, of following Allah's guidance, of following messengers, or of following desires. Verse 2:143 establishes that the ummah follows the middle way. Verse 7:157 describes the Prophet as following the guidance of Allah. The Quran warns against following shaytan's footsteps (2:168, 2:208). The hadith establishes that every nation follows its dead — meaning each ummah follows its leaders and scholars.
shades.hadith_ar: مَا مِنْ نَبِيٍّ إِلَّا قَدْ سَلَفَ مِنْهُ أُمَّةٌ تَتْبَعُ سُنَّتَهَا
shades.hadith_en: There is no prophet except that his ummah has preceded following his sunnah

shades.explanation: at-Tabi'un (the followers) refers to the generation that followed the Companions. In Quran 9:100, Allah describes the Muhajirun, the Ansar, and those who followed them in goodness — promising forgiveness and Paradise. The Tabi'un are the second best generation of Islam. They followed the Companions in faith and deed. The Prophet ﷺ stated: 'The best of generations is my generation, then those who follow them, then those who follow them.' This hadith emphasizes the importance of following the early generations.
shades.hadith_ar: خَيْرُ الْقُرُونِ قَرْنِي، ثُمَّ الَّذِينَ يَلُونَهُمْ، ثُمَّ الَّذِينَ يَلُونَهُمْ
shades.hadith_en: The best of generations is my generation, then those who follow them, then those who follow them

shades.name_ar: التَّبَعُ - مَا يَتْبَعُ الشَّيْءَ مِنْ أَثَرٍ أَوْ عَاقِبَةٍ
shades.explanation: at-Taba' (the trailing, what follows) refers to what follows an action — its consequence, its trail, or its aftermath. In Quran 2:170, Allah warns: 'We have been commanded to disbelieve in what our forefathers followed.' The taba' here refers to the religious traditions inherited from ancestors. In Surah al-Baqarah 2:170, the disbelievers say: 'Indeed we found our fathers following a religion.' This illustrates the unthinking following of ancestral traditions. The Quran distinguishes between following with insight (al-iqtida) and blind following (al-taqlid).
shades.hadith_ar: لَا يُؤْمِنُ أَحَدُكُمْ حَتَّى يَكُونَ الْهَوَى تَبَعًا لِمَا جِئْتُ بِهِ
shades.hadith_en: None of you believes until his desires follow what I have brought

shades.name_ar: الِاتِّبَاعُ - الْمُوَافَقَةُ عَلَى الطَّرِيقِ بِعِلْمٍ وَبَصِيرَةٍ
shades.explanation: Ittiba' (the following of truth) is distinguished from mere taba'. Ittiba' implies conscious agreement and following of guidance with knowledge and insight. In Quran 3:20, Allah commands: 'Say [to them]: Follow [ittabi'u] what Allah has revealed.' Ittiba' in Sufism is one of the highest stations — it is following the Prophet in his outer and inner states. Al-Qushayri distinguishes between ittiba' (to follow) and iqtida (to imitate). The hadith states: 'Whoever holds fast to my sunnah in a time of corruption will have the reward of a hundred martyrs.' Ittiba' is therefore the way of preservation and revival.
shades.hadith_ar: مَنْ تَمَسَّكَ بِسُنَّتِي عِنْدَ فَسَادِ أُمَّتِي فَلَهُ أَجْرُ مِائَةِ شَهِيدٍ
shades.hadith_en: Whoever holds fast to my sunnah in a time of corruption of my ummah will have the reward of a hundred martyrs

meaning.en: To inform, tell news. The root denotes the act of reporting significant news.
meaning.ar: النَّبَأُ: الْخَبَرُ، وَهُوَ الْخَبَرُ الَّذِي لَهُ شَأْنٌ

lexical_analysis.ibn_faris: النُّبُوءَةُ: الْإِخْبَارُ بِالْخَبَرِ الْعَظِيمِ. وَالنَّبِيُّ: الْمُنَبَّأُ عَنْهُ
lexical_analysis.al_raghib: النَّبَأُ: الْخَبَرُ ذُو الْخَطَرِ. وَالنَّبِيُّ: الْمُخْبِرُ عَنِ اللَّهِ تَعَالَى

quran_examples.ar: عَمَّ يَتَسَآءَلُونَ عَنِ ٱلنَّبَإِ ٱلۡعَظِيمِ
quran_examples.en: About what are they asking each other? About the great news
For every tidings there is a fixed place
quran_examples.context: Every news has its time of fulfillment

hadith.ar: كَانَ حَقًّا عَلَيْنَا نَصْرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ
hadith.en: It was due from Us to help the believers

hadith.ar: الْأَنْبِيَاءُ إِخْوَةٌ مِنْ عَلَّاتٍ
hadith.en: The prophets are brothers from different mothers

shades.name_ar: النَّبَأُ - الْخَبَرُ الْعَظِيمُ، الْخَبَرُ ذُو الْخَطَرِ
shades.explanation: an-Naba' (the news, the tidings) in the Quran is a major tidings or news of great significance. Surah an-Naba' (78) is named after this root. The Quran mentions the naba' al-'azim (the great news — 78:2), referring to the news of the Day of Resurrection. Al-Raghib distinguishes naba' from khabar: naba' is significant news with weight and impact. In 6:67, Allah says: 'Every naba' has a fixed place.' The hadith Qudsi states that Allah has 99 Names and whoever enumerates them will enter Paradise — the divine names are the 'great news' for the believers.
shades.hadith_ar: إِنَّ اللَّهَ عِنْدَهُ عِلْمُ السَّاعَةِ وَيُنَزِّلُ الْغَيْثَ وَيَعْلَمُ مَا فِي الْأَرْحَامِ
shades.hadith_en: Indeed Allah has knowledge of the Hour and sends down the rain and knows what is in the wombs

shades.explanation: an-Nabiyy (the prophet) is the human being to whom revelation is sent. The Quran mentions numerous prophets: Adam, Nuh, Ibrahim, Musa, Isa, Muhammad, and many others. Al-Raghib says nubuwwah (prophethood) is derived from naba' because the prophet brings significant news from Allah. The Quran distinguishes between nabi (prophet) and rasul (messenger). The hadith states: 'My example and the example of the prophets before me is like a man who built a house and completed it except for the space of one brick — I am that brick and I am the seal of the prophets.' The nubuwwah brings the divine news to humanity.
shades.hadith_ar: مَثَلِي وَمَثَلُ الْأَنْبِيَاءِ مِنْ قَبْلِي كَمَثَلِ رَجُلٍ بَنَى بَيْتًا فَأَحْسَنَهُ إِلَّا مَوْضِعَ لَبِنَةٍ
shades.hadith_en: My example and the example of the prophets before me is like a man who built a house and beautified it except for the place of one brick

shades.name_en: an-Naba' al-Azim - The Great News of Resurrection
shades.explanation: an-Naba' al-Azim (the great news) is mentioned in 78:2 as the central theme of Surah al-Naba': 'About what are they asking each other? About the great news.' The Quran places this news — the news of the Day of Resurrection, the Gathering, the Reckoning, and the final destiny — as the most significant event in existence. Classical exegetes call it the 'great news' because it concerns all of humanity, all of jinn, and all of creation. The hadith states: 'The standing before Allah on the Day of Resurrection — the sweat will reach up to the ears of the people.' This naba' al-'azim is what the prophets were sent to deliver.
shades.hadith_ar: عَنِ السَّاعَةِ مَا الَّتِي يَقُومُ فِيهَا النَّاسُ مِنْ قُبُورِهِمْ
shades.hadith_en: About the Hour, when will the people rise from their graves

shades.explanation: Yunabbi'u (to inform, to reveal) is the verb form used by Allah to describe His action of revealing news to the prophets. In 3:179, Allah says: 'Allah would not leave the believers in that state in which you are, until He separates the evil from the good.' Yunabbi' in the Quran is also used for revelation: 'We will tell them [yunabbi'uhum] of their deeds' (3:178), 'Then We will tell them [sa-nunabbi'uhum] of what they did' (5:14, 9:94, 9:105, 22:70, 24:24, 31:23, 33:8, 39:7, 41:22, 47:27, 53:38, 58:7, 64:7, 99:7, 100:9). The hadith states: 'Allah does not impose on a soul any burden beyond its capacity.' This naba' is the divine communication that completes the religion.
shades.hadith_ar: لَا يُكَلِّفُ اللَّهُ نَفْسًا إِلَّا وُسْعَهَا
shades.hadith_en: Allah does not burden a soul beyond its capacity

meaning.en: To help, give victory. The root denotes the act of supporting and overcoming.
meaning.ar: النَّصْرُ: الْإِعَانَةُ عَلَى الْعَدُوِّ، وَالْفَوْزُ عَلَيْهِ

lexical_analysis.ibn_faris: النُّونُ وَالصَّادُ وَالرَّاءُ: نَصَرَهُ يَنْصُرُهُ إِذَا أَعَانَهُ
lexical_analysis.al_raghib: النَّصْرُ: الْإِعَانَةُ عَلَى الْعَدُوِّ. وَالنَّصِيرُ: الْمُعِينُ

quran_examples.ar: إِذَا جَآءَ نَصۡرُ ٱللَّهِ وَٱلۡفَتۡحُ
quran_examples.en: When the help of Allah comes and the victory

quran_examples.ar: إِن تَنصُرُواْ ٱللَّهَ يَنصُرۡكُمۡ وَيُثَبِّتۡ أَقۡدَامَكُمۡ
quran_examples.en: If you aid Allah, He will aid you and firm your feet
quran_examples.context: The promise of victory to the believers

hadith.ar: لَا تَقُصَّ رُؤْيَاكَ عَلَى إِخْوَتِكَ فَيَكِيدُوا لَكَ كَيۡدًا
hadith.en: Do not relate your vision to your brothers lest they plot against you

hadith.ar: إِذَا جَاءَ نَصْرُ اللَّهِ وَالْفَتْحُ، فَسَبِّحْ بِحَمْدِ رَبِّكَ وَاسْتَغْفِرْهُ إِنَّهُ كَانَ تَوَّابًا
hadith.en: When the help of Allah and the victory come, glorify the praise of your Lord and seek His forgiveness

shades.explanation: an-Nasr (the help, the victory) in the Quran is one of the most frequent divine acts. Allah is an-Nasir (the Helper) — He helps His allies (awliya') and gives victory to His messengers. Surah an-Nasr (110) is named after this root. The Quran mentions Allah's promise of victory: 'If you aid Allah, He will aid you' (47:7). The hadith Qudsi states: 'Whoever shows enmity to a friend of Mine, I have declared war against him.' Victory (nasr) in the Quran has multiple dimensions: military victory (fath), divine support (ta'yid), and the ultimate triumph of truth over falsehood. The nasr of Allah is certain and arrives at His appointed time.
shades.hadith_ar: مَنْ عَادَى لِي وَلِيًّا فَقَدْ آذَنْتُهُ بِالْحَرْبِ
shades.hadith_en: Whoever shows enmity to a friend of Mine, I have declared war against him

shades.explanation: an-Nasir (the Helper) is one of the divine Names. The Quran describes Allah as 'the best of helpers' (3:150, 8:40, 22:40). Al-Nasir is the One who helps His servants against their enemies, both external and internal. The hadith states: 'The believer is from Allah like a man who seizes the forelock of his horse — it pulls him and he pulls it.' The believer trusts in an-Nasir even when human helpers fail. The Quran warns: 'If Allah should aid you, no one can overcome you; but if He should forsake you, who is there that can aid you after Him?' (3:160). The believer's reliance is on an-Nasir alone.
shades.hadith_ar: إِنْ يَنصُرْكُمُ اللَّهُ فَلَا غَالِبَ لَكُمْ
shades.hadith_en: If Allah should aid you, no one can overcome you

shades.name_ar: الْمَنْصُورُ - الَّذِي نَصَرَهُ اللَّهُ عَلَى الْأَعْدَاءِ
shades.explanation: al-Mansur (the victorious one) in the Quran refers to the one whom Allah has given victory. In 3:39, the angel Gabriel says to Zakariyya: 'I am the messenger of your Lord to announce to you [the birth of] a purified boy [Yahya].' The Quran says: 'And they were, as they fought, victoriously aided [mansurin]' (61:14). al-Mansur is one who has both divine support and human agency working in concert. The hadith states: 'A group from my ummah will continue to be victorious over the truth.' The ta'ifa mansura (the victorious group) is a famous concept — a community that upholds truth until the Day of Resurrection.
shades.hadith_ar: لَا تَزَالُ طَائِفَةٌ مِنْ أُمَّتِي ظَاهِرِينَ عَلَى الْحَقِّ
shades.hadith_en: A group from my ummah will continue to be victorious over the truth

shades.name_ar: الْفَتْحُ - فَتْحُ الْبَلَدِ، الْحُكْمُ، النَّصْرُ الْبَيِّنُ
shades.explanation: Fath (the opening, the conquest) is closely related to nasr in meaning. Fath is the clear, decisive victory — the opening of a country or the decision of a matter. In 48:1, Allah says: 'Indeed We have given you a clear conquest [fath-an mubinan]' — referring to the Treaty of Hudaybiyya which was a hidden victory. Fath in the Quran includes: military conquest (fath al-bilad), decisive judgment (fath al-hukm), opening of the heart (fath al-qalb), and the opening of the gates of mercy. The hadith states: 'The conquest of Constantinople will indeed take place.' The fath of Constantinople (1453) was a milestone in Islamic history.
shades.hadith_ar: لَقَدْ صَدَقَ اللَّهُ رَسُولَهُ الرُّؤْيَا بِالْحَقِّ لَتَدْخُلُنَّ الْمَسْجِدَ الْحَرَامَ إِنْ شَاءَ اللَّهُ آمِنِينَ
shades.hadith_en: Allah has fulfilled His Messenger's vision with truth — you will surely enter al-Masjid al-Haram in safety

meaning.en: To decree, measure. The root denotes the act of pre-ordaining and measuring.
meaning.ar: الْقَدْرُ: تَقْدِيرُ الشَّيْءِ وَمِقْدَارُهُ، الْقُدْرَةُ عَلَيْهِ

lexical_analysis.ibn_faris: الْقَافُ وَالدَّالُ وَالرَّاءُ أَصْلٌ صَحِيحٌ يَدُلُّ عَلَى قُوَّةِ الشَّيْءِ
lexical_analysis.al_raghib: الْقَدْرُ: تَقْدِيرُ الْأَشْيَاءِ مِنْ مَبَادِئِهَا. وَالْقَادِرُ: ذُو الْقُدْرَةِ

quran_examples.ar: إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ عَلَىٰ كُلِّ شَىۡءٍۢ قَدِيرٌۢ
quran_examples.en: Indeed Allah is over all things competent

quran_examples.ar: إِنَّا كُلَّ شَىۡءٍ خَلَقۡنَـٰهُ بِقَدَرٍۢ
quran_examples.en: Indeed, all things We created with predestination

hadith.ar: إِنَّ اللَّهَ قَدَّرَ مَقَادِيرَ الْخَلْقِ قَبْلَ أَنْ يَخْلُقَ السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضَ
hadith.en: Allah ordained the measures of creation before He created the heavens and the earth

hadith.ar: كُلُّ شَيْءٍ بِقَدَرٍ حَتَّى الْعَجْزِ وَالْكَيْسِ
hadith.en: Everything is by decree, even incapacity and cleverness

shades.explanation: al-Qadr (the power, the decree) in the Quran is the divine attribute of measuring, ordaining, and bringing things to pass according to a precise plan. Allah is al-Qadir (the All-Powerful), al-Muqtadir (the Determiner), and al-Qahhar (the Subduer). The Quran emphasizes qadr repeatedly: 'Allah has power over all things' (2:20, 2:106, 2:109, 2:148, 2:259, 3:26, 3:165, 3:189, 4:85, 5:17, 5:40, 5:120, 6:17, 8:41, 8:60, 9:39, 10:3, 10:107, 11:4, 13:9, 13:16, 16:77, 17:99, 18:45, 22:6, 22:39, 24:45, 27:9, 29:20, 30:50). The decree of Allah is precise, just, and unalterable.
shades.hadith_ar: الْقَدْرُ الَّذِي قَدَّرَ اللَّهُ عَلَى عِبَادِهِ مِنَ الْمَعَايِشِ
shades.hadith_en: The decree which Allah has ordained for His servants regarding provisions

shades.name_ar: الْقَادِرُ - الَّذِي لَا يُعْجِزُهُ شَيْءٌ، الْمُنْعِمُ بِالْقُدْرَةِ
shades.explanation: al-Qadir (the All-Powerful) is one of the most frequent Names of Allah in the Quran. Al-Qadir is the One who has full power over all things and from whom nothing is impossible. The Quran states: 'Allah is Able to do all things' (qadir 'ala kulli shay'in — repeated many times). The famous Ayat al-Kursi (2:255) describes Allah as 'the Ever-Living, the Sustainer of existence, neither drowsiness overtakes Him nor sleep.' The hadith states: 'Allah has ninety-nine Names, one hundred minus one, and whoever enumerates them will enter Paradise.' al-Qadir is the Source of all power.
shades.hadith_ar: إِنَّ اللَّهَ عَلَىٰ كُلِّ شَيْءٍ قَدِيرٌ
shades.hadith_en: Indeed Allah is Able to do all things

shades.name_en: al-Qada' wa al-Qadar - The Decree and Destiny
shades.name_ar: الْقَضَاءُ وَالْقَدَرُ - تَقْدِيرُ اللَّهِ لِلْأَشْيَاءِ قَبْلَ وُجُودِهَا
shades.explanation: al-Qada' wa al-Qadar (the decree and destiny) refers to Allah's pre-eternal measurement of all things before they come into existence. The hadith on iman states: 'You believe in Allah, His angels, His Books, His Messengers, and the Last Day, and you believe in al-qadar, its good and its bad.' This is the sixth pillar of iman. The Quran says: 'Indeed all things We created with predestination [qadar]' (54:49) and 'No affliction strikes except by permission of Allah' (64:11). The believer accepts qadar with patience and gratitude.
shades.hadith_ar: الْإِسْلَامُ أَنْ تَشْهَدَ أَنْ لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا اللَّهُ وَأَنَّ مُحَمَّدًا رَسُولُ اللَّهِ
shades.hadith_en: Islam is to testify that there is no god but Allah and that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah

shades.name_ar: الْمُقَدَّرُ - مَا قَدَّرَهُ اللَّهُ وَكَتَبَهُ فِي اللَّوْحِ الْمَحْفُوظِ
shades.explanation: al-Muqaddar (the ordained, the decreed) refers to what Allah has preordained in al-Lawh al-Mahfuz (the Preserved Tablet). The hadith Qudsi states: 'Allah ordained [qaddara] the measures of creation fifty thousand years before creating the heavens and the earth.' Everything has its qadar — its time, place, cause, and consequence. The Quran says: 'Indeed, all things We created with predestination' (54:49) and 'Your Lord has created whatever He wills and He chooses' (28:68). al-Muqaddar encompasses rizq (provision), ajal (term), and sa'adah wa shaqa (happiness and misery).
shades.hadith_ar: قَدَّرَ اللَّهُ مَقَادِيرَ الْخَلْقِ قَبْلَ أَنْ يَخْلُقَ السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضَ بِخَمْسِينَ أَلْفَ سَنَةٍ
shades.hadith_en: Allah ordained the measures of creation fifty thousand years before creating the heavens and the earth

meaning.en: To determine, resolve. The root denotes firm intention and resolve.

lexical_analysis.ibn_faris: الْعَيْنُ وَالزَّايُ وَالْمِيمُ: الْعَزْمُ الْجَزْمُ مِنَ الْأُمُورِ
lexical_analysis.al_raghib: الْعَزْمُ: إِرَادَةُ الشَّيْءِ وَتَصْمِيمُ الْعَزِيمَةِ عَلَيْهِ

quran_examples.ar: فَٱصۡبِرۡ كَمَا صَبَرَ أُوْلُواْ ٱلۡعَزۡمِ مِنَ ٱلرُّسُلِ
quran_examples.en: Be patient as those of firm resolve among the messengers were patient
quran_examples.context: The command to be patient like the great prophets

quran_examples.ar: وَكَذَٰلِكَ جَعَلۡنَـٰكُمۡ أُمَّةًۭ وَسَطًۭا لِّتَكُونُوا۟ شُهَدَآءَ عَلَى ٱلنَّاسِ
quran_examples.en: And thus We have made you a middle nation that you will be witnesses over the people
quran_examples.context: The ummah of the middle way

hadith.ar: الْمُؤْمِنُ الْقَوِيُّ خَيْرٌ وَأَحَبُّ إِلَى اللَّهِ مِنَ الْمُؤْمِنِ الضَّعِيفِ
hadith.en: The strong believer is better and more beloved to Allah than the weak believer

hadith.ar: إِذَا أَمَرْتُكُمْ بِأَمْرٍ فَأْتُوا مِنْهُ مَا اسْتَطَعْتُمْ
hadith.en: When I command you with a matter, do of it what you are able

shades.name_ar: الْعَزْمُ - الْقَصْدُ الْجَزْمُ، التَّصْمِيمُ عَلَى الْأَمْرِ
shades.explanation: al-'Azm (the determination, the firmness) in the Quran is one of the most important qualities of the prophets and the righteous. The phrase ulu al-'azm (the possessors of firm resolve) refers to the greatest prophets who faced extraordinary trials — Nuh, Ibrahim, Musa, Isa, and Muhammad ﷺ. Verse 46:35 says: 'Be patient as those of determination [ulu al-'azm] were patient.' Al-Ghazali (Ihya') treats 'azm as the highest station after tawakkul — the firm resolve to execute the divine command. The hadith states: 'The strong believer is better and more beloved to Allah than the weak believer, and there is good in both.' 'Azm combines inner strength with outward action.
shades.hadith_ar: اصْبِرْ كَمَا صَبَرَ أُولُو الْعَزْمِ مِنَ الرُّسُلِ
shades.hadith_en: Be patient as the possessors of firm resolve among the messengers were patient

shades.name_ar: الْعَزِيزُ - الَّذِي لَا يُغَالَبُ، ذُو الْقُوَّةِ الْمَطْلَقَةِ
shades.explanation: al-'Aziz (the Mighty, the Almighty) is one of the most frequent Names of Allah in the Quran. Al-'Aziz is the One who is mighty, invincible, and from whom nothing can be taken by force. The Quran describes Allah as 'al-'Aziz al-Hakim' (the Mighty, the Wise) repeatedly. The attribute of 'izza (might) in Allah is the opposite of dhillah (humility) — but only in His essence. For His servants, Allah often chooses 'adhillatan (humility) for them in this world to elevate them in the hereafter. The hadith states: 'Allah says: Whoever shows enmity to a friend of Mine, I have declared war against him.' al-'Aziz protects His friends with His might.
shades.hadith_ar: الْعَزِيزُ الْحَكِيمُ
shades.hadith_en: The Mighty, the Wise

shades.name_ar: الْعِزَّةُ - الْقُوَّةُ الَّتِي لَا تُقْهَرُ، الْمَجْدُ
shades.explanation: al-'Izzah (the might, the glory) is the divine attribute of invincible power. The Quran says: 'And to Allah belongs the 'izzah and to His Messenger and to the believers' (63:8). The believer seeks 'izzah only from Allah — not from wealth, lineage, or worldly power. The famous hadith Qudsi states: 'O My servants, if the first of you and the last of you and the jinn and mankind all stood in one place and asked of Me, I would give to each one what he asked — that would not diminish what is with Me except as a needle dipped in the sea.' 'Izzah is the exclusive attribute of Allah, but He grants it to His sincere servants.
shades.hadith_ar: مَنْ أَرَادَ بِأَنْ يُعِزَّ اللَّهَ الْمُسْلِمِينَ
shades.hadith_en: Whoever intends to honor the Muslims, Allah will honor them

shades.name_en: Ulu al-'Azm - The Possessors of Firm Resolve
shades.name_ar: أُولُو الْعَزْمِ - الرُّسُلُ الْعِظَامُ، أَصْحَابُ الْقَصْدِ الْجَزْمِ
shades.explanation: Ulu al-'Azm (the possessors of firm resolve) are the five greatest prophets in Islamic theology: Nuh, Ibrahim, Musa, Isa, and Muhammad ﷺ. The Quran mentions them in 4:163-165 as 'those whom We favored from the messengers.' They faced trials that would have broken lesser prophets — Nuh faced 950 years of opposition, Ibrahim was thrown into fire, Musa confronted Pharaoh, Isa was rejected by his people, and Muhammad faced the combined opposition of Quraysh and the hypocrites. The hadith states: 'I was sent to the entire jinn and mankind.' The ulu al-'azm are the role models for human determination in the face of adversity.
shades.hadith_ar: أُولَـٰٓئِكَ ٱلَّذِينَ أَنۡعَمَ ٱللَّهُ عَلَيۡهِم مِّنَ ٱلنَّبِيِّـۧنَ
shades.hadith_en: Those are the ones whom Allah has favored among the prophets

meaning.en: To enter. The root denotes the act of going into or entering.
meaning.ar: الدُّخُولُ: وُصُولُ الشَّيْءِ إِلَى الشَّيْءِ مِنْ خَارِجٍ

lexical_analysis.ibn_faris: الدَّالُ وَالْخَاءُ وَاللَّامُ أَصْلٌ وَاحِدٌ يَدُلُّ عَلَى وُصُولِ الشَّيْءِ إِلَى الشَّيْءِ
lexical_analysis.al_raghib: الدُّخُولُ: وُصُولُ الشَّيْءِ إِلَى الشَّيْءِ دَاخِلًا. وَالدَّارُ: الْمَنْزِلُ الَّذِي يُدْخَلُ فِيهِ

quran_examples.ar: وَلَيۡسَ ٱلۡبِرَّ بِأَن تَأۡتُواْ ٱلۡبُيُوتَ مِن ظُهُورِهَا
quran_examples.en: Righteousness is not that you turn your faces toward the east or the west, but [true] righteousness is [in] one who believes in Allah
quran_examples.context: Entering houses from the proper doors

quran_examples.ar: يَـٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ لَا يَسۡخَرۡ قَوۡمٌۭ مِّن قَوۡمٍ
quran_examples.en: O you who have believed, let not a people ridicule [another] people

hadith.ar: لَا يُؤْمِنُ أَحَدُكُمْ حَتَّى يُحِبَّ لِأَخِيهِ مَا يُحِبُّ لِنَفْسِهِ
hadith.en: None of you believes until he loves for his brother what he loves for himself

hadith.ar: مِنْ سَعَادَةِ الْمَرْءِ الْمَسْجِدُ الَّذِي يَجْلِسُ فِيهِ
hadith.en: From a person's happiness is the mosque in which he sits

shades.name_ar: الدُّخُولُ - وُصُولُ الشَّيْءِ إِلَى الشَّيْءِ دَاخِلًا
shades.explanation: ad-Dukhul (the entering) in the Quran is used both literally (entering a place, a house, a town) and metaphorically (entering Islam, entering Paradise, entering Hell). The Quran commands: 'O you who believe, do not enter houses other than your own houses until you have greeted [their inhabitants]' (24:27). The believer enters into Allah's religion with sincerity, and on the Day of Judgment, enters Paradise or Hell. The hadith states: 'None of you believes until I am more beloved to him than his father, his children, and all mankind.' This is the 'entering' into faith — the inner transformation.
shades.hadith_ar: مَنْ كَانَ فِي هَـٰذِهِ ٱلۡأَعۡمَىٰ فَهُوَ فِى ٱلۡأَخِرَةِ أَعۡمَىٰ
shades.hadith_en: Whoever was blind in this world will be blind in the Hereafter

shades.name_ar: الدَّارُ - الْمَنْزِلُ، الْبَيْتُ، الْحَيُّ الَّذِي يُسْكَنُ
shades.explanation: ad-Dar (the home, the abode) in the Quran refers to the dwelling place. There are three abodes: dar al-dunya (the abode of this world), dar al-akhira (the abode of the Hereafter), and dar al-salam (the abode of peace — Paradise). The Quran says: 'And Allah invites to the abode of peace [dar al-salam]' (10:25). The hadith states: 'When you enter a house, mention the Name of Allah.' The daxala (entered) is also used for entering a covenant or a contract. The believer's goal is to enter dar al-salam through faith and good deeds.
shades.hadith_ar: إِذَا دَخَلَ أَحَدُكُمْ بَيْتَهُ فَلْيَذْكُرِ اسْمَ اللَّهِ
shades.hadith_en: When one of you enters his house, let him mention the Name of Allah

shades.explanation: al-Madkhal (the entry point) is the place or means of entry. The Quran uses 'madkhal' for the entry into Egypt (12:67), the entry into a town (2:189), and the entry of the spirit into the body. The famous hadith states: 'Actions are judged by intentions, and every person will get what they intended.' The 'madkhal' in Sufism is the beginning of the spiritual path — the gate through which the seeker enters. Al-Qushayri describes the madkhal of the Sufi path as the moment of tawba (repentance) and resolution to follow the sunnah. Without the correct madkhal, the journey goes astray.
shades.hadith_ar: إِنَّمَا الْأَعْمَالُ بِالنِّيَّاتِ وَإِنَّمَا لِكُلِّ امْرِئٍ مَا نَوَى
shades.hadith_en: Indeed actions are judged by intentions, and each person will have what they intended

shades.name_ar: الْمُدَّخَلُونَ - الَّذِينَ يَدْخُلُونَ فِيمَا لَا يَعْنِيهِمْ
shades.explanation: The Quran uses 'mudakhala' in the sense of meddling or sneaking into matters. In 9:77-78, the hypocrites 'tried to deceive Allah and the believers, but they only deceived themselves' (khada'u Allaha wa khada'ahum — using deception). The mudakhala (meddling) is the act of inserting oneself into affairs one has no business in. The hadith states: 'From the perfection of a person's Islam is his leaving what does not concern him.' The believer avoids the mudakhala of doubt, suspicion, and interference in matters that are not his concern. The Quran praises those who 'turn away from useless talk' (23:3).
shades.hadith_ar: مِنْ حُسْنِ إِسْلَامِ الْمَرْءِ تَرْكُهُ مَا لَا يَعْنِيهِ
shades.hadith_en: From the perfection of a person's Islam is his leaving what does not concern him

meaning.en: To give glad tidings. The root denotes the act of announcing good news.
meaning.ar: الْبُشْرَى: الْخَبَرُ السَّارُّ، إِعْلَامُ الشَّيْءِ السَّارِّ

lexical_analysis.ibn_faris: الْبَاءُ وَالشِّينُ وَالرَّاءُ أَصْلٌ وَاحِدٌ يَدُلُّ عَلَى طَلَاقَةِ الْوَجْهِ
lexical_analysis.al_raghib: الْبُشْرَى: إِعْلَامُ الْإِنْسَانِ بِمَا يَسُرُّهُ. وَالْبَشِيرُ: الْمُعْلِمُ بِهِ

quran_examples.ar: وَبَشِّرِ ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوا۟ وَعَمِلُواْ ٱلصَّـٰلِحَـٰتِ أَنَّ لَهُمۡ جَنَّـٰتٍۢ
quran_examples.en: And give good tidings to those who believe and do righteous deeds that they will have gardens [in Paradise]

quran_examples.ar: مَا يُبَشَّرُونَ وَمَا تُنذِرُونَ قَدْ جَاءَكُمۡ
quran_examples.en: There did come to you [O mankind] glad tidings and warnings

hadith.ar: مَنْ كَانَ يُؤْمِنُ بِاللَّهِ وَالْيَوْمِ الْآخِرِ فَلْيَقُلْ خَيْرًا أَوْ لِيَصْمُتْ
hadith.en: Whoever believes in Allah and the Last Day should speak good or remain silent

hadith.ar: إِنَّ الَّذِينَ سَبَقَتْ لَهُمْ مِنَّا الْحُسْنَىٰ أُولَـٰٓئِكَ عَنْهَا مُبۡعَدُونَ
hadith.en: Indeed those who have preceded from Us in goodness — they will be far removed from it [Hell]

shades.name_ar: الْبُشْرَى - الْخَبَرُ السَّارُّ، الْإِعْلَامُ بِمَا يَسُرُّ
shades.explanation: al-Bushra (the good tidings) in the Quran is the announcement of what brings joy to the heart. The Quran uses it for: (1) glad tidings of Paradise to the believers (2:25, 3:133, 4:18, 9:38, 10:64), (2) glad tidings of mercy from Allah (2:64, 3:126), (3) glad tidings of victory (27:13, 31:7, 37:101), (4) glad tidings of prophethood (2:89, 4:165), and (5) glad tidings of Paradise at the moment of death (41:30). al-Raghib says bushra is news that brings joy, in contrast to nu'ra or inzar (warning). The hadith states: 'Whoever believes in Allah and the Last Day, let him speak good or remain silent.' Bushra is the joyful announcement.
shades.hadith_ar: وَبَشِّرِ الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا أَنَّ لَهُمْ قَدَمَ صِدْقٍ عِنْدَ رَبِّهِمْ
shades.hadith_en: And give good tidings to those who believe that they have a sure footing with their Lord

shades.name_en: al-Mubashshirun - The Bearers of Good Tidings
shades.explanation: al-Mubashshirun (the bearers of good tidings) in the Quran are the angels and prophets who announce glad tidings. The Quran describes the prophets as 'mubashshirun wa mundhirun' (bearers of glad tidings and warners — 2:213, 5:48, 6:48, 11:2, 13:7, 17:15, 18:56, 25:56, 33:45, 34:28, 35:24, 39:71). Each prophet fulfills two functions: giving glad tidings to the obedient, warning the disobedient. The hadith Qudsi states: 'My servant has drawn near to Me through voluntary acts until I love him. And when I love him, I become his hearing with which he hears, his sight with which he sees.' The mubashshirun are the messengers of divine love.
shades.hadith_ar: وَمَا نُرۡسِلُ ٱلۡمُرۡسَلِينَ إِلَّا مُبَشِّرِينَ وَمُنذِرِينَ
shades.hadith_en: We do not send the messengers except as bearers of good tidings and warners
