shades.explanation: Yubashshiru (to give glad tidings) is the verb form used by Allah in the Quran. Allah 'gives glad tidings' to His servants of various rewards: 'Allah gives glad tidings [yubashshiru] to those who believe and do righteous deeds that they will have gardens [in Paradise]' (2:25). The glad tidings are conditioned upon faith and righteous deeds. The hadith states: 'A man once heard a voice in the clouds saying: Water your garden.' The hadith Qudsi states: 'Whoever shows enmity to a friend of Mine, I have declared war against him.' The 'bishaara' (glad tidings) come to those who establish a deep connection with Allah.
shades.hadith_ar: مَنْ عَادَى لِي وَلِيًّا فَقَدْ آذَنْتُهُ بِالْحَرْبِ
shades.hadith_en: Whoever shows enmity to a friend of Mine, I have declared war against him

shades.name_en: Bashir - The Herald of Good Tidings
shades.name_ar: الْبَشِيرُ - الَّذِي يُبَشِّرُ، حَامِلُ الْخَبَرِ السَّارِّ
shades.explanation: al-Bashir (the herald of good tidings) is mentioned in the Quran as one of the names of the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ (2:119, 3:80, 7:188, 10:2, 11:2, 13:38, 17:77, 18:110, 25:56, 27:2, 33:1, 34:28, 35:24, 41:6, 48:8, 61:6). The Prophet is al-Bashir al-Mundhir (the bearer of glad tidings and the warner). The hadith states: 'The Messenger of Allah is the seal of the prophets. There will be no prophet after him.' The Prophet's role is twofold: bashara (glad tidings) for those who obey, and indhar (warning) for those who disobey. The Quran gives both functions together as the full manifestation of prophethood.
shades.hadith_ar: مَثَلُ الَّذِي خَلَقَ السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضَ بِالْحَقِّ
shades.hadith_en: He is the One who created the heavens and the earth in truth

meaning.en: To provide, give sustenance. The root denotes the act of giving provision.
meaning.ar: الرِّزْقُ: مَا يُسْتَعْمَلُ لِبَقَاءِ الْإِنْسَانِ وَحَيَاتِهِ

lexical_analysis.ibn_faris: الرَّاءُ وَالزَّايُ وَالْقَافُ أَصْلٌ وَاحِدٌ يَدُلُّ عَلَى إِعْطَاءِ الشَّيْءِ
lexical_analysis.al_raghib: الرِّزْقُ: مَا يَنْفَعُ الْإِنْسَانَ أَوِ الْحَيَوَانَ. وَالرَّزَّاقُ: الَّذِي يُعْطِيهِ

quran_examples.ar: وَمَن يَتَوَكَّلۡ عَلَى ٱللَّهِ فَهُوَ حَسۡبُهُۥٓ
quran_examples.en: And whoever relies upon Allah — then He is sufficient for him
quran_examples.context: The reliance on Allah for provision

quran_examples.ar: وَمَا مِن دَآبَّةٍۢ فِى ٱلۡأَرۡضِ وَلَا طَـٰٓئِرٍۢ يَطِيرُ بِجَنَاحَيۡهِ إِلَّآ أُمَمٌ أَمۡثَالُكُم
quran_examples.en: And there is no creature on [or within] the earth or bird that flies with its wings except [that they are] communities like you

hadith.ar: لَوْ أَنَّكُمْ تَتَوَكَّلُونَ عَلَى اللَّهِ حَقَّ تَوَكُّلِهِ لَرَزَقَكُمْ كَمَا يَرْزُقُ الطَّيْرَ
hadith.en: If you were to rely upon Allah with true reliance, He would provide for you as He provides for the birds

hadith.ar: كَانَ رَزْقُ عَلِيٍّ قَصِيرًا
hadith.en: Ali's provision was short

shades.explanation: ar-Rizq (the provision) in the Quran is everything that benefits the servant — material or spiritual. Rizq includes: sustenance in this world (food, drink, wealth), sustenance in the grave (barzakh), and sustenance in the Hereafter (Paradise). Allah is ar-Razzaq (the Provider) — One of His Names. The Quran says: 'And whoever fears Allah, He will provide for him a way out [makhraja]' (65:2-3) and 'And whoever relies upon Allah — then He is sufficient for him' (65:3). The hadith states: 'Were you to rely upon Allah with true reliance, He would provide for you as He provides for the birds — they go out hungry in the morning and return full in the evening.' Rizq is pre-ordained and arrives at its appointed time.
shades.hadith_ar: لَوْ أَنَّكُمْ تَتَوَكَّلُونَ عَلَى اللَّهِ حَقَّ تَوَكُّلِهِ لَرَزَقَكُمْ كَمَا يَرْزُقُ الطَّيْرَ
shades.hadith_en: If you were to rely upon Allah with true reliance, He would provide for you as He provides for the birds

shades.name_ar: الرَّزَّاقُ - كَثِيرُ الرِّزْقِ، الَّذِي يَرْزُقُ الْخَلْقَ
shades.explanation: ar-Razzaq (the Provider) is one of the most beloved Names of Allah. ar-Razzaq is the One who provides for all of His creation — humans, jinn, animals, even the smallest creatures. The famous hadith of the Prophet at Jannah (heaven) describes 99 Names of Allah, but does not mention al-Rahman and al-Rahim because these are linked to creation itself. The 'rizq' of Allah is divided in pre-eternity. Some scholars distinguish between rizq 'aam (general provision — for all creation) and rizq 'khaas (special provision — for the believers). The Quran says: 'There is no creature on [or within] the earth or bird that flies with its wings except [that they are] communities like you' (6:38). All are provided for by ar-Razzaq.
shades.hadith_ar: إِنَّ اللَّهَ هُوَ الرَّزَّاقُ ذُو الْقُوَّةِ الْمَتِينُ
shades.hadith_en: Indeed Allah is the Provider, the possessor of strength, the firm

shades.name_ar: الرِّزْقُ الْحَلَالُ - مَا يَجُوزُ أَكْلُهُ وَتَمَلُّكُهُ شَرْعًا
shades.explanation: ar-Rizq al-Halal (the lawful provision) is what is permitted to consume and own according to Islamic law. The Quran forbids the 'rizaq al-haram' (unlawful provision) and commands seeking the 'khayr' (good) of what Allah has provided. The hadith states: 'O people, Allah is Good and only accepts what is good.' al-Halal is critical — many Muslims lose barakah in their rizq because they engage in haram. The Quran says: 'Eat from the good things We have provided for you and do not commit transgression on the earth' (2:60). al-Ghazali in Ihya' discusses the rizq halal as essential for the validity of worship — haram rizq invalidates du'a and frustrates good deeds.
shades.hadith_ar: أَيُّهَا النَّاسُ كُلُوا مِمَّا فِي الْأَرْضِ حَلَالًا طَيِّبًا
shades.hadith_en: O mankind, eat from whatever is on the earth [that is] lawful and good

shades.explanation: Tarziq (to provide sustenance) is one of Allah's continuous acts. The Quran says: 'Allah extends provision for whom He wills and restricts it' (13:26, 17:30, 29:62, 30:37, 34:36, 39:52). The believer seeks rizq through halal means and trusts Allah for the outcome. The hadith states: 'Strange is the affair of the believer — all of it is good for him.' The believer knows that tarziq is in Allah's hands and therefore is content with whatever comes. al-Qushayri treats the 'rida bi ar-rizq' (contentment with provision) as one of the high stations of Sufism — accepting Allah's decree with the heart.
shades.hadith_ar: وَمَا مِن دَآبَّةٍۢ فِى ٱلۡأَرۡضِ إِلَّا عَلَى ٱللَّهِ رِزۡقُهَا
shades.hadith_en: And there is no creature on [or within] the earth or bird that flies with its wings except that they are communities like you

meaning.en: To be at hand. The root denotes the hand or that which is in proximity.

lexical_analysis.ibn_faris: الْيَاءُ وَالدَّالُ أَصْلٌ وَاحِدٌ يَدُلُّ عَلَى قُوَّةٍ
lexical_analysis.al_raghib: الْيَدُ: عُضْوُ الْإِنْسَانِ الَّذِي يَبْطِشُ بِهِ

quran_examples.ar: بَلْ يَدَاهُ مَبۡسُوطَتَانِ
quran_examples.en: Rather, both His hands are extended
quran_examples.context: The divine attribute of the hands

quran_examples.ar: إِنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ يُبَايِعُونَكَ إِنَّمَا يُبَايِعُونَ ٱللَّهَ
quran_examples.en: Indeed, those who pledge allegiance to you, they are actually pledging allegiance to Allah
quran_examples.context: The pledge of allegiance under the tree

hadith.ar: الْيَدُ الْعُلْيَا خَيْرٌ مِنَ الْيَدِ السُّفْلَى
hadith.en: The upper hand is better than the lower hand

hadith.ar: مَا مَلَأَ يَدَ اللَّهِ مِنْ صَدَقَةٍ
hadith.en: Nothing decreases the Hand of Allah from giving

shades.name_ar: الْيَدُ - عُضْوُ الْإِنْسَانِ الَّذِي يَبْطِشُ بِهِ
shades.explanation: al-Yad (the hand) in the Quran has multiple meanings: (1) the literal hand of a human or animal, (2) the hand of Allah - one of the most discussed divine attributes, (3) metaphorical for power, dominion, or control, (4) the hand of a covenant or oath. The Quran says: 'The hand of Allah is over their hands' (48:10) - referring to the covenant of allegiance. The hadith states: 'The believer's hand is more generous than Allah's' - meaning Allah's giving does not decrease. al-Ash'ari and Maturidi differ on the interpretation of yad Allah: Mu'tazila say it means power, Sunnis affirm the hand as an attribute without tashbih.
shades.hadith_ar: يَدُ اللَّهِ فَوْقَ أَيْدِيهِمْ
shades.hadith_en: The hand of Allah is over their hands

shades.name_en: Yadu Allah - The Hand of Allah
shades.name_ar: يَدُ اللَّهِ - صِفَةُ اللَّهِ الَّتِي أَثْبَتَهَا لِنَفْسِهِ
shades.explanation: Yadu Allah (the Hand of Allah) is one of the divine attributes affirmed by Ahl al-Sunnah. The Quran says: 'Both His hands are outstretched' (5:64), 'The hand of Allah is over their hands' (48:10), 'And He created with His hands' (38:75 - referring to Adam). Ahl al-Sunnah affirm yad as an attribute of Allah without asking how (bi la kayfa) and without likening to creation (la tashbih). The hadith states: 'Allah's Hand is full, never diminished by spending.' Some scholars hold two hands (both right), others multiple hands. The Quran's emphasis on yad is to assert divine power, generosity, and creative agency.
shades.hadith_ar: كِتَابُ اللَّهِ حَدِيثٌ وَالنَّبِيُّ حَدِيثٌ حَيٌّ
shades.hadith_en: The Book of Allah is alive and the Prophet is alive

shades.name_ar: الْيَدُ الْعُلْيَا - الْيَدُ الْمُعْطِيَةُ، يَدُ السَّخَاءِ
shades.explanation: al-Yad al-'Ulya (the upper hand) refers to the hand that gives, not the hand that receives. The hadith states: 'The upper hand is better than the lower hand: the upper hand is the one that gives, and the lower hand is the one that receives.' The Quran mentions this concept in 17:29: 'And do not make your hand [chained] to your neck [out of greed] nor extend it [too far] and become bankrupt.' Generosity is the upper hand, miserliness is the lower hand. al-Ghazali in Ihya' discusses the balance between generosity (is'ar) and prudence (ihtiyat).
shades.hadith_ar: الْيَدُ الْعُلْيَا خَيْرٌ مِنَ الْيَدِ السُّفْلَى، وَالْيَدُ الْعُلْيَا هِيَ الْمُنْفِقَةُ
shades.hadith_en: The upper hand is better than the lower hand; the upper hand is the one that gives

shades.name_en: Tayad - To Aid by the Hand
shades.explanation: Tayad (to aid by the hand) is the verbal noun form of ydy, meaning to help, support, or back someone. The Quran says: 'And We gave him [Ibrahim] Isaac and Jacob - all [of them] We guided' (6:84), and 'And We gave him [Yusuf] strength [ayyadah]' (12:21). Tayad in the Quran is Allah's support of His prophets and allies - He strengthens them, makes them firm, and gives them power. The hadith states: 'The strong believer is better and more beloved to Allah than the weak believer.' The tayad of Allah is not limited to physical strength - it includes spiritual firmness, prophetic wisdom, and the support of angels.
shades.hadith_ar: وَاذْكُرُوا إِذْ أَنتُمْ قَلِيلٌ مُّسْتَضْعَفُونَ فِي الْأَرْضِ
shades.hadith_en: And remember when you were few and oppressed on the earth

meaning.en: To be common, general. The root denotes generality or paternal unclehood.

lexical_analysis.ibn_faris: الْعَيْنُ وَالْمِيمُ أَصْلٌ يَدُلُّ عَلَى اشْتِرَاكٍ
lexical_analysis.al_raghib: الْعَمُّ: أَخُو الْأَبِ. وَالْعُمُومُ: الشَّامِلُ لِجَمِيعِ الْأَفْرَادِ

quran_examples.ar: قُل لَّآ أَسۡـَٔلُكُمۡ عَلَيۡهِ أَجۡرًا إِلَّا ٱلۡمَوَدَّةَ فِى ٱلۡقُرۡبَىٰ
quran_examples.en: Say: I do not ask of you for it any reward except the love of the near relatives
quran_examples.context: The reward of the prophetic message

quran_examples.ar: وَٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُوٓاْ أَعۡمَـٰلُهُمۡ كَسَرَابٍۢ
quran_examples.en: And those who disbelieve - their deeds are like a mirage

hadith.ar: لَا يُؤْمِنُ أَحَدُكُمْ حَتَّى يُحِبَّ لِأَخِيهِ مَا يُحِبُّ لِنَفْسِهِ
hadith.en: None of you believes until he loves for his brother what he loves for himself

hadith.ar: مَنْ أَحَبَّ أَنْ يُبْسَطَ لَهُ فِي رِزْقِهِ فَلْيَصِلْ رَحِمَهُ
hadith.en: Whoever wishes that his provision be expanded, let him maintain ties of kinship

shades.name_ar: الْعَمُّ - أَخُو الْأَبِ، الْمُشْتَرَكُ بَيْنَ اثْنَيْنِ
shades.explanation: al-'Amm (the paternal uncle) is the brother of one's father. The maternal uncle is khawwal or khal. The paternal uncle is 'amm. The 'amm is a special relative in Arab culture and in Islamic law - he is from the asabah (paternal male relatives). The Quran says: 'Say: I do not ask of you any reward for it, except love of the near relatives [al-qurba]' (42:23). Some commentators say al-qurba here means the family of the Prophet. The hadith states: 'Maintain ties of kinship, and Allah will extend your provision.' The 'amm is one of the closest male relatives of the paternal line.
shades.hadith_ar: حَقُّ الْوَلَدِ عَلَى الْوَالِدِ أَنْ يُحَسِّنَ اسْمَهُ وَأَدَبَهُ
shades.hadith_en: The right of a child over his father is that he gives him a good name and good manners

shades.name_ar: الْعُمُومُ - الْعَامُّ، الشَّامِلُ لِأَكْثَرَ مِنْ وَاحِدٍ
shades.explanation: al-'Umum (the common, the general) is the opposite of al-khusus (the specific). The Quran uses umum and aamm for general versus specific. The Quranic commands are usually aamm (general) unless context narrows them. The hadith states: 'Allah has ninety-nine Names, one hundred minus one, and whoever enumerates them will enter Paradise.' The umumiyyah of a ruling means it applies generally to all cases, not specifically to one individual.
shades.hadith_ar: الْأَمْرُ يَقَعُ عَامًّا وَيُرَادُ بِهِ الْخَاصُّ
shades.hadith_en: The command comes generally but is intended specifically

shades.explanation: al-'Amama (the paternal unclehood) is the kinship of the paternal uncle. In pre-Islamic Arabia, the 'amm was one of the most powerful family ties. In Islamic law, the 'amm has specific rights: (1) He is among those who inherit in certain cases with asabah, (2) He has the right to be treated with kindness (birr), (3) His bad treatment is a sin. The hadith states: 'The 'amm is from the people of Allah and from the people of the house.'
shades.hadith_ar: مَنْ أَحَبَّ أَنْ يُبْسَطَ لَهُ فِي رِزْقِهِ فَلْيَصِلْ رَحِمَهُ
shades.hadith_en: Whoever wishes that his provision be expanded, let him maintain ties of kinship

shades.explanation: al-'Awwam (the common people, the public) refers to ordinary people. The Quran uses amma (active participle) for those who follow. The hadith states: 'You will follow the ways of those before you, handspan by handspan, cubit by cubit.' The 'awwam are the ordinary believers - they follow the scholars, the pious, and the religious authorities. al-Ghazali in Ihya' describes the 'awwam as those whose practice is at the level of the outer sharia, while the khawass (elite) have inner realization as well.
shades.hadith_ar: كُلُّكُمْ رَاعٍ وَكُلُّكُمْ مَسْئُولٌ عَنْ رَعِيَّتِهِ
shades.hadith_en: Each of you is a shepherd, and each of you is responsible for his flock

meaning.en: To be mighty, honored. The root denotes might and honor.
meaning.ar: الْعِزُّ: الشَّدِيدُ الْقَهَّارُ، الَّذِي لَا يُضَامُّ

lexical_analysis.ibn_faris: الْعَيْنُ وَالزَّايُ أَصْلٌ يَدُلُّ عَلَى مَنَعَةٍ وَقُوَّةٍ
lexical_analysis.al_raghib: الْعِزُّ: الْمَنَعَةُ وَالْقُوَّةُ. وَالْعَزِيزُ: الَّذِي لَا يُغَالَبُ

quran_examples.ar: لِلَّهِ ٱلۡعِزَّةُ وَلِرَسُولِهِۦ وَلِلۡمُؤۡمِنِينَ
quran_examples.en: To Allah belongs the might, and to His Messenger and to the believers

quran_examples.ar: ٱلَّذِينَ يَتَرَبَّصُونَ بِكُمۡ فَإِن كَانَ لَكُمۡ فَتۡحٌۭ مِّنَ ٱللَّهِ
quran_examples.en: Those who wait for [the worst] for you - if you have a victory from Allah, they say: Were we not with you?
quran_examples.context: The hypocrites seeking might from both sides

hadith.ar: مَنْ أَحَبَّ الْعِزَّ بِالْبَاطِلِ أَذَلَّهُ اللَّهُ
hadith.en: Whoever seeks honor through falsehood, Allah will humiliate him

hadith.ar: إِنَّ اللَّهَ يُحِبُّ الْمُتَوَاضِعِينَ
hadith.en: Indeed Allah loves the humble
hadith.source: Sahih Muslim (Commentary on al-Mu'izz and al-Mudhill)

shades.explanation: al-'Izz (the might, the glory) in the Quran is one of the most sublime divine attributes. The 'izz belongs to Allah alone (63:8): 'And to Allah belongs the 'izz and to His Messenger and to the believers.' al-'Izz is the attribute of invincible power, sovereignty, and honor. The Quran repeatedly contrasts 'izz Allah with 'izz al-taghut (the might of the false deities — 4:139, 38:82). The believer seeks 'izz only from Allah. The hadith states: 'Whoever seeks the 'izz through wealth, Allah will humiliate him.' The 'izz of the believer lies in taqwa, not in wealth or status.
shades.hadith_ar: وَلِلَّهِ ٱلۡعِزَّةُ وَلِرَسُولِهِۦ وَلِلۡمُؤۡمِنِينَ
shades.hadith_en: And to Allah belongs the 'izz and to His Messenger and to the believers

shades.name_ar: الْعَزِيزُ - الَّذِي لَا يُغَالَبُ، الَّذِي يَقْهَرُ الْجَبَابِرَةَ
shades.explanation: al-'Aziz (the Almighty, the Mighty) is one of the most frequent divine Names in the Quran. The Quran describes Allah as 'al-'Aziz al-Hakim' (the Mighty, the Wise) repeatedly. al-'Aziz is the One who is mighty, invincible, and from whom nothing can be taken by force. The famous Ayat al-Kursi (2:255) describes Allah as 'al-Hayy al-Qayyum'. al-'Aziz is paired with al-Hakim (the Wise) and al-Ghafur (the Forgiving). The hadith Qudsi states: 'Whoever shows enmity to a friend of Mine, I have declared war against him.' al-'Aziz protects His friends with His might.
shades.hadith_ar: الْعَزِيزُ الْحَكِيمُ
shades.hadith_en: The Mighty, the Wise

shades.name_ar: الْمُعِزُّ - الَّذِي يُعِزُّ مَنْ يَشَاءُ مِنْ عِبَادِهِ
shades.explanation: al-Mu'izz (the Honorer) is one of the divine Names mentioned in the famous hadith of the Names: 'Allah says: I am as My servant thinks of Me, and I am with him when he remembers Me.' al-Mu'izz is the One who honors His servants — granting them dignity, status, and 'izza (might). The hadith on the 99 Names includes al-Mu'izz (the Honorer) and al-Mudhill (the Humiliator). Allah honors the mu'minun (believers) and humiliates the kuffar (disbelievers) according to His wisdom. The Quran says: 'Allah does not change the condition of a people until they change what is in themselves' (13:11). The believer seeks honor from al-Mu'izz.
shades.hadith_ar: مَنْ عَادَى لِي وَلِيًّا فَقَدْ آذَنْتُهُ بِالْحَرْبِ
shades.hadith_en: Whoever shows enmity to a friend of Mine, I have declared war against him

shades.name_ar: الْمُذِلُّ - الَّذِي يُذِلُّ مَنْ يَشَاءُ مِنَ الْكَافِرِينَ
shades.explanation: al-Mudhill (the Humiliator) is paired with al-Mu'izz in the hadith of the 99 Names. al-Mudhill is the One who humiliates — bringing disgrace to the arrogant and the disbelievers. The Quran says: 'So Allah will humiliate them [yu'dhilluhum] and give them a painful punishment' (9:18). The 'izza (might) in the worldly sense often leads to 'adhillah (humility) in the hereafter. Pharaoh, Nimrod, and Abu Jahl were the most 'aziz in this world but the most mudhill on the Day of Judgment. The hadith states: 'If you knew what I know, you would laugh little and weep much.'
shades.hadith_ar: فَسَيَحۡشُرُهُمۡ عَلَىٰ هَـٰذِهِ ٱلۡحَقِّ عَلَىٰ كُلِّ خَبِيرٍ
shades.hadith_en: He will surely gather them on the Day of Resurrection over the truth, over all things, the All-Aware

meaning.en: To return, refuse. The root denotes the act of returning or refusing.
meaning.ar: الْأَبُ: الرَّجُلُ الَّذِي يُنْسَبُ إِلَيْهِ الْوَلَدُ، وَالْإِبَاءُ: الرَّفْضُ

lexical_analysis.ibn_faris: الْهَمْزَةُ وَالْبَاءُ أَصْلٌ يَدُلُّ عَلَى الْأَبِوَّةِ أَوِ الرُّجُوعِ
lexical_analysis.al_raghib: الْأَبُ: أَصْلُ الْمَوْلُودِ. وَأَبَى: رَفَضَ

quran_examples.ar: أَمۡ كُنتُمۡ شُهَدَآءَ إِذۡ حَضَرَ يَعۡقُوبَ ٱلۡمَوۡتُ
quran_examples.en: Or were you witnesses when death approached Yaqub, when he said to his sons: What will you worship after me?

quran_examples.ar: وَوَصَّيۡنَا ٱلۡإِنسَـٰنَ بِوَٰلِدَيۡهِ إِحۡسَـٰنًا
quran_examples.en: And We have enjoined upon man [care] for his parents with kindness

hadith.ar: الْجَنَّةُ تَحْتَ أَقْدَامِ الْأُمَّهَاتِ
hadith.en: Paradise lies beneath the feet of mothers

hadith.ar: كُونُوا رَبِّيِّينَ بِمَا كُنتُمۡ تُعَلِّمُونَ ٱلۡكِتَـٰبَ
hadith.en: Be learned men of religion (rabbaniyyin) because of what you used to teach the Book

shades.name_ar: الْأَبُ - الْأَبُ، الرَّجُلُ الَّذِي يُنْسَبُ إِلَيْهِ الْوَلَدُ
shades.explanation: al-Ab (the father) in the Quran is the male parent. The Quran says: 'We have enjoined upon man [care] for his parents. His mother carried him in hardship and bore him in hardship' (46:15). The Quran repeatedly commands birr al-walidayn (kindness to parents). The ab (father) is also used metaphorically for: the founder of a nation (Abu Bakr, Abu Hurayra), the head of a community (Yaqub is called 'ab al-asbab' — father of the tribes, 2:133), and the originator of an idea (the 'ab of a thing). The hadith states: 'The garden of Jannah is beneath the feet of mothers.' The 'ab is the protector, sustainer, and guide of the child.
shades.hadith_ar: وَوَصَّيۡنَا ٱلۡإِنسَـٰنَ بِوَٰلِدَيۡهِ إِحۡسَـٰنًا
shades.hadith_en: And We have enjoined upon man [care] for his parents with kindness

shades.name_ar: الْأُبُوَّةُ - صِفَةُ الْأَبِ، نِسْبَةُ الْوَلَدِ إِلَيْهِ
shades.explanation: al-Ubuwwah (fatherhood) in the Quran and hadith is one of the most sacred relationships. Allah describes Himself metaphorically as having 'Ubudiyyah (servanthood) for Him, and He gives man the great status of ubuwwah (fatherhood). The Prophet ﷺ said: 'None of you truly believes until he loves for his brother what he loves for himself.' The father's rights include: (1) being honored in old age, (2) obedience in good matters, (3) kindness and respect, (4) financial support if needed. The Quran mentions the 'ab with tenderness in 2:133 (Yaqub as 'ab al-asbab), 19:42-49 (Ibrahim's father Azar), and 21:52-66 (the broken idols).
shades.hadith_ar: كُونُوا رَبِّيِّينَ بِمَا كُنتُمۡ تُعَلِّمُونَ ٱلۡكِتَـٰبَ
shades.hadith_en: Be [rabbaniyyin] because of what you used to teach the Book

shades.name_en: Abu al-Asbab - Father of the Tribes
shades.name_ar: أَبُو ٱلۡأَسۡبَاطِ - الْجَدُّ الْأَعْلَى، أَبُو الْقَبَائِلِ
shades.explanation: Abu al-Asbab (the father of the tribes) is the title given to Prophet Yaqub (Jacob) in 2:133: 'And Yaqub, when he was dying: O my sons, worship Allah, this religion of your father.' Yaqub had twelve sons who became the twelve tribes of Israel. The 'ab in this title refers to the originator or founder of a lineage. The Quran uses 'ab' in this sense for Abraham (father of all prophets), Adam (father of mankind), and Yaqub (father of the tribes). The hadith states: 'Adam and Moses argued, and Adam defeated Moses in argument.' The 'abu al-asbab' represents the gathering of nations under one ancestor.
shades.hadith_ar: قَالَ يَـٰبَنِىَّ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ ٱصۡطَفَىٰ لَكُمُ ٱلدِّينَ فَلَا تَمُوتُنَّ إِلَّا وَأَنتُم مُّسۡلِمُونَ
shades.hadith_en: He said: O my sons, Allah has chosen for you this religion, so do not die except while you are Muslims

shades.name_en: Walid al-Ab - The Son of the Father, The Ancestor
shades.name_ar: وَلَدُ الْأَبِ - الذُّرِّيَّةُ الْمُتَسَلِّلَةُ مِنَ الْأَبِ
shades.explanation: Walid al-Ab (the son of the father) refers to the descendants who trace through the paternal line. The Quran mentions the walad (son) of Adam (5:27-32 — the story of the two sons of Adam), and the walad of Ibrahim (15:53, 37:113 — Isma'il and Ishaq). The walad of the ab is the fruit of his efforts and lineage. The Quran warns against 'attributing children to other than their fathers' — a great sin. The hadith states: 'The child belongs to the marriage (al-firash) and the fornicator gets the stone.' This hadith establishes the firm principle of paternal attribution in Islamic law.
shades.hadith_ar: ٱلۡوَلَدُ لِلۡفِرَاشِ وَلِلۡعَاهِرِ ٱلۡحَجَرُ
shades.hadith_en: The child belongs to the marriage bed, and the fornicator gets the stone

meaning.en: To spend, be spent. The root denotes spending or tunneling (hypocrisy).
meaning.ar: النَّفَقُ: مَا يُنْفِقُهُ الْإِنْسَانُ مِنْ مَالِهِ

lexical_analysis.ibn_faris: النُّونُ وَالْفَاءُ وَالْقَافُ أَصْلٌ يَدُلُّ عَلَى خُرُوجٍ
lexical_analysis.al_raghib: النِّفَاقُ: إِظْهَارُ الْإِسْلَامِ وَإِخْفَاءُ الْكُفْرِ

quran_examples.ar: إِذَا جَآءَكَ ٱلۡمُنَـٰفِقُونَ قَالُواْ نَشۡهَدُ إِنَّكَ لَرَسُولُ ٱللَّهِ
quran_examples.en: When the hypocrites come to you, they say: We testify that you are indeed the Messenger of Allah

quran_examples.ar: يَـٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوٓاْ إِنَّ كَثِيرًۭا مِّنَ ٱلۡأَحۡبَارِ وَٱلرُّهۡبَانِ
quran_examples.en: O you who have believed, indeed many of the scholars and monks devour the wealth of people unjustly

hadith.ar: مَنۡ كُنَّ فِيهِ كَانَ مُنَافِقًا خَالِصًا
hadith.en: Whoever has these four is a pure hypocrite

hadith.ar: الدِّينَارُ تَقَحَّمَ الدِّينَارَ سَبْعَمِائَةِ ضِعْفٍ
hadith.en: A dirham can outstrip a dirham by seven hundred times

shades.name_ar: النَّفَقُ - مَا يُنْفِقُهُ الْإِنْسَانُ مِنْ مَالِهِ
shades.explanation: an-Nafaq (the expense, the spending) in the Quran refers to what a person spends from his wealth for good causes. The Quran emphasizes nafaqat as one of the key characteristics of the believers: 'Those who spend [yunfiqun] in ease and hardship' (3:134). Nafaq includes: zakat (obligatory charity), sadaqa (voluntary charity), and infaq fi sabil Allah (spending in the way of Allah). The Quran says: 'Whatever you spend, He will replace it; He is the best of providers' (34:39). The hadith states: 'A dirham can outstrip another dirham by 700 times.' The nafaqat are the wings of taqwa.
shades.hadith_ar: مَثَلُ الَّذِينَ يُنۡفِقُونَ أَمۡوَٰلَهُمۡ فِى سَبِيلِ ٱللَّهِ كَمَثَلِ حَبَّةٍ
shades.hadith_en: The example of those who spend their wealth in the way of Allah is like a seed [of grain]

shades.explanation: an-Nifaq (the hypocrisy) is the act of showing Islam outwardly while hiding disbelief inwardly. The munafiqun (hypocrites) are mentioned extensively in the Quran, particularly in Surah al-Munafiqun (63), Surah al-Tawbah (9), and other passages. The nifaq has two types: i'tiqadi (of belief) and 'amali (of action). The hadith states: 'Three are the signs of the hypocrite: when he speaks he lies, when he promises he breaks, and when he is entrusted he betrays.' The Prophet said there are four signs of perfect hypocrisy. The munafiqun are the most dangerous to the ummah.
shades.hadith_ar: أَرَبَعٌ مَنۡ كُنَّ فِيهِ كَانَ مُنَافِقًا خَالِصًا
shades.hadith_en: Four (characteristics) are signs of a pure hypocrite

shades.name_ar: الْمُنَافِقُونَ - الَّذِينَ يُظۡهِرُونَ ٱلۡإِسۡلَامَ وَيُبۡطِنُونَ ٱلۡكُفۡرَ
shades.explanation: al-Munafiqun (the hypocrites) in the Quran are a distinct group in Madinah who outwardly professed Islam while secretly plotting against the Muslim community. Their leader was Abdullah ibn Ubayy ibn Salul. The Quran describes them in detail: 'When the hypocrites come to you, they say: We testify that you are indeed the Messenger of Allah' (63:1). They took oaths to deceive Allah, but Allah knows their deceit. The hadith states: 'Whoever fights for a cause not clear, but supports a group, he has died a death of jahiliyyah.' The munafiqun were warned of the lowest level of Hellfire.
shades.hadith_ar: إِنَّ ٱلۡمُنَـٰفِقِينَ فِى ٱلدَّرۡكِ ٱلۡأَسۡفَلِ مِنَ ٱلنَّارِ
shades.hadith_en: Indeed the hypocrites will be in the lowest depths of the Fire

shades.name_ar: النَّفَقَاتُ - جَمْعُ النَّفَقَةِ، مَا يُنْفَقُ فِي الْوُجُوهِ الشَّرْعِيَّةِ
shades.explanation: an-Nafaqat (the expenditures, the charities) in the Quran refers to the plural of nafaqa - the various forms of spending. The Quran mentions nafaqat in the context of jihad, family support, and charity. The Quran says: 'And let not those who are stingy with what Allah has given them of His bounty think it is good for them - rather it is bad for them' (3:180). The nafaqat al-husna (good expenditures) refers to spending in righteous causes. The hadith states: 'The best sadaqa is that given when one is in need of it, and one gives it from what is excess for him.' al-Ghazali in Ihya' distinguishes between the levels of sadaqa and nafaqat.
shades.hadith_ar: مَنۡ يُوقَ شُحَّ نَفۡسِهِۦ فَأُوْلَـٰٓئِكَ هُمُ ٱلۡمُفۡلِحُونَ
shades.hadith_en: And whoever is saved from the stinginess of his soul - those are the successful ones

meaning.en: To eat, consume. The root denotes the act of eating or consuming.

lexical_analysis.ibn_faris: الْهَمْزَةُ وَالْكَافُ وَاللَّامُ أَصْلٌ يَدُلُّ عَلَى أَخْذِ الطَّعَامِ
lexical_analysis.al_raghib: الْأَكْلُ: تَنَاوُلُ الطَّعَامِ. وَأَكَلَ: اسْتَهْلَكَ

quran_examples.ar: كُلُواْ وَٱشۡرَبُواْ مِن رِّزۡقِ ٱللَّهِ
quran_examples.en: Eat and drink from the provision of Allah

quran_examples.ar: يَـٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلنَّاسُ كُلُواْ مِمَّا فِى ٱلۡأَرۡضِ حَلَـٰلًۭا طَيِّبًۭا
quran_examples.en: O mankind, eat from whatever is on the earth [that is] lawful and good

hadith.ar: سَمِّ اللَّهَ وَكُلْ بِيَمِينِكَ وَكُلْ مِمَّا يَلِيكَ
hadith.en: Mention the Name of Allah, eat with your right hand, and eat from what is nearest to you

hadith.ar: الْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ الَّذِي أَطْعَمَنَا وَسَقَانَا وَجَعَلَنَا مُسْلِمِينَ
hadith.en: Praise be to Allah who fed us and gave us drink and made us Muslims

shades.explanation: al-Akl (the eating) in the Quran is the act of taking food and drink. The Quran mentions akl repeatedly: 'Eat and drink from the provision of Allah' (2:60). The 'akl' has both literal and metaphorical meanings: (1) eating food, (2) consuming property unjustly (akl al-amwal bil-batil), (3) eating fire (eating the fruit of Zaqqum in Hellfire). The Quran warns against akl al-riba (eating usury), akl al-mal bil-batil (consuming property unjustly), and akl al-yatama (eating the wealth of orphans). The halal akl (lawful eating) is essential for the validity of worship.
shades.hadith_ar: كُلُوا مِن طَيِّبَاتِ مَا رَزَقۡنَاكُمۡ
shades.hadith_en: Eat from the good things We have provided for you

shades.explanation: at-Ta'am (the food) in the Quran refers to that which is eaten. The Quran mentions various foods: the manna and quails given to the Children of Israel (2:57, 7:160, 20:80), the food that the birds brought to the family of Iram and Iram's daughters (3:37), and the food of Paradise (2:25, 13:35, 47:15). The food of this world is limited, but the food of Paradise is endless. The hadith states: 'The most beloved of foods to Allah is that which is touched by many hands (shared meal).' The ta'am of the believer is blessed.
shades.hadith_ar: يَـٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ كُلُواْ مِن طَيِّبَاتِ مَا رَزَقۡنَـٰكُمۡ
shades.hadith_en: O you who have believed, eat from the good things We have provided for you

shades.name_en: al-Aklu wa al-Shirb - The Eating and Drinking
shades.explanation: al-Aklu wa al-Shirb (the eating and drinking) is mentioned together in the Quran to describe the activities of this world. The Quran says: 'Say: Who has forbidden the adornment of Allah which He has produced for His servants and the good [lawful] things of provision?' (7:32). Eating and drinking are blessings from Allah, not in themselves sinful. The Quran praises those who eat and drink halal in gratitude to Allah. The hadith states: 'O Allah, bless for us what You have provided us and protect us from the punishment of fire. We say Bismillah before eating and Alhamdulillah after eating.'
shades.hadith_ar: بِسْمِ اللَّهِ فَإِنَّهُ لَا يَضَعُ الشَّيْطَانُ يَدَهُ فِي طَعَامٍ
shades.hadith_en: Mention the Name of Allah; the shaytan will not put his hand in it

shades.name_ar: الْآكِلُ - الَّذِي يَأْكُلُ، الصِّفَةُ الْمُتَعَلِّقَةُ بِالطَّعَامِ
shades.explanation: al-Akil (the eater) is the active participle of akl. The Quran uses al-akil in various contexts: 'They would never have killed him [the calf of Samiri] because they are eaters of it' (20:92 - referring to the calf's body that the Children of Israel worshipped being dead and unable to eat). The 'akil' in the Quran also refers to the consuming of wealth unjustly - akil al-amwal - which is a major sin. The hadith states: 'Whoever consumes the wealth of an orphan unjustly will eat fire into his belly on the Day of Judgment.' The legitimate 'akil' is the one who eats from halal means with gratitude to Allah.
shades.hadith_ar: إِنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ يَأۡكُلُونَ أَمۡوَٰلَ ٱلۡيَتَـٰمَىٰ ظُلۡمًا إِنَّمَا يَأۡكُلُونَ فِى بُطُونِهِمۡ نَارًۭا
shades.hadith_en: Indeed those who consume the wealth of orphans unjustly are only consuming into their bellies fire

meaning.en: To do, make. The root denotes the act of doing or performing.

lexical_analysis.ibn_faris: الْفَاءُ وَالْعَيْنُ وَاللَّامُ أَصْلٌ يَدُلُّ عَلَى حُدُوثِ الشَّيْءِ
lexical_analysis.al_raghib: الْفِعْلُ: الْعَمَلُ الْمَصْدُورُ عَنِ الْفَاعِلِ

quran_examples.ar: وَمَا تَفۡعَلُواْ مِنۡ خَيۡرٍۢ يَعۡلَمۡهُ ٱللَّهُ
quran_examples.en: And whatever you do of good - indeed Allah is Knowing of it

quran_examples.ar: إِنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ وَعَمِلُواْ ٱلصَّـٰلِحَـٰتِ أُوْلَـٰٓئِكَ هُمۡ خَيۡرُ ٱلۡبَرِيَّةِ
quran_examples.en: Indeed, those who have believed and done righteous deeds - they are the best of creatures
quran_examples.context: The reward of the believers who act

hadith.ar: إِنَّمَا ٱلۡأَعۡمَـٰلُ بِٱلنِّيَّـٰتِ
hadith.en: Indeed deeds are judged by intentions

hadith.ar: كُلُّكُمۡ رَاعٍ وَكُلُّكُمۡ مَسۡئُولٌ عَنۡ رَعِيَّتِهِ
hadith.en: Each of you is a shepherd, and each of you is responsible for his flock

shades.name_ar: الْفِعْلُ - الْعَمَلُ، مَا يَصْدُرُ عَنِ الْإِنْسَانِ
shades.explanation: al-Fi'l (the deed, the action) in the Quran refers to what is done. al-Fi'l is one of the three parts of Arabic grammar (ism, fi'l, harf). The Quran says: 'And whatever you do of good deeds [min khayyatin] - indeed Allah is Knowing of it' (2:197). The af'al (plural of fi'l) are the deeds of the servant — both outward and inward. al-Ghazali in Ihya' divides the af'al into: af'al al-qalb (actions of the heart — intentions, beliefs), af'al al-lisan (actions of the tongue — dhikr, dua), and af'al al-jawarih (actions of the limbs — salah, sadaqa). All are judged by their intentions.
shades.hadith_ar: مَنۡ عَمِلَ صَـٰلِحًۭا فَلِنَفۡسِهِۦ
shades.hadith_en: Whoever does a righteous deed - it is for [the benefit of] his soul

shades.explanation: al-'Amal (the deed, the work) in the Quran is closely related to al-fi'l. The Quran pairs iman (faith) with 'amal (deed): 'Those who believe and do righteous deeds [wa 'amilu al-salihati]' (2:25). The 'amal in the Quran has three levels: (1) al-'amal al-salih (the righteous deed — worthy of reward), (2) al-'amal al-sayyi' (the evil deed — worthy of punishment), (3) al-'amal al-mubtil (the void deed — done without sincerity). The famous hadith states: 'Indeed actions are judged by intentions, and each person will have what he intended.' Without niyyah (intention), the 'amal is empty.
shades.hadith_ar: إِنَّمَا ٱلۡأَعۡمَـٰلُ بِٱلنِّيَّـٰتِ
shades.hadith_en: Indeed deeds are judged by intentions

shades.name_en: al-Mu'min al-'Amil - The Believer Who Acts
shades.name_ar: الْمُؤْمِنُ الْعَامِلُ - الَّذِي يَجْمَعُ بَيْنَ الْإِيمَانِ وَالْعَمَلِ
shades.explanation: al-Mu'min al-'Amil (the believer who acts) is the one who combines iman (faith) with 'amal (deed). The Quran praises such people: 'Indeed, those who have believed and done righteous deeds - they are the best of creatures' (98:7). The mu'min al-'amil does not suffice with mere belief — he acts upon his belief, following the sunnah and the guidance. The hadith states: 'The strong believer is better and more beloved to Allah than the weak believer, and there is good in both.' Strength in 'amal comes from sincerity, knowledge, and consistent action. al-Ghazali emphasizes that 'amal without 'ilm is blind, and 'ilm without 'amal is void.
shades.hadith_ar: إِنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ وَعَمِلُواْ ٱلصَّـٰلِحَـٰتِ أُوْلَـٰٓئِكَ هُمۡ خَيۡرُ ٱلۡبَرِيَّةِ
shades.hadith_en: Indeed, those who have believed and done righteous deeds - they are the best of creatures

shades.name_ar: الْفَاعِلُ - مَنْ يَصْدُرُ مِنْهُ الْفِعْلُ، الصَّانِعُ
shades.explanation: al-Fa'il (the doer, the actor) in the Quran refers to the one who performs an action. The Quran distinguishes between al-fa'il al-mukhtar (the free agent who acts by choice) and the one compelled. The believer is a fa'il — a free agent — and is accountable for his actions. The hadith states: 'Each of you is a shepherd and each of you is responsible for his flock.' The fa'il in the Quran has levels: (1) al-fa'il al-kamil (the complete doer — one whose deeds are perfect in form and intention), (2) al-fa'il al-naqis (the deficient doer — one whose deeds lack sincerity). The Quran praises the muhsinin (those who do ihsan - excellent deeds).
shades.hadith_ar: كُلُّكُمۡ رَاعٍ وَكُلُّكُمۡ مَسۡئُولٌ عَنۡ رَعِيَّتِهِ
shades.hadith_en: Each of you is a shepherd, and each of you is responsible for his flock

meaning.en: To transgress, attack. The root denotes aggression or enmity.
meaning.ar: الْعَدُوُّ: الضِّدُّ، وَالْعُدْوَانُ: التَّجَاوُزُ عَنِ الْحَدِّ

lexical_analysis.ibn_faris: الْعَيْنُ وَالدَّالُ وَالْوَاوُ أَصْلٌ يَدُلُّ عَلَى مُجَاوَزَةٍ
lexical_analysis.al_raghib: الْعَدُوُّ: الْخَصْمُ. وَالْعُدْوَانُ: التَّجَاوُزُ عَنِ الْحَقِّ

quran_examples.ar: وَلَا تَعۡتَدُوٓاْ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ لَا يُحِبُّ ٱلۡمُعۡتَدِينَ
quran_examples.en: But do not commit excess, for Allah does not love those who commit excess

quran_examples.ar: وَإِن تَصۡبِرُواْ وَتَتَّقُواْ لَا يَضُرُّكُمۡ كَيۡدُهُمۡ شَيۡـًٔا
quran_examples.en: And if you are patient and fear Allah, their plot will not harm you at all

hadith.ar: إِيَّاكُمْ وَالظُّلْمَ فَإِنَّ الظُّلْمَ ظُلُمَاتٌ يَوْمَ الْقِيَامَةِ
hadith.en: Beware of zulm (injustice), for it will be darkness on the Day of Resurrection

hadith.ar: أَنَّ اللَّهَ لَمْ يَجْعَلْ لِصَاحِبِ الْحَدِّ سَبِيلًا
hadith.en: Indeed Allah has not made a way for the one who transgresses the limits

shades.explanation: al-'Aduw (the enemy) in the Quran is one who opposes and opposes by hostility. The Quran says: 'And if you are patient and fear Allah, their plot will not harm you at all' (3:120). The 'aduw in the Quran has three meanings: (1) the human enemy (al-'aduw al-mubin - the open enemy), (2) the devil (al-'aduw al-mujtan - the hidden enemy — Satan), (3) the inner enemy (the nafs al-ammarah). The believer must befriend the awliya' (allies) of Allah and avoid the a'da' (enemies) of Allah. The hadith states: 'The strong believer is better and more beloved to Allah than the weak believer.' The believer is firm against his enemies, both internal and external.
shades.hadith_ar: يَـٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ لَا تَتَّخِذُواْ عَدُوِّى وَعَدُوَّكُمۡ أَوۡلِيَآءَ
shades.hadith_en: O you who have believed, do not take My enemies and your enemies as allies

shades.explanation: al-'Adawani (the transgression) in the Quran refers to exceeding the limits. The Quran says: 'And do not commit aggression on the earth' (2:60). The 'adwan is one of the major sins - exceeding the bounds set by Allah. The Quran warns: 'Do not exceed the limits, for those who exceed the limits of Allah are unjust oppressors' (65:1). al-Ghazali in Ihya' describes the 'adwan as the act of going beyond the limits of sharia. The hadith states: 'Do not transgress against Allah's limits and do not disobey Him in His commands.' The 'adwan is punished by Allah with the most severe punishment.
shades.hadith_ar: وَلَا تَعۡتَدُوٓاْ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ لَا يُحِبُّ ٱلۡمُعۡتَدِينَ
shades.hadith_en: But do not commit excess, for Allah does not love those who commit excess

shades.name_ar: يَعْدُو - يَتَجَاوَزُ الْحَدَّ، يُسِرِعُ فِي الشَّيْءِ
shades.explanation: Ya'du (to attack, to transgress) is the verb form of the root. The Quran says: 'You will surely be tested in your possessions and in yourselves' (3:186). The ya'du (transgression) is tested in many forms: by wealth, by family, by one's own body. The Quran says: 'Indeed we belong to Allah, and to Him we shall return' (2:156). This is the response to ya'du - sabr (patience) and istirja' (return to Allah). The hadith states: 'Whoever is tested with ya'du (transgression) and is patient, Allah will compensate him with the best of rewards.'
shades.hadith_ar: كُلُّ ابْنِ آدَمَ خَطَّاءٌ وَخَيْرُ الْخَطَّائِينَ التَّوَّابُونَ
shades.hadith_en: Every son of Adam sins, and the best of sinners are those who repent

shades.explanation: al-Mu'tadi (the transgressor) in the Quran refers to one who exceeds the bounds set by Allah. The Quran says: 'These are the limits of Allah, so do not approach them' (2:187). The mu'tadi transgresses by going beyond the legitimate boundaries. The hadith states: 'The mu'tadi is the one who goes beyond the limits.' al-Mu'tadi is not only the one who transgresses against others, but also the one who transgresses against himself (al-mu'tadi 'ala nafsihi). The Quran praises the muqtasid (the moderate) and warns against the mu'tadi. The famous hadith states: 'The most beloved deeds to Allah are the most consistent, even if small.'
shades.hadith_ar: وَٱعۡلَمُوٓاْ أَنَّ ٱللَّهَ يَعۡلَمُ مَا فِىٓ أَنفُسِكُمۡ فَٱحۡذَرُوهُ
shades.hadith_en: And know that Allah knows what is within yourselves, so beware of Him

meaning.en: To be in excess, to grace. The root denotes grace, virtue, and excess.

lexical_analysis.ibn_faris: الْفَاءُ وَالضَّادُ وَاللَّامُ أَصْلٌ يَدُلُّ عَلَى زِيَادَةٍ
lexical_analysis.al_raghib: الْفَضْلُ: الْإِحْسَانُ الزَّائِدُ عَلَى الْوَاجِبِ

quran_examples.ar: وَلَوۡ أَنَّ أَهۡلَ ٱلۡقُرَىٰٓ ءَامَنُواْ وَٱتَّقَوۡاْ لَفَتَحۡنَا عَلَيۡهِم بَرَكَـٰتٍۢ مِّنَ ٱلسَّمَآءِ
quran_examples.en: And if the people of the towns had believed and feared Allah, We would have opened upon them blessings from the heaven
quran_examples.context: The opening of blessings through faith

quran_examples.ar: وَعَدَ ٱللَّهُ ٱلۡمُؤۡمِنِينَ وَٱلۡمُؤۡمِنَـٰتِ جَنَّـٰتٍۢ تَجۡرِى مِن تَحۡتِهَا ٱلۡأَنۡهَـٰرُ
quran_examples.en: Allah has promised the believing men and believing women gardens below which rivers flow

hadith.ar: مَنْ لَمْ يَشْكُرِ الْقَلِيلَ لَمْ يَشْكُرِ الْكَثِيرَ
hadith.en: Whoever does not thank the few will not thank the much

hadith.ar: لَوْ أَنَّ لِلَّهِ عَمَلًا لَكَانَ الْمَوْتُ
hadith.en: If Allah had a deed, it would be death

shades.explanation: al-Fadl (the virtue, the grace) in the Quran is one of the most repeated divine attributes. The Quran says: 'If you do good, you do good for yourselves' (17:7). al-Fadl is the additional grace of Allah beyond what is strictly due. Allah is al-Fadil (the Most Gracious), al-Mufaddil (the Distinguisher of grace), and al-Munazzil (the Revealer of grace). The Quran says: 'If Allah should aid you, no one can overcome you' (3:160). The fadl of Allah is the source of all goodness.
shades.hadith_ar: وَٱللَّهُ ذُو ٱلۡفَضۡلِ ٱلۡعَظِيمِ
shades.hadith_en: And Allah is the possessor of great bounty

shades.name_ar: الْمُفَضِّلُ - الَّذِي يُفَضِّلُ بَيْنَ الْعِبَادِ بِفَضْلِهِ
shades.explanation: al-Mufaddil (the Distinguisher of Grace) is the One who distinguishes His servants with various grades of grace. The Quran says: 'And We have caused some of them to excel others in ranks' (43:32). The fadl of Allah is not equal for everyone - some people are given more, others less. The Quran warns against riya' (showing off) with the fadl. The hadith states: 'Whoever Allah wishes good for, He afflicts him with trials.' The trials are part of the fadl of Allah - they raise the ranks of the believers.
shades.hadith_ar: وَلَا تَلُمُزُوٓاْ أَنفُسَكُمۡ وَلَا تَنَابَزُواْ بِٱلۡأَلۡقَـٰبِ
shades.hadith_en: Do not insult one another and do not call each other by [offensive] nicknames

shades.name_ar: الْفَضْلُ الْكُبْرَى - فَضْلُ اللَّهِ فِي الدُّنْيَا وَالْآخِرَةِ
shades.explanation: al-Fadl al-Kubra (the greatest grace) refers to the most magnificent divine grace - Paradise. The Quran says: 'And whoever is saved from the stinginess of his soul - those are the successful ones' (64:16). The fadl of Allah is not limited to this world - the Hereafter is the greater fadl. The Quran says: 'But the good pleasure of Allah is greater [fadl Allah akbar]' (9:72). al-Ghazali in Ihya' discusses the multiple levels of fadl - the outward fadl of rizq and the inner fadl of iman and yaqin.
shades.hadith_ar: وَمَا عِندَ ٱللَّهِ خَيۡرٌۭ وَأَبۡقَىٰ
shades.hadith_en: But what is with Allah is better and more lasting

shades.name_ar: التَّفَضُّلُ - إِنْعَامُ اللَّهِ عَلَى عِبَادِهِ بِمَا يَفُوقُ الْحَقَّ
shades.explanation: Tafaddul (to bestow grace) in the Quran refers to Allah's act of grace. The Quran says: 'Whoever desires the harvest of the Hereafter - We will increase for him in his harvest' (42:20). The tafaddul of Allah is beyond measure. The Quran says: 'And if you should count the favors of Allah, you could not enumerate them' (14:34, 16:18). The hadith states: 'Whoever has been given the fadl, let him show it to those who do not have it.' The believer shares the fadl of Allah with others.
shades.hadith_ar: إِن تُبۡدُواْ ٱلصَّدَقَـٰتِ فَنِعِمَّا هِىَ
shades.hadith_en: If you disclose your charitable expenditures, they are good

meaning.en: To return. The root denotes the act of coming back or returning.

lexical_analysis.ibn_faris: الرَّاءُ وَالْجِيمُ وَالْعَيْنُ أَصْلٌ يَدُلُّ عَلَى الْعَوْدِ
lexical_analysis.al_raghib: الرُّجُوعُ: الْعَوْدُ إِلَى الْأَصْلِ. وَالتَّوْبَةُ: الرُّجُوعُ إِلَى اللَّهِ

quran_examples.ar: مَن يُصِبۡتَهُ ٱلۡعَذَابُ فَقَدۡ أُجِرَ ٱلۡمُجۡرِمِينَ
quran_examples.en: Whoever is touched by the punishment - then indeed He has transgressed
quran_examples.context: The return of sins upon the sinner

quran_examples.ar: وَلَا يَتَّخِذِ ٱلۡمُؤۡمِنُونَ ٱلۡكَـٰفِرِينَ أَوۡلِيَآءَ مِن دُونِ ٱلۡمُؤۡمِنِينَ
quran_examples.en: And let not the believers take disbelievers as allies rather than believers

hadith.ar: إِنَّمَا الْأَعْمَالُ بِالنِّيَّاتِ
hadith.en: Indeed deeds are judged by intentions

hadith.ar: إِنَّ اللَّهَ يَقْبَلُ تَوْبَةَ الْعَبْدِ مَا لَمْ يُغَرْغِرْ
hadith.en: Indeed Allah accepts the repentance of the servant as long as the soul has not reached the throat

shades.explanation: ar-Ruju' (the return) in the Quran is one of the most fundamental concepts. The Quran mentions the return of the soul to the body (32:11), the return to Allah on the Day of Judgment (3:28, 8:44), and the return of the believers to Allah in repentance (2:160, 9:104). al-Raghib distinguishes between ruju' (return) and 'awda (repetition). The ruju' of the soul is the most significant - everyone must return to Allah. The hadith states: 'You will return to Allah as you were created - without any deeds.' The ruju' is to the place of original creation.
shades.hadith_ar: كُلُّ نَفۡسٍۢ ذَآئِقَةُ ٱلۡمَوۡتِۖ وَإِنَّمَا تُوَفَّوۡنَ أُجُورَكُمۡ يَوۡمَ ٱلۡقِيَـٰمَةِ
shades.hadith_en: Every soul will taste death, and you will only be given your full compensation on the Day of Resurrection

shades.name_en: al-Awda - The Returning, The Coming Back
shades.explanation: al-'Awda (the returning, the coming back) in the Quran refers to returning to a state or a place. The Quran says: 'And they will find what they did placed before them' (18:49). The 'awda is for the one who comes back to Allah - a beautiful 'awda. The famous hadith states: 'Allah says: O My servant, if you return to Me, I will return to you.' The 'awda of Allah is more perfect than the 'awda of the servant. The Quran says: 'Indeed, He is the One who accepts repentance from His servants' (42:3, 42:25, 42:27). The 'awda is the act of turning back to Allah with remorse.
shades.hadith_ar: إِنَّ اللَّهَ يَقْبَلُ تَوْبَةَ الْعَبْدِ مَا لَمْ يُغَرْغِرْ
shades.hadith_en: Indeed Allah accepts the repentance of the servant as long as the soul has not reached the throat

shades.explanation: at-Taraju' (the mutual returning) refers to two things returning to each other or canceling each other out. In Islamic law, at-taraju' is used in the context of sales, contracts, and reconciliation. The Quran says: 'And if they reconcile, Allah will cause their reconciliation' (4:130). The hadith states: 'Reconciliation between people is better than all prayers and fasting.' al-Qushayri uses at-taraju' to describe the spiritual journey of the seeker - returning to Allah after every station, then returning to the world, and so on until reaching the final maqam (station).
shades.hadith_ar: وَإِن تُصۡلِحُواْ وَتَتَّقُواْ فَإِنَّ ٱللَّهَ كَانَ غَفُورًۭا رَّحِيمًا
shades.hadith_en: But if you correct yourselves and fear Allah - then indeed Allah is Forgiving and Merciful

shades.name_ar: الْمُنِيبُ - الَّذِي رَجَعَ إِلَى اللَّهِ بِالطَّاعَةِ وَالتَّوْبَةِ
shades.explanation: al-Munib (the one who returns to Allah) is one who turns back to Allah in obedience and repentance. The Quran says: 'And give good tidings to those who are turning [to Allah] [al-munibin]' (13:30, 30:13, 39:8, 50:8). al-Munib is the one whose heart is constantly oriented toward Allah. The hadith states: 'Whoever does an evil deed, let him not despair of Allah's mercy.' al-Munib is one of the highest stations - the one whose every action returns to Allah. al-Ghazali in Ihya' describes the munib as one who is constantly in tawba (repentance), never feeling safe from Allah's wrath, never despairing of His mercy.
shades.hadith_ar: إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ يُحِبُّ ٱلتَّوَّـٰبِينَ وَيُحِبُّ ٱلۡمُتَطَهِّرِينَ
shades.hadith_en: Indeed Allah loves those who repent and those who purify themselves

meaning.en: To be safe, secure. The root denotes safety, security, faith, or trust.

lexical_analysis.ibn_faris: الْهَمْزَةُ وَالْمِيمُ وَالنُّونُ أَصْلٌ يَدُلُّ عَلَى الطُّمَأْنِينَةِ
lexical_analysis.al_raghib: الْأَمَانُ: ضِدُّ الْخَوْفِ. وَالْإِيمَانُ: التَّصْدِيقُ الْجَازِمُ

quran_examples.ar: ٱللَّهُ وَلِىُّ ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ يُخۡرِجُهُم مِّنَ ٱلۡظُلُمَـٰتِ إِلَى ٱلنُّورِ
quran_examples.en: Allah is the ally of those who believe; He brings them out of darkness into light
quran_examples.context: Allah as the protector of believers

quran_examples.ar: وَمَن دَخَلَهُۥ كَانَ ءَامِنًۭا
quran_examples.en: And whoever enters it [the Sacred Mosque] is safe
quran_examples.context: The safety of the Sacred Mosque

hadith.ar: الْمُسْلِمُ مَنْ سَلِمَ الْمُسْلِمُونَ مِنْ لِسَانِهِ وَيَدِهِ
hadith.en: The Muslim is the one from whose tongue and hand other Muslims are safe

hadith.ar: الْإِيمَانُ بِضْعٌ وَسَبْعُونَ شُعْبَةً
hadith.en: Faith has seventy-odd branches

shades.explanation: al-Aman (the safety, the security) in the Quran is one of the most precious blessings. The Quran says: 'Whoever enters it [the Sacred Mosque] is safe' (3:97). al-Aman is the opposite of al-khawf (fear). Allah promises al-aman to those who have iman: 'Allah is the ally of those who believe; He brings them out of darkness into light' (2:257). al-Aman is also the state of dar al-islam (the abode of Islam). The hadith states: 'The Muslim is the one from whose tongue and hand other Muslims are safe.' al-Aman is the foundation of society and worship.
shades.hadith_ar: الْمُسْلِمُ مَنْ سَلِمَ الْمُسْلِمُونَ مِنْ لِسَانِهِ وَيَدِهِ
shades.hadith_en: The Muslim is the one from whose tongue and hand other Muslims are safe

shades.explanation: al-Mu'minun (the believers) in the Quran are those who have iman (faith). The Quran describes the mu'minun in detail: 'The believers are only those who believe in Allah and His Messenger and then doubt not but strive with their wealth and their lives in the cause of Allah. It is those who are the truthful' (49:15). The Quran uses different shades of mu'min: (1) al-mu'min al-sadiq (the truthful believer), (2) al-mu'min al-khass (the special believer — those who combine iman and ihsan), (3) al-mu'min al-zall (the sinning believer — who has iman but commits sins). The hadith states: 'No one truly believes until he loves for his brother what he loves for himself.'
shades.hadith_ar: إِنَّمَا ٱلۡمُؤۡمِنُونَ ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ بِٱللَّهِ وَرَسُولِهِۦ
shades.hadith_en: The believers are only those who believe in Allah and His Messenger

shades.explanation: al-Iman (the faith, the belief) in the Quran has three levels: (1) tasdiq al-qalb (confirmation of the heart — inner conviction), (2) iqrar al-lisan (declaration with the tongue), (3) 'amal al-jawarih (action with the limbs). The famous hadith of Jibril defines iman as: 'To believe in Allah, His angels, His Books, His Messengers, and the Last Day, and to believe in al-qadar, its good and its bad.' The Quran says: 'The bedouins say: We have believed. Say: You have not [yet] believed; but say: We have submitted [aslamna], for faith has not yet entered your hearts' (49:14). Iman increases with obedience and decreases with disobedience.
shades.hadith_ar: الْإِيمَانُ بِضْعٌ وَسَبْعُونَ شُعْبَةً فَأَفْضَلُهَا قَوْلُ لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا اللَّهُ وَأَدْنَاهَا إِمَاطَةُ الْأَذَى عَنِ الطَّرِيقِ
shades.hadith_en: Faith has seventy-odd branches; the highest is saying 'there is no god but Allah' and the lowest is removing a harmful object from the road

shades.name_ar: الْأَمِينُ - الَّذِي يُؤْمَنُ عَلَيْهِ، الصَّادِقُ الْمَأْمُونُ
shades.explanation: al-Amin (the trustworthy) is one of the most noble titles. The Quran describes Prophet Muhammad ﷺ as 'al-amin' in the famous verse of Surah al-Qalam (68:4 - 'And indeed, you are of a great moral character'). The amin is the one who is entrusted with secrets, wealth, and responsibilities. The hadith states: 'The Muslim is the one from whose tongue and hand other Muslims are safe, and the muhajir is the one who abandons what Allah has forbidden.' The amin is the one who keeps trusts and is faithful to his covenants. The Prophet Muhammad was known as al-Amin even before prophethood.
shades.hadith_ar: وَإِنَّكَ لَعَلَىٰ خُلُقٍۢ عَظِيمٍۢ
shades.hadith_en: And indeed, you are of a great moral character

meaning.en: To march, be still. The root denotes marching or being still/calm.

lexical_analysis.ibn_faris: الرَّاءُ وَالْكَافُ وَالدَّالُ أَصْلٌ يَدُلُّ عَلَى سُكُونٍ
lexical_analysis.al_raghib: الرُّكُوعُ: الِانْحِنَاءُ لِلتَّعَظِيمِ

quran_examples.ar: وَأَقِيمُواْ ٱلصَّلَوٰةَ وَءَاتُواْ ٱلزَّكَوٰةَ وَٱرۡكَعُواْ مَعَ ٱلرَّـٰكِعِينَ
quran_examples.en: And establish prayer and give zakah and bow with those who bow
quran_examples.context: The command to bow in prayer

quran_examples.ar: وَٱلۡخَيۡلَ وَٱلۡبِغَالَ وَٱلۡحَمِيرَ لِتَرۡكَبُوهَا
quran_examples.en: And He created the horses, mules, and donkeys for you to ride them

hadith.ar: إِنِّي رَأَيْتُ جِبْرِيلَ يَمْشِي فِي أَزِقَّةِ الْمَدِينَةِ
hadith.en: I saw Jibril walking in the streets of Madinah

hadith.ar: مَا أَنْزَلَ اللَّهُ دَاءً إِلَّا أَنْزَلَ لَهُ شِفَاءً
hadith.en: Allah has not sent down any disease without sending down a cure for it

shades.name_ar: الرَّكْدُ - الْمَشْيُ بِسُكُونٍ، السُّكُونُ إِلَى الْأَرْضِ
shades.explanation: ar-Rakd (the marching) in the Quran refers to a slow, dignified walk. The Quran says: 'And when you travel throughout the land, there is no blame upon you for shortening the prayer' (4:101). The rakd in the Quran is used for the marching of the armies, the march of the believers, and the movement of the heavens. The Prophet Muhammad was known for his rakd - his dignified walk. The hadith states: 'I saw Jibril walking in the streets of Madinah.' The rakd is an act of serious purpose - moving with intention toward a goal.
shades.hadith_ar: رَأَيْتُ جِبْرِيلَ يَمْشِي فِي أَزِقَّةِ الْمَدِينَةِ
shades.hadith_en: I saw Jibril walking in the streets of Madinah

shades.name_ar: الرُّكُوعُ - الْخُضُوعُ، الِانْحِنَاءُ لِلَّهِ فِي الصَّلَاةِ
shades.explanation: ar-Ruku' (the bowing down) in the Quran is one of the pillars of salah (prayer). The Quran says: 'Bow with those who bow' (2:43). ar-Ruku' is the act of bowing down before Allah in submission and humility. It is one of the highest acts of physical worship - placing the head below the level of the heart. The hadith states: 'The slave is closest to his Lord when he is in sujud (prostration).' ar-Ruku' precedes sujud in the prayer. The ruku' is a state of absolute humility before the divine.
shades.hadith_ar: يَـٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ ٱرۡكَعُواْ وَٱسۡجُدُوا۟
shades.hadith_en: O you who have believed, bow and prostrate and worship your Lord

shades.name_ar: الرَّاكِبُ - مَنْ يَرْكَبُ الْمَرْكُوبَ، الْمُتَمَتِّعُ بِالْمَرْكَبِ
shades.explanation: ar-Rakib (the rider) in the Quran is the one who rides a mount. The Quran says: 'And He created the horses, mules, and donkeys for you to ride' (16:8). The rakib in the Quran includes: the one who rides a horse, the one who rides a camel, and the one who rides any means of transportation. The hadith states: 'Allah has not created any disease without creating a cure for it.' The rakib in Sufism is the one who is mounted on the spiritual journey - traveling through the stations of the path.
shades.hadith_ar: مَا أَنْزَلَ اللَّهُ دَاءً إِلَّا أَنْزَلَ لَهُ شِفَاءً
shades.hadith_en: Allah has not sent down any disease without sending down a cure for it

shades.explanation: al-Markab (the vessel, the mount) in the Quran refers to that which is ridden. The Quran mentions various markab: horses (khayl), mules (bighal), donkeys (hamir), camels ('ibil), and ships (fulk). The Quran says: 'And among His signs is that He created for you mates from among yourselves, that you may dwell in tranquility with them' (30:21). The markab in Sufism is the means of spiritual travel. al-Qushayri uses markab al-tariq as the means by which the seeker travels to Allah.
shades.hadith_ar: وَٱلۡخَيۡلَ وَٱلۡبِغَالَ وَٱلۡحَمِيرَ لِتَرۡكَبُوهَا
shades.hadith_en: And He created the horses, mules, and donkeys for you to ride them

meaning.en: To form, image. The root denotes the act of giving form or shape.
meaning.ar: الصُّورَةُ: الشَّكْلُ، وَالتَّصْوِيرُ: جَعْلُ الشَّيْءِ عَلَى صُورَةٍ

lexical_analysis.ibn_faris: الصَّادُ وَالْوَاوُ وَالرَّاءُ أَصْلٌ يَدُلُّ عَلَى تَصْوِيرٍ
lexical_analysis.al_raghib: الصُّورَةُ: الشَّكْلُ الَّذِي يَكُونُ عَلَيْهِ الشَّيْءُ

quran_examples.ar: هُوَ ٱللَّهُ ٱلۡخَـٰلِقُ ٱلۡبَارِئُ ٱلۡمُصَوِّرُ
quran_examples.en: He is Allah, the Creator, the Inventor, the Fashioner
quran_examples.context: The three creative attributes of Allah

quran_examples.ar: إِذۡ قَالَ رَبُّكَ لِلۡمَلَـٰٓئِكَةِ إِنِّى خَـٰلِقٌۢ بَشَرًۭا مِّن طِينٍۢ
quran_examples.en: When your Lord said to the angels: I am going to create a human being from clay

hadith.ar: خَلَقَ اللَّهُ آدَمَ عَلَى صُورَتِهِ
hadith.en: Allah created Adam in His own form

hadith.ar: لَا تَسُبُّوا الدَّهْرَ فَإِنَّ اللَّهَ هُوَ الدَّهْرُ
hadith.en: Do not curse time, for Allah is time

shades.name_ar: الصُّورَةُ - الشَّكْلُ، الْهَيْئَةُ الَّتِي يُصَوَّرُ بِهَا الشَّيْءُ
shades.explanation: as-Suwara (the image, the form) in the Quran is mentioned in the context of the creation of Adam: 'I will create a human being from clay and form him' (38:71). as-Suwara is the form that Allah gives to each being. al-Raghib says taswir (imaging) is the act of forming something. The suwara of Allah is perfect - He created the human being in the best of forms. The famous hadith states: 'Allah created Adam in His own form' - this is one of the most discussed hadith in Islamic theology. The form of Adam is the prototype of all human form.
shades.hadith_ar: إِنَّا خَلَقۡنَا ٱلۡإِنسَـٰنَ فِىٓ أَحۡسَنِ تَقۡوِيمٍۢ
shades.hadith_en: We have certainly created the human being in the best of stature

shades.explanation: at-Taswir (the imaging, the forming) in the Quran refers to the act of forming or imaging. The Quran says: 'He is Allah, the Creator, the Inventor, the Fashioner [al-Musawwir]' (59:24). al-Musawwir is one of the Names of Allah - the One who gives form to His creation. The taswir of Allah is the act of giving each being its perfect form. The hadith Qudsi states: 'My servant has drawn near to Me through voluntary acts until I love him.' The form of Adam is unique among creation.
shades.hadith_ar: هُوَ ٱللَّهُ ٱلۡخَـٰلِقُ ٱلۡبَارِئُ ٱلۡمُصَوِّرُ
shades.hadith_en: He is Allah, the Creator, the Inventor, the Fashioner

shades.name_ar: الْمُصَوِّرُ - الَّذِي يُصَوِّرُ الْأَشْيَاءَ عَلَى أَشْكَالِهَا
shades.explanation: al-Musawwir (the Fashioner, the Former) is one of the Names of Allah - the One who gives form to His creation. The Quran says: 'He is Allah, the Creator, the Inventor, the Fashioner' (59:24). al-Musawwir is the One who gives each creature its form, its features, and its function. The hadith states: 'Allah created Adam in His own form.' The Musawwir's work is perfect - He does not create anything in vain. The believer reflects on the suwar (forms) of Allah's creation and draws nearer to Him.
shades.hadith_ar: خَلَقَ آدَمَ عَلَى صُورَتِهِ
shades.hadith_en: Allah created Adam in His own form

shades.explanation: as-Suwar (the forms, the images) in the Quran refers to the multiple forms of Allah's creation. The Quran says: 'And the heaven He constructed and gave it form and made it seven heavens' (79:28). The suwar of the heavens and the earth are infinite in variety. The hadith Qudsi states: 'My servant has drawn near to Me through voluntary acts until I love him. And when I love him, I become his hearing with which he hears.' The believer sees the suwar of Allah's creation with the eyes of the heart.
shades.hadith_ar: ٱلَّذِى خَلَقَ سَبۡعَ سَمَـٰوَٰتٍۢ طِبَاقًۭا
shades.hadith_en: It is He who created seven heavens in layers

meaning.en: To strive, struggle. The root denotes the act of striving or making effort.

lexical_analysis.ibn_faris: الْجِيمُ وَالْهَاءُ وَالدَّالُ أَصْلٌ يَدُلُّ عَلَى مَشَقَّةٍ
lexical_analysis.al_raghib: الْجِهَادُ: الْمُبَالَغَةُ فِي الْجَهْدِ

quran_examples.ar: وَٱلَّذِينَ جَـٰهَدُواْ فِينَا لَنَهۡدِيَنَّهُمۡ سُبُلَنَا
quran_examples.en: And those who strive for Us - We will surely guide them to Our ways
quran_examples.context: The promise of divine guidance for the strivers

quran_examples.ar: لَا يُكَلِّفُ اللَّهُ نَفۡسًا إِلَّا وُسۡعَهَا
quran_examples.en: Allah does not burden a soul beyond its capacity

hadith.ar: الْمُجَاهِدُ مَنْ جَاهَدَ نَفْسَهُ
hadith.en: The mujahid is the one who struggles against his own self

hadith.ar: إِذَا اجْتَهَدَ الْحَاكِمُ فَأَصَابَ فَلَهُ أَجْرَانِ
hadith.en: When the judge exerts effort and reaches the right answer, he gets two rewards

shades.explanation: al-Jihad (the striving, the struggle) in the Quran has multiple dimensions: (1) jihad al-nafs (struggle against the self), (2) jihad al-shaytan (struggle against Satan), (3) jihad al-sayyi'at (struggle against evil deeds), (4) jihad bi al-mal wa al-nafs (struggle with wealth and self - in defense of Islam), (5) jihad al-talab (armed jihad - in defense of the ummah). The Quran says: 'And those who strive [jahadu] for Us - We will surely guide them to Our ways' (29:69). The hadith states: 'The mujahid is the one who strives against his nafs for the sake of Allah.' al-Jihad is the path of the muwahhid (the one who affirms tawhid).
shades.hadith_ar: وَٱلَّذِينَ جَـٰهَدُواْ فِينَا لَنَهۡدِيَنَّهُمۡ سُبُلَنَا
shades.hadith_en: And those who strive for Us - We will surely guide them to Our ways

shades.name_ar: الْجُهْدُ - الطَّاقَةُ، الْمَشَقَّةُ الَّتِي يَحْتَمِلُهَا الْإِنْسَانُ
shades.explanation: al-Juhd (the effort, the capacity) in the Quran refers to one's capacity or effort. The Quran says: 'Allah does not burden a soul beyond its capacity [jus'taha]' (2:286). The juhd is the utmost effort one can make. The hadith states: 'Strive with all your juhd (utmost effort) for the dunya and akhira.' al-Juhd is the maximum effort within one's capacity. The famous hadith Qudsi states: 'My servant has drawn near to Me through voluntary acts until I love him.' The believer exerts his juhd in worship, work, and service.
shades.hadith_ar: لَا يُكَلِّفُ اللَّهُ نَفۡسًا إِلَّا وُسۡعَهَا
shades.hadith_en: Allah does not burden a soul beyond its capacity

shades.name_ar: الْمُجَاهِدُ - مَنْ يُبَالِغُ فِي الْجِهَادِ، الْكَافِحُ
shades.explanation: al-Mujahid (the striver) in the Quran is the one who exerts effort in the way of Allah. The Quran says: 'Indeed, Allah has purchased from the believers their lives and their properties in exchange for Paradise. They fight [yuqatiluna] in the cause of Allah' (9:111). The mujahid is the one who has dedicated his life to the cause of Allah. The hadith states: 'A morning or evening spent in the cause of Allah is better than the world and all that is in it.' The mujahid ranks among the highest in Paradise - the shuhada (martyrs) and the salihin (the righteous).
shades.hadith_ar: مِقْعَدُكَ مِقْعَدُ صِدْقٍ عِندَ مَلِيكٍ مُّقْتَدِرٍ
shades.hadith_en: Your place is a place of truth, with an All-Powerful Sovereign

shades.explanation: al-Ijtihad (the personal effort) is a technical term in Islamic jurisprudence (usul al-fiqh). al-Ijtihad is the maximum intellectual effort a qualified jurist (mujtahid) exerts to derive legal rulings from the sources of sharia. The mujtahid is the one who has reached the level of ijtihad - he can issue independent legal opinions (ijtihad). The Quran says: 'And We did not send before you any messenger or prophet except that when he spoke [talamma], Satan would throw [tumniyy] into his recitation' (22:52). The mujtahid works within the framework of the Quran and Sunnah. al-Ghazali in al-Mustasfa discusses the levels and conditions of ijtihad.
shades.hadith_ar: إِذَا اجْتَهَدَ الْحَاكِمُ فَأَصَابَ فَلَهُ أَجْرَانِ
shades.hadith_en: When the judge exerts effort and reaches the right answer, he gets two rewards

meaning.en: To draw near, approach. The root denotes the act of drawing close.

lexical_analysis.ibn_faris: الْقَافُ وَالرَّاءُ وَالْبَاءُ أَصْلٌ يَدُلُّ عَلَى دُنُوٍّ
lexical_analysis.al_raghib: الْقُرْبُ: ضِدُّ الْبُعْدِ. وَالْقَرِيبُ: مَنْ قَلَّتْ مَسَافَتُهُ

quran_examples.ar: وَنَحۡنُ أَقۡرَبُ إِلَيۡهِ مِنۡ حَبۡلِ ٱلۡوَرِيدِ
quran_examples.en: And We are closer to him than his jugular vein

quran_examples.ar: وَإِذَا سَأَلَكَ عِبَادِى عَنِّى فَإِنِّى قَرِيبٌ
quran_examples.en: And when My servants ask you concerning Me - indeed I am near
quran_examples.context: The response to the question about Allah's nearness

hadith.ar: أَقْرَبُ مَا يَكُونُ الْعَبْدُ مِنْ رَبِّهِ وَهُوَ سَاجِدٌ
hadith.en: The slave is closest to his Lord while he is in prostration

hadith.ar: إِنَّ اللَّهَ قَرِيبٌ مِنَ الْمُحْسِنِينَ
hadith.en: Indeed Allah is near to the doers of good

shades.explanation: al-Qurb (the nearness, the approach) in the Quran is one of the most fundamental concepts. The qurb of Allah to His servant is a reality that the believer seeks. The Quran says: 'And We have already created man and know what his nafs whispers to him, and We are closer to him than his jugular vein' (50:16). al-Qurb has two dimensions: (1) al-qurb al-makani (spatial nearness), (2) al-qurb al-ma'nawi (spiritual nearness). The hadith Qudsi states: 'My servant has drawn near to Me through voluntary acts until I love him.' The qurb of the believer is achieved through obedience, remembrance, and sincere love.
shades.hadith_ar: وَنَحۡنُ أَقۡرَبُ إِلَيۡهِ مِنۡ حَبۡلِ ٱلۡوَرِيدِ
shades.hadith_en: And We are closer to him than his jugular vein

shades.name_ar: الْقَرِيبُ - الَّذِي يَلِي الشَّيْءَ، قَرِيبُ الْمَسَافَةِ
shades.explanation: al-Qarib (the Near One) is one of the Names of Allah - the One who is near to His servants. The Quran says: 'And if My servants ask you concerning Me - indeed I am near [qarib]' (2:186). al-Qarib is the One who is near to every servant - closer than the jugular vein. The qurb of Allah is not spatial - it is the proximity of knowledge, power, mercy, and response. The hadith states: 'Allah is with the one who remembers Him.' al-Qarib responds to the du'a of the supplicant, even if he is far away. The believer always finds al-Qarib in his worship.
shades.hadith_ar: وَإِذَا سَأَلَكَ عِبَادِى عَنِّى فَإِنِّى قَرِيبٌ
shades.hadith_en: And when My servants ask you concerning Me - indeed I am near

shades.name_ar: الْمُقَرَّبُ - مَنْ يُقَرَّبُ إِلَى اللَّهِ، الَّذِي بَلَغَ الدَّرَجَةَ الْعُلْيَا
shades.explanation: al-Muqarrab (the Drawn-Near One) in the Quran refers to the angels and the believers who are drawn near to Allah. The Quran mentions 'al-muqarrabun' (the drawn-near ones) as one of the three groups of those who receive the Record of deeds (83:18-21). The muqarrabun are the highest rank in Paradise - they receive the Record in their right hand. The hadith states: 'The people of Paradise will see their Lord.' The muqarrabun are those who have reached the station of ihsan (excellence). al-Ghazali in Ihya' discusses the maqam al-muqarrabin (the station of those drawn near) as the highest spiritual rank.
shades.hadith_ar: يَـٰٓأَيَّتُهَا ٱلنَّفۡسُ ٱلۡمُطۡمَئِنَّةُ ٱرۡجِعِىٓ إِلَىٰ رَبِّكِ رَاضِيَةً مَّرۡضِيَّةً
shades.hadith_en: O reassured soul, return to your Lord, well-pleased and pleasing [to Him]

shades.name_en: Taqarrub - The Act of Drawing Near
shades.explanation: at-Taqarrub (the act of drawing near) in the Quran refers to the believer's act of drawing near to Allah through obedience. The famous hadith Qudsi states: 'My servant has drawn near to Me through voluntary acts until I love him. And when I love him, I become his hearing with which he hears, his sight with which he sees, his hand with which he strikes, his foot with which he walks. If he asks Me, I will surely give him. If he seeks refuge in Me, I will surely protect him.' The taqarrub of the believer is achieved through nawafil (voluntary acts), dhikr (remembrance), and sincere worship. The maqam al-muqarrabin is the result of consistent taqarrub.
shades.hadith_ar: مَنْ عَادَى لِي وَلِيًّا فَقَدْ آذَنْتُهُ بِالْحَرْبِ
shades.hadith_en: Whoever shows enmity to a friend of Mine, I have declared war against him

meaning.en: To be safe, submit. The root denotes peace, safety, and submission.
meaning.ar: السَّلَامُ: ضِدُّ الْحَرْبِ، وَالْإِسْلَامُ: الِاسْتِسْلَامُ لِلَّهِ

lexical_analysis.ibn_faris: السِّينُ وَاللَّامُ وَالْمِيمُ أَصْلٌ يَدُلُّ عَلَى سَلَامَةٍ
lexical_analysis.al_raghib: السَّلَامُ: ضِدُّ الْحَرْبِ. وَالْإِسْلَامُ: الِانْقِيَادُ لِلَّهِ

quran_examples.ar: هُوَ ٱللَّهُ ٱلَّذِى لَآ إِلَـٰهَ إِلَّا هُوَ ٱلۡمَلِكُ ٱلۡقُدُّوسُ ٱلسَّلَـٰمُ
quran_examples.en: He is Allah, other than whom there is no deity, the Sovereign, the Pure, the Perfection-Giving

quran_examples.ar: وَإِن يُصۡلِحُواْ يُؤۡتِهِمُ ٱللَّهُ أَجۡرًا
quran_examples.en: And if they reconcile, Allah will give them a great reward

hadith.ar: لَا تَدْخُلُوا الْجَنَّةَ حَتَّى تُؤْمِنُوا وَلَا تُؤْمِنُوا حَتَّى تَحَابُّوا
hadith.en: You will not enter Paradise until you believe, and you will not believe until you love one another

hadith.ar: أَفْضَلُ الصِّيَامِ صِيَامُ دَاوُدَ كَانَ يَصُومُ يَوْمًا وَيُفْطِرُ يَوْمًا
hadith.en: The best of fasting is the fasting of Dawud - he would fast one day and break the fast one day

shades.explanation: as-Salam (the peace) in the Quran is one of the most comprehensive divine attributes. Allah is as-Salam (the Source of Peace) - the One who is free from any defect. The Quran says: 'He is Allah, other than whom there is no deity, the Sovereign, the Pure, the Perfection-Giving [as-Salam]' (59:23). as-Salam is also the greeting of Paradise: 'Their greeting therein will be Salam' (10:10). The Salam of Allah to His servants on the Day of Judgment is the ultimate peace. The hadith states: 'You will not enter Paradise until you believe, and you will not believe until you love one another.' The Salam of the believers is a sign of their iman.
shades.hadith_ar: هُوَ ٱللَّهُ ٱلَّذِى لَآ إِلَـٰهَ إِلَّا هُوَ ٱلۡمَلِكُ ٱلۡقُدُّوسُ ٱلسَّلَـٰمُ
shades.hadith_en: He is Allah, other than whom there is no deity, the Sovereign, the Pure, the Perfection-Giving

shades.explanation: al-Islam (the submission to Allah) in the Quran is the religion of submission to Allah alone. The Quran says: 'Indeed, the religion in the sight of Allah is Islam' (3:19). Islam is derived from silm (peace) and istislam (submission). The five pillars of Islam are: (1) shahada (declaration of faith), (2) salah (five daily prayers), (3) zakat (obligatory charity), (4) sawm (fasting in Ramadan), (5) hajj (pilgrimage to Makkah). The hadith states: 'Islam is to testify that there is no god but Allah and that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah, to establish prayer, to give zakat, to fast in Ramadan, and to perform hajj if able.'
shades.hadith_ar: إِنَّ الدِّينَ عِندَ اللَّهِ الْإِسْلَامُ
shades.hadith_en: Indeed, the religion in the sight of Allah is Islam

shades.explanation: as-Sulhu (the peace, the reconciliation) in the Quran is the act of making peace between parties. The Quran says: 'And if they reconcile [aslaha], Allah will cause their reconciliation' (4:130). as-Sulhu is a fundamental Islamic principle - it is better than continued conflict. The famous hadith states: 'Reconciliation between people is better than all prayers and fasting.' al-Qushayri uses as-Sulhu in the spiritual sense - the peace between the heart and Allah, the soul and the body, the dunya and the akhirah. The sulhu of the believer is constant - he seeks peace with Allah through obedience and peace with people through justice.
shades.hadith_ar: وَإِن تُصۡلِحُواْ وَتَتَّقُواْ فَإِنَّ ٱللَّهَ كَانَ غَفُورًۭا رَّحِيمًا
shades.hadith_en: But if you correct yourselves and fear Allah - then indeed Allah is Forgiving and Merciful

shades.explanation: al-Muslim (the submitter) in the Quran is the one who has submitted to Allah. The Quran says: 'And who is better in religion than one who submits himself to Allah while being a doer of good' (4:125). The Muslim is the one who follows the Quran and the Sunnah, who has the inner state of surrender and the outer state of obedience. The famous hadith states: 'The Muslim is the one from whose tongue and hand other Muslims are safe, and the muhajir is the one who abandons what Allah has forbidden.' The Muslim has five characteristics of iman: belief in Allah, His angels, His books, His messengers, and the Last Day.
shades.hadith_ar: الْمُسْلِمُ مَنْ سَلِمَ الْمُسْلِمُونَ مِنْ لِسَانِهِ وَيَدِهِ
shades.hadith_en: The Muslim is the one from whose tongue and hand other Muslims are safe

meaning.en: To build, son. The root denotes construction or son/child.
meaning.ar: الْبِنَاءُ: إِقَامَةُ الشَّيْءِ، وَالِابْنُ: وَلَدُ الذَّكَرِ

lexical_analysis.ibn_faris: الْبَاءُ وَالنُّونُ وَالْيَاءُ أَصْلٌ يَدُلُّ عَلَى بِنَاءٍ أَوْ نَسَبٍ
lexical_analysis.al_raghib: الْبِنَاءُ: ضِدُّ الْهَدْمِ. وَالِابْنُ: وَلَدُ الذَّكَرِ

quran_examples.ar: وَإِذۡ يَرۡفَعُ إِبۡرَٰهِـۧمُ ٱلۡقَوَاعِدَ مِنَ ٱلۡبَيۡتِ وَإِسۡمَـٰعِيلُ
quran_examples.en: And when Ibrahim and Ismail were raising the foundations of the House
quran_examples.context: The raising of the Ka'bah foundations

quran_examples.ar: لَا تَقُمۡ فِيهِ أَبَدًۭا لَّمَسۡجِدٌ أُسِّسَ عَلَى ٱلتَّقۡوَىٰ مِنۡ أَوَّلِ يَوۡمٍ
quran_examples.en: Do not stand [for prayer] within it ever - a mosque founded on righteousness from the first day

hadith.ar: مَنْ بَنَى مَسْجِدًا لِلَّهِ بَنَى اللَّهُ لَهُ بَيْتًا فِي الْجَنَّةِ
hadith.en: Whoever builds a mosque for Allah, Allah will build for him a house in Paradise

hadith.ar: الْوَلَدُ لِلْفِرَاشِ وَلِلْعَاهِرِ الْحَجَرُ
hadith.en: The child belongs to the marriage bed, and the fornicator gets the stone

shades.explanation: al-Bina' (the building, the construction) in the Quran refers to the act of constructing. The Quran mentions: (1) the building of the Ka'bah (2:127, 22:29), (2) the building of the heavens and the earth (2:22, 3:96, 9:109, 14:48, 30:9, 39:5, 50:6, 51:47, 79:27, 91:5), (3) the building of houses and towers (4:78, 26:128, 89:6-7), (4) the building of mosques (9:17, 9:108, 24:36). The bina' of Allah is the most perfect - He built the heavens without pillars visible to you. The hadith states: 'Whoever builds a mosque for Allah, Allah will build for him a house in Paradise.'
shades.hadith_ar: وَإِذۡ يَرۡفَعُ إِبۡرَٰهِـۧمُ ٱلۡقَوَاعِدَ مِنَ ٱلۡبَيۡتِ وَإِسۡمَـٰعِيلُ
shades.hadith_en: And when Ibrahim and Ismail were raising the foundations of the House

shades.explanation: al-Ibn (the son) in the Quran is the male offspring. The Quran mentions numerous sons: (1) the sons of Adam (5:27-32), (2) the sons of Nuh (11:42-43, 71:21-28), (3) the sons of Ibrahim (37:83-113), (4) the sons of Yaqub (2:133, 12:14, 12:80), (5) the sons of Israel (Bani Isra'il - 2:47, 7:105, 26:17, 27:14, 32:23, 40:53, 44:30, 45:16, 46:10). al-Ibn in the Quran has both literal and metaphorical meanings. The famous hadith states: 'The child belongs to the marriage bed, and the fornicator gets the stone.' The 'ibn al-sabil (son of the road) is the traveler. The 'ibn in Sufism represents the spiritual son - the one who inherits spiritual knowledge.
shades.hadith_ar: إِذۡ قَالَ يُوسُفُ لِأَبِيهِ يَـٰٓأَبَتِ إِنِّى رَأَيۡتُ أَحَدَ عَشَرَ كَوۡكَبًۭا
shades.hadith_en: When Yusuf said to his father: O my father, indeed I have seen [in a dream] eleven stars

shades.name_en: Bani Isra'il - The Children of Israel
shades.name_ar: بَنُو إِسۡرَٰٓءِيلَ - ذُرِّيَّةُ يَعۡقُوبَ، نَسْلُ إِسْرَائِيلَ
shades.explanation: Bani Isra'il (the Children of Israel) are the descendants of Yaqub (Israel) - the twelve tribes. The Quran mentions Bani Isra'il extensively - they are the nation to whom Musa was sent. Surah al-Baqarah mentions them extensively, as does Surah al-A'raf. The Bani Isra'il received many favors from Allah: (1) the Torah, the Psalms, and the Gospel, (2) prophethood, (3) kingship, (4) divine favor, (5) manna and quails. The Quran praises them when they obey and criticizes them when they disobey. The hadith states: 'You will follow the ways of those before you, handspan by handspan, cubit by cubit.' The Bani Isra'il are the spiritual predecessors of the Muslim ummah.
shades.hadith_ar: يَـٰبَنِىٓ إِسۡرَٰٓءِيلَ ٱذۡكُرُواْ نِعۡمَتِىَ ٱلَّتِىٓ أَنۡعَمۡتُ عَلَيۡكُمۡ
shades.hadith_en: O Children of Israel, remember My favor which I have bestowed upon you

shades.explanation: al-Mabni (the built, the constructed) in the Quran refers to that which has been constructed. The Quran says: 'And the heaven He constructed and gave it form' (79:28). The Mabni in the spiritual sense is the heart that has been built on taqwa - the firm foundation. The famous hadith states: 'The believer's heart is the throne of al-Rahman.' The Mabni of the believer's heart is built on iman, taqwa, and love. al-Ghazali in Ihya' describes the tarbiya (education) of the heart as the construction of a building - first the foundation, then the walls, then the roof. The Mabni is firm and unshakeable.
shades.hadith_ar: أَفَمَنۡ أَسَّسَ بُنۡيَـٰنَهُۥ عَلَىٰ تَقۡوَىٰ مِنَ ٱللَّهِ وَرِضۡوَٰنٍ
shades.hadith_en: Is he who founded his building on righteousness [taqwa] from Allah and [His] good pleasure better

meaning.en: To quench, drink. The root denotes drinking until satisfied or narration.
meaning.ar: الرِّيُّ: الشُّرْبُ حَتَّى الرِّيِّ، وَالرِّوَايَةُ: نَقْلُ الْحَدِيثِ

lexical_analysis.ibn_faris: الرَّاءُ وَالْوَاوُ وَالْيَاءُ أَصْلٌ يَدُلُّ عَلَى رِيٍّ أَوْ نَقْلٍ
lexical_analysis.al_raghib: الرِّيُّ: شُرْبُ الشَّيْءِ بِكَمَالِهِ. وَالرَّوْضَةُ: الْبُسْتَانُ

quran_examples.ar: مَّثَلُ ٱلۡجَنَّةِ ٱلَّتِى وُعِدَ ٱلۡمُتَّقُونَ فِيهَآ أَنۡهَـٰرٌۭ مِّن مَّآءٍ
quran_examples.en: The description of Paradise which the righteous are promised: therein are rivers of water

quran_examples.ar: فَلَمَّا فَصَلَ طَالُوتُ بِٱلۡجُنُودِ قَالَ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ سَيُمۡلِيهَا
quran_examples.en: And when Talut marched out with the army, he said: Indeed Allah will test you with a river

hadith.ar: بَيْنَ بَيْتِي وَمِنْبَرِي رَوْضَةٌ مِنْ رِيَاضِ الْجَنَّةِ
hadith.en: Between my house and my minbar is a rawda from the riyad of Paradise

hadith.ar: سَيَكُونُ فِي أُمَّتِي فِتَنٌ
hadith.en: There will be fitan (trials) in my ummah

shades.name_ar: الرِّيُّ - الشُّرْبُ حَتَّى الرِّيِّ، الِانْتِهَاءُ مِنَ الشَّرَابِ
shades.explanation: ar-Ri (the drinking) in the Quran refers to the act of drinking until one's thirst is fully quenched.
