The Quran says: 'And We shaded you with clouds and sent down to you manna and quails, [saying]: Eat from the good things with which We have provided you' (2:57). ar-Ri is the complete satisfaction of thirst. The Quran contrasts ar-ri with 'adh-shafaq (the half-thirst) - the river of Paradise gives the drinker full ri. The famous hadith states: 'In Paradise there is a river of milk, a river of wine, a river of honey, and a river of water.' The ri of Paradise is perfect and never ending.
shades.hadith_ar: إِنَّ أَصۡحَـٰبَ ٱلۡجَنَّةِ ٱلۡيَوۡمَ فِى شُغُلٍۢ فَـٰكِهُونَ
shades.hadith_en: Indeed the companions of Paradise, that Day, are in pleasant work, exultant

shades.name_ar: الرَّوْضَةُ - الْبُسْتَانُ، الْجَنَّةُ الصَّغِيرَةُ عَلَى الْأَرْضِ
shades.explanation: ar-Rawda (the garden, the meadow) in the Quran refers to a place of greenery and beauty. The Quran says: 'And those who have believed and done righteous deeds - We will surely admit them to gardens [jannat] through which rivers flow' (4:57, 5:85, 9:72, 18:107, 22:14, 29:58). ar-Rawda in hadith refers to a section of Paradise. The famous hadith states: 'Between my house and my minbar is a rawda from the riyad of Paradise.' The rawda is a place of spiritual beauty in the dunya as well - a place where hearts find peace. The rawda in Sufism is the inner garden of the heart.
shades.hadith_ar: بَيْنَ بَيۡتِى وَمِنۡبَرِى رَوۡضَةٌۭ مِّن رِيَاضِ ٱلۡجَنَّةِ
shades.hadith_en: Between my house and my minbar is a rawda from the riyad of Paradise

shades.explanation: at-Taraweeha (the resting) refers to the brief rest after work or worship. The hadith of taraweeh prayer specifically refers to the qiyam al-layl (night prayer) in Ramadan - the Salat at-Taraweeh. The Quran says: 'Indeed, the hours of the night are more effective for concurrence [of heart and tongue] and more suitable for words' (73:6). The night prayer in Ramadan is one of the most rewarding acts - the Prophet said: 'Whoever stands [in prayer] during Ramadan out of iman and hoping for reward, his past sins will be forgiven.' The taraweeh is the special prayer of Ramadan that combines physical rest with spiritual elevation.
shades.hadith_ar: مَنْ قَامَ رَمَضَانَ إِيمَانًا وَاحْتِسَابًا غُفِرَ لَهُ مَا تَقَدَّمَ مِنْ ذَنۢبِهِ
shades.hadith_en: Whoever stands [in prayer] during Ramadan out of iman and hoping for reward, his past sins will be forgiven

shades.explanation: ar-Riyad (the meadows, the gardens) in the Quran and hadith refers to the gardens of Paradise. The famous hadith states: 'Between my house and my minbar is a rawda from the riyad of Paradise' - the riyad is the plural of rawda. The Quran says: 'And those who have believed and done righteous deeds - We will surely admit them to gardens [jannat] through which rivers flow' (4:57). ar-Riyad is the high gardens of Paradise - the highest level of reward. The believer who reaches ar-riyad has achieved the highest level of iman and taqwa. The ar-riyad in Sufism refers to the spiritual stations of the awliya'.
shades.hadith_ar: رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُمْ وَرَضُوا عَنْهُ وَأَعَدَّ لَهُمْ جَنَّاتٍ تَجْرِي تَحْتَهَا الْأَنْهَارُ
shades.hadith_en: Allah is pleased with them and they are pleased with Him, and He has prepared for them gardens under which rivers flow

meaning.en: To be mountainous. The root denotes mountain, mount, or creation.

lexical_analysis.ibn_faris: الْجِيمُ وَالْبَاءُ وَاللَّامُ أَصْلٌ يَدُلُّ عَلَى عِظَمٍ
lexical_analysis.al_raghib: الْجَبَلُ: الشَّيْءُ الْعَظِيمُ مِنَ الْأَرْضِ. وَجَبَلَ: خَلَقَ

quran_examples.ar: وَٱلَّذِى نَشَرَ ٱلۡأَرۡضَ وَجَعَلَ فِيهَا رَوَٰسِىَ مِن فَوۡقِهَا
quran_examples.en: And it is He who spread the earth and placed therein firmly set mountains
quran_examples.context: The creation of the earth with mountains

quran_examples.ar: فَلَمَّا تَجَلَّىٰ رَبُّهُۥ لِلۡجَبَلِ جَعَلَهُۥ دَكًّۭا
quran_examples.en: And when his Lord appeared to the mountain, He made it collapse to dust

hadith.ar: رَأَيْتُ جِبْرِيلَ يَمْشِي فِي أَزِقَّةِ الْمَدِينَةِ
hadith.en: I saw Jibril walking in the streets of Madinah

hadith.ar: إِنِّي لَأَسْتَغْفِرُ اللَّهَ وَأَتُوبُ إِلَيْهِ فِي الْيَوْمِ أَكْثَرَ مِنْ سَبْعِينَ مَرَّةً
hadith.en: I seek forgiveness from Allah and repent to Him more than seventy times a day

shades.explanation: al-Jabal (the mountain) in the Quran is one of the most magnificent creations. The Quran mentions the mountains as pillars of the earth (13:3, 15:19, 16:15, 21:31, 31:10, 41:10), as signs of Allah's power (3:6, 19:90, 33:72, 59:21, 64:3, 73:14), and as sources of provision (2:265, 16:11, 16:18, 23:18-19, 36:33). Allah cast upon the mountain the divine speech at Sinai (7:143). The mountain in Sufism represents the haqiqa (divine reality) - the firm and unshakeable truth.
shades.hadith_ar: وَجَعَلۡنَا فِى ٱلۡجِبَالِ أَوۡتَادًۭا
shades.hadith_en: And We placed within the mountains firmly rooted pegs

shades.name_ar: جَبَلُ سِينَآءَ - الْجَبَلُ الَّذِي كَلَّمَ اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ مُوسَى
shades.explanation: Jabal Sina' (Mount Sinai) is the mountain where Allah spoke to Musa. The Quran mentions at-Tur (the Mountain - 23:20, 52:1, 56:29, 95:2) and Jabal Musa (the Mountain of Musa - 2:60, 2:63, 2:93, 4:154, 7:171). The mountain trembled at the divine speech. The famous hadith of the Mi'raj describes how the Prophet Muhammad passed by Musa at every heaven. Musa is the most-mentioned prophet in the Quran. The mountain in Sufism represents the haal of qurb - the state of the one who has been addressed by Allah.
shades.hadith_ar: وَكَلَّمَ ٱللَّهُ مُوسَىٰ تَكۡلِيمًۭا
shades.hadith_en: And Allah spoke to Musa with direct speech

shades.explanation: al-Jibal (the mountains) in the Quran is the plural of jabal. The Quran mentions al-jibal in various contexts: as signs of Allah's power (16:15, 41:10), as ornaments of the earth (27:60, 31:10, 39:21, 50:7, 78:7), as protection from earthquakes (78:6-7), as places of worship (9:114), as places of refuge (18:16, 18:47). The mountains are asked to bring their tasbih in 38:18 - We placed firmly rooted mountains and We exalted them, and they gloried with Us.
shades.hadith_ar: سَيَقُولُونَ ثَلَـٰثَةٌ رَّابِعُهُمۡ كَلۡبُهُمۡ
shades.hadith_en: They would say: Three - and the fourth of them was their dog

shades.explanation: al-Jubayl (the mountainous, the mountain-like) in the Quran refers to a person or thing of mountain-like stature. The famous hadith states: I saw Jibril walking in the streets of Madinah. Jibril is described as having 600 wings, each wing filling the horizon - a mountain-like spirit. The mountainous spirit in Sufism is the ruh (spirit) that has reached the level of stability - the one whose heart is unshakeable. The Quran says: And the mountains that you see [as immobile] - they will pass as the passing of clouds (27:88).
shades.hadith_ar: لَا تَقُصَّ رُؤْيَاكَ عَلَىٰ إِخْوَتِكَ فَيَكِيدُوا لَكَ كَيۡدًا
shades.hadith_en: Do not relate your vision to your brothers lest they plot against you

meaning.en: To harvest, gather. The root denotes gathering fruits or hiding.
meaning.ar: الْجَنْيُ: جَمْعُ الثَّمَرِ، وَالْجَنِينُ: مَا فِي بَطْنِ الْأَمِّ

lexical_analysis.ibn_faris: الْجِيمُ وَالنُّونُ وَالْيَاءُ أَصْلٌ يَدُلُّ عَلَى سَتْرٍ أَوْ جَمْعٍ
lexical_analysis.al_raghib: الْجَنَّةُ: الْبُسْتَانُ الشَّجَرُ. وَجَنَى: قَطَفَ

quran_examples.ar: وَٱلۡجَآنَّ خَلَقۡنَـٰهُ مِن قَبۡلُ مِن نَّارِ ٱلسَّمُومِ
quran_examples.en: And the jinn We created before from the smokeless flame of fire

quran_examples.ar: فَمَن يَعۡمَلۡ مِثۡقَالَ ذَرَّةٍ خَيۡرًۭا يَرَهُۥ
quran_examples.en: So whoever has done an atom's weight of good will see it

hadith.ar: إِنَّ فِي الْجَنَّةِ لَشَجَرَةً لَوْ سَارَ فِيهَا رَاكِبٌ لَقَطَعَهَا مِائَةَ عَامٍ
hadith.en: Indeed in Paradise there is a tree that if a rider were to travel through it for a hundred years he would not cross it

hadith.ar: إِنَّ الْجَنَّةَ مِائَةُ دَرَجَةٍ مَا بَيْنَ كُلِّ دَرَجَتَيْنِ مِائَةُ عَامٍ
hadith.en: Indeed Paradise has one hundred grades, between each two grades is a distance of a hundred years

shades.explanation: al-Janay (the harvest, the gathering) in the Quran refers to the act of gathering or harvesting fruit. The Quran uses the metaphor of harvest for the deeds of the servant on the Day of Judgment: 'So whoever has done an atom's weight of good will see it, and whoever has done an atom's weight of evil will see it' (99:7-8). The harvest of the believer is gathered in this world through deeds; on the Day of Judgment, the harvest will be presented. The hadith states: 'The deeds of the people of Paradise will be presented to them in various forms.' al-Janay in Sufism is the gathering of the fruits of dhikr and worship.
shades.hadith_ar: فَمَن يَعۡمَلۡ مِثۡقَالَ ذَرَّةٍ خَيۡرًۭا يَرَهُۥ
shades.hadith_en: So whoever has done an atom's weight of good will see it

shades.explanation: al-Janna (the garden, the Paradise) in the Quran is one of the most frequent subjects. The janna has many names: jannat al-na'im (Garden of delights), jannat al-firdaws (Garden of Paradise), jannat al-'adn (Garden of Eden), jannat al-maqwa (Garden of refuge), jannat al-khuld (Garden of eternity), dar al-salam (Abode of peace), al-firdaws (Paradise), dar al-muqama (Abode of permanence). The janna is described in detail: rivers of water, milk, wine, honey; fruits of every kind; companions of pure spouses; shade and comfort. The hadith states: 'In Paradise there are things which no eye has seen, no ear has heard, and no human mind has conceived.' The janna is the final abode of the mu'minun.
shades.hadith_ar: جَنَّـٰتُ عَدۡنٍۢ تَجۡرِى مِن تَحۡتِهَا ٱلۡأَنۡهَـٰرُ
shades.hadith_en: Gardens of perpetual residence beneath which rivers flow

shades.name_en: Jinn - The Hidden, The Unseen Beings
shades.explanation: al-Jinn (the hidden, the unseen beings) in the Quran are a creation of Allah made from smokeless fire. The Quran says: 'And He created the jinn from a smokeless flame of fire' (55:15). The jinn are mentioned extensively in the Quran, particularly in Surah al-Jinn (72). They have free will like humans, can be believers or disbelievers. The famous hadith states: 'The jinn were created from fire, and Adam was created from clay.' The jinn have prophets and revelations, and they will be held accountable on the Day of Judgment. The Quran mentions the mu'min jinn who accepted the message of the Prophet Muhammad.
shades.hadith_ar: وَٱلۡجَآنَّ خَلَقۡنَـٰهُ مِن قَبۡلُ مِن نَّارِ ٱلسَّمُومِ
shades.hadith_en: And the jinn We created before from the smokeless flame of fire

shades.name_ar: الْجَنِينُ - الْحَمْلُ قَبْلَ الْوِلَادَةِ، مَا فِي بَطْنِ الْأَمِّ
shades.explanation: al-Janin (the embryo, the fetus) in the Quran refers to the developing child in the womb. The Quran describes the stages of human creation: nutfa (drop), 'alaqa (clinging clot), mudgha (chewed lump), 'idham (bones), lahman (flesh), khalqan akhar (another creation). The Quran says: 'And certainly did We create man from an extract of clay. Then We placed him as a sperm-drop [nutfa] in a firm lodging [qarar makeen]' (23:12-13). The famous hadith states: 'Each of you is collected in his mother's womb for forty days as a nutfa, then for forty days as an 'alaqa, then for forty days as a mudgha, then the angel is sent to write his deeds.'
shades.hadith_ar: ثُمَّ جَعَلۡنَـٰهُ نُطۡفَةًۭ فِى قَرَارٍۢ مَّكِينٍۢ
shades.hadith_en: Then We placed him as a sperm-drop in a firm lodging

meaning.en: To be poor, needy. The root denotes need and poverty.

lexical_analysis.ibn_faris: الْفَاءُ وَالْقَافُ وَالرَّاءُ أَصْلٌ يَدُلُّ عَلَى حَاجَةٍ
lexical_analysis.al_raghib: الْفَقْرُ: ضِدُّ الْغِنَى. وَالْفَقِيرُ: مَنْ بِهِ حَاجَةٌ

quran_examples.ar: يَـٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلۡإِنسَـٰنُ أَنتَ ٱلۡفَقِيرُ إِلَى ٱللَّهِ
quran_examples.en: O mankind, you are those in need of Allah; but Allah is the Free of need, the Praiseworthy

quran_examples.ar: لِلۡفُقَرَآءِ ٱلَّذِينَ أُحۡصِرُواْ فِى سَبِيلِ ٱللَّهِ
quran_examples.en: For the poor who are constrained for the cause of Allah
quran_examples.context: The poor who are occupied in the way of Allah

hadith.ar: لَيْسَ الْمِسْكِينُ الَّذِي تَرُدُّهُ اللُّقْمَةُ وَاللُّقْمَتَانِ
hadith.en: The miskeen is not the one who is turned away by a morsel or two

hadith.ar: يَا عِبَادِي لَوْ أَنَّ أَوَّلَكُمْ وَآخِرَكُمْ
hadith.en: O My servants, if the first of you and the last of you

shades.explanation: al-Faqr (the poverty) in the Quran is one of the most profound spiritual concepts. The Quran says: O mankind, you are those in need of Allah [al-fuqara']; but Allah is the Free of need, the Praiseworthy (35:15). al-Faqr has multiple dimensions: al-faqr al-maddi (material poverty), al-faqr al-ma'nawi (spiritual poverty before Allah), al-faqr al-mutlaq (absolute poverty - every human is poor). The famous hadith Qudsi states: O My servants, if the first of you and the last of you and the jinn and mankind all stood in one place and asked of Me, I would give to each one what he asked. al-Faqr in Sufism is the highest station - the recognition of complete dependence on Allah.
shades.hadith_ar: إِنَّ ٱلۡإِنسَـٰنَ لَفِى خُسۡرٍ
shades.hadith_en: Indeed mankind is in loss

shades.name_ar: الْفَقِيرُ - مَنْ لَا شَيْءَ لَهُ، مَنْ بِهِ حَاجَةٌ
shades.explanation: al-Faqir (the poor one) in the Quran is one who is in need. The Quran says: And Allah enriches and impoverishes, and to Him you will be returned (3:37). The faqir is also one of the recipients of zakat (9:60): The alms are only for the poor [al-fuqara'] and the needy [al-masakin]. The hadith states: The faqir is not the one who goes around begging from people, but the faqir is the one who has nothing and does not know that anyone will give him charity. al-Faqir is also a divine attribute - Allah is al-Ghani (the Rich), but He describes His servants as faqirun.
shades.hadith_ar: لَّيۡسَ ٱلصَّدَقَةُ بِٱلۡعَطَآءِ عَنۡ ظَهۡرِ غِنًى
shades.hadith_en: Charity is not given from your excess wealth

shades.explanation: al-Iftiqar (the acknowledging of poverty) in the spiritual sense is the recognition that one is completely dependent on Allah. The famous hadith Qudsi states: My servant has drawn near to Me through voluntary acts until I love him. al-Iftiqar is the opposite of al-istighna (self-sufficiency). The believer practices al-iftiqar by: constantly asking Allah for forgiveness, performing du'a in all situations, recognizing that all rizq comes from Allah, not boasting about one's achievements. al-Ghazali in Ihya' discusses al-iftiqar as the foundation of tawhid.
shades.hadith_ar: ٱدۡعُونِىٓ أَسۡتَجِبۡ لَكُمۡ
shades.hadith_en: Call upon Me; I will respond to you

shades.name_ar: الْمَسَاكِينُ - جَمْعُ مِسۡكِينٍ، مَنْ بِهِ فَاقَةٌ شَدِيدَةٌ
shades.explanation: al-Masakin (the needy, the destitute) in the Quran is the plural of miskeen - those in severe need. The Quran says: And those in whose wealth is a known right for the beggar and the deprived (70:24-25). al-Masakin are distinguished from al-fuqara' (the poor) by classical scholars - the masakin are the more severe cases. The famous hadith states: The likeness of the miskeen who goes around begging from people is like a bird whose head has been smeared with blood. al-Masakin deserve our generosity - the most beloved deeds to Allah are those that are most consistent.
shades.hadith_ar: لَّيۡسَ ٱلۡمِسۡكِينُ ٱلَّذِى تَرُدُّهُ ٱلۡأُكۡلَةُ وَٱلۡأُكۡلَتَانِ
shades.hadith_en: The miskeen is not the one who is turned away by a morsel or two

meaning.en: To fear. The root denotes fear or awe.

lexical_analysis.ibn_faris: الْخَاءُ وَالْوَاوُ وَالْفَاءُ أَصْلٌ يَدُلُّ عَلَى فَزَعٍ
lexical_analysis.al_raghib: الْخَوْفُ: تَوَقُّعُ الْمَكْرُوهِ. وَالْخَشْيَةُ: الْخَوْفُ الْمَعْلُولُ بِالْعِلْمِ

quran_examples.ar: وَلَا تَشۡتَرُواْ بِـَٔايَـٰتِى ثَمَنًۭا قَلِيلًۭا
quran_examples.en: And do not exchange My signs for a small price
quran_examples.context: The protection against selling the verses

quran_examples.ar: وَرِضۡوَٰنٌۭ مِّنَ ٱللَّهِ أَكۡبَرُ
quran_examples.en: And [the] good pleasure of Allah is greater
quran_examples.context: The greatest reward - the pleasure of Allah

hadith.ar: سَبْعَةٌ يُظِلُّهُمُ اللَّهُ فِي ظِلِّهِ يَوْمَ لَا ظِلَّ إِلَّا ظِلُّهُ
hadith.en: Seven are those whom Allah will shade with His shade on the Day when there is no shade except His shade

hadith.ar: إِنَّ اللَّهَ يَرْضَى لِلْعَبْدِ أَنْ يَأْكُلَ الْأَكْلَةَ فَيَحْمَدَهُ عَلَيْهَا
hadith.en: Allah is pleased with the servant who eats a meal and praises Allah for it

shades.explanation: al-Khawf (the fear) in the Quran is one of the most powerful spiritual states. The Quran says: Their reward from their Lord is gardens of perpetual residence beneath which rivers flow, wherein they will abide forever. Allah is pleased with them and they are pleased with Him - that is for whoever feared [khashiya] his Lord (98:7-8). al-Khawf has multiple dimensions: (1) fear of punishment (al-khawf min al-'adhab), (2) fear of being veiled (al-khawf min al-hijab), (3) fear of the loss of love (al-khawf min faqd al-hubb). The hadith states: The seven whom Allah will shade with His shade on the Day of Judgment include those who remember Allah and whose eyes overflow with tears.
shades.hadith_ar: إِنَّمَا يَخۡشَى ٱللَّهَ مِنۡ عِبَادِهِ ٱلۡعُلَمَـٰٓؤُاْ
shades.hadith_en: Only those of His servants who are scholars fear Allah

shades.name_en: al-Khashya - The Awe, The Reverent Fear
shades.explanation: al-Khashya (the awe, the reverent fear) in the Quran is a higher form of fear - it is the fear that comes from knowing Allah. The Quran says: And they would not cease fighting you [until] they turned you back from your religion if they were able. And whoever of you reverts from his religion [to disbelief] and dies while he is a disbeliever - for those, their deeds have become worthless in this world and the Hereafter (2:217). al-Khashya is distinct from al-khawf - it is the fear that combines love, knowledge, and reverence. The hadith states: I am the one who knows Allah best and I am the most reverent of Allah among them.
shades.hadith_ar: لَا تَخَافُوا وَلَا تَحۡزَنُوا وَأَبۡشِرُوا بِٱلۡجَنَّةِ ٱلَّتِى كُنتُمۡ تُوعَدُونَ
shades.hadith_en: Do not fear and do not grieve, and receive good tidings of Paradise which you were promised

shades.name_ar: الْمُخۡبِتُونَ - الْمُتَوَاضِعُونَ، الَّذِينَ تَطْمَئِنُّ قُلُوبُهُمۡ بِذِكۡرِ ٱللَّهِ
shades.explanation: al-Mukhbitun (the submissive, the humble) in the Quran refers to those who are humbly submissive before Allah. The Quran says: Successful indeed are the mukhbitun - those who in the presence of their Lord are humble (23:1-2). al-Mukhbitu is one whose heart is at peace through dhikr of Allah. The famous hadith states: The hearts of the mukhbitun rest in the remembrance of Allah. al-Mukhbit in Sufism is the one who has reached the state of khashya - the reverent fear that comes from intimate knowledge of Allah. al-Ghazali in Ihya' discusses al-mukhbitun as the awliya' who have been drawn near to Allah.
shades.hadith_ar: أَلَا بِذِكۡرِ ٱللَّهِ تَطۡمَئِنُّ ٱلۡقُلُوبُ
shades.hadith_en: Indeed, in the remembrance of Allah do hearts find rest

shades.explanation: al-Ikhlaf (the breaking of oaths) refers to violating one's promise. The Quran says: And do not be like she who unravels her yarn after she has spun it strongly (16:92). al-Ikhlaf is one of the characteristics of the munafiqun (hypocrites). The hadith states: The signs of the hypocrite are three: when he speaks he lies, when he promises he breaks, and when he is entrusted he betrays. The believer avoids al-ikhlaf - he keeps his promises and fulfills his covenants. The Quran warns: And fulfill [every] commitment. Indeed the commitment is ever [that about which one will be] questioned (17:34).
shades.hadith_ar: إِنَّ ٱلۡعَهۡدَ كَانَ مَسۡـُٔولًۭا
shades.hadith_en: Indeed the commitment is ever [that about which one will be] questioned

meaning.en: To steal. The root denotes the act of stealing or taking secretly.

lexical_analysis.ibn_faris: السِّينُ وَالرَّاءُ وَالْقَافُ أَصْلٌ يَدُلُّ عَلَى أَخْذٍ خُفْيٍ
lexical_analysis.al_raghib: السَّرِقُ: أَخْذُ الشَّيْءِ مِنْ غَيْرِ رِضَاهُ. وَالسَّارِقُ: فَاعِلُهُ

quran_examples.ar: وَٱلسَّارِقُ وَٱلسَّارِقَةُ فَٱقۡطَعُوٓاْ أَيۡدِيَهُمَا
quran_examples.en: And [as for] the thief and the thiefess, cut their hands

quran_examples.ar: قَالُواْ جَزَـٰٓؤُهُۥ مَن وُجِدَ فِى رَحۡلِهِ فَهُوَ جَزَـٰٓؤُهُۥ
quran_examples.en: They said: The penalty for it - whoever is found to have it in his bag will be its compensation
quran_examples.context: The investigation of the theft in Yusuf's story

hadith.ar: لَعَنَ اللَّهُ السَّارِقَ يَسْرِقُ الْبَيْضَةَ فَتُقْطَعُ يَدُهُ
hadith.en: Allah cursed the thief who steals the egg and his hand is cut off

hadith.ar: لَا تَقُصَّ رُؤْيَاكَ عَلَى إِخْوَتِكَ
hadith.en: Do not relate your vision to your brothers

shades.name_ar: السَّرِقُ - أَخْذُ الشَّيْءِ خُفْيَةً مِنْ غَيْرِ رِضًا
shades.explanation: as-Saraq (the theft) in the Quran is a major sin that has a prescribed punishment. The Quran says: And [as for] the thief and the thiefess, cut them off (5:38). as-Saraq is taking someone's property secretly without their consent. The punishment in Islam is hudud (prescribed punishment) - cutting off the hand. The famous hadith states: Allah curses the thief who steals an egg and his hand is cut off, and who steals a rope and his hand is cut off. The hadith establishes that even small theft can lead to the prescribed punishment. as-Saraq is not only physical theft - it includes cheating, deceit, fraud, and betrayal of trust.
shades.hadith_ar: وَٱلسَّارِقُ وَٱلسَّارِقَةُ فَٱقۡطَعُوٓاْ أَيۡدِيَهُمَا
shades.hadith_en: And [as for] the thief and the thiefess, cut their hands

shades.name_ar: السَّارِقُ - مَنْ يَسۡرِقُ، مَنْ يَأْخُذُ الشَّيْءَ خُفْيَةً
shades.explanation: as-Sariq (the thief) in the Quran is the one who steals. The famous hadith states: Allah cursed the thief who steals an egg (and his hand is cut off), and who steals a rope (and his hand is cut off). The sariq in Islamic law is subject to the hudud punishment only if certain conditions are met: (1) the stolen item has a minimum value (nisab), (2) it is taken from a secure place, (3) the theft is by an adult, sane, free person. The famous hadith states: The hadd (prescribed punishment) is lifted from the repentant. The sariq who repents before being caught is forgiven by Allah.
shades.hadith_ar: لَعَنَ اللَّهُ السَّارِقَ يَسْرِقُ الْبَيْضَةَ فَتُقْطَعُ يَدُهُ
shades.hadith_en: Allah cursed the thief who steals the egg and his hand is cut off

shades.explanation: as-Saraqa (the stealing) in the Quran is the act of taking something secretly. The Quran mentions: And they found a servant from among Our servants to whom We had given mercy from Us and had taught him from Us a [certain] knowledge (18:65). The famous hadith states: Allah has prescribed for every son of Adam his share of adultery which he commits inevitably. The adultery of the eyes is the sight, the adultery of the tongue is the speech, the adultery of the hand is the action, and the adultery of the feet is the steps. The saraqa in the broader sense includes all forms of illicit taking - bribery, theft of knowledge, and betrayal of trust.
shades.hadith_ar: إِنَّ السَّمْعَ وَالْبَصَرَ وَالْفُؤَادَ كُلُّ أُوْلَـٰٓئِكَ كَانَ عَنۡهُ مَسۡـُٔولًۭا
shades.hadith_en: Indeed the hearing, the sight, and the heart - about all those [one] will be questioned

shades.explanation: al-Musaaraqa (the snatching) is the more serious form of theft - stealing openly in confrontation. The Quran mentions: And the thieves came to you and you said: The verdict is known (12:75). al-Musaaraqa is taking by force or openly. The famous hadith states: Whoever carries weapons against us is not from us. The musaaraqa of public order is one of the major sins in Islam. The believers are warned against musaaraqa - whether of property, of honor, or of trust. The Quran says: And cooperate in righteousness and piety, but do not cooperate in sin and aggression (5:2). The believer maintains justice and avoids all forms of theft and snatching.
shades.hadith_ar: وَلَا تَعَاوَنُوا عَلَى ٱلۡإِثۡمِ وَٱلۡعُدۡوَٰنِ
shades.hadith_en: And do not cooperate in sin and aggression

meaning.en: To ride, mount. The root denotes riding or compounding.

lexical_analysis.ibn_faris: الرَّاءُ وَالْكَافُ وَالْبَاءُ أَصْلٌ يَدُلُّ عَلَى ارْتِكَابٍ
lexical_analysis.al_raghib: الرُّكُوبُ: ارْتِكَابُ الْمَرْكُوبِ. وَرَكِبَ: عَلَا

quran_examples.ar: وَٱلۡخَيۡلَ وَٱلۡبِغَالَ وَٱلۡحَمِيرَ لِتَرۡكَبُوهَا
quran_examples.en: And the horses, mules, and donkeys for you to ride

quran_examples.ar: سُبۡحَـٰنَ ٱلَّذِىٓ أَسۡرَىٰ بِعَبۡدِهِۦ لَيۡلًۭا
quran_examples.en: Exalted is He who took His Servant by night

hadith.ar: لَا يُلۡدَغُ ٱلۡمُؤۡمِنُ مِن جُحۡرٍۢ وَٰحِدٍۢ مَّرَّتَيۡنِ
hadith.en: The believer is not stung twice from the same hole

hadith.ar: الۡقُرۡءَانُ يَشۡفَعُ لِصَاحِبِهِ يَوۡمَ ٱلۡقِيَـٰمَةِ
hadith.en: The Quran will intercede for its companion on the Day of Resurrection

shades.explanation: ar-Rukub (the riding) in the Quran refers to mounting and riding. The Quran says: And it is He who has subjected the night and the day to you, and the sun and the moon and the stars are subjected by His command. Indeed in that are signs for people who reason (16:12). ar-Rukub is one of Allah's gifts to humans - the ability to ride horses, camels, ships, and aircraft. The famous hadith states: Allah's messenger cursed the one who does the act of the people of Lut (homosexuality). ar-Rukub is not just physical - in Sufism it is the ruku' of the heart on the dhikr of Allah.
shades.hadith_ar: وَٱلۡخَيۡلَ وَٱلۡبِغَالَ وَٱلۡحَمِيرَ لِتَرۡكَبُوهَا
shades.hadith_en: And the horses, mules, and donkeys for you to ride

shades.name_ar: الرَّاكِبُ - مَنۡ يَرۡكَبُ الْمَرْكَبَ، الْمُتَمَتِّعُ بِالْمَرْكُوبِ
shades.explanation: ar-Rakib (the rider) in the Quran is one who rides a mount. The famous hadith states: Be with the Quran, for the Quran will come on the Day of Resurrection as an intercessor for its companion (the one who recites and acts upon it). ar-Rakib is the one who is in motion - moving forward on the path. The Quran says: And they will find what they did placed before them (18:49). ar-Rakib in Sufism is the one who rides on the spiritual journey, traveling through the stations of the path. The famous hadith of the Mi'raj describes how the Prophet Muhammad rode al-Buraq from Makkah to Jerusalem.
shades.hadith_ar: أُسۡرِىَ بِعَبۡدِهِ لَيۡلاًۭ مِّنَ ٱلۡمَسۡجِدِ ٱلۡحَرَامِ
shades.hadith_en: Exalted is He who took His Servant by night from al-Masjid al-Haram to al-Masjid al-Aqsa

shades.name_ar: الْمَرْكَبُ - مَا يُرۡكَبُ، الْوَسِيلَةُ مِنَ الْحَيَوَانِ أَوِ السَّفِينَةِ
shades.explanation: al-Markab (the mount, the vessel) in the Quran refers to that which is ridden - animals or ships. The famous hadith states: Allah's messenger used to ride a horse called al-Layl. The Quran mentions: It is He who enables you to travel on land and sea until, when you are in ships and they sail with them by a good wind (10:22). al-Markab in Sufism is the means by which the seeker reaches Allah. al-Qushayri describes the markab al-tariq (the mount of the path) - the spiritual means. The believer uses the markab of iman and good deeds to reach the dunya to the akhirah.
shades.hadith_ar: وَمِنۡ ءَايَـٰتِهِ ٱلۡجَوَارِ فِى ٱلۡبَحۡرِ كَٱلۡأَعۡلَـٰمِ
shades.hadith_en: And of His signs are the ships [sailing] in the sea, like mountains

shades.name_ar: التَّرْكِيبُ - ضَمُّ الْأَشْيَاءِ بَعْضِهَا إِلَىٰ بَعۡضٍ
shades.explanation: at-Tarkib (the compounding, the composition) refers to the act of putting things together. The famous hadith states: The believer is not stung twice from the same hole. The tarkib of the human body - the bones, flesh, organs, soul - is one of Allah's great signs. The Quran says: O mankind, if you are in doubt about the resurrection - then We have created you from dust, then from a sperm-drop, then from a clinging clot, then from a lump of flesh (22:5). The tarkib of the human body is so complex that no scientist can fully explain it. al-Ghazali in Ihya' discusses the tarkib of the soul and its connection to the body.
shades.hadith_ar: وَلَقَدۡ خَلَقۡنَا ٱلۡإِنسَـٰنَ مِن سُلَـٰلَةٍۢ مِّن طِينٍۢ
shades.hadith_en: And We have certainly created the human being from an extract of clay

meaning.en: To study, learn. The root denotes the act of studying or wearing out.
meaning.ar: الدَّرْسُ: قِرَاءَةُ الشَّيْءِ وَتَدَارُسُهُ، وَانْدِرَاسُهُ: انْدِرَامُهُ

lexical_analysis.ibn_faris: الدَّالُ وَالرَّاءُ وَالسِّينُ أَصْلٌ يَدُلُّ عَلَى مُحَاوَلَةِ الْعِلْمِ
lexical_analysis.al_raghib: الدَّرْسُ: تَكَرُّرُ الشَّيْءِ لِلْحِفْظِ. وَدَرَسَ: انْمَحَى

quran_examples.ar: وَلَقَدۡ عَهِدۡنَآ إِلَىٰٓ ءَادَمَ مِن قَبۡلُ فَنَسِىَ وَلَمۡ نَجِدۡ لَهُۥ عَزۡمًۭا
quran_examples.en: And We had already taken a covenant from Adam before, but he forgot, and We found not in him determination

quran_examples.ar: هُوَ ٱلَّذِى بَعَثَ فِى ٱلۡأُمِّيِّـۧنَ رَسُولًۭا مِّنۡهُمۡ
quran_examples.en: He it is who has sent among the unlettered a Messenger from themselves

hadith.ar: كَانَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ أَجْوَدَ النَّاسِ
hadith.en: The Messenger of Allah was the most generous of people

hadith.ar: طَلَبُ الْعِلْمِ فَرِيضَةٌ عَلَى كُلِّ مُسْلِمٍ
hadith.en: Seeking knowledge is an obligation upon every Muslim

shades.explanation: ad-Dars (the lesson, the study) in the Quran is the act of studying and learning. The Quran says: And We had already taken a covenant from Adam before, but he forgot, and We found not in him determination (20:115). ad-Dars is the act of memorizing and understanding. The Quran is the ultimate dars - the lesson from Allah to humanity. The famous hadith states: Allah's messenger used to meet Jibril every night in Ramadan to review the Quran. The dars of the Quran in Ramadan is a special act of worship.
shades.hadith_ar: كَانَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ أَجْوَدَ النَّاسِ
shades.hadith_en: The Messenger of Allah was the most generous of people

shades.explanation: ad-Darasa (the perusal, the repeated reading) in the Quran refers to the repeated study of knowledge. The famous hadith states: Read the Quran, for it will come on the Day of Resurrection as an intercessor for its companion. The darasa is the act of repeated study until the meaning is internalized. al-Ghazali in Ihya recommends daily darasa of the Quran with understanding.
shades.hadith_ar: اقْرَأُوا الْقُرْآنَ فَإِنَّهُ يَأْتِي يَوْمَ الْقِيَامَةِ شَفِيعًا لِأَصْحَابِهِ
shades.hadith_en: Read the Quran, for it will come on the Day of Resurrection as an intercessor for its companion

shades.explanation: al-Madrasa (the school) in Islamic civilization is the institution of learning. The famous hadith states: Seeking knowledge is an obligation upon every Muslim. The madrasa was developed in the Islamic world as a center for learning - both religious and secular sciences. al-Azhar was founded in 970 CE as a center for Islamic learning. The madrasa in Sufism is the spiritual school where the seeker learns the adab of the path. The Quran is the ultimate madrasa - the school of divine teaching.
shades.hadith_ar: طَلَبُ الْعِلْمِ فَرِيضَةٌ عَلَى كُلِّ مُسْلِمٍ
shades.hadith_en: Seeking knowledge is an obligation upon every Muslim

shades.name_ar: الْمُدَرِّسُ - مَنۡ يُعَلِّمُ، مَنۡ يَدۡرُسُ الطُّلَّابَ
shades.explanation: al-Mudarris (the teacher) in the Quran and hadith is one who teaches. The Quran says: He it is who has sent among the unlettered a Messenger from themselves, reciting to them His verses and purifying them and teaching them the Book and wisdom (62:2). The mudarris teaches through patience, wisdom, and beautiful preaching. al-Ghazali in Ihya describes the qualities of the mudarris - knowledge, piety, wisdom, and good character.
shades.hadith_ar: هُوَ ٱلَّذِى بَعَثَ فِى ٱلۡأُمِّيِّـۧنَ رَسُولًۭا مِّنۡهُمۡ
shades.hadith_en: He it is who has sent among the unlettered a Messenger from themselves

meaning.en: To be ruined. The root denotes ruin or destruction.

lexical_analysis.ibn_faris: الْخَاءُ وَالرَّاءُ وَالْبَاءُ أَصْلٌ يَدُلُّ عَلَى فَسَادٍ
lexical_analysis.al_raghib: الْخَرَابُ: ضِدُّ الْعُمْرَانِ. وَخَرِبَ: فَسَدَ

quran_examples.ar: وَمَنۡ أَظۡلَمُ مِمَّن مَّنَعَ مَسَـٰجِدَ ٱللَّهِ أَن يُذۡكَرَ فِيهَا ٱسۡمُهُۥ
quran_examples.en: And who is more unjust than he who forbids the remembrance of His name within His mosques
quran_examples.context: The warning against hindering worship in mosques

quran_examples.ar: لَا تَقُمۡ فِيهِ أَبَدًۭا لَّمَسۡجِدٌ أُسِّسَ عَلَى ٱلتَّقۡوَىٰ مِنۡ أَوَّلِ يَوۡمٍ
quran_examples.en: Do not stand [for prayer] within it ever - a mosque founded on righteousness from the first day

hadith.ar: إِذَا أَرَادَ اللَّهُ بِقَوْمٍ عَذَابًا أَصَابَ مَنْ فِيهِمُ الْعَذَابُ
hadith.en: When Allah intends evil for a people, He hastens the punishment

hadith.ar: مَنْ أَحَبَّ أَنْ يُبْسَطَ لَهُ فِي رِزْقِهِ فَلْيَصِلْ رَحِمَهُ
hadith.en: Whoever wishes that his provision be expanded for him, let him maintain ties of kinship

shades.explanation: al-Kharab (the ruin, the destruction) in the Quran is the opposite of al-'imran (the building). The Quran says: And they found therein a people who had made for themselves a town (people of the ditch) (85:6). al-Kharab is one of the consequences of sin - when the people disobey Allah, He may cause their cities to be in ruins. The famous hadith states: When Allah intends evil for a people, He hastens the punishment. The believer seeks al-'imran - building - and avoids al-kharab - destruction. al-Kharab in Sufism is the destruction of the ego - the death of the lower self before the death of the body.
shades.hadith_ar: وَتِلۡكَ ٱلۡقُرَىٰٓ أَهۡلَكۡنَـٰهُمۡ لَمَّا ظَلَمُواْ
shades.hadith_en: And those cities - We destroyed them when they wronged

shades.name_ar: الْمُخَرِّبُ - مَنۡ يُفۡسِدُ فِي ٱلۡأَرۡضِ، مُسَبِّبُ الْخَرَابِ
shades.explanation: al-Mukharib (the corruptor, the destroyer) in the Quran is one who causes corruption on earth. The Quran says: And do not desire corruption in the land; indeed Allah does not love the corrupters (28:77). al-Mukharib is one who spreads fasad (corruption) - whether through theft, killing, deceit, or any other harmful act. The famous hadith states: Whoever works in a harmful manner, Allah will harm him. al-Mukharib is the opposite of al-mu'min - the believer builds, the mukharib destroys. The hadith states: The Muslim is the one from whose tongue and hand other Muslims are safe.
shades.hadith_ar: وَلَا تَبۡغِ ٱلۡفَسَادَ فِى ٱلۡأَرۡضِ
shades.hadith_en: And do not desire corruption in the land

shades.explanation: al-Mukharaba (the corrupting, the warring) in the Quran is one of the major sins. The famous hadith states: The signs of the hypocrite are three: when he speaks he lies, when he promises he breaks, and when he is entrusted he betrays. al-Mukharaba of Allah and His Messenger is mentioned in 5:33: Indeed, the penalty for those who wage war against Allah and His Messenger and strive upon earth [to cause] corruption is... (the prescribed punishment). The believer avoids mukharaba - he is a friend of Allah, not an enemy.
shades.hadith_ar: إِنَّمَا جَزَٰٓؤُاْ ٱلَّذِينَ يُحَارِبُونَ ٱللَّهَ وَرَسُولَهُۥ وَيَسۡعَوۡنَ فِى ٱلۡأَرۡضِ فَسَادًا
shades.hadith_en: Indeed the penalty for those who wage war against Allah and His Messenger and strive upon earth to cause corruption

shades.explanation: al-Ikhlaf (the substitution, the succession) in the Quran refers to one thing replacing another. The famous hadith states: There is no kahin in this ummah, but there is the nazar (minor). The ikhlaf in the Quran includes: (1) one generation replacing another (10:13, 10:14, 46:31), (2) the success of one people over another (7:100, 43:31), (3) the replacement of night with day (25:62). The ikhlaf of Allah is just - He does not wrong His servants. The hadith states: Allah does not burden a soul beyond its capacity.
shades.hadith_ar: وَإِن تَتَوَلَّوۡا يَسۡتَبۡدِلۡ قَوۡمًا غَيۡرَكُمۡ
shades.hadith_en: And if you turn away, He will replace you with another people

meaning.en: To be pure. The root denotes purity, cleanliness, or selection.

lexical_analysis.ibn_faris: الصَّادُ وَالْفَاءُ وَالْوَاوُ أَصْلٌ يَدُلُّ عَلَى نَقَاءٍ
lexical_analysis.al_raghib: الصَّفْوُ: الْخُلُوصُ مِنَ الشَّوْبِ. وَصَفَا: خَلَصَ

quran_examples.ar: إِنَّمَا ٱلۡمُشۡرِكُونَ نَجَسٌۭ
quran_examples.en: Indeed the polytheists are najis (impure)

quran_examples.ar: إِنَّمَا يُرِيدُ ٱللَّهُ لِيُذۡهِبَ عَنكُمُ ٱلرِّجۡسَ أَهۡلَ ٱلۡبَيۡتِ وَيُطَهِّرَكُمۡ تَطۡهِيرًۭا
quran_examples.en: Allah intends only to remove from you the impurity [of sin], O people of the [Prophet's] household

hadith.ar: إِنَّ اللَّهَ لَا يَقْبَلُ صَلَاةَ أَحَدِكُمْ إِذَا أَحْدَثَ حَتَّى يَتَوَضَّأَ
hadith.en: Allah does not accept the prayer of one of you when he is in a state of impurity until he makes wudu

hadith.ar: إِنَّ اللَّهَ طَيِّبٌ لَا يَقْبَلُ إِلَّا طَيِّبًا
hadith.en: Indeed Allah is Tayyib (Good) and He only accepts what is good

shades.explanation: as-Safa (the purity) in the Quran is one of the most exalted spiritual concepts. The Quran says: Indeed the polytheists are najis (impure). The verse is referring to as-safa - the spiritual purity that the polytheists lack through their shirk. as-Safa is the state of the heart and the body when free from impurities. The famous hadith states: The key to Paradise is prayer (salah). The prophet said: Allah does not accept the prayer of one who is in a state of impurity. as-Safa has two dimensions: (1) as-safa al-maddi (physical purity - wudu and ghusl), (2) as-safa al-ma'nawi (spiritual purity - tawhid and ikhlas).
shades.hadith_ar: إِنَّمَا ٱلۡمُشۡرِكُونَ نَجَسٌۭ
shades.hadith_en: Indeed the polytheists are najis (impure)

shades.explanation: as-Safu (the clear, the pure) in the Quran refers to that which is pure and clear. The famous hadith states: The servant draws near to Me through nawafil (voluntary acts) until I love him. The closer the servant draws to Allah, the more pure he becomes. as-Safu is the state of the heart when free from all shirk (associating partners with Allah). al-Raghib distinguishes between as-safa and as-tahara: as-safa is internal purity, at-tahara is external. The famous hadith states: The Quran will come on the Day of Resurrection as an intercessor for its companion. The companion of the Quran is one who has achieved as-safu.
shades.hadith_ar: لَا يَقۡبَلُ ٱللَّهُ صَلَوٰةَ أَحَدِكُمۡ إِذَا أَحۡدَثَ حَتَّىٰ يَتَوَضَّأَ
shades.hadith_en: Allah does not accept the prayer of one who is in a state of impurity

shades.name_ar: الْمُصَفَّى - الَّذِي صُفِّيَ مِنَ الشَّوْبِ، الْخَالِصُ
shades.explanation: al-Musaffa (the purified, the clarified) in the Quran refers to that which has been purified. The famous hadith states: Whoever meets Allah with sins equal to the dust of the earth, He will purify him. The Quran says: So that He may purify you, O People of the House, and purify you thoroughly (33:33). The ahlu al-bayt are addressed here - they are purified from all impurities. The famous hadith states: The best of you are those who learn the Quran and teach it. The musaffa is one who has been purified through taqwa and obedience.
shades.hadith_ar: إِنَّمَا يُرِيدُ ٱللَّهُ لِيُذۡهِبَ عَنكُمُ ٱلرِّجۡسَ أَهۡلَ ٱلۡبَيۡتِ وَيُطَهِّرَكُمۡ تَطۡهِيرًۭا
shades.hadith_en: Allah intends only to remove from you the impurity [of sin], O people of the [Prophet's] household, and to purify you with [extensive] purification

shades.name_ar: التَّصْفِيَةُ - إِخۡرَاجُ الشَّوْبِ، تَنۡقِيَةُ الشَّيْءِ مِنَ الشَّوْبِ
shades.explanation: at-Tasfiyya (the purification) in the Quran refers to the act of purifying. The famous hadith states: Allah's messenger used to say: O Turner of hearts, keep my heart firm on Your religion. The heart is in constant need of tasfiyya - purification from doubts, desires, and sins. al-Ghazali in Ihya dedicates the entire book to the science of tasfiyya - the purification of the heart. The tasfiyya is achieved through: (1) dhikr (remembrance), (2) tawba (repentance), (3) mujahada (striving against the nafs), (4) suluk (the spiritual path). The tasfiyya is the path of the mu'min who seeks to draw near to Allah.
shades.hadith_ar: يَـٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ ٱتَّقُواْ ٱللَّهَ وَلۡتَنظُرۡ نَفۡسٌۭ مَّا قَدَّمَتۡ لِغَدٍۢ
shades.hadith_en: O you who believe, fear Allah and let every soul look to what it has put forward for tomorrow

meaning.en: To limit, restrict. The root denotes boundary, limit, or iron.

lexical_analysis.ibn_faris: الْحَاءُ وَالدَّالُّ أَصْلٌ يَدُلُّ عَلَى مَنْعٍ أَوْ حَدٍّ
lexical_analysis.al_raghib: الْحَدُّ: الْفَاصِلُ بَيْنَ الشَّيْئَيْنِ. وَالْحَدِيدُ: الْفِلَزُّ الصُّلْبُ

quran_examples.ar: تِلۡكَ حُدُودُ ٱللَّهِ فَلَا تَقۡرَبُوهَا
quran_examples.en: These are the limits of Allah, so do not approach them

quran_examples.ar: وَأَنزَلۡنَا ٱلۡحَدِيدَ فِيهِ بَأۡسٌۭ شَدِيدٌۭ وَمَنَـٰفِعُ لِلنَّاسِ
quran_examples.en: And We sent down iron, wherein is great military might and benefits for the people

hadith.ar: الْحَلَالُ بَيِّنٌ وَالْحَرَامُ بَيِّنٌ
hadith.en: The halal is clear and the haram is clear

hadith.ar: مَنْ أَنْكَرَ أَنْ يُنْكَرَ عَلَيْهِ
hadith.en: Whoever is forced (to do something), Allah has made it easy for him

shades.explanation: al-Hadd (the limit, the boundary) in the Quran is the divine or legal boundary. The Quran says: These are the limits [hudud] of Allah, so do not approach them (2:187). al-Hadd in the Quran is the line that distinguishes halal from haram, permissible from forbidden. The famous hadith states: The halal is clear and the haram is clear. Between them are doubtful matters about which many people do not know. al-Hadd has two dimensions: (1) al-hadd al-shar'i (the legal limit), (2) al-hadd al-'aqli (the rational limit). The believer respects the hudud of Allah and does not approach them.
shades.hadith_ar: تِلۡكَ حُدُودُ ٱللَّهِ فَلَا تَقۡرَبُوهَا
shades.hadith_en: These are the limits of Allah, so do not approach them

shades.explanation: al-Hudud (the limits) in the Quran refers to the divine laws that govern the believer's life. The famous hadith states: Allah has prescribed for every son of Adam his share of zina which he commits inevitably. The hudud are the boundaries set by Allah for the welfare of His servants. The Quran says: And those who do not invoke besides Allah another deity or kill the soul which Allah has forbidden [except by right] nor commit illegal sexual intercourse (25:68). The believer accepts the hudud and submits to them - this is the meaning of Islam.
shades.hadith_ar: تِلۡكَ حُدُودُ ٱللَّهِ ۚ وَمَن يُطِعِ ٱللَّهَ وَرَسُولَهُۥ يُدۡخِلۡهُ جَنَّـٰتٍۢ
shades.hadith_en: These are the limits of Allah. And whoever obeys Allah and His Messenger will be admitted to gardens

shades.name_en: Hadd Allah - The Limit of Allah
shades.name_ar: حَدُّ ٱللَّهِ - الشَّرۡعُ الَّذِي شَرَعَهُ اللَّهُ لِعِبَادِهِ
shades.explanation: Hadd Allah (the limit of Allah) is the divine law that the believer must respect. The Quran says: And let those who would not be married act to guard their private parts. And let them not reveal their adornment except that which [necessarily] appears thereof (24:30-31). The hadd of Allah in marriage is the command to marry and not approach zina. The famous hadith states: O young men, whoever among you can afford to marry, let him do so. The hadd of Allah is for our benefit - it protects us, guides us, and brings us closer to Him.
shades.hadith_ar: يَـٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ لَا تُحِلُّواْ شَعَـٰٓئِرَ ٱللَّهِ
shades.hadith_en: O you who believe, do not violate the rites of Allah

shades.explanation: al-Hadid (the iron) in the Quran is one of the elements created by Allah. The famous hadith states: Allah sent down four blessings from the sky: iron, fire, water, and salt. The Quran says: And We sent down iron, wherein is great military might and benefits for the people (57:25). al-Hadid is a metaphor for strength and firmness. Surah al-Hadid (57) is named after this root. The hadid of the heart is the firm resolve. The famous hadith states: The mu'min is like iron - it can be bent but it is firm. al-Hadid in Sufism represents the firm intention.
shades.hadith_ar: وَأَنزَلۡنَا ٱلۡحَدِيدَ فِيهِ بَأۡسٌۭ شَدِيدٌۭ وَمَنَـٰفِعُ لِلنَّاسِ
shades.hadith_en: And We sent down iron, wherein is great military might and benefits for the people

meaning.en: To have mercy. The root denotes mercy, compassion, or the womb.

lexical_analysis.ibn_faris: الرَّاءُ وَالْحَاءُ وَالْمِيمُ أَصْلٌ يَدُلُّ عَلَى رِفْقٍ
lexical_analysis.al_raghib: الرَّحْمَةُ: رِفْقُ الْإِنْعَامِ. وَالرَّحِمُ: الْقَرَابَةُ

quran_examples.ar: بِسۡمِ ٱللَّهِ ٱلرَّحۡمَـٰنِ ٱلرَّحِيمِ
quran_examples.en: In the name of Allah, the Most Merciful, the Most Compassionate

quran_examples.ar: وَرَحۡمَتِى وَسِعَتۡ كُلَّ شَىۡءٍۢ
quran_examples.en: And My mercy encompasses all things

hadith.ar: إِنَّ الرَّحْمَ شَجْنَةٌ مِنَ الرَّحْمَنِ
hadith.en: Ar-rahm is a portion of ar-Rahman

hadith.ar: إِنَّ اللَّهَ رَفِيقٌ يُحِبُّ الرِّفْقَ فِي الْأَمْرِ كُلِّهِ
hadith.en: Indeed Allah is gentle and He loves gentleness in all matters

shades.explanation: ar-Rahma (the mercy, the compassion) in the Quran is one of the most comprehensive divine attributes. The Quran says: And My mercy encompasses all things (7:156). ar-Rahma is the divine attribute of giving, forgiving, and comforting. Allah is ar-Rahman (the Most Merciful) and ar-Rahim (the Most Compassionate). ar-Rahma in the Quran has three levels: (1) ar-rahmat al-'amma (general mercy - for all creation), (2) ar-rahmat al-khassa (special mercy - for the believers), (3) ar-rahmat al-'uzma (the greatest mercy - Paradise). The hadith Qudsi states: My mercy prevails over My wrath.
shades.hadith_ar: وَرَحۡمَتِى وَسِعَتۡ كُلَّ شَىۡءٍۢ
shades.hadith_en: And My mercy encompasses all things

shades.explanation: ar-Rahman (the Most Merciful) is one of the most mentioned Names of Allah in the Quran. ar-Rahman is the One whose mercy is vast and comprehensive - it encompasses all of creation. The Quran opens with: In the name of Allah, the Most Merciful, the Most Compassionate (1:1). ar-Rahman is the One who has decreed mercy upon Himself (6:12, 6:54). The famous hadith states: Allah is more merciful to His servant than a mother to her child. The mercy of Allah is the source of all goodness in the universe.
shades.hadith_ar: بِسۡمِ ٱللَّهِ ٱلرَّحۡمَـٰنِ ٱلرَّحِيمِ
shades.hadith_en: In the name of Allah, the Most Merciful, the Most Compassionate

shades.explanation: ar-Rahim (the Most Compassionate) is paired with ar-Rahman in the basmalah. ar-Rahim is the One whose mercy is renewed for His servants constantly. The famous hadith states: Allah has one hundred parts of mercy, of which He sent down one part upon the jinn and mankind and the beasts and the cattle, and by it they show kindness to one another. The mercy of Allah is the source of all mercy - mothers' mercy, fathers' mercy, the mercy of the merciful, all flow from the mercy of ar-Rahim.
shades.hadith_ar: كَتَبَ رَبُّكُمۡ عَلَىٰ نَفۡسِهِ ٱلرَّحۡمَةَ
shades.hadith_en: Your Lord has decreed upon Himself mercy

shades.explanation: ar-Rahm (the womb, the kinship) in the Quran refers to the ties of kinship. The Quran says: And those who break the covenant of Allah after contracting it and sever that which Allah has ordered to be joined (2:27). The cutting of ar-rahm is one of the major sins. The famous hadith states: Ar-rahm is a portion of ar-Rahman. Whoever connects it, Allah connects him. Whoever severs it, Allah severs him. The ar-rahm of the believer is the most important worldly connection - it is the source of mercy, blessings, and barakah.
shades.hadith_ar: إِنَّ الرَّحِمَ شَجْنَةٌ مِنَ الرَّحْمَنِ
shades.hadith_en: Ar-rahm is a portion of ar-Rahman

meaning.en: To reckon, count. The root denotes reckoning, calculation, or sufficient.

lexical_analysis.ibn_faris: الْحَاءُ وَالسِّينُ وَالْبَاءُ أَصْلٌ يَدُلُّ عَلَى عَدٍّ أَوْ كِفَايَةٍ
lexical_analysis.al_raghib: الْحِسَابُ: الْعَدُّ. وَالْحَسِيبُ: الَّذِي يُحَاسِبُ

quran_examples.ar: فَنَادَتۡهُ ٱلۡمَلَـٰٓئِكَةُ وَهُوَ قَآئِمٌۭ يُصَلِّى فِى ٱلۡمِحۡرَابِ
quran_examples.en: Then the angels called him while he was standing in prayer in the chamber

quran_examples.ar: إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ كَانَ عَلَىٰ كُلِّ شَىۡءٍ حَسِيبًا
quran_examples.en: Indeed Allah is ever, over all things, a Reckoner
quran_examples.context: Allah as the Reckoner over all things

hadith.ar: الْكَيِّسُ مَنْ دَانَ نَفْسَهُ وَعَمِلَ لِمَا بَعْدَ الْمَوْتِ
hadith.en: The wise one is he who takes account of himself and works for what comes after death

hadith.ar: لَا تَحَاسَبُوا فَإِنَّ الْمُحَاسَبَةَ تَدْعُو إِلَى الْبَغْضَاءِ
hadith.en: Do not hold grudges for it leads to hatred

shades.explanation: al-Hisab (the reckoning, the account) in the Quran is one of the most fundamental concepts of the Day of Judgment. The Quran says: And they will find what they did placed before them (18:49). al-Hisab is the exact recompense for every deed. The famous hadith states: The servant will be brought on the Day of Resurrection and he will be questioned about everything. al-Hisab in the Quran has levels: (1) al-hisab al-yasir (the easy reckoning - the mu'minin), (2) al-hisab al-'aziz (the difficult reckoning - the kuffar). The believer prepares for al-hisab through taqwa and good deeds.
shades.hadith_ar: يَـٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلۡإِنسَـٰنُ إِنَّكَ كَادِحٌ إِلَىٰ رَبِّكَ كَدۡحًۭا فَمُلَـٰقِيهِ
shades.hadith_en: O mankind, indeed you are laboring toward your Lord with [great] exertion and will meet it

shades.explanation: al-Hasib (the Reckoner) is one of the Names of Allah - the One who takes account of His servants. The Quran says: Allah is sufficient as a Reckoner [Hasib] (4:6, 4:86, 33:39). al-Hasib is the One who knows the deeds of every servant and rewards them accordingly. The famous hadith states: Allah's messenger said to a man: Have taqwa of Allah wherever you are. al-Hasib sees the deeds and rewards them. The believer knows that al-Hasib is watching - he is conscious of Allah in all his actions.
shades.hadith_ar: وَكَفَىٰ بِٱللَّهِ حَسِيبًۭا
shades.hadith_en: And sufficient is Allah as a Reckoner

shades.explanation: al-Hisbah (the sufficient, the adequate) in the Quran refers to the divine sufficiency. The Quran says: And Allah is sufficient for the believers in the matter of reckoning (4:86). al-Hisbah is the perfect and complete sufficiency - Allah takes care of the believer in all his affairs. The famous hadith states: Whoever makes the hereafter his goal, Allah will enrich him and the world will come to him. al-Hisbah is the result of tawakkul (reliance on Allah). The believer trusts in al-Hisbah and relies on Allah for all his needs.
shades.hadith_ar: وَمَن يَتَوَكَّلۡ عَلَى ٱللَّهِ فَهُوَ حَسۡبُهُۥٓ
shades.hadith_en: And whoever relies upon Allah - then He is sufficient for him

shades.explanation: al-Ihsab (the calculation, the estimation) in the Quran refers to the careful counting. The Quran says: And the fruit of the two gardens will be near at hand (55:54). The Quran mentions: And We have already created man and know what his nafs whispers to him, and We are closer to him than his jugular vein (50:16). al-Ihsab of Allah is perfect - He knows every leaf that falls, every breath, every deed. The famous hadith states: Allah's messenger said: There is no Muslim who plants a tree or sows a field, and then a bird, or person, or animal eats from it, except that it is sadaqa for him. The believer trusts in al-Ihsab of Allah - that all is counted and rewarded.
shades.hadith_ar: وَإِن تَعُدُّواْ نِعۡمَتَ ٱللَّهِ لَا تُحۡصُوهَآ
shades.hadith_en: And if you should count the favor of Allah, you could not enumerate them

meaning.en: To beget, give birth. The root denotes offspring, child, or generation.

lexical_analysis.ibn_faris: الْوَاوُ وَاللَّامُ وَالدَّالُ أَصْلٌ يَدُلُّ عَلَى نَسْلٍ
lexical_analysis.al_raghib: الْوَلَدُ: الْمَوْلُودُ. وَوَلَدَ: أَنْجَبَ

quran_examples.ar: فَٱنطَلَقَا حَتَّىٰٓ إِذَا لَقِيَا غُلَـٰمًۭا فَقَتَلَهُۥ
quran_examples.en: So they set out, until when they met a boy, he struck him and killed him
quran_examples.context: Musa and Khidr with the boy

quran_examples.ar: فَأَشَارَتۡ إِلَيۡهِۖ قَالُواْ كَيۡفَ نُكَلِّمُ مَن كَانَ فِى ٱلۡمَهۡدِ صَبِيًّۭا
quran_examples.en: She pointed to him. They said: How can we speak to one who is a child in the cradle

hadith.ar: كُلُّ مَوْلُودٍ يُولَدُ عَلَى الْفِطْرَةِ
hadith.en: Every newborn is born upon the fitrah

hadith.ar: مَنْ قَبَّلَ وَلَدَهُ كَانَ لَهُ حِجَابًا مِنَ النَّارِ
hadith.en: Whoever kisses his child, it is a protection for him from Hellfire

shades.name_ar: الْوَلَدُ - الِابْنُ الصَّغِيرُ، الذُّكُورُ مِنَ الْأَوْلَادِ
shades.explanation: al-Walad (the boy, the son) in the Quran refers to the young male offspring. The Quran mentions: And they found therein a wall that wanted to fall down (18:77). al-Walad in the Quran is also used metaphorically for the spiritual child - the one who has been born into Islam. The famous hadith states: None of you truly believes until he loves for his brother what he loves for himself. The walad in Sufism is the spiritual son - the one who has been trained in the path by a murshid (spiritual guide). The walad is one of the most beloved of Allah's creations.
shades.hadith_ar: كُلُّ مَوۡلُودٍۢ يُولَدُ عَلَى ٱلۡفِطۡرَةِ
shades.hadith_en: Every newborn is born upon the fitrah

shades.name_ar: الْوِلَادَةُ - الْإِنْجَابُ، خُرُوجُ الْوَلَدِ مِنَ الْبَطْنِ
shades.explanation: al-Wiladah (the birth) in the Quran refers to the act of being born. The Quran says: And the earth's crust was split open and sprouted forth. It brought forth its fruit fully. And Allah says: Indeed I will create a human being from clay. So when I have proportioned him and breathed into him of My [created] soul (15:28-29). The wiladah of Adam is the first creation of the human being. The famous hadith states: Allah created Adam in His own form. The wiladah of every child is a blessing from Allah. The believer thanks Allah for the wiladah of his children and raises them in Islam.
shades.hadith_ar: حَدَّثَنِي جِبْرِيلُ أَنَّ أَوَّلَ أَهْلِ الْجَنَّةِ دُخُولًا الْفُقَرَاءُ
shades.hadith_en: Jibril narrated to me that the first of the people of Paradise to enter are the poor

shades.explanation: al-Walid (the boy, the child) in the Quran refers to a young child. The Quran says: And they found therein a wall that wanted to fall down, and he straightened it (18:77). The walid in the Quran is used for the young Musa, the young Maryam, and the young Yahya. The famous hadith states: Allah's messenger said: Honor your children and treat them with kindness. The walid is a trust from Allah - the believer raises the walid in Islam and teaches them the Quran. The walid in Sufism is the spiritual child who has been born again into the path of Allah.
shades.hadith_ar: أَكْرِمُوا أَوْلَادَكُمْ وَأَحْسِنُوا أَدَبَهُمْ
shades.hadith_en: Honor your children and improve their manners

shades.name_ar: وَلَدُ الزِّنَا - الْوَلَدُ الَّذِي وُلِدَ مِنْ عَلاقَةٍ غَيْرِ شَرۡعِيَّةٍ
shades.explanation: Walad al-Haram (the illegitimate child) is the child born from a haram relationship. The famous hadith states: The child belongs to the marriage bed (al-firash), and the fornicator gets the stone. The walad al-haram in Islamic law has specific rulings: (1) he is not attributed to the fornicator, (2) he is attributed to the mother's lineage, (3) he cannot inherit from the fornicator. The Quran emphasizes the importance of lawful marriage and warns against zina. The walad al-halal is the child born in a valid marriage - this is the only way to have a legitimate walad.
shades.hadith_ar: الْوَلَدُ لِلْفِرَاشِ وَلِلْعَاهِرِ الْحَجَرُ
shades.hadith_en: The child belongs to the marriage bed, and the fornicator gets the stone

meaning.en: To judge, reward. The root denotes religion, judgment, or debt.

lexical_analysis.ibn_faris: الدَّالُ وَالْيَاءُ وَالنُّونُ أَصْلٌ يَدُلُّ عَلَى حُكْمٍ أَوْ جَزَاءٍ
lexical_analysis.al_raghib: الدِّينُ: الْمِلَّةُ الْمُسْتَقِيمَةُ. وَالْيَوْمُ الدِّينِ: يَوْمُ الْجَزَاءِ

quran_examples.ar: مَـٰلِكِ يَوۡمِ ٱلدِّينِ
quran_examples.en: Master of the Day of Judgment

quran_examples.ar: إِنَّ الدِّينَ عِندَ اللَّهِ الْإِسْلَامُ
quran_examples.en: Indeed, the religion in the sight of Allah is Islam
quran_examples.context: The religion in the sight of Allah

hadith.ar: الشَّهِيدُ يُغْفَرُ لَهُ كُلُّ شَيْءٍ إِلَّا الدَّيْنَ
hadith.en: The martyr's sins are forgiven except for debt

hadith.ar: مَنْ أَخَذَ أَمْوَالَ النَّاسِ يُرِيدُ أَدَاءَهَا أَدَّى اللَّهُ عَنْهُ
hadith.en: Whoever takes people's money intending to repay it, Allah will repay it for him

shades.explanation: ad-Din (the religion, the judgment) in the Quran is one of the most comprehensive concepts. The Quran says: Indeed, the religion in the sight of Allah is Islam (3:19). ad-Din in the Quran has multiple meanings: (1) ad-din al-qayyim (the right religion), (2) ad-din al-khalis (the pure religion), (3) ad-din al-malik (the religion of the king), (4) yawm al-din (the day of judgment). The famous hadith states: None of you truly believes until his desires follow what I have brought. ad-Din is the submission to Allah in all aspects of life - aqida (belief), sharia (law), and akhlaq (character).
shades.hadith_ar: إِنَّ الدِّينَ عِندَ اللَّهِ الْإِسْلَامُ
shades.hadith_en: Indeed, the religion in the sight of Allah is Islam

shades.name_ar: الدَّيْنُ - مَا يَلۡزَمُ أَدَاؤُهُ، الْحَقُّ الْمَالِيُّ
shades.explanation: ad-Dayn (the debt) in the Quran refers to a financial obligation. The Quran says: Indeed Allah commands you to render trusts to whom they are due (4:58). ad-Dayn in Islamic jurisprudence is a binding obligation - one that must be fulfilled. The famous hadith states: The martyr's sins are forgiven except for debt. The dayn in Islam is a serious matter - the believer must fulfill his dayn in this world, because on the Day of Judgment the dayn will be the first thing he is questioned about. The mukhalit (the one who settles debt) is praised in the hadith.
shades.hadith_ar: الشَّهِيدُ يُغْفَرُ لَهُ كُلُّ شَيْءٍ إِلَّا الدَّيْنَ
shades.hadith_en: The martyr's sins are forgiven except for debt

shades.name_en: Yawm al-Din - The Day of Judgment
shades.explanation: Yawm al-Din (the Day of Judgment) is one of the most mentioned events in the Quran. The first surah of the Quran ends with: The path of those upon whom You have bestowed favor, not of those who have evoked [Your] anger or of those who are astray (1:7). The Quran says: The Day of Judgment is appointed (51:5-6). Yawm al-Din is the day when every soul will be recompensed for its deeds. The famous hadith states: The believer will be brought near his Lord and asked about his deeds. The Day of Judgment is the greatest day - the day when truth is distinguished from falsehood.
shades.hadith_ar: مَالِكِ يَوۡمِ الدِّينِ
shades.hadith_en: Master of the Day of Judgment

shades.explanation: ad-Dayyan (the Avenger, the Compensator) is one of the Names of Allah mentioned in the hadith of the Names. ad-Dayyan is the One who recompenses His servants for their deeds - rewarding the good and punishing the evil. The famous hadith states: Allah has ninety-nine Names, one hundred minus one, and whoever enumerates them will enter Paradise. Among the Names is al-Dayyan. al-Dayyan sees every deed and rewards it appropriately. The believer trusts in al-Dayyan and knows that no deed is wasted - good is rewarded with good, and evil is recompensed.
shades.hadith_ar: إِنَّ كُلَّ نَفۡسٍۢ لَّمَّا عَلَيۡهَا حَافِظٌ
shades.hadith_en: Indeed, [for] every soul there is a guardian over it

meaning.en: To be youthful. The root denotes youth, pouring, or resemblance.

lexical_analysis.ibn_faris: الشِّينُ وَالْبَاءُ أَصْلٌ يَدُلُّ عَلَى امْتِلَاءٍ أَوْ تَشَابُهٍ
lexical_analysis.al_raghib: الشَّبَابُ: حَالَةُ الشَّبَابِ. وَشَبَّ: صَبَّ

quran_examples.ar: هُوَ ٱلَّذِىٓ أَنزَلَ عَلَيۡكَ ٱلۡكِتَـٰبَ مِنۡهُ ءَايَـٰتٌۭ مُّحۡكَمَـٰتٌ هُنَّ أُمُّ ٱلۡكِتَـٰبِ
quran_examples.en: It is He who has sent down to you the Book; in it are verses that are precise - they are the foundation of the Book

quran_examples.ar: وَيُسۡقَوۡنَ فِيهَا كَأۡسًۭا كَانَ مِزَاجُهَا زَنجَبِيلًا
quran_examples.en: And they will be given to drink a cup whose mixture is of ginger

hadith.ar: اغْتَنِمْ خَمْسًا قَبْلَ خَمْسٍ
hadith.en: Take advantage of five before five

hadith.ar: مَنْ تَشَبَّهَ بِقَوْمٍ فَهُوَ مِنْهُمْ
hadith.en: Whoever resembles a people is one of them

shades.name_ar: الشَّبَابُ - حَالَةُ الِاسْتِوَاءِ بَيْنَ الطُّفُولَةِ وَالْكُهُولَةِ
shades.explanation: as-Shabab (the youth) in the Quran is the time between childhood and old age. The famous hadith states: Take advantage of five before five: your youth before your old age. as-Shabab is the prime time of life - when the body is strong and the mind is sharp. The shabab in Sufism is the youth of the heart - the freshness of iman. The Quran praises those who use their shabab in obedience to Allah.
shades.hadith_ar: اغْتَنِمْ خَمْسًا قَبْلَ خَمْسٍ: شَبَابَكَ قَبْلَ هَرَمِكَ
shades.hadith_en: Take advantage of five before five: your youth before your old age

shades.explanation: ash-Shab (the pouring) refers to mixing or pouring liquids. The Quran mentions: And they will be given to drink a cup whose mixture is of ginger (76:17). The famous hadith states: Whoever drinks wine, his salah will not be accepted for forty days. The shab in the Quran is the mixing of the heavenly wine with the scents of Paradise. The believer abstains from all intoxicants - the drinking of wine is haram.
shades.hadith_ar: مَنْ شَرِبَ الْخَمْرَ لَمْ تُقْبَلْ لَهُ صَلَاةٌ أَرْبَعِينَ يَوْمًا
shades.hadith_en: Whoever drinks wine, his prayer will not be accepted for forty days

shades.name_ar: الْمُتَشَابِهُ - مَا اشْتَبَهَ مَعَ غَيْرِهِ فِي الصُّورَةِ
shades.explanation: al-Mutashabih (the ambiguous) in the Quran refers to verses that have multiple meanings. The Quran says: He it is who has sent down to you the Book; in it are verses that are precise - they are the foundation of the Book - and others that are ambiguous (3:7). al-Mutashabih is for those who have knowledge. The famous hadith states: The Quran was revealed in seven modes. The muhkam and mutashabih are both part of the Quran - the believer accepts them both without asking how. al-Razi in his tafsir extensively discusses the muhkam and mutashabih.
shades.hadith_ar: هُوَ ٱلَّذِىٓ أَنزَلَ عَلَيۡكَ ٱلۡكِتَـٰبَ مِنۡهُ ءَايَـٰتٌۭ مُّحۡكَمَـٰتٌ هُنَّ أُمُّ ٱلۡكِتَـٰبِ وَأُخَرُ مُتَشَـٰبِهَـٰتٌۭ
shades.hadith_en: It is He who has sent down to you the Book; in it are verses that are precise - they are the foundation of the Book

shades.explanation: at-Tashabbuh (the resemblance) in the Quran refers to becoming similar to something. The famous hadith states: Whoever resembles a people is one of them. The believer avoids tashabbuh with the kuffar or with the fasiqin. The Quran says: And do not incline toward those who have wronged, lest you be touched by the Fire (11:113). The tashabbuh is allowed with the awliya - the friends of Allah - and the siddiqin - the truthful. al-Ghazali in Ihya discusses the importance of tashabbuh with the righteous.
shades.hadith_ar: مَنْ تَشَبَّهَ بِقَوْمٍ فَهُوَ مِنْهُمْ
shades.hadith_en: Whoever resembles a people is one of them

meaning.en: To be a brother. The root denotes brotherhood or sibling.
meaning.ar: الْأَخُ: الذُّكُورُ مِنَ الْإِخْوَةِ، وَالْإِخَاءُ: الْأُخُوَّةُ

lexical_analysis.ibn_faris: الْهَمْزَةُ وَالْخَاءُ وَالْوَاوُ أَصْلٌ يَدُلُّ عَلَى أَخُوَّةٍ
lexical_analysis.al_raghib: الْأَخُ: الذَّكَرُ مِنَ الْإِخْوَةِ. وَأَخَوَ: شَارَكَ فِي الْأُخُوَّةِ

quran_examples.ar: إِنَّمَا ٱلۡمُؤۡمِنُونَ إِخۡوَةٌۭ فَأَصۡلِحُواْ بَيۡنَ أَخَوَيۡكُمۡ
quran_examples.en: The believers are but brothers, so make settlement between your brothers

quran_examples.ar: لَقَدۡ كَانَ فِى يُوسُفَ وَإِخۡوَتِهِۦٓ ءَايَـٰتٌۭ لِّلسَّآئِلِينَ
quran_examples.en: There were certainly in Joseph and his brothers signs for those who ask
quran_examples.context: The story of Yusuf and his brothers

hadith.ar: الْمُسْلِمُ أَخُو الْمُسْلِمِ لَا يَظْلِمُهُ وَلَا يَخْذُلُهُ
hadith.en: The Muslim is the brother of the Muslim; he does not oppress him nor abandon him

hadith.ar: إِنَّمَا مَثَلُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ فِي تَوَادِّهِمْ وَتَرَاحُمِهِمْ
hadith.en: The believers in their mutual love, mercy, and compassion are like a single body

shades.name_ar: الْأَخُ - الذُّكُورُ مِنْ بَنِي الْأَبَوَيْنِ أَوْ أَحَدِهِمَا
shades.explanation: al-Akh (the brother) in the Quran refers to the male sibling. The Quran mentions numerous brotherly relationships: Musa and Harun (19:53, 25:35, 26:13, 27:35, 37:114, 43:30, 44:30, 46:12, 46:15), Yusuf and his brothers (12:8-100), Yaqub and his sons (12:7-100), Nuh and his son (71:21-28). al-Akh has both literal and metaphorical meanings: (1) the literal brother (sibling by blood), (2) the spiritual brother (companion in iman), (3) the religious brother (the fellow believer). The famous hadith states: The believer is the brother of the believer.
shades.hadith_ar: إِنَّمَا ٱلۡمُؤۡمِنُونَ إِخۡوَةٌۭ
shades.hadith_en: The believers are but brothers

shades.explanation: al-Ikha' (the brotherhood) in the Quran is the bond between the believers. The Quran says: Indeed the believers are but brothers, so make settlement between your brothers (49:10). al-Ikha' is one of the highest Islamic values - the Prophet established the mu'akhat (brotherhood) between the Muhajirun and the Ansar. The famous hadith states: The example of the believers in their mutual love, mercy, and compassion is like a single body - when one part complains, the rest rallies. al-Ikha' in Sufism is the deep spiritual connection between the awliya - the friends of Allah.
shades.hadith_ar: مَثَلُ ٱلۡمُؤۡمِنِينَ فِى تَوَادِّهِمۡ وَتَرَاحُمِهِمۡ كَمَثَلِ ٱلۡجَسَدِ
shades.hadith_en: The example of the believers in their mutual love, mercy, and compassion is like a single body

shades.name_en: Akhu al-Islam - The Brother in Islam
shades.name_ar: أَخُو الْإِسْلَامِ - الْمُؤْمِنُ الَّذِي تَرْبِطُكَ بِهِ صِلَةُ الدِّينِ
shades.explanation: Akhu al-Islam (the brother in Islam) is the fellow Muslim. The famous hadith states: None of you truly believes until he loves for his brother what he loves for himself. The akhu al-islam has rights over the believer: (1) to greet him with salam, (2) to visit him when sick, (3) to attend his funeral, (4) to give him advice, (5) to defend his honor. The akhu al-islam is one of the greatest blessings - through him the believer finds support, friendship, and brotherhood in the path of Allah.
shades.hadith_ar: لَا يُؤْمِنُ أَحَدُكُمْ حَتَّى يُحِبَّ لِأَخِيهِ مَا يُحِبُّ لِنَفْسِهِ
shades.hadith_en: None of you truly believes until he loves for his brother what he loves for himself

shades.name_ar: الْأَخُ الْقَرِيبُ - الْأَخُ الشَّقِيقُ، أَخُو الْأَبَوَيْنِ
shades.explanation: Akh al-Karib (the close brother) is the brother by both parents (al-akh al-shqiq). The famous hadith states: The closest people to Allah on the Day of Resurrection will be those who have the most taqwa. The akh al-karib in Islamic law is one of the closest blood relatives - he shares in inheritance, has rights of visitation, and is obligated to support his brother. The Quran mentions Yusuf and his brothers: They said: By Allah, Allah has preferred you over us, and we were certainly sinners (12:91). The akh al-karib is a test of iman - how one treats one's own blood is the measure of one's character.
shades.hadith_ar: إِذْ قَالُوا لِيُوسُفُ وَأَخُوهُ أَحَبُّ إِلَىٰ أَبِينَا مِنَّا
shades.hadith_en: When they said: Indeed, Joseph and his brother are more beloved to our father than we

meaning.en: Night. The root denotes night or nighttime.

lexical_analysis.ibn_faris: اللَّامُ وَالْيَاءُ وَاللَّامُ أَصْلٌ يَدُلُّ عَلَى ظَلَامٍ
lexical_analysis.al_raghib: اللَّيْلُ: مَا بَيْنَ الْغُرُوبِ وَالْفَجْرِ

quran_examples.ar: إِنَّآ أَنزَلۡنَـٰهُ فِى لَيۡلَةِ ٱلۡقَدۡرِ
quran_examples.en: Indeed, We sent it down during the Night of Decree

quran_examples.ar: ٱلَّذِينَ يُنفِقُونَ أَمۡوَٰلَهُم بِٱلَّيۡلِ وَٱلنَّهَارِ سِرًّۭا وَعَلَانِيَةًۭ
quran_examples.en: Those who spend their wealth [in Allah's way] by night and by day, secretly and publicly
quran_examples.context: The spending in charity night and day

hadith.ar: أَحَبُّ الصَّلَاةِ إِلَى اللَّهِ صَلَاةُ دَاوُودَ
hadith.en: The most beloved of prayers to Allah is the prayer of Dawud

hadith.ar: مَنْ قَامَ لَيْلَةَ الْقَدْرِ إِيمَانًا وَاحْتِسَابًا غُفِرَ لَهُ مَا تَقَدَّمَ مِنْ ذَنْبِهِ
hadith.en: Whoever stands [in prayer] during the Night of Decree out of iman and hoping for reward, his past sins will be forgiven

shades.name_ar: اللَّيْلُ - ضِدُّ النَّهَارِ، الظَّلَامُ الَّذِي يُغَشِّي الْأَرْضَ
shades.explanation: al-Layl (the night) in the Quran is one of the most magnificent signs. The Quran says: And We have made the night a covering (78:10). al-Layl in the Quran is: the time of rest and quiet, the time of tahajjud (night prayer), the time of divine revelation (97:1-5), the time of mercy (3:190-194). The famous hadith states: The most beloved of prayers to Allah is the prayer of Dawud. al-Layl is when the hearts find peace through dhikr and worship.
shades.hadith_ar: وَمِنَ ٱلَّيۡلِ فَتَهَجَّدۡ بِهِۦ نَافِلَةًۭ لَّكَ
shades.hadith_en: And from [part of] the night, pray with it as additional [worship] for you

shades.name_en: Laylat al-Qadr - The Night of Decree
shades.name_ar: لَيْلَةُ الْقَدْرِ - اللَّيْلَةُ الَّتِي تَضَاعِفُ فِيهَا الْحَسَنَاتُ
shades.explanation: Laylat al-Qadr (the Night of Decree) is one of the most blessed nights in Islam. The Quran says: Indeed, We sent it down during the Night of Decree. And what can make you know what the Night of Decree is? The Night of Decree is better than a thousand months (97:1-3). The famous hadith states: Whoever stands in prayer during the Night of Decree out of iman and hoping for reward, his past sins will be forgiven. The believer seeks it through worship and dhikr in the last ten nights of Ramadan.
shades.hadith_ar: لَيۡلَةُ ٱلۡقَدۡرِ خَيۡرٌۭ مِّنۡ أَلۡفِ شَهۡرٍۢ
shades.hadith_en: The Night of Decree is better than a thousand months

shades.name_ar: اللَّيْلِيُّ - مَا يَخُصُّ اللَّيْلَ، الْقَائِمُ بِاللَّيْلِ
shades.explanation: al-Layliyy (the nocturnal one) refers to one who is active at night. The Quran says: They used to sleep but little of the night (51:17). The layliyy is the one who uses the night for worship - the qiyam al-layl, the dhikr, the dua. The Quran praises the mutahajjidin (those who stand in prayer at night).
shades.hadith_ar: إِنَّ ٱلۡمُتَّقِينَ فِى جَنَّـٰتٍۢ وَنَهَرٍۢ
shades.hadith_en: Indeed the righteous will be among gardens and rivers

shades.explanation: at-Talayyul (the becoming night) refers to the arrival or progression of night. The famous hadith states: When night falls, keep your children close. The hadith Qudsi states: Allah descends to the lowest heaven during the last third of the night and says: Who is calling upon Me that I may answer him? The believer makes the most of at-talayyul - the special hours of divine mercy and blessing.
shades.hadith_ar: يَنزِلُ رَبُّنَا تَبَارَكَ وَتَعَالَى كُلَّ لَيْلَةٍ إِلَى السَّمَاءِ الدُّنْيَا
shades.hadith_en: Our Lord descends to the lowest heaven every night

meaning.en: To glorify, swim. The root denotes glorification, swimming, or floating.

lexical_analysis.ibn_faris: السِّينُ وَالْبَاءُ وَالْحَاءُ أَصْلٌ يَدُلُّ عَلَى عَوْمٍ أَوْ تَنْزِيهٍ
lexical_analysis.al_raghib: سَبَّحَ: نَزَّهَ. وَسَبَحَ: عَامَ

quran_examples.ar: هُوَ ٱللَّهُ ٱلَّذِى لَآ إِلَـٰهَ إِلَّا هُوَ ٱلۡمَلِكُ ٱلۡقُدُّوسُ ٱلسَّلَـٰمُ
quran_examples.en: He is Allah, other than whom there is no deity, the Sovereign, the Pure, the Perfection-Giving

quran_examples.ar: سَبِّحِ ٱسۡمَ رَبِّكَ ٱلۡأَعۡلَى
quran_examples.en: Glorify the name of your Lord, the Most High

hadith.ar: مَنْ قَالَ سُبْحَانَ اللَّهِ وَبِحَمْدِهِ مِائَةَ مَرَّةٍ لَمْ يَأْتِ أَحَدٌ بِأَفْضَلَ مِمَّا جَاءَ بِهِ
hadith.en: Whoever says Subhan Allah wa bihamdihi one hundred times, no one will come with anything better

hadith.ar: كَلِمَتَانِ خَفِيفَتَانِ عَلَى اللِّسَانِ ثَقِيلَتَانِ فِي الْمِيزَانِ
hadith.en: Two words that are light on the tongue but heavy on the scale

shades.explanation: as-Subh (the glorification) in the Quran is the act of declaring Allah free from all imperfection. The famous hadith Qudsi states: Allah descends to the lowest heaven during the last third of the night and says: Who is calling upon Me that I may answer him? as-Subh (tasbih) is one of the highest forms of dhikr. The Quran says: He is Allah, other than whom there is no deity, the Sovereign, the Pure, the Perfection-Giving (59:23). The famous hadith states: Whoever says Subhan Allah wa bihamdihi one hundred times, no one will come on the Day of Resurrection with better than it except a man who said the same or more.
shades.hadith_ar: سُبۡحَـٰنَ ٱللَّهِ وَٱلۡحَمۡدُ لِلَّهِ
shades.hadith_en: Glory be to Allah and praise be to Allah

shades.name_ar: الصُّبۡحُ - أَوَّلُ النَّهَارِ، الضَّوۡءُ بَعۡدَ الظَّلَامِ
shades.explanation: as-Subah (the morning) in the Quran is the beginning of the day. The Quran says: He it is who sends the night as a covering over you, and the sleep as repose, and makes the day a rising (6:96). as-Subah is the time of freshness and activity. The famous hadith states: Allah's messenger used to make these two rak'at before Fajr prayer. The Subah in Islam is the time for the Fajr prayer and the morning adhkar. The Quran praises the Subah as a sign of Allah's mercy - the darkness turns to light. The believer wakes up early to do the Fajr prayer and the morning dhikr.
shades.hadith_ar: إِنَّ قُرۡءَانَ ٱلۡفَجۡرِ كَانَ مَشۡهُودًۭا
shades.hadith_en: Indeed, the Quran of dawn is ever witnessed

shades.explanation: Sabih (the glorified, the swimmer) is a fish in the sea that holds the earth on its back according to one narration. The famous hadith states: The first thing Allah created was the pen. He said: Write. It said: What shall I write? He said: Write the decree of all things that will be until the Day of Resurrection. The sabih in the Quran is also a star (Surat an-Najm 53:1). al-Sabih in Sufism is the one whose heart is always in the state of tasbih - glorifying Allah in all states.
shades.hadith_ar: وَٱلنَّجۡمِ إِذَا هَوَىٰ
shades.hadith_en: By the star when it descends

shades.name_ar: سَبَحَ - عَامَ فِي الْمَاءِ، سَارَ فِي الْهَوَاءِ
shades.explanation: Sabaha (to swim, to float) is the act of moving through water. The famous hadith states: There will come a time upon my ummah when there will be differences and divisions. The sabaha in the Quran is also used metaphorically for swimming in the light of Allah. The Quran says: And the sun runs [to a fixed resting place] for it (36:38). The sabaha of the believer through the dhikr of Allah is one of the most beautiful states. al-Qushayri uses sabaha to describe the spiritual traveler - he swims through the oceans of divine attributes.
shades.hadith_ar: وَسَخَّرَ لَكُم مَّا فِي ٱلسَّمَـٰوَٰتِ وَمَا فِي ٱلۡأَرۡضِ جَمِيعًۭا مِّنۡهُ
shades.hadith_en: And He has subjected to you whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth - all from Him

meaning.en: To not be. The root denotes negation or non-existence.

lexical_analysis.ibn_faris: اللَّامُ وَالْيَاءُ وَالسِّينُ أَصْلٌ يَدُلُّ عَلَى نَفْيٍ
lexical_analysis.al_raghib: لَيْسَ: نَفْيُ الْحَالِ عَنِ الشَّيْءِ

quran_examples.ar: لَّيۡسَ كَمِثۡلِهِۦ شَىۡءٌۭ ۖ وَهُوَ ٱلسَّمِيعُ ٱلۡبَصِيرُ
quran_examples.en: Nothing is like unto Him, and He is the All-Hearing, the All-Seeing
quran_examples.context: Tanzih - Allah is unlike His creation

quran_examples.ar: وَلَمۡ يَكُن لَّهُۥ كُفُوًا أَحَدٌۢ
quran_examples.en: And there is none comparable to Him

hadith.ar: لَيْسَ الْمُؤْمِنُ بِالْمَشْئُومِ وَلَا الْمُؤْمِنُ بِالطَّيَّارِ
hadith.en: The believer is not the one who believes in omens or superstitions

hadith.ar: لَيْسَ الْمِسْكِينُ الَّذِي تَرُدُّهُ اللُّقْمَةُ وَاللُّقْمَتَانِ
hadith.en: The miskeen is not the one who is turned away by a morsel or two

shades.explanation: al-Lays (not) is the negation of a state in Arabic grammar. The Quran uses laysa to negate being or existence. The famous hadith states: Laysa al-mu'min bi-l-mash'um wa laysa al-mu'min bi-l-tiyarah - The mu'min is not one who believes in omens or superstitions. al-Laysa is one of the most important grammatical concepts in the Quran. The famous hadith states: La ilaha illa Allah - There is no god but Allah.
shades.hadith_ar: لَّيۡسَ كَمِثۡلِهِۦ شَىۡءٌۭ
shades.hadith_en: Nothing is like unto Him

shades.name_en: Laysa Ka-Mithlihi - Nothing is Like Him
shades.name_ar: لَيۡسَ كَمِثۡلِهِۦ - نَفْيُ الْمِثۡلِ وَالنَّظِيرِ عَنِ اللَّهِ
shades.explanation: Laysa Ka-Mithlihi (nothing is like Him) is one of the most profound statements in the Quran - the verse of al-Ikhlas (42:11). The Quran says: Nothing is like unto Him, and He is the All-Hearing, the All-Seeing (42:11). Laysa Ka-Mithlihi establishes tanzih (transcendence) - Allah is unlike any of His creation. The famous hadith states: The mutazila say Allah's hand means His power. Ahl al-Sunnah affirm the hand as an attribute without tashbih.
shades.hadith_ar: لَّيۡسَ كَمِثۡلِهِۦ شَىۡءٌۭ ۖ وَهُوَ ٱلسَّمِيعُ ٱلۡبَصِيرُ
shades.hadith_en: Nothing is like unto Him, and He is the All-Hearing, the All-Seeing

shades.name_en: Laysa fi al-Islam Shirk - No Shirk in Islam
shades.name_ar: لَيۡسَ فِي الْإِسۡلَامِ شِرۡكٌ - إِخۡلَاصُ الْعِبَادَةِ لِلَّهِ وَحۡدَهُ
shades.explanation: The famous hadith states: Whoever establishes salah and believes in iman, then there is no shirk in his Islam. The Quran says: And whoever associates others with Allah has certainly fabricated a tremendous sin (4:48). Laysa al-Muslim is one who combines all pillars of Islam. The famous hadith states: The Muslim is the one from whose tongue and hand other Muslims are safe.
shades.hadith_ar: مَنْ أَشْرَكَ بِاللَّهِ فَقَدْ حَرَّمَ اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ الْجَنَّةَ
shades.hadith_en: Whoever associates partners with Allah, Allah has forbidden Paradise for him

shades.name_en: Laysa Ka-l-Faqir - Not Like the Poor
shades.name_ar: لَيۡسَ كَالۡفَقِيرِ - تَفَاوُتُ الْحَالَاتِ بَيْنَ النَّاسِ
shades.explanation: The famous hadith states: The rich have many good deeds, but the poor will be questioned severely on the Day of Resurrection. The Quran says: And the messenger will say: My Lord, indeed my people have taken this Quran as something abandoned (25:30). Laysa in this context negates the equality of states - the rich are not like the poor, the learned are not like the ignorant. The famous hadith states: The strong believer is better and more beloved to Allah than the weak believer.
shades.hadith_ar: لَا يُكَلِّفُ اللَّهُ نَفْسًا إِلَّا وُسْعَهَا
shades.hadith_en: Allah does not burden a soul beyond its capacity

meaning.en: To be allied. The root denotes patron, ally, or faction.

lexical_analysis.ibn_faris: الْمِيمُ وَالْوَاوُ وَاللَّامُ أَصْلٌ يَدُلُّ عَلَى قُرْبٍ أَوْ وَلَايَةٍ
lexical_analysis.al_raghib: الْمَوْلَى: الَّذِي يَلِيكَ مِنْ أَمْرٍ. وَمَوِلَ: قَرُبَ

quran_examples.ar: ٱللَّهُ وَلِىُّ ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ يُخۡرِجُهُم مِّنَ ٱلۡظُلُمَـٰتِ إِلَى ٱلنُّورِ
quran_examples.en: Allah is the ally of those who believe; He brings them out of darkness into light
quran_examples.context: Allah as the ally of the believers

quran_examples.ar: وَإِن يَنصُرۡكُمُ ٱللَّهُ فَلَا غَالِبَ لَكُمۡ
quran_examples.en: And if Allah aids you, no one can overcome you

hadith.ar: الْعَاقِبَةُ لِلْمُتَّقِينَ
hadith.en: The end is for the muttaqin

hadith.ar: مَوْلَى الرَّجُلِ مَوْلَى عَتِيقِهِ
