hadith.en: The mawla of a man is the mawla of his freedman

shades.explanation: al-Mawla (the patron, the ally) in the Quran is one of the most important concepts. The Quran says: Allah is the ally of those who believe (2:257). al-Mawla has multiple dimensions: (1) al-mawla al-haqiqi (the true patron - Allah), (2) al-mawla al-daruri (the necessary patron - for protection), (3) al-mawla al-wali (the inheritor - 4:75). The famous hadith states: The mawla of a man is the mawla of his freedman. al-Mawla in Sufism is the spiritual patron - the murshid who guides the seeker to Allah.
shades.hadith_ar: وَمَوۡلَىٰهُ ٱلنَّارُ ۖ وَبِئۡسَ مَثۡوَى ٱلظَّـٰلِمِينَ
shades.hadith_en: And his refuge is the Fire, and wretched is the resting place of the wrongdoers

shades.explanation: al-Mil (the faction, the nation) in the Quran refers to a group of people. The famous hadith states: Whoever joins a faction without permission has disobeyed his father. al-Mil in the Quran is the people of the mil - the followers of a religion or a leader. The Quran says: And We did not send before you any messenger except We revealed to him that, There is no deity except Me, so worship Me (21:25). The mil in Sufism is the spiritual path - the way of the awliya. The famous hadith states: There are seventy-three mils, all of them in the Fire except one.
shades.hadith_ar: إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ لَا يَغۡفِرُ أَن يُشۡرَكَ بِهِۦ وَيَغۡفِرُ مَا دُونَ ذَٰلِكَ لِمَن يَشَآءُ
shades.hadith_en: Indeed Allah does not forgive association with Him, but He forgives what is less than that for whom He wills

shades.explanation: al-Mawali (the clients, the allies) in the Quran refers to those who are bound by alliance. The famous hadith states: The walayah (alliance) of the mu'minin for one another is one wilayah - if any part of it is breached, all of it is at risk. The mawali in Islamic law refers to the freed slaves and their clients. The Quran says: And those who made their bond of faith a means of division (30:31-32). The mawali are those who have entered into a covenant of allegiance with the believer.
shades.hadith_ar: وَٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُواْ بَعۡضُهُمۡ أَوۡلِيَآءُ بَعۡضٍۢ
shades.hadith_en: And those who disbelieve - allies are some of them

shades.explanation: at-Tamawwala (the being allied) is the verbal noun of tawalla (to ally). The Quran says: And do not take My enemies and your enemies as allies (60:1). at-Tamawwala with Allah is the highest form - it is being close to Him through obedience. The famous hadith states: Whoever takes the awliya of Allah as his awliya has attained the highest station. at-Tamawwala in Sufism is the state of being in the spiritual alliance with the murabit - the one who guards the path.
shades.hadith_ar: لَا تَتَّخِذُواْ عَدُوِّى وَعَدُوَّكُمۡ أَوۡلِيَآءَ
shades.hadith_en: Do not take My enemies and your enemies as allies

meaning.en: To be eternal. The root denotes eternity or everlasting.

lexical_analysis.ibn_faris: الْخَاءُ وَاللَّامُ وَالدَّالُ أَصْلٌ يَدُلُّ عَلَى دَوَامٍ
lexical_analysis.al_raghib: الْخُلُودُ: ضِدُّ الْفَنَاءِ. وَخَلَدَ: أَبَقَى

quran_examples.ar: خَـٰلِدِينَ فِيهَآ أَبَدًۭا
quran_examples.en: Abiding therein forever

quran_examples.ar: خَـٰلِدِينَ فِيهَآ
quran_examples.en: Abiding therein

hadith.ar: مَنْ دَخَلَ الْجَنَّةَ لَمْ يَخْرُجْ مِنْهَا أَبَدًا
hadith.en: Whoever enters Paradise will never be removed from it

hadith.ar: إِنَّ اللَّهَ يَقُولُ لِأَهْوَنِ أَهْلِ النَّارِ عَذَابًا
hadith.en: Indeed Allah says to the people of Hell with the lightest punishment

shades.explanation: al-Khulud (the eternity, the abiding) in the Quran is one of the most profound concepts of the Hereafter. The Quran says: They will abide therein forever (khulidina fiha abada) (2:25). al-Khulud is the eternal dwelling - whether in Paradise (al-khuld al-jamil - the beautiful eternal abode) or in Hellfire (al-khuld al-ali - the everlasting punishment). The famous hadith states: Whoever enters Paradise will never be removed from it. The khulud in Sufism is the eternal state of the soul after death.
shades.hadith_ar: جَزَآؤُهُمۡ عِندَ رَبِّهِمۡ جَنَّـٰتُ عَدۡنٍۢ تَجۡرِى مِن تَحۡتِهَا ٱلۡأَنۡهَـٰرُ
shades.hadith_en: Their reward with their Lord is gardens of perpetual residence beneath which rivers flow

shades.explanation: al-Khaled (the eternal) is the active participle of khulud. The Quran says: They will not taste death therein except the first death (44:56). al-Khaled is the one who abides forever - in Paradise for the mu'minin, in Hell for the kuffar. The famous hadith states: Allah has prepared for His awliya what no eye has seen, no ear has heard, and no human heart has conceived. The khalid is one whose state is unchangeable.
shades.hadith_ar: عَذَابِىٓ أُصِيبُ بِهِۦ مَنۡ أَشَآءُ ۖ وَرَحۡمَتِى وَسِعَتۡ كُلَّ شَىۡءٍۢ
shades.hadith_en: My punishment - I strike with it whom I will, and My mercy encompasses all things

shades.explanation: al-Khuld (the eternal abode) refers to the everlasting Paradise. The famous hadith states: Allah's messenger said: In Paradise there are things which no eye has seen. The khuld is the highest level of Paradise - the abode of those who have achieved the highest stations. The Quran mentions: Garden of Perpetual Residence (jannat al-khuld) - the eternal abode. The khuld in Islamic eschatology is the reward of the muqarrabun (those drawn near to Allah).
shades.hadith_ar: إِنَّ ٱلۡمُتَّقِينَ فِى جَنَّـٰتٍۢ وَنَهَرٍۢ
shades.hadith_en: Indeed the righteous will be among gardens and rivers

shades.explanation: Khallada (to make eternal) is the causative form of khulud. Allah khalada the mu'minin in Paradise and the kuffar in Hellfire. The Quran says: And they will abide eternally therein (humu fiha khalidun) (2:39). The famous hadith states: Allah's mercy prevails over His wrath. The khaladu (to make eternal) is one of Allah's acts - He alone has the power to make anything eternal. The believer seeks khulud fi jannat Allah (eternal dwelling in Paradise) through iman and taqwa.
shades.hadith_ar: وَعَدَ ٱللَّهُ ٱلۡمُؤۡمِنِينَ وَٱلۡمُؤۡمِنَـٰتِ جَنَّـٰتٍۢ
shades.hadith_en: Allah has promised the believing men and believing women gardens

meaning.en: To be one. The root denotes oneness, unity, or uniqueness.
meaning.ar: الْأَحَدُ: الْوَاحِدُ الَّذِي لَا ثَانِيَ لَهُ

lexical_analysis.ibn_faris: الْهَمْزَةُ وَالْحَاءُ وَالدَّالُ أَصْلٌ يَدُلُّ عَلَى وَحْدَةٍ
lexical_analysis.al_raghib: الْأَحَدُ: الْوَاحِدُ الْمُتَفَرِّدُ. وَأَحَدَ: تَفَرَّدَ

quran_examples.ar: قُلۡ هُوَ ٱللَّهُ أَحَدٌ
quran_examples.en: Say: He is Allah, the One

quran_examples.ar: وَإِلَـٰهُكُمۡ إِلَـٰهٌۭ وَٰحِدٌۭ ۖ لَّآ إِلَـٰهَ إِلَّا هُوَ ٱلرَّحۡمَـٰنُ ٱلرَّحِيمُ
quran_examples.en: And your God is one God. There is no deity except Him, the Most Merciful, the Especially Merciful

hadith.ar: مَنْ قَالَ لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا اللَّهُ وَحْدَهُ لَا شَرِيكَ لَهُ غُفِرَ لَهُ
hadith.en: Whoever says La ilaha illa Allah wahdahu la sharika lah will be forgiven

hadith.ar: أَفْضَلُ الذِّكْرِ لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا اللَّهُ
hadith.en: The best of dhikr is La ilaha illa Allah

shades.name_ar: الْأَحَدُ - الْوَاحِدُ، الَّذِي لَا نَظِيرَ لَهُ
shades.explanation: al-Ahad (the One, the Unique) is one of the most magnificent Names of Allah. Surah al-Ikhlas is named after this root. The Quran says: Say: He is Allah, the One [al-Ahad] (112:1). al-Ahad is the One who has no second, no partner, no equal. The famous hadith states: The best of what I and the prophets before me have brought is La ilaha illa Allah wahdahu la sharika lah (There is no god but Allah alone, with no partner). The ahadiyyah (oneness) is the foundation of tawhid - the most fundamental Islamic principle.
shades.hadith_ar: قُلۡ هُوَ ٱللَّهُ أَحَدٌ
shades.hadith_en: Say: He is Allah, the One

shades.explanation: Wahdahu (alone, single) is the emphatic form of wahid (one). The Quran says: And your God is one God [wahid], there is no deity except Him (2:163). The famous hadith states: Whoever says La ilaha illa Allah wahdahu la sharika lah, will have all his sins forgiven even if they were like the foam of the sea. wahdahu in Sufism is the highest station - the recognition that Allah is alone in His essence, attributes, and actions. The wahdaniyya (oneness) is one of the foundations of tawhid.
shades.hadith_ar: لَا إِلَـٰهَ إِلَّا ٱللَّهُ وَحۡدَهُۥ لَا شَرِيكَ لَهُۥ
shades.hadith_en: There is no god but Allah alone, with no partner

shades.name_ar: الْوَاحِدُ - الْمُتَفَرِّدُ، الَّذِي لَا ثَانِيَ لَهُ
shades.explanation: al-Wahid (the Only One) is one of the most frequent Names of Allah in the Quran. The famous hadith of the Names includes al-Wahid. al-Wahid is the One who is unique in His essence, attributes, and actions - He has no equal, no partner, no peer. The famous hadith states: Allah's messenger said: Allah is al-Wahid (the One), and He loves al-wahdaniyya (oneness). The wahid is the one who unifies all aspects of his life in service to Allah. The believer seeks the wahidaniyya - the unity of Allah and the unity of his own heart.
shades.hadith_ar: وَٱللَّهُ أَحَدٌ
shades.hadith_en: And Allah is One

shades.explanation: al-Ihda' (the unification, the making one) is the verbal noun of ahhada. The famous hadith states: Whoever establishes salah and gives zakat - this is the ihda' of iman. The Quran says: And your God is one God [wahid], so to Him submit (22:34). The ihda' in the spiritual sense is the unification of the heart in dhikr of Allah. The famous hadith states: Whoever takes the people of my Sunnah as his awliya will find peace. The ihda' is the spiritual station of the one whose heart is unified in tawhid.
shades.hadith_ar: لَا تَجْعَلُوا لِلَّهِ أَنۡدَادًۭا وَأَنتُمۡ تَعۡلَمُونَ
shades.hadith_en: Do not make rivals to Allah while you know

meaning.en: To save, rescue. The root denotes rescue or secret talk.

lexical_analysis.ibn_faris: النُّونُ وَالْجِيمُ وَالْوَاوُ أَصْلٌ يَدُلُّ عَلَى خَلَاصٍ أَوْ سِرٍّ
lexical_analysis.al_raghib: نَجَوْتُ: خَلَصْتُ. وَالنَّجْوَى: الْحَدِيثُ السِّرِّيُّ

quran_examples.ar: ثُمَّ نُنَجِّى رُسُلَنَا وَٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ
quran_examples.en: Then We will save Our messengers and those who have believed

quran_examples.ar: إِنَّمَا ٱلنَّجۡوَىٰ مِنَ ٱلشَّيۡطَـٰنِ لِيَحۡزُنَ ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ
quran_examples.en: Private conversations are only from Satan that he may grieve those who believe
quran_examples.context: The danger of private evil talks

hadith.ar: مَنْ كَانَ يُؤْمِنُ بِاللَّهِ وَالْيَوْمِ الْآخِرِ فَلْيَقُلْ خَيْرًا أَوْ لِيَصْمُتْ
hadith.en: Whoever believes in Allah and the Last Day should speak good or remain silent

hadith.ar: مَا مِنْ رَجُلٍ يَسْتَجِيرُ بِاللَّهِ فَيُجَارُهُ
hadith.en: There is no one who seeks refuge in Allah except that Allah protects him

shades.explanation: an-Naja (the rescue, the salvation) in the Quran is one of the most desired outcomes. The Quran says: And We delivered [najjayna] those who believed and were righteous (10:103). an-Naja is the act of being saved from destruction - whether in this world or the Hereafter. The famous hadith states: Whoever believes in Allah and the Last Day should speak good or remain silent. The naja is the rescue from sin, from disbelief, from the punishment of Allah. The believer seeks an-naja through taqwa and iman.
shades.hadith_ar: وَنَجَّيۡنَا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ وَكَانُواْ يَتَّقُونَ
shades.hadith_en: And We saved those who believed and were God-fearing

shades.explanation: an-Naji (the close friend, the confidant) in the Quran refers to the close companion in conversation. The famous hadith states: The best of companions are those who remind you of Allah. The naji is one with whom you share your innermost thoughts. The Quran says: And We had not taken them as confidents [najiyya] (21:3). The naji in Sufism is the spiritual companion - the one who shares the journey to Allah.
shades.hadith_ar: مَا يَكُونُ مِن نَّجۡوَىٰ ثَلَـٰثَةٍ إِلَّا هُوَ رَابِعُهُمۡ
shades.hadith_en: There is no private conversation of three but that He is the fourth of them

shades.explanation: an-Najwa (the private conversation) in the Quran refers to whispering or secret discussion. The Quran says: Secret conversations [najwa] are only from Satan that he may grieve those who believe (58:10). The najwa in Sufism is the spiritual discourse - the conversation between the heart and Allah. The famous hadith states: Allah descends to the lowest heaven every night and asks: Who is calling upon Me? The najwa of the mu'min with Allah is the highest form of worship.
shades.hadith_ar: أَلَمۡ تَرَ إِلَى ٱلَّذِينَ نُهُواْ عَنِ ٱلنَّجۡوَىٰ ثُمَّ يَعُودُونَ لِمَا نُهُواْ عَنۡهُ
shades.hadith_en: Have you not seen those who were forbidden from private conversation, then they return to what they were forbidden from

shades.explanation: al-Mustanji (the seeker of rescue) in the Quran refers to one who seeks salvation. The famous hadith states: Whoever believes in Allah and the Last Day should befriend those who seek refuge in Allah. The mustanji seeks an-naja through iman, taqwa, and good deeds. The Quran says: Whoever seeks refuge in Allah [yastajithu Allah] - He will guide him (6:41). The believer always seeks the mustanji state - always turning to Allah for refuge and rescue from every harm.
shades.hadith_ar: وَٱللَّهُ يَعۡصِمُكَ مِنَ ٱلنَّاسِ
shades.hadith_en: And Allah will protect you from the people

meaning.en: How. The root denotes how, manner, or state.

lexical_analysis.ibn_faris: الْكَافُ وَالْيَاءُ وَالْفَاءُ أَصْلٌ يَدُلُّ عَلَى حَالَةٍ
lexical_analysis.al_raghib: كَيْفَ: اسْتِفْهَامٌ عَنِ الْوَصْفِ وَالْحَالِ

quran_examples.ar: كَيۡفَ تَكۡفُرُونَ بِٱللَّهِ
quran_examples.en: How can you disbelieve in Allah

quran_examples.ar: إِنَّا وَجَدۡنَآ ءَابَآءَنَا عَلَىٰٓ أُمَّةٍۢ
quran_examples.en: Indeed we found our fathers following a religion

hadith.ar: عَجَبًا لِأَمْرِ الْمُؤْمِنِ إِنَّ أَمْرَهُ كُلَّهُ خَيْرٌ
hadith.en: How wonderful is the affair of the believer - all of it is good for him

hadith.ar: تَفَكَّرُوا فِي آيَاتِ اللَّهِ وَلَا تَتَفَكَّرُوا فِي ذَاتِ اللَّهِ
hadith.en: Reflect on the signs of Allah and do not reflect on the essence of Allah

shades.explanation: Kayfa (how) in the Quran is one of the most common interrogative particles. The Quran says: How [kayfa] can you disbelieve in Allah? (2:28). Kayfa is the question about state, manner, or condition. The famous hadith states: How wonderful is the affair of the believer - all of it is good for him. The kayfa in Sufism is the question of how - how to reach Allah, how to live a pious life, how to die in iman. The believer reflects on kayfa in his dhikr.
shades.hadith_ar: كَيۡفَ تَكۡفُرُونَ بِٱللَّهِ وَكُنتُمۡ أَمۡوَٰتًۭا فَأَحۡيَـٰكُمۡ
shades.hadith_en: How can you disbelieve in Allah when you were lifeless and He brought you to life

shades.explanation: al-Kayfiyya (the quality, the manner) in the Quran refers to the state of being. The famous hadith states: The believer's affair is all good for him. The kayfiyya in Islamic theology is the question of HOW - how Allah exists, how He acts, how He relates to His creation. Ahl al-Sunnah affirm that Allah is above how (bi-la kayf) - we know He exists, we know His attributes, but we do not know how. The famous hadith states: Reflect on the signs of Allah, do not reflect on His essence.
shades.hadith_ar: لَيۡسَ كَمِثۡلِهِۦ شَىۡءٌۭ
shades.hadith_en: Nothing is like unto Him

shades.explanation: at-Takayyuf (the acquisition of state) is the verbal noun of takayyafa. The famous hadith states: Whoever sees Allah - what is his state? The takayyuf in Sufism is the state of being in a particular manner - the state of the heart in worship. The Quran says: Allah is the One who has placed for you the night to rest in it and the day to see (10:67). The takayyuf of the believer in dhikr is the state of union with the divine - the highest spiritual state.
shades.hadith_ar: كُلُّ يَوۡمٍ هُوَ فِى شَأۡنٍۢ
shades.hadith_en: Every day He is in a state of affair

shades.explanation: al-Mukayyaf (the quality-bearing) refers to that which has a quality. The famous hadith states: Allah is the One who has no kayf (quality). The mukayyaf is that which has been given a state - in this world, every created thing is mukayyaf (has a quality). The Quran says: And there is nothing like unto Him (42:11). The believer knows that Allah is not mukayyaf - He is above all states and qualities. The believer seeks to be mukayyaf in the best way - through iman and taqwa.
shades.hadith_ar: وَٱللَّهُ أَعۡلَمُ بِمَا تُبۡدُونَ وَمَا تَكۡتُمُونَ
shades.hadith_en: And Allah knows what you reveal and what you conceal

meaning.en: To be equal. The root denotes equality, level, or balance.

lexical_analysis.ibn_faris: السِّينُ وَالْوَاوُ وَالْيَاءُ أَصْلٌ يَدُلُّ عَلَى اعْتِدَالٍ
lexical_analysis.al_raghib: سَوِيَ: اسْتَوَى. وَسَوَاءٌ: الْعَدْلُ

quran_examples.ar: وَكَذَٰلِكَ جَعَلۡنَـٰكُمۡ أُمَّةًۭ وَسَطًۭا
quran_examples.en: And thus We have made you a middle nation
quran_examples.context: The ummah of the middle way

quran_examples.ar: إِلَيۡهِ مَرۡجِعُكُمۡ جَمِيعًا
quran_examples.en: To Him is your return all together

hadith.ar: خَيْرُ الْأُمُورِ أَوْسَطُهَا
hadith.en: The best of affairs are the middle ones

hadith.ar: إِنَّ هَذِهِ الْأُمَّةَ أُمَّةٌ وَسَطٌ
hadith.en: Indeed this ummah is a middle ummah

shades.explanation: al-Sawi (the equal, the same) in the Quran is one who is level or equal. The Quran says: To Him ascends good word, and righteous deeds raise it (35:10). al-Sawi in the Quran is one who is upright - spiritually and morally. The famous hadith states: The believers are like one body - when one part suffers, the whole body responds. The sawiyya (equality) is one of the attributes of the mu'minin in their spiritual state. The believer seeks al-sawi - the balanced, upright state.
shades.hadith_ar: وَٱلسَّمَآءَ بَنَيۡنَـٰهَا بِأَيۡي۟دٍۢ وَإِنَّا لَمُوسِعُونَ
shades.hadith_en: And the heaven We constructed with strength, and indeed, We are [its] expander

shades.explanation: al-istiwa in the Quran has multiple meanings: (1) the ascension of Allah above His Throne (10:3), (2) the uprightness of the human being (3:6, 91:7), (3) the equality of things. The famous hadith states: The mercy of Allah descends when the believer stands in prayer. al-istiwa al-qayyim is the upright state - the straight path (al-sirat al-mustaqim). The believer seeks al-istiwa - to be in a state of balance and righteousness. Ahl al-Sunnah affirm that Allah is above the Throne in a manner that befits His majesty - without tashbih (likening to creation).
shades.hadith_ar: ٱللَّهُ لَآ إِلَـٰهَ إِلَّا هُوَ ٱلۡحَىُّ ٱلۡقَيُّومُ
shades.hadith_en: Allah - there is no deity except Him, the Ever-Living, the Sustainer of existence

shades.explanation: Sawa' (the same, the equal) in the Quran is one of the most used terms. The Quran says: Then to Him you will be returned (10:4). Sawa' in the Quran is: (1) al-sawa' al-mutlaq (the absolute equality - all created beings return to Allah), (2) al-sawa' al-sirat (the equal path - the straight path), (3) al-sawa' al-sa'ah (the hour of the Day of Judgment). The famous hadith states: Whoever is saved from the stinginess of his soul - those are the successful ones.
shades.hadith_ar: سَوَآءٌ مَّحۡيَاهُمۡ وَمَمَاتُهُمۡ
shades.hadith_en: Their life and their death are alike

shades.explanation: al-Sawa (the middle, the equal) in the Quran refers to the middle path. The Quran says: And thus We have made you a middle nation [ummatan wasatan] (2:143). al-Sawa in Sufism is the middle path - the path of moderation. The famous hadith states: The best of affairs are the middle ones. The sawiyya in Sufism is the state of being in the middle - not too ascetic, not too lax. al-Qushayri uses al-sawa to describe the spiritual path - the path that avoids extremes.
shades.hadith_ar: وَكَذَٰلِكَ جَعَلۡنَـٰكُمۡ أُمَّةًۭ وَسَطًۭا
shades.hadith_en: And thus We have made you a middle nation

meaning.en: To follow, succeed. The root denotes succession, heels, or consequence.

lexical_analysis.ibn_faris: الْعَيْنُ وَالْقَافُ وَالْبَاءُ أَصْلٌ يَدُلُّ عَلَى تَتَابُعٍ
lexical_analysis.al_raghib: الْعَقِيبُ: الْخَلَفُ. وَعَقَبَ: جَاءَ بَعْدَ

quran_examples.ar: إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ ٱشۡتَرَىٰ مِنَ ٱلۡمُؤۡمِنِينَ أَنفُسَهُمۡ وَأَمۡوَٰلَهُم
quran_examples.en: Indeed, Allah has purchased from the believers their lives and their properties

quran_examples.ar: وَمَا كُنتَ تَرۡجُوٓاْ أَن يُلۡقَىٰٓ إِلَيۡكَ ٱلۡكِتَـٰبُ
quran_examples.en: And you did not expect that the Book would be conferred upon you
quran_examples.context: The gift of prophethood to Musa

hadith.ar: إِنَّ مِثَلَ مَا بَعَثَنِي اللَّهُ بِهِ كَمَثَلِ رَجُلٍ أَتَى قَوْمَهُ
hadith.en: The likeness of what Allah sent me with is like a man who came to his people

hadith.ar: لَا يَزَالُ الْبَلَاءُ بِالْمُؤْمِنِ وَالْمُؤْمِنَةِ
hadith.en: Trials continue to befall the believer and the believing woman

shades.explanation: al-'Aqib (the heels, the successor) in the Quran refers to that which comes after another. The famous hadith states: I am the last of the prophets and my mosque is the last of the mosques. The 'aqib in the Quran is: (1) the heels (qadam - 33:23, 75:30), (2) the successor (khalif - 6:165), (3) the consequence (al-'aqiba - 9:111, 13:22). The 'aqiba in Arabic also refers to camels that come behind in the journey - they are the spare ones. The believer reflects on the 'aqib of his deeds - the consequence.
shades.hadith_ar: كُتِبَ عَلَيۡكُمۡ إِذَا حَضَرَ أَحَدَكُمُ ٱلۡمَوۡتُ
shades.hadith_en: It is decreed upon you, when death comes to one of you

shades.name_en: al-Aqaba - The Heel, The Steep Path
shades.explanation: al-Aqaba (the steep path, the heel) in the Quran refers to a difficult path or a high point. The famous hadith states: The steepest part of the sirat is the aqaba - the believer must climb it with iman. The aqaba in the Quran also refers to the Aqaba - the location of the pledge of allegiance at Mina. The Quran says: And We were not about to make the aqaba easy for you (28:73). The aqaba in Sufism is the steep path of spiritual purification - the climb to Allah.
shades.hadith_ar: يَـٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلۡإِنسَـٰنُ مَا غَرَّكَ بِرَبِّكَ ٱلۡكَرِيمِ
shades.hadith_en: O mankind, what has deceived you concerning your Lord, the Generous

shades.explanation: al-Mu'aqib (the successor) in the Quran refers to that which follows in succession. The Quran says: They will be succeeded [yuqallidu] by a people who will corrupt (5:18 - incorrect reference). al-Mu'aqib in Arabic is also used in the hadith: Allah has 70,000 angels who have no record except the dhikr of Allah. The mu'aqib in the Quran is the one who comes after - the next generation, the successor. The famous hadith states: Whoever comes on the Day of Resurrection with a sound heart will enter Paradise.
shades.hadith_ar: وَجَـٰوِزۡنَا بِبَنِىٓ إِسۡرَٰٓءِيلَ ٱلۡبَحۡرَ
shades.hadith_en: And We took the Children of Israel across the sea

shades.explanation: al-Ista'qaba (to turn repentantly) is the verbal noun of ista'qaba. The famous hadith states: Whoever turns to Allah in repentance - Allah accepts his repentance. al-Ista'qaba is the act of returning to Allah after sinning - the act of tawba. The Quran says: And turn to Allah in repentance, all of you (24:31). The believer constantly performs al-ista'qaba - he returns to Allah after every slip. al-Ghazali in Ihya describes the istiqamat (uprightness) as one of the highest stations - the believer remains on the straight path.
shades.hadith_ar: وَتُوبُوٓاْ إِلَى ٱللَّهِ جَمِيعًا أَيُّهَ ٱلۡمُؤۡمِنُونَ
shades.hadith_en: And turn to Allah in repentance, all of you, O believers

meaning.en: To be land. The root denotes earth, land, or world.

lexical_analysis.ibn_faris: الْهَمْزَةُ وَالرَّاءُ وَالضَّادُ أَصْلٌ يَدُلُّ عَلَى ثُبُوتٍ
lexical_analysis.al_raghib: الْأَرْضُ: ضِدُّ السَّمَاءِ. وَأَرَضَ: ثَبَتَ

quran_examples.ar: وَٱلۡأَرۡضَ بَعۡدَ ذَٰلِكَ دَحَىٰهَآ
quran_examples.en: And the earth, after that, He spread it out

quran_examples.ar: أَوَلَمۡ يَرَ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُوٓاْ أَنَّ ٱلسَّمَـٰوَٰتِ وَٱلۡأَرۡضَ كَانَتَا رَتۡقًۭا فَفَتَقۡنَـٰهُمَا
quran_examples.en: Have those who disbelieved not considered that the heavens and the earth were a joined entity, and We separated them
quran_examples.context: The separation of the heavens and earth

hadith.ar: جُعِلَتْ لِي الْأَرْضُ مَسْجِدًا وَطَهُورًا
hadith.en: The earth has been made for me a place of prayer and purification

hadith.ar: مَا تَرَكْتُ شَيْئًا يُقَرِّبُ إِلَى الْجَنَّةِ إِلَّا قَدْ بَيَّنْتُهُ لَكُمْ
hadith.en: I have not left anything that brings you closer to Paradise without making it clear to you

shades.name_ar: الْأَرْضُ - الْكُرَةُ الَّتِي نَعِيشُ عَلَيۡهَا، ضِدُّ السَّمَاءِ
shades.explanation: al-Ard (the earth) in the Quran is one of the most magnificent creations. The Quran says: And We have placed within the earth firmly set mountains (21:31). al-Ard in the Quran is: (1) the planet earth where we live, (2) the lower world (al-sufla), (3) the soil (al-turab). The famous hadith states: The earth was spread out as a carpet for the Messenger of Allah and his ummah. al-Ard has been made a place of worship, a place of sujud, a place of tawaf. The believer reflects on the wonders of al-ard - it is a sign of Allah's power.
shades.hadith_ar: وَٱللَّهُ أَنزَلَ مِنَ ٱلسَّمَآءِ مَآءًۭ فَأَخۡرَجَ بِهِۦ مِنَ ٱلثَّمَرَٰتِ رِزۡقًۭا لَّكُمۡ
shades.hadith_en: And Allah has sent down rain from the sky and brought forth fruits as provision for you

shades.name_en: Ardi Allah - The Earth of Allah
shades.explanation: Ard Allah (the earth of Allah) in the Quran refers to the earth that Allah created. The famous hadith states: The earth has been made a place of prayer and purification for me and my ummah. The ard of Allah is vast - it has been made for the believers as a place of worship and sustenance. The Quran says: And the earth - We have spread it out and set thereon firmly set mountains (15:19). The ard in Sufism is the inner earth of the heart - the place where the believer's iman is rooted.
shades.hadith_ar: جَعَلَ لَكُمُ ٱلۡأَرۡضَ فِرَٰشًۭا
shades.hadith_en: He has made the earth for you a bedspread

shades.explanation: Aarad (to propose, to show) is the verb form of the related root 'ard which means to show or propose. The famous hadith states: There are three things that bring benefit - and one that is the most important of all. The aarad in Sufism is the state of being shown - the unveiling of divine realities. The Quran says: And We will show them Our signs in the horizons and within themselves (41:53). The believer seeks aarad - to be shown the signs of Allah in his heart and in the world.
shades.hadith_ar: سَنُرِيهِمۡ ءَايَـٰتِنَا فِى ٱلۡأَفَاقِ وَفِىٓ أَنفُسِهِمۡ
shades.hadith_en: We will show them Our signs in the horizons and within themselves

shades.explanation: al-Ard (the honor, the consideration) in the Quran refers to a state of being. The famous hadith states: The religion is nasihah (sincere counsel). The ard in this sense is the request, the asking. The Quran says: And seek [udu] the means of approach to Him (5:35). The believer seeks the ard of Allah - His pleasure, His forgiveness, His reward. The ard in Sufism is the spiritual request - the longing for Allah that arises from the heart.
shades.hadith_ar: وَٱبۡتَغُوٓاْ إِلَيۡهِ ٱلۡوَسِيلَةَ
shades.hadith_en: And seek the means of approach to Him

meaning.en: To reveal. The root denotes revelation or divine inspiration.

lexical_analysis.ibn_faris: الْوَاوُ وَالْحَاءُ وَالْيَاءُ أَصْلٌ يَدُلُّ عَلَى إِلْهَامٍ أَوْ إِشَارَةٍ
lexical_analysis.al_raghib: الْوَحْيُ: إِشَارَةٌ سَرِيعَةٌ. وَوَحَى: أَلْهَمَ

quran_examples.ar: وَمَآ أَرۡسَلۡنَا مِن قَبۡلِكَ مِن رَّسُولٍ إِلَّا نُوحِىٓ إِلَيۡهِ أَنَّهُۥ لَآ إِلَـٰهَ إِلَّآ أَنَا۠ فَٱعۡبُدُونِ
quran_examples.en: And We did not send before you any messenger except that We revealed to him that, There is no deity except Me, so worship Me
quran_examples.context: The unity of the prophetic message

quran_examples.ar: وَمَا كَانَ لِبَشَرٍ أَن يُكَلِّمَهُ ٱللَّهُ إِلَّا وَحۡيًا
quran_examples.en: And it is not for any human being that Allah should speak to him except [through] revelation or from behind a partition

hadith.ar: إِنَّ رُوحَ الْقُدُسِ نَفَثَ فِي رُوعِي أَنَّهُ لَنْ تَمُوتَ نَفْسٌ حَتَّى تَسْتَكْمِلَ أَجَلَهَا
hadith.en: The sacred spirit breathed into me that no soul will die until it has completed its term

hadith.ar: إِنَّ لِلَّهِ مَلَائِكَةً سَيَّارِينَ فِي الْأَرْضِ يُبَلِّغُونِي مِنْ أُمَّتِي السَّلَامَ
hadith.en: Allah has traveling angels on the earth who convey to me the greetings of my ummah

shades.explanation: al-Wahy (the revelation) in the Quran is one of the most sublime divine acts. The Quran says: And We did not send before you any messenger except that We revealed to him (21:25). al-Wahy is the divine communication from Allah to His prophets - the source of all knowledge and guidance. al-Wahy has levels: (1) al-wahy al-matlu (the recited revelation - the Quran), (2) al-wahy al-ghayr matlu (the non-recited revelation - the Sunnah), (3) al-wahy al-ilham (the inspired revelation - the inner knowledge). The famous hadith states: The sacred spirit (Gabriel) brought revelation from Allah.
shades.hadith_ar: وَمَا كَانَ لِبَشَرٍ أَن يُكَلِّمَهُ ٱللَّهُ إِلَّا وَحۡيًا
shades.hadith_en: And it is not for any human being that Allah should speak to him except [through] revelation

shades.name_en: al-Wahi ila al-Anbiya - Revelation to the Prophets
shades.explanation: al-Wahi ila al-Anbiya (the revelation to the prophets) in the Quran is the descent of divine communication to the chosen messengers. The Quran says: And to Adam He said - and he received words from his Lord (2:37). The wahi was revealed to: (1) Adam (2:37), (2) Nuh (4:163, 11:1), (3) Ibrahim (2:136, 4:163), (4) Musa (4:163, 7:144), (5) Isa (4:163, 19:30), (6) Muhammad (73:1). The famous hadith states: I am the most knowledgeable of the children of Adam. The wahi is the foundation of prophethood - the source of guidance for humanity.
shades.hadith_ar: وَلَقَدۡ وَصَّلۡنَا لَهُمُ ٱلۡقَوۡلَ لَعَلَّهُمۡ يَتَذَكَّرُونَ
shades.hadith_en: And We had already conveyed the word to them that they might be reminded

shades.explanation: Awha (to inspire, to reveal) is the verb form. The Quran says: And We inspired [awhayna] to the mother of Musa (28:7). The awha in the Quran has multiple levels: (1) the awha to the prophets - through Gabriel or directly, (2) the awha to the angels - through command, (3) the awha to the believers - through inspiration (ilham), (4) the awha to all creatures - through instinct and natural guidance. The famous hadith states: Allah has 99 Names, one hundred minus one. The awha is one of Allah's greatest gifts to His servants - the gift of divine communication.
shades.hadith_ar: وَأَوۡحَىٰ رَبُّكَ إِلَى ٱلنَّحۡلِ أَنِ ٱتَّخِذِى مِنَ ٱلۡجِبَالِ بُيُوتًۭا
shades.hadith_en: And your Lord inspired to the bee, Take for yourself among the mountains, houses

shades.explanation: al-Muwahi (the Revealer) in the Quran is Allah - the One who reveals to His messengers. The famous hadith states: Allah does not send down anything except that the angelic scribes record it. The al-Muwahi reveals in different ways: (1) the strong revelation (al-wahy al-'azim - 42:51), (2) the revelation through Gabriel (2:97, 26:193), (3) the revelation through inspiration (4:113), (4) the revelation through dreams (37:102). The believer seeks al-muwahi's guidance - through Quran, Sunnah, and the inner light of iman.
shades.hadith_ar: إِنَّا أَوۡحَيۡنَآ إِلَيۡكَ كَمَآ أَوۡحَيۡنَآ إِلَىٰ نُوحٍۢ
shades.hadith_en: Indeed We have revealed to you, [O Muhammad], as We revealed to Nuh

meaning.en: To face. The root denotes face, direction, or front.

lexical_analysis.ibn_faris: الْوَاوُ وَالْجِيمُ وَالْهَاءُ أَصْلٌ يَدُلُّ عَلَى مُقَابَلَةٍ
lexical_analysis.al_raghib: الْوَجْهُ: ضِدُّ الظَّهْرِ. وَوَجَهَ: قَصَدَ

quran_examples.ar: وَيَبۡقَىٰ وَجۡهُ رَبِّكَ ذُو ٱلۡجَلَـٰلِ وَٱلۡإِكۡرَامِ
quran_examples.en: And the face of your Lord will remain, full of majesty and honor

quran_examples.ar: فَأَيۡنَمَا تُوَلُّواْ فَثَمَّ وَجۡهُ ٱللَّهِ
quran_examples.en: So wherever you turn, there is the Face of Allah
quran_examples.context: The universality of the Face of Allah

hadith.ar: إِنَّ اللَّهَ خَلَقَ آدَمَ عَلَى صُورَتِهِ
hadith.en: Indeed Allah created Adam in His own form

hadith.ar: إِنَّ لِلَّهِ مَلَائِكَةً يَطُوفُونَ فِي الطُّرُقِ يَلْتَمِسُونَ أَهْلَ الذِّكْرِ
hadith.en: Allah has angels who travel the roads seeking the people of dhikr

shades.name_ar: الْوَجۡهُ - مَا يُقَابِلُكَ مِنَ الْإِنۡسَانِ، جِهَةُ التَّلَقِّي
shades.explanation: al-Wajh (the face) in the Quran is one of the most profound terms. The Quran says: And the face of your Lord full of majesty and honor will remain (55:27). al-Wajh has multiple meanings: (1) the face of a human being, (2) the Face of Allah - the divine essence, (3) the front or direction, (4) the aspect or presence. The famous hadith states: The Heart of the believer lies between two fingers of the Most Merciful. The wajh in Sufism is the spiritual face - the outward sign of the heart's state.
shades.hadith_ar: كُلُّ شَىۡءٍ هَالِكٌ إِلَّا وَجۡهَهُۥ
shades.hadith_en: Everything will be destroyed except His Face

shades.name_en: Wajh Allah - The Face of Allah
shades.name_ar: وَجۡهُ اللَّهِ - الصِّفَةُ الْإِلَهِيَّةُ، الذَّاتُ الْمُقَدَّسَةُ
shades.explanation: Wajh Allah (the Face of Allah) is one of the most discussed divine attributes in Islamic theology. The Quran says: The Face of your Lord will remain, full of majesty and honor (55:27). Ahl al-Sunnah affirm al-wajh as an attribute of Allah without tashbih (likening to creation) and without tashbih of the direction. The famous hadith states: Allah has ninety-nine Names. al-Wajh is the attribute of divine presence - the One who is the ultimate goal of all creation. The believer seeks al-wajh Allah - His pleasure, His reward, His presence.
shades.hadith_ar: يَبۡقَىٰ وَجۡهُ رَبِّكَ ذُو ٱلۡجَلَـٰلِ وَٱلۡإِكۡرَامِ
shades.hadith_en: The face of your Lord, Owner of Majesty and Honor, will remain

shades.explanation: al-Mu'ajaha (face to face) in the Quran refers to meeting directly. The famous hadith Qudsi states: I have prepared for My righteous servants what no eye has seen. The mu'ajaha in Sufism is the highest spiritual state - meeting Allah directly. The Quran says: So when you have made a decision, then rely upon Allah (3:159). The mu'ajaha is the reward of the muqarrabun (those drawn near to Allah) - they will see Allah face to face in Paradise. The famous hadith states: The people of Paradise will see their Lord without any doubt.
shades.hadith_ar: إِنَّ أَوۡلِيَآءَ ٱللَّهِ لَا خَوۡفٌ عَلَيۡهِمۡ وَلَا هُمۡ يَحۡزَنُونَ
shades.hadith_en: Indeed the awliya of Allah - no fear shall be upon them, nor shall they grieve

shades.name_ar: التَّوَجُّهُ - التَّوَجُّهُ نَحۡوَ اللَّهِ، الْإِقۡبَالُ عَلَيۡهِ
shades.explanation: at-Tawajjuh (the turning, the direction) in the Quran refers to the act of turning toward Allah. The Quran says: To Allah belongs the East and the West, so wherever you turn there is the face of Allah (2:115). at-Tawajjuh is the spiritual act of directing the heart toward Allah. The famous hadith states: The believer turns toward Allah in every state. at-Tawajjuh in Sufism is one of the highest stations - the seeker who has turned fully toward Allah in his heart.
shades.hadith_ar: فَأَيۡنَمَا تُوَلُّواْ فَثَمَّ وَجۡهُ ٱللَّهِ
shades.hadith_en: So wherever you turn, there is the Face of Allah

meaning.en: To return, reward. The root denotes reward or garment.

lexical_analysis.ibn_faris: الثَّاءُ وَالْوَاوُ وَالْبَاءُ أَصْلٌ يَدُلُّ عَلَى رُجُوعٍ أَوْ لِبَاسٍ
lexical_analysis.al_raghib: ثَابَ: رَجَعَ. وَالثَّوْبُ: الْمَلْبَسُ

quran_examples.ar: إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ يُدۡخِلُ ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ وَعَمِلُواْ ٱلصَّـٰلِحَـٰتِ جَنَّـٰتٍۢ تَجۡرِى مِن تَحۡتِهَا ٱلۡأَنۡهَـٰرُ
quran_examples.en: Indeed Allah will admit those who believe and do righteous deeds to gardens beneath which rivers flow

quran_examples.ar: ثُمَّ لۡيَقۡضُواْ تَفَثَهُمۡ وَلۡيُوفُواْ نُذُورَهُمۡ وَلۡيَطَوَّفُواْ بِٱلۡبَيۡتِ ٱلۡعَتِيقِ
quran_examples.en: Then let them purify themselves, fulfill their vows, and circumambulate the Ancient House

hadith.ar: مَنْ جَاءَ بِالْحَسَنَةِ فَلَهُ عَشْرُ أَمْثَالِهَا
hadith.en: Whoever comes with a good deed will have ten times its like

hadith.ar: إِنَّ مَثَلَ الَّذِي يَعْمَلُ سُوءًا ثُمَّ يَتُوبُ مِنْ بَعْدِهِ
hadith.en: The example of one who does evil then repents

shades.explanation: ath-Thawb (the garment) in the Quran is one of the most mentioned items. The Quran says: O children of Adam, We have bestowed upon you clothing to conceal your private parts and as adornment (7:26). ath-Thawb has both literal and metaphorical meanings: (1) the literal garment (libas - 2:187), (2) the garment of taqwa (the garment of God-consciousness - 7:26), (3) the garments of Paradise (18:31, 22:23). The famous hadith states: Eat and drink, but do not waste - Allah does not love the wasters. The thawb in Sufism is the inner garment of iman.
shades.hadith_ar: يَـٰبَنِىٓ ءَادَمَ قَدۡ أَنزَلۡنَا عَلَيۡكُمۡ لِبَاسًۭا يُوَٰرِى سَوۡءَٰتِكُمۡ
shades.hadith_en: O children of Adam, We have bestowed upon you clothing to conceal your private parts

shades.explanation: ath-Thawab (the reward, the recompense) in the Quran is one of the most beautiful concepts. The Quran says: And the reward of the Hereafter is better for those who believed and were conscious of Allah (12:57). ath-Thawab is the divine reward for righteous deeds. The famous hadith states: Whoever comes on the Day of Resurrection with a good deed will have ten times its like. ath-Thawab in Islam is: (1) the reward in this life (barakah), (2) the reward in the grave (jannat al-barzakh), (3) the reward in the Hereafter (jannat al-akhirah).
shades.hadith_ar: جَزَآؤُاْ ٱلۡإِحۡسَـٰنِ إِلَّا ٱلۡإِحۡسَـٰنُ
shades.hadith_en: The reward of goodness is nothing but goodness

shades.explanation: ath-Tha'ifa (the group, the faction) in the Quran refers to a group of people. The Quran says: And if there are among you those who believe and those who disbelieve, then be patient until Allah judges between us (7:87). ath-Tha'ifa is one of the ways Allah tests His servants - the existence of different groups. The famous hadith states: A group from my ummah will continue to be victorious over the truth. The ta'ifa in Sufism is the spiritual community - the jamā'ah of the seekers.
shades.hadith_ar: وَلَا تَزَالُ طَائِفَةٌۭ مِّنۡ أُمَّتِى ظَاهِرِينَ عَلَى ٱلۡحَقِّ
shades.hadith_en: A group from my ummah will continue to be victorious over the truth

shades.explanation: at-Tawaf (the circumambulating) is the ritual of walking around the Ka'bah seven times during Hajj or Umrah. The Quran says: And let them purify themselves and complete their vows and circumambulate [yatwaffu] the Ancient House (22:29). at-Tawaf is one of the pillars of Hajj and Umrah. The famous hadith states: The tawaf around the Ka'bah is prayer - but Allah has allowed speaking during it. The tawaf in Sufism is the spiritual circumambulation - the heart turning around the dhikr of Allah.
shades.hadith_ar: ثُمَّ لۡيَطَوَّفُواْ بِٱلۡبَيۡتِ ٱلۡعَتِيقِ
shades.hadith_en: Then let them circumambulate the Ancient House

meaning.en: To reach, attain. The root denotes reaching or delivering.

lexical_analysis.ibn_faris: الْبَاءُ وَاللَّامُ وَالْغَيْنُ أَصْلٌ يَدُلُّ عَلَى وُصُولٍ
lexical_analysis.al_raghib: بَلَغَ: وَصَلَ. وَالْبَالِغُ: الَّذِي بَلَغَ الْحُلُمَ

quran_examples.ar: يَـٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلرَّسُولُ بَلِّغۡ مَآ أُنزِلَ إِلَيۡكَ مِن رَّبِّكَ
quran_examples.en: O Messenger, announce what has been revealed to you from your Lord
quran_examples.context: The command to deliver the message

quran_examples.ar: وَٱبۡتَلُواْ ٱلۡيَتَـٰمَىٰ حَتَّىٰٓ إِذَا بَلَغُواْ ٱلنِّكَاحَ
quran_examples.en: And test the orphans until they reach marriageable age

hadith.ar: بَلِّغُوا عَنِّي وَلَوْ آيَةً
hadith.en: Convey from me, even if it is one verse

hadith.ar: رُفِعَ الْقَلَمُ عَنْ ثَلَاثَةٍ
hadith.en: The pen is lifted from three

shades.explanation: al-Bulugh (the reaching) in the Quran is one of the most fundamental concepts. The Quran says: That he may attain his full maturity and reach his appointed term (22:5). al-Bulugh in the Quran is: al-bulugh al-'umr (reaching maturity), al-bulugh al-risala (delivering the message), al-bulugh al-maqsud (reaching the goal). The famous hadith states: Convey from me, even if it is one verse. al-Bulugh is the attainment of the goal through iman, taqwa, and good deeds.
shades.hadith_ar: لِّيُبَلِّغَ أَشُدَّهُۥ وَيَبۡلُغَ أَيَّامَهُ
shades.hadith_en: That he may attain his full maturity and reach his appointed term

shades.explanation: al-Baligh (the adult) in the Quran is one who has reached puberty. The Quran says: And test the orphans until they reach marriageable age (4:6). The baligh is fully responsible for his deeds. The famous hadith states: The pen is lifted from three: from the sleeper until he awakes, from the child until he reaches puberty. The baligh in Sufism is one who has reached spiritual maturity - the state of being close to Allah.
shades.hadith_ar: وَٱبۡتَلُواْ ٱلۡيَتَـٰمَىٰ حَتَّىٰٓ إِذَا بَلَغُواْ ٱلنِّكَاحَ
shades.hadith_en: And test the orphans until they reach marriageable age

shades.explanation: al-Balagha (the message) in the Quran is one of the most noble acts. The Quran says: O Messenger, announce what has been revealed to you from your Lord (5:67). al-Balagha is the act of delivering the message - one of the highest deeds. The famous hadith states: Convey from me, even if it is one verse. The balagha in Sufism is the transmission of divine knowledge from the murshid to the seeker.
shades.hadith_ar: يَـٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلرَّسُولُ بَلِّغۡ مَآ أُنزِلَ إِلَيۡكَ مِن رَّبِّكَ
shades.hadith_en: O Messenger, announce what has been revealed to you from your Lord

shades.explanation: al-Muballigh (the deliverer) in the Quran is one who delivers the message. The famous hadith states: There will be a time upon my ummah when people will say: Look at the muballigh who is delivering the message. The muballigh in Islam is the one who conveys the message of Allah to His servants. The muballigh in Sufism is the murshid - the one who delivers divine knowledge to the seekers.
shades.hadith_ar: بَلِّغُوا عَنِّي وَلَوْ آيَةً
shades.hadith_en: Convey from me, even if it is one verse

meaning.en: To be few. The root denotes fewness, little, or smallness.

lexical_analysis.ibn_faris: الْقَافُ وَاللَّامُ أَصْلٌ يَدُلُّ عَلَى قِلَّةٍ
lexical_analysis.al_raghib: قَلَّ: لَمْ يَكْثُرْ. وَقَلِيلٌ: ضِدُّ كَثِيرٍ

quran_examples.ar: وَقَلِيلٌۭ مِّنۡ عِبَادِىَ ٱلشَّكُورُ
quran_examples.en: And how few of My servants are truly grateful

quran_examples.ar: وَلَا تَقۡعُدُواْ بِكُلِّ صِرَٰطٍۢ تُوعِدُونَ
quran_examples.en: And do not sit on every road, threatening

hadith.ar: طُوبَى لِلْغُرَبَاءِ
hadith.en: How wonderful for the strangers

hadith.ar: لَا تَكْثُرُوا الْكَلَامَ بِغَيْرِ ذِكْرِ اللَّهِ
hadith.en: Do not speak much without the dhikr of Allah

shades.explanation: al-Qilla (the few) in the Quran is the opposite of al-kathra (the many). The Quran says: And how few of My servants are truly grateful (34:13). al-Qilla in the Quran is: al-qilla al-'adadiyya (few in number), al-qilla al-zamaniyya (few in time). The famous hadith states: A few people who follow the truth are better than many who follow falsehood. al-Qilla in Sufism is the state of being content with little.
shades.hadith_ar: وَقَلِيلٌۭ مِّنۡ عِبَادِىَ ٱلشَّكُورُ
shades.hadith_en: And how few of My servants are truly grateful

shades.explanation: al-Qalil (the little) in the Quran is one of the most frequent qualifiers. al-Qalil in the Quran is: qalil al-'adad (few in number - 7:86), qalil al-'amal (few in deeds), qalil al-'ilm (little in knowledge). The Quran says: How little you are grateful (16:18, 40:61). The qalil in Sufism is the state of being content with little - the inner poverty before Allah.
shades.hadith_ar: قَلِيلًا مَّا تَشۡكُرُونَ
shades.hadith_en: How little you are grateful

shades.explanation: Qallada (to find little) is the verb form of qilla. The famous hadith states: Whoever is saved from the stinginess of his soul has attained success. The qallada in Sufism is the state of feeling that one's good deeds are few. The Quran says: And those who believe and do righteous deeds - We will surely admit them to gardens (4:57). The qallada of the righteous believer - his good deeds seem few compared to what he owes to Allah.
shades.hadith_ar: وَقَلِيلٌۭ مِّنَ ٱلۡأَخِرِينَ
shades.hadith_en: And few of the latter

shades.explanation: al-Muqallad (the entrusted) in the Quran refers to one who is entrusted with authority. The Quran says: Those to whom We had given the Book before it - they are believers in it (28:52). al-Muqallad is one who is entrusted with responsibility. The famous hadith states: Each of you is a shepherd and each of you is responsible for his flock. The muqallad in Sufism is the one who has been given spiritual authority - the murshid who guides the seekers.
shades.hadith_ar: قُلۡ لَّا أَسۡـَٔلُكُمۡ عَلَيۡهِ أَجۡرًا
shades.hadith_en: Say: I do not ask of you for it any reward

meaning.en: To harm. The root denotes harm or damage.

lexical_analysis.ibn_faris: الضَّادُ وَالرَّاءُ أَصْلٌ يَدُلُّ عَلَى ضَرَرٍ
lexical_analysis.al_raghib: الضَّرُّ: ضِدُّ النَّفْعِ. وَضَرَّ: أَذَى

quran_examples.ar: قُلۡ أَعُوذُ بِرَبِّ ٱلنَّاسِ
quran_examples.en: Say: I seek refuge in the Lord of mankind
quran_examples.context: The refuge in Allah from evil

quran_examples.ar: فَمَنِ ٱضۡطُرَّ غَيۡرَ بَاغٍۢ وَلَا عَادٍۢ فَلَآ إِثۡمَ عَلَيۡهِ
quran_examples.en: But whoever is forced by necessity without willful disobedience, there is no sin upon him
quran_examples.context: The permissibility in case of necessity

hadith.ar: مَنْ آذَى مُسْلِمًا آذَاهُ اللَّهُ
hadith.en: Whoever harms a Muslim, Allah will harm him

hadith.ar: لَا يُؤْمِنُ الْمُسْلِمُ مَنْ لَمْ يَأْمَنْ جَارُهُ بَوَائِقَهُ
hadith.en: The Muslim is not the one whose neighbor is not safe from his evil

shades.explanation: ad-Darr (the harm) in the Quran is one of the most mentioned evils. The Quran says: Say: I seek refuge in the Lord of mankind (114:1). ad-Darr in the Quran is: ad-darr al-maddi (material harm), ad-darr al-ma'nawi (spiritual harm), ad-darr al-akhira (the harm of the Hereafter). The famous hadith states: Allah does not burden a soul beyond its capacity.
shades.hadith_ar: قُلۡ أَعُوذُ بِرَبِّ ٱلنَّاسِ
shades.hadith_en: Say: I seek refuge in the Lord of mankind

shades.explanation: ad-Darar (the persistent harm) in the Quran refers to repeated harm. The Quran says: But whoever returns to wrongdoing - We will punish him (5:95). ad-Darar is the act of repeatedly harming others - one of the major sins. The famous hadith states: The believer is not the one who harms others. ad-Darar in Sufism is the persistent harm to the spiritual path - the return to sins after repentance.
shades.hadith_ar: لَا ضَيۡرَ ۖ إِلَّا ضَرَآءَ ٱلۡعَيۡشِ ٱلۡأَخِرَةِ
shades.hadith_en: There is no harm except the harm of the life of the Hereafter

shades.explanation: al-Mudir (the one who harms) in the Quran is one who causes harm. The famous hadith states: Whoever harms a Muslim, Allah will harm him. al-Mudir is one who causes harm to others - through word, deed, or intention. al-Mudir in Sufism is the one who causes harm to the spiritual path - the one who turns others away from Allah.
shades.hadith_ar: مَنْ آذَى مُسْلِمًا آذَاهُ اللَّهُ
shades.hadith_en: Whoever harms a Muslim, Allah will harm him

shades.explanation: Idtarra (to be forced) is the verb form indicating duress. The Quran says: But whoever is forced by necessity without willful disobedience - there is no sin upon him (2:173). al-Idtirar is the state of being compelled by necessity - which permits what is normally haram. The famous hadith states: Allah does not burden a soul beyond its capacity. al-Idtirar in Sufism is the state of spiritual compulsion - the seeker drawn to Allah by His grace.
shades.hadith_ar: فَمَنِ ٱضۡطُرَّ غَيۡرَ بَاغٍۢ وَلَا عَادٍۢ فَلَآ إِثۡمَ عَلَيۡهِ
shades.hadith_en: But whoever is forced by necessity without willful disobedience, there is no sin upon him

meaning.en: To be mighty, severe. The root denotes might or distress.

lexical_analysis.ibn_faris: الْبَاءُ وَالْهَمْزَةُ وَالسِّينُ أَصْلٌ يَدُلُّ عَلَى شِدَّةٍ
lexical_analysis.al_raghib: الْبَأْسُ: الشِّدَّةُ فِي الْحَرْبِ. وَبَأَسَ: اشْتَدَّ

quran_examples.ar: وَٱذۡكُرُوٓاْ إِذۡ أَنتُمۡ قَلِيلٌۭ مُّسۡتَضۡعَفُونَ فِى ٱلۡأَرۡضِ
quran_examples.en: And remember when you were few and oppressed in the land

quran_examples.ar: وَلَنَبۡلُوَنَّكُم بِشَىۡءٍۢ مِّنَ ٱلۡخَوۡفِ وَٱلۡجُوعِ وَنَقۡصٍۢ مِّنَ ٱلۡأَمۡوَٰلِ
quran_examples.en: And We will surely test you with something of fear and hunger

hadith.ar: الْمُؤْمِنُ الْقَوِيُّ خَيْرٌ وَأَحَبُّ إِلَى اللَّهِ مِنَ الْمُؤْمِنِ الضَّعِيفِ
hadith.en: The strong believer is better and more beloved to Allah than the weak believer

hadith.ar: إِنَّمَا الْأَعْمَالُ بِالنِّيَّاتِ
hadith.en: Indeed deeds are judged by intentions

shades.explanation: al-Ba's (the might, the distress) in the Quran has dual meanings: (1) al-ba's al-harb (military might), (2) al-ba's al-ba'sa' (distress, hardship). The Quran says: And remember when you were few and oppressed in the land (8:26). al-Ba's in the Quran is used for the trials of the believers and the might of Allah. The famous hadith states: The strong believer is better and more beloved to Allah than the weak believer. al-Ba's in Sufism is the trial that purifies the soul.
shades.hadith_ar: وَٱذۡكُرُوٓاْ إِذۡ أَنتُمۡ قَلِيلٌۭ مُّسۡتَضۡعَفُونَ فِى ٱلۡأَرۡضِ
shades.hadith_en: And remember when you were few and oppressed in the land

shades.explanation: al-Ba'sa' (the distress) in the Quran refers to severe hardship. The Quran says: And We will surely test you with something of fear and hunger and a loss of wealth and lives and fruits (2:155). The ba'sa' is one of the tests of Allah - it purifies the believer and raises his rank. The famous hadith states: How wonderful is the affair of the believer - all of it is good for him. The ba'sa' in Sufism is the spiritual trial - the state of being tested in the path to Allah.
shades.hadith_ar: لَقَدۡ كَانَ لَكُمۡ فِى رَسُولِ ٱللَّهِ أُسۡوَةٌ حَسَنَةٌ
shades.hadith_en: There has certainly been for you in the Messenger of Allah an excellent example

shades.explanation: al-Ba'is (the mighty, the brave) in the Quran refers to the strong and brave. The Quran says: And those who strive for Us - We will surely guide them to Our ways (29:69). The ba'is is the brave mujahid who fights for the cause of Allah. The famous hadith states: The best of the warriors are those who fight for the sake of Allah. The ba'is in Sufism is the spiritual warrior - the one who fights the ego and the passions for the sake of Allah.
shades.hadith_ar: وَجَـٰهِدُوا فِى ٱللَّهِ حَقَّ جِهَادِهِۦ
shades.hadith_en: And strive for Allah with the striving due to Him

shades.explanation: Yabisu (to be hard, severe) is the verb form. The famous hadith states: The most beloved of deeds to Allah is the most consistent, even if small. The yabisu in the Quran is the state of being severe - whether in hardship or in punishment. The Quran says: So Allah punished them for their sins (3:11). The yabisu in Sufism is the strict adherence to the path - the believer who is firm in his obedience to Allah.
shades.hadith_ar: فَأَصَابَهُمۡ سَيِّئَاتُ مَا كَسَبُواْ
shades.hadith_en: And evil consequences struck them for what they had earned

meaning.en: To spend the night, house. The root denotes house or night residence.

lexical_analysis.ibn_faris: الْبَاءُ وَالْيَاءُ وَالتَّاءُ أَصْلٌ يَدُلُّ عَلَى مَكَانِ سُكْنَى
lexical_analysis.al_raghib: الْبَيْتُ: الْمَنْزِلُ. وَبَاتَ: أَقَامَ بِاللَّيْلِ

quran_examples.ar: وَٱجۡعَلۡنَا بِمَنَآسِكَ وَمِن ذُرِّيَّـٰتِنَآ أُمَّةًۭ يُسۡلِمُونَ لَكَ
quran_examples.en: And take, [O Ibrahim], from the Site a place of prayer

quran_examples.ar: لَّن تَنفِعَكُمُ ٱلۡأَرۡحَامُ وَلَآ ٱلۡأَوۡلَـٰدُ يَوۡمَ ٱلۡقِيَـٰمَةِ
quran_examples.en: Never will kinship benefit you on the Day of Resurrection

hadith.ar: صَلَاةُ الْجَمَاعَةِ تَفْضُلُ صَلَاةَ الْفَذِّ بِسَبْعٍ وَعِشْرِينَ دَرَجَةً
hadith.en: Prayer in congregation is 27 degrees better than praying alone

hadith.ar: إِنَّ اللَّهَ حَرَّمَ مَكَّةَ يَوْمَ خَلَقَ السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضَ
hadith.en: Indeed Allah has made Makkah sacred the day He created the heavens and the earth

shades.explanation: al-Bayt (the house) in the Quran is one of the most frequent terms. The Quran says: And [recall] when We made the House [bayt] a place of return for the people and [a place of] security (2:125). al-Bayt in the Quran has multiple meanings: (1) al-bayt al-mamur (the much-frequented house - 52:4), (2) al-bayt al-ma'mur (the populated house - the Ka'bah), (3) al-bayt al-haram (the sacred house). The famous hadith states: Allah made Makkah sacred the day He created the heavens and the earth. The bayt in Sufism is the heart - the house of the believer's iman.
shades.hadith_ar: وَٱجۡعَلُواْ بُيُوتَكُمۡ قِبۡلَةً
shades.hadith_en: And make your houses a direction [of prayer]

shades.explanation: al-Bayt al-Haram (the Sacred House) in the Quran is the Ka'bah in Makkah. The Quran says: And [due] to Allah from the people is a pilgrimage to the House - for whoever is able to find thereto a way (3:97). The Bayt al-Haram is the qiblah of all Muslims - the direction of prayer. The famous hadith states: Allah has made Makkah sacred and has not made it haram for any other. The bayt in Sufism is the spiritual house - the place where the seeker meets his Lord.
shades.hadith_ar: جَعَلَ ٱللَّهُ ٱلۡكَعۡبَةَ ٱلۡبَيۡتَ ٱلۡحَرَامَ قِيَـٰمًۭا لِّلنَّاسِ
shades.hadith_en: Allah has made the Ka'bah, the Sacred House, a standing place for the people

shades.name_en: Baytu al-Mal - The House of Wealth
shades.name_ar: بَيۡتُ الۡمَالِ - مَكَانُ حِفۡظِ الْأَمۡوَالِ الْعَامَّةِ
shades.explanation: Baytu al-Mal (the house of wealth) in Islamic law refers to the public treasury. The Quran says: And know that whatever thing you gain - a fifth of it is for Allah and for the Messenger (8:41). Baytu al-Mal is the institution of the public treasury - established by the Prophet to manage the financial affairs of the Muslim ummah. The famous hadith states: The best of rulers are those who maintain the baytu al-mal and fulfill its obligations. The baytu al-mal in Sufism is the heart - the place where divine gifts are stored.
shades.hadith_ar: وَٱعۡلَمُوٓاْ أَنَّمَا غَنِمۡتُم مِّن شَىۡءٍۢ فَأَنَّ لِلَّهِ خُمُسَهُۥ
shades.hadith_en: And know that whatever thing you gain - a fifth of it is for Allah

shades.explanation: al-Batiyy (the inhabitant) in the Quran refers to one who lives in the house. The famous hadith states: The best of houses are those in which the orphans are treated kindly. al-Batiyy in the Quran is the one who is settled in the home - the one who maintains the family. al-Batiyy in Sufism is the one who is established in the dhikr of Allah - the home of his heart is filled with divine remembrance.
shades.hadith_ar: وَمَثَلُ ٱلَّذِينَ يُنفِقُونَ أَمۡوَٰلَهُمۡ فِى سَبِيلِ ٱللَّهِ
shades.hadith_en: And the example of those who spend their wealth in the way of Allah

meaning.en: To be rich, sufficient. The root denotes richness or self-sufficiency.

lexical_analysis.ibn_faris: الْغَيْنُ وَالنُّونُ وَالْيَاءُ أَصْلٌ يَدُلُّ عَلَى اسْتِغْنَاءٍ
lexical_analysis.al_raghib: الْغِنَى: ضِدُّ الْفَقْرِ. وَغَنِيَ: اسْتَغْنَى

quran_examples.ar: يَـٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلۡإِنسَـٰنُ أَنتَ ٱلۡفَقِيرُ إِلَى ٱللَّهِ وَٱللَّهُ هُوَ ٱلۡغَنِىُّ ٱلۡحَمِيدُ
quran_examples.en: O mankind, you are those in need of Allah; but Allah is the Free of need, the Praiseworthy

quran_examples.ar: وَمَن يَتَّقِ ٱللَّهَ يَجۡعَل لَّهُۥ مَخۡرَجًۭا
quran_examples.en: And whoever fears Allah, He will provide for him a way out

hadith.ar: لَيْسَ الْمِسْكِينُ الَّذِي تَرُدُّهُ اللُّقْمَةُ
hadith.en: The miskeen is not the one who is turned away by a morsel

hadith.ar: أَغْنَى رَجُلًا بَعَسَبٍ أَوْ بِفَسَبٍ
hadith.en: A man may become rich through work or through inheritance

shades.explanation: al-Ghina (the richness) in the Quran is one of the most important concepts. The Quran says: And whoever fears Allah, He will provide for him a way out (65:2). al-Ghina in the Quran has dual meanings: (1) al-ghina al-maddi (material richness), (2) al-ghina al-qalbi (spiritual richness - contentment). The famous hadith states: The richest of you is the one who is richest in iman. al-Ghina in Sufism is the state of contentment - the inner richness that comes from iman.
shades.hadith_ar: وَمَن يُطِعِ ٱللَّهَ وَٱلرَّسُولَ فَأُوْلَـٰٓئِكَ مَعَ ٱلَّذِينَ أَنۡعَمَ ٱللَّهُ عَلَيۡهِم
shades.hadith_en: And whoever obeys Allah and the Messenger will be with those whom Allah has blessed

shades.name_ar: الْغَنِيُّ - الَّذِي لَا يَحۡتَاجُ إِلَى غَيۡرِهِ
shades.explanation: al-Ghani (the Self-Sufficient) is one of the most frequent Names of Allah in the Quran. al-Ghani is the One who is free from all need - He is the Self-Sufficient, the One who enriches His servants. The Quran says: O mankind, you are those in need of Allah [al-fuqara']; but Allah is the Free of need [al-Ghani], the Praiseworthy (35:15). The famous hadith states: Allah is al-Ghani - He has no need for the worship of His servants. al-Ghani is paired with al-Hamid (the Praiseworthy) in the Quran.
shades.hadith_ar: لَّن يَسۡتَنكِفَ ٱلۡمَسِيحُ أَن يَكُونَ عَبۡدًۭا لِّلَّهِ
shades.hadith_en: The Messiah would never disdain to be a servant of Allah

shades.explanation: al-Mustaghni (the self-sufficient) in the Quran refers to one who considers himself independent. The Quran says: And whoever is saved from the stinginess of his soul - those are the successful ones (64:16). The mustaghni is one who considers himself in need of nothing - but this is a delusion for the kuffar. The famous hadith states: The rich have many good deeds. al-Mustaghni in Sufism is the one who has become independent of created beings - the state of pure tawakkul (reliance on Allah).
shades.hadith_ar: وَمَن يَتَوَكَّلۡ عَلَى ٱللَّهِ فَهُوَ حَسۡبُهُۥٓ
shades.hadith_en: And whoever relies upon Allah - then He is sufficient for him

shades.explanation: Taghana (to suffice, to enrich) is the verb form of ghina. The Quran says: And if they turn away - Allah is Free of need [taghana] (3:97). taghana Allah is the sufficiency - He has no need of the servant's obedience. The famous hadith states: My servants, if the first of you and the last of you stood before Me and asked of Me, I would give each one what he asked - that would not diminish what is with Me. al-Ghana is the divine sufficiency - the believer seeks this state through iman and tawakkul.
shades.hadith_ar: يَـٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلۡإِنسَـٰنُ أَنتَ ٱلۡفَقِيرُ إِلَى ٱللَّهِ
shades.hadith_en: O mankind, you are those in need of Allah

meaning.en: To be a man. The root denotes man, foot, or strength.

lexical_analysis.ibn_faris: الرَّاءُ وَالْجِيمُ وَاللَّامُ أَصْلٌ يَدُلُّ عَلَى ثَبَاتٍ
lexical_analysis.al_raghib: الرَّجُلُ: الذَّكَرُ مِنَ الْحَيَوَانِ. وَرَجَلَ: ثَبَتَ

quran_examples.ar: وَمَن يَعۡمَلۡ مِنَ ٱلصَّـٰلِحَـٰتِ مِن ذَكَرٍ أَوۡ أُنثَىٰ وَهُوَ مُؤۡمِنٌۭ
quran_examples.en: And whoever does righteous deeds, whether male or female, while being a believer
quran_examples.context: The equality of men and women in deeds

quran_examples.ar: مِّنَ ٱلۡمُؤۡمِنِينَ رِجَالٌۭ صَدَقُواْ مَا عَـٰهَدُواْ ٱللَّهَ عَلَيۡهِۦ
quran_examples.en: Among the believers are men who have been true to their covenant with Allah

hadith.ar: خَيْرُكُمْ خَيْرُكُمْ لِأَهْلِهِ وَأَنَا خَيْرُكُمْ لِأَهْلِي
hadith.en: The best of you are those who are best to their families, and I am the best of you to my family

hadith.ar: لَا يَزَالُ الْبَلَاءُ بِالْمُؤْمِنِ وَالْمُؤْمِنَةِ
hadith.en: Trials continue to befall the believer and the believing woman

shades.explanation: al-Rajul (the man) in the Quran is one of the most frequent terms. The Quran says: And whoever does righteous deeds, whether male or female, while being a believer - they will enter Paradise (4:124). al-Rajul in the Quran has multiple meanings: (1) al-rajul al-bashari (a human male), (2) al-rajul al-kamil (a complete man), (3) al-rajul al-mumin (a believing man). The famous hadith states: The best of you are those who learn the Quran and teach it. The rajul in Sufism is the spiritual man - the one who has reached spiritual perfection.
shades.hadith_ar: لَّيۡسَ ٱلۡأَعۡمَىٰ وَلَا ٱلۡأَعۡشَىٰ
shades.hadith_en: Not equal are the blind and the seeing

shades.explanation: Rajul al-Karim (the generous man) in the Quran is the one who is generous with his wealth and his time. The Quran says: And if they turn away from you, then rely upon Allah (8:62). The rajul al-karim is one of the praised qualities in the Quran - the generous believer. The famous hadith states: The generous man is close to Allah, close to Paradise, close to the people. al-Karim in Sufism is one who gives without counting - the spiritual generosity of the believer to others.
shades.hadith_ar: وَجَـٰهِدۡهُمۡ بِهِۦ جِهَادًۭا كَبِيرًۭا
shades.hadith_en: And struggle against them with it with great struggle

shades.explanation: ar-Rijl (the foot) in the Quran is mentioned in various contexts. The Quran says: And the feet will bear witness to what they earned (36:65). The rijl is the lower limb of the human body - the part that walks. The famous hadith states: The feet of the son of Adam will not move from before his Lord on the Day of Resurrection until he is questioned about five things. ar-Rijl in Sufism is the footstep on the spiritual path - the movement of the heart toward Allah.
shades.hadith_ar: وَتَذُوبُ أَبۡصَـٰرُهُمۡ تَرۡهَقُهُمۡ ذِلَّةٌۭ
shades.hadith_en: And their eyes will be humbled, overwhelming them will be humiliation

shades.explanation: ar-Rajal (the men, the group) in the Quran is the plural of rajul. The Quran says: Among the believers are men [rijal] who have been true to their covenant with Allah (33:23). The rijal in the Quran is the men who are steadfast - the truthful believers. The famous hadith states: The rijal of iman are those who are firm in their faith. The rijal in Sufism is the spiritual men - the awliya who have reached the highest stations of faith.
shades.hadith_ar: مِّنَ ٱلۡمُؤۡمِنِينَ رِجَالٌۭ صَدَقُواْ مَا عَـٰهَدُواْ ٱللَّهَ عَلَيۡهِ
shades.hadith_en: Among the believers are men who have been true to their covenant with Allah

meaning.en: To be high. The root denotes height, elevation, or exaltation.

lexical_analysis.ibn_faris: الْعَيْنُ وَاللَّامُ وَالْوَاوُ أَصْلٌ يَدُلُّ عَلَى عُلُوٍّ
lexical_analysis.al_raghib: الْعُلُوُّ: ضِدُّ السُّفُولِ. وَعَلَا: رَفَعَ

quran_examples.ar: سَبِّحِ ٱسۡمَ رَبِّكَ ٱلۡأَعۡلَى
quran_examples.en: Glorify the name of your Lord, the Most High

quran_examples.ar: ٱللَّهُ لَآ إِلَـٰهَ إِلَّا هُوَ ٱلۡحَىُّ ٱلۡقَيُّومُ
quran_examples.en: Allah - there is no deity except Him, the Ever-Living, the Sustainer of existence

hadith.ar: سُبْحَانَ رَبِّيَ الْأَعْلَى
hadith.en: Glory be to my Lord, the Most High

hadith.ar: إِنَّ اللَّهَ هُوَ الْعَلِيُّ الْكَبِيرُ
hadith.en: Indeed Allah is the Most High, the Supreme

shades.name_en: al-'Ala - The Highest, The Most Exalted
shades.explanation: al-'Ala (the highest) in the Quran is one of the most magnificent attributes. Surah al-A'la (87) is named after this root. The Quran says: Glorify the name of your Lord, the Most High [al-A'la] (87:1). al-'Ala is the attribute of supreme elevation - Allah is above all in His essence, attributes, and actions. The famous hadith states: Allah is al-'Ali al-Kabir (the Most High, the Supreme). al-'Ala in Sufism is the highest spiritual station - the state of fana' (annihilation) in Allah.
shades.hadith_ar: سَبِّحِ ٱسۡمَ رَبِّكَ ٱلۡأَعۡلَى
shades.hadith_en: Glorify the name of your Lord, the Most High

shades.explanation: al-'Ali (the Most High) is one of the most frequent Names of Allah in the Quran. al-'Ali is the One who is above all in His essence and attributes - the Most High. The Quran says: He is the Most High [al-'Ali], the Grand [al-Kabir] (2:255). The famous hadith states: Allah is al-'Ali al-Kabir. al-'Ali is paired with al-Kabir - the High and the Supreme. al-'Ali is the One to whom the believer turns in hardship - the Most High from whom the believer seeks help.
shades.hadith_ar: لَّا تُدۡرِكُهُ ٱلۡأَبۡصَـٰرُ وَهُوَ يُدۡرِكُ ٱلۡأَبۡصَـٰرَ
shades.hadith_en: Vision perceives Him not, but He perceives [all] vision

shades.explanation: al-Istila (the elevation) in the Quran refers to the act of being high. The Quran says: And they took besides Allah other deities that they would be for them a source of strength (45:10). al-Istila in the Quran is: (1) al-istila al-ruhiyy (spiritual elevation), (2) al-istila al-maddi (material elevation). The famous hadith states: The believer is constantly tested - the most tested are the prophets, then the righteous, then the best. al-Istila in Sufism is the elevation of the soul - the spiritual climb to Allah.
shades.hadith_ar: وَفَوۡقَ كُلِّ ذِى عِلۡمٍ عَلِيمٌ
shades.hadith_en: And above every knowledgeable one is one who knows

shades.explanation: al-Mu'tali (the one who ascends) in the Quran refers to one who rises high. The famous hadith states: Allah descends to the lowest heaven every night. The mu'tali in Sufism is the one who has ascended through the spiritual stations. The Quran says: And He subjected to you whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth (45:13). The mu'tali is the believer who has risen above the material world and its attachments - the one whose spirit is connected to the divine.
shades.hadith_ar: عَٱلِمُ ٱلۡغَيۡبِ وَٱلشَّهَـٰدَةِ ٱلۡكَبِيرُ ٱلۡمُتَعَالِ
shades.hadith_en: Knower of the unseen and the witnessed, the Grand, the Most High

meaning.en: To enjoy. The root denotes enjoyment or goods.

lexical_analysis.ibn_faris: الْمِيمُ وَالتَّاءُ وَالْعَيْنُ أَصْلٌ يَدُلُّ عَلَى انْتِفَاعٍ
lexical_analysis.al_raghib: مَتَعَ: أَنْفَعَ. وَمَتَاعٌ: شَيْءٌ يُنْتَفَعُ بِهِ

quran_examples.ar: قُلۡ مَتَـٰعُ ٱلدُّنۡيَا قَلِيلٌۭ
quran_examples.en: Say: The enjoyment of this world is little
quran_examples.context: The temporary nature of the dunya

quran_examples.ar: وَإِن تَعُدُّواْ نِعۡمَتَ ٱللَّهِ لَا تُحۡصُوهَآ
quran_examples.en: And if you should count the favor of Allah, you could not enumerate them

hadith.ar: الدُّنْيَا سِجْنُ الْمُؤْمِنِ وَجَنَّةُ الْكَافِرِ
hadith.en: The world is the prison of the believer and the paradise of the disbeliever

hadith.ar: لَوْ تَعْلَمُونَ مَا أَعْلَمُ لَضَحِكْتُمْ قَلِيلًا وَلَبَكَيْتُمْ كَثِيرًا
hadith.en: If you knew what I know, you would laugh little and weep much

shades.explanation: al-Mata' (the enjoyment) in the Quran is one of the most frequent terms. The Quran says: And whatever enjoyment you have - it is from Allah (16:18). al-Mata' in the Quran has multiple meanings: (1) al-mata' al-dunya (the goods of this world), (2) al-mata' al-akhira (the goods of the Hereafter), (3) al-mata' al-zahir (visible goods), (4) al-mata' al-batin (hidden goods). The famous hadith states: If you knew what I knew, you would laugh little and weep much. al-Mata' in Sufism is the temporary enjoyment of the world - the believer takes only what helps him reach Allah.
shades.hadith_ar: أُحِلَّ لَكُمۡ لَيۡلَةَ ٱلصِّيَامِ ٱلرَّفَثُ إِلَىٰ نِسَآئِكُمۡ
shades.hadith_en: It has been made permissible for you the night preceding fasting to go to your wives

shades.explanation: al-Mutta'in (the enjoyers) in the Quran refers to those who take enjoyment. The Quran says: And We gave them enjoyment for a little (2:126). al-Mutta'in are those who enjoy the dunya - but they will be questioned about every blessing on the Day of Judgment. The famous hadith states: The world is the believer's prison and the disbeliever's paradise. al-Mutta'in in Sufism is the state of taking enjoyment only in Allah - the pure pleasure of His dhikr.
shades.hadith_ar: إِنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُواْ يَتَمَتَّعُونَ وَيَأۡكُلُونَ كَمَا تَأۡكُلُ ٱلۡأَنۡعَـٰمُ
shades.hadith_en: Indeed those who disbelieve enjoy themselves and eat as grazing livestock eat

shades.explanation: al-Mata'un (a brief enjoyment) in the Quran refers to a short period of enjoyment. The Quran says: Say: The enjoyment of this world is little (4:77). al-Mata'un is the brief enjoyment of the dunya - the believer knows that this world is temporary. The famous hadith states: Remember much the one who severs relationships. al-Mata'un in Sufism is the state of brief pleasure - the believer uses it wisely, knowing it will not last.
shades.hadith_ar: قُلۡ مَتَـٰعُ ٱلدُّنۡيَا قَلِيلٌۭ
shades.hadith_en: Say: The enjoyment of this world is little

shades.explanation: Tamatta'a (to be pleased) is the verb form of mata'. The Quran says: And whoever disbelieves - let not his disbelief grieve you (3:177). The tamatta'a of the disbeliever is in the dunya - but it has no value in the akhirah. The famous hadith states: A time will come when the best property will be sheep. al-Tamatta'a in Sufism is the state of taking pleasure in the divine remembrance - the believer who has lost himself in the beauty of Allah.
shades.hadith_ar: وَمَن يُرِدۡ ثَوَابَ ٱلۡأَخِرَةِ نُؤۡتِهِۦ مِنۡهَا
shades.hadith_en: And whoever desires the reward of this world - We will give him of it

meaning.en: To entrust. The root denotes trust, reliance, or appointment.

lexical_analysis.ibn_faris: الْوَاوُ وَالْكَافُ وَاللَّامُ أَصْلٌ يَدُلُّ عَلَى اعْتِمَادٍ
lexical_analysis.al_raghib: الْوَكِيلُ: الْمُفَوَّضُ إِلَيْهِ الْأَمْرُ. وَوَكَلَ: اعْتَمَدَ

quran_examples.ar: وَتَوَكَّلۡ عَلَى ٱللَّهِ ۖ وَكَفَىٰ بِٱللَّهِ وَكِيلًۭا
quran_examples.en: And put your trust in Allah; and sufficient is Allah as Disposer of affairs

quran_examples.ar: وَمَن يَتَوَكَّلۡ عَلَى ٱللَّهِ فَهُوَ حَسۡبُهُۥٓ
quran_examples.en: And whoever relies upon Allah - then He is sufficient for him

hadith.ar: لَوْ أَنَّكُمْ تَتَوَكَّلُونَ عَلَى اللَّهِ حَقَّ تَوَكُّلِهِ لَرَزَقَكُمْ
hadith.en: If you relied upon Allah with true reliance, He would provide for you

hadith.ar: الْمُؤْمِنُ لِلْمُؤْمِنِ كَالْبُنْيَانِ
hadith.en: The believer to the believer is like a building

shades.explanation: al-Wakil (the trustee) in the Quran is one of the most magnificent Names of Allah. The Quran says: And put your trust in Allah, for Allah is the best disposer of affairs (8:62). al-Wakil is the One to whom the servant entrusts his affairs. The famous hadith states: Allah has appointed an angel in charge of the womb. al-Wakil is paired with al-Hafiz - He protects and manages the affairs of His servants.
shades.hadith_ar: وَتَوَكَّلۡ عَلَى ٱللَّهِ ۖ وَكَفَىٰ بِٱللَّهِ وَكِيلًۭا
shades.hadith_en: And put your trust in Allah; and sufficient is Allah as Disposer of affairs

shades.explanation: at-Tawakkul (the reliance) in the Quran is one of the highest spiritual stations. The Quran says: And whoever relies upon Allah - then He is sufficient for him (65:3). The famous hadith states: Were you to rely upon Allah with true reliance, He would provide for you as He provides for the birds. at-Tawakkul in Sufism is one of the highest stations - the believer's heart is attached to Allah alone.
shades.hadith_ar: وَمَن يَتَوَكَّلۡ عَلَى ٱللَّهِ فَهُوَ حَسۡبُهُۥٓ
shades.hadith_en: And whoever relies upon Allah - then He is sufficient for him

shades.explanation: al-Muwakkil (the appointed) in the Quran is one who is entrusted with authority. The famous hadith states: Each of you is a shepherd and each of you is responsible for his flock. al-Muwakkil in Sufism is the one who has been given spiritual authority - the murshid who guides the seekers.
shades.hadith_ar: إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ يُحِبُّ ٱلتَّوَّٰبِينَ وَيُحِبُّ ٱلۡمُتَطَهِّرِينَ
shades.hadith_en: Indeed Allah loves those who repent and those who purify themselves

shades.name_ar: الۡوُكَلَاءُ - جَمۡعُ وَكِيلٍ، الۡحُفَاظُ عَلَى الۡأُمُورِ
shades.explanation: al-Wukala (the trustees) in the Quran refers to those entrusted with affairs. The famous hadith states: Allah does not burden a soul beyond its capacity. The Quran says: O you who believe, do not betray Allah and the Messenger or betray your trusts while you know (8:27). The wukala in Islam are responsible to Allah for their actions.
shades.hadith_ar: يَـٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ لَا تَخُونُواْ ٱللَّهَ وَٱلرَّسُولَ
shades.hadith_en: O you who have believed, do not betray Allah and the Messenger

meaning.en: To think, suppose. The root denotes thought, suspicion, or assumption.

lexical_analysis.ibn_faris: الظَّاءُ وَالنُّونُ أَصْلٌ يَدُلُّ عَلَى تَوَهُّمٍ
lexical_analysis.al_raghib: الظَّنُّ: اعْتِقَادُ الرَّجَحَانِ. وَظَنَّ: تَوَهَّمَ

quran_examples.ar: وَمَا يَتَّبِعُ أَكۡثَرُهُمۡ إِلَّا ظَنًّا
quran_examples.en: And most of them follow nothing but assumption

quran_examples.ar: وَسَيۡعۡلَمُ ٱلَّذِينَ ظَلَمُوٓاْ أَىَّ مُنقَلَبٍۢ يَنقَلِبُونَ
quran_examples.en: And those who have wronged will know what return they will receive

hadith.ar: إِيَّاكُمْ وَالظَّنَّ فَإِنَّ الظَّنَّ أَكْذَبُ الْحَدِيثِ
hadith.en: Beware of assumption, for assumption is the most lying of speech

hadith.ar: حَسْبُكَ أَنْ تَكُونَ مَعَ مَنْ تُحِبُّ
hadith.en: It is enough for you to be with those you love

shades.explanation: az-Zann (the supposition) in the Quran is one of the most frequent terms. The Quran says: And most of them follow nothing but assumption (10:36). az-Zann in the Quran has multiple shades: al-zann al-mujmal (general), al-zann al-khass (specific), al-zann al-ghalib (overwhelming probability). The famous hadith states: Beware of zann - for zann is the most lying of speech. az-Zann in Sufism is intuitive knowledge.
shades.hadith_ar: وَمَا يَتَّبِعُ أَكۡثَرُهُمۡ إِلَّا ظَنًّا
shades.hadith_en: And most of them follow nothing but assumption

shades.explanation: az-Zanin (the thinker) in the Quran is one who assumes or suspects. The Quran says: They think upon Allah the worst of assumptions (8:30). The zanin is one who suspects - either with positive or negative thoughts. The famous hadith states: Beware of zann in everything. az-Zanin in Sufism is the seeker whose intuition is sharp.
shades.hadith_ar: وَلَا تَحۡسَبَنَّ ٱللَّهَ غَـٰفِلًا عَمَّا يَعۡمَلُ ٱلۡظَّـٰلِمُونَ
shades.hadith_en: And never think of Allah unaware of what the wrongdoers do

shades.name_ar: الظَّنُّ الۡغَالِبُ - مَا غَلَبَ عَلَى الظَّنِّ صِحَّتُهُ
shades.explanation: az-Zann al-Ghalib (the overwhelming probability) in Islamic law refers to a supposition that is more likely true than not. az-Zann al-ghalib in Islamic fiqh is used to establish legal rulings. The famous hadith states: The believer's supposition of Allah is always good - for he trusts in His mercy.
shades.hadith_ar: إِنَّ ٱلۡأَبۡرَارَ لَفِى نَعِيمٍ
shades.hadith_en: Indeed the righteous will be in delight

shades.explanation: at-Tazayyun (the suspicion) in the Quran refers to acting upon one's assumptions. at-Tazayyun is the act of following one's zann without seeking knowledge. The famous hadith states: The most beloved of deeds to Allah are those that are most consistent, even if small. at-Tazayyun in Sufism is the speculation about Allah - the believer should think well of Allah always.
shades.hadith_ar: وَٱللَّهُ غَفُورٌۭ رَّحِيمٌۭ
shades.hadith_en: And Allah is Forgiving, Merciful

meaning.en: To dwell, be at peace. The root denotes peace, dwelling, or tranquility.

lexical_analysis.ibn_faris: السِّينُ وَالْكَافُ وَالنُّونُ أَصْلٌ يَدُلُّ عَلَى ثَبَاتٍ
lexical_analysis.al_raghib: سَكَنَ: أَقَامَ. وَالسَّكِينَةُ: الْوَقَارُ

quran_examples.ar: هُوَ ٱلَّذِىٓ أَنزَلَ ٱلسَّكِينَةَ فِى قُلُوبِ ٱلۡمُؤۡمِنِينَ
quran_examples.en: It is He who sent down tranquility into the hearts of the believers
quran_examples.context: The descent of tranquility in the battle of Hunayn

quran_examples.ar: وَٱللَّهُ جَعَلَ لَكُم مِّن بُيُوتِكُمۡ سَكَنًۭا
quran_examples.en: And Allah has made for you from your homes a place of rest
quran_examples.context: The home as a place of rest

hadith.ar: عَجَبًا لِأَمْرِ الْمُؤْمِنِ إِنَّ أَمْرَهُ كُلَّهُ خَيْرٌ
hadith.en: How wonderful is the affair of the believer - all of it is good for him

hadith.ar: إِنَّ أَرْوَاحَ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ لَيَتَلَاقَوْنَ
hadith.en: Indeed the spirits of the believers meet and ask about each other

shades.explanation: as-Sakinah (the tranquility) in the Quran is one of the most magnificent gifts. The Quran says: He is the one who sent down tranquility into the hearts of the believers (48:4). as-Sakinah is the inner peace that Allah places in the hearts of the believers. The famous hadith states: The believer's affair is all good for him. as-Sakinah in Sufism is the highest station of the heart.
shades.hadith_ar: هُوَ ٱلَّذِىٓ أَنزَلَ ٱلسَّكِينَةَ فِى قُلُوبِ ٱلۡمُؤۡمِنِينَ
shades.hadith_en: It is He who sent down tranquility into the hearts of the believers

shades.explanation: al-Maskan (the dwelling) in the Quran is the place of residence. The Quran says: And Allah has made for you your homes a place of rest (16:80). al-Maskan is one of Allah's gifts - the place where the family lives in peace. al-Maskan in Sufism is the spiritual dwelling - the heart where the believer resides with Allah.
shades.hadith_ar: وَٱللَّهُ جَعَلَ لَكُم مِّن بُيُوتِكُمۡ سَكَنًۭا
shades.hadith_en: And Allah has made for you from your homes a place of rest

shades.explanation: as-Sukun (the calm) in the Quran is the opposite of motion. The Quran says: And among His signs is that the heaven and earth remain by His command (30:25). as-Sukun is the state of being at rest - the stillness of the believer. The famous hadith states: The believer is at peace with Allah's decree. as-Sukun in Sufism is the state of being settled in Allah.
shades.hadith_ar: وَمِنۡ ءَايَـٰتِهِۦٓ أَن تَقُومَ ٱلسَّمَآءُ وَٱلۡأَرۡضُ بِأَمۡرِهِۦ
shades.hadith_en: And of His signs is that the heaven and earth remain by His command

shades.explanation: at-Taskin (the making peaceful) in the Quran refers to Allah's act of placing peace in the heart. The Quran says: It is He who sent down tranquility into the hearts of the believers (48:4). at-Taskin is the divine act of calming the heart. The famous hadith states: Allah does not burden a soul beyond its capacity. at-Taskin in Sufism is the act of becoming at peace - the believer's journey to Allah through dhikr.
shades.hadith_ar: إِذۡ يُوحِى رَبُّكَ إِلَى ٱلۡمَلَـٰٓئِكَةِ أَنِّى مَعَكُمۡ
shades.hadith_en: When your Lord revealed to the angels: I am with you

meaning.en: To perish. The root denotes perishing, destruction, or death.

lexical_analysis.ibn_faris: الْهَاءُ وَاللَّامُ وَالْكَافُ أَصْلٌ يَدُلُّ عَلَى فَنَاءٍ
lexical_analysis.al_raghib: هَلَكَ: مَاتَ أَوْ فَنِيَ. وَالْهَلَاكُ: الْمَوْتُ

quran_examples.ar: وَمَآ أَهۡلَكۡنَا مِن قَرۡيَةٍ إِلَّا وَلَهَا كِتَابٌۭ مَّعۡلُومٌ
quran_examples.en: And We did not destroy any city except that it had a known decree
quran_examples.context: The destruction of the ancient peoples

quran_examples.ar: وَجَآءَتۡ سَكۡرَةُ ٱلۡمَوۡتِ بِٱلۡحَقِّ
quran_examples.en: And the intoxication of death will bring the truth

hadith.ar: لَا تُعَذِّبْ بِالنَّارِ عِبَادَكَ الَّذِينَ يُحِبُّونَكَ
hadith.en: Do not punish with the Fire Your servants who love You

hadith.ar: سِيرُوا عَلَى أَثَرِ مَنْ مَاتَ فَإِنَّكُمْ لَا تَدْرُونَ مَا هَلَكَ
hadith.en: Travel in the footsteps of those who died, for you do not know how they perished

shades.explanation: al-Halak (the destruction, the perishing) in the Quran is one of the most mentioned states.
