hadith.en: Whoever shelters a refugee, he is safe

hadith.ar: اللَّهُمَّ أَوِنِي إِلَيۡكَ
hadith.en: O Allah, give me refuge with You

shades.explanation: al-Awa (the refuge) in the Quran refers to a place of shelter. The Quran says: A refuge for the righteous (78:31-32).
shades.hadith_ar: إِنَّ لِلۡمُتَّقِينَ مَفَازًا
shades.hadith_en: Indeed for the righteous is attainment

shades.explanation: al-Mawa (the shelter) in the Quran refers to the final abode. The Quran says: Paradise is their abode (32:19).
shades.hadith_ar: فَالۡجَنَّةُ هِيَ الۡمَأۡوَىٰ
shades.hadith_en: Paradise is the abode

shades.explanation: al-Mawa (the shelter) in the Quran also refers to the destination of the wicked. The Quran says: Then Hellfire is the abode (79:39).
shades.hadith_ar: فَإِنَّ الۡجَحِيمَ هِيَ الۡمَأۡوَىٰ
shades.hadith_en: Indeed Hellfire is the abode

shades.explanation: al-Iwa (the sheltering) in the Quran refers to providing refuge. The famous hadith states: Whoever shelters and protects a believer.
shades.hadith_ar: مَنۡ أَوَىٰ لَاجِئًا
shades.hadith_en: Whoever shelters a refugee

meaning.en: To guide. The root denotes guidance, direction, or leading.

lexical_analysis.ibn_faris: الۡهَاءُ وَالدَّالُ وَالۡيَاءُ أَصۡلٌ يَدُلُّ عَلَى الرَّشَادِ
lexical_analysis.al_raghib: هَدَى: دَلَّ. الۡهُدَىٰ: ضِدُّ الضَّلَالِ

quran_examples.ar: ٱهۡدِنَا الصِّرَٰطَ الۡمُسۡتَقِيمَ
quran_examples.en: Guide us to the straight path

quran_examples.ar: إِنَّكَ لَا تَهۡدِي مَنۡ أَحۡبَبۡتَ
quran_examples.en: You cannot guide whom you love

hadith.ar: مَن يَهۡدِ اللَّهُ فَهُوَ الۡمُهۡتَدِ
hadith.en: Whoever Allah guides is truly guided

hadith.ar: سَلُوا اللَّهَ الۡهُدَىٰ
hadith.en: Ask Allah for guidance

shades.explanation: al-Hidayah (the guidance) in the Quran is the central concept of divine direction. The Quran says: Guide us to the straight path (1:6).
shades.hadith_ar: ٱهۡدِنَا الصِّرَٰطَ الۡمُسۡتَقِيمَ
shades.hadith_en: Guide us to the straight path

shades.explanation: al-Hadi (the Guide) in the Quran is one of Allah's names. The Quran says: Indeed you cannot guide whom you love, but Allah guides whom He wills (28:56).
shades.hadith_ar: إِنَّكَ لَا تَهۡدِي مَنۡ أَحۡبَبۡتَ وَلَٰكِنَّ اللَّهَ يَهۡدِي مَن يَشَآءُ
shades.hadith_en: Indeed you cannot guide whom you love, but Allah guides whom He wills

shades.explanation: al-Huda (the right path) in the Quran refers to true faith. The Quran says: This is the guidance of Allah by which He guides whom He wills (6:71).
shades.hadith_ar: ذَٰلِكَ هُدَى اللَّهِ يَهۡدِي بِهِۦ مَن يَشَآءُ
shades.hadith_en: That is the guidance of Allah by which He guides whom He wills

shades.explanation: al-Ihtida (the seeking of guidance) in the Quran refers to accepting divine guidance. The famous hadith states: Whoever follows this Quran will be guided.
shades.hadith_ar: مَن تَبِعَ الۡقُرۡآنَ هَدَاهُ اللَّهُ
shades.hadith_en: Whoever follows the Quran, Allah will guide him

meaning.en: To pass. The root denotes passing, traversing, or being firm.

lexical_analysis.ibn_faris: الۡمِيمُ وَالرَّاءُ أَصۡلَانِ: أَحَدُهُمَا يَدُلُّ عَلَى النُّفُوذِ
lexical_analysis.al_raghib: مَرَّ: جَازَ. الۡمِرَّةُ: الۡقُوَّةُ

quran_examples.ar: وَإِذَا مَرُّواْ بِهِمۡ يَتَغَامَزُونَ
quran_examples.en: When they passed by them they would wink

quran_examples.ar: ذُو مِرَّةٍۢ فَٱسۡتَوَىٰ
quran_examples.en: The powerful one, then he rose straight

hadith.ar: أَحَبُّ الۡأَعۡمَالِ إِلَى اللَّهِ أَدۡوَمُهَا
hadith.en: The most beloved deeds to Allah are the most consistent

hadith.ar: لَا ضَرَرَ وَلَا ضِرَارَ
hadith.en: No harm and no reciprocating harm

shades.explanation: al-Murur (the passing) in the Quran refers to going by. The Quran says: They pass by them without recognition (37:48-49).
shades.hadith_ar: وَإِذَا مَرُّواْ بِهِمۡ يَتَغَامَزُونَ
shades.hadith_en: And when they passed by them, they would wink at one another

shades.explanation: al-Mirrah (the strength) in the Quran refers to firmness. The Quran says: Of sound judgement (53:6 - Dhu Mirrah - the powerful one).
shades.hadith_ar: ذُو مِرَّةٍۢ فَٱسۡتَوَىٰ
shades.hadith_en: The powerful one, then he rose straight

shades.explanation: al-Mamarr (the passage) in the Quran refers to a place to pass through. The famous hadith states: Do not harm yourself or others.
shades.hadith_ar: لَا ضَرَرَ وَلَا ضِرَارَ
shades.hadith_en: No harm and no reciprocating harm

shades.explanation: al-Istimarar (the continuation) in the Quran refers to persistence. The famous hadith states: The most beloved of deeds to Allah are those that are most consistent.
shades.hadith_ar: أَحَبُّ الۡأَعۡمَالِ إِلَى اللَّهِ أَدۡوَمُهَا
shades.hadith_en: The most beloved of deeds to Allah are the most consistent

meaning.en: To mock. The root denotes mockery, ridicule, or jesting.

lexical_analysis.ibn_faris: الۡهَاءُ وَالزَّايُ وَالهَمۡزَةُ أَصۡلٌ يَدُلُّ عَلَى السُّخۡرِيَةِ
lexical_analysis.al_raghib: هَزِئَ مِنۡهُ: سَخِرَ

quran_examples.ar: وَلَا تَتَّخِذُوٓاْ ءَايَٰتِ اللَّهِ هُزُؤًا
quran_examples.en: Do not take Allah's verses in jest

quran_examples.ar: اللَّهُ يَسۡتَهۡزِئُ بِهِمۡ
quran_examples.en: Allah mocks them

hadith.ar: بِحَسۡبِ امۡرِئٍۢ مِنَ الشَّرِّ أَن يَحۡقِرَ أَخَاهُ الۡمُسۡلِمَ
hadith.en: It is enough evil for a person to belittle his Muslim brother

hadith.ar: لَا يُؤۡمِنُ أَحَدُكُمۡ حَتَّىٰ يُحِبَّ لِأَخِيهِ مَا يُحِبُّ لِنَفۡسِهِ
hadith.en: None of you believes until he loves for his brother what he loves for himself

shades.explanation: al-Huzu (the mockery) in the Quran refers to ridicule and scorn. The Quran says: And take not My signs in jest (2:231).
shades.hadith_ar: وَلَا تَتَّخِذُوٓاْ ءَايَٰتِ اللَّهِ هُزُؤًا
shades.hadith_en: And do not take the verses of Allah in jest

shades.explanation: al-Istihza (the ridicule) in the Quran refers to mocking. The Quran says: Those who mock the believers (9:79).
shades.hadith_ar: إِنَّ الَّذِينَ أَجۡرَمُواْ كَانُواْ مِنَ الَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ يَضۡحَكُونَ
shades.hadith_en: Indeed those who committed crimes used to laugh at those who believed

shades.explanation: al-Mustahziun (the mockers) in the Quran refers to those who ridicule. The Quran says: Indeed Allah mocks them and lets them wander in their transgression (2:15).
shades.hadith_ar: اللَّهُ يَسۡتَهۡزِئُ بِهِمۡ وَيَمُدُّهُمۡ
shades.hadith_en: Allah mocks them and gives them leeway

shades.explanation: al-Haza (the ridicule) in the Quran refers to scornful treatment. The famous hadith states: It is enough evil for a person to belittle his Muslim brother.
shades.hadith_ar: بِحَسۡبِ امۡرِئٍۢ مِنَ الشَّرِّ أَن يَحۡقِرَ أَخَاهُ الۡمُسۡلِمَ
shades.hadith_en: It is enough evil for a person to belittle his Muslim brother

meaning.en: To be three. The root denotes the number three, third, or grouping of three.
meaning.ar: ثَلَاثَةٌ: عَدَدٌ. الثُّلُثُ: جُزۡءٌ مِن ثَلَاثَةٍ

lexical_analysis.ibn_faris: الثَّاءُ وَاللَّامُ وَالثَّاءُ أَصۡلٌ يَدُلُّ عَلَى الجُزۡءِ
lexical_analysis.al_raghib: ثَلَاثَةٌ: العَدَدُ المَعۡرُوفُ

quran_examples.ar: سَيَقُولُونَ ثَلَٰثَةٌ
quran_examples.en: They will say three

quran_examples.ar: مَا يَكُونُ مِن نَّجۡوَىٰ ثَلَٰثَةٍ
quran_examples.en: There is no private conversation of three

hadith.ar: إِذَا كَانَ ثَلَاثَةٌ فَلَا يَتَنَاجَى اثۡنَانِ دُونَ الثَّالِثِ
hadith.en: When there are three, let not two converse privately excluding the third

hadith.ar: أَحَبُّ الصِّيَامِ إِلَى اللَّهِ صِيَامُ دَاوُۥدَ
hadith.en: The most beloved fasting to Allah was the fasting of David

shades.explanation: ath-Thalath (the three) in the Quran refers to the number three. The Quran says: They will say three, the fourth of them is their dog (18:22).
shades.hadith_ar: سَيَقُولُونَ ثَلَٰثَةٌ رَّابِعُهُمۡ كَلۡبُهُمۡ
shades.hadith_en: They will say three, the fourth of them is their dog

shades.explanation: ath-Thalathah (the three) in the Quran refers to groups of three. The Quran says: There is no private conversation of three (58:7).
shades.hadith_ar: مَا يَكُونُ مِن نَّجۡوَىٰ ثَلَٰثَةٍ
shades.hadith_en: There is no private conversation of three

shades.explanation: ath-Thuluth (the third) in the Quran refers to a portion. The Quran says: And for them is a third of what he leaves (4:12).
shades.hadith_ar: فَلَهُمَا الثُّلُثُ مِمَّا تَرَكَ
shades.hadith_en: Then for them is a third of what he left

shades.explanation: ath-Thalith (the third) in the Quran refers to position. The famous hadith states: When three of you are together, let not two converse privately excluding the third.
shades.hadith_ar: إِذَا كَانَ ثَلَاثَةٌ فَلَا يَتَنَاجَى اثۡنَانِ دُونَ الثَّالِثِ
shades.hadith_en: When there are three, let not two converse privately excluding the third

meaning.en: To appear. The root denotes appearing, beginning, or desert dwelling.

lexical_analysis.ibn_faris: الۡبَاءُ وَالدَّالُ وَالۡوَاوُ أَصۡلٌ يَدُلُّ عَلَى الظُّهُورِ
lexical_analysis.al_raghib: بَدَا: ظَهَرَ. بَدِيعُ السَّمَاوَاتِ: خَالِقُهَا

quran_examples.ar: بَدِيعُ السَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَالۡأَرۡضِ
quran_examples.en: Originator of the heavens and the earth

quran_examples.ar: الۡأَعۡرَابُ أَشَدُّ كُفۡرًا وَنِفَاقًا
quran_examples.en: The Bedouins are stronger in disbelief

hadith.ar: مَن سَكَنَ البَادِيَةَ جَفَا
hadith.en: Whoever settles in the desert becomes harsh

hadith.ar: بَدَأَ الۡإِسۡلَامُ غَرِيبًا
hadith.en: Islam began as something strange

shades.explanation: al-Bida (the beginning) in the Quran refers to initial creation. The Quran says: Say, 'He is the One Who originated you the first time' (32:7).
shades.hadith_ar: الَّذِي أَحۡسَنَ كُلَّ شَيۡءٍ خَلۡقَهُۥ
shades.hadith_en: He Who perfected everything He created

shades.explanation: al-Badu (the desert) in the Quran refers to the Bedouin dwelling. The Quran says: The Bedouins are stronger in disbelief and hypocrisy (9:97).
shades.hadith_ar: الۡأَعۡرَابُ أَشَدُّ كُفۡرًا وَنِفَاقًا
shades.hadith_en: The Bedouins are stronger in disbelief and hypocrisy

shades.explanation: al-Badi (the Originator) in the Quran is one of Allah's names. The Quran says: Originator of the heavens and the earth (2:117).
shades.hadith_ar: بَدِيعُ السَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَالۡأَرۡضِ
shades.hadith_en: Originator of the heavens and the earth

shades.explanation: al-Badawah (the Bedouin life) in the Quran refers to desert dwelling. The famous hadith states: Whoever settles in the desert becomes harsh.
shades.hadith_ar: مَن سَكَنَ البَادِيَةَ جَفَا
shades.hadith_en: Whoever settles in the desert becomes harsh

meaning.en: To create. The root denotes creation, being free, or disassociating.

lexical_analysis.ibn_faris: الۡبَاءُ وَالرَّاءُ وَالۡهَمۡزَةُ أَصۡلٌ يَدُلُّ عَلَى الخَلۡقِ
lexical_analysis.al_raghib: بَرَأَ اللَّهُ الخَلۡقَ: خَلَقَهُمۡ

quran_examples.ar: خَلَقَ السَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَالۡأَرۡضَ بِالۡحَقِّ
quran_examples.en: He created the heavens and the earth with truth

quran_examples.ar: بَرَاءَةٌۭ مِّنَ اللَّهِ وَرَسُولِهِۦٓ
quran_examples.en: A declaration of disassociation from Allah

hadith.ar: اللَّهُمَّ إِنِّي أَبۡرَأُ إِلَيۡكَ مِنَ الۡحَوۡلِ وَالۡقُوَّةِ
hadith.en: O Allah, I declare innocence to You from all might and power

hadith.ar: إِنَّ اللَّهَ يُحِبُّ التَّوَّابِينَ وَيُحِبُّ الۡمُتَطَهِّرِينَ
hadith.en: Allah loves those who repent and purify themselves

shades.explanation: al-Bara (the creation) in the Quran refers to bringing into existence. The Quran says: And He created the heavens and the earth in truth (64:3).
shades.hadith_ar: خَلَقَ السَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَالۡأَرۡضَ بِالۡحَقِّ
shades.hadith_en: He created the heavens and the earth with truth

shades.explanation: al-Bari (the Creator) in the Quran is one of Allah's names. The Quran says: He is the Creator of the heavens and the earth (6:101).
shades.hadith_ar: بَدِيعُ السَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَالۡأَرۡضِ
shades.hadith_en: Originator of the heavens and the earth

shades.explanation: al-Baraah (the freedom) in the Quran refers to being free or innocent. The Quran says: [This is] a declaration of disassociation [from the polytheists] (9:1).
shades.hadith_ar: بَرَاءَةٌۭ مِّنَ اللَّهِ وَرَسُولِهِۦٓ
shades.hadith_en: A declaration of disassociation from Allah and His Messenger

shades.explanation: at-Tabari (the declaring innocent) in the Quran refers to acquittal. The famous hadith states: I am free from every Muslim who dwells among the polytheists.
shades.hadith_ar: أَنَا بَرِيءٌ مِن كُلِّ مُسۡلِمٍ يُقِيمُ بَيۡنَ أَظۡهُرِ الۡمُشۡرِكِينَ
shades.hadith_en: I am free from every Muslim who dwells among the polytheists

meaning.en: To overcome. The root denotes prevailing, victory, or dominance.

lexical_analysis.ibn_faris: الۡغَيۡنُ وَاللَّامُ وَالۡبَاءُ أَصۡلٌ يَدُلُّ عَلَى القُوَّةِ
lexical_analysis.al_raghib: غَلَبَ: قَهَرَ. غَالِبٌ: قَاهِرٌ

quran_examples.ar: وَاللَّهُ غَالِبٌ عَلَىٰٓ أَمۡرِهِۦ
quran_examples.en: Allah is dominant over His affair

quran_examples.ar: وَلِلَّهِ الۡأَمۡرُ مِن قَبۡلُ وَمِنۢ بَعۡدُ
quran_examples.en: To Allah belongs the matter before and after

hadith.ar: لَا يُلۡدَغُ الۡمُؤۡمِنُ مِن جُحۡرٍۢ وَاحِدٍ مَّرَّتَيۡنِ
hadith.en: The believer is not bitten from the same hole twice

hadith.ar: يَمۡحَقُ اللَّهُ الرِّبَا وَيُرۡبِي الصَّدَقَٰتِ
hadith.en: Allah destroys usury and increases charity

shades.explanation: al-Ghalab (the overcoming) in the Quran refers to prevailing. The Quran says: The truth has come, and falsehood will not start [anything] nor return (34:49).
shades.hadith_ar: وَقُلۡ جَآءَ الۡحَقُّ وَمَا يُبۡدِئُ الۡبَٰطِلُ وَمَا يُعِيدُ
shades.hadith_en: Say: The truth has come, and falsehood neither originates nor returns

shades.explanation: al-Ghalib (the Overcomer) in the Quran refers to Allah's supremacy. The Quran says: And Allah is dominant over His affair (12:21).
shades.hadith_ar: وَاللَّهُ غَالِبٌ عَلَىٰٓ أَمۡرِهِۦ وَلَٰكِنَّ أَكۡثَرَ النَّاسِ لَا يَعۡلَمُونَ
shades.hadith_en: Allah is dominant over His affair, but most people do not know

shades.explanation: al-Ghalabah (the victory) in the Quran refers to triumph. The Quran says: And to Allah belongs the victory before and after [the battle] (30:4-5).
shades.hadith_ar: وَلِلَّهِ الۡأَمۡرُ مِن قَبۡلُ وَمِنۢ بَعۡدُ
shades.hadith_en: And to Allah belongs the matter before and after

shades.explanation: al-Maghlubah (the overcome) in the Quran refers to being defeated. The famous hadith states: The believers are not bitten from the same hole twice.
shades.hadith_ar: لَا يُلۡدَغُ الۡمُؤۡمِنُ مِن جُحۡرٍۢ وَاحِدٍ مَّرَّتَيۡنِ
shades.hadith_en: The believer is not bitten from the same hole twice

meaning.en: To migrate. The root denotes migrating, abandoning, or forsaking.

lexical_analysis.ibn_faris: الۡهَاءُ وَالۡجِيمُ وَالرَّاءُ أَصۡلٌ يَدُلُّ عَلَى التَّرۡكِ
lexical_analysis.al_raghib: هَجَرَ: تَرَكَ. الۡهِجۡرَةُ: الخُرُوجُ مِنۡ أَرۡضِ الشِّرۡكِ

quran_examples.ar: وَاهۡجُرۡهُمۡ هَجۡرًا جَمِيلًا
quran_examples.en: Abandon them in a gracious manner

quran_examples.ar: وَٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ وَهَاجَرُواْ
quran_examples.en: Those who believed and emigrated

hadith.ar: الۡمُهَاجِرُ مَنۡ هَجَرَ مَا نَهَى اللَّهُ عَنۡهُ
hadith.en: The emigrant is the one who abandons what Allah forbade

hadith.ar: مَنۡ هَاجَرَ إِلَى اللَّهِ وَرَسُولِهِۦ
hadith.en: Whoever emigrates to Allah and His Messenger

shades.explanation: al-Hijrah (the migration) in the Quran refers to leaving one's home for Allah. The Quran says: Indeed those who believed and those who emigrated and strove in the cause of Allah (8:74).
shades.hadith_ar: وَالَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ وَهَاجَرُواْ وَجَٰهَدُواْ فِي سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ
shades.hadith_en: Those who believed, emigrated, and strove in the cause of Allah

shades.explanation: al-Hajr (the abandonment) in the Quran refers to forsaking. The Quran says: And abandon them in a gracious manner (73:10).
shades.hadith_ar: وَاهۡجُرۡهُمۡ هَجۡرًا جَمِيلًا
shades.hadith_en: And abandon them in a gracious manner

shades.explanation: al-Muhajir (the emigrant) in the Quran refers to one who migrates. The famous hadith states: The real emigrant is the one who abandons what Allah has forbidden.
shades.hadith_ar: الۡمُهَاجِرُ مَنۡ هَجَرَ مَا نَهَى اللَّهُ عَنۡهُ
shades.hadith_en: The real emigrant is the one who abandons what Allah has forbidden

shades.explanation: al-Hajir (the prudent) in the Quran refers to one who abandons sin. The famous hadith states: Whoever migrates for the sake of Allah, he reaches what he intended.
shades.hadith_ar: مَنۡ هَاجَرَ فِي سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ وَجَدَ فِي الۡأَرۡضِ مُرَاغَمًا كَثِيرًا
shades.hadith_en: Whoever emigrates for the sake of Allah will find much refuge

meaning.en: To stay. The root denotes staying, remaining, or lingering.

lexical_analysis.ibn_faris: اللَّامُ وَالۡبَاءُ وَالثَّاءُ أَصۡلٌ يَدُلُّ عَلَى الإِقَامَةِ
lexical_analysis.al_raghib: لَبِثَ: مَكَثَ وأَقَامَ

quran_examples.ar: وَلَبِثُواْ فِي كَهۡفِهِمۡ ثَلَٰثَ مِائَةٍ
quran_examples.en: They remained in their cave for three hundred

quran_examples.ar: يَوۡمَ يَدۡعُوكُمۡ فَتَسۡتَجِيبُونَ
quran_examples.en: The Day He calls you and you respond

hadith.ar: دَعۡ مَا يَرِيبُكَ إِلَىٰ مَا لَا يَرِيبُكَ
hadith.en: Leave what makes you doubt for what does not make you doubt

hadith.ar: لَبِثۡتُ مَعَ النَّبِيِّ
hadith.en: I stayed with the Prophet

shades.explanation: al-Lubth (the staying) in the Quran refers to remaining in a place. The Quran says: They remained in their cave for three hundred years (18:25).
shades.hadith_ar: وَلَبِثُواْ فِي كَهۡفِهِمۡ ثَلَٰثَ مِائَةٍ سِنِينَ
shades.hadith_en: And they remained in their cave for three hundred years

shades.explanation: al-Labith (the lingering) in the Quran refers to staying. The Quran says: They will cry out: You did not remain but a little (17:52).
shades.hadith_ar: يَوۡمَ يَدۡعُوكُمۡ فَتَسۡتَجِيبُونَ
shades.hadith_en: The Day He calls you and you respond

shades.explanation: al-Lubth (the respite) in the Quran refers to a delay. The famous hadith states: The best of you are those with the most excellent character.
shades.hadith_ar: إِنَّ مِنۡ أَحۡسَنِكُمۡ أَخۡلَاقًا أَنۡتُمۡ
shades.hadith_en: Indeed the best of you in character are you

shades.explanation: al-Iltibath (the confusion) in the Quran refers to remaining uncertain. The famous hadith states: Leave what makes you doubt for what does not make you doubt.
shades.hadith_ar: دَعۡ مَا يَرِيبُكَ إِلَىٰ مَا لَا يَرِيبُكَ
shades.hadith_en: Leave what makes you doubt for what does not make you doubt

meaning.en: To sit. The root denotes sitting, remaining, or staying in place.

lexical_analysis.ibn_faris: الۡقَافُ وَالۡعَيۡنُ وَالدَّالُ أَصۡلٌ يَدُلُّ عَلَى الۡقَرَارِ
lexical_analysis.al_raghib: قَعَدَ: جَلَسَ. الۡقَاعِدُ: الجَالِسُ

quran_examples.ar: لَّا يَسۡتَوِي الۡقَٰعِدُونَ مِنَ الۡمُؤۡمِنِينَ
quran_examples.en: Not equal are those who sit among the believers
quran_examples.context: Those who sit versus those who strive

quran_examples.ar: تَرَى الظَّالِمِينَ مُشۡفِقِينَ
quran_examples.en: You see the wrongdoers fearful

hadith.ar: صَلَاةُ الۡقَاعِدِ عَلَىٰ نِصۡفِ صَلَاةِ الۡقَائِمِ
hadith.en: The prayer of the seated is half that of the standing

hadith.ar: مَنۡ قَعَدَ مَقۡعَدًا لَا يَذۡكُرُ اللَّهَ فِيهِ
hadith.en: Whoever sits in a place and does not remember Allah

shades.explanation: al-Quud (the sitting) in the Quran refers to remaining seated. The Quran says: Not equal are those who sit [at home] among the believers (4:95).
shades.hadith_ar: لَّا يَسۡتَوِي الۡقَٰعِدُونَ مِنَ الۡمُؤۡمِنِينَ
shades.hadith_en: Not equal are those who sit among the believers

shades.explanation: al-Qaid (the seated) in the Quran refers to those who remain behind. The Quran says: And those who sit at home are not equal to those who strive (4:95).
shades.hadith_ar: غَيۡرُ أُوْلِي الضَّرَرِ
shades.hadith_en: Other than those with hardship

shades.explanation: al-Maqad (the place of sitting) in the Quran refers to a sitting place. The Quran says: You will see the wrongdoers fearful of what they have earned (42:22).
shades.hadith_ar: تَرَى الظَّالِمِينَ مُشۡفِقِينَ
shades.hadith_en: You see the wrongdoers fearful

shades.explanation: al-Qaadah (the sitting posture) in the Quran refers to a mode of sitting. The famous hadith states: The prayer of the one who sits is half that of the standing.
shades.hadith_ar: صَلَاةُ الۡقَاعِدِ عَلَىٰ نِصۡفِ صَلَاةِ الۡقَائِمِ
shades.hadith_en: The prayer of the seated person is half that of the standing

meaning.en: To be pure. The root denotes purity, sincerity, or being free from mixture.

lexical_analysis.ibn_faris: الۡخَاءُ وَاللَّامُ وَالصَّادُ أَصۡلٌ يَدُلُّ عَلَى الصَّفَاءِ
lexical_analysis.al_raghib: خَلَصَ: صَفَا. الۡإِخۡلَاصُ: تَوۡحِيدُ اللَّهِ

quran_examples.ar: مُخۡلِصِينَ لَهُ الدِّينَ
quran_examples.en: Sincere to Him in religion

quran_examples.ar: إِنَّهُۥ مِنۡ عِبَادِنَا الۡمُخۡلَصِينَ
quran_examples.en: Indeed he was one of Our sincere servants

hadith.ar: إِنَّ اللَّهَ لَا يَنظُرُ إِلَىٰ صُوَرِكُمۡ
hadith.en: Allah does not look at your forms

hadith.ar: قُلۡ هُوَ اللَّهُ أَحَدٌ ۞ اللَّهُ الصَّمَدُ
hadith.en: Say: He is Allah, the One. Allah, the Eternal Refuge

shades.explanation: al-Ikhlas (the sincerity) in the Quran refers to pure devotion. The Quran says: And they were not commanded except to worship Allah, [being] sincere to Him in religion (98:5).
shades.hadith_ar: وَمَآ أُمِرُوٓاْ إِلَّا لِيَعۡبُدُواْ اللَّهَ مُخۡلِصِينَ لَهُ الدِّينَ
shades.hadith_en: They were commanded only to worship Allah, sincere to Him in religion

shades.explanation: al-Khalis (the pure) in the Quran refers to something unadulterated. The Quran says: And you would see the sun when it rose inclining from their cave (18:17).
shades.hadith_ar: مَا لَهُم مِّن دُونِهِۦ مِن وَلِيٍّۢ وَلَا يُشۡرِكُ فِي حُكۡمِهِۦٓ أَحَدًا
shades.hadith_en: They have no protector besides Him, nor does He share His rule with anyone

shades.explanation: al-Mukhlis (the devoted servant) in the Quran refers to one purified in faith. The famous hadith states: The most sincere of people in devotion are those who hide their good deeds.
shades.hadith_ar: أَخۡلَصُواْ الۡعَمَلَ لِلَّهِ
shades.hadith_en: They made their deed pure for Allah

shades.explanation: al-Khulus (the purity) in the Quran refers to spiritual clarity. The famous hadith states: Allah does not look at your forms but at your hearts.
shades.hadith_ar: إِنَّ اللَّهَ لَا يَنظُرُ إِلَىٰ صُوَرِكُمۡ وَلَٰكِنۡ يَنظُرُ إِلَىٰ قُلُوبِكُمۡ
shades.hadith_en: Allah does not look at your forms but at your hearts

meaning.en: To turn away. The root denotes turning away, lying, or perverting the truth.

lexical_analysis.ibn_faris: الۡهَمۡزَةُ وَالۡفَاءُ وَالۡكَافُ أَصۡلٌ يَدُلُّ عَلَى الصَّرۡفِ
lexical_analysis.al_raghib: أَفَكَ: كَذِبٌ. قَوۡمٌ مَّأۡفُوكُونَ: مَصۡرُوفُونَ

quran_examples.ar: يُؤۡفَكُ عَنۡهُ مَنۡ أُفِكَ
quran_examples.en: Turned away from it is he who is turned away

quran_examples.ar: إِنَّ الَّذِينَ جَآءُو بِالۡإِفۡكِ
quran_examples.en: Those who came with the slander

hadith.ar: إِنَّ مِنۡ أَعۡظَمِ الۡفِرَىٰ أَن يَدَّعِيَ الرَّجُلُ مَا لَمۡ يَرَ
hadith.en: Among the greatest falsehoods is claiming what one did not see

hadith.ar: إِيَّاكُمۡ وَالۡكَذِبَ فَإِنَّ الۡكَذِبَ يَهۡدِي إِلَى الۡفُجُورِ
hadith.en: Beware of lying, for lying leads to wickedness

shades.explanation: al-Afk (the turning away) in the Quran refers to perversion of truth. The Quran says: Turned away are those who turn away from the truth (51:9).
shades.hadith_ar: يُؤۡفَكُ عَنۡهُ مَنۡ أُفِكَ
shades.hadith_en: Turned away from it is he who is turned away

shades.explanation: al-Ifk (the lie) in the Quran refers to slander and falsehood. The Quran says: Indeed those who came with the slander are a group among you (24:11).
shades.hadith_ar: إِنَّ الَّذِينَ جَآءُو بِالۡإِفۡكِ عُصۡبَةٌ مِّنكُمۡ
shades.hadith_en: Indeed those who came with the slander are a group among you

shades.explanation: al-Mu'tafikat (the overturned cities) in the Quran refers to the destroyed cities of Lot's people. The Quran says: The overturned [cities] He made them fall (53:53).
shades.hadith_ar: وَالۡمُؤۡتَفِكَةَ أَهۡوَىٰ
shades.hadith_en: And the overturned city He threw down

shades.explanation: al-Afik (the liar) in the Quran refers to one who fabricates. The famous hadith states: The worst of lies is when a person claims to have seen what he did not see.
shades.hadith_ar: إِنَّ مِنۡ أَعۡظَمِ الۡفِرَىٰ
shades.hadith_en: Indeed from the greatest falsehoods

meaning.en: To grow ripe. The root denotes ripening, yielding, or producing fruit.

lexical_analysis.ibn_faris: الۡهَمۡزَةُ وَالنُّونُ وَالۡيَاءُ أَصۡلٌ يَدُلُّ عَلَى الإِدۡرَاكِ
lexical_analysis.al_raghib: أَنَى الشَّيۡءُ: حَانَ وَقۡتُهُ

quran_examples.ar: وَهُوَ الَّذِيٓ أَنزَلَ مِنَ السَّمَآءِ مَآءً
quran_examples.en: And He is the One who sends down water from the sky

quran_examples.ar: جَنَّٰتٍۢ مَّعۡرُوشَٰتٍۢ وَغَيۡرَ مَعۡرُوشَٰتٍۢ
quran_examples.en: Gardens trellised and untrellised

hadith.ar: أَنَى ثَمَرُ النَّخۡلِ
hadith.en: The dates ripened

hadith.ar: كُلُّ شَيۡءٍ إِذَا أَنَى يَأۡكُلُ
hadith.en: Everything when it ripens is eaten

shades.explanation: al-Ana (the fresh fruit) in the Quran refers to ripening produce. The Quran says: And in the fruits there is ripeness (6:99).
shades.hadith_ar: وَنُخَيِّرُهُمۡ عَلَىٰ خَيۡرِ الۡأَنَامِ
shades.hadith_en: And We preferred them over the best of creation

shades.explanation: al-Inawan (the ripening) in the Quran refers to the time of harvest. The Quran says: When it yields its fruit and ripens (6:141).
shades.hadith_ar: وَجَنَّٰتٍ مِّنۡ أَعۡنَٰبٍۢ
shades.hadith_en: And gardens of grapevines

shades.explanation: al-Mana (the yield) in the Quran refers to provision. The famous hadith states: The best of provision is that which suffices.
shades.hadith_ar: يَا بَنِي آدَمَ خُذُواْ زِينَتَكُمۡ عِندَ كُلِّ مَسۡجِدٍۢ
shades.hadith_en: O children of Adam, take your adornment at every mosque

shades.explanation: al-Ayn (the not ripe) in the Quran refers to unripe fruit. The famous hadith states: Dates ripen and become sweet.
shades.hadith_ar: إِذَا أَنَى ثَمَرُ النَّخۡلِ
shades.hadith_en: When the dates ripen

meaning.en: To disobey. The root denotes disobedience, rebellion, or sin.

lexical_analysis.ibn_faris: الۡعَيۡنُ وَالصَّادُ وَالۡيَاءُ أَصۡلٌ يَدُلُّ عَلَى التَّمَرُّدِ
lexical_analysis.al_raghib: عَصَى: خَالَفَ. الۡعَاصِي: المُخَالِفُ

quran_examples.ar: وَمَن يَعۡصِ اللَّهَ وَرَسُولَهُۥ
quran_examples.en: Whoever disobeys Allah and His Messenger

quran_examples.ar: وَإِذۡ قُلۡنَا لِلۡمَلَٰٓئِكَةِ
quran_examples.en: When We said to the angels

hadith.ar: كُلُّ بَنِي آدَمَ خَطَّاءٌۭ وَخَيۡرُ الۡخَطَّائِينَ التَّوَّابُونَ
hadith.en: All children of Adam are sinners and the best of sinners are the repentant

hadith.ar: الۡيَدُ الۡعُلۡيَا خَيۡرٌۭ مِنَ الۡيَدِ السُّفۡلَىٰ
hadith.en: The upper hand is better than the lower hand

shades.explanation: al-Eisyan (the disobedience) in the Quran refers to rebellion against Allah. The Quran says: And whoever disobeys Allah and His Messenger has surely strayed (33:36).
shades.hadith_ar: وَمَن يَعۡصِ اللَّهَ وَرَسُولَهُۥ فَقَدۡ ضَلَّ ضَلَٰلًا مُّبِينًا
shades.hadith_en: Whoever disobeys Allah and His Messenger has surely strayed clearly

shades.explanation: al-Easi (the disobedient) in the Quran refers to one who rebels. The Quran says: Indeed Pharaoh exalted himself in the land (28:4).
shades.hadith_ar: إِنَّ فِرۡعَوۡنَ عَلَا فِي الۡأَرۡضِ
shades.hadith_en: Indeed Pharaoh exalted himself in the land

shades.explanation: al-Measiyah (the disobedient deed) in the Quran refers to sin. The famous hadith states: All the children of Adam are sinners, and the best of sinners are those who repent.
shades.hadith_ar: كُلُّ بَنِي آدَمَ خَطَّاءٌۭ وَخَيۡرُ الۡخَطَّائِينَ التَّوَّابُونَ
shades.hadith_en: All the children of Adam are sinners, and the best of sinners are the repentant

shades.explanation: al-Eisyan (the rebellion) in the Quran refers to Iblis's defiance. The Quran says: And [mention] when We said to the angels: Prostrate to Adam (2:34).
shades.hadith_ar: وَإِذۡ قُلۡنَا لِلۡمَلَٰٓئِكَةِ ٱسۡجُدُواْ لِأٓدَمَ فَسَجَدُوٓاْ إِلَّآ إِبۡلِيسَ
shades.hadith_en: When We said to the angels: Prostrate to Adam, they prostrated except Iblis

meaning.en: To narrate. The root denotes narrating, telling, or following a track.

lexical_analysis.ibn_faris: الۡقَافُ وَالصَّادُ أَصۡلٌ وَاحِدٌ يَدُلُّ عَلَى التَّتَبُّعِ
lexical_analysis.al_raghib: قَصَّ الأَثَرَ: تَبِعَهُ. الۡقِصَّةُ: الخَبَرُ

quran_examples.ar: نَحۡنُ نَقُصُّ عَلَيۡكَ أَحۡسَنَ الۡقَصَصِ
quran_examples.en: We relate to you the best of stories

quran_examples.ar: وَقَالَتۡ لِأُخۡتِهِۦ قُصِّيهِ
quran_examples.en: She said to his sister: Track him

hadith.ar: كَفَىٰ بِالۡمَرۡءِ كَذِبًا أَن يُحَدِّثَ بِكُلِّ مَا سَمِعَ
hadith.en: It is enough of a lie to narrate everything one hears

hadith.ar: أَحۡسَنُ الۡحَدِيثِ كِتَٰبُ اللَّهِ
hadith.en: The best speech is the Book of Allah

shades.explanation: al-Qasas (the narration) in the Quran refers to stories of the prophets. The Quran says: We relate to you the best of stories (12:3).
shades.hadith_ar: نَحۡنُ نَقُصُّ عَلَيۡكَ أَحۡسَنَ الۡقَصَصِ
shades.hadith_en: We relate to you the best of stories

shades.explanation: al-Qass (the relating) in the Quran refers to telling a tale. The Quran says: And recite to them the news of the two sons of Adam (5:27).
shades.hadith_ar: وَٱتۡلُ عَلَيۡهِمۡ نَبَأَ ٱبۡنَيۡ ءَادَمَ بِالۡحَقِّ
shades.hadith_en: And recite to them the news of the two sons of Adam in truth

shades.explanation: al-Qassas (the teller of tales) in the Quran refers to one who narrates. The famous hadith states: Do not narrate everything you hear.
shades.hadith_ar: كَفَىٰ بِالۡمَرۡءِ كَذِبًا أَن يُحَدِّثَ بِكُلِّ مَا سَمِعَ
shades.hadith_en: It is enough of a lie for a man to narrate everything he hears

shades.explanation: al-Iqtisas (the retelling) in the Quran refers to following a trail. The Quran says: And his mother said to his sister: Track him (28:11).
shades.hadith_ar: وَقَالَتۡ لِأُخۡتِهِۦ قُصِّيهِ
shades.hadith_en: And she said to his sister: Track him

meaning.en: To turn away. The root denotes turning, averting, or exceeding limits.

lexical_analysis.ibn_faris: الصَّادُ وَالرَّاءُ وَالۡفَاءُ أَصۡلٌ يَدُلُّ عَلَى التَّحۡوِيلِ
lexical_analysis.al_raghib: صَرَفَ: حَوَّلَ. أَسۡرَفَ: جَاوَزَ الۡحَدَّ

quran_examples.ar: وَلَقَدۡ صَرَّفۡنَا لَهُمۡ
quran_examples.en: And We have turned about for them

quran_examples.ar: وَلَا تُسۡرِفُوٓاْ
quran_examples.en: And do not be extravagant

hadith.ar: كُلُواْ وَٱشۡرَبُواْ وَتَصَدَّقُواْ
hadith.en: Eat, drink, and give charity

hadith.ar: إِنَّ اللَّهَ كَتَبَ الۡإِحۡسَانَ عَلَىٰ كُلِّ شَيۡءٍۢ
hadith.en: Allah has decreed excellence in everything

shades.explanation: as-Sarf (the turning away) in the Quran refers to diverting or averting. The Quran says: And We have turned about their account (46:27).
shades.hadith_ar: وَلَقَدۡ صَرَّفۡنَا لَهُمۡ
shades.hadith_en: And We have turned about for them

shades.explanation: as-Sarif (the averter) in the Quran refers to one who diverts. The Quran says: And incite not against me (9:48).
shades.hadith_ar: وَصَرَّفۡنَا فِيهِ مِنَ الۡوَعِيدِ
shades.hadith_en: And We have warned them with threats

shades.explanation: al-Musrif (the extravagant) in the Quran refers to one who exceeds limits. The Quran says: And do not be extravagant. Indeed He does not like the extravagant (6:141).
shades.hadith_ar: وَلَا تُسۡرِفُوٓاْ إِنَّهُۥ لَا يُحِبُّ الۡمُسۡرِفِينَ
shades.hadith_en: And do not be extravagant. Indeed He does not like the extravagant

shades.explanation: al-Israf (the wastefulness) in the Quran refers to excess. The famous hadith states: Eat and drink and give charity without extravagance.
shades.hadith_ar: كُلُواْ وَٱشۡرَبُواْ وَتَصَدَّقُواْ وَٱلۡبَسُواْ فِي غَيۡرِ إِسۡرَافٍۢ
shades.hadith_en: Eat, drink, give charity, and dress without extravagance

meaning.en: To strive. The root denotes striving, endeavoring, or walking briskly.

lexical_analysis.ibn_faris: السِّينُ وَالۡعَيۡنُ وَالۡيَاءُ أَصۡلٌ يَدُلُّ عَلَى الجُهۡدِ
lexical_analysis.al_raghib: سَعَى: جَهِدَ. السَّعۡيُ: العَمَلُ

quran_examples.ar: وَأَن لَّيۡسَ لِلۡإِنسَٰنِ إِلَّا مَا سَعَىٰ
quran_examples.en: Man has nothing but what he strives for

quran_examples.ar: وَمَنۡ أَرَادَ الۡأٓخِرَةَ وَسَعَىٰ لَهَا
quran_examples.en: Whoever desires the Hereafter and strives for it

hadith.ar: إِنَّ الصَّفَا وَالۡمَرۡوَةَ مِن شَعَآئِرِ اللَّهِ
hadith.en: Indeed Safa and Marwa are among Allah's symbols

hadith.ar: السَّاعِي عَلَى الۡأَرۡمَلَةِ وَالۡمِسۡكِينِ كَالۡمُجَاهِدِ
hadith.en: One who strives for the widow and poor is like a mujahid

shades.explanation: as-Say (the striving) in the Quran refers to effort and exertion. The Quran says: And that man has nothing but what he strives for (53:39).
shades.hadith_ar: وَأَن لَّيۡسَ لِلۡإِنسَٰنِ إِلَّا مَا سَعَىٰ
shades.hadith_en: And man has nothing but what he strives for

shades.explanation: as-Sai (the striver) in the Quran refers to one who exerts effort. The Quran says: O you who believe, when you rise to prayer, wash your faces (5:6).
shades.hadith_ar: وَمَنۡ أَرَادَ الۡأٓخِرَةَ وَسَعَىٰ لَهَا سَعۡيَهَا
shades.hadith_en: Whoever desires the Hereafter and strives for it with due effort

shades.explanation: as-Saiy (the walking) in the Quran refers to brisk walking. The famous hadith states: Indeed the (ritual) walking between Safa and Marwa is an act of Allah.
shades.hadith_ar: إِنَّ الصَّفَا وَالۡمَرۡوَةَ مِن شَعَآئِرِ اللَّهِ
shades.hadith_en: Indeed Safa and Marwa are among the symbols of Allah

shades.explanation: al-Mas'ah (the striving effort) in the Quran refers to righteous deeds. The famous hadith states: The striving of the one who does it is the best of striving.
shades.hadith_ar: سَعۡيُ الۡعَامِلِ خَيۡرٌۭ لَّهُۥ
shades.hadith_en: The effort of the worker is best for him

meaning.en: To travel. The root denotes traveling, journeying, or moving.

lexical_analysis.ibn_faris: السِّينُ وَالۡيَاءُ وَالرَّاءُ أَصۡلٌ يَدُلُّ عَلَى المَشۡيِ
lexical_analysis.al_raghib: سَارَ: مَشَى. سَيۡرُ: المَرۡةُ الوَاحِدَةُ

quran_examples.ar: سِيرُواْ فِي الۡأَرۡضِ
quran_examples.en: Travel through the earth

quran_examples.ar: سِيرُواْ فِيهَا لَيَالِيَ وَأَيَّامًا آمِنِينَ
quran_examples.en: Travel through them by night and day, secure

hadith.ar: السَّفَرُ قِطۡعَةٌۭ مِنَ الۡعَذَابِ
hadith.en: Travel is a portion of punishment

hadith.ar: الۡمُسَافِرُ إِلَى اللَّهِ لَا يَضِلُّ
hadith.en: The traveler to Allah does not go astray

shades.explanation: as-Sayr (the traveling) in the Quran refers to journeying. The Quran says: Travel through the earth and see (3:137).
shades.hadith_ar: سِيرُواْ فِي الۡأَرۡضِ
shades.hadith_en: Travel through the earth

shades.explanation: as-Sair (the wayfarer) in the Quran refers to a traveler. The Quran says: And travel by day and night (34:18).
shades.hadith_ar: سِيرُواْ فِيهَا لَيَالِيَ وَأَيَّامًا آمِنِينَ
shades.hadith_en: Travel through them by night and day, secure

shades.explanation: al-Masir (the destination) in the Quran refers to the final outcome. The famous hadith states: The best journey is the journey for knowledge.
shades.hadith_ar: سَيۡرُ الۡعِلۡمِ خَيۡرٌۭ
shades.hadith_en: The journey for knowledge is best

shades.explanation: at-Tasyir (the facilitating) in the Quran refers to making something go. The Quran says: And the mountains - how they are erected (88:19-20).
shades.hadith_ar: وَإِلَى الۡجِبَالِ كَيۡفَ نُصِبَتۡ
shades.hadith_en: And to the mountains - how they are set up

meaning.en: To fly. The root denotes flying, birds, or omens.

lexical_analysis.ibn_faris: الطَّاءُ وَالۡيَاءُ وَالرَّاءُ أَصۡلٌ يَدُلُّ عَلَى الخَفَّةِ
lexical_analysis.al_raghib: طَارَ: حَلَّقَ. الطَّائِرُ: مَا يَطِيرُ

quran_examples.ar: وَلَا طَٰٓئِرٍۢ يَطِيرُ بِجَنَاحَيۡهِ
quran_examples.en: Nor a bird that flies with its wings

quran_examples.ar: طَٰٓئِرُهُم مَّعَهُمۡ
quran_examples.en: Their omen is with them

hadith.ar: لَا طِيَرَةَ
hadith.en: There is no superstition in omens

hadith.ar: إِنَّ الۡمَلَائِكَةَ تَضَعُ أَجۡنِحَتَهَا
hadith.en: The angels lower their wings

shades.explanation: at-Tayr (the bird) in the Quran refers to flying creatures. The Quran says: No creature moves on the earth nor flies with its wings (6:38).
shades.hadith_ar: وَمَا مِن دَآبَّةٍۢ فِي الۡأَرۡضِ وَلَا طَٰٓئِرٍۢ
shades.hadith_en: No creature on earth nor bird that flies

shades.explanation: at-Ta'ir (the flying) in the Quran refers to that which flies. The Quran says: Their bird of omen is with them (36:19).
shades.hadith_ar: طَٰٓئِرُهُم مَّعَهُمۡ
shades.hadith_en: Their omen is with them

shades.explanation: at-Tayr (the omen) in the Quran refers to divination by birds. The famous hadith states: There is no [superstition in the] flight of birds or omens.
shades.hadith_ar: لَا طِيَرَةَ
shades.hadith_en: There is no superstition

shades.explanation: at-Tayaran (the flight) in the Quran refers to soaring. The famous hadith states: The angels spread their wings for the seeker of knowledge.
shades.hadith_ar: إِنَّ الۡمَلَائِكَةَ لَتَضَعُ أَجۡنِحَتَهَا
shades.hadith_en: Indeed the angels lower their wings

meaning.en: To know. The root denotes knowing, recognizing, or being aware.

lexical_analysis.ibn_faris: الدَّالُ وَالرَّاءُ وَالۡيَاءُ أَصۡلٌ يَدُلُّ عَلَى العِلۡمِ
lexical_analysis.al_raghib: دَرَى: عَلِمَ. دَرِايةً: عِلۡمًا

quran_examples.ar: مَا لَيۡسَ لَكَ بِهِۦ عِلۡمٌ
quran_examples.en: That of which you have no knowledge

quran_examples.ar: إِذۡ تَبَرَّأَ الَّذِينَ ٱتُّبِعُواْ
quran_examples.en: When those who were followed disown

hadith.ar: وَمَنۡ يَهۡدِ اللَّهُ فَهُوَ الۡمُهۡتَدِ
hadith.en: Whoever Allah guides is the guided one

hadith.ar: دَعۡ مَا لَا يَعۡنِيكَ
hadith.en: Leave what does not concern you

shades.explanation: ad-Diryah (the knowledge) in the Quran refers to awareness. The Quran says: And you do not have any knowledge of it (17:36).
shades.hadith_ar: وَمَا لَكَ بِهِۦ مِنۡ عِلۡمٍ
shades.hadith_en: You have no knowledge of it

shades.explanation: ad-Dari (the aware) in the Quran refers to one who knows. The Quran says: And those who disbelieve say to those who believe: Follow our way (2:166).
shades.hadith_ar: إِذۡ تَبَرَّأَ الَّذِينَ ٱتُّبِعُواْ مِنَ ٱلَّذِينَ ٱتَّبَعُواْ
shades.hadith_en: When those who were followed disown those who followed

shades.explanation: al-Istidra (the stealthy approach) in the Quran refers to gradual punishment. The famous hadith states: Allah misguides no one but He first guides.
shades.hadith_ar: مَنۡ يَهۡدِ اللَّهُ فَهُوَ الۡمُهۡتَدِ
shades.hadith_en: Whoever Allah guides is guided

shades.explanation: ad-Darawa (the familiarity) in the Quran refers to experience. The famous hadith states: A believer is not stung from the same hole twice.
shades.hadith_ar: لَا يُلۡدَغُ الۡمُؤۡمِنُ مِن جُحۡرٍۢ وَاحِدٍ مَّرَّتَيۡنِ
shades.hadith_en: A believer is not stung from the same hole twice

meaning.en: To succeed. The root denotes success, triumph, or salvation.

lexical_analysis.ibn_faris: الۡفَاءُ وَالۡوَاوُ وَالزَّايُ أَصۡلٌ يَدُلُّ عَلَى النَّجَاةِ
lexical_analysis.al_raghib: فَازَ: نَجَا. الۡفَوۡزُ: الظَّفَرُ بِالۡجَنَّةِ

quran_examples.ar: إِنَّ لِلۡمُتَّقِينَ مَفَازًا
quran_examples.en: Indeed for the righteous is attainment

quran_examples.ar: أُو۟لَٰٓئِكَ هُمُ الۡفَائِزُونَ
quran_examples.en: Those are the successful ones

hadith.ar: مَن قَالَ لَآ إِلَٰهَ إِلَّا اللَّهُ كَانَتۡ لَهُ فَوۡزًا
hadith.en: Whoever says La ilaha illa Allah has success

hadith.ar: الۡمُؤۡمِنُ الۡقَوِيُّ خَيۡرٌۭ وَأَحَبُّ إِلَى اللَّهِ
hadith.en: The strong believer is better and more beloved to Allah

shades.explanation: al-Fawz (the success) in the Quran refers to triumph. The Quran says: Indeed the righteous are in attainment (78:31).
shades.hadith_ar: إِنَّ لِلۡمُتَّقِينَ مَفَازًا
shades.hadith_en: Indeed for the righteous is attainment

shades.explanation: al-Faiz (the successful) in the Quran refers to one who achieves salvation. The Quran says: The successful are indeed those who succeed (23:111).
shades.hadith_ar: أُو۟لَٰٓئِكَ هُمُ الۡفَائِزُونَ
shades.hadith_en: Those are the successful ones

shades.explanation: al-Mafaz (the place of success) in the Quran refers to salvation. The famous hadith states: Whoever says La ilaha illa Allah, it will be his salvation.
shades.hadith_ar: إِنَّ لِلۡمُتَّقِينَ مَفَازًا
shades.hadith_en: Indeed for the righteous is success

shades.explanation: al-Fawzan (the great success) in the Quran refers to ultimate triumph. The famous hadith states: The religion is naseehah (sincerity).
shades.hadith_ar: الدِّينُ النَّصِيحَةُ
shades.hadith_en: The religion is sincerity

meaning.en: To cover. The root denotes covering, overwhelming, or veiling.

lexical_analysis.ibn_faris: الۡغَيۡنُ وَالشِّينُ وَالۡيَاءُ أَصۡلٌ يَدُلُّ عَلَى السَّتۡرِ
lexical_analysis.al_raghib: غَشَاهُ: غَطَّاهُ. الۡغَاشِيَةُ: القِيَامَةُ

quran_examples.ar: هَلۡ أَتَىٰكَ حَدِيثُ الۡغَاشِيَةِ
quran_examples.en: Has the report of the Overwhelming Event come to you?

quran_examples.ar: وَعَلَىٰٓ أَبۡصَٰرِهِمۡ غِشَٰوَةٌ
quran_examples.en: On their eyes is a covering

hadith.ar: كُلُّ مُسۡكِرٍ خَمۡرٌۭ
hadith.en: Every intoxicant is khamr

hadith.ar: أَوَّلُ مَا يُحَاسَبُ بِهِ الۡعَبۡدُ الصَّلَاةُ
hadith.en: The first thing the servant is held accountable for is prayer

shades.explanation: al-Ghashiyah (the overwhelming event) in the Quran refers to the Day of Judgment. The Quran says: Has there come to you the report of the Overwhelming [Event]? (88:1).
shades.hadith_ar: هَلۡ أَتَىٰكَ حَدِيثُ الۡغَاشِيَةِ
shades.hadith_en: Has there come to you the report of the Overwhelming Event?

shades.explanation: al-Ghishawah (the covering) in the Quran refers to a veil. The Quran says: And on their hearing and their eyes is a covering (2:7).
shades.hadith_ar: وَعَلَىٰ سَمۡعِهِمۡ وَعَلَىٰٓ أَبۡصَٰرِهِمۡ غِشَٰوَةٌ
shades.hadith_en: And on their hearing and their eyes is a covering

shades.explanation: al-Ghashiy (the veiler) in the Quran refers to what covers. The famous hadith states: Every intoxicant is khamr, and every intoxicant is forbidden.
shades.hadith_ar: كُلُّ مُسۡكِرٍ خَمۡرٌۭ وَكُلُّ مُسۡكِرٍ حَرَامٌ
shades.hadith_en: Every intoxicant is khamr and every intoxicant is forbidden

shades.explanation: al-Ghashya (the unconsciousness) in the Quran refers to fainting. The famous hadith states: The first thing for which a servant will be held accountable is prayer.
shades.hadith_ar: أَوَّلُ مَا يُحَاسَبُ بِهِ الۡعَبۡدُ الصَّلَاةُ
shades.hadith_en: The first thing a servant is held accountable for is prayer

meaning.en: To argue. The root denotes arguing, disputing, or debating.

lexical_analysis.ibn_faris: الۡجِيمُ وَالدَّالُ وَاللَّامُ أَصۡلٌ يَدُلُّ عَلَى الخُصُومَةِ
lexical_analysis.al_raghib: جَادَلَ: نَاظَرَ. الۡجَدَلُ: شِدَّةُ الخِصَامِ

quran_examples.ar: وَجَٰدِلۡهُم بِالَّتِي هِيَ أَحۡسَنُ
quran_examples.en: Argue with them in the best way

quran_examples.ar: قَدۡ سَمِعَ اللَّهُ قَوۡلَ الَّتِي تُجَٰدِلُكَ
quran_examples.en: Allah has heard the statement of she who pleads

hadith.ar: أَنَا زَعِيمٌۢ بِبَيۡتٍۢ فِي رَبَضِ الۡجَنَّةِ لِمَن تَرَكَ الۡمِرَآءَ
hadith.en: I guarantee a house in Paradise for one who gives up arguing

hadith.ar: إِنَّ أَبۡغَضَ الرِّجَالِ إِلَى اللَّهِ الۡأَلَدُّ الْخَصِمُ
hadith.en: The most hateful to Allah is the stubborn disputant

shades.explanation: al-Jidal (the argumentation) in the Quran refers to disputation. The Quran says: And argue with them in a way that is best (16:125).
shades.hadith_ar: وَجَٰدِلۡهُم بِالَّتِي هِيَ أَحۡسَنُ
shades.hadith_en: And argue with them in the best way

shades.explanation: al-Mujadalah (the pleading) in the Quran refers to disputation. The Quran says: Allah has heard the statement of she who pleads with you concerning her husband (58:1).
shades.hadith_ar: قَدۡ سَمِعَ اللَّهُ قَوۡلَ الَّتِي تُجَٰدِلُكَ فِي زَوۡجِهَا
shades.hadith_en: Allah has heard the statement of she who pleads with you concerning her husband

shades.explanation: al-Jadl (the disputation) in the Quran refers to intense debate. The famous hadith states: I am a guarantor of a house on the outskirts of Paradise for one who gives up arguing even if he is right.
shades.hadith_ar: أَنَا زَعِيمٌۢ بِبَيۡتٍۢ فِي رَبَضِ الۡجَنَّةِ لِمَن تَرَكَ الۡمِرَآءَ
shades.hadith_en: I guarantee a house on the outskirts of Paradise for one who gives up arguing

shades.explanation: al-Judalah (the skill in debate) in the Quran refers to eloquence in argument. The famous hadith states: The most hateful of men to Allah is the stubborn disputant.
shades.hadith_ar: إِنَّ أَبۡغَضَ الرِّجَالِ إِلَى اللَّهِ الۡأَلَدُّ الْخَصِمُ
shades.hadith_en: The most hateful of men to Allah is the stubborn disputant

meaning.en: To gather. The root denotes an army, soldiers, or a host.

lexical_analysis.ibn_faris: الۡجِيمُ وَالنُّونُ وَالدَّالُ أَصۡلٌ يَدُلُّ عَلَى الجَمۡعِ
lexical_analysis.al_raghib: جُنُودُ اللَّهِ: خَلۡقُهُ الَّذِينَ يُقَاتِلُونَ بِأَمۡرِهِ

quran_examples.ar: وَلِلَّهِ جُنُودُ السَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَالۡأَرۡضِ
quran_examples.en: To Allah belong the soldiers of the heavens and the earth

quran_examples.ar: وَمَا يَعۡلَمُ جُنُودَ رَبِّكَ إِلَّا هُوَ
quran_examples.en: No one knows the soldiers of your Lord except Him

hadith.ar: خَيۡرُكُمۡ مَن تَعَلَّمَ الۡقُرۡآنَ وَعَلَّمَهُ
hadith.en: The best of you are those who learn the Quran and teach it

hadith.ar: اللَّهُمَّ بِكَ أَصُولُ وَبِكَ أُجُولُ
hadith.en: O Allah, with You I advance and with You I retreat

shades.explanation: al-Jund (the army) in the Quran refers to a military force. The Quran says: And never did We send a prophet to a city but We seized its people with poverty and hardship (7:94).
shades.hadith_ar: وَلِلَّهِ جُنُودُ السَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَالۡأَرۡضِ
shades.hadith_en: And to Allah belong the soldiers of the heavens and the earth

shades.explanation: al-Jundullah (the soldiers of Allah) in the Quran refers to angelic forces. The Quran says: And no one knows the soldiers of your Lord except Him (74:31).
shades.hadith_ar: وَمَا يَعۡلَمُ جُنُودَ رَبِّكَ إِلَّا هُوَ
shades.hadith_en: And no one knows the soldiers of your Lord except Him

shades.explanation: al-Jundiyyah (the military service) in the Quran refers to serving in Allah's cause. The famous hadith states: The soldier on guard is in a state of fasting and prayer.
shades.hadith_ar: الرَّبِيطُ عَلَىٰ جُنُودِ اللَّهِ فِي سَبِيلِهِ
shades.hadith_en: The guardian of Allah's soldiers in His cause

shades.explanation: al-Jund (the host) in the Quran refers to a congregation. The famous hadith states: The best of you are those who learn the Quran and teach it.
shades.hadith_ar: خَيۡرُكُمۡ مَن تَعَلَّمَ الۡقُرۡآنَ وَعَلَّمَهُ
shades.hadith_en: The best of you are those who learn the Quran and teach it

meaning.en: To raise. The root denotes raising, elevating, or exalting.

lexical_analysis.ibn_faris: الرَّاءُ وَالۡفَاءُ وَالۡعَيۡنُ أَصۡلٌ يَدُلُّ عَلَى العُلُوِّ
lexical_analysis.al_raghib: رَفَعَ: عَلَا. الرَّفۡعُ: ضِدُّ الخَفۡضِ

quran_examples.ar: وَرَفَعۡنَٰهُ مَكَانًا عَلِيًّا
quran_examples.en: We raised him to a high station

quran_examples.ar: يَرۡفَعِ اللَّهُ الَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ
quran_examples.en: Allah raises those who believe

hadith.ar: اللَّهُمَّ ارۡفَعۡ رَايَةَ الۡحَقِّ
hadith.en: O Allah, raise the banner of truth

hadith.ar: مَن رُفِعَ لِذِكۡرِ اللَّهِ بَيۡتٌۭ
hadith.en: Whoever raises a house for Allah's remembrance

shades.explanation: ar-Rafa (the raising) in the Quran refers to elevation. The Quran says: And we raised him to a high station (19:57).
shades.hadith_ar: وَرَفَعۡنَٰهُ مَكَانًا عَلِيًّا
shades.hadith_en: And We raised him to a high station

shades.explanation: ar-Rafi (the Exalter) in the Quran refers to Allah. The Quran says: He [Allah] raises those who believe and those who have been given knowledge (58:11).
shades.hadith_ar: يَرۡفَعِ اللَّهُ الَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ مِنكُمۡ وَالَّذِينَ أُوتُواْ الۡعِلۡمَ
shades.hadith_en: Allah raises those who believe and those given knowledge

shades.explanation: ar-Rufah (the height) in the Quran refers to honor. The famous hadith states: O Allah, raise the banner of truth.
shades.hadith_ar: اللَّهُمَّ ارۡفَعۡ رَايَةَ الۡحَقِّ
shades.hadith_en: O Allah, raise the banner of truth

shades.explanation: al-Marfu (the raised) in the Quran refers to that which is elevated. The famous hadith states: The most beloved of houses to Allah is a house raised for His remembrance.
shades.hadith_ar: أَحَبُّ البُيُوتِ إِلَى اللَّهِ بَيۡتٌۭ رُفِعَ لِذِكۡرِهِ
shades.hadith_en: The most beloved house to Allah is one raised for His remembrance

meaning.en: To fold. The root denotes folding, bending, or the number two.

lexical_analysis.ibn_faris: الثَّاءُ وَالنُّونُ وَالۡيَاءُ أَصۡلٌ يَدُلُّ عَلَى الۡعَطۡفِ
lexical_analysis.al_raghib: ثَنَى: عَطَفَ. الۡمَثَانِي: القُرۡآنُ

quran_examples.ar: أَلَا إِنَّهُمۡ يَثۡنُونَ صُدُورَهُمۡ
quran_examples.en: Indeed they fold up their chests

quran_examples.ar: سَبۡعًا مِّنَ الۡمَثَانِي
quran_examples.en: Seven of the often repeated

hadith.ar: نِعۡمَتَانِ مَغۡبُونٌۭ فِيهِمَا كَثِيرٌۭ مِنَ النَّاسِ
hadith.en: Two blessings many are deceived about

hadith.ar: الۡمَثَانِي سَبۡعَةُ أَحۡرُفٍۢ
hadith.en: The mathani are seven letters

shades.explanation: ath-Thany (the folding) in the Quran refers to bending. The Quran says: And they fold up their chests (11:5).
shades.hadith_ar: أَلَا إِنَّهُمۡ يَثۡنُونَ صُدُورَهُمۡ
shades.hadith_en: Indeed they fold up their chests

shades.explanation: ath-Thani (the second) in the Quran refers to the next in order. The Quran says: And said to his companion: Do not grieve (9:40).
shades.hadith_ar: إِذۡ يَقُولُ لِصَٰحِبِهِۦ لَا تَحۡزَنۡ
shades.hadith_en: When he said to his companion: Do not grieve

shades.explanation: al-Mathani (the often repeated) in the Quran refers to the seven oft-repeated verses (Surah al-Fatiha). The Quran says: And We have given you seven of the often repeated (15:87).
shades.hadith_ar: وَلَقَدۡ ءَاتَيۡنَٰكَ سَبۡعًا مِّنَ الۡمَثَانِي
shades.hadith_en: We have given you seven of the often repeated

shades.explanation: al-Ithn (the two) in the Quran refers to the number two. The famous hadith states: Two [blessings] many people are deceived about: health and free time.
shades.hadith_ar: نِعۡمَتَانِ مَغۡبُونٌۭ فِيهِمَا كَثِيرٌۭ مِنَ النَّاسِ
shades.hadith_en: Two blessings many people are deceived about

meaning.en: To love. The root denotes love, affection, or desire.

lexical_analysis.ibn_faris: الۡوَاوُ وَالدَّالُ أَصۡلٌ يَدُلُّ عَلَى المَحَبَّةِ
lexical_analysis.al_raghib: وَدَّ: أَحَبَّ. الۡوَدُودُ: اللَّهُ سُبۡحَانَهُ

quran_examples.ar: سَيَجۡعَلُ لَهُمُ الرَّحۡمَٰنُ وُدًّا
quran_examples.en: The Most Merciful will appoint for them affection

quran_examples.ar: وَهُوَ الۡغَفُورُ الۡوَدُودُ
quran_examples.en: He is the Forgiving, the Loving

hadith.ar: لَا تَدۡخُلُونَ الۡجَنَّةَ حَتَّىٰ تُؤۡمِنُواْ وَلَا تُؤۡمِنُواْ حَتَّىٰ تَحَابُّواْ
hadith.en: You will not enter Paradise until you love one another

hadith.ar: اللَّهُمَّ أَلِّفۡ بَيۡنَ قُلُوبِنَا
hadith.en: O Allah, unite our hearts

shades.explanation: al-Wudd (the love) in the Quran refers to affection. The Quran says: Indeed those who believe and do righteous deeds, the Most Merciful will appoint for them affection (19:96).
shades.hadith_ar: إِنَّ الَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ وَعَمِلُواْ الصَّٰلِحَٰتِ سَيَجۡعَلُ لَهُمُ الرَّحۡمَٰنُ وُدًّا
shades.hadith_en: Indeed those who believe and do righteous deeds, the Most Merciful will appoint for them affection

shades.explanation: al-Wadud (the Loving) in the Quran is one of Allah's names. The Quran says: And He is the Forgiving, the Loving (85:14).
shades.hadith_ar: وَهُوَ الۡغَفُورُ الۡوَدُودُ
shades.hadith_en: And He is the Forgiving, the Loving

shades.explanation: al-Mawaddah (the affection) in the Quran refers to mutual love. The Quran says: He created for you from yourselves mates that you may find tranquility in them, and He placed between you affection and mercy (30:21).
shades.hadith_ar: وَجَعَلَ بَيۡنَكُم مَّوَدَّةً وَرَحۡمَةً
shades.hadith_en: And placed between you affection and mercy

shades.explanation: al-Widad (the mutual love) in the Quran refers to brotherly affection. The famous hadith states: You will not enter Paradise until you believe, and you will not believe until you love one another.
shades.hadith_ar: لَا تَدۡخُلُونَ الۡجَنَّةَ حَتَّىٰ تُؤۡمِنُواْ وَلَا تُؤۡمِنُواْ حَتَّىٰ تَحَابُّواْ
shades.hadith_en: You will not enter Paradise until you believe, and you will not believe until you love one another

meaning.en: To be just. The root denotes justice, equity, or being equal.

lexical_analysis.ibn_faris: الۡعَيۡنُ وَالدَّالُ وَاللَّامُ أَصۡلٌ يَدُلُّ عَلَى الۡمُسَاوَاةِ
lexical_analysis.al_raghib: عَدَلَ: أَقۡسَطَ. الۡعَدۡلُ: ضِدُّ الجَوۡرِ

quran_examples.ar: إِنَّ اللَّهَ يَأۡمُرُ بِالۡعَدۡلِ
quran_examples.en: Allah commands justice

quran_examples.ar: وَأَقۡسِطُوٓاْ إِنَّ اللَّهَ يُحِبُّ الۡمُقۡسِطِينَ
quran_examples.en: Be just, Allah loves the just

hadith.ar: الۡمُقۡسِطُونَ عَلَىٰ مَنَابِرَ مِن نُّورٍۢ
hadith.en: The just will be on thrones of light

hadith.ar: إِنَّ اللَّهَ يَأۡمُرُ بِالۡعَدۡلِ وَالۡإِحۡسَٰنِ
hadith.en: Allah commands justice and excellence

shades.explanation: al-Eadl (the justice) in the Quran refers to fairness and equity. The Quran says: Allah commands justice and good conduct (16:90).
shades.hadith_ar: إِنَّ اللَّهَ يَأۡمُرُ بِالۡعَدۡلِ وَالۡإِحۡسَٰنِ
shades.hadith_en: Indeed Allah commands justice and good conduct

shades.explanation: al-Eadil (the just) in the Quran refers to one who is fair. The Quran says: And be just. Indeed Allah loves the just (49:9).
shades.hadith_ar: وَأَقۡسِطُوٓاْ إِنَّ اللَّهَ يُحِبُّ الۡمُقۡسِطِينَ
shades.hadith_en: And be just. Indeed Allah loves those who act justly

shades.explanation: al-Eadl (the equivalent) in the Quran refers to compensation or ransom. The Quran says: And if you substitute [one wife for another]... (4:20).
shades.hadith_ar: فَلَن تَعۡدِلُواْ وَلَوۡ حَرَصۡتُمۡ
shades.hadith_en: You will never be able to be just [between wives] even if you strive

shades.explanation: al-Eudul (the just persons) in the Quran refers to upright witnesses. The famous hadith states: The just will be on thrones of light on the Day of Judgment.
shades.hadith_ar: الۡمُقۡسِطُونَ عَلَىٰ مَنَابِرَ مِن نُّورٍۢ
shades.hadith_en: The just will be on thrones of light

meaning.en: To encompass. The root denotes encompassing, surrounding, or comprehending.

lexical_analysis.ibn_faris: الۡحَاءُ وَالۡوَاوُ وَالطَّاءُ أَصۡلٌ يَدُلُّ عَلَى الجَمۡعِ
lexical_analysis.al_raghib: أَحَاطَ: جَمَعَ وَاسۡتَوۡعَبَ

quran_examples.ar: وَاللَّهُ مُحِيطٌۢ بِالۡكَٰفِرِينَ
quran_examples.en: Allah encompasses the disbelievers

quran_examples.ar: وَاللَّهُ بِمَا یَعۡمَلُونَ مُحِیطٌۭ
quran_examples.en: Allah encompasses what they do

hadith.ar: رَحۡمَتِي وَسِعَتۡ كُلَّ شَيۡءٍۢ
hadith.en: My mercy encompasses all things

hadith.ar: اللَّهُ لَا يَحُوطُهُ شَيۡءٌۭ
hadith.en: Nothing encompasses Allah

shades.explanation: al-Hawt (the encompassing) in the Quran refers to surrounding something. The Quran says: And Allah encompasses the disbelievers from all sides (2:19).
shades.hadith_ar: وَاللَّهُ مُحِيطٌۢ بِالۡكَٰفِرِينَ
shades.hadith_en: And Allah encompasses the disbelievers

shades.explanation: al-Muhit (the Encompasser) in the Quran refers to Allah's all-encompassing power. The Quran says: And Allah encompasses what they do (3:120).
shades.hadith_ar: وَاللَّهُ بِمَا یَعۡمَلُونَ مُحِیطٌۭ
shades.hadith_en: And Allah encompasses what they do

shades.explanation: al-Hiyatah (the circumference) in the Quran refers to surrounding area. The famous hadith states: Allah encompasses all things in His mercy.
shades.hadith_ar: رَحۡمَتِي وَسِعَتۡ كُلَّ شَيۡءٍۢ
shades.hadith_en: My mercy encompasses all things

shades.explanation: al-Ihatah (the comprehensive knowledge) in the Quran refers to complete understanding. The famous hadith states: I have not seen anything that more encompasses the good deeds than intellect.
shades.hadith_ar: مَا رَأَيۡتُ شَيۡئًا قَطُّ أَحۡوَطَ لِلۡخَيۡرِ
shades.hadith_en: I have not seen anything more encompassing of good

meaning.en: To grow. The root denotes growing, originating, or raising.

lexical_analysis.ibn_faris: النُّونُ وَالشِّينُ وَالهَمۡزَةُ أَصۡلٌ يَدُلُّ عَلَى الحُدُوثِ
lexical_analysis.al_raghib: نَشَأَ: حَدَثَ. النَّشۡأَةُ: الخَلۡقُ

quran_examples.ar: وَأَنَّ عَلَيۡهِ النَّشۡأَةَ الۡأُخۡرَىٰ
quran_examples.en: Upon Him is the other creation

quran_examples.ar: إِنَّ نَاشِئَةَ اللَّيۡلِ هِيَ أَشَدُّ وَطۡئًا
quran_examples.en: Indeed the rising of the night is more intense

hadith.ar: كُلُّ مَوۡلُودٍۢ يُولَدُ عَلَى الۡفِطۡرَةِ
hadith.en: Every child is born upon the fitrah

hadith.ar: إِنَّ اللَّهَ بَدَأَ النَّشۡأَةَ
hadith.en: Allah began the creation

shades.explanation: an-Nash'ah (the growth) in the Quran refers to origination and development. The Quran says: And that upon Him is the [next] creation (53:47).
shades.hadith_ar: وَأَنَّ عَلَيۡهِ النَّشۡأَةَ الۡأُخۡرَىٰ
shades.hadith_en: And that upon Him is the other creation

shades.explanation: al-Munshi (the Originator) in the Quran refers to the One who creates. The Quran says: And He it is who originates creation (10:34).
shades.hadith_ar: قُلۡ هَلۡ مِن شُرَكَآئِكُم مَّن يَبۡدَؤُاْ الۡخَلۡقَ
shades.hadith_en: Say: Are there among your partners any who originate creation?

shades.explanation: an-Nashi' (the growing youth) in the Quran refers to a young person developing. The Quran says: Indeed the rising of the night is more intense in impression (73:6).
shades.hadith_ar: إِنَّ نَاشِئَةَ اللَّيۡلِ هِيَ أَشَدُّ وَطۡئًا
shades.hadith_en: Indeed the rising of the night is more intense in impression

shades.explanation: an-Nishwah (the raising) in the Quran refers to bringing up. The famous hadith states: A child is raised in the fitrah (natural disposition).
shades.hadith_ar: كُلُّ مَوۡلُودٍۢ يُولَدُ عَلَى الۡفِطۡرَةِ
shades.hadith_en: Every child is born upon the fitrah

meaning.en: To hope. The root denotes hoping, expecting, or deferring.

lexical_analysis.ibn_faris: الرَّاءُ وَالۡجِيمُ وَالۡوَاوُ أَصۡلٌ يَدُلُّ عَلَى التَّوَقُّعِ
lexical_analysis.al_raghib: رَجَا: أَمَّلَ. الإِرۡجَاءُ: التَّأۡخِيرُ

quran_examples.ar: فَمَن كَانَ يَرۡجُواْ لِقَآءَ رَبِّهِۦ
quran_examples.en: Whoever hopes for the meeting with his Lord

quran_examples.ar: وَآخَرُونَ مُرۡجَوۡنَ لِأَمۡرِ اللَّهِ
quran_examples.en: And others are deferred for the command of Allah

hadith.ar: لَا يَيۡأَسۡ مِن رَّوۡحِ اللَّهِ إِلَّا الۡقَوۡمُ الۡكَٰفِرُونَ
hadith.en: None despairs of Allah's mercy except the disbelieving people

hadith.ar: مَنۡ كَانَ يُؤۡمِنُ بِاللَّهِ وَالۡيَوۡمِ الۡأٓخِرِ فَلۡيَقُلۡ خَيۡرًا أَوۡ لِيَصۡمُتۡ
hadith.en: Whoever believes in Allah and the Last Day, let him speak good or remain silent

shades.explanation: ar-Raja (the hope) in the Quran refers to expecting Allah's mercy. The Quran says: So whoever hopes for the meeting with his Lord, let him do righteous work (18:110).
shades.hadith_ar: فَمَن كَانَ يَرۡجُواْ لِقَآءَ رَبِّهِۦ فَلۡيَعۡمَلۡ عَمَلًا صَٰلِحًا
shades.hadith_en: Whoever hopes for the meeting with his Lord, let him do righteous work

shades.explanation: ar-Rajai (the hopeful) in the Quran refers to one who anticipates good. The famous hadith states: Hope for what pleases Allah and fear what angers Him.
shades.hadith_ar: أَرۡجُو اللَّهَ وَأَخَافُ عَذَابَهُ
shades.hadith_en: I hope for Allah and fear His punishment

shades.explanation: al-Irja (the deferring) in the Quran refers to postponing judgment. The Quran says: And others are deferred for the command of Allah (9:106).
shades.hadith_ar: وَآخَرُونَ مُرۡجَوۡنَ لِأَمۡرِ اللَّهِ
shades.hadith_en: And others are deferred for the command of Allah

shades.explanation: ar-Rajawah (the expectation) in the Quran refers to anticipating divine mercy. The famous hadith states: Hope in Allah and do not despair of His mercy.
shades.hadith_ar: لَا تَيۡأَسُواْ مِن رَّحۡمَةِ اللَّهِ
shades.hadith_en: Do not despair of the mercy of Allah

meaning.en: To glorify. The root denotes glorification, praise, or swimming/floating.

lexical_analysis.ibn_faris: السِّينُ وَالۡبَاءُ وَالۡحَاءُ أَصۡلٌ يَدُلُّ عَلَى التَّنزِيهِ
lexical_analysis.al_raghib: سَبَّحَ: قَالَ سُبۡحَانَ اللَّهِ. سَبَحَ: عَامَ

quran_examples.ar: سُبۡحَانَ رَبِّكَ رَبِّ الۡعِزَّةِ
quran_examples.en: Exalted is your Lord, the Lord of might

quran_examples.ar: تُسَبِّحُ لَهُ السَّمَٰوَٰتُ السَّبۡعُ
quran_examples.en: The seven heavens exalt Him

hadith.ar: أَحَبُّ الۡكَلَامِ إِلَى اللَّهِ سُبۡحَانَ اللَّهِ وَبِحَمۡدِهِ
hadith.en: The most beloved words to Allah are subhanAllah wa bihamdihi

hadith.ar: مَن قَالَ سُبۡحَانَ اللَّهِ وَبِحَمۡدِهِ
hadith.en: Whoever says subhanAllah wa bihamdihi... his sins are forgiven

shades.explanation: at-Tasbih (the glorification) in the Quran refers to exalting Allah above imperfection. The Quran says: Exalted is your Lord, the Lord of might, above what they describe (37:180).
shades.hadith_ar: سُبۡحَانَ رَبِّكَ رَبِّ الۡعِزَّةِ عَمَّا يَصِفُونَ
shades.hadith_en: Exalted is your Lord, the Lord of might, above what they describe

shades.explanation: as-Sabbih (the glorifier) in the Quran refers to one who praises Allah. The Quran says: The seven heavens and the earth and whatever is in them exalt Him (17:44).
shades.hadith_ar: تُسَبِّحُ لَهُ السَّمَٰوَٰتُ السَّبۡعُ وَالۡأَرۡضُ
shades.hadith_en: The seven heavens and the earth exalt Him

shades.explanation: as-Subhan (the glory) in the Quran refers to Allah's transcendence. The famous hadith states: The most beloved words to Allah are subhanAllah.
shades.hadith_ar: أَحَبُّ الۡكَلَامِ إِلَى اللَّهِ سُبۡحَانَ اللَّهِ
shades.hadith_en: The most beloved words to Allah are subhanAllah

shades.explanation: al-Musabbih (the one who glorifies) in the Quran refers to those who praise Allah. The famous hadith states: Whoever says subhanAllah wa bihamdihi a hundred times, his sins are forgiven.
shades.hadith_ar: مَن قَالَ سُبۡحَانَ اللَّهِ وَبِحَمۡدِهِ مِائَةَ مَرَّةٍ
shades.hadith_en: Whoever says subhanAllah wa bihamdihi a hundred times

meaning.en: To be heavy. The root denotes weight, heaviness, or burdens.

lexical_analysis.ibn_faris: الثَّاءُ وَالۡقَافُ وَاللَّامُ أَصۡلٌ يَدُلُّ عَلَى الثِّقَلِ
lexical_analysis.al_raghib: ثَقُلَ: صَارَ ثَقِيلًا. الثَّقَلَانِ: الجِنُّ وَالإِنسُ

quran_examples.ar: إِنَّا سَنُلۡقِي عَلَيۡكَ قَوۡلًا ثَقِيلًا
quran_examples.en: We will cast upon you a heavy word

quran_examples.ar: وَالۡوَزۡنُ يَوۡمَئِذٍ الۡحَقُّ
quran_examples.en: The weighing on that Day is the truth

hadith.ar: إِنِّي تَارِكٌۭ فِيكُمُ الثَّقَلَيۡنِ
hadith.en: I leave among you the two weighty things

hadith.ar: أَثۡقَلُ شَيۡءٍ فِي الۡمِيزَانِ حُسۡنُ الۡخُلُقِ
hadith.en: The heaviest thing on the scale is good character

shades.explanation: ath-Thiql (the weight) in the Quran refers to heaviness. The Quran says: And the weighing on that Day is the truth (7:8).
shades.hadith_ar: وَالۡوَزۡنُ يَوۡمَئِذٍ الۡحَقُّ
shades.hadith_en: And the weighing on that Day is the truth

shades.explanation: ath-Thaqal (the burdens) in the Quran refers to heavy loads. The Quran says: Indeed We will cast upon you a heavy word (73:5).
shades.hadith_ar: إِنَّا سَنُلۡقِي عَلَيۡكَ قَوۡلًا ثَقِيلًا
shades.hadith_en: Indeed We will cast upon you a heavy word

shades.explanation: ath-Thaqalan (the two heavy things) in the Quran refers to mankind and jinn. The famous hadith states: I leave among you two weighty things: the Book of Allah and my family.
shades.hadith_ar: إِنِّي تَارِكٌۭ فِيكُمُ الثَّقَلَيۡنِ
shades.hadith_en: I leave among you the two weighty things

shades.explanation: at-Tathqil (the making heavy) in the Quran refers to weighing down. The famous hadith states: The heaviest thing on the scale is good character.
shades.hadith_ar: أَثۡقَلُ شَيۡءٍ فِي الۡمِيزَانِ حُسۡنُ الۡخُلُقِ
shades.hadith_en: The heaviest thing on the scale is good character

meaning.en: To reward. The root denotes reward, recompense, or returning.

lexical_analysis.ibn_faris: الثَّاءُ وَالۡوَاوُ وَالۡبَاءُ أَصۡلٌ يَدُلُّ عَلَى الرُّجُوعِ
lexical_analysis.al_raghib: ثَابَ: رَجَعَ. الثَّوَابُ: الجَزَاءُ

quran_examples.ar: وَمَا الۡحَيَوٰةُ الدُّنۡيَا إِلَّا مَتَاعُ الۡغُرُورِ
quran_examples.en: The life of this world is but enjoyment of delusion

quran_examples.ar: وَاتَّخِذُواْ مِن مَّقَامِ إِبۡرَٰهِۦمَ مُصَلًّى
quran_examples.en: Take from the standing place of Abraham a place of prayer

hadith.ar: إِنَّ اللَّهَ لَا يُضِيعُ أَجۡرَ الۡمُحۡسِنِينَ
hadith.en: Allah does not let the reward of the good-doers go to waste

hadith.ar: أَجۡرُ الصَّابِرِينَ غَيۡرُ مَمۡنُونٍۢ
hadith.en: The reward of the patient is without limit

shades.explanation: ath-Thawab (the reward) in the Quran refers to divine recompense. The Quran says: And with Allah is the best reward (3:185).
shades.hadith_ar: وَمَا عِندَ اللَّهِ خَيۡرٌۭ لِّلۡأَبۡرَارِ
shades.hadith_en: What is with Allah is best for the righteous

shades.explanation: ath-Thaib (the rewarder) in the Quran refers to the One who gives recompense. The famous hadith states: Allah does not let the reward of the doer of good go to waste.
shades.hadith_ar: إِنَّ اللَّهَ لَا يُضِيعُ أَجۡرَ الۡمُحۡسِنِينَ
shades.hadith_en: Allah does not let the reward of the good-doers go to waste

shades.explanation: at-Tathwib (the returning) in the Quran refers to coming back. The famous hadith states: The one who is rewarded is the one who is patient in this world.
shades.hadith_ar: أَجۡرُ الصَّابِرِينَ لَا يُحۡصَىٰ
shades.hadith_en: The reward of the patient cannot be counted

shades.explanation: al-Mathabah (the place of reward) in the Quran refers to the station of return. The famous hadith states: The best reward of the Hereafter is Paradise.
shades.hadith_ar: إِنَّ أَحۡسَنَ الثَّوَابِ الۡجَنَّةُ
shades.hadith_en: Indeed the best reward is Paradise

meaning.en: To be empty. The root denotes emptiness, seclusion, or being alone.

lexical_analysis.ibn_faris: الۡخَاءُ وَاللَّامُ وَالۡوَاوُ أَصۡلٌ يَدُلُّ عَلَى الفَرَاغِ
lexical_analysis.al_raghib: خَلَا: فَرَغَ. الۡخَلۡوَةُ: الاِنۡفِرَادُ

quran_examples.ar: فَإِذَا فَرَغۡتَ فَٱنصَبۡ
quran_examples.en: When you have completed, then stand

quran_examples.ar: وَاذۡكُر رَّبَّكَ فِي نَفۡسِكَ
quran_examples.en: Remember your Lord within yourself

hadith.ar: خَيۡرُ الۡأَعۡمَالِ مَا كَانَ فِي خَلۡوَةٍ
hadith.en: The best deeds are those done in seclusion

hadith.ar: خَلَا لِلَّهِ فِي الخَلۡوَةِ
hadith.en: Devote yourself to Allah in seclusion

shades.explanation: al-Khala (the emptiness) in the Quran refers to being alone or unoccupied. The Quran says: And when you are alone, say (9:36).
shades.hadith_ar: فَإِذَا فَرَغۡتَ فَٱنصَبۡ
shades.hadith_en: When you have completed [your duties], then stand

shades.explanation: al-Khalwah (the seclusion) in the Quran refers to being alone. The Quran says: And when you are alone, remember Allah (7:205).
shades.hadith_ar: وَاذۡكُر رَّبَّكَ فِي نَفۡسِكَ
shades.hadith_en: And remember your Lord within yourself

shades.explanation: al-Ikhla (the being empty) in the Quran refers to vacating. The famous hadith states: The best of actions are those done in seclusion.
shades.hadith_ar: خَيۡرُ الۡأَعۡمَالِ مَا كَانَ فِي خَلۡوَةٍ
shades.hadith_en: The best of deeds are those done in seclusion

shades.explanation: al-Khali (the empty one) in the Quran refers to that which is vacant. The famous hadith states: We have returned from the lesser jihad to the greater jihad.
shades.hadith_ar: رَجَعۡنَا مِنَ الۡجِهَادِ الۡأَصۡغَرِ إِلَى الۡجِهَادِ الۡأَكۡبَرِ
shades.hadith_en: We have returned from the lesser jihad to the greater jihad

meaning.en: To be certain. The root denotes certainty, sure knowledge, or conviction.

lexical_analysis.ibn_faris: الۡيَاءُ وَالۡقَافُ وَالنُّونُ أَصۡلٌ يَدُلُّ عَلَى الثَّبَاتِ
lexical_analysis.al_raghib: يَقِنَ: ثَبَتَ. الۡيَقِينُ: العِلۡمُ الۡجَازِمُ

quran_examples.ar: وَاعۡبُدۡ رَبَّكَ حَتَّىٰ يَأۡتِيَكَ الۡيَقِينُ
quran_examples.en: Worship your Lord until the certainty comes to you

quran_examples.ar: وَهُم بِالۡأٓخِرَةِ هُمۡ يُوقِنُونَ
quran_examples.en: They are certain of the Hereafter

hadith.ar: الۡيَقِينُ هُوَ الإِيمَانُ كُلُّهُ
hadith.en: Certainty is the whole of faith

hadith.ar: لَوۡ أَنَّكُمۡ كُنۡتُمۡ تُوقِنُونَ لَمَشَيۡتُمۡ عَلَى الۡبَحۡرِ
hadith.en: If you had certainty, you would walk on the sea

shades.explanation: al-Yaqin (the certainty) in the Quran refers to firm knowledge. The Quran says: And worship your Lord until there comes to you the certainty [death] (15:99).
shades.hadith_ar: وَاعۡبُدۡ رَبَّكَ حَتَّىٰ يَأۡتِيَكَ الۡيَقِينُ
shades.hadith_en: And worship your Lord until there comes to you the certainty

shades.explanation: al-Muqin (the certain person) in the Quran refers to one of firm faith. The Quran says: And those who are certain of the Hereafter (27:3).
shades.hadith_ar: وَهُم بِالۡأٓخِرَةِ هُمۡ يُوقِنُونَ
shades.hadith_en: And they are certain of the Hereafter

shades.explanation: al-Yaqin al-Haqq (the absolute certainty) in the Quran refers to ultimate truth. The famous hadith states: Certainty is the whole of faith.
shades.hadith_ar: الۡيَقِينُ هُوَ الإِيمَانُ كُلُّهُ
shades.hadith_en: Certainty is the whole of faith

shades.explanation: al-Istiqan (the being certain) in the Quran refers to conviction. The famous hadith states: If you had certainty, you would walk on the sea.
shades.hadith_ar: لَوۡ أَنَّكُمۡ كُنۡتُمۡ تُوقِنُونَ لَمَشَيۡتُمۡ عَلَى الۡبَحۡرِ
shades.hadith_en: If you had certainty, you would walk on the sea

meaning.en: Ten. The root denotes the number ten, companionship, or association.

lexical_analysis.ibn_faris: الۡعَيۡنُ وَالشِّينُ وَالرَّاءُ أَصۡلٌ يَدُلُّ عَلَى العَدَدِ
lexical_analysis.al_raghib: عَشَرَةٌ: العَدَدُ المَعۡرُوفُ. عَاشِرٌ: صَاحِبٌ

quran_examples.ar: مَن جَآءَ بِالۡحَسَنَةِ فَلَهُۥ عَشۡرُ أَمۡثَالِهَا
quran_examples.en: Whoever comes with a good deed will have ten times the like

quran_examples.ar: وَعَاشِرُوهُنَّ بِالۡمَعۡرُوفِ
quran_examples.en: Live with them honorably

hadith.ar: خَيۡرُكُمۡ خَيۡرُكُمۡ لِأَهۡلِهِۦ
hadith.en: The best of you are the best to their families

hadith.ar: مَنۡ كَانَ يُؤۡمِنُ بِاللَّهِ وَالۡيَوۡمِ الۡأٓخِرِ فَلۡيُحۡسِنۡ إِلَىٰ جَارِهِ
hadith.en: Whoever believes in Allah and the Last Day, let him be good to his neighbor

shades.explanation: al-Easharah (the ten) in the Quran refers to the number ten. The Quran says: For ten days (2:234).
shades.hadith_ar: فَاجۡلِدُوهُمۡ ثَمَٰنِينَ جَلۡدَةً
shades.hadith_en: Flog each of them eighty lashes

shades.explanation: al-Eashr (the tenth part) in the Quran refers to a tithe. The Quran says: For ten days (2:234).
shades.hadith_ar: وَيَزِيدُهُمۡ عَشۡرًا
shades.hadith_en: And He will increase them tenfold

shades.explanation: al-Mu'asharah (the social interaction) in the Quran refers to companionship. The famous hadith states: Live with them honorably.
shades.hadith_ar: وَعَاشِرُوهُنَّ بِالۡمَعۡرُوفِ
shades.hadith_en: And live with them honorably

shades.explanation: al-Eashir (the associate) in the Quran refers to a close companion. The famous hadith states: The best of you are those who are best to their families.
shades.hadith_ar: خَيۡرُكُمۡ خَيۡرُكُمۡ لِأَهۡلِهِۦ
shades.hadith_en: The best of you are the best to their families

meaning.en: To be amazed. The root denotes wonder, astonishment, or marvel.

lexical_analysis.ibn_faris: الۡعَيۡنُ وَالۡجِيمُ وَالۡبَاءُ أَصۡلٌ يَدُلُّ عَلَى الۡغَرَابَةِ
lexical_analysis.al_raghib: عَجِبَ: تَعَجَّبَ. عَجِيبٌ: غَرِيبٌ

quran_examples.ar: بَلۡ عَجِبۡتَ وَيَسۡخَرُونَ
quran_examples.en: But you wonder while they mock

quran_examples.ar: وَمَا كَانَ رَبُّكَ نَسِيًّا
quran_examples.en: And your Lord is not forgetful

hadith.ar: عَجَبًا لِّلۡمُؤۡمِنِ إِنَّ أَمۡرَهُۥ كُلَّهُۥ خَيۡرٌۭ
hadith.en: Amazing is the believer: all his affairs are good

hadith.ar: إِنَّ مِنَ الۡبَيَانِ لَسِحۡرًا
hadith.en: Indeed some eloquence is magic

shades.explanation: al-Eajab (the amazement) in the Quran refers to wonder or astonishment. The Quran says: But you wonder while they mock (37:12).
shades.hadith_ar: بَلۡ عَجِبۡتَ وَيَسۡخَرُونَ
shades.hadith_en: But you wonder while they mock

shades.explanation: al-Eajib (the amazing) in the Quran refers to something wondrous. The Quran says: And your Lord is not forgetful (19:64).
shades.hadith_ar: وَمَا كَانَ رَبُّكَ نَسِيًّا
shades.hadith_en: And your Lord is not forgetful

shades.explanation: al-Eujaib (the strange thing) in the Quran refers to something extraordinary. The famous hadith states: The affair of the believer is amazing.
shades.hadith_ar: عَجَبًا لِّلۡمُؤۡمِنِ
shades.hadith_en: Amazing is the affair of the believer

shades.explanation: at-Taeajjub (the wondering) in the Quran refers to expressing astonishment. The famous hadith states: I wonder at the believer, for nothing happens to him but good.
shades.hadith_ar: عَجَبًا لِّلۡمُؤۡمِنِ لَا يَقۡضِي اللَّهُ لَهُ قَضَاءً إِلَّا كَانَ خَيۡرًا
shades.hadith_en: Amazing is the believer: Allah decrees nothing for him but good

meaning.en: To deceive. The root denotes deception, delusion, or being fooled.

lexical_analysis.ibn_faris: الۡغَيۡنُ وَالرَّاءُ أَصۡلٌ يَدُلُّ عَلَى الخَدِيعَةِ
lexical_analysis.al_raghib: غَرَّ: خَدَعَ. الۡغَرُورُ: الشَّيۡطَانُ

quran_examples.ar: وَلَا يَغُرَّنَّكُم بِاللَّهِ الۡغَرُورُ
quran_examples.en: Let not the deluder delude you concerning Allah

quran_examples.ar: زَيَّنَ لَهُمُ الشَّيۡطَٰنُ أَعۡمَٰلَهُمۡ
quran_examples.en: Satan beautified their deeds for them

hadith.ar: إِيَّاكُمۡ وَالدُّنۡيَا فَإِنَّهَا حُلۡوَةٌ خَضِرَةٌ
hadith.en: Beware of this world, for it is sweet and green

hadith.ar: لَا تَبِعۡ مَا لَيۡسَ عِندَكَ
hadith.en: Do not sell what you do not have

shades.explanation: al-Ghurur (the delusion) in the Quran refers to being deceived. The Quran says: And let not the life of this world delude you (31:33).
shades.hadith_ar: وَلَا يَغُرَّنَّكُم بِاللَّهِ الۡغَرُورُ
shades.hadith_en: And let not the deluder delude you concerning Allah

shades.explanation: al-Gharr (the deception) in the Quran refers to trickery. The Quran says: And Satan deceived them (47:25).
shades.hadith_ar: زَيَّنَ لَهُمُ الشَّيۡطَٰنُ أَعۡمَٰلَهُمۡ
shades.hadith_en: Satan beautified their deeds for them

shades.explanation: al-Gharrar (the hazard) in the Quran refers to risk. The famous hadith states: Do not sell what is not with you (prohibition of gharar).
shades.hadith_ar: لَا تَبِعۡ مَا لَيۡسَ عِندَكَ
shades.hadith_en: Do not sell what you do not have

shades.explanation: al-Gharur (the deluder) in the Quran refers to Satan. The famous hadith states: Beware of this world, for it is sweet and green.
shades.hadith_ar: إِيَّاكُمۡ وَالدُّنۡيَا فَإِنَّهَا حُلۡوَةٌ خَضِرَةٌ
shades.hadith_en: Beware of this world, for it is sweet and green

meaning.en: To be easy. The root denotes ease, gentleness, or humiliation.

lexical_analysis.ibn_faris: الۡهَاءُ وَالۡوَاوُ وَالنُّونُ أَصۡلٌ يَدُلُّ عَلَى الضَّعۡفِ
lexical_analysis.al_raghib: هَانَ: سَهُلَ. أَهَانَ: أَذَلَّ

quran_examples.ar: يَمۡشُونَ عَلَى الۡأَرۡضِ هَوۡنًا
quran_examples.en: They walk on the earth gently

quran_examples.ar: وَلَا تَهِنُواْ وَلَا تَحۡزَنُواْ
quran_examples.en: Do not be weak and do not grieve

hadith.ar: مَنۡ أَهَانَ مُؤۡمِنًا أَهَانَهُ اللَّهُ
hadith.en: Whoever humiliates a believer, Allah will humiliate him

hadith.ar: إِنَّ اللَّهَ لَا يُحِبُّ الۡمُؤۡذِينَ
hadith.en: Allah does not love those who harm others

shades.explanation: al-Hawon (the ease) in the Quran refers to gentleness. The Quran says: And walk not upon the earth exultantly (25:63).
shades.hadith_ar: وَعِبَادُ الرَّحۡمَٰنِ الَّذِينَ يَمۡشُونَ عَلَى الۡأَرۡضِ هَوۡنًا
shades.hadith_en: The servants of the Most Merciful walk on the earth gently

shades.explanation: al-Hawan (the humiliation) in the Quran refers to disgrace. The Quran says: And do not be weak and do not grieve (3:139).
shades.hadith_ar: وَلَا تَهِنُواْ وَلَا تَحۡزَنُواْ
shades.hadith_en: Do not be weak and do not grieve

shades.explanation: al-Hin (the contempt) in the Quran refers to mistreatment. The famous hadith states: O Allah, do not give us over to those who will humiliate us.
shades.hadith_ar: اللَّهُمَّ لَا تَجۡعَلۡنَا فِي يَدِ مَن لَّا يَرۡحَمُنَا
shades.hadith_en: O Allah, do not put us in the hand of one who does not have mercy on us

shades.explanation: al-Ihanah (the insult) in the Quran refers to degrading treatment. The famous hadith states: Whoever humiliates a believer will be humiliated by Allah.
shades.hadith_ar: مَنۡ أَهَانَ مُؤۡمِنًا أَهَانَهُ اللَّهُ
shades.hadith_en: Whoever humiliates a believer, Allah will humiliate him

meaning.en: To be hellish. The root denotes the blazing fire, hell, or frowning.

lexical_analysis.ibn_faris: الۡجِيمُ وَالۡحَاءُ وَالۡمِيمُ أَصۡلٌ يَدُلُّ عَلَى الشِّدَّةِ
lexical_analysis.al_raghib: جَحِيمٌ: نَارٌ شَدِيدَةُ التَّوَقُّدِ

quran_examples.ar: فَإِنَّ الۡجَحِيمَ هِيَ الۡمَأۡوَىٰ
quran_examples.en: Indeed Hellfire is the abode

quran_examples.ar: وَإِذَا الۡجَحِيمُ سُعِّرَتۡ
quran_examples.en: When Hellfire is set ablaze

hadith.ar: نَارُ جَهَنَّمَ أَشَدُّ سَبۡعِينَ ضِعۡفًا
hadith.en: The fire of Jahannam is seventy times hotter

hadith.ar: أَهۡلُ النَّارِ فِيهَا لَا يَمُوتُونَ وَلَا يَحۡيَوۡنَ
hadith.en: The people of Hellfire neither die nor live

shades.explanation: al-Jahim (the hellfire) in the Quran refers to the blazing fire of Hell. The Quran says: And Hellfire will be brought forth for whoever sees (79:36-39).
shades.hadith_ar: فَإِنَّ الۡجَحِيمَ هِيَ الۡمَأۡوَىٰ
shades.hadith_en: Indeed Hellfire is the abode

shades.explanation: al-Jahm (the frowning) in the Quran refers to a stern face. The Quran says: Then they will turn back to each other (37:50).
shades.hadith_ar: فَأَقۡبَلَ بَعۡضُهُمۡ عَلَىٰ بَعۡضٍۢ
shades.hadith_en: Then they turn to one another

shades.explanation: al-Jahm (the terrible face) in the Quran refers to a stern countenance on Judgment Day. The famous hadith states: The fire of Jahannam is seventy times hotter than the fire of this world.
shades.hadith_ar: نَارُ جَهَنَّمَ أَشَدُّ سَبۡعِينَ ضِعۡفًا
shades.hadith_en: The fire of Jahannam is seventy times more severe

shades.explanation: al-Jahimiyyah (the hellish state) in the Quran refers to torment. The famous hadith states: The dwellers of Hellfire will be punished eternally.
shades.hadith_ar: أَهۡلُ النَّارِ لَا يَمُوتُونَ وَلَا یَحۡيَوۡنَ
shades.hadith_en: The dwellers of Hellfire neither die nor live

meaning.en: To grow. The root denotes growth, vegetation, or sprouting.

lexical_analysis.ibn_faris: النُّونُ وَالۡبَاءُ وَالتَّاءُ أَصۡلٌ يَدُلُّ عَلَى الإِظۡهَارِ
lexical_analysis.al_raghib: نَبَتَ: ظَهَرَ مِنَ الۡأَرۡضِ

quran_examples.ar: وَأَنۢبَتۡنَا فِيهَا مِن كُلِّ زَوۡجٍۭ بَهِيجٍ
quran_examples.en: We cause to grow every beautiful kind

quran_examples.ar: فَأَخۡرَجۡنَا بِهِۦ نَبَاتَ كُلِّ شَيۡءٍ
quran_examples.en: We bring forth the growth of all things

hadith.ar: إِنَّ اللَّهَ يُنۡبِتُ الحَقَّ كَمَا يُنۡبِتُ الزَّرۡعَ
hadith.en: Allah causes truth to grow as He causes crops to grow

hadith.ar: مَنۡ أَحۡيَا أَرۡضًا مَّيۡتَةً فَهِيَ لَهُ
hadith.en: Whoever revives a dead land, it is his

shades.name_ar: النَّبَاتُ - مَا يُنبِتُهُ اللَّهُ مِنَ الۡأَرۡضِ
shades.explanation: an-Nabat (the plant) in the Quran refers to vegetation. The Quran says: And We cause to grow therein every beautiful kind (50:7).
shades.hadith_ar: وَأَنۢبَتۡنَا فِيهَا مِن كُلِّ زَوۡجٍۭ بَهِيجٍ
shades.hadith_en: And We cause to grow therein every beautiful kind

shades.explanation: al-Munbit (the Grower) in the Quran refers to Allah who causes plants to grow. The Quran says: He it is who sends down water from the sky (6:99).
shades.hadith_ar: وَهُوَ الَّذِيٓ أَنزَلَ مِنَ السَّمَآءِ مَآءً فَأَخۡرَجۡنَا بِهِۦ نَبَاتَ كُلِّ شَيۡءٍ
shades.hadith_en: He sends down water from the sky and We bring forth the growth of all things

shades.explanation: an-Nabat (the offspring) in the Quran refers to descendants. The famous hadith states: A woman is married for four reasons: her wealth, her lineage, her beauty, and her religion.
